contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $X$ and $Y$ be real Hilbert spaces and let $K:X\to Y$ be a compact linear operator of infinite rank, viewed as an inverse model with exact datum $Kx$. Here compact means that the image of every bounded subset has compact closure. Write $N(K)=\{x\in X:Kx=0\}$ and $H_0=\overline{\operatorname{ran}K}$. Fix a positive singular system $(s_j,v_j,u_j)_{j\in\mathbb N}$ for $K$, where $\mathbb N=\{1,2,3,\ldots\}$, $s_1\ge s_2\ge\cdots>0$, $s_j\to0$, $Kv_j=s_ju_j$, $(v_j)$ is a complete orthonormal basis of $N(K)^\perp$, and $(u_j)$ is a complete orthonormal basis of $H_0$. A complete orthonormal basis is an orthonormal family whose closed linear span is the whole indicated subspace. These are the compact SVD conventions; in particular, this model concerns minimum-norm representatives in $N(K)^\perp$ and does not estimate a kernel component.

For a truth $x\in N(K)^\perp$, let $\theta_j=\langle x,v_j\rangle_X$. The complete-basis coefficient map identifies $N(K)^\perp$ bijectively and isometrically with $\ell^2(\mathbb N,\mathbb R)$, so every $\theta\in\ell^2(\mathbb N,\mathbb R)$ is a model parameter. For $\epsilon>0$, take the functional white-noise experiment on the separable Hilbert space $H_0$ with observations $Y_x(g)=\langle Kx,g\rangle_Y+\epsilon W(g)$, where $W$ is centered, has covariance $\mathbb E[W(g)W(h)]=\langle g,h\rangle_Y$, and has independent standard-normal values on every finite orthonormal tuple. The countable complete basis makes $H_0$ separable. Define $\xi_j=W(u_j)$ and $Z_j=Y_x(u_j)/s_j$. The sequence sample space is $\mathbb R^{\mathbb N}$ with the product Borel sigma-algebra, meaning the sigma-algebra generated by its coordinate projections. The coordinate law is the pushforward of the functional experiment under $y\mapsto(y(u_j)/s_j)_{j\in\mathbb N}$; this map is measurable because each coordinate is a cylinder evaluation followed by scalar multiplication. The compact SVD expansion gives $\langle Kx,u_j\rangle_Y=s_j\theta_j$, and the positive-noise white-noise coordinate theorem gives the independent standard-normal coordinates $\xi_j$. Hence the normalized coordinates satisfy $Z_j=\theta_j+\epsilon s_j^{-1}\xi_j,\qquad j\in\mathbb N.$

For the zero-noise boundary $\epsilon=0$, define the sequence experiment separately by the point mass at $\theta$, so $Z_j=\theta_j$. This boundary is not an instance of the positive-noise functional experiment.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Assume Countable Choice and use the Gaussian sequence inverse model with singular values $s_j>0$, inverse-noise weights $\sigma_j=s_j^{-1}$, and parameter coordinates $\theta=(\theta_j)\in\ell^2$. Let $a=(a_j)$ be a positive nondecreasing sequence with $a_j\to\infty$, and let $\sigma=(\sigma_j)$ be a positive nondecreasing sequence with $\sigma_j\to\infty$. For $\varepsilon>0$, put $\eta_j=\theta_j/\sigma_j$ and observe $Y_j=Z_j/\sigma_j=\eta_j+\varepsilon\xi_j$, where $Z$ is the normalized observation in the Gaussian sequence inverse model and the $\xi_j$ are independent standard normal random variables. For $0<q\le2$ and $r>0$, define
$$\Theta_q(r)=\left\{\eta\in\mathbb R^{\mathbb N}:(\sigma_j\eta_j)_{j\ge1}\in\ell^2,\ \sum_{j=1}^{\infty}|a_j\sigma_j\eta_j|^q\le1,\ \sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\sigma_j^2\eta_j^2\ge r^2\right\}.$$
Test $H_0:\eta=0$ against $H_1:\eta\in\Theta_q(r)$ by a product-Borel measurable randomized test $\psi:\mathbb R^{\mathbb N}\to[0,1]$, where $\psi(y)$ is the rejection probability. Its type-I error and maximal type-II error are
$$\alpha_\varepsilon(\psi)=\mathbb E_{\varepsilon,0}\psi,\qquad \beta_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r),\psi)=\sup_{\eta\in\Theta_q(r)}\mathbb E_{\varepsilon,\eta}(1-\psi).$$
When $\Theta_q(r)=\varnothing$, define $\beta_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r),\psi)=\beta_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r),\alpha)=\gamma_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r))=0$, the convention that no type-II error occurs when no alternative is possible. For $\alpha\in(0,1)$ define
$$\beta_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r),\alpha)=\inf_{\psi:\,\alpha_\varepsilon(\psi)\le\alpha}\beta_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r),\psi),\qquad \gamma_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r))=\inf_\psi\{\alpha_\varepsilon(\psi)+\beta_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r),\psi)\}.$$
A positive family $r_\varepsilon^*\to0$ is a minimax separation rate if $\gamma_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r_\varepsilon))\to1$ and $\beta_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r_\varepsilon),\alpha)\to1-\alpha$ for every $\alpha\in(0,1)$ whenever $r_\varepsilon/r_\varepsilon^*\to0$, while $\gamma_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r_\varepsilon))\to0$ and $\beta_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r_\varepsilon),\alpha)\to0$ for every $\alpha\in(0,1)$ whenever $r_\varepsilon/r_\varepsilon^*\to\infty$.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume Countable Choice. In the Gaussian sequence detection experiment, let $v\in\Theta_q(r)$ have finite support $J$ and put
$$u(v)^2=\frac{1}{2\varepsilon^4}\sum_{j\in J}v_j^4.$$
Let $\pi_v$ be the uniform probability law on the finite family of mean sequences whose $j$th coordinate is independently $+v_j$ or $-v_j$ for $j\in J$ and is zero off $J$, and let $P_{\pi_v}$ be the corresponding mixture sampling law. Then its likelihood ratio with respect to the null law is
$$L_v=\frac{dP_{\pi_v}}{dP_{\varepsilon,0}}=\prod_{j\in J}\exp\!\left(-\frac{v_j^2}{2\varepsilon^2}\right)\cosh\!\left(\frac{v_jY_j}{\varepsilon^2}\right),$$
it satisfies
$$\mathbb E_{\varepsilon,0}L_v^2=\prod_{j\in J}\cosh\!\left(\frac{v_j^2}{\varepsilon^2}\right),\qquad \mathbb E_{\varepsilon,0}(L_v-1)^2\le \exp(u(v)^2)-1,$$
and the minimax risks obey
$$\gamma_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r))\ge1-\frac12\sqrt{\exp(u(v)^2)-1},\qquad \beta_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r),\alpha)\ge1-\alpha-\frac12\sqrt{\exp(u(v)^2)-1}$$
for every $\alpha\in(0,1)$.

facts:
**Given:** Countable Choice, $\varepsilon>0$, $v\in\Theta_q(r)$ of finite support, and the null and alternative laws in the Gaussian sequence detection experiment.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: Countable Choice is inherited from the Gaussian sequence inverse model.

[F1] [[def-ip-gaussian-sequence-inverse-model]] and [[thm-ip-white-noise-spectral-sequence-representation]]: after scaling the normalized observation by $s_j=\sigma_j^{-1}$, $Y_j=\eta_j+\varepsilon\xi_j$ with independent standard normal coordinates $\xi_j$.

[F2] [[def-ip-minimax-detection-risk-and-separation]]: $\alpha_\varepsilon(\psi)=\mathbb E_{\varepsilon,0}\psi$, $\beta_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r),\psi)=\sup_{\eta\in\Theta_q(r)}\mathbb E_{\varepsilon,\eta}(1-\psi)$, and $\gamma_\varepsilon$ is the infimum of their sum.

[F3] [[lem-normal-density-has-total-mass-one]]: the standard normal density is $\varphi(x)=(2\pi)^{-1/2}e^{-x^2/2}$ and integrates to one.

[F4] [[thm-independent-random-elements-have-product-joint-law]]: a finite tuple of independent coordinates has the product of its marginal laws.

[F5] [[lem-finite-measure-uniqueness-on-a-pi-system]]: probability measures agreeing on a generating pi-system agree on its generated sigma-algebra.

[F6] [[def-total-variation-distance-for-probability-laws]]: $\|P-Q\|_{\rm TV}=\sup_A|P(A)-Q(A)|$ over measurable events.

[F7] [[thm-c-one-change-of-variables-for-nonnegative-lebesgue-measurable-functions]]: translation of the standard normal density preserves its integral, so $\mathbb E e^{tG}=e^{t^2/2}$ for $G\sim N(0,1)$ by completing the square.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $H$ be a separable real Hilbert space with a fixed complete orthonormal basis $(u_j)$, indexed by $J=\{1,\ldots,m\}$ for $m\in\mathbb N_0$ or by $J=\mathbb N_{>0}$; the empty basis covers $H=\{0\}$. Let $Y_x(g)=\langle Kx,g\rangle_H+\epsilon Z(g)$ be the isonormal white-noise experiment with $\epsilon>0$, and write $\mu_j=\langle Kx,u_j\rangle_H$. For every parameter $x$ and every basis index $j$, the observations $Y_x(u_j)$ are independent and have laws $N(\mu_j,\epsilon^2)$, where $N$ is the scalar normal law defined in the experiment.

For $g\in H$, set $P_Ng=\sum_{j\in J,\ j\le N}\langle g,u_j\rangle_Hu_j$, with $P_N=I$ once all vectors of a finite basis have been included. Then

$$Y_x(g)=L^2(\mathbb P)\text{-}\lim_{N\to\infty}\sum_{j\in J,\ j\le N}\langle g,u_j\rangle_HY_x(u_j).$$

Thus every finite collection of observation functionals is reconstructed from the coefficient sequence in mean square. This does not assert almost-sure convergence of the full sequence of partial sums, a simultaneous path identity for all test vectors, or an $H$-valued observation.

More precisely, let $\mathcal C_H$ be the cylinder sigma-algebra on $\mathbb R^H$, let $\mathcal C_J$ be the sigma-algebra on $\mathbb R^J$ generated by its coordinate evaluations, and let $P_x$ be the field sampling law. Define $S:\mathbb R^H\to\mathbb R^J$ by $S(y)_j=y(u_j)$ and $Q_x=S_*P_x$, where a pushforward is $S_*P_x(B)=P_x(S^{-1}(B))$. There is a measurable map $T:(\mathbb R^J,\mathcal C_J)\to(\mathbb R^H,\mathcal C_H)$, depending only on the indexed basis, such that for every parameter $x$,

$$S_*P_x=Q_x,\qquad T_*Q_x=P_x,\qquad S\circ T=\operatorname{id}_{\mathbb R^J}.$$

These parameter-independent maps give equivalence of the field cylinder experiment and its coefficient experiment. One such map is the following. For $k\ge1$ and $g\in H$, let $N_k(g)$ be the least integer $N\ge k$ with $\|g-P_Ng\|_H\le2^{-k}$ and put

$$a_{g,k}(z)=\sum_{j\in J,\ j\le N_k(g)}\langle g,u_j\rangle_Hz_j,\qquad T(z)(g)=\begin{cases}\lim_{k\to\infty}a_{g,k}(z),&\text{if the limit exists in }\mathbb R,\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}$$

For each fixed $x$ and $g$, $T(S(Y_x))(g)=Y_x(g)$ almost surely, and the same holds jointly for each fixed finite list of test vectors. The exceptional event may depend on $x$ and on that list; no intersection over all $g\in H$ is asserted. In dimension zero the coefficient space is a singleton and $T$ returns the field with value zero at $g=0$.

If $H=L^2([0,1])$ and the basis is one of the wavelet or trigonometric bases used to define the negative Sobolev carrier $H(\delta)$, then under countable choice and for $\delta>1/2$ the same coordinate sequence is a Borel Gaussian random element in $H(\delta)$ with mean coefficients $Kx$ and noise level $\epsilon$. In infinite dimension it is not an $L^2([0,1])$-valued sample.

facts:
[F1] [[def-ip-isonormal-white-noise-experiment]]: The process is linear into $L^2(\mathbb P)$, centered, has covariance $\mathbb E[Z(g)Z(h)]=\langle g,h\rangle_H$, and has independent standard-normal coordinates on every finite orthonormal tuple.

[F2] [[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]: A complete orthonormal family has dense finite linear span in $H$; an orthogonal projection onto a finite span is given by the corresponding finite coefficient sum.

[F3] [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-in-an-inner-product-space]]: For vectors $v,w$ in a real or complex inner-product space, $|\langle v,w\rangle|\le\|v\|\,\|w\|$.

[F4] [[def-negative-sobolev-space-for-white-noise]]: For $\delta>0$, $H(\delta)$ has squared coefficient norm $\sum_{l,k}a_l^{-1}(\log a_l)^{-2\delta}|c_{lk}|^2$, and the coefficient map embeds $L^2([0,1])$ continuously into $H(\delta)$.

[F5] [[lem-white-noise-is-borel-gaussian-on-negative-sobolev-space]]: Under countable choice, for the specified wavelet or trigonometric basis and $\delta>1/2$, the independent standard-normal coefficient sequence is almost surely a Borel Gaussian random element of $H(\delta)$ and is not an $L^2([0,1])$-valued random element.

[F6] [[thm-chebyshev-markov-inequality-for-the-integral]]: For any nonnegative measurable $f$ on a measure space and $t>0$, $\mu\{f\ge t\}\le t^{-1}\int f\,d\mu$; the space need not be finite or discrete.

[F7] [[thm-first-borel-cantelli]]: If measurable events have summable probabilities, their limsup has probability zero; independence is not required.

[F8] [[thm-sequential-suprema-infima-limsup-liminf-and-pointwise-limits-are-measurable]]: The limsup and liminf of a sequence of measurable real functions are measurable, as is their equality set.

[F9] [[lem-finite-measure-uniqueness-on-a-pi-system]]: Finite measures agreeing on a generating pi-system and on the whole space agree on the generated sigma-algebra.

[F10] [[lem-law-of-a-random-element-is-a-probability-measure]]: The pushforward law of a measurable random element is a probability measure.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: Countable choice states that every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function.

**Given:** The experiment and hypotheses in the Statement, a fixed complete finite or countable orthonormal basis, and, for the final clause, the stated $L^2([0,1])$ basis and $\delta>1/2$.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $H$ be a separable real Hilbert space, where separable means having a countable dense subset, and let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$ be a probability space. A real isonormal Gaussian process on $H$ is a family $Z(g)$ of real random variables with finite second moments, indexed by $g\in H$, such that $g\mapsto[Z(g)]$ is linear into $L^2(\mathbb P)$, $\mathbb E Z(g)=0$, and $\mathbb E[Z(g)Z(h)]=\langle g,h\rangle_H$. It is also required that for every finite orthonormal tuple $(e_1,\ldots,e_m)$ the variables $Z(e_1),\ldots,Z(e_m)$ are independent and each has density $\varphi(t)=(2\pi)^{-1/2}e^{-t^2/2}$. For any finite list of vectors, expressing them in an orthonormal basis of their finite-dimensional span shows that their process values have the corresponding linear-image Gaussian law. Here $L^2(\mathbb P)$ identifies square-integrable random variables that agree almost surely. When $H\ne\{0\}$, all unit-vector marginals have the same law; write $N(a,\sigma^2)$ for the law of $a+\sigma Z(e)$ for any unit vector $e\in H$ and $\sigma\ge0$.

Let $X$ be a set, let $\Theta\subseteq X$ be a nonempty parameter set, let $K:X\to H$ be a signal map, and let $\epsilon>0$. For $x\in\Theta$ and $g\in H$, define the observation functional

$$Y_x(g)=\langle Kx,g\rangle_H+\epsilon Z(g).$$

The associated statistical inverse experiment has sample space $\mathbb R^H$ with the cylinder sigma-algebra generated by the evaluation maps $y\mapsto y(g)$, and its sampling law $P_x$ is the law of the random function $g\mapsto Y_x(g)$. Each sample is indexed by test functionals on $H$; it is not asserted to be a vector in $H$ or to have a continuous path. If $H=\{0\}$, linearity forces $Z(0)=0$ and the experiment is deterministic.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume Countable Choice and the minimax detection-risk definition with $0<q<2$, $a_j=j^\alpha$, $\sigma_j=j^\beta$, and $\alpha,\beta>0$. Let $r_\varepsilon\to0$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$, and put
$$\lambda=\frac{\alpha+\beta}{2}-\frac{\beta}{q}.$$
For $\lambda>0$, put $A=2\alpha+1/q-1/2$, $B=2(\alpha+\beta)+1/q$, and $D=\alpha+\beta(1-2/q)>0$. Choose any $\delta_\varepsilon>0$ with $\delta_\varepsilon\to0$ and $\delta_\varepsilon\log\varepsilon^{-1}\to\infty$, set $\widetilde r_\varepsilon=r_\varepsilon(1-\delta_\varepsilon)$, and define
$$u_\varepsilon^2=2\inf\left\{\sum_{j\ge1}h_j^2\sinh^2(z_j^2/2):\ 0\le h_j\le1,\ z_j\ge0,\ \sum_{j\ge1}j^{2\beta}h_jz_j^2\ge\frac{\widetilde r_\varepsilon^2}{\varepsilon^2},\ \sum_{j\ge1}j^{q(\alpha+\beta)}h_jz_j^q\le\frac1{\varepsilon^q}\right\}.$$
For each fixed significance level $\ell\in(0,1)$, the sharp errors have Gaussian form
$$\beta_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r_\varepsilon),\ell)=\Phi(H_\ell-u_\varepsilon)+o(1),\qquad \gamma_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r_\varepsilon))=2\Phi(-u_\varepsilon/2)+o(1),$$
where $\Phi(t)=(2\pi)^{-1/2}\int_{-\infty}^t e^{-x^2/2}\,dx$ and $H_\ell$ is its $(1-\ell)$-quantile. Moreover, if $r_\varepsilon=o(\varepsilon^{a_c})$ with $a_c=(q\alpha+1-q/2)/(q(\alpha+\beta)+1)$, then
$$u_\varepsilon\sim c_{\alpha,\beta,q}\,\varepsilon^{-A/D}r_\varepsilon^{B/D}$$
for a constant $c_{\alpha,\beta,q}>0$. Without this additional restriction on $r_\varepsilon$, the sharp error formulas above remain valid for every $r_\varepsilon\to0$, and a minimax separation rate is
$$r_\varepsilon^*=\varepsilon^{A/B}.$$
If $\lambda\le0$, for the same fixed significance level $\ell\in(0,1)$ put $n_\varepsilon=r_\varepsilon^{-1/\alpha}$ and $D_\varepsilon=n_\varepsilon^{-\beta}r_\varepsilon/\varepsilon-\sqrt{2\log n_\varepsilon}$. Then the sharp errors have degenerate form
$$\beta_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r_\varepsilon),\ell)=(1-\ell)\Phi(-D_\varepsilon)+o(1),\qquad \gamma_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r_\varepsilon))=\Phi(-D_\varepsilon)+o(1),$$
and a sharp separation-rate normalization is
$$r_\varepsilon^*=\Lambda\,\varepsilon^{\alpha/(\alpha+\beta)}(\log\varepsilon^{-1})^{\alpha/[2(\alpha+\beta)]},\qquad \Lambda=\left(\frac{2}{\alpha+\beta}\right)^{\alpha/[2(\alpha+\beta)]}.$$
Thus the sparse boundary $\lambda=0$ belongs to the degenerate regime, and the two regimes have different separation rates.

The deterministic globalized score-and-maximum family and the finite maximum tests constructed in the proof are asymptotically minimax in the Gaussian and degenerate regimes, respectively; the significance tests include deterministic randomization to satisfy the exact level constraint.

facts:
**Given:** Countable Choice, the sequence experiment and alternatives in the Statement. Write $s=\alpha+\beta$, use $\ell\in(0,1)$ for the fixed significance level, and put $X_i=Y_i/\varepsilon=\mu_i+G_i$, where $\mu_i=\eta_i/\varepsilon$. The supplied normal probability law has density $\phi$ and distribution function $\Phi$.

[F1] [[def-ip-minimax-detection-risk-and-separation]]: the actual alternatives satisfy $\sum i^{2\beta}\mu_i^2\ge r^2/\varepsilon^2$ and $\sum i^{qs}|\mu_i|^q\le\varepsilon^{-q}$; finite-support alternatives are allowed, and tests are randomized product-Borel maps.

[F2] [[lem-ip-sparse-gaussian-extremal-profile]] supplies the positive scalar certificate $a,b$, inverse profile $z(x)$, coefficient $d(x)=x^{2\beta}/(2a(z(x)))$, constants $c_0,c_1,c_2,M_1,M_2$, their endpoint bounds and Riemann sums, and the relaxed extremal equivalent when $n\to\infty,h_0\to0$.

[F3] [[lem-ip-finite-independent-array-fourth-moment-normal-limit]]: given normalized Gaussian probability laws, finite centered independent arrays whose summed variances tend to $v>0$ and whose summed fourth moments tend to zero have distribution functions converging uniformly to $\Phi(\,\cdot\,/\sqrt v)$, under Countable Choice.

[F4] [[def-ip-isonormal-white-noise-experiment]] supplies independent standard-normal coordinates, including their normalized scalar probability density. Normalization is a hypothesis of that supplied process; no stronger-choice normalization theorem is used.

[F5] [[thm-c-one-change-of-variables-for-nonnegative-lebesgue-measurable-functions]] supplies scalar affine changes of variables under Countable Choice.

[F6] [[thm-chebyshev-markov-inequality-for-the-integral]] gives Markov's inequality, including Chebyshev's inequality by applying it to a squared centered variable.

[F7] [[thm-independent-random-elements-have-product-joint-law]] and [[thm-factorization-of-expectations-for-independent-variables]] identify finite independent coordinate laws and factor their integrable products. [[thm-sigma-finite-product-measure-exists-is-rectangular-and-is-unique]] supplies the finite probability products used for finite priors.

[F8] [[thm-monotone-convergence-for-the-integral]] and [[thm-dominated-convergence]] justify the specified nonnegative series and dominated scalar integrals.

[F9] [[lem-finite-measure-uniqueness-on-a-pi-system]] identifies probability laws agreeing on finite cylinders of the product sigma-algebra.

[F10] [[lem-taylor-lagrange-remainder-from-mean-value]] bounds a third-order Taylor remainder by the supremum of the third derivative times the cube of the increment, divided by six.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: Countable Choice is assumed; all other limits and finite products below use the supplied coordinate laws. No full-Choice central-limit theorem is invoked.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume Countable Choice and the minimax detection-risk definition with $q=2$. For each $\varepsilon$, suppose $\Theta_2(r_\varepsilon)$ is nonempty and has a finite-support fourth-power minimizer $\widetilde\eta_\varepsilon$ with profile $\widetilde\eta_{\varepsilon,j}^2=z_0^2\sigma_j^2(1-Aa_j^2)_+$ as in the extremal-profile lemma. Put
$$u_\varepsilon^2=\frac{1}{2\varepsilon^4}\sum_j\widetilde\eta_{\varepsilon,j}^4,\qquad w_{\varepsilon,j}=\frac{\widetilde\eta_{\varepsilon,j}^2}{\sqrt{2\sum_j\widetilde\eta_{\varepsilon,j}^4}},\qquad w_{\varepsilon,0}=\max_jw_{\varepsilon,j},$$
and define
$$T_\varepsilon=\sum_jw_{\varepsilon,j}\bigl((Y_j/\varepsilon)^2-1\bigr),\qquad \psi_{\varepsilon,H}=\mathbf1_{\{T_\varepsilon>H\}}.$$
If $u_\varepsilon\to0$, then $\gamma_\varepsilon(\Theta_2(r_\varepsilon))\to1$ and $\beta_\varepsilon(\Theta_2(r_\varepsilon),\alpha)\to1-\alpha$ for every $\alpha\in(0,1)$. If $u_\varepsilon\to\infty$, then for every fixed $c\in(0,1)$ the tests $\psi_{\varepsilon,cu_\varepsilon}$ have total error tending to zero.

For the extremal profile, define the finite sums
$$J_1=\sum_j\sigma_j^4(1-Aa_j^2)_+,\quad J_2=A\sum_ja_j^2\sigma_j^4(1-Aa_j^2)_+,\quad J_0=\sum_j\sigma_j^4(1-Aa_j^2)_+^2.$$
The active constraints imply
$$r_\varepsilon^2=A\frac{J_1}{J_2},\qquad u_\varepsilon^2=\left(\frac{r_\varepsilon}{\varepsilon}\right)^4\frac{J_0}{2J_1^2}.$$

facts:
**Given:** Countable Choice; $q=2$; a nonempty class $\Theta_2(r_\varepsilon)$; a finite-support minimizing profile satisfying both active constraints; and the Gaussian sequence detection experiment.

[F1] [[def-ip-minimax-detection-risk-and-separation]]: $\alpha_\varepsilon(\psi)=\mathbb E_0\psi$, $\beta_\varepsilon(\Theta_2(r),\psi)=\sup_{\eta\in\Theta_2(r)}\mathbb E_\eta(1-\psi)$, and $\gamma_\varepsilon$ is the infimum total error.

[F2] [[lem-ip-q2-ellipsoid-extremal-profile-is-minimizer]]: $\widetilde\eta_j^2=z_0^2\sigma_j^2(1-Aa_j^2)_+$ minimizes $\sum_j\eta_j^4$ over $\Theta_2(r)$ and satisfies $\sum_j\sigma_j^2\widetilde\eta_j^2=r^2$, $\sum_ja_j^2\sigma_j^2\widetilde\eta_j^2=1$.

[F3] [[lem-ip-gaussian-product-mixture-testing-bound]]: for a finite-support feasible $v$, its symmetric sign mixture has total-variation distance at most $\tfrac12\sqrt{\exp(u(v)^2)-1}$ from the null; consequently it gives the displayed minimax lower bounds.

[F4] [[def-ip-isonormal-white-noise-experiment]] and [[lem-standard-normal-fourth-moment]]: the noise coordinates are independent standard normals with even density, first and third moments zero, and second and fourth moments $1$ and $3$.

[F5] [[thm-chebyshev-markov-inequality-for-the-integral]]: Chebyshev's inequality bounds a tail probability by the variance divided by the squared deviation.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: Countable Choice is the assumption of the upstream Gaussian sequence model.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the $q=2$ ellipsoid detection-boundary theorem, Countable Choice, and the Axiom of Choice. Along a sequence for which $u_\varepsilon$ is bounded above and bounded away from zero and $w_{\varepsilon,0}\to0$, the minimax level-$\alpha$ type-II error and minimax total error satisfy
$$\beta_\varepsilon(\Theta_2(r_\varepsilon),\alpha)=\Phi(H_\alpha-u_\varepsilon)+o(1),\qquad \gamma_\varepsilon(\Theta_2(r_\varepsilon))=2\Phi(-u_\varepsilon/2)+o(1),$$
where $\Phi$ is the standard normal distribution function and $H_\alpha$ is defined by $\Phi(H_\alpha)=1-\alpha$. Let $c_{\varepsilon,\alpha}=\inf\{t:\mathbb P_{\varepsilon,0}(T_\varepsilon\le t)\ge1-\alpha\}$; then $\mathbb P_{\varepsilon,0}(T_\varepsilon>c_{\varepsilon,\alpha})\le\alpha$ and $c_{\varepsilon,\alpha}\to H_\alpha$. The weighted tests with thresholds $c_{\varepsilon,\alpha}$ and $u_\varepsilon/2$ attain these asymptotics, while the uncalibrated threshold $H_\alpha$ has asymptotic size $\alpha$. The vanishing-largest-weight condition is required for this Gaussian sharp branch.

facts:
**Given:** The q=2 detection-boundary statistic $T_\varepsilon$, finite-support extremal mean $\widetilde\eta_\varepsilon$, $u_\varepsilon$, and weights $w_{\varepsilon,j}$; AC and Countable Choice; $u_\varepsilon$ bounded above and away from zero; $w_{\varepsilon,0}\to0$.

[F1] [[thm-ip-ellipsoid-detection-boundary]]: $2\sum_jw_{\varepsilon,j}^2=1$, every alternative has statistic mean $m_\eta=\sum_jw_{\varepsilon,j}(\eta_j/\varepsilon)^2\ge u_\varepsilon$, and $\operatorname{Var}_\eta(T_\varepsilon)\le1+4w_{\varepsilon,0}m_\eta$.

[F2] [[lem-ip-weighted-chi-square-triangular-array-limit]]: under the null, $T_\varepsilon\Rightarrow N(0,1)$ when $w_{\varepsilon,0}\to0$.

[F3] [[lem-ip-gaussian-product-mixture-testing-bound]]: for the symmetric sign mixture on $\widetilde\eta_\varepsilon$, $L_\varepsilon=dP_{\pi}/dP_0=\prod_j e^{-\delta_j/2}\cosh(\sqrt{\delta_j}G_j)$, where $\delta_j=\widetilde\eta_{\varepsilon,j}^2/\varepsilon^2$ and $G_j=Y_j/\varepsilon$ under the null.

[F4] [[def-ip-isonormal-white-noise-experiment]] and [[lem-standard-normal-fourth-moment]]: under the null the $G_j$ are independent standard normals with even density, second moment $1$, fourth moment $3$, and finite eighth moment (the latter follows by two further integrations by parts against the Gaussian density).

[F5] [[thm-slutsky-for-real-random-variables]]: adding a term converging to zero in probability preserves convergence in distribution.

[F6] [[thm-portmanteau-theorem]]: convergence in distribution gives convergence of bounded uniformly continuous test expectations and convergence of probabilities on Borel sets whose boundaries have limiting probability zero.

[F7] [[thm-chebyshev-markov-inequality-for-the-integral]]: Chebyshev's inequality bounds a tail probability by the variance divided by the squared deviation.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: AC is used through the weighted Lindeberg–Feller theorem in [F2].

[A2] [[def-countable-choice]]: Countable Choice is inherited from the Gaussian sequence experiment.

contract.heading: Example
contract.text:
Take $q=1$, $\alpha=\beta=1$, $a_j=j$, and $\sigma_j=j$ in the Gaussian sequence detection experiment. Then the sparse boundary parameter is $\lambda=0$, the source-normalized constant is $\Lambda=1$, and a minimax separation rate has order
$$r_\varepsilon^*\asymp\varepsilon^{1/2}(\log\varepsilon^{-1})^{1/4}\qquad(\varepsilon\downarrow0).$$

facts:
**Given:** Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), $q=1$, $\alpha=\beta=1$, $\varepsilon\downarrow0$, and the Gaussian sequence experiment over $\Theta_1(r)$.

[F1] [[def-ip-minimax-detection-risk-and-separation]]: $\eta\in\Theta_1(r)$ means $\sum_i i^2|\eta_i|\le1$ and $\sum_i i^2\eta_i^2\ge r^2$; the null coordinates are independent $N(0,\varepsilon^2)$.

[F2] [[thm-factorization-of-expectations-for-independent-variables]] and [[lem-finite-measure-uniqueness-on-a-pi-system]]: nonnegative functions of finitely many independent coordinates have factorized expectations; finite measures agreeing on the generating finite-coordinate rectangular cylinders and on total mass agree on the sequence sigma-algebra.

[F3] [[def-ip-isonormal-white-noise-experiment]]: $Y_i/\varepsilon$ is standard normal under the null, with density $\varphi(x)=(2\pi)^{-1/2}e^{-x^2/2}$. This given probability law already supplies $\int_{\mathbb R}\varphi(x)\,dx=1$.

[F4] [[thm-c-one-change-of-variables-for-nonnegative-lebesgue-measurable-functions]]: under countable choice, completing the square and translating the given normalized density in [F3] gives $\mathbb E e^{tG}=e^{t^2/2}\int_{\mathbb R}\varphi(x-t)\,dx=e^{t^2/2}$ for every real $t$.

[F5] [[thm-chebyshev-markov-inequality-for-the-integral]]: Markov's inequality therefore gives $\mathbb P(|G|>t)\le2e^{-t^2/2}$ for $t>0$.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $Y$ be a closed connected oriented smooth three-manifold. A pointed genus-$g$ Heegaard diagram for $Y$ consists of an embedded splitting $Y=U_\alpha\cup_\Sigma U_\beta$, where $\Sigma=\partial U_\alpha$ is a closed oriented genus-$g$ surface and each $U$ is a handlebody, meaning a regular neighborhood of a finite connected graph; ordered systems $\boldsymbol\alpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_g)$ and $\boldsymbol\beta=(\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_g)$ of pairwise disjoint smooth simple closed curves bounding specified disjoint proper compression disks in the respective handlebodies, each disk system cutting its handlebody into one ball; and one point $z$ off the curves. Opposite-system curves meet transversely in finitely many points. This is closed-manifold data; it includes neither a knot nor a second marked point.

Write $q:\Sigma^g\to\operatorname{Sym}^g(\Sigma)=\Sigma^g/S_g$ for the permutation quotient. The product tori are the images
$$T_\alpha=q(\alpha_1\times\cdots\times\alpha_g),\qquad T_\beta=q(\beta_1\times\cdots\times\beta_g).$$
The group $S_g$ acts on the ambient product, rather than on a fixed ordered product of distinct attaching circles. A generator is an intersection $x\in T_\alpha\cap T_\beta$; equivalently it selects one intersection point on each curve of each system. There are finitely many generators. For $g=0$ the symmetric product and both empty products are one point, with the empty generator.

A Whitney class $\phi\in\pi_2(x,y)$ is a relative homotopy class of maps of a closed disk with two marked boundary points into the symmetric product, taking its two boundary arcs into $T_\alpha,T_\beta$ and its marked points to $x,y$. Its domain is the integral two-chain of complementary regions; its coefficient at an interior point $p$ is the intersection multiplicity $n_p(\phi)$ with $\{p\}+\operatorname{Sym}^{g-1}(\Sigma)$. In particular $n_z(\phi)$ is the basepoint coefficient. A periodic domain is an integral region two-chain whose boundary is an integral sum of full attaching circles. The domain of a class $\psi\in\pi_2(x,x)$ is periodic. Such a class is normalized when $n_z(\psi)=0$. Write $\mu(\phi)$ for the real Fredholm index of the disk linearization, before quotienting longitudinal translation; well-definedness and its topological index formula are properties to be proved in the analytic and index theory.

For a periodic domain P, cap its full attaching-circle boundary with the specified compression disks, using the boundary multiplicities and orientations, to obtain the integral class $H(P)\in H_2(Y;\mathbb Z)$. A Spin-c structure $\mathfrak s$ is a lift of the oriented tangent frame bundle through $\operatorname{Spin}^c(3)\to SO(3)$; $c_1(\mathfrak s)$ is the first Chern class of its determinant line, with determinant character $[s,u]\mapsto u^2$. **Weak admissibility in the specified Spin-c sector $\mathfrak s$** means that EVERY nonzero integral periodic domain P with $n_z(P)=0$ and $\langle c_1(\mathfrak s),H(P)\rangle=0$ has both positive and negative region coefficients. This condition is imposed even when the sector has no diagram generators. It is a condition on domains and the intended sector, not only on periodic classes based at existing generators.

The ordinary sector module $\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H,\mathfrak s)$ uses generators with Morse Spin-c label $\mathfrak s_z(x)=\mathfrak s$. The label is defined by compatible handle Morse data: replace the gradient in disjoint tubes around the generator's index-one/index-two trajectories and the basepoint's index-zero/index-three trajectory by nonsingular fields, and take the Spin-c lift of their oriented perpendicular planes. Its actual construction, independence properties and periodic-index formula are obligations of the Spin-c and index theory. In particular the equality between the index of a REALIZED normalized periodic class based at x and the Chern evaluation in $\mathfrak s_z(x)$ is not assumed as its own proof. A realized-generator test alone is not substituted for the stated domain condition.

An **admissible diagram for the full single-diagram hat module** satisfies this sector condition for EVERY Spin-c structure on Y, including the sectors with no generators. The full module below uses all generators and hence all intended sectors; an empty sector contributes a zero summand but is not omitted from the admissibility test. Equivalently this full-diagram condition is global weak admissibility: every nonzero periodic domain with $n_z=0$ has both signs. The equivalence uses the actual zero-Chern Spin-c sector constructed from complete Heegaard data in [[lem-complete-heegaard-data-have-a-zero-chern-spin-c-sector]]; it is not inferred from a generator existing in that sector. For a SINGLE specified sector, ordinary weak admissibility remains the stated Chern-kernel condition and need not imply global weakness. No assertion of the full group from a diagram tested only at its represented sectors is made.

For $g>0$ choose a complex structure $j$ and positive area form on $\Sigma$. Analytic data include a smooth path $J_t$ on the symmetric product, constant on actual neighborhoods of $t=0,1$. On a fixed neighborhood of the diagonal and the point-divisors for a chosen interior point of every complementary region, including $z$, it agrees with the integrable structure $\operatorname{Sym}^g(j)$; away from that neighborhood it is tame for the form descended from the product surface area form. The path is chosen in a sufficiently small nearly symmetric class. Product-integrable normal forms near the finitely many transverse generators may be included among its specified auxiliary choices. Existence of such choices and of the regular perturbations needed below remains a mathematical obligation. A holomorphic strip is an actual smooth finite-Dirichlet-energy map $u:\mathbb R\times[0,1]\to\operatorname{Sym}^g(\Sigma)$ satisfying
$$u_s+J_t(u)u_t=0,\qquad u(s,0)\in T_\alpha,\quad u(s,1)\in T_\beta,$$
with uniform generator limits at both longitudinal ends. The space in class $\phi$ is $\mathcal M_J(\phi)$, and translation in $s$ acts on it. Regular means that its actual linearized operator is surjective at the solutions being counted. Local multiplicity positivity, Fredholmness, the class index and compactness are results to be proved, not choices of which maps to count.

The hat diagram-level module $\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H;\mathbb F_2)$ is free over $\mathbb F_2$ on the generators. For regular data for which the displayed quotient sets are finite and, for each $x$, only finitely many nonempty pairs $(y,\phi)$ occur, its candidate count operator is
$$\widehat\partial x=\sum_y\ \sum_{\substack{\phi\in\pi_2(x,y)\\\mu(\phi)=1,\ n_z(\phi)=0}}\#_2\bigl(\mathcal M_J(\phi)/\mathbb R\bigr)y.$$
Here $\#_2$ is parity of an actual finite zero-dimensional quotient. For $g=0$ the operator is zero on the empty generator. That the required regular finite counts exist, that $\widehat\partial^2=0$, and that its homology is invariant under changing pointed admissible diagrams and auxiliary choices are separate analytic and move theorems. Once these hold, the common homology is denoted $\widehat{HF}(Y;\mathbb F_2)$. No filtered chain-homotopy invariant, integral orientations or absolute grading is asserted by this definition.

Comparisons of embedded diagrams permit orientation-preserving isomorphisms carrying $Y$, its two handlebodies, their oriented surface, the attaching systems and $z$ to the specified counterparts, equivalently compatible collared extensions of the surface map. Curve-factor reordering gives the corresponding product identification. Analytic data are transported by the induced symmetric-product map, including $j$, the area form, protected neighborhoods and $J_t$. The intended count identification is the actual pushforward of generators and disk classes with these transported data; its compatibility with the operator requires proof. An ambient isotopy is not assumed to act as the identity. Comparison of independently chosen perturbations likewise requires the continuation theorem.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $D$ be a finite regular diagram of an oriented link $L$ with ordered crossing set $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. The resolution cube has vertices $I\in\{0,1\}^n$, and $D(I)$ is obtained by applying the indicated local smoothing at every crossing. The link-surgery filtered module associated to $D$ is the direct sum
$$
C_D=\bigoplus_{I\in\{0,1\}^n}\widehat{CF}(\Sigma(D(I));\mathbb F_2),
$$
with the summand for $I$ in increasing filtration degree $n-|I|$. Choose the subordinate Heegaard multi-diagram, compatible perturbation data and top-generator cycles for successive attaching-curve systems. The diagonal component of the candidate differential is the ordinary hat disk differential. For $I<J$ coordinatewise, sum over every ordered path $I=I_0<I_1<\cdots<I_r=J$ changing one coordinate at each step. Its summand counts the zero-dimensional holomorphic $(r+2)$-gon spaces with input at the $I$ vertex, the selected top-generator cycles between each pair of successive attaching systems, and output at the $J$ vertex. The count includes the allowed source conformal parameters and imposes zero basepoint multiplicity. These are the surgery polygon maps; the component is zero if $I\nleq J$. Thus changing several crossings is a sum over paths and polygon counts, not an arbitrary direct edge map. The increasing filtration is $F_pC_D=\bigoplus_{|I|\ge n-p}\widehat{CF}(\Sigma(D(I));\mathbb F_2)$, extended by zero below $0$ and by $C_D$ at and above $n$. Thus a component increasing $|I|$ lowers its filtration degree and preserves every $F_p$. The cube direction and the reduced Khovanov cochain degree remain separate indices. The polygon-count finiteness, square-zero, and total-homology identifications are justified by the surgery lemma, which labels its actual Ozsváth–Szabó construction and top-input/filling calculations as external inputs, separately from the retained local analytic theorem and finite filtration algebra.

The local smoothing labels are those of Ozsváth–Szabó Figure1: in the chart with northwest–southeast over-strand, 0 joins the two left and two right endpoints, and 1 joins the two top and two bottom endpoints. These become A and B on the mirror chart, respectively. This fixes the convention for the consumers without a diagram-invariance assertion. The general surgery lemma also applies to links in arbitrary closed oriented three-manifolds; this definition is only its branched-cover instance.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $F$ be an oriented smooth surface and let $c:S^1\hookrightarrow F$ be a smooth embedded circle. Choose an annular coordinate map $\phi:S^1\times[-1,1]\to A\subset F$ whose product orientation agrees with the orientation of $F$ and whose core $\phi(S^1\times\{0\})$ is $c(S^1)$. Choose a smooth function $\rho:[-1,1]\to[0,1]$ that is $0$ near $-1$ and $1$ near $1$. The positive **Dehn twist about $c$ in the chosen annular coordinates** is the diffeomorphism that is the identity outside $A$ and on $A$ is
$$
\phi(e^{i\theta},t)\longmapsto\phi(e^{i(\theta+2\pi\rho(t))},t).
$$
The negative Dehn twist is its inverse. The annular coordinates and cutoff are part of the data whenever a representative diffeomorphism is used; its mapping class is its class under smooth isotopy through orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms of $F$.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Let $\tau$ be the positive half-twist mapping class of a disk interchanging two marked branch points and fixed near the disk boundary. Choose its standard supported half-turn representative in coordinates compatible with the local branched square charts, and take its unique smooth lift to the connected two-fold branched cover which fixes the annular boundary pointwise. Its smooth isotopy class relative to that boundary is the positive Dehn twist about the core when the half-twist orientation agrees with the annular orientation, and is the inverse twist when the orientation is reversed. A positive half-twist here is the usual supported rotation through $+\pi$ in an oriented disk coordinate containing the two points, interpolated to the identity outside that coordinate disk; the assertion is independent of its cutoff representative.

facts:
**Given:** The disk with two branch points, its connected two-fold simple branched cover, and the supported positive half-twist. All calculations below are finite and use no choice axiom.

[F2] [[thm-path-lifting-for-covering-maps]] and [[thm-homotopy-lifting-for-covering-maps]] give unique continuation and unique isotopy lifting once one sheet is specified. They apply to the ordinary cover away from the two branch points; the explicit local square coordinate fills those points below.

For either orientation of $L(3,1)$, the standard genus-one pointed Heegaard diagram has three intersection generators and its $\widehat{CF}$ differential over $\mathbb F_2$ is zero. contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume ACω. Let a finite pointed Heegaard multidiagram have actual complete handlebody disk systems for closed oriented three-manifolds, with a basepoint in every one-system cut component. Ordered polygons use distinct labeled, pairwise transverse attaching systems; when an operation repeats a geometric system, use its separately labeled small transverse auxiliary copies. For the full hat operations impose global weak multidiagram admissibility: every nonzero full-curve multiperiodic domain vanishing at all basepoints has both signs. For operations in a specified total Spin-c family, ordinary weak admissibility is also allowed: every nonzero formal periodic domain difference in the capped Spin-c kernel, normalized at every mark and with Chern evaluation zero, has both signs. The same formal sector condition is imposed on each relevant boundary pair, including intended sectors with no generators. In this ordinary weak branch all basepoint multiplicities are fixed to zero, the required arities and compact auxiliary parameter families are finite, and counts use the corresponding fixed actual index bands. Strict all-mark normalized strong admissibility is a further allowed branch; it is not substituted for ordinary weakness. For a single diagram the full-module admissibility convention tests all intended Spin-c sectors, including empty sectors, and implies the required global weak domain condition.

In positive symmetric rank choose, among the auxiliary data, an arbitrarily small pointed Hamiltonian representative with no triple product-torus intersection, following its pair generators and transporting its domains, actual Spin-c labels and admissibility. Fix that representative. Compatible generic source-dependent perturbations, coherent over the required conformal faces and auxiliary parameter families, then make the disk and polygon spaces entering the hat differential, continuation, handleslide, stabilization and surgery operations regular with their actual expected dimensions. The common protected tensor and arbitrary constant product-angle end charts can be prescribed, and coherent perturbations can be arbitrarily small about a supplied compatible reference model. Auxiliary polygon and anchored-continuation parameter families here keep the autonomous end paths fixed and regular on the required energy budget; regular compatible parameter-boundary data may be retained. No slice-regularity assertion is made for arbitrary parameter-varying autonomous end paths. This does not assert regularity by almost-complex variations alone on an arbitrary fixed triple, or invariance under the preliminary curve choice.

Dimensions include every allowed conformal and auxiliary family parameter. Quotient only actual source automorphisms: longitudinal translation acts freely on autonomous nonconstant two-ended strips; an anchored source-dependent continuation strip and a three-marked triangle have no translation quotient. Every total zero-dimensional space used in a mod-two count is finite, across all its literal realized classes and with its specified labels. The one-dimensional spaces entering the chain-map, composition and homotopy identities compactify to actual compact one-manifolds. At fixed data their boundaries are precisely the matching rigid polygon–polygon conformal splittings and strip–polygon breakings. In an auxiliary family the broken configurations are the rigid joint fiber configurations at one common parameter, together with the prescribed parameter-boundary strata; they need not be products of individually rigid parameterized polygon spaces. Every such broken end has an exhaustive gluing collar. For the zero-basepoint operations no nonconstant sphere or one-torus boundary disk survives; thus the specified boundary-degeneration terms vanish, and there is no further escape or uncontrolled periodic-domain end. Boundary parity gives the differential square-zero identity and the polygon chain-map, composition and homotopy identities.

At symmetric rank zero retain the original empty systems and use the point target directly: the differential is zero, the matching constant triangle is counted once, higher rigid operations vanish, and the conformal and parameter boundary identities are the actual source-space identities. No triple-torus exclusion or free translation quotient is imposed on that point map.

This is the analytic count theorem. It does not construct a subordinate surgery diagram, prove that a named top generator is a cycle, identify the homology of a surgery total complex with a filling, or prove Heegaard-move invariance. Those remain duties of the respective operation constructions.

facts:
**Given:** The actual finite pointed multidiagram, complete cut systems, the stated operation-specific domain admissibility, any fixed total Spin-c label, finite required arities and auxiliary parameter spaces, and the zero-basepoint hat count convention.

[F1] The full single-diagram definition quantifies weak admissibility in every intended Spin-c sector, even empty ones. Complete Heegaard data admit an actual zero-Chern Spin-c sector under ACω, so that full-module condition is equivalent to global mixed signs of normalized periodic domains. A single specified-sector weak condition is not asserted to imply this. ([[def-hat-heegaard-floer-complex-of-a-closed-three-manifold]], [[lem-complete-heegaard-data-have-a-zero-chern-spin-c-sector]])

[F2] Positive-rank small triple-free representatives exist, with pair generators followed and actual source-dependent transports of polygon map spaces. The finite Morse Spin-c construction carries the actual lift, including torsion, and the capped-domain lattice under attaching-curve isotopies. In an ordinarily weak specified sector the nonnegative domains at each fixed entire mark vector and finite actual index set are finite. Strict admissibility additionally gives a lower strip index and finite domains in every bounded upper-index family; that additional conclusion is not used for the ordinary weak branch. ([[lem-pointed-transverse-multidiagrams-admit-small-triple-free-curve-representatives]], [[lem-heegaard-polygon-spin-c-difference-is-the-capped-periodic-domain]], [[lem-strong-polygon-admissibility-bounds-indices-and-positive-domains]])

[F3] On a globally weak multidiagram, coherent source-dependent choices exist with all-index regular zero-marked end strips and polygons, genuine endpoint collars, actual arbitrary product-angle charts, prescribed compatible protected geometry and arbitrarily small perturbations about a compatible reference. The proved finite-count theorem gives stable-source compactness, actual index budgets, exhaustive nonlinear gluing, compact Hausdorff one-manifolds and all zero-marked A-infinity boundaries, including the direct rank-zero model and relative parameter construction. ([[thm-globally-weak-multidiagrams-admit-coherent-all-index-regular-polygon-data]], [[thm-globally-weak-zero-marked-polygons-have-finite-counts-and-a-infinity-boundaries]])

Its proof first obtains the finite lower-index band before taking limits, and retains all actual Spin-c extension and marked-degree data. ([[thm-strictly-admissible-triple-free-polygons-have-full-marked-low-dimensional-counts]])

[F5] Actual fixed-background source-dependent continuation solutions have anchored compactness, all-index regular perturbations, finite counts, exhaustive collars and compact one-manifold parameter boundaries. The central component is not divided by translation; its autonomous escaping end levels are. ([[thm-fixed-background-zero-marked-continuation-counts-give-chain-homotopy-equivalences]])

[F6] The actual point-divisor bundle admits a smooth connection flat in its canonical frame near the boundary tori, with bounded curvature and the degree identity $n_a=-(2\pi i)^{-1}\int u^*F$. Actual finite-ended polygon charts, source-local universal regularity, domain-energy bounds, stable-source compactness and regular-tree gluing are proved without global or strong admissibility as premises; those assumptions enter only their applications to energy bounds. The bounded-energy autonomous argument uses dense time-slice injective sites and its free-image test. contract.heading: Definition
contract.text: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. An oriented lens space is an oriented closed $3$-manifold obtained by gluing two solid tori by an orientation-reversing boundary homeomorphism. For coprime integers $p>0$ and $q$, let $L(p,q)$ denote the oriented union of the exterior of the unknot in the oriented $3$-sphere and a solid torus whose meridian is identified with the slope $p[\mu_U]+q[\lambda_U]$ on the unknot exterior. Thus this library uses the convention $L(p,q)=E_U(p/q)$; no symbol $L(0,q)$ is assigned.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume ACω. For every closed connected oriented smooth three-manifold $Y$, the homology of the hat Heegaard Floer complex over $\mathbb F_2$ is independent, up to isomorphism, of the pointed admissible Heegaard diagram used to define it. The assertion is invariance of the group $\widehat{HF}(Y;\mathbb F_2)$; it does not assert a diagram-independent filtered chain homotopy type.

The finite Heegaard Spin construction supplies a determinant-trivial sector, so this is equivalent to the global mixed-sign condition. Every supplied complete geometric diagram has the actual finite winding preparation to a globally weak one. Actual globally weak chosen hat complexes and their square-zero finite differentials exist. Actual attaching isotopies have regular-interval transport and birth/death equivalences. Their proof supplies the uniform paired-dual winding preparation and explicit unit-pair cancellation. [F4] Transported diagram data identify actual counts by inverse chain isomorphisms. Actual fixed-background continuation now allows independently supplied generator jets and full boundary tensors. After that operation aligns chosen canonical data, the stated fixed-background full-boundary and changing-background theorems give actual equivalences with their common generator prescriptions. ([[lem-closed-pointed-diagram-isomorphisms-identify-hat-counts]], [[thm-fixed-symmetric-background-hat-complexes-with-different-boundary-values-are-equivalent]], [[thm-changing-complex-background-zero-marked-continuations-are-chain-equivalences]], [[thm-fixed-background-hat-continuations-allow-independent-generator-data]])

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the countable-choice Heegaard Floer analytic package. Let $Y$ be any closed oriented three-manifold and let $\mathbb L$ be an ordered framed $n$-component link in $Y$. On its $i$th exterior boundary torus let $\mu_i$ be the meridian and $\lambda_i$ the chosen framing longitude. Use the three filling slopes $\lambda_i$, $\mu_i+\lambda_i$ and $\mu_i$, labelled $0,1,\infty$, respectively; $\infty$ restores the original unfilled component. For $I\in\{0,1,\infty\}^n$ let $Y(I)$ be the simultaneous filling specified by $I$. Fix an admissible pointed Heegaard multi-diagram subordinate to these surgeries and the compatible perturbation and top-generator choices used by the polygon construction. The mod-two polygon maps on
$$C(\mathbb L)=\bigoplus_{I\in\{0,1\}^n}\widehat{CF}(Y(I);\mathbb F_2)$$
form a differential with components only from $I$ to $J\ge I$ coordinatewise. It preserves the increasing filtration
$$F_pC(\mathbb L)=\bigoplus_{|I|\ge n-p}\widehat{CF}(Y(I);\mathbb F_2),$$
extended by zero below zero and by the whole module at and above $n$. Its total homology is isomorphic to $\widehat{HF}(Y(\infty,\ldots,\infty);\mathbb F_2)=\widehat{HF}(Y;\mathbb F_2)$. For $n=1$, the total complex is the mapping cone of the $0$-to-$1$ surgery map and is quasi-isomorphic to the hat complex of the third, $\infty$ filling; this yields the long exact surgery sequence for every surgery triad, with its cyclic ordering. For $n=0$ the cube is the single hat complex of $Y$. No filtered quasi-isomorphism between distinct surgery presentations is included.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: For the $k$-component planar unlink $U_k$, its double branched cover is $\#^{\,k-1}(S^2\times S^1)$, with $\Sigma(U_1)=S^3$. Over $\mathbb F_2$, the hat Floer group of this cover is identified with the exterior algebra on a $(k-1)$-dimensional vector space, hence has rank $2^{k-1}$. Under these identifications, the cobordism maps for the saddle cobordisms between unlink resolutions are the multiplication and comultiplication maps of the two-dimensional Frobenius algebra $\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)$ after reduction at a marked component. The identification includes the marked-circle cases and fixes the basis conventions needed to compare the first surgery differential with the reduced Khovanov cube.

[F3] The actual analytic foundations [[lem-os-disk-and-polygon-analytic-foundations]] provide finite zero-basepoint disk and polygon counts, compactified boundaries, exhaustive gluing and the resulting identities under their actual operation-specific global weak, ordinary specified-sector weak or strict admissibility hypotheses. These local identities do not compute the exterior-algebra basis or its $H_1$ action, prove a named top input is a cycle, or identify an unlink saddle map with a prescribed Frobenius map.

The statement includes the actual triangle-map/$H_1$-action computation, not merely the dimension of the group.

Its commutative square(13) identifies EVERY immediate surgery edge in the same state bases. Unmarked merge identifies $\gamma_1,\gamma_2$; unmarked split has new kernel $\gamma_1-\gamma_2$; setting $\gamma_0=0$ gives both marked cases. This is an external input at the chosen finite diagram, not arbitrary unlink naturality or a new locally proved count.

contract.text: Let $T$ be either oriented trefoil in $S^3$. contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
**Input:** a nonempty finite regular oriented link diagram $D$ and a total order $c_1<\cdots<c_n$ on its crossing set. A diagram object is supplied as mathematical input; this procedure does not parse a serialized string.

**Output:** the normalized bigraded Khovanov cochain module $C^{i,j}(D)$ and its candidate differential $d:C^{i,j}(D)\to C^{i+1,j}(D)$, constructed by the following finite instructions.

1. Enumerate every state $v:C(D)\to\{0,1\}$ once. Form the crossingless resolution by using the A-smoothing at $v(c)=0$ and the B-smoothing at $v(c)=1$.
2. For each state, create one tensor factor of the integral Frobenius algebra for each resolution circle and place the resulting tensor product in cohomological degree $|v|-n_-$ and quantum degree $|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum\deg(a)$ for its circle labels $a$.
3. For each state and each crossing $c_j$ with $v(c_j)=0$, create the edge to $v+e_j$. Apply multiplication if that smoothing change merges two circles, comultiplication if it splits one circle, the identity on other tensor factors, and the sign $(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}v(c_i)}$. Sum the edge maps out of every state to obtain $d$.
4. Return the finite direct sum of the state modules with these degrees and maps. The square-zero property is the separate local lemma named by `justified_by`.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text: Let $(D,p)$ be a finite regular oriented link diagram with a marked point $p$ away from crossings, and let $C(D;\mathbb F_2)$ be its normalized Khovanov cochain complex over $\mathbb F_2$ obtained from the algebra $\mathcal A=\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)$ with $\deg_q(1)=1$ and $\deg_q(X)=-1$. On each resolution state, let $X_p$ multiply by $X$ on the circle containing $p$ and act as the identity on the other circle factors. Define the reduced complex by $\widetilde C(D,p)=C(D;\mathbb F_2)/\operatorname{im}X_p$, with the surviving based-circle label $1$ assigned reduced quantum degree $0$ by the shift $\widetilde j=j-1$. Its cohomology is $\widetilde{Kh}^{i,\widetilde j}(D,p;\mathbb F_2)$. The basepoint may lie on any component; for a link, independence of the chosen component is a separate theorem.

facts:
**Given:** A finite regular oriented link diagram $(D,p)$ and its normalized Khovanov cube over $\mathbb F_2$.

[F1] The circle algebra is $\mathcal A=\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)$, with multiplication $m$ and comultiplication $\Delta(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1$, $\Delta(X)=X\otimes X$ ([[def-khovanov-frobenius-algebra-and-cube-of-resolutions]]).

[F2] Every cube edge is the corresponding merge map $m$ or split map $\Delta$, tensored with identities on unaffected circles ([[alg-khovanov-chain-complex-from-diagram]]).

[F3] The signed Khovanov differential squares to zero over the integral algebra, and hence its reduction modulo two also squares to zero ([[lem-khovanov-cube-differential-squares-to-zero]]).

[F4] Each diagram produces a finite normalized cochain complex ([[thm-khovanov-chain-complex-from-diagram-procedure-properties]]).

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $D$ be a nonempty finite regular oriented link diagram in an oriented $3$-sphere, with finite crossing set $C(D)$. Fix a unit viewing normal $n$ and orient the projection plane $P$ so $(u,v)$ is positive exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is positive in the ambient $3$-space. At a crossing $c$, define its sign as the sign of $\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})$, where the two nonzero projected tangent vectors follow the oriented over- and under-strands. Let $n_+$ and $n_-$ be the numbers of positive and negative crossings.

Set $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$, with $\deg(1)=1$ and $\deg(X)=-1$. Its unit, multiplication, counit, and comultiplication are
$$
\eta(1)=1,\qquad m(1\otimes1)=1,\quad m(1\otimes X)=m(X\otimes1)=X,\quad m(X\otimes X)=0,
$$
$$
\epsilon(1)=0,\quad\epsilon(X)=1,\qquad \Delta(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1,\quad\Delta(X)=X\otimes X.
$$
Thus $m$ and $\Delta$ have quantum degree $-1$, while $\eta$ and $\epsilon$ have degree $+1$.

Choose a total order $c_1<\cdots<c_n$ on $C(D)$. A resolution state is a function $v:C(D)\to\{0,1\}$; at $v(c)=0$ use the A-smoothing and at $v(c)=1$ use the B-smoothing from the Kauffman source chart. Write $|v|=\sum_c v(c)$, let $D_v$ be the crossingless resolution, and let $k(v)$ be its number of circles. Assign the state module $\mathcal A^{\otimes k(v)}$. For an edge $v\to v+e_j$ changing crossing $c_j$ from $0$ to $1$, use $m$ if the local smoothing merges two circles and $\Delta$ if it splits one circle, tensored with the identity on all other factors, and multiply this map by $(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}v(c_i)}$. The resulting direct sum has cohomological degree
$$i(v)=|v|-n_-$$
and the generator with circle labels $1$ or $X$ has quantum degree
$$j(v)=|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum_{\text{circle labels }a}\deg(a).$$
This defines the normalized integral Khovanov cube and its candidate degree-zero cochain differential; the assertion that the differential squares to zero is a separate lemma.

The Frobenius identity that controls a merge-split face is represented by the two equal composites below. The diagram records the maps only; the proof verifies the equality on the basis $\{1,X\}^{\otimes2}$ and does not rely on the drawing.

```tikzcd
\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A \arrow[r,"m"] \arrow[d,"\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id}"'] & \mathcal A \arrow[d,"\Delta"] \\
\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A \arrow[r,"\mathrm{id}\otimes m"'] & \mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A
```

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented link diagram, order its crossings as $c_1<\cdots<c_n$, and form the direct sum of state modules $\mathcal A^{\otimes k(v)}$ over all functions $v:C(D)\to\{0,1\}$. Here $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$, each crossing is changed from its A-smoothing at $0$ to its B-smoothing at $1$, and the edge map is the multiplication $m$ for a merge or comultiplication $\Delta$ for a split, multiplied by $(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}v(c_i)}$ on the edge at $c_j$. Then the sum $d$ of all edge maps satisfies $d^2=0$.

facts:
**Given:** The finite ordered crossing set, the state modules and edge maps in the Lemma.

[F2] The differential is the sum of the signed edge maps, and the sign on the edge changing coordinate $j$ is $(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}v(c_i)}$ ([[alg-khovanov-chain-complex-from-diagram]]).

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: For a finite regular oriented link diagram $D$ with $n$ ordered crossings, the procedure that enumerates all $2^n$ smoothing states, assigns one copy of $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$ per resolution circle, places a generator in degrees $i=|v|-n_-$ and $j=|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum\deg(a)$, and sums the signed merge or split edge maps terminates after finitely many operations. Its output is a finite direct sum of finite-rank free abelian groups with a differential of bidegree $(1,0)$ satisfying $d^2=0$; hence it is a bounded bigraded cochain complex.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Let $D,D'$ be finite regular oriented link diagrams related by a planar isotopy or one oriented Reidemeister move. Let $\bar C(D)$ be the integral signed state cube before the writhe shifts, with cohomological degree $|v|$ and quantum degree $|v|+\sum\deg(a)$, and normalize it by $C(D)=\bar C(D)[n_-]\{2n_--n_+\}$ to obtain the state degrees $i=|v|-n_-$ and $j=|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum\deg(a)$. Before normalization, a positive type-I curl gives $\bar C(D_+)\simeq\bar C(D)\{1\}$, a negative type-I curl gives $\bar C(D_-)\simeq\bar C(D)[-1]\{-2\}$, a type-II move gives $\bar C(D_{II})\simeq\bar C(D)[-1]\{-1\}$, and a type-III move gives an unshifted equivalence. Consequently the normalized complexes are bigraded chain homotopy equivalent. If $D,D'$ are based knot diagrams and the move disk is disjoint from the basepoint, the same chain homotopy equivalence descends to their reduced quotient complexes, equivalently to the cut-tangle complexes with interval module $M=\mathbb Z$, $X\cdot1=0$.

**Given:** The normalized integral state complexes of two diagrams that differ by one local move; for the based clause, both move disks avoid the marked point.

[F1] $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$ has basis $1,X$, with $m(1\otimes1)=1$, $m(1\otimes X)=m(X\otimes1)=X$, $m(X\otimes X)=0$, $\Delta(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1$, and $\Delta(X)=X\otimes X$; the maps satisfy associativity, coassociativity and the Frobenius identities ([[def-khovanov-frobenius-algebra-and-cube-of-resolutions]]).

[F2] A state with $r$ coordinates equal to $1$ is shifted by $r$ in quantum degree, and its edge signs are $(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}v(c_i)}$ ([[def-khovanov-frobenius-algebra-and-cube-of-resolutions]]).

[F3] The raw state complex becomes normalized by cohomological shift $[n_-]$ and quantum shift $\{2n_--n_+\}$; in the convention $C[s]^i=C^{i+s}$ and $M\{s\}_j=M_{j+s}$ these shifts give exactly $i=|v|-n_-$ and $j=|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum\deg(a)$ ([[def-khovanov-frobenius-algebra-and-cube-of-resolutions]]).

[F4] For a based knot, the quotient removes the based-circle $X$ label and is identified statewise with the interval module $M=\mathbb Z$, $X\cdot1=0$. Local maps commuting with $X_p$ descend to this quotient, including when a local saddle meets the distinguished resolution component ([[def-reduced-khovanov-cohomology-of-a-knot]]).

[F5] The explicit four-face RII retraction, two signed RIII Gaussian cancellations, tensor-factor conventions, quantum degrees, and commutation with exterior saddle maps and $X_p$ are proved in [[lem-khovanov-signed-local-cancellation-models]] (local-map, cancellation-rule, RII, RIII, grading and exterior-differential proof paragraphs).

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $J=J_1\cup\cdots\cup J_n$ be an oriented link of $n\ge1$ smooth components in $S^3$. Choose pairwise disjoint closed tubular neighborhoods $N(J_i)$, let $X=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}(\bigcup_iN(J_i))$, and let $\mu_i$ be the positive meridian of $J_i$. Let $\lambda_i$ be the longitude parallel to $J_i$ with zero self-linking. Alexander duality identifies $H_1(X;\mathbb Z)$ with $\mathbb Z^n$ on the meridian basis $[\mu_1],\ldots,[\mu_n]$; for $i\ne j$, define $\operatorname{lk}_{S^3}(J_i,J_j)$ to be the $j$-th coordinate of $[\lambda_i]$, the usual oriented linking number. Use the boundary-torus intersection convention $\mu_i\mathbin{\cdot}\lambda_i=+1$. Give $J_i$ an integer framing $f_i$ and fill along $\delta_i=\lambda_i+f_i\mu_i$. Let $A$ be the symmetric integer matrix with $A_{ii}=f_i$ and $A_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}_{S^3}(J_i,J_j)$ for $i\ne j$. Assume $\det A\ne0$, and let $Y$ be the resulting oriented surgery manifold, oriented as the boundary of the 4-dimensional surgery handlebody with outward normal first. Then $H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^n/A\mathbb Z^n$. For torsion classes $[C],[D]\in H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)$ represented by oriented 1-cycles, choose $m>0$ and an integral 2-chain $F$ with $\partial F=mC$ and define $\lambda_Y([C],[D])=(F\mathbin{\cdot}D)/m\pmod{\mathbb Z}$, where the intersection is signed by the orientation of $Y$. If $x,y\in\mathbb Z^n$ are meridian-coordinate representatives of $[C],[D]$, then
$$
\lambda_Y([x],[y])=-x^TA^{-1}y\pmod{\mathbb Z}.
$$

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, the framed link, its surgery slopes, the symmetric linking matrix $A$, and $\det A\ne0$.

[A1] Full AC is the choice-function axiom required by Alexander duality. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] A finite oriented link in $S^3$ is compact and locally contractible; Alexander duality identifies the first homology of its complement with $\mathbb Z^n$, with the positive meridians as coordinate generators. [[def-oriented-link-in-s-three-and-ambient-isotopy]], [[thm-alexander-duality-for-compact-locally-contractible-subsets-of-a-sphere]]

[F2] The open complement of a nonempty smooth link is connected and deformation retracts onto its compact exterior. [[lem-the-complement-of-an-oriented-link-is-a-connected-smooth-three-manifold]]

[F3] The positive meridians use the total-linking normalization: each positive component meridian maps to $1$ under the sum of the Alexander-duality component coordinates. [[def-one-variable-alexander-module-of-an-oriented-link]]

[F4] Mayer–Vietoris is exact for the collar-thickened cover by the exterior and the attached solid tori. [[thm-mayer-vietoris-sequence-in-singular-homology]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume AC. Let $B$ be a compact connected oriented smooth four-manifold with $H_*(B;\mathbb Q)\cong H_*(\mathrm{point};\mathbb Q)$ and connected rational homology sphere boundary $Y$. Assume $Y$ has a nonsingular framed-link surgery presentation with the boundary orientation and linking convention of the surgery linking-form result. The coefficient sequence $0\to\mathbb Z\to\mathbb Q\to\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z\to0$ gives an isomorphism $\beta:H^1(Y;\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)\to H^2(Y;\mathbb Z)$. Define the cohomological linking pairing by
$$\lambda_Y(x,y)=\langle\beta^{-1}(x)\smile y,[Y]\rangle\in\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z.$$
Let $M$ be the image of restriction $H^2(B;\mathbb Z)\to H^2(Y;\mathbb Z)$ and $M^\perp=\{x:\lambda_Y(m,x)=0\text{ for every }m\in M\}$. Then the boundary Spin$^c$ structures extending over $B$ form one affine coset of $M$, the pairing is nonsingular, $M=M^\perp$, and $|M|^2=|H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)|$.

facts:
**Given:** AC, the compact connected oriented smooth rational homology four-ball $B$, connected boundary $Y$, and the nonsingular surgery presentation specified in the statement.

[A1] AC is assumed by the finite-triangulation, Poincare-Lefschetz, UCT, and Bockstein suppliers used below ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

[F1] Compact smooth manifolds admit finite triangulations, so the integral homology groups of $B$ are finitely generated ([[thm-compact-smooth-manifolds-with-corners-admit-relative-finite-triangulations]]).

[F2] For a compact oriented four-manifold with boundary, cap product gives $H^j(B,Y;\mathbb Z)\cong H_{4-j}(B;\mathbb Z)$ and $H^j(B;\mathbb Z)\cong H_{4-j}(B,Y;\mathbb Z)$ under AC ([[thm-poincare-lefschetz-duality]]).

[F3] The pair $(B,Y)$ has the cohomology and homology long exact sequences, and cohomology of a free integral chain complex satisfies the UCT exact sequence ([[thm-long-exact-sequence-of-a-pair-in-singular-cohomology]], [[thm-long-exact-sequence-of-a-pair-in-singular-homology]], [[thm-universal-coefficient-theorem-for-cohomology-over-a-pid]]).

[F4] The connecting map for a short exact coefficient sequence is defined by lifting cocycles and taking the coboundary; it is independent of the chosen lift and representative ([[def-bockstein-connecting-operation]], [[lem-the-bockstein-is-independent-of-lift-and-cocycle-representative]]).

[F5] Cup product is natural under inclusion; for a rational homology sphere, Poincare duality identifies $H^2(Y;\mathbb Z)$ with $H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)$, and the surgery supplier fixes the chain-linking convention as $-A^{-1}$ for a nonsingular matrix $A$ ([[prop-cup-product-is-natural-unital-and-associative]], [[thm-poincare-duality-for-oriented-topological-manifolds]], [[lem-cyclic-cover-linking-form-inverse-matrix]]).

[F6] Once a Spin$^c$ lift is given, the isomorphism classes of lifts form an affine $H^2(-;\mathbb Z)$-space ([[lem-spin-c-structures-form-an-h2-torsor]]). Boundary restriction is the actual normal-first rank-four-to-rank-three principal reduction and is equivariant for the restriction of line bundles and $H^2$ ([[lem-boundary-spin-c-restriction-and-line-twists-are-equivariant]]).

[F7] Every compact connected oriented smooth rational homology four-ball admits at least one Spin$^c$ structure ([[lem-rational-homology-four-ball-admits-spinc]]).

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Use the Ozsvath–Szabo orientation convention $L(p,1)$ given by positive $p$-surgery on the unknot and label its Spin$^c$ structures by $i\in\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z$, represented by $0\le i<p$. For every integer $p\ge1$,
$$d(L(p,1),i)=\frac{(2i-p)^2-p}{4p}.$$
For the opposite orientation the correction terms are negated, with the conjugate Spin$^c$ label understood.

facts:
[F1] [[lem-lens-space-q-one-triangles-and-cyclic-handle-maps]] supplies the explicit individual index-zero, basepoint-zero count-one triangles, their cyclic maps and Chern evaluation $k=2i-p$ on a generator of square $-p$.

[F2] [[lem-rational-heegaard-floer-absolute-grading-and-cobordism-maps]] constructs the absolute grading, with the sphere generator at degree zero, and proves the degree formula for these actual fixed-Spin$^c$ handle maps.

[F3] [[lem-heegaard-floer-correction-term-heegaard-invariance]] identifies the correction term as the bottom degree of the infinity image. The convention in the statement is [[def-lens-space-surgery-orientation-convention]].

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume AC. Let $Q\subset\mathbb{CP}^2$ be the nonsingular complex conic parametrized by $[s:t]\mapsto[s^2:st:t^2]$, let $N(Q)$ be a closed tubular disk bundle, and let $B_2=\overline{\mathbb{CP}^2\setminus\operatorname{int}N(Q)}$. Then $B_2$ is a smooth compact four-manifold with $H_*(B_2;\mathbb Q)\cong H_*(\mathrm{point};\mathbb Q)$. Its boundary is the circle bundle of Euler number $4$ over $S^2$, hence is the lens space $L(4,1)$ up to orientation; orient $B_2$ so that the boundary agrees with the stated lens-space convention.

facts:
**Given:** AC and the complex-oriented projective plane, its conic $Q$, and a closed tubular disk bundle $N(Q)$.

[A1] AC is assumed by the UCT, tubular-neighbourhood, Thom, Poincare-duality, geometric-intersection, and self-intersection suppliers; AC implies the ACω hypotheses of the lens-space convention ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]).

[F1] The standard filtration $\mathbb{CP}^0\subset\mathbb{CP}^1\subset\mathbb{CP}^2$ and affine charts give one cell in dimensions $0,2,4$; cellular and universal-coefficient comparison compute its integral homology and cohomology ([[def-complex-projective-space-and-holomorphic-charts]], [[thm-cellular-homology-computes-singular-homology]], [[thm-universal-coefficient-theorem-for-cohomology-over-a-pid]]).

[F2] Excision identifies $H^*(\mathbb{CP}^2,B_2;\mathbb Z)$ with $H^*(N(Q),\partial N(Q);\mathbb Z)$, and the normalized oriented rank-two Thom class identifies the latter with $H^{*-2}(Q;\mathbb Z)$ and evaluates $+1$ on each positive normal disk. Its relative-to-absolute image in degree two is the Poincare dual of $Q$, with sign $(-1)^{2\cdot2}=+1$ ([[thm-excision-for-singular-cohomology]], [[thm-thom-isomorphism-for-oriented-vector-bundles]], [[def-thom-class-by-fiberwise-normalization]], [[lem-normal-thom-class-realizes-the-poincare-dual-of-a-submanifold]]).

[F3] The complex orientation supplies the fundamental class; Poincare duality identifies $H^2(\mathbb{CP}^2;\mathbb Z)$ with $H_2(\mathbb{CP}^2;\mathbb Z)$; the geometric intersection pairing equals the Poincare-dual cup pairing and depends only on homology classes; homotopic maps induce the same homology map; and the local sign of a transverse intersection is determined by the ordered tangent orientations ([[def-fundamental-class-of-a-compact-oriented-manifold]], [[thm-poincare-duality-for-oriented-topological-manifolds]], [[thm-geometric-intersection-equals-the-poincare-dual-cup-pairing]], [[cor-homotopic-maps-induce-the-same-map-on-singular-homology]], [[def-local-oriented-intersection-sign]], [[def-geometric-intersection-pairing-on-a-closed-oriented-manifold]], [[def-oriented-intersection-number]]).

[F4] The self-intersection of a compact oriented surface in an oriented four-manifold equals the Euler number of its oriented normal bundle ([[def-self-intersection-number-of-an-oriented-submanifold]], [[thm-self-intersection-is-the-euler-number-of-the-normal-bundle]]).

[F5] The lens-space convention defines $L(p,1)$ by $+p$ filling of the standard unknot exterior; the nonsingular surgery matrix gives $H_1\cong\mathbb Z/p$ ([[def-lens-space-surgery-orientation-convention]], [[lem-cyclic-cover-linking-form-inverse-matrix]]). The lens-space convention assumes countable choice, which follows from AC ([[def-countable-choice]], [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]).

[F6] The cohomology long exact sequence of the pair $(\mathbb{CP}^2,B_2)$ computes the cohomology of the complement from the relative and absolute groups ([[thm-long-exact-sequence-of-a-pair-in-singular-cohomology]]).

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented $3$-sphere, choose its compact exterior $E_K$ with boundary torus $T_K$, and let $\mu$ and $\lambda$ be its positive meridian and preferred longitude. The exterior homology theorem gives $H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z[\mu]$. Let $\phi:\pi_1(E_K)\to\mathbb Z$ be the composite of abelianization with the homomorphism $[\mu]\mapsto1$. For an integer $q\ge2$, let $\phi_q$ be the composite $\pi_1(E_K)\xrightarrow{\phi}\mathbb Z\to\mathbb Z/q\mathbb Z$, and let $p_q:E_q\to E_K$ be the connected cover classified by $\ker\phi_q$. On $T_K$, the homomorphism sends $[\mu]\mapsto1$ and $[\lambda]\mapsto0$, so the preimage of $T_K$ is a connected torus cover whose fundamental group corresponds to $\langle\mu^q,\lambda\rangle$. Let $\widetilde\mu$ be the closed lift of $\mu^q$. Attach a solid torus to $E_q$ with its meridian identified with $\widetilde\mu$; the resulting oriented closed $3$-manifold is the $q$-fold cyclic branched cover $\Sigma_q(K)$. In tubular coordinates near $K$, the extended map to $S^3$ has local form $(s,w)\mapsto(s,w^q)$, and the deck group $\mathbb Z/q\mathbb Z$ acts by $w\mapsto e^{2\pi i/q}w$.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume AC. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $D\subset B^4$ be a smooth properly embedded disk with boundary $K$. Let $W_D$ be the connected double cover of $B^4$ branched along $D$. Then $W_D$ is a rational homology four-ball and its oriented boundary is the double branched cover $\Sigma_2(K)$ formed using the positive-meridian convention. This assertion concerns smooth disks only and makes no claim for locally flat topological disks.

facts:
**Given:** AC, a smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$, and a smooth proper disk $D\subset B^4$ with $\partial D=K$.

[A1] AC is assumed by the published smooth-disk cover theorem ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

[F1] The cyclic branched cover uses the homomorphism sending a positive meridian to the generator of $\mathbb Z/2$; its boundary is the branched cover of the boundary knot with the induced orientation ([[def-cyclic-branched-cover-of-a-knot]]).

[F2] The connected double cover of $B^4$ branched over a smooth properly embedded disk is a rational homology ball under AC ([[lem-double-cover-branched-over-a-slice-disk-is-a-rational-homology-ball]]).
