contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ bound a connected compact oriented Seifert surface $F$ of genus $g$. Choose a disk-band decomposition of $F$ with one disk and $2g$ bands, and use its band-core basis $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ to form the positive-push Seifert matrix $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. For $q\ge2$, define the symmetric block matrix $M_q(V)$ of size $2g(q-1)$ by specifying its $2g\times2g$ blocks, indexed by $1\le k,\ell\le q-1$:
$$(M_q(V))_{k\ell}=\begin{cases}V+V^T,&k=\ell,\\-V^T,&\ell=k+1,\\-V,&k=\ell+1,\\0,&|k-\ell|\ge2.\end{cases}$$
Push the interior of $F$ into $B^4$ while keeping $K$ on $S^3=\partial B^4$, cut $B^4$ along a thickened copy of the pushed-in surface, and take $q$ copies. For $i=1,\ldots,q-1$, glue the positive face of copy $i$ to the negative face of copy $i+1$ by reflecting the normal coordinate; do not glue the last positive face to the first negative face. Call the resulting $q$-fold cyclic branched cover $W_q(F)$. It has one $0$-handle and $2g(q-1)$ $2$-handles, and its framed attaching link has linking matrix $M_q(V)$. The boundary branched cover, with the boundary marking induced by the covering map, is $\Sigma_q(K)$.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, the oriented knot $K$, a connected compact oriented Seifert surface $F$, its disk-band decomposition, the ordered band-core basis, and $q\ge2$.

[A1] Full AC implies the countable-choice hypothesis of the finite surface normal-form supplier. [[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]

[F1] A Seifert surface is connected, compact, smooth, oriented, and embedded with oriented boundary $K$; its genus is the integer $g$ with $\chi(F)=1-2g$. [[def-oriented-seifert-surface]]

[F2] Under countable choice, a connected compact surface with one boundary component has a disk-band handle form with $2g$ bands and a standard integral homology basis given by the band cores. [[lem-finite-chart-surface-normal-forms-supply-jordan-disks-and-torsion-free-groups]]

[F3] The positive-push Seifert matrix has entries $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$, with the positive normal determined by the surface and ambient orientations. [[def-knot-seifert-pairing-and-matrix]]

[F4] The $q$-fold branched cover of $S^3$ is formed from the meridian-mod-$q$ cover of the compact exterior by filling the lift of $\mu^q$. [[def-cyclic-branched-cover-of-a-knot]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume AC. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot admitting a smooth properly embedded disk $D\subset B^4$ (a smooth embedding of the closed disk with interior in $\operatorname{int}B^4$ and boundary $K\subset S^3$). Let $W_D$ be its connected double cover branched along $D$, so $H_*(W_D;\mathbb Q)\cong H_*(\mathrm{point};\mathbb Q)$, and let $Y=\Sigma_2(K)$ be the oriented double branched cover of $S^3$ using the positive-meridian convention. Then $H_*(Y;\mathbb Q)\cong H_*(S^3;\mathbb Q)$. Define the torsion linking pairing $\lambda_Y$ on $H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)$ by $\lambda_Y([C],[D])=(F\cdot D)/n\pmod{\mathbb Z}$ when $\partial F=nC$, with signed intersection in the oriented $Y$. Under Poincare duality, the restriction image of $\operatorname{Spin}^c(W_D)$ in $\operatorname{Spin}^c(Y)$ is an affine coset of a subgroup $M\subseteq H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)$ with $M=M^\perp$, where $M^\perp=\{x:\lambda_Y(m,x)=0\text{ for every }m\in M\}$; such a subgroup is a metabolizer. It has $|M|^2=|H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)|$. Every extending structure $\mathfrak t$ in this coset satisfies $d(Y,\mathfrak t)=0$. No conclusion is asserted for a merely locally flat topological disk (a topological embedding with local flat disk charts but no smoothness hypothesis) or for nonextending boundary structures.

facts:
**Given:** AC, a smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$, and a smooth proper slice disk $D\subset B^4$.

[A1] AC is assumed by the smooth slice-cover and extension-set suppliers ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

[F1] The connected cover branched over $D$ is a rational homology four-ball and its boundary is $Y=\Sigma_2(K)$ under the positive-meridian convention ([[lem-slice-disk-double-cover-is-rational-homology-ball]]).

[F2] For a rational ball with connected rational-homology-sphere boundary, the extending Spin$^c$ structures form one affine coset of a self-annihilating subgroup of the boundary torsion cohomology, and that subgroup has square-root order ([[lem-rational-ball-spin-c-extension-set-metabolizer]]).

[F3] A Spin$^c$ structure extending over a smooth rational homology four-ball has correction term zero ([[thm-correction-term-obstruction-from-rational-ball]]).

[F4] The double branched cover has the nonsingular Seifert-surface surgery presentation; its meridian linking form uses the matrix inverse convention fixed by the positive-meridian surgery supplier ([[lem-branched-cover-surgery-presentation-from-seifert-surface]], [[lem-cyclic-cover-linking-form-inverse-matrix]]).

contract.text: The false claim is: if a closed oriented three-manifold $Y$ with $H_*(Y;\mathbb Q)\cong H_*(S^3;\mathbb Q)$ bounds a smooth compact four-manifold $B$ with $H_*(B;\mathbb Q)\cong H_*(\mathrm{point};\mathbb Q)$, then a nonzero correction term $d(Y,\mathfrak t)$ for any boundary Spin$^c$ structure $\mathfrak t$ obstructs the existence of $B$.

facts:
**Given:** AC, the rational ball $B_2$ with boundary $L(4,1)$, and the lens-space label $i=0$.

[A1] AC is assumed by the construction and the extension-set supplier ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

[F1] The conic complement is a rational homology four-ball with boundary $L(4,1)$ in the selected orientation ([[lem-rational-ball-b2-bounds-lens-l4]]).

[F2] The surgery matrix for $L(4,1)$ is nonsingular and its first homology has order $4$ ([[lem-cyclic-cover-linking-form-inverse-matrix]]).

[F3] Over a rational-ball boundary, the extending Spin$^c$ structures form a coset of order $\sqrt{|H_1(Y)|}$, and every extending structure has zero correction term ([[lem-rational-ball-spin-c-extension-set-metabolizer]], [[thm-correction-term-obstruction-from-rational-ball]]).

[F4] For the selected orientation, $d(L(4,1),i)=((2i-4)^2-4)/16$ ([[lem-heegaard-floer-correction-terms-lens-space-lp1]]).

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the smooth normal-bundle structure used in the
framing clause. For a knot component $K$, its normal bundle is the fibrewise
quotient $\nu K=TS^3|_K/TK$, and a normal section is a smooth section of this
bundle.

Let $D$ be a regular oriented link diagram in a projection plane $P$ of an
oriented $3$-sphere, after moving the link off the point at infinity. Fix the
unit viewing normal $n$ pointing toward the viewer. Orient $P$ by the rule that
an ordered basis $(u,v)$ of $P$ is positive exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is a positive
basis of the ambient $3$-space. At a crossing $c$, let $v_{\rm over}$ and
$v_{\rm under}$ be the nonzero projected tangent vectors following the
orientations of the overpassing and underpassing strands. Define
$$\operatorname{sgn}(c):=\operatorname{sgn}\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})\in\{+1,-1\}.$$
Reversing the orientation of $P$ reverses every crossing sign.

This convention makes the positive geometric Artin half twist positive. In
the braid chart $(x,y,t)$ with ambient orientation $(x,y,t)$, view along $+y$;
the induced positive orientation of the $(x,t)$ projection plane is the ordered
basis $(\partial_t,\partial_x)$. For the positive half twist, label $i$ moves
from $x=-h$ to $x=h$ below the midpoint, while label $i+1$ moves from $x=h$ to
$x=-h$ above it, with $h>0$. Thus the over and under projected tangent vectors
in coordinates $(t,x)$ are $(1,-2h)$ and $(1,2h)$, whose determinant is
$4h>0$.

The **writhe** of $D$ is
$$\operatorname{wr}(D):=\sum_{c\text{ a crossing of }D}\operatorname{sgn}(c).$$
For a link component $K_i$, its **self-writhe**
$\operatorname{wr}_i(D)$ is the sum over crossings whose two branches belong to
$K_i$; the total writhe also includes all mixed crossings between distinct
components.

The **blackboard framing** of a component of $D$ is the homotopy class of the
normal section represented by the positive quarter-turn in $P$ of the projected
oriented tangent. The projection is an immersion, so this vector never
vanishes; it is perpendicular to the projected tangent, hence also to the
spatial tangent, and therefore represents a nonzero normal section of the
component in the ambient $3$-sphere.

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.8,>=stealth]
  \draw[->] (-1,0) -- (1,0) node[right] {$v_{\rm over}$};
  \draw[->] (0,-1) -- (0,1) node[above] {$v_{\rm under}$};
  \node[above left] at (0,0) {$+1$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

In the displayed local chart, the over tangent is the positive horizontal
vector and the under tangent is the positive vertical vector, so the determinant
is $+1$. This figure illustrates the determinant rule only; no proof below
depends on a picture.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $P$ be the projection plane in an oriented $3$-sphere and let $n$ be the
unit viewing normal pointing toward the viewer. Orient $P$ so that $(u,v)$ is
a positive basis exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is a positive ambient basis. A
**crossing code** has a
finite set $C$ of crossing labels and a finite set $D$ of **darts**, where a
dart is one directed half-edge incident to a crossing. A fixed-point-free
involution $\alpha:D\to D$ pairs the two ends of each edge: $\alpha^2=\mathrm{id}$
and $\alpha(d)\ne d$. A vertex map $v:D\to C$ records the crossing incident to
each dart. A **rotation system** is the permutation $\sigma$ whose cycles give
the clockwise order of darts at each crossing. Each crossing has four darts;
the two over-strand darts and the two under-strand darts are opposite in that
cyclic order. An arrow on each dart records whether its edge is directed into
or out of its incident crossing. The pairing $\alpha$ must join one incoming
end to one outgoing end. At a crossing, each opposite pair has one incoming
and one outgoing dart, so following an edge and then the opposite dart defines
the oriented link components. A code is **connected** when the graph with
vertices $C$ and edges the $\alpha$-pairs is connected.

The sign of an oriented crossing is $+1$ or $-1$ according as
$\det(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})$ is positive or negative, where the two
tangent vectors follow the oriented over- and under-strands. This item fixes
the local cyclic-order convention as follows. Starting with the outgoing
over-dart and reading counterclockwise, a positive crossing has order
$(O_{\rm out},U_{\rm out},O_{\rm in},U_{\rm in})$; a negative crossing has
order $(O_{\rm out},U_{\rm in},O_{\rm in},U_{\rm out})$. The stored crossing
sign and cyclic order must agree. This is the page's explicit sign convention.
It agrees with the current KT-03 supplier: reversing its positive
counterclockwise order from outgoing over gives the clockwise record
$(O_{\rm out},U_{\rm in},O_{\rm in},U_{\rm out})$.

For a nonempty connected crossing graph, let $V=|C|$, $E=|D|/2$, and let
$F$ be the number of cycles of the face permutation $\phi=\alpha\circ\sigma$.
A **spherical code** is a code satisfying $V-E+F=2$. A spherical code becomes a
**plane code** by distinguishing one face as the outer face and deleting a
point in that face from the sphere. The crossingless one-component code is a separate case: its Gauss data are one empty component word, its DT pairing and crossing-sign vector are empty at $c=0$, and its PD data are the single loop `Loop[1]`; every format also carries an orientation marker, `ccw` or `cw`, for the unit circle $S^1=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:x^2+y^2=1\}$ in the oriented plane, and the outer-face marker is `outside`. Thus the crossingless code records which direction orients its circle. It has no crossing graph or face-permutation test. Disconnected crossing graphs and disconnected crossingless links are outside this code class.

A **normalized planar-diagram code** with $c>0$ has crossing labels
$C=\{1,\ldots,c\}$ and four dart positions $0,1,2,3$ at each crossing, in
clockwise order beginning with the outgoing over-dart. The opposite pair
$(0,2)$ is over and $(1,3)$ is under. For sign $+1$, the clockwise record is
$(O_{\rm out},U_{\rm in},O_{\rm in},U_{\rm out})$; for sign $-1$ it is
$(O_{\rm out},U_{\rm out},O_{\rm in},U_{\rm in})$. Edge labels are assigned
by scanning crossings in increasing order and their four dart positions in
order, giving the next positive integer to the pair containing the first
not-yet-labelled dart. The outer face is recorded by its least dart in its
face cycle. These rules remove arbitrary edge-name and face-name choices;
different crossing labelings may still represent the same diagram. At $c=0$
a normalized code is the crossingless record with one of the two orientation
markers above.

A **Gauss code** for an oriented diagram records, in traversal order on each
oriented component, a signed crossing label: $+j$ means the component passes
over at crossing $j$, and $-j$ means it passes under. For a knot there is one
cyclic word; for a link there is one cyclic word per component. Each crossing
label must occur exactly twice in total, once positively and once negatively.
When $c>0$, every listed component word is nonempty; a separate crossingless
component is not part of this code class. The zero-crossing case is only the
one-component code specified above.
The code also carries a separate algebraic crossing-sign vector
$\varepsilon_j\in\{+1,-1\}$, one entry for each label. Choosing a basepoint
turns the knot's cyclic word into a based word; changing the basepoint
cyclically shifts the word, and relabeling crossings changes only their names.
The visit order, over/under signs, and crossing-sign vector determine the
crossing rotation system; it is realizable in the sphere only when the
resulting code is spherical. A plane Gauss code also carries an identifier of
one cycle of its face permutation to designate the outer face.

A **signed Dowker–Thistlethwaite code**, in this page's convention, encodes a
based oriented knot with $c$ crossings by numbering its $2c$ visits
$1,\ldots,2c$ in traversal order. For each odd visit $2j-1$, record the even
visit $2k$ paired with it as $d_j=+2k$ when the odd visit is over and
$d_j=-2k$ when it is under; also record the algebraic crossing sign
$\varepsilon_j\in\{+1,-1\}$ for crossing label $j$, the pair containing odd
visit $2j-1$. Its parity conditions are that
$|d_1|,\ldots,|d_c|$ are exactly the even numbers $2,4,\ldots,2c$, each once,
and each paired crossing has one over-visit and one under-visit. The separate
$\varepsilon_j$ records the crossing sign; signed DT conventions elsewhere
may encode signs differently. The associated cyclic traversal and crossing
signs determine a rotation system, which must pass the same spherical
realizability test. A plane DT code also carries an identifier of one cycle
of its face permutation to designate the outer face.

An **oriented planar-diagram code** labels each edge segment by an integer and
lists its two incident darts at crossing records. Each crossing record lists
its four directed edge ends in clockwise order, beginning with the outgoing
over-dart, and records which opposite pair is over, the orientation of each
strand, and the crossing sign. Every edge label occurs exactly twice, once as
an incoming end and once as an outgoing end. The code must satisfy the local
crossing-order rule above; its crossing graph must be connected when nonempty;
and its rotation system must satisfy $V-E+F=2$. The record also carries an
identifier of one cycle of its face permutation as the outer face. Thus an
arbitrary word in labels, even when each label occurs twice, is not declared
realizable until all incidence, orientation, crossing, connectedness, and
face-count tests pass.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. The bounded region of a smooth embedded
circle in the oriented plane, together with its boundary, is a smooth manifold
with boundary diffeomorphic to the closed standard disk. Let $D_0,D_1$ be two
such closed regions. Every orientation-preserving smooth boundary
diffeomorphism $b:\partial D_0\to\partial D_1$ extends to an
orientation-preserving diffeomorphism $B:D_0\to D_1$. More precisely, for
specified smooth inward collars $c_i:\partial D_i\times[0,\epsilon)\to D_i$
with $c_i(p,0)=p$, the extension may be required to satisfy
$B(c_0(p,r))=c_1(b(p),r)$ for every sufficiently small $r\ge0$. In addition, given interior points $p_i\in D_i$ and an orientation-preserving smooth diffeomorphism $q$ from a neighborhood of $p_0$ onto a neighborhood of $p_1$, the extension can agree with $q$ near $p_0$ while retaining the prescribed boundary collars.

[F1] A smooth map with invertible derivative is a local diffeomorphism, without a choice hypothesis ([[lem-choice-free-smooth-inverse-function-theorem-in-euclidean-space]]).

[F2] A simple polygon has exactly one bounded complementary region and one unbounded complementary region, with the polygon as the frontier of both ([[thm-polygonal-jordan-curve]]).

[F3] A simple polygonal region has a finite straight triangulation ([[thm-simple-polygon-admits-a-triangulation]]), and a connected finite plane graph has $V-E+F=2$ ([[thm-euler-formula-for-connected-plane-graphs]]).

[F4] Under Countable Choice, attaching a standard smooth disk along an embedded boundary disk, with the corner rounded, preserves the diffeomorphism type ([[lem-boundary-connected-sum-with-a-disk-does-not-change-the-diffeomorphism-type]]).

[F5] Under Countable Choice, an isotopy of embeddings of a compact smooth manifold with boundary into a boundaryless manifold of the same dimension, constant near the two time endpoints, extends to a smooth ambient isotopy supported in any specified neighborhood of its track ([[lem-isotopy-extension-for-a-compact-source-with-boundary]]).

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For every valid connected one-component
oriented code with a selected outer face, the reconstruction procedure
produces a regular oriented diagram representing that code. Any two such
diagrams with the same code differ only by crossing and edge relabeling and
are planar isotopic. The normalized planar-diagram code of a diagram with $c$
crossings appears among the candidates enumerated at bound $c$. This statement
concerns diagrams and their finite codes; it does not identify distinct codes
that may represent the same knot type. The finite realization and enumeration
claims are choice-free; $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is assumed only for the smooth
ambient-isotopy uniqueness clause.

**Given:** The Axiom of Countable Choice and a valid connected one-component oriented code with $c$ crossings and a selected outer face.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: Countable Choice is the axiom that every countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

[F1] [[def-planar-diagram-gauss-and-dowker-codes]]: the code specifies a finite crossing set, paired darts, crossing rotations, oriented opposite strands, over/under data, signs, and a face selector; its normalized PD form fixes crossing labels, edge labels, and the face identifier, while the crossingless form carries one of two orientation markers.

[F2] [[lem-planar-diagram-code-realizability-and-face-validation]]: for a nonempty connected code with the prescribed local crossing data, the Euler face condition $V-E+F=2$ gives a spherical realization, and a selected face gives the plane model.

[F3] [[thm-planar-code-validation-and-diagram-reconstruction-procedure-properties]]: the validator terminates and reconstructs a diagram exactly for codes satisfying the stated syntax, incidence, crossing, component, connectedness, face, and outer-face conditions.

[F4] [[thm-enumerate-diagrams-up-to-crossing-bound-procedure-properties]]: at every nonnegative crossing bound, the enumerator returns every normalized connected one-component code of at most that size that passes validation.

[F5] [[def-planar-isotopy-of-link-diagrams]]: planar isotopy is a jointly smooth orientation-preserving ambient isotopy of $\mathbb R^2$ carrying the diagram image, strand orientations, and over/under data.

[F6] [[lem-choice-free-smooth-inverse-function-theorem-in-euclidean-space]]: independent differentials give smooth local coordinates.

[F7] [[thm-fundamental-theorem-on-flows]]: a smooth vector field has a unique smooth local flow on an open time-state domain.

[L1] [[lem-smooth-jordan-disk-boundary-maps-extend-to-diffeomorphisms]]: under Countable Choice, a smooth embedded circle bounds a smooth disk, and an orientation-preserving boundary diffeomorphism extends across such disks with any prescribed matching boundary collars and any prescribed positive interior diffeomorphism germ.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $D$ be a nonempty finite regular oriented link diagram: a projection of a finite union of oriented circles with finitely many transverse double points, no triple points, and one overpassing branch specified at each double point. Let $c(D)$ be its number of crossings and $m(D)$ its number of components. An arc is a connected strand segment cut at each undercrossing; each component with no undercrossings contributes one closed arc. Write $a(D)$ for the number of arcs. If $q(D)$ components have no undercrossings, then $a(D)=c(D)+q(D)$ and $0\le q(D)\le m(D)$.

A supplied finite code for $D$ has code length $L$, the total number of bits in that literal code, including its tags, signs, labels, and separators. The length depends on the chosen encoding. In particular, for one of the tagged Gauss, signed Dowker–Thistlethwaite, or oriented planar-diagram formats, $L$ is the bit length of the supplied valid code in that format. The procedures in this page take typed mathematical diagrams or valid codes as stated; no string parser or malformed-code behavior is included in any operation count.

For an integer $z$, define its signed-magnitude bit length by $\ell_{\mathbb Z}(0)=1$ and $\ell_{\mathbb Z}(z)=1+\lceil\log_2(|z|+1)\rceil$ for $z\ne0$. For a Laurent polynomial $P(A)=\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}z_jA^j$ with finite support, define its coefficient-bit size as $0$ if $P=0$, and otherwise as $\max_{j:z_j\ne0}\ell_{\mathbb Z}(z_j)$. Its absolute Laurent degree is $\max_{j:z_j\ne0}|j|$, with value $0$ for $P=0$. For a prime $p$, elements of $\mathbb F_p$ are represented exactly by residues $0,\ldots,p-1$, and their representation uses $\lceil\log_2p\rceil$ bits.

An exact output is the complete integer, finite list, or Laurent polynomial with its integer coefficients and exponents. A floating-point approximation is not an exact output. A field-operation count treats each addition, subtraction, multiplication, division by a nonzero element, and equality test in $\mathbb F_p$ as one operation; this convention does not assert that these operations have constant bit cost as $p$ varies.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Let $p$ be an odd prime. A Fox $p$-coloring of a finite regular oriented link diagram $D$ assigns an element of $\mathbb F_p$ to each arc and satisfies $2x_o=x_i+x_j$ at every crossing, where $x_o$ is the overarc color and $x_i,x_j$ are the two underarc colors. If $D'$ is obtained from $D$ by planar isotopy or one oriented Reidemeister move of type R1, R2, or R3, restriction outside the move disk gives a bijection from the Fox $p$-colorings of $D$ to those of $D'$. Consequently the number of Fox $p$-colorings is unchanged along every finite sequence of such moves. The local bijections use no choice principle.

[F3] [[def-oriented-reidemeister-moves]]: each local move is supported in a disk, all strand orientation/sign variants are included, and a planar isotopy transports the diagram and its decorations.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
The input is a nonempty unoriented regular link diagram $D$: a finite immersed
planar projection of one or more circles with finitely many transverse double
points, no triple points, and over/under data at each double point. Let $C(D)$
be its finite crossing set. At each crossing take the local chart in which the
over-strand runs southwest to northeast and is drawn continuously over the
under-strand, which runs northwest to southeast with a gap at the intersection.
The A-smoothing joins the two left endpoints and the two right endpoints, with
weight $A$; the B-smoothing joins the two top endpoints and the two bottom
endpoints, with weight $A^{-1}$. These labels are transported with
orientation-preserving changes of local coordinates. Put
$\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$. The output is the Laurent polynomial $\langle D\rangle$.

1. Set an accumulator $p:=0$ in $\mathbb Z[A^{\pm1}]$.
2. For each function $S:C(D)\to\{A,B\}$, smooth every crossing according to
   $S$, obtaining a crossingless diagram with $|S|$ circles. Count the A- and
   B-smoothings as $a(S)$ and $b(S)$, and replace
   $$p\quad\text{by}\quad p+A^{a(S)-b(S)}\delta^{|S|-1}.$$
3. Return $p$ after all states have been processed.

The input is a mathematical diagram object, not a serialized string. The
procedure specifies no parsing or malformed-string rejection behavior. Since
the diagram has at least one component, every complete smoothing has
$|S|\ge1$ and every exponent of $\delta$ is nonnegative.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $D$ be a nonempty unoriented regular link diagram with $c$ crossings and $m\ge1$ components, and let $\langle D\rangle=\sum_j z_jA^j$ be its exact Kauffman bracket. Its Laurent exponents satisfy $|j|\le 3c+2m-2$, and its signed-magnitude coefficient-bit size, as defined in the encoded diagram size definition, is at most $m+2c+1$. Consequently, a knot diagram ($m=1$) has Laurent degree and coefficient-bit size bounded linearly in $c+1$.

The state-sum algorithm admits a naive exact implementation taking
$O(2^c(c+m+1)^4)$ elementary bit steps in the following model. Its typed
input gives $c$ and the number $u$ of crossingless components in
self-delimiting binary: each number is encoded by $b$ ones, a zero, and its
$b$ ordinary binary digits, with $b\ge1$ the number of those digits.
These fields are followed by the edge-pairing table on the $4c$
endpoints indexed by crossing and local port. Its entries are ordered by
endpoint index and each uses $\max(1,\lceil\log_2(4c+1)\rceil)$ bits.
At each crossing the ports are northwest, northeast,
southeast, southwest in the bracket's fixed local chart; the two smoothing
pairings are therefore fixed pairs of port indices. The table is assumed to
be the incidence data of the given diagram. Polynomial arithmetic uses dense
arrays of signed binary integer coefficients, and one tape-cell read, write,
or head move on a fixed finite number of binary work tapes costs one step.
For knots this bound is $O(2^c(c+1)^4)$. It is a bound for this explicit
indexed implementation, not for arbitrary black-box polynomial operations.
Constructing the indexed input from an arbitrary literal code of length $L$,
reading other labels or padding, and processing geometric coordinates are
outside this bound.

[F2] [[alg-kauffman-bracket-state-sum]]: the bracket term of a state $S$ is $A^{a(S)-b(S)}\delta^{|S|-1}$ with $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$; $a(S)+b(S)=c$, and $|S|$ is the number of circles after smoothing.

[F3] [[thm-kauffman-bracket-state-sum-procedure-properties]]: the state-sum procedure visits exactly the $2^c$ maps from the crossing set to $\{A,B\}$ and returns the displayed sum.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $A$ be an indeterminate and let $D$ be a typed nonempty unoriented regular
link diagram with finite crossing set $C(D)$. At each crossing use the chart
with the over-strand southwest-to-northeast: A joins the left endpoints and the
right endpoints with weight $A$, while B joins the top endpoints and bottom
endpoints with weight $A^{-1}$. The Kauffman bracket state-sum algorithm
terminates after exactly $2^{|C(D)|}$ state visits and returns
$$\sum_{S:C(D)\to\{A,B\}}A^{a(S)-b(S)}(-A^2-A^{-2})^{|S|-1},$$
where $a(S)$ and $b(S)$ count the two smoothing types and $|S|$ counts the
circles in the smoothed diagram. The algorithm takes a mathematical diagram
as input and makes no claim about parsing strings or rejecting malformed
encodings.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$.

The input is a finite regular oriented link diagram together with its declared
components. If it does not have exactly two components, return
`invalid-input`. For a two-component diagram $D$, initialize $s:=0$ and make
one pass over its finite crossing list. At each crossing whose branches lie on
different components, add
$$\operatorname{sgn}\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})$$
to $s$, where the determinant is taken in the oriented projection plane; ignore
self-crossings. Return $s/2$. The even-sum lemma establishes that this output is
an integer and is the diagram's linking number.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented link diagram with $c$ crossings, $m\ge1$ components, and $a$ arcs as defined in the encoded diagram size definition. For a two-component diagram, after one constant-size component-count check, the linking-number scan visits exactly the $c$ crossings, makes at most $c$ component/sign tests and $c$ integer additions, and returns the exact integer half-sum of mixed crossing signs; its absolute value is at most $c/2$ and it is invariant under ambient isotopy of the oriented link.

For any such diagram and any odd prime $p$, the Fox coloring system has one row per crossing and one column per arc over $\mathbb F_p$. Matrix construction uses at most $2c$ field additions to combine repeated arc coefficients and $ca$ zero-entry writes. If row reduction uses $r$ pivots and has $f=a-r$ free variables, then $r\le\min(c,a)$, pivot search uses at most $ca$ entry tests, and row reduction uses at most $ra+2r(c-1)a$ field arithmetic operations. The algorithm returns exactly $p^f$ Fox colorings. Listing the full solution set after reduction uses at most $p^f(2f(a-f)+a)$ field arithmetic and output-write operations. If only the count is required, $p^f$ can instead be computed by repeated squaring using at most $2\lceil\log_2(f+1)\rceil$ integer multiplications, with at most $f\lceil\log_2p\rceil+1$ magnitude bits. The input convention gives $a\le c+m$, so these bounds depend only on crossings, components, and field size. The coloring count is invariant under ambient isotopy of the oriented link. Field operations count as unit-cost operations; no bit-time bound for those operations or polynomial-time evaluation claim is made.

**Given:** The Axiom of Countable Choice, a finite regular oriented link diagram $D$, and an odd prime $p$.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is the axiom of countable choice.

[F1] [[def-encoded-diagram-size-and-exact-output]]: $c$ is the crossing count, $m$ the number of link components, and $a=c+q\le c+m$ where $q$ counts components with no undercrossings; each finite-field operation is counted as one operation.

[F2] [[alg-oriented-linking-number-from-diagram]]: for exactly two components, the procedure scans the finite crossing list once, adds the sign of each mixed crossing, ignores self-crossings, and returns half the sum.

[F3] [[thm-oriented-linking-number-scan-terminates-and-is-correct]]: the scan terminates after exactly one iteration per crossing and returns the integer linking number.

[F4] [[lem-linking-number-even-sum-and-reidemeister-invariance]]: the mixed crossing-sign half-sum is an integer and is unchanged by every oriented Reidemeister move and planar isotopy; under ACω it is invariant for ambient-isotopic oriented links.

[F5] [[alg-dihedral-fox-colorings]]: for each crossing the matrix row is $2x_o-x_i-x_j=0$ over $\mathbb F_p$; row reduction uses at most $a$ pivots and the output is formed from free-variable assignments.

[F6] [[thm-dihedral-fox-colorings-terminate-and-are-correct]]: if the reduced system has $f$ free variables, the algorithm terminates and returns exactly $p^f$ solutions, namely all Fox $p$-colorings.

[F7] [[lem-dihedral-fox-coloring-count-is-reidemeister-invariant]]: each oriented Reidemeister move and planar isotopy preserves the Fox $p$-coloring count by an explicit bijection.

[F8] [[thm-oriented-reidemeister-equivalence-theorem]]: under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, two ambient-isotopic oriented regular diagrams are connected by a finite sequence of planar isotopies and oriented Reidemeister moves.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $D$ be a regular oriented diagram
of a two-component oriented link in $S^3$, with components $K_1,K_2$. Write
$$S(D):=\sum_{c\text{ between }K_1\text{ and }K_2}\operatorname{sgn}(c).$$
Then $S(D)$ is even, and
$$\operatorname{lk}_D(K_1,K_2):=\frac{S(D)}2\in\mathbb Z$$
is unchanged by planar isotopy and by each oriented Reidemeister move of types
I, II, and III. Thus it has the same value on any two regular diagrams of
ambient-isotopic oriented links. It is symmetric in $K_1,K_2$; reversing exactly
one component changes its sign, and reversing both components leaves it
unchanged.

[F5] A type-I move creates or deletes one self-crossing; a type-II move creates or deletes two crossings of opposite sign; a type-III move preserves the signs and over/under data of its three crossings ([[def-oriented-reidemeister-moves]]).

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Input a finite regular oriented link diagram $D$ with $a$ arcs and $c$ crossings,
fixed finite orderings of its arcs and crossings, and an odd prime $p$. The algorithm returns the full set
$\operatorname{Col}_p(D)$ of assignments of residues in $\mathbb F_p$ to the
arcs satisfying the Fox crossing equations, together with
$|\operatorname{Col}_p(D)|$.

1. Create one variable $x_j$ for each arc in the supplied order, and process
   crossings in the supplied order.
2. At each crossing with overarc $o$ and the two underarcs $i$ and $j$, append
   the homogeneous linear equation $2x_o-x_i-x_j=0$ over $\mathbb F_p$.
   At a crossing, add the coefficients of any repeated arc in that row.
3. Starting with the first column and first unused row, scan columns from left
   to right. In a column with a nonzero entry in an unused row, choose the
   first such row, swap it into the next pivot row, divide it by its nonzero
   pivot, and add multiples of it to every other row to clear that column.
   Advance the pivot row by one. If the column has no such entry, leave it
   free and continue to the next column.
4. After all columns have been processed, assign every free variable
   independently any value in $\mathbb F_p$ and solve the reduced equations
   for the pivot variables. Return each resulting assignment once and the
   number returned.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $D$ be a nonempty oriented link diagram with $c$ crossings and $m\ge1$ components. The state-sum portion of the normalized bracket computation visits exactly $2^c$ smoothing states; computing the writhe correction requires one pass over the $c$ crossing signs. Its exact normalized output $f_D(A)=(-A^3)^{-\operatorname{wr}(D)}\langle D\rangle$ has absolute Laurent degree at most $6c+2m-2$ and signed coefficient-bit size at most $m+2c+1$. For a knot diagram, these output bounds are linear in $c+1$.

Using the indexed endpoint-pairing input and dense signed binary-array
implementation of the exact bracket bit-growth theorem, together with the
$c$ crossing signs supplied as bits, the normalized bracket can be computed in
$O(2^c(c+m+1)^4)$ elementary bit steps. This is
$O(2^c(c+1)^4)$ for knots. Input records are assumed to describe the given
typed diagram; arbitrary literal-code reading and parsing, extra padding or
labels, and geometric-coordinate processing are outside this implementation
bound. The finite computations are choice-free. Under the Axiom of Countable
Choice, $f_D$ is an invariant of the ambient-isotopy class of the oriented
link. No polynomial-time Jones evaluation is asserted.

facts:
**Given:** A nonempty regular oriented link diagram $D$ with $c$ crossings, $m\ge1$ components, and $A$ an indeterminate.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is the axiom of countable choice.

[F1] [[def-encoded-diagram-size-and-exact-output]]: the crossing count is $c$, the component count is $m$, and Laurent coefficient-bit size uses the signed-magnitude convention.

[F2] [[alg-kauffman-bracket-state-sum]]: every state contributes $A^{a(S)-b(S)}(-A^2-A^{-2})^{|S|-1}$ to the exact Laurent polynomial.

[F3] [[thm-kauffman-bracket-state-sum-procedure-properties]]: the state-sum procedure visits exactly the $2^c$ smoothing assignments and returns the displayed bracket.

[F4] [[thm-exact-bracket-output-bit-growth-bound]]: the raw bracket has absolute Laurent degree at most $3c+2m-2$ and signed coefficient-bit size at most $m+2c+1$. Its specified indexed endpoint-pairing and dense binary-array implementation takes $O(2^c(c+m+1)^4)$ elementary bit steps, excluding arbitrary literal-code parsing.

[F5] [[thm-normalized-bracket-is-an-oriented-link-invariant]]: with crossing signs $\operatorname{sgn}(c)\in\{+1,-1\}$ and $\operatorname{wr}(D)=\sum_c\operatorname{sgn}(c)$, the normalization $(-A^3)^{-\operatorname{wr}(D)}\langle D\rangle$ is unchanged under oriented Reidemeister moves and is an ambient-link invariant under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $A$ be an indeterminate and let $D$
be a nonempty regular oriented link diagram in an oriented $3$-sphere. Fix a
unit viewing normal $n$ and orient the projection plane $P$ so $(u,v)$ is
positive exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is positive in the ambient $3$-space. At each
crossing define $\operatorname{sgn}(c)=\operatorname{sgn}\det_P(v_{\rm over},
v_{\rm under})$ from the oriented projected tangents and set
$\operatorname{wr}(D)=\sum_c\operatorname{sgn}(c)$. At each crossing use the
local source chart in which the over-strand runs southwest to northeast; the
A-smoothing joins the left endpoints and the right endpoints with weight $A$,
and the B-smoothing joins the top endpoints and the bottom endpoints with
weight $A^{-1}$. Labels are transported by orientation-preserving changes of
local coordinates. Let $C(D)$ be the finite crossing set. A state is a map
$S:C(D)\to\{A,B\}$; let $a(S)$ and $b(S)$ count its A- and B-smoothings, and
let $|S|$ be the number of circles after all crossings are smoothed. Set
$$\langle D\rangle= \sum_{S:C(D)\to\{A,B\}}A^{a(S)-b(S)}(-A^2-A^{-2})^{|S|-1}.$$
Define
$$f_D(A)=(-A^3)^{-\operatorname{wr}(D)}\langle D\rangle,$$
where $\operatorname{wr}(D)$ is the sum of the determinant signs of its
oriented crossings. If two such diagrams represent ambient-isotopic
oriented links, their $f_D(A)$ values are equal. Thus $f_D$ defines an
invariant of nonempty oriented links.

facts:
**Given:** The Axiom of Countable Choice and two nonempty regular oriented
diagrams of ambient-isotopic oriented links.

[A1] The Axiom of Countable Choice is the assumption $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]).

[F1] The normalized bracket is unchanged by planar isotopy and every oriented
R1, R2, or R3 move ([[lem-kauffman-bracket-curl-and-writhe-correction]]).

[F2] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, two ambient-isotopic regular oriented link
diagrams are connected by a finite sequence of planar isotopies and oriented
Reidemeister moves ([[thm-oriented-reidemeister-equivalence-theorem]]).

[F3] Every oriented link may be moved off the point at infinity into $\mathbb R^3$,
and the directions giving regular projections are dense in $S^2$
([[def-oriented-link-in-s-three-and-ambient-isotopy]],
[[lem-every-oriented-link-admits-a-regular-projection]]).

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
**Input:** A valid normalized oriented planar-diagram code $C$ for a connected one-component knot diagram, with $c$ crossings. A positive-crossing-count code records its finite crossing labels, four darts at each crossing, edge pairings, clockwise rotations, strand orientations, over/under pairs, crossing signs, and one outer face. A crossingless code records one oriented circle and its outer face.

**Output:** A finite ordered list of pairs $(E,\mu)$, where $E$ is a valid normalized one-component knot code and $\mu$ records either the finite crossing/edge relabeling identifying the unchanged planar-isotopy class or a local disk boundary, move type, and orientation/sign variant witnessing one oriented R1, R2, or R3 move from $C$ to $E$. Different labelings of the same candidate may appear more than once.

**Finite comparison rules:** Two normalized codes represent the same code class when some bijection of their finite crossing labels and edge labels carries all dart incidences, crossing rotations, orientations, signs, component cycles, and outer-face data of one code to the other. To test whether two codes differ by one move, enumerate all finite choices of local edge intervals and crossing subrecords of sizes allowed by R1, R2, or R3; test that the codes agree outside the chosen disk boundary and that the two local records are one of the standard orientation/sign variants of that move. The local-site test uses the exact variants in the oriented Reidemeister-move definition.

**Instructions:**

1. Validate $C$ with the planar-code validation procedure. If it is invalid, return its first invalid-code result.
2. Set $N:=c+2$ and run the bounded normalized-diagram enumerator with bound $N$. It returns a finite list of reconstructed one-component knot-diagram candidates.
3. For each candidate, form the finite set of normalized code representatives obtained by assigning crossing labels and edge labels in every permitted order and applying the code's normalization rule.
4. For each representative $E$, apply the finite comparison rules. Append $E$ with a relabeling certificate if it is the same code class as $C$, or with the successful local-site certificate if a comparison certifies one R1, R2, or R3 move between them. Preserve the enumerator order and retain duplicates.
5. Return the accumulated list.

The bound $c+2$ includes every one-move result because R1 changes crossing count by one, R2 by two, and R3 by zero. This procedure lists candidates one move away; it does not decide whether two arbitrary codes are related by any number of moves.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
**Input:** A finite tagged Gauss code, signed Dowker–Thistlethwaite code, or
oriented planar-diagram code in the conventions of this page. The crossing
count $c$ is a nonnegative integer. When $c>0$, the code includes the finite
crossing labels, edge-end incidences, strand arrows, over/under data, crossing
signs, and a distinguished outer face. When $c=0$, the only admissible input
for this procedure is the one-component crossingless code specified in the
code definition.

**Output:** Either `Invalid(reason, witness)`, where `reason` is the first
failed check below and `witness` identifies the offending field, label, or
crossing, or `Valid(diagram, components, faces, outerFace)`. Here `diagram` is
a finite gluing record consisting of one crossing disk per vertex, one
rectangular edge band for each pair of darts under $\alpha$, and one cap disk
per cycle of the face permutation. Each band is attached at its recorded dart ports, and each
crossing disk records its clockwise order, strand orientations, over/under
pair, and sign. `components` lists the oriented link cycles, `faces` lists the
face-permutation cycles, and `outerFace` is the selected cycle. The gluing
record represents a polygonal spherical diagram; deleting a point in its
selected face gives the plane model. The procedure tests realizability of
this code only; it does not compare the represented link with another code.

**Instructions:**

1. Read the tag and crossing count. If the tag is unknown or $c$ is not a
   nonnegative integer, return `invalid-header` with that field.

2. If $c=0$, accept only one empty Gauss component word, the empty signed-DT
   code, or the single `Loop[1]` PD record, each with exactly one orientation
   marker, `ccw` or `cw`. Return
   `invalid-crossingless-code` otherwise. For an accepted input return the
   standard circle with the marked orientation, one component, its two sphere
   faces, and the `outside` face selector. Do not run crossing-graph tests.

3. For a Gauss code with $c>0$, reject an empty component word. Check that
   every label lies in $\{1,\ldots,c\}$, occurs exactly twice in total, and
   occurs once with each over/under sign. Check that its separate crossing-sign
   vector has length $c$ and entries in $\{+1,-1\}$. Return
   `invalid-crossing-label` for the first out-of-range label,
   `invalid-crossing-visit-count` with the label and its over/under counts for
   any visit failure, or `invalid-crossing-sign-vector` with the first bad
   position. Turn successive visits on each component word into directed edge
   labels, including each cyclic last-to-first edge, numbering these segments
   in the listed component order and then in traversal order, and form the
   crossing records from the over/under visits and the stored crossing signs.

4. For a signed DT code, check that its pairing list and sign vector each have
   length $c$, each pairing value has absolute value in
   $\{2,4,\ldots,2c\}$, every such absolute value occurs once, and every sign
   is $+1$ or $-1$. Return `invalid-dt-pairing` with the first bad index for a
   pairing failure, or `invalid-crossing-sign-vector` with the first bad
   position for a sign failure. The odd visit $2j-1$ is crossing $j$; if
   $d_j>0$ it is the over-visit and if $d_j<0$ it is the under-visit. At the
   even visit paired with $2j-1$, use crossing label $j$ and the opposite
   over/under sign. Decode visits in order $1,\ldots,2c$ into the corresponding
   signed Gauss word and continue with step 3.

5. For a PD code, check that there are exactly $c$ crossing records and four
   dart occurrences at each record. Return `invalid-crossing-record` with the
   first bad record otherwise. Use the edge labels and arrows in the records
   to form the paired-dart involution, crossing rotations, over/under pairs,
   and crossing signs.

6. In every nonempty encoding, check that each edge label has exactly two
   occurrences, one incoming and one outgoing; each crossing has exactly four
   incident darts; the opposite pairs are exactly one over-strand and one
   under-strand; each strand has one incoming and one outgoing end; and the
   cyclic order matches the stored crossing sign. Return, in that order,
   `invalid-edge-incidence`, `invalid-crossing-valence`,
   `invalid-over-under-pair`, `invalid-strand-orientation`, or
   `invalid-crossing-sign-order`, with the first offending label or crossing.

7. Starting at each as-yet unvisited outgoing dart, cross its edge by $\alpha$
   to the incoming dart at the other endpoint and continue through the
   opposite dart of that same strand. Stop only when the starting outgoing
   dart is reached. If an end is missing, a dart repeats before that return, or
   any dart remains uncovered after all cycles are traced, return
   `invalid-component-closure` with the first such dart. Then test the crossing
   graph for connectedness; if it is disconnected, return
   `disconnected-crossing-graph`.

8. Compute $\phi=\alpha\circ\sigma$ on all darts by finite table lookup and
   list its cycles. Put $V=c$, $E=|D|/2$, and $F=$ the number of cycles. If
   $V-E+F\ne2$, return `non-spherical-face-count` with $(V,E,F)$. If the
   supplied outer-face identifier is not one of these cycles, return
   `invalid-outer-face` with that identifier.

9. For a passing code, choose the lexicographically first spanning tree in the
   finite edge ordering. Root it at the least crossing label and attach its
   tree bands in increasing distance from that root, using the recorded cyclic
   gaps. Then attach the remaining edge bands in increasing edge-label order.
   Use the distinguished face for the plane projection, replace each crossing
   disk by its prescribed transverse crossing, attach one cap disk along each
   face cycle, and lift the over-strand above the under-strand. Return this
   finite gluing record, the directed components, the face cycles, and the
   outer-face identifier.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
**Input:** A nonnegative integer crossing bound $N$.

**Output:** A finite ordered list of reconstructed knot-diagram candidates. A
candidate is a `Valid` output of the planar-code validation procedure whose
code is a normalized planar-diagram code with one oriented component and at
most $N$ crossings. Repeated candidates up to crossing relabeling or planar
isotopy are allowed; the list is not a list of knot types.

**Instructions:**

1. If $N$ is not a nonnegative integer, return `invalid-bound`.
2. Initialize the output list empty. Pass the two normalized crossingless
   one-component codes, with `ccw` and `cw` orientation markers in that order,
   through the validator and append both outputs first.
3. For each $c=1,\ldots,N$ in increasing order, use crossing labels
   $\{1,\ldots,c\}$ and the four normalized dart positions at each crossing.
   Enumerate every crossing-sign vector in lexicographic order, with
   $-1<+1$. The sign determines the incoming and outgoing positions at each
   crossing by the normalized-code convention.
4. For each sign vector, enumerate every bijection from the set of its
   $2c$ outgoing darts to its $2c$ incoming darts in lexicographic order.
   Pair each outgoing dart with its image to obtain the edge involution, and
   assign edge labels by the normalized-code rule.
5. Compute the cycles of $\phi=\alpha\circ\sigma$ for each pairing. For each
   cycle, in increasing order of its least dart, select that cycle in turn as
   the outer face and form the corresponding normalized PD code.
6. Pass each code through the planar-code validation procedure. Append its
   reconstructed output if and only if the validator returns `Valid` and the
   directed component tracing has exactly one cycle. Return the list after
   the finite loops end.

This procedure enumerates normalized finite codes and reconstructed diagrams;
it neither identifies equivalent codes nor decides whether two candidates
represent isotopic knots.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
**Input:** Two valid normalized oriented planar-diagram codes $C_0,C_1$ for connected one-component knot diagrams.

**Output:** The algorithm returns Found(path) only if it has a finite sequence of code classes from $C_0$ to $C_1$, with a finite local-move certificate for each adjacent pair. It has no negative-output branch. It may run forever if the target code class is never reached.

**Instructions:**

1. Validate both input codes using the planar-code validation procedure. If either is invalid, return that first invalid-code result. For each valid code, form its canonical representative by checking all bijections of its finite crossing labels and edge labels, recomputing the prescribed edge normalization, and selecting the lexicographically least resulting code.
2. Set the initial frontier to the singleton containing the canonical representative of $C_0$. Initialize a discovered-code set with that representative and an empty predecessor record.
3. At the beginning of each breadth layer, test every code in the current frontier against the canonical representative of $C_1$. If one matches, follow its stored predecessor records back to $C_0$, reverse the resulting finite list, and return the path with its move certificates.
4. Otherwise, for each code $C$ in the current frontier, call the Reidemeister-neighbor algorithm. For each returned pair $(E,\mu)$, canonicalize $E$ by the finite relabeling procedure in step 1. If its canonical representative has not been discovered, add it to the next frontier and store $(C,\mu)$ as its predecessor record.
5. Replace the current frontier by the next frontier and repeat from step 3. If a layer is empty, continue with empty layers; do not return “inequivalent.”

Code equality in this procedure means equality of canonical representatives under the finite crossing/edge relabelings of the normalized code convention. Every loop in one layer is finite; the number of layers has no fixed bound.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $C_0,C_1$ be valid normalized oriented planar-diagram codes for connected one-component knot diagrams. The breadth-first Reidemeister search terminates with a finite move witness whenever the represented oriented knots are ambient-isotopic. If they are inequivalent, the search has no negative-output branch and does not halt with a negative answer; failure to find a path through any fixed finite depth $N$ says only that no path of length at most $N$ has yet been found. This is a semidecision result, not a decision or complexity-class result for knot equivalence.

facts:
**Given:** The Axiom of Countable Choice and two valid normalized oriented planar-diagram codes for connected one-component knot diagrams.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is the axiom of countable choice.

[F1] [[alg-reidemeister-move-neighbors-from-code]]: on a code with $c$ crossings, the neighbor procedure enumerates all valid code candidates through crossing bound $c+2$ and retains exactly those with a finite local R1, R2, R3, or planar-isotopy certificate.

[F2] [[alg-enumerate-diagrams-up-to-crossing-bound]]: for a nonnegative bound $N$, the procedure enumerates normalized connected one-component codes with at most $N$ crossings by finite sign-vector, dart-pairing, face-selector, and validation loops.

[F3] [[thm-enumerate-diagrams-up-to-crossing-bound-procedure-properties]]: the bounded enumerator terminates and includes every normalized connected one-component code through the supplied crossing bound; it does not identify knot types.

[F4] [[thm-planar-code-validation-and-diagram-reconstruction-procedure-properties]]: validation of each finite code terminates and reconstructs its oriented diagram exactly when the listed code and face conditions hold.

[F5] [[thm-valid-code-reconstructs-the-declared-link-diagram]]: under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, a valid connected one-component code reconstructs its declared diagram, and code relabelings describe the same planar-isotopy class.

[F6] [[alg-breadth-first-reidemeister-search]]: each layer is tested against the target, then expanded by the finite neighbor procedure; the algorithm stores predecessor certificates and has no negative-output branch.

[F7] [[thm-oriented-reidemeister-equivalence-theorem]]: under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, two ambient-isotopic oriented diagrams are related by a finite sequence of planar isotopies and oriented Reidemeister moves.

contract.text:
For every nonnegative integer $N$, the bounded enumeration procedure
terminates and returns exactly the reconstructed candidates represented by
normalized connected one-component planar-diagram codes with at most $N$
crossings. Each returned candidate has a valid spherical face structure and a
selected outer face. The procedure does not identify candidates that represent

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
For every finite input in the three code formats, the validation and
reconstruction procedure terminates. It returns an invalid-code reason
exactly when the first failed syntax, incidence, orientation, component,
connectedness, face-count, or outer-face condition in its stated order occurs;
otherwise it returns the crossing-disk/edge-band model of the represented
oriented diagram, its oriented components, its face cycles, and its selected
outer face.

facts:
**Given:** A finite tagged Gauss, signed DT, or oriented PD input with its declared crossing count and, when nonempty, its crossing data and outer-face field.

[F1] [[def-planar-diagram-gauss-and-dowker-codes]]: Gauss labels occur as one over-visit and one under-visit at each crossing; signed DT codes pair each odd visit with a distinct even visit and carry a separate crossing-sign vector; PD codes give the edge incidences, oriented strands, opposite over/under pairs, crossing signs, and face selector.

[F2] [[alg-planar-code-validation-and-diagram-reconstruction]]: the procedure checks the header, code-specific visit or record conditions, incidences, valence, over/under pairs, strand orientations, crossing-sign order, component cycles, crossing-graph connectedness, face cycles, Euler count, and outer-face identifier in the listed order, then builds the finite crossing-disk/edge-band model.

[F3] [[lem-planar-diagram-code-realizability-and-face-validation]]: a nonempty connected code satisfying the local crossing and orientation conditions has a spherical realization exactly when $V-E+F=2$; choosing one face gives its plane model. The crossingless one-component code is realized by the standard circle.

[F4] [[def-planar-diagram-gauss-and-dowker-codes]]: at $c=0$, the Gauss word and DT data are empty, the PD data are `Loop[1]`, an orientation marker is either `ccw` or `cw`, and the outer-face marker is `outside`.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text: Let $P$ and $Q$ be compact piecewise-linear polyhedra. A **piecewise-linear map** $f:P\to Q$ is a map that is simplicial after suitable finite subdivisions of triangulations of $P$ and $Q$. A **subpolyhedron** $A$ of $Q$ is a subset represented by the realization of a subcomplex in some finite linear triangulation of $Q$. A map $f:P\to Q$ is a **piecewise-linear embedding** if it is piecewise-linear, its image $f(P)$ is a subpolyhedron of $Q$, and $f:P\to f(P)$ is a piecewise-linear homeomorphism. A finite simplicial triangulation of a closed piecewise-linear $n$-manifold is **combinatorial** if the link of every $k$-simplex is a piecewise-linear sphere of dimension $n-k-1$. Thus in a closed combinatorial $3$-manifold every triangular face has link $S^0$ and is incident to exactly two tetrahedra.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: No closed nonorientable piecewise-linear surface embeds in the standard oriented piecewise-linear three-sphere $S^3$.

facts:
**Given:** A closed PL surface $F$ embedded in the standard oriented PL $3$-sphere.

[F1] [[cor-homology-of-spheres]]: $H_2(S^3;\mathbb F_2)=0$.

[F2] [[thm-cellular-homology-computes-singular-homology]]: the finite triangulation used below computes singular homology with coefficients in $\mathbb F_2$.

[F3] [[def-cellular-homology]] and [[thm-cellular-boundary-is-the-incidence-degree-matrix]]: the cellular chain groups are generated by oriented cells, and each boundary coefficient is the signed sum of incident-cell coefficients.

[F4] [[def-r-orientation-of-a-topological-manifold]]: an orientation of an $n$-manifold is a continuous section choosing a generator of each local integral homology group $H_n(M,M\setminus\{x\};\mathbb Z)$; this is the definition used for both the ambient sphere and the surface $F$.

[F5] [[def-oriented-cellular-chain-group]]: an orientation of a tetrahedral cell selects its integral cellular generator.

[F6] [[lem-pl-embedded-polyhedron-admits-compatible-subcomplex-triangulation]]: a finite subdivision of the ambient triangulation contains $F$ as a subcomplex.

[F7] [[def-induced-boundary-orientation]]: the orientation induced on a face is determined by the outward-normal-first convention.

[F8] [[lem-the-cellular-boundary-squares-to-zero]]: the cellular boundary operator satisfies $\partial^2=0$.

[F9] [[def-oriented-link-in-s-three-and-ambient-isotopy]] and [[def-pl-embedding-and-subpolyhedron]]: the ambient is the standard oriented PL $3$-sphere. The finite triangulation in [F6] is a subdivision of its standard combinatorial triangulation, so every triangular face has link $S^0$ and exactly two tetrahedral cofaces.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Let $Q$ be a compact piecewise-linear polyhedron with a fixed finite linear triangulation $T$. If $f:P\to Q$ is a piecewise-linear embedding of a compact piecewise-linear polyhedron, then some finite subdivision $T'$ of $T$ contains $f(P)$ as the realization of a subcomplex.

facts:
**Given:** A compact piecewise-linear polyhedron $Q$, a finite linear triangulation $T$ of $Q$, and a piecewise-linear embedding $f:P\to Q$.

[F1] [[def-pl-embedding-and-subpolyhedron]]: $f(P)$ is a subcomplex in some finite linear triangulation $T_0$ of $Q$.

[F2] [[lem-two-finite-linear-subdivisions-have-a-common-simplicial-refinement]]: two finite linear triangulations of the same polyhedron have a common finite linear refinement.

[F3] [[def-simplicial-subcomplex-star-closure-and-link]]: a subcomplex is closed under taking faces.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Assume countable choice, as required for the smooth normal-bundle structure in the tubular-neighbourhood interface. Let $K:S^1\to S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot, let $\nu(K)=TS^3|_K/TK$ be its quotient normal bundle, and let $\Phi:\Omega\to S^3$ be a tubular-neighbourhood map from an open neighbourhood $\Omega$ of the zero section in $\nu(K)$ that restricts to the inclusion of $K$. Choose a radius $\epsilon>0$ whose closed disk subbundle $D_\epsilon\nu(K)$ is contained in $\Omega$, and set $N(K)=\Phi(D_\epsilon\nu(K))$. The **exterior** of this chosen tube is
$$
E_K:=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}_{S^3}N(K).
$$
Retain its boundary $T_K:=\partial E_K=\partial N(K)$, orient $E_K$ by restriction of the fixed orientation of $S^3$, and orient $T_K$ as the boundary of $E_K$. The choice of tubular map and radius is part of the input to this definition.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume countable choice. Let $K:S^1\to S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot with a supplied product tubular embedding $\Phi:S^1\times D^2_{2\epsilon}\to S^3$. There is a polygonal knot $P$ inside this tube and a smooth rounding $K'$ of $P$ such that $K'$ is smoothly ambient isotopic to $K$ by an isotopy supported in the tube. If $K$ is supplied with a finite regular projection diagram $D$, the polygonal approximation and rounding can be chosen to have the same crossing code as $D$. A homeomorphism supported in the larger tube carries $P$ to $K'$, preserves the boundary torus of the radius-$\epsilon$ tube, and sends each marked fibre meridian to itself up to orientation. Conversely, every polygonal knot $P$ with a finite product regular neighborhood can be rounded in pairwise disjoint vertex balls to a smooth knot $P^\sharp$; a homeomorphism supported in those balls carries its compact exterior and marked meridian to those of $P^\sharp$. If a regular projection diagram is supplied, the rounding balls can be chosen away from crossing charts, so the crossing code is unchanged. These clauses compare smooth knot type through smooth knots and polygonal exterior models through homeomorphisms; they do not treat a nonsmooth polygonal curve as a smooth isotopy slice.

facts:
**Given:** Countable choice, a smooth oriented knot $K$, its supplied product tube, and optionally a finite regular projection diagram $D$.

[F1] [[def-oriented-link-in-s-three-and-ambient-isotopy]]: $K$ is a smooth embedding of $S^1$; smooth ambient isotopy is a path of ambient diffeomorphisms carrying the embedding at every time.

[F2] [[def-knot-exterior]]: the chosen tube defines a compact exterior and boundary torus.

[F3] [[def-knot-meridian-and-preferred-longitude]]: a fibre circle of the normal disk tube is the marked meridian; an ambient map of the product tube transports this peripheral class.

[A1] $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is used through the existing smooth isotopy extension theorem; all partitions, approximations and local disk maps below use only finite constructions.

[F4] [[def-countable-choice]]: $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ supplies the cutoff data in the smooth isotopy extension theorem.

[F5] [[thm-isotopy-extension]]: under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, a smooth isotopy of a compact source embedding whose track lies in an open set extends to a smooth ambient isotopy supported in that open set.

[F6] [[def-regular-oriented-link-diagram]] and [[def-planar-diagram-gauss-and-dowker-codes]]: a finite regular diagram has finitely many transverse crossings, disjoint small crossing disks, and compact arc portions separated away from those disks; its crossing code records the local incidence and over/under order.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text: Assume countable choice as in the chosen tubular-neighbourhood data. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot with chosen exterior $E_K$ and boundary torus $T_K=\partial E_K$, and let $p:T_K\to K$ be the projection of the chosen normal-disk tube. Orient each normal disk so that its positive tangent direction followed by its oriented normal basis agrees with the orientation of $S^3$. A **meridian** $\mu$ is the oriented boundary of one such normal disk. A **degree-one parallel curve** is a simple closed curve $\lambda$ in $T_K$ for which $p|_\lambda:\lambda\to K$ has degree $+1$. A **preferred longitude** is a degree-one parallel curve satisfying $i_*[\lambda]=0$ in $H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)$, where $i:T_K\hookrightarrow E_K$ is inclusion. This is a condition on a curve; this definition alone asserts neither existence nor uniqueness. Reversing the orientation of $K$ reverses the orientations of both $\mu$ and any degree-one parallel curve. If a subgroup $P\le\pi_1(E_K,x)$ is specified using a path from $x$ to $T_K$, record it only up to replacing it by $gPg^{-1}$ for $g\in\pi_1(E_K,x)$.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Here a parametrized PL ball means a finite polyhedron supplied with a piecewise linear homeomorphism, with piecewise linear inverse, to a convex polyhedral ball of the stated dimension. All subpolyhedra and maps in the following assertions are finite.

(a) Let $B_1,B_2$ be parametrized PL three-balls and $D_i\subset\partial B_i$ parametrized PL two-disks. Every PL homeomorphism $f:D_1\to D_2$ extends to a PL homeomorphism $B_1\to B_2$.

(b) The space obtained by gluing two parametrized PL three-balls along parametrized PL two-disks in their boundaries, by a specified PL homeomorphism, is a parametrized PL three-ball.

(c) Let $B$ and $A\subset B$ be parametrized PL three-balls, with $A\ne B$. Suppose $A\cap\partial B=\partial A\cap\partial B=D$ is a parametrized PL two-disk and $A\setminus D\subset\operatorname{Int}B$. Impose the following standard boundary-window condition at $C=\partial D$: every point of $C$ has a PL coordinate neighborhood in which
$$B=\{(u,v,w):w\ge0\},\qquad A=\{(u,v,w):w\ge0,\ v\le0\},\qquad D=\{w=0,\ v\le0\}.$$
The equalities are understood after intersection with the coordinate neighborhood, and $C$ corresponds to $v=w=0$. Then $Q=\overline{B\setminus A}$, with closure in $B$, is a parametrized PL three-ball.

No assertion about a sphere in an arbitrary PL three-manifold is assumed. In (c) the closure of the set difference is essential: $B\setminus\operatorname{Int}_{\mathbb R^3}A$ would retain the interior of the contact disk as an extra sheet. These statements introduce no choice hypothesis.

facts:
**Given:** The finite parametrized balls, marked disks, maps and, for (c), the displayed boundary-window charts.

[F1] A simple polygon has a polygonal disk on its bounded side; prescribed PL boundary maps extend over polygonal disks ([[lem-finite-polygonal-disk-and-collar-surgery]]).

[F2] Finite convex cell decompositions and finite PL embedded polyhedra admit compatible triangulations and subdivisions ([[lem-finite-convex-cell-complexes-admit-compatible-triangulations]], [[lem-pl-embedded-polyhedron-admits-compatible-subcomplex-triangulation]]).

[F3] A compact locally PL collared subpolyhedron has a PL collar, including at boundary vertices of the subpolyhedron ([[lem-compact-locally-collared-pl-subpolyhedron-has-pl-collar]]).

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $T$ be a finite simplicial triangulation of a compact PL three-manifold $M$. Every PL embedded projective plane in $\operatorname{Int}M$ meets $T^{(1)}$. The manifold may be nonorientable and may contain projective planes. No irreducibility or choice hypothesis is imposed.

More precisely, every compact subset of $\operatorname{Int}M\setminus T^{(1)}$ lies in the interior of an explicitly parametrized finite thickening of the dual graph, built from convex three-ball vertex pieces and standard disk-prism edge pieces. An embedded projective plane in such a thickening would lift into a parametrized finite tree of these balls, contradicting its nonorientability.

facts:
**Given:** The finite triangulation and a hypothetical embedded projective plane $S$ missing its one-skeleton and lying in $\operatorname{Int}M$.

[F1] The projective plane is the finite polygonal surface with attaching word $aa$ and is nonorientable. Removing a point in the open polygonal face gives an open Mobius band, which retracts onto its core circle; this retraction is obtained by its rectangle-with-reversed-ends model. Thus every polygonal loop may be moved off that point and then onto a power of the core, while twice the core bounds the polygonal face. ([[ex-projective-plane-polygonal-schema]])

[F2] Two parametrized finite PL three-balls glued along marked parametrized boundary disks by a given PL map form a parametrized PL three-ball. Consequently a finite tree of such pieces is a parametrized ball, by successively deleting a leaf and applying that assertion to its one attaching window. Prisms with convex disk bases are themselves parametrized balls. ([[lem-parametrized-pl-balls-absorb-standard-boundary-windows]])

[F3] No closed nonorientable PL surface embeds in the standard PL three-sphere, and therefore none embeds in a parametrized PL three-ball: compose its parameter with the standard inclusion of the convex ball into $\mathbb R^3\subset S^3$. ([[lem-no-closed-nonorientable-pl-surface-in-s-three]])

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume countable choice. Let $K:S^1\to S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot with a supplied product tubular neighborhood, and let $E_K$ be its compact exterior with peripheral torus $T_K$, fibre meridian $\mu$, and the unique degree-one generator $[\lambda]$ of the kernel of $H_1(T_K;\mathbb Z)\to H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)$ supplied by the product-tube Mayer–Vietoris calculation. Then $K$ is ambient isotopic in the smooth category to the standard unknot if and only if $E_K$ contains a properly embedded piecewise-linear disk $D$ whose boundary is not null-homotopic in $T_K$. Every such disk has $[\partial D]=[\lambda]$ or $-[\lambda]$ and has odd mod-two intersection with the original marked meridian $\mu$.

facts:
**Given:** Countable choice, the smooth oriented knot, its supplied product tube, and the exterior and marked peripheral data in the Statement.

[A1] Countable choice is the standing hypothesis; the local finite rounding, surface normal forms and smooth isotopy interfaces below use this hypothesis. ([[def-countable-choice]])

[F1] Every essential exterior disk has longitude class up to sign and odd intersection with the original fibre meridian. ([[lem-essential-disk-boundary-is-longitude]])

[F2] A peripheral curve of core degree $1$ or $-1$ cobounds a finite piecewise smooth annulus with the core, smooth on a collar of the core boundary. ([[lem-degree-one-peripheral-curves-cobound-annuli-with-tube-core]])

[F3] A finite compatible whole-star surface with an already smooth boundary collar has a smooth embedded replacement with the same topology and exactly the same boundary, fixed on a smaller collar. Smooth transverse proper disks conversely have PL proper approximations preserving the boundary's isotopy class. ([[lem-finite-compatible-pl-surfaces-admit-relative-smooth-roundings]], [[lem-smooth-proper-disks-have-compatible-pl-approximations]])

[F4] A smooth knot bounds a smooth embedded disk exactly when it has genus zero, and genus zero is equivalent under countable choice to smooth ambient isotopy to the oriented unknot. ([[lem-knot-genus-zero-iff-unknot]])

[F5] The PL convention here is the compatible PL structure of the supplied smooth exterior, represented by a whole-star smooth triangulation with boundary subcomplex and tangent-half-space fans. A PL disk can therefore be made a subcomplex by finite common subdivision, and its simplex restrictions have injective derivative fans. This is the ordinary meaning of PL in this smooth exterior, rather than a separate arbitrary topological marking. A representing finite whole-star triangulation is obtained by the finite coordinate-box and fitting construction of [[thm-compact-smooth-manifolds-with-corners-admit-relative-finite-triangulations]]; that supplier explicitly declares its ambient full-AC hypothesis dispensable and its actual finite construction uses no additional choice. The rounding and approximation clauses of [F3] use this same chosen compatible structure throughout.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For every smooth oriented knot $K$ in $S^3$, its Seifert genus is zero if and only if $K$ is ambient isotopic through orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms to the standard unknot.

facts:
**Given:** AC$_\omega$ and a smooth oriented knot $K$.

[F1] Genus is the minimum genus of a connected compact oriented spanning surface; a genus-zero surface with one boundary circle is topologically a disk. For smooth input, the disk-and-band construction in steps 7.1–12.1 of [[lem-finite-c2-surface-carriers-have-smooth-normal-forms-and-relative-cap-approximations]] gives a smooth disk parametrization, including its boundary collar: its interval and circle extensions are smooth for smooth data, and all subsequent disk/band moves are smooth. ([[def-oriented-seifert-surface-and-knot-genus]], [[lem-finite-chart-surface-normal-forms-supply-jordan-disks-and-torsion-free-groups]])

[F2] An isotopy of an embedded compact circle extends to an ambient isotopy under AC$_\omega$. ([[thm-isotopy-extension]], [[def-countable-choice]])

contract.heading: Statement

facts:
**Given:** A valid connected one-component oriented planar knot code with $n$ crossings and a specified polygonal realization $P$ of that code.

[F1] [[def-planar-diagram-gauss-and-dowker-codes]]: the code gives a finite connected four-valent graph, directed strand pairings, over/under data and a face permutation.

[F2] [[lem-planar-diagram-code-realizability-and-face-validation]]: when $V-E+F=2$, the rotation system has a spherical polygonal realization with disk faces.

[F3] [[alg-planar-code-validation-and-diagram-reconstruction]]: a passing code yields one crossing disk per crossing, one edge band per edge, and one cap per face, with recorded ports and face cycles.

[F4] [[thm-planar-code-validation-and-diagram-reconstruction-procedure-properties]]: the output gluing record represents the oriented link diagram described by the input code.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
For a code with a nonempty connected crossing graph, let $C$ be its finite
crossing set, $D$ its darts, $\alpha$ its fixed-point-free edge-pairing
involution, $\sigma$ its clockwise crossing rotation, and
$\phi=\alpha\circ\sigma$ its face permutation. A **spherical realization**
means a polygonal embedding on the oriented sphere whose vertex rotations and
edge pairings are exactly $\sigma$ and $\alpha$; its faces are the cycles of
$\phi$. If every crossing has four darts with the prescribed opposite
over/under pairs, arrows, and sign-consistent cyclic order, then such a
realization exists if and only if $V-E+F=2$, where $V=|C|$, $E=|D|/2$, and
$F$ is the number of cycles of $\phi$. Choosing one face as the outer face
and deleting a point in it gives the corresponding plane realization. The
crossingless one-component code is the single circle and is handled
separately.

facts:
**Given:** A finite connected oriented crossing code with nonempty crossing set, edge-pairing involution, clockwise crossing rotations, over/under pairs, strand arrows, crossing signs, and face permutation as defined above.

[F1] [[def-planar-diagram-gauss-and-dowker-codes]]: darts are paired by a fixed-point-free involution; crossing rotations are clockwise four-cycles; faces are the cycles of $\alpha\circ\sigma$; over/under strands are opposite pairs, each directed through the crossing.

[F2] [[lem-connected-plane-multigraph-euler-formula]]: every finite connected polygonal plane multigraph, including loops and parallel edges, satisfies $V-E+F=2$.

[F3] [[def-regular-oriented-link-diagram]]: a regular oriented link diagram is a projection image with the over/under datum at each double point and orientations of the strands; its double points are finite and transverse, with no triple points.

[F4] [[lem-finite-polygonal-disk-and-collar-surgery]]: a finite connected plane graph has a compact disk-and-band neighbourhood; filling its bounded complementary boundary circles produces a closed disk. Its polygonal-disk argument gives a piecewise-linear parametrization by a convex polygon.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume countable choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot with a finite regular projection diagram $D$ having $n$ crossings and a supplied product tube. There is a polygonal knot $P$ inside that tube with the same crossing code as $D$ and a smooth rounding $K^\sharp$ of $P$ such that $K^\sharp$ is smoothly ambient isotopic to $K$. The compact exterior of this same $P$ has a good triangulation with at most $C(n+1)$ tetrahedra and a marked path for the original meridian with at most $C(n+1)$ boundary edges, for one universal constant $C$. The peripheral-preserving exterior homeomorphism transfers this model to $K^\sharp$.

facts:
**Given:** Countable choice, a smooth knot $K$, its finite regular diagram $D$, and a supplied product tube.

[A1] $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is used only through the smooth isotopy extension in [[lem-smooth-to-pl-knot-exterior-ambient-isotopy]].

[F1] [[lem-smooth-to-pl-knot-exterior-ambient-isotopy]]: $D$ admits a polygonal knot $P$ with the same code; a smooth rounding $K^\sharp$ is smoothly ambient isotopic to $K$; and a homeomorphism carries $P$'s exterior and marked meridian to those of $K^\sharp$.

[F2] [[lem-good-linear-size-exterior-triangulation-from-diagram]]: for a specified polygonal realization $P$ of the code, the construction triangulates that same exterior with at most $C_0(n+1)$ tetrahedra and a meridian path of at most $C_0(n+1)$ edges.
