contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
**Input:** A finite tagged Gauss code, signed Dowker–Thistlethwaite code, or oriented planar-diagram code in the code conventions of the planar-code definition, and a mode, either **Haken** or **JT**.

**Output:** The first validation error with its witness; **not-a-knot** for a valid code with more than one component; **disk-certificate** with a normal-coordinate vector and its finite witness data; or **no-candidate** after the selected search is exhausted.

**Procedure:**

1. Run the planar-code validation procedure. Return its first invalid result if validation fails. If the validated code represents more than one component, return **not-a-knot**.
2. Let $n$ be its crossing count. Construct the good triangulated exterior $E$ with $t\le C(n+1)$ tetrahedra and the marked original meridian path.
3. In Haken mode, enumerate all vectors $v\in\mathbb Z^{7t}$ with $0\le v_i\le t2^{7t+2}$ in lexicographic order. Retain a vector only if it satisfies all matching equations and quadrilateral restrictions and is fundamental. Fundamentalness supplies connectedness. Compute nonempty-boundary, Euler-characteristic, and mod-two meridian-intersection data from the compressed coordinates, without expanding the surface. Return **disk-certificate** at the first vector passing these tests; return **no-candidate** after the finite box is exhausted.
4. In JT mode, let $A$ be the integer matching matrix and put $m=7t$. Enumerate all subsets $Z\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}$ in lexicographic order. For each $Z$, append the equations $v_i=0$ for $i\in Z$ to $Av=0$. If the combined matrix has rank $m-1$ and its one-dimensional kernel contains a nonzero nonnegative vector, compute the unique relatively prime nonnegative integer generator $v$ of that ray. Require that its positive-coordinate support be exactly the complement of $Z$; this visits each ray once, at its exact zero-coordinate support. Discard vectors that violate the quadrilateral restriction. A primitive generator on an extreme ray is fundamental, so its surface is connected. Compute nonempty-boundary, Euler-characteristic, and mod-two meridian-intersection data from the compressed coordinates, without expanding the surface. Return **disk-certificate** at the first passing vector; return **no-candidate** after all subsets have been processed.

The candidate tests use the boundary arcs and Euler-characteristic data computed from the compressed normal coordinates. No correctness or complexity assertion is part of this algorithm definition.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
A supplied finite PL embedding of the standard PL two-sphere in $\mathbb R^3$ bounds a compact parametrized PL three-ball; its two complementary components are the bounded ball interior and a connected unbounded exterior. A supplied finite PL embedding of the standard PL two-sphere in the standard PL three-sphere bounds two parametrized PL three-balls, and a PL homeomorphism of that three-sphere carries it to the common boundary in a standard double of a convex three-ball. All parameters and homeomorphisms are finite PL on the compact spaces in question. No choice hypothesis is introduced.

This is a PL assertion in already supplied standard PL ambient spaces. It does not assert triangulability of arbitrary topological three-manifolds or tame arbitrary wild sphere embeddings.

facts:
**Given:** The supplied finite PL embedding of a standard PL two-sphere in the stated standard PL ambient space.

[F1] A generic-height polyhedral two-sphere with one minimum, one maximum and regular links elsewhere has an explicit finite PL ball parameter ([[lem-no-saddle-polyhedral-two-spheres-bound-parametrized-pl-balls]]).

[F2] Positive Alexander height complexity admits two strictly simpler finite PL sphere reductions whose supplied balls reconstruct the original supplied ball ([[lem-innermost-critical-height-loops-admit-strict-pl-cap-reduction]]).

[F3] Prescribed boundary-disk maps of parametrized PL balls extend over the balls, with finite PL inverse ([[lem-parametrized-pl-balls-absorb-standard-boundary-windows]]).

[F4] Finite convex cell complexes admit compatible triangulations ([[lem-finite-convex-cell-complexes-admit-compatible-triangulations]]).

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Two embedded normal surfaces with the same normal vector in a finite simplicial triangulation are carried to one another by a finite PL homeomorphism of the ambient manifold preserving every simplex setwise.

Consequently, if $D_0,D_1$ are disjoint connected normal disks with the same vector, they cobound a parametrized PL product $D^2\times[0,1]$. Its two end disks are $D_0,D_1$, its vertical boundary is in $\partial M$, and it contains no original triangulation vertex. Its interval fibers remain in their original ambient simplex. The assertion concerns the supplied PL triangulation, not an arbitrary topological marking or a smooth extension problem.

facts:
**Given:** The finite triangulation and the two equal-vector normal surfaces, or the two disks in the consequence.

[F1] Equal vectors determine the same ordered edge-point counts, the same face-arc pairings after matching those points, and the same tetrahedral boundary circles and disk types. ([[lem-compatible-normal-vectors-admit-original-triangulation-regular-sum-diagrams]])

[F2] Finite simple polygonal curves in a polygonal disk or standard polyhedral sphere separate it into the stated disk regions, and prescribed PL boundary maps extend over parametrized polygonal disks. ([[thm-polygonal-jordan-curve]], [[thm-simple-polygon-admits-a-triangulation]], [[lem-parametrized-pl-balls-absorb-standard-boundary-windows]])

[F3] A finite PL embedding of a parametrized sphere in standard $\mathbb R^3$ bounds a parametrized PL ball. Prescribed maps of parametrized ball boundaries extend over the balls by coning compatible boundary triangulations in their convex models. ([[thm-finite-pl-schoenflies-in-dimension-three]], [[lem-parametrized-pl-balls-absorb-standard-boundary-windows]])

contract.heading: Statement

facts:
**Given:** The positive geometric half twist, its inverse, the determinant crossing-sign convention, and the Kauffman bracket chart specified in the statement.

[F1] In the positive geometric generator, strand $i$ moves from $x=-h$ to $x=h$ below the midpoint and strand $i+1$ moves from $x=h$ to $x=-h$ above it; the inverse reverses the crossing ([[def-elementary-geometric-half-twist]]).

[F2] The crossing sign is $\operatorname{sgn}\det(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})$, and this convention assigns sign $+1$ to the positive geometric Artin half twist ([[def-oriented-crossing-sign-writhe-and-blackboard-framing]]).

[F3] In the stated chart a crossing contributes $A$ times its $A$-smoothing plus $A^{-1}$ times its $B$-smoothing; the loop value is $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$ ([[def-kauffman-bracket-smoothing-and-loop-value]]).

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: For a connected regular link diagram $D$ with $c$ crossings, the Laurent-polynomial span of its Kauffman bracket is at most $4c$. If $D$ is reduced and alternating, then changing any one crossing from the all-$A$ state or the all-$B$ state merges two distinct state circles, both extreme coefficients are nonzero, and the bracket span is exactly $4c$. The span of a nonzero Laurent polynomial is its largest exponent minus its smallest exponent.

facts:
**Given:** A connected regular link diagram $D$ with $c$ crossings, with all-$A$ and all-$B$ smoothing states as defined by the bracket convention.

[F1] The bracket is the finite sum $\langle D\rangle=\sum_S A^{a(S)-b(S)}\delta^{|S|-1}$ with $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$; its states are choices of one smoothing at each crossing ([[def-kauffman-bracket-smoothing-and-loop-value]]).

[F2] In a connected alternating diagram, successive crossing visits along every component alternate between over and under, and reducedness means no projection region has a crossing more than once on its boundary ([[def-reduced-alternating-link-diagram]]).

[F3] Every connected regular projection has a checkerboard coloring ([[lem-connected-regular-link-diagram-has-checkerboard-coloring]]).

[F4] The Tait graph has checkerboard regions as vertices and crossings as edges ([[def-tait-graph-of-a-link-diagram]]).

[F5] For a connected plane graph, $|V|-|E|+|F|=2$ ([[thm-euler-formula-for-connected-plane-graphs]]).

[F6] For a connected projection with at least one crossing, either Tait graph is connected ([[lem-connected-projection-has-connected-tait-graphs]]).

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Every connected reduced alternating diagram $D$ of an oriented link $L$ realizes the crossing number of its underlying unoriented link: $c(D)=c(L)$.

facts:
**Given:** $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, an oriented link $L$, and a connected reduced alternating diagram $D$ representing it.

[A1] $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ selects from every countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable-choice]]).

[F1] The crossing number is the least crossing count among regular diagrams of the underlying unoriented link ([[def-crossing-number-of-link]]).

[F2] A disconnected projection represents a split link ([[lem-disconnected-link-diagram-represents-a-split-link]]).

[F3] A connected alternating diagram represents a nonsplit link ([[lem-connected-alternating-link-is-nonsplit]]).

[F4] Every connected reduced alternating diagram has bracket span $4c(D)$, and every connected diagram $E$ has bracket span at most $4c(E)$ ([[lem-connected-diagram-bracket-span-bound-and-alternating-equality]]).

[F5] The normalized bracket is an oriented link invariant under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[thm-normalized-bracket-is-an-oriented-link-invariant]]).

[F6] A reduced alternating diagram is connected and alternating by definition ([[def-reduced-alternating-link-diagram]]).

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $A$ and $t$ be formal variables and $K$ a
nonempty oriented link. At each crossing of a regular diagram $D$ use the
source chart with over-strand southwest-to-northeast: A joins left and right
endpoints with coefficient $A$, and B joins top and bottom endpoints with
coefficient $A^{-1}$. A state $S:C(D)\to\{A,B\}$ assigns one smoothing at every
crossing; let $a(S)$ and $b(S)$ count these choices and $|S|$ count the
resulting circles. Fix a unit viewing normal $n$ and orient the projection
plane $P$ so $(u,v)$ is positive exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is positive in the
ambient oriented $3$-sphere. Define
$$\operatorname{sgn}(c)=\operatorname{sgn}\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under}), \qquad \operatorname{wr}(D)=\sum_c\operatorname{sgn}(c),$$
$$f_K(A)=(-A^3)^{-\operatorname{wr}(D)} \sum_{S:C(D)\to\{A,B\}}A^{a(S)-b(S)}(-A^2-A^{-2})^{|S|-1}.$$
For an $n$-strand braid $\beta$ whose oriented closure is $K$, let
$e:B_n\to\mathbb Z$ be the homomorphism $e(\sigma_i)=1$, where $\sigma_i$
is the positive geometric Artin half twist. Let $H(n)$ be the type-A Hecke
algebra with generators $T_i$, quadratic relation $T_i^2=(v-1)T_i+v$, braid
relations, and distant commutation, and let $\pi_n(\sigma_i)=T_i$. Its
normalized Markov trace $\operatorname{tr}_n$ satisfies
$\operatorname{tr}_n(1)=1$, cyclicity, tower restriction, and
$\operatorname{tr}_{n+1}(xT_n)=z\operatorname{tr}_n(x)$. Define the library
Jones value by
$$V_K(t)=s^{e(\beta)}\left(-\frac{s^2+1}{s}\right)^{n-1} \operatorname{tr}_n(\pi_n(\beta))\Big|_{v=s^2,\,z=-1/(s^2+1),\,t=s^2},$$
where $s=t^{1/2}$. With $A=t^{-1/4}$, these values satisfy
$$V_K(t)=f_K(t^{-1/4}).$$

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, a nonempty oriented link $K$, a braid closure of $K$, and
the two polynomial constructions in the statement.

[A1] Full AC means that every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

[F1] Full AC implies countable choice
([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]).

[F2] The positive Artin half twist has determinant crossing sign $+1$; the
opposite reflected half twist exchanges over and under and has sign $-1$
([[def-oriented-crossing-sign-writhe-and-blackboard-framing]],
[[def-elementary-geometric-half-twist]]).

[F3] The braid exponent sum is additive, with $e(\sigma_i)=1$ and
$e(\sigma_i^{-1})=-1$
([[def-exponent-sum-of-a-braid]]).

[F4] For every braid closure, the normalized bracket satisfies
$$f_{\widehat\beta}(A)=(-A^3)^{-\operatorname{wr}(\widehat\beta)} \langle\widehat\beta\rangle,$$
and its value is independent of the regular diagram under AC$ _\omega$
([[thm-normalized-bracket-is-an-oriented-link-invariant]]).

$$\langle\widehat\beta\rangle =\delta^{n-1}(-A)^{e(\beta)}\operatorname{tr}_n(\pi_n(\beta)) \big|_{v=A^{-4},\,z=-1/(A^{-4}+1)},\qquad \delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$$
([[lem-hecke-bracket-trace-dictionary-and-local-descent]]).

[F6] The library Jones value is invariant under braid equivalence and Markov
moves under full AC, and is given by the trace formula in the Statement
([[thm-the-hecke-trace-construction-is-an-oriented-link-invariant]],
[[def-temperley-lieb-quotient-and-jones-specialization]]).

[F7] Every nonempty oriented link has a braid closure under full AC
([[thm-alexanders-closed-braid-theorem]],
[[def-closure-of-a-geometric-braid]]).

[F8] Every element of $B_n$ is represented by a finite word in the Artin
generators and their inverses; each letter is one geometric half twist or its
opposite, and the closure joins the braid endpoints
([[def-braid-group-by-the-artin-presentation]],
[[def-elementary-geometric-half-twist]],
[[def-closure-of-a-geometric-braid]]).

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume full AC and let $D$ be a connected reduced alternating diagram with $c$ crossings. At every crossing, changing one smoothing from the all-$A$ state or from the all-$B$ state merges two distinct state circles; these are A- and B-adequacy. The Kauffman bracket has $A$-span $4c$. If $D$ represents a knot $K$, then the library Jones polynomial has $t$-span $c$, and every $c'$-crossing diagram of $K$ has $t$-span at most $c'$ under the convention $t=A^{-4}$. The span of a nonzero Laurent polynomial is its largest exponent minus its smallest exponent.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC and a connected reduced alternating diagram $D$ with $c$ crossings.

[F1] In a reduced alternating diagram, successive crossing visits along each component switch over-under, and no complementary region has a crossing more than once on its boundary ([[def-reduced-alternating-link-diagram]]).

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Fix the round metric and orientation on $S^3$. An **$m$-singular oriented knot** is a smooth immersion $K:S^1\to S^3$ with exactly $m$ distinct transverse double points and no other self-intersections; each double-point image has exactly two preimages with linearly independent tangent vectors, and the preimage pairs are disjoint. The knot has no framing. Choose disjoint small balls around its double points, each containing no other part of the singular knot. At each double point there are two **resolutions**, obtained by separating the two local branches in the ball; label them $+$ and $-$ so the resolved crossing signs are respectively $+1$ and $-1$ under the convention that, in a diagram whose positive viewing normal agrees with the ambient orientation, the sign is $\operatorname{sgn}\det(v_{\mathrm{over}},v_{\mathrm{under}})$ and the positive Artin half twist has sign $+1$.

A **framed oriented knot** is a smooth oriented embedding $K:S^1\hookrightarrow S^3$ together with a homotopy class through nowhere-zero smooth sections of its oriented rank-two normal bundle. For an immersion $K:S^1\to S^3$, including one with double points, define its branchwise normal bundle over the parameter circle by $\nu_K:=K^*TS^3/dK(TS^1)$, oriented so that a positive tangent followed by a positive normal basis gives the ambient orientation. Because $dK$ has rank one at every parameter, its image is locally a smooth line subbundle and this quotient is locally a rank-two bundle. Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the framed clauses below, so these normal quotient bundles have their smooth vector-bundle structures. A **framed $m$-singular knot** has finitely many transverse double points and finitely many simple zeroes of a smooth section of $\nu_K$, all disjoint; its number $m$ of singularities is the number of double points plus the number of zeroes. A simple zero is one at which the derivative of the section in an oriented local trivialization is nonzero. Resolve double points as above, extending the normal section over the local resolution balls; each resulting section determines a framing homotopy class. To resolve a framing zero at parameter $t=0$, choose the oriented normal trivialization so the section is $t e_1$ near $0$, with $e_2$ the positive quarter-turn of $e_1$; replace it by $t e_1+\delta e_2$ or $t e_1-\delta e_2$ for sufficiently small $\delta>0$. These are the $+$ and $-$ resolutions of that zero and determine the framing classes on the resolved knots.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring. For an $R$-valued ambient-isotopy invariant $V$ of unframed oriented knots and an $m$-singular knot $K$, its **finite difference** is
$$
D_mV(K):=\sum_{\epsilon\in\{+1,-1\}^m}\left(\prod_{i=1}^m\epsilon_i\right)V(K_\epsilon),
$$
where $K_\epsilon$ resolves singularity $i$ positively when $\epsilon_i=+1$ and negatively when $\epsilon_i=-1$. For $m=0$, set $D_0V(K)=V(K)$. The same formula defines $D_mV$ for an invariant of framed knots on framed singular knots, counting both double points and framing zeroes among the $m$ singularities. For one double point it reads $V(K_+)-V(K_-)$; the zero resolutions use the local normal-section model just specified. An invariant has **type at most $n$** if $D_{n+1}V$ vanishes on every $(n+1)$-singular object in its category. It has **exact type $n$** if it has type at most $n$ but not type at most $n-1$. Type at most $-1$ means the zero invariant, so a nonzero type-at-most-zero invariant has exact type zero. For an unframed link, replace $S^1$ by a finite disjoint union of oriented circles, allow marked self- or mixed double points, and use the same resolution sum. For a framed link, take a normal section on each component and count its simple zeroes together with all double points.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Assume full AC for the library Jones invariant. An oriented link is a finite
disjoint union of oriented smooth circles embedded in $S^3$, considered up to
ambient isotopy; an oriented classical knot is the one-component case. For an
oriented link $L\subset S^3$, let $V_L(x)\in\mathbb Z[x^{\pm1}]$ be the
library-normalized Jones polynomial, with $V_U(x)=1$ for the unknot $U$;
write $V_K$ for its value on a knot $K$. Here $x=t^{1/2}$ in the library
convention $t=A^{-4}$, so an oriented skein triple satisfies
$$x^{-2}V_{L_+}(x)-x^2V_{L_-}(x)=(x-x^{-1})V_{L_0}(x).$$
Set $p=x-x^{-1}$. By the unique Laurent decomposition, write
$$V_K(x)=\sum_{q\ge0}(a_q(K)+b_q(K)x)p^q,$$
where $a_q(K),b_q(K)\in\mathbb Z$ and only finitely many are nonzero. The
**Jones–Vassiliev coefficient vector of order $q$** is
$$f_q(K):=(a_q(K),b_q(K))^{\mathsf T},$$
and $c_q(K):=a_q(K)+b_q(K)$. This is the algebraic coefficient-vector
definition used by Carmi and Cohen. The claim that the coordinates of $f_q$
are finite-type invariants of order at most $q$ is a separate theorem and is
not part of this definition.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $K$ be an unoriented link type in $S^3$. Its **crossing number** $c(K)$ is the least element of
$$\{\,n\in\mathbb N:\text{some regular diagram of }K\text{ has exactly }n\text{ crossings}\,\}.$$

facts:
**Given:** $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and an unoriented link type $K$ in $S^3$.

[F1] A link is a finite disjoint union of smoothly embedded circles in $S^3$, and it may be moved off $\infty$ into $\mathbb R^3$ before projection ([[def-oriented-link-in-s-three-and-ambient-isotopy]]).

[F2] A regular diagram is a finite planar projection with transverse double points, no triple points, and over-under data ([[def-regular-oriented-link-diagram]]).

[F3] Under countable choice, every oriented link admits a regular projection ([[lem-every-oriented-link-admits-a-regular-projection]]).

[F4] Every nonempty subset of $\mathbb N$ has a least element ([[thm-well-ordering-principle]]).

[A1] Countable choice, abbreviated $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, selects one element from each member of a countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable-choice]]).

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text: Assume full AC and let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot. The **enhanced A-polynomial** $\widetilde A_K(M,L)$ is the primitive square-free Laurent polynomial defining the union of one-dimensional peripheral-eigenvalue image components arising from irreducible characters of $\pi_1(E_K)$. It is defined up to multiplication by $\pm M^aL^b$. The ordinary A-polynomial is the least common multiple $A_K=\operatorname{lcm}(\widetilde A_K,L-1)$, up to a Laurent unit, where the least common multiple uses each distinct irreducible Laurent factor only once; the factor $L-1$ is the contribution of the abelian character component, and an irreducible component may also contribute that same factor.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text: Assume full AC and let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot with exterior $E_K$, positive meridian $\mu$, and preferred longitude $\lambda$. Define $\mathcal E_K\subset(\mathbb C^*)^2$ to consist of all pairs $(M,L)$ for which some representation $\rho:\pi_1(E_K)\to SL_2(\mathbb C)$ has a common invariant line on which $\rho(\mu)$ acts by $M$ and $\rho(\lambda)$ acts by $L$. The Zariski closure is the smallest Zariski-closed algebraic subset containing $\mathcal E_K$; let $V_K$ be the union of its one-dimensional irreducible components, where an irreducible component is a maximal irreducible closed subset. Zero-dimensional image components are omitted. The **ordinary A-polynomial** $A_K(M,L)$ is the Laurent polynomial generating the vanishing ideal of $V_K$, chosen square-free (no repeated irreducible factors) and with primitive integer coefficients (their greatest common divisor is one). It is determined up to multiplication by $\pm M^aL^b$ for $a,b\in\mathbb Z$. Its reduced curve includes the abelian component $L=1$; equivalently, its representative in $\mathbb Z[M,L]$ is divisible by $L-1$.

contract.heading: Statement refuted
contract.text:
Assume full AC for the Jones invariant and $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for $c(K)$.
A classical knot is a smooth embedding $S^1\hookrightarrow S^3$ considered
up to ambient isotopy. A regular diagram is a generic plane projection with
only transverse double points, each marked with over/under information. The
false universal extension is: for every classical knot $K$, including the
unknot, there is an integer $q$ with $2\le q\le3c(K)$ and
$f_q(K)\ne(0,0)^{\mathsf T}$. Here $V_K(x)$ is the normalized library Jones
polynomial with $V_U(x)=1$, $f_q(K)=(a_q(K),b_q(K))^{\mathsf T}$ is defined by
the unique expansion $V_K(x)=\sum_{q\ge0}(a_q(K)+b_q(K)x)(x-x^{-1})^q$, and
$c(K)$ is the least crossing number of a regular diagram of $K$.

The boundary input is the unknot $U$, represented by the crossing-free circle:

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.9,line cap=round]
  \draw[thick] (0,0) circle (0.55);
  \node at (0,-0.9) {$U$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, and the unknot $U$ with its one-component crossing-free diagram.

[F1] The library Jones polynomial has $V_U(x)=1$, and the coefficient vector is obtained from the unique finite expansion in powers of $p=x-x^{-1}$ ([[def-jones-vassiliev-coefficient-vectors]]).

[F2] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, $c(K)$ is the least element of the set of crossing counts of regular diagrams representing $K$ ([[def-crossing-number-of-link]]).

[A1] Full AC is the family-choice assertion ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

[A2] $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ selects an element from each countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable-choice]]).

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Work with smooth oriented knots in the standard oriented three-sphere; a knot is a one-component oriented link. A **finite planar code for an oriented knot diagram** consists of finite vertex and edge sets, incidence data, a cyclic order of the four half-edges at every crossing vertex, a pairing of opposite half-edges into the two local branches, an orientation of each edge, and a choice of which branch is over at each crossing. Every other vertex is a bend vertex of valence two. The code includes a finite plane-drawing certificate: rational coordinates for the vertices and bends, and a finite polygonal path for every edge. The certificate must realize the incidences and cyclic orders, have no edge self-intersection, and have pairwise disjoint edge interiors except at the specified bend and crossing vertices; at a crossing the two branches must be transverse. These conditions are checked by finitely many exact segment-intersection tests. Edge orientations must join coherently across each paired branch and each bend vertex, and following the edges through the crossing pairings and the degree-two bend vertices must give one oriented circle. Thus an admissible code represents a connected regular oriented diagram of a single knot. If there are no crossing vertices, the code is one oriented polygonal circle and has one arc. Smooth each bend in a small disk disjoint from all crossings and other edges; the resulting smooth diagram has the same crossing data.

An **under-arc** is a maximal portion of the oriented circle between consecutive points where the knot passes under at a crossing; the over branch is not cut. With no crossings the entire circle is the unique under-arc. A **positive meridian** of an oriented branch is the oriented boundary of a small normal disk, with disk orientation chosen so that the oriented tangent to the branch followed by the disk orientation agrees with the ambient orientation of $S^3$. Planarity, incidence, orientation consistency, one-component tracing and the over/under data are input validity conditions; a procedure receiving an invalid finite record must report invalid input rather than repair it. The code stores no algebraic crossing sign: the oriented plane and the direction of the over branch determine which incident under branch is on its left and which is on its right.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text: Input a valid finite planar code for one regular oriented knot diagram and a basepoint in the interior of an edge, away from every crossing and bend. Traverse the oriented code once starting at the basepoint. At each crossing, consider the first branch reached by this traversal. If that branch is under, record the crossing and exchange its over/under label; otherwise leave the crossing unchanged. Return the finite list of recorded crossing changes and the updated planar code. For a code with no crossings, return the empty list and the unchanged code. The input is the valid finite code defined for an oriented knot diagram; this procedure has no invalid-input branch.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Every smooth oriented knot in $S^3$ has an admissible finite planar code whose rational polygonal drawing certificate represents a regular oriented diagram of that knot.

facts:
**Given:** The Axiom of Countable Choice and a smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$.

[A1] The Axiom of Countable Choice, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. [[def-countable-choice]]

[F1] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the knot can be moved off infinity and projected regularly; the projection has finitely many transverse double points and no triple points. [[lem-every-oriented-link-admits-a-regular-projection]]

[F2] A finite planar code records a rational polygonal path for every edge, exact incidence and over/under data, transverse crossing vertices, and one oriented component. [[def-knot-planar-code]]

[F3] Regularity is the condition that the projected knot is an immersion with only finitely many transverse double points and no higher multiple points. [[def-regular-oriented-link-diagram]]

[F4] An isotopy of embeddings of a compact circle extends to an ambient isotopy under AC$_\omega$. [[def-oriented-link-in-s-three-and-ambient-isotopy]], [[thm-isotopy-extension]]

contract.text: For every admissible finite planar code of a regular oriented knot diagram and every basepoint in the interior of an edge, the descending-diagram procedure terminates, visits each crossing record once, and returns a finite updated code and a crossing-change list with at most one entry per crossing. The updated code is admissible and its first-encounter branch at each crossing is the overpassing branch. No claim about efficient minimization of $u(K)$ is made.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K:S^1\hookrightarrow S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere, and let $F\subset S^3$ be a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface with boundary $K$, oriented so that its boundary orientation is the given orientation of $K$. Let $g$ be the nonnegative integer determined by $\chi(F)=1-2g$. Choose an ordered integral basis $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ of the first singular homology group $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$, represented by integral one-cycles on $F$. Orient the normal line of $F$ by requiring $(n,u,v)$ to be positively oriented in $S^3$ whenever $(u,v)$ is a positive tangent basis of $F$. The positive push-off $a_i^+$ is the cycle carried to a sufficiently small positive normal level in a bicollar of $F$.

For disjoint oriented closed curves $J,L\subset S^3$, orient a meridian $\mu_L$ of $L$ so that a positive tangent to $L$ followed by a positive basis of its normal disk gives the ambient orientation. The linking number $\operatorname{lk}(J,L)$ is the integer determined by $[J]=\operatorname{lk}(J,L)[\mu_L]$ in $H_1(S^3\setminus L;\mathbb Z)$, using the Alexander-duality identification that sends $[\mu_L]$ to $1$. Extend linking additively over integral one-cycles. The Seifert pairing is $\theta_F(x,y)=\operatorname{lk}(x^+,y)$, and its matrix in the chosen basis is $V=(V_{ij})_{i,j=1}^{2g}$, where $V_{ij}=\theta_F(a_i,a_j)=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. The surface and basis are part of the data; this definition asserts no knot-only matrix invariant.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $D_+$ and $D_-$ be finite regular oriented diagrams that agree outside one crossing neighborhood and differ inside it by switching which branch is over. Let $V_+$ and $V_-$ be the Seifert matrices obtained from their oriented disk-and-band surfaces. There are corresponding integral bases in which either $V_+=V_-$ or $V_+-V_-=\pm vv^T$ for some integral column vector $v$. In particular, $\operatorname{rank}(V_+-V_-)\le1$.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, two oriented knot diagrams differing at one crossing, and their Seifert disk-and-band constructions.

[A1] Full AC is the choice-function axiom used by the knot Seifert-pairing convention. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] The Seifert construction smooths each crossing by the orientation-compatible pairing and adds one half-twisted band per original crossing. [[alg-seifert-surface-from-diagram]]

[F2] For a knot diagram, the resulting disk-and-band data can be realized as a connected compact oriented embedded spanning surface. [[lem-seifert-bands-embedded-orientable-boundary-correct]]

[F3] In an ordered integral basis, the Seifert matrix has entries $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$, where $a_i^+$ is the positive normal push-off. [[def-knot-seifert-pairing-and-matrix]]

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented link diagram with exactly one component, and let $c$ be its number of crossings. Perform the following construction in its projection sphere $S^2$.

1. Choose a point $q\in S^2$ outside the finite diagram. In pairwise disjoint small disks about the crossings, replace each crossing by the unique noncrossing smoothing compatible with the strand orientations. Let the resulting oriented circles be the Seifert circles and let $s$ be their number.
2. For each Seifert circle $C$, take the closure of the component of $S^2\setminus C$ that does not contain $q$. Under the stated choice axiom, each such region is an embedded compact disk. The finite family of disk regions is nested or disjoint. Orient each disk to induce the given orientation of its boundary circle, then place nested disks at distinct nearby heights ordered by inclusion; the resulting disk interiors are pairwise disjoint in $S^3$.
3. For every original crossing, attach one rectangular band along short boundary intervals on the two smoothing arcs. A half-twist means a single $180$-degree turn of the band across the crossing neighborhood. Choose its direction, endpoint orientations, and over/under order to match the original crossing.
4. Return the finite disk-and-band construction data together with $(s,c)$.

The returned data are a finite attached two-dimensional complex. This algorithm's definition alone does not assert that the resulting image is embedded, is a surface, is connected, or has the original knot as boundary; the separate correctness lemma establishes those properties.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For every finite regular oriented diagram with exactly one component, the Seifert diagram procedure terminates after one finite smoothing scan and one finite band-record scan. It returns exactly one disk record for each Seifert circle and exactly one band record for each original crossing. Termination alone asserts no embeddedness, boundary equality, or genus minimality.

facts:
**Given:** $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and a regular oriented knot diagram $D$.

[A1] The Axiom of Countable Choice is the sequence principle stated in the item. ([[def-countable-choice]])

[F1] The procedure performs one oriented smoothing at each crossing, records the Seifert circles, and then records one band for each crossing. ([[alg-seifert-surface-from-diagram]])

[F2] A regular oriented diagram has finitely many double points, all transverse, and no triple points. ([[def-regular-oriented-link-diagram]])

[F3] Smoothing every crossing produces a finite disjoint union of oriented simple closed curves. ([[def-seifert-smoothing-and-seifert-circles-of-an-oriented-link-diagram]])

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented diagram of a single knot, and let the Seifert algorithm supply its finite disk-and-band construction data. These disks and bands can be realized in $S^3$ as a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface $F$ with exactly one boundary component, whose oriented boundary is the knot represented by $D$. The bands can be chosen mutually disjoint and disjoint from disk interiors except at their attaching intervals.

facts:
**Given:** $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, a regular oriented knot diagram $D$, and the finite output data of the Seifert algorithm.

[F1] At each crossing the unique noncrossing pairing compatible with the strand orientations is used; performing this at all crossings gives a finite disjoint union of oriented simple closed curves in $S^2$. ([[def-seifert-smoothing-and-seifert-circles-of-an-oriented-link-diagram]])

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Fix a coordinate orientation-reversing reflection $r:S^3\to S^3$ for the mirror convention. Let $K$ and $J$ be smooth oriented knots in the standard oriented three-sphere. A connected-sum datum consists of one smoothly embedded closed three-ball around a short subarc of $K$ and one around a short subarc of $J$, each meeting its knot in a single trivial properly embedded arc, together with the fixed standard orientation-reversing boundary identification of the two standard oriented ball boundaries that joins the oriented arcs into one circle. Choose this standard map once in the standard two-ball model so that it commutes with $r$ and an orientation-preserving half-turn interchanging the two balls preserves the joining convention. Here a trivial arc is an embedded interval in a ball that is carried by an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism of ball-arc pairs to a straight diameter. Remove the interiors of the two balls and glue the remaining boundary spheres using this fixed identification; the resulting oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere is a connected sum of $K$ and $J$, denoted $K\#J$ for the specified datum.

The **standard unknot** is the oriented unit circle in a fixed coordinate two-plane of $S^3\subset\mathbb R^4$. A knot is **nontrivial** if it is not ambient isotopic through orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms of $S^3$ to the standard unknot. A nontrivial knot is **prime** if it has no connected-sum presentation whose two summand knots are both nontrivial.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Identify the oriented $S^3$ with the unit sphere in $\mathbb R^4$ by an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism and fix the standard height $h(x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4)=x_4$. Its only critical points are the two poles, and each regular level is a 2-sphere. A **Morse representative** of a smooth oriented knot $K$ is a knot ambient isotopic to $K$ on which $h$ has only nondegenerate critical points. Define the **bridge number** $b(K)$ as the minimum number of local maxima of $h$ on a Morse representative of $K$. The standard unknot is the oriented unit circle in a fixed coordinate 2-plane of $S^3$.

A **regular oriented diagram** is a projection of a smooth oriented knot with finitely many transverse double points, no other multiple points, and an over/under choice at each double point. A **crossing change** switches which branch is over at one chosen double point and leaves the projection and strand orientations unchanged. Define the **unknotting number** $u(K)$ as the minimum number of crossing changes needed to turn some regular diagram of a representative of $K$ into a diagram of the standard unknot. Both minima are taken in subsets of $\mathbb N$. The Morse-representative set is nonempty by the first well-definedness result below; under countable choice the regular-diagram existence result and the descending-diagram theorem below make the unknotting set nonempty. The bridge-number definition and the least-element argument in $\mathbb N$ require no choice; countable choice is used only to invoke the stated regular-projection supplier for $u(K)$.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K=K_1\#K_2$ be a smooth oriented connected sum with both factors nontrivial. Let $S$ be a regular level sphere giving a bridge position: $S$ divides $S^3$ into two balls, and in each ball the knot is a finite collection of properly embedded arcs, each of which cobounds an embedded disk with an arc on $S$; the disks in each ball are pairwise disjoint. Let $P$ be a smooth decomposing sphere meeting $K$ transversely in two points and cutting it into the given two oriented factors. Put $E=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$ and let $A=P\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$ be the resulting annulus, where $N(K)$ is a small closed tubular neighborhood. Assume the inclusion-induced map $\pi_1(A)\to\pi_1(E)$ is injective and that there is no embedded disk in $E$, with interior disjoint from $A\cup\partial E$, whose boundary is the union of a properly embedded arc in $A$ that does not cobound a disk in $A$ with a subarc of $\partial A$ and an arc in $\partial E$. Then, after isotoping $P$ through spheres meeting $K$ twice and changing only the bridge-spanning disk systems for the fixed pair $(K,S)$, one can arrange that $P\cap S$ is exactly one simple closed curve and that the union of the upper and lower bridge-spanning disks meets $P$ in exactly two arcs, each joining one point of $P\cap K$ to a point of $P\cap S$.

facts:
**Given:** The stated countable-choice hypothesis, fixed bridge pair $(K,S)$ and initial spanning disks, the specified two-puncture sphere $P$, and the two essential-annulus hypotheses.

[F1] A knot exterior is irreducible under countable choice. [[lem-knot-exterior-is-irreducible]]

[F2] Smooth Schoenflies identifies both sides of a smooth sphere simultaneously with balls, by an ambient isotopy. [[thm-smooth-schoenflies-for-embedded-two-sphere-in-s-three]]

[F3] Supplied smooth ball windows admit collar-compatible attachment and removal. [[lem-choice-free-smooth-parametrized-ball-windows-and-disk-absorption]]

[F4] A compact smooth embedding isotopy extends ambiently. [[thm-isotopy-extension]]

[F5] The oriented factors obtained from a two-puncture sphere by boundary caps are the connected-sum factors, independently of the cap choices. [[lem-knot-decomposing-sphere-realizes-connected-sum]], [[lem-knot-connected-sum-well-defined]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For two smooth oriented knots, changing either representative by oriented ambient isotopy, changing the sufficiently small coordinate ball and trivial subarc used for either knot, or changing the positive local frame used to identify that ball with the standard oriented ball does not change the oriented ambient-isotopy class of the connected-sum knot, when the boundary gluing map is the fixed standard orientation-reversing map from the definition.

facts:
**Given:** The Axiom of Countable Choice and two smooth oriented knots with connected-sum data as in the Definition.

[F1] A knot is a smooth embedding of one oriented circle in the standard oriented three-sphere, and equivalence of oriented knots is by an orientation-preserving ambient isotopy. ([[def-oriented-link-in-s-three-and-ambient-isotopy]])

[F2] The connected-sum datum uses an orientation-preserving embedding of a standard ball-arc pair into each knot and a fixed standard boundary gluing. ([[def-knot-connected-sum-and-prime-knot]])

[F3] Under the Axiom of Countable Choice, an isotopy of embeddings of a compact manifold with boundary into a boundaryless manifold extends to an ambient isotopy supported near its track. ([[thm-isotopy-extension]])

[A1] The Axiom of Countable Choice is the sequence-choice principle stated in the item. ([[def-countable-choice]])

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in $S^3$, and let $S\subset S^3$ be a smoothly embedded sphere transverse to $K$ in exactly two points. Cutting along $S$ gives two properly embedded arcs; cap each arc by an orientation-compatible simple arc on $S$, pushed slightly into the corresponding boundary collar to obtain oriented knots $K_1$ and $K_2$. Then the oriented isotopy class of $K$ is the connected sum $K_1\#K_2$.

facts:
**Given:** AC$_\omega$, a smooth oriented knot $K$, and a smooth sphere $S$ transverse to $K$ in two points.

[F1] Smooth Schoenflies supplies an ambient isotopy taking $S$ to the equator; its endpoint identifies both ball sides simultaneously, with the same equatorial boundary parametrization. ([[thm-smooth-schoenflies-for-embedded-two-sphere-in-s-three]])

[F2] The fixed standard ball-arc connected-sum construction is independent of its local choices under AC$_\omega$. ([[def-knot-connected-sum-and-prime-knot]], [[lem-knot-connected-sum-well-defined]], [[def-countable-choice]])

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume countable choice. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth knot with a chosen closed tubular neighborhood $N(K)$, and let $E_K=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$. Every smoothly embedded two-sphere in the interior of $E_K$ bounds a smoothly embedded closed three-ball contained in $E_K$.

facts:
**Given:** Countable choice, a smooth knot $K\subset S^3$, its chosen closed tubular neighborhood $N(K)$, and a smooth embedded sphere $S\subset\operatorname{int}E_K$.

[F1] Countable choice is the axiom that every countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-countable-choice]]).

[F2] Under countable choice, $S$ separates $S^3$ into two components whose closures are smooth three-balls with common boundary $S$ ([[thm-smooth-schoenflies-for-embedded-two-sphere-in-s-three]], Statement).

[F3] $E_K=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$, where $N(K)$ is connected and contains $K$ ([[def-knot-exterior]], Definition).

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume countable choice. Let $S\subset S^3$ be the image of a smooth embedding of the standard $S^2$. There is a smooth ambient isotopy $H_t:S^3\to S^3$, with $H_0=\operatorname{id}$, such that $H_1(S)$ is the standard equatorial sphere $E$. In particular $S^3\setminus S$ has exactly two components. Their closures $B_+$ and $B_-$ are smoothly embedded standard closed $3$-balls with common boundary $S$. If $D_+$ and $D_-$ denote the standard closed hemispheres bounded by $E$, the labels can be chosen so that the restrictions $H_1:B_\pm\to D_\pm$ are diffeomorphisms with the same boundary restriction $H_1|_S:S\to E$. Thus the ball identifications are compatible on their boundary and on a common two-sided collar of that boundary.

facts:
**Given:** Countable choice and the smooth embedded sphere $S\subset S^3$.

[F1] A generic linear height on a compact Euclidean embedded smooth manifold is Morse ([[thm-generic-height-functions-on-an-embedded-compact-manifold-are-morse]]). Its finitely many critical values can be separated by arbitrarily small local bump perturbations without changing its critical points or Hessians ([[lem-finitely-many-critical-values-can-be-separated-locally]]).

[F2] Under countable choice a regular nullhomotopic circle on an oriented surface bounds a compact disk; on a sphere both complementary closures are disk regions ([[lem-finite-chart-surface-normal-forms-supply-jordan-disks-and-torsion-free-groups]], clause 4). In the plane use the explicit linear contraction. Smooth disk parametrizations, including collar-compatible boundary maps, are obtained by the smooth-input disk-and-band construction in steps 7.1–13.1 of [[lem-finite-c2-surface-carriers-have-smooth-normal-forms-and-relative-cap-approximations]]. In particular the two disks obtained by cutting a smooth sphere along a regular circle are smooth disks.

[F3] Each sphere obtained by capping a height piece with at most one critical point bounds a smooth standard ball ([[lem-capped-elementary-height-spheres-bound-smooth-balls]]).

[F4] A disk attachment or its reverse is absorbed without changing the smooth manifold type, and an embedded standard ball is ambient isotopic to a coordinate round ball ([[lem-smooth-ball-windows-and-boundary-disk-absorption]]).

[F5] Smooth isotopies of compact embedded submanifolds extend to ambient isotopies under countable choice ([[thm-isotopy-extension]]).

[A1] Countable choice is [[def-countable-choice]]. Its use is inherited from the local disk, smooth normal-form and isotopy-extension suppliers [F2]–[F5]; it is an assumption of this local proof, not a claim that the classical theorem requires that axiom intrinsically. The surgeries and their reversal form finite constructions.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice used by the bridge-number definition. For every smooth oriented knot $K$ in the standard $S^3$, $b(K)=1$ if and only if $K$ is ambient isotopic through orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms to the fixed oriented coordinate circle used as the standard unknot.

facts:
**Given:** $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and a smooth oriented knot $K$ in the standard $S^3$.

[A1] The definition of $b(K)$ is the least number of local maxima over Morse representatives, and the standard unknot is the fixed coordinate circle. [[def-knot-bridge-position-and-unknotting-number]]

[F1] The set of Morse representatives is nonempty for every smooth knot. [[lem-knot-admits-morse-height-representative]]

[F2] A proper arc with one height maximum (or minimum) in a height ball bounds a bridge disk with any prescribed simple boundary arc joining its endpoints on the level sphere. [[lem-one-extremum-arc-is-boundary-parallel]]

[F3] A smooth oriented knot bounds a genus-zero spanning surface exactly when it is ambient isotopic to the standard unknot. [[lem-knot-genus-zero-iff-unknot]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For any two smooth oriented knots $K$ and $J$ in $S^3$, the bridge number of their oriented connected sum satisfies
$$b(K\#J)=b(K)+b(J)-1.$$

facts:
**Given:** AC$_\omega$ and smooth oriented knots $K,J\subset S^3$.

[A1] The Axiom of Countable Choice, written AC$_\omega$. [[def-countable-choice]]

[F1] The bridge-number minima are over nonempty subsets of $\mathbb N$ and are attained, and changing the connected-sum datum preserves the oriented knot class. [[def-knot-bridge-position-and-unknotting-number]], [[lem-knot-connected-sum-well-defined]]

[F2] The connected sum is represented by removing a small trivial ball-arc neighborhood from each summand and gluing the two boundary spheres with the fixed arc-matching convention. [[def-knot-connected-sum-and-prime-knot]]

[F3] The essential-annulus normalization for the fixed bridge pair is [[lem-bridge-sphere-normalization]]. Its two final disk-intersection arcs end on $P\cap S$, away from the knot.

[F4] A knot exterior has $H_1(E;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z[\mu]$. [[lem-knot-exterior-h1-is-generated-by-meridian]]

[F5] Knot exteriors are irreducible under countable choice, and an incompressible boundary-compressible annulus in an irreducible smooth torus-boundary manifold is boundary-parallel. [[lem-knot-exterior-is-irreducible]], [[lem-boundary-compressible-annulus-is-boundary-parallel]]

[F6] Smooth Schoenflies gives an ambient isotopy of a smooth sphere to the equator with compatible ball-side parameters. Disk-window attachment and removal preserve the displayed ball type. [[thm-smooth-schoenflies-for-embedded-two-sphere-in-s-three]], [[lem-choice-free-smooth-parametrized-ball-windows-and-disk-absorption]]

[F7] Compact smooth embedding isotopies extend ambiently. [[thm-isotopy-extension]]

[F8] A two-puncture sphere determines the stated oriented connected-sum factors by boundary caps; the unknot is the connected-sum identity and has bridge number one. [[lem-knot-decomposing-sphere-realizes-connected-sum]], [[thm-oriented-knot-connected-sum-is-a-commutative-monoid]], [[thm-bridge-one-is-unknot]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. On oriented ambient-isotopy classes of smooth knots in $S^3$, the connected-sum operation is associative and commutative, and the standard unknot is a two-sided identity. Here “commutative monoid” means a set with an associative binary operation, a two-sided identity, and equality after interchanging the two inputs.

facts:
**Given:** AC$_\omega$ and the oriented connected-sum construction.

[F1] The connected sum is formed by gluing the complements of trivial ball-arc pairs with a fixed standard orientation-reversing map, chosen symmetrically in the two-ball model. ([[def-knot-connected-sum-and-prime-knot]])

[F2] Changing the local representatives, charts, and sufficiently small ball-arc choices does not change the resulting oriented knot class. ([[lem-knot-connected-sum-well-defined]])

[A1] AC$_\omega$ is the countable-choice hypothesis used by the local-choice lemma. ([[def-countable-choice]])

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot with a chosen closed product
tubular neighborhood $N(K)$, exterior $E_K=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$,
and positive meridian $\mu_K$. Then
$$H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z[\mu_K].$$
The assertion uses integral singular homology and the stated tube convention.

facts:
**Given:** The chosen product tube, exterior, and positive-meridian convention.

[F1] [[def-knot-exterior]] fixes $N(K)$ and $E_K$; [[def-knot-meridian-and-preferred-longitude]] orients $\mu_K$ as the boundary of a positive normal disk.

[F2] [[thm-cellular-homology-computes-singular-homology]] and [[thm-cellular-boundary-is-the-incidence-degree-matrix]]: the product torus has the CW structure with one vertex, two one-cells and one two-cell attached by the commutator; its cellular boundary map in degree two is zero, so $H_1(\partial N(K);\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^2$ on the meridian and product section.

[F3] [[thm-excision-for-singular-homology]] and [[thm-long-exact-sequence-of-a-pair-in-singular-homology]]: relative homology is unchanged by excision and each pair has its natural long exact sequence.

[F4] [[cor-homology-of-spheres]]: $H_1(S^3;\mathbb Z)=H_2(S^3;\mathbb Z)=0$, and $H_1(S^1;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z$, $H_2(S^1;\mathbb Z)=0$.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Let $M$ be a compact connected orientable irreducible $3$-manifold whose boundary components are tori. Let $A\subset M$ be a connected properly embedded incompressible annulus with $\partial A\subset\partial M$. If $A$ is boundary-compressible, then $A$ is boundary-parallel.

facts:
**Given:** The compact connected orientable irreducible smooth three-manifold with torus boundary, the incompressible proper annulus $A$, and a boundary-compressing disk $D$.

[F1] The disk obstructions, irreducibility and boundary-parallel product have the conventions of [[def-incompressibility-seifert-fibration-and-jsj-system]], Definition.

[F2] Smooth essential torus curves are primitive, finite disjoint families admit smooth affine normalization, and their complementary strips have smooth annulus parameters, without choice ([[lem-choice-free-smooth-torus-curves-and-annulus-strips]], Statement).

[F3] A parametrized ball with a parametrized boundary disk window is the standard marked pair; with supplied collars, disk attachment and removal preserve ball type, without choice ([[lem-choice-free-smooth-parametrized-ball-windows-and-disk-absorption]], Statement).

[F9] Every compact smooth boundary-preimage surface has a boundary-fixed smooth embedding neatification with an explicit topological ambient extension. The actual smooth disk obstructions and boundary-compressing witnesses transport as stated in the endpoint-witness supplier. Products here are the products in the original Definition; on a broad nonneat input their pullbacks are topological products, not newly asserted smooth collars. contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Assume full AC. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the oriented standard $3$-sphere, let $F$ be a connected compact smooth oriented surface with oriented boundary $K$, let $V$ be the matrix of the Seifert pairing $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$ in an ordered integral basis, and let $\omega\in S^1\setminus\{1\}$. Define the **Levine–Tristram Hermitian matrix** by
$$H_\omega(V)=(1-\omega)V+(1-\bar\omega)V^T.$$
It is Hermitian because $V$ is real and $\bar\omega=\omega^{-1}$. Its signature is the number of positive eigenvalues minus the number of negative eigenvalues, both counted with multiplicity and with zero eigenvalues omitted. When $\Delta_K(\omega)\ne0$, define $\sigma_\omega(K)$ to be this signature. At a root $\omega_0\ne1$ of $\Delta_K$, define $\sigma_{\omega_0}(K)$ to be the arithmetic mean of the two one-sided limits of $\sigma_{e^{i\theta}}(K)$ as $\theta$ approaches an argument of $\omega_0$ from below and above. The invariance and one-sided-existence lemmas justify treating these values as independent of the chosen surface and basis.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, a smooth oriented knot, a connected compact oriented spanning surface, an ordered integral basis, and a point $\omega$ on the unit circle other than $1$.

[A1] Full AC is the stated ambient axiom for the Alexander-module and Seifert-pairing conventions. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] For real $V$, $H_\omega(V)^*=H_\omega(V)$ because conjugation exchanges the coefficients of $V$ and $V^T$. [[lem-levine-tristram-hermitian-form-singular-set]]

[F2] Integral basis change is unimodular congruence; elementary surface enlargements are the two rank-two Seifert matrices in the S-equivalence definition. [[def-seifert-matrix-s-equivalence]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume full AC. For every smooth oriented knot $K$, the classical signature $\sigma_{-1}(K)$ of the positive-push Seifert form is independent of the chosen connected spanning surface and integral basis, and it satisfies
$$|\sigma_{-1}(K)|\le 2u(K).$$
Zero eigenvalues are omitted when computing the signature of a Hermitian matrix.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC and a smooth oriented knot $K$.

[A1] Full AC implies the countable-choice hypothesis of the unknotting-number definition. [[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]

[F1] The unknotting set is nonempty and $u(K)$ is its least element, measured by finite sequences of crossing changes in regular diagrams. [[def-knot-bridge-position-and-unknotting-number]]

[F2] A single crossing change admits corresponding Seifert matrices with difference zero or $\pm vv^T$. [[lem-seifert-matrices-differ-rank-one-under-crossing-change]]

[F3] Two Hermitian matrices differing by rank at most one have signatures differing by at most two, with zero eigenvalues omitted. [[lem-rank-one-hermitian-signature-perturbation]]

[F4] The positive-push matrix gives $H_{-1}(V)=2(V+V^T)$; surface and basis changes preserve its signature. At a nonroot this is the declared invariant $\sigma_{-1}$. [[def-levine-tristram-hermitian-form-and-signature]], [[lem-seifert-stabilization-preserves-levine-tristram-signature]], [[lem-levine-tristram-hermitian-form-singular-set]]

[F5] The skew part $V-V^T$ is the unimodular intersection pairing of a knot Seifert surface. [[lem-seifert-matrix-skew-part-is-surface-intersection]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume full AC. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot, let $F$ be any connected compact smooth oriented spanning surface of genus $g$, let $V$ be its positive-push Seifert matrix, and let $\omega\in S^1\setminus\{1\}$. The Hermitian matrix
$$H_\omega=(1-\omega)V+(1-\bar\omega)V^T$$
is singular if and only if the normalized knot Alexander polynomial $\Delta_K$ vanishes at $\omega$.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, an oriented knot $K$, a genus-$g$ spanning surface with Seifert matrix $V$, and $\omega\in S^1\setminus\{1\}$.

[A1] Full AC supplies the Alexander-module and Seifert-pairing interfaces. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] For this surface, $\det(V-tV^T)$ is a unit associate of the Alexander polynomial, and its value at $t=1$ is $\det(V-V^T)=\pm1$. [[thm-seifert-determinant-is-the-knot-alexander-polynomial]], [[lem-square-seifert-presentation-and-alexander-normalization]], [[def-alexander-polynomial-from-the-first-elementary-ideal]]

[F2] The matrix determinant is reciprocal up to the unit $t^{2g}$, and the Alexander polynomial differs from it by a Laurent unit. [[thm-seifert-determinant-is-the-knot-alexander-polynomial]]
scope: Literal contract/Facts extraction only; accepted proof body not inspected.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume full AC. For every $\omega\in S^1\setminus\{1\}$, changing an ordered basis by an integral unimodular congruence or changing a knot Seifert matrix by either elementary enlargement or reduction preserves the signature of $H_\omega$. Consequently, the nonroot Levine–Tristram signature and its one-sided-average value at every Alexander root are independent of the spanning surface and basis.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, an oriented knot Seifert matrix $V$, its two enlargement matrices, and $\omega\in S^1\setminus\{1\}$.

[A1] Full AC supplies the Seifert pairing and surface hypotheses. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] A basis change is $V\mapsto P^TVP$ for $P\in GL_{2g}(\mathbb Z)$; knot surfaces are related by isotopies and the two enlargements. [[def-knot-seifert-pairing-and-matrix]], [[lem-seifert-matrices-of-a-knot-are-s-equivalent]], [[def-seifert-matrix-s-equivalence]]

[F2] Signature is the positive eigenvalue count minus negative eigenvalue count of a finite Hermitian matrix. [[def-levine-tristram-hermitian-form-and-signature]]

[F3] The one-sided signature limits at every Alexander root exist, so their arithmetic averages are defined. [[lem-levine-tristram-one-sided-averages-exist]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented embedded circle in the oriented standard three-sphere, let $F$ be a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface with boundary $K$, and let $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ be any ordered integral basis of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$ with Seifert matrix $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. Let $J_F$ be the matrix of the algebraic intersection form on $F$, with a transverse intersection of oriented curves $u,v$ counted positively exactly when their ordered tangent vectors form a positive basis of $TF$. Then $V-V^T=J_F$. The matrix $J_F$ is skew-symmetric and unimodular; when $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ is a standard handle basis, it is a direct sum of blocks $\begin{psmallmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{psmallmatrix}$.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, an oriented knot $K$, a connected compact oriented spanning surface $F$, its oriented normal bicollar, and an integral basis of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$.

[A1] Full AC is the choice-function axiom and supplies the stated countable-choice interfaces. [[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]

[F1] A compact genus-$g$ surface with one boundary component has first homology free of rank $2g$ and a standard handle basis. In that basis the handle curves meet in one positive/negative pair per handle and all other pairs are disjoint. [[lem-finite-chart-surface-normal-forms-supply-jordan-disks-and-torsion-free-groups]]

[F2] The Seifert pairing is bilinear on homology classes; linking is symmetric and positive push-offs may move through the positive normal collar. [[lem-seifert-pairing-well-defined]]

[F3] The positive normal is oriented so that $(n,u,v)$ is a positive ambient basis whenever $(u,v)$ is a positive tangent basis of $F$. [[def-knot-seifert-pairing-and-matrix]]

[F4] The algebraic intersection sign is the local orientation sign of the ordered tangent bases, with the curve factor and surface factor ordered as specified. [[def-oriented-intersection-number]], [[def-local-oriented-intersection-sign]]

[F5] A basis curve $a_j$ is an oriented knot and therefore has a supplied compact oriented spanning surface; with a regular link diagram, linking with that curve is the signed intersection with the surface. [[thm-every-oriented-knot-bounds-a-seifert-surface]], [[thm-linking-number-equals-signed-intersection]], [[def-oriented-link-in-s-three-and-ambient-isotopy]], [[def-regular-oriented-link-diagram]], [[lem-every-oriented-link-admits-a-regular-projection]]

[F6] Countable-choice transversality permits the spanning-surface intersections below to be made transverse, and their intersection traces have the stated boundary; the signed boundary count of a compact oriented one-manifold is zero. [[thm-transversality-homotopy-theorem]], [[prop-relative-transversality-preserves-a-map-on-a-closed-good-region]], [[thm-transverse-preimage-for-manifolds-with-boundary]], [[lem-oriented-boundary-of-a-compact-oriented-one-manifold-has-zero-signed-count]]

contract.heading: Example
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $T$ be the standard right-handed trefoil represented by the closure of the two-strand braid with three positive crossings. In its standard oriented three-crossing projection, label the under-arcs $a,b,c$ so that the crossing triples $(o,t,s)$ of over-arc, target under-arc and source under-arc are $(b,c,a)$, $(c,a,b)$ and $(a,b,c)$, where source and target are determined by the positive in-plane normal to the oriented over-strand. Define bridge number as the minimum number of local maxima over Morse representatives in the fixed standard height on $S^3$, and unknotting number as the minimum number of crossing changes needed to turn a regular diagram of a representative into the fixed standard unknot diagram. Then $b(T)=2$ and $u(T)=1$.

facts:
**Given:** $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and the stated oriented three-crossing trefoil diagram.

[A1] The Axiom of Countable Choice, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. [[def-countable-choice]]

[F1] Bridge number is the minimum number of local maxima in a Morse representative for the fixed standard height. [[def-knot-bridge-position-and-unknotting-number]]

[F2] Unknotting number is the minimum number of crossing changes from a regular diagram of the knot to a diagram of the fixed standard unknot. A regular diagram records its transverse double points, strand orientations and over/under data. [[def-knot-bridge-position-and-unknotting-number]], [[def-regular-oriented-link-diagram]]

[F3] A valid finite planar code gives one positive-meridian generator per under-arc and one crossing conjugacy relator per crossing; the crossing-free one-component code has one generator and no relators, and the resulting presentation maps isomorphically to the knot group. [[def-knot-planar-code]], [[alg-knot-wirtinger-presentation-from-code]], [[thm-knot-wirtinger-presentation-correctness]]

[F4] At every oriented crossing, if $s$ and $t$ are the source and target under-sides determined by the positive in-plane normal of the over-strand, then $m_t=m_o^{-1}m_s m_o$. [[lem-wirtinger-local-meridian-conjugacy]]

[F5] An ambient isotopy ends at an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism, which is a homeomorphism; it induces an isomorphism of complement fundamental groups because the inverse diffeomorphism induces the inverse group map. [[def-oriented-link-in-s-three-and-ambient-isotopy]], [[def-diffeomorphism-and-local-diffeomorphism-of-manifolds]], [[def-based-loops-and-fundamental-group]], [[def-induced-homomorphism-on-fundamental-groups]], [[thm-induced-fundamental-group-map-functoriality]], [[def-group-isomorphism-and-automorphism]]

[F6] Every oriented Reidemeister move on a regular diagram is realized by an ambient isotopy; in particular, oriented Reidemeister-II cancellation and Reidemeister-I curl deletion preserve the represented knot. [[def-oriented-reidemeister-moves]], [[lem-each-oriented-reidemeister-move-is-realized-by-ambient-isotopy]]

[F7] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, a knot has bridge number one if and only if it is ambient isotopic to the fixed standard unknot. [[thm-bridge-one-is-unknot]]

[F8] A group presentation $\langle a,b\mid r\rangle$ is the free group on $a,b$ modulo the normal closure of $r$. [[def-group-presentation]]

[F9] Fundamental-group multiplication is associative and each loop class has the inverse represented by the reversed loop. [[thm-fundamental-group-laws]]

[F10] A continuous real-valued function on a nonempty compact metric space attains a maximum. [[thm-extreme-value-metric]]

[F11] The standard unit circle is the unit Euclidean sphere in $\mathbb R^2$ with its induced Euclidean metric. [[def-euclidean-spheres-and-closed-balls]]

[F12] Every closed bounded subset of $\mathbb R^2$ is compact in the Euclidean metric. [[thm-heine-borel-rn]]

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text: Define a finite procedure $\mathsf{Wirtinger}(D,a_0)$ on a finite planar code $D$ for one oriented knot and a designated under-arc $a_0$ as follows. First check all incidence, valence, branch-pairing, crossing over/under, edge-orientation, and one-component conditions in the code. For each pair of rational line segments in the drawing certificate, compute the determinant of their direction vectors. If it is nonzero, solve the two-coordinate linear intersection equations and check whether the solution lies on both closed segments. If the determinant is zero, test collinearity and overlap by exact rational determinant and endpoint-order comparisons. Accept an intersection only when it is a shared declared bend or crossing vertex with the recorded incidence, and at a crossing verify that the two branch direction vectors have nonzero determinant. Reject self-intersections and all unrecorded intersections. If any check fails, return `invalid-input`. Otherwise traverse the oriented knot once starting at $a_0$, label the maximal under-arcs $a_1,\ldots,a_m$, and introduce one symbol $x_i$ for the positive meridian of each $a_i$. For each crossing $v$, read its oriented over-tangent and positive in-plane normal. Let $a_s$ be the under-side from which that normal points and $a_t$ the side toward which it points, and read the over-arc $a_o$. Append exactly the relator $x_o^{-1}x_sx_ox_t^{-1}$. Equivalently, if the incoming under-tangent follows that normal, append $x_o^{-1}x_{\rm in}x_ox_{\rm out}^{-1}$; otherwise append $x_ox_{\rm in}x_o^{-1}x_{\rm out}^{-1}$. The orientation of a positive meridian is fixed locally by requiring the knot tangent followed by the normal-disk orientation to give the ambient orientation. Once a complement basepoint and basing paths to the meridians are fixed, interpret $x_i$ as the corresponding based positive meridian. Return the finite group presentation with generators $x_1,\ldots,x_m$ and this one relator per crossing. The procedure uses only finite scans and terminates.

facts:
**Given:** A finite planar code and a designated under-arc.

[F1] A valid code contains finite incidence, crossing, orientation, component, and planar-embedding data, with one under-arc between successive underpassing points; the crossing-free code has one under-arc. [[def-knot-planar-code]]

[F2] At every crossing, the incoming and outgoing under-meridians are related by conjugation by the over-meridian, with direction determined by the oriented chart. [[lem-wirtinger-local-meridian-conjugacy]]

[F3] A finite group presentation is a quotient of the free group on its finite generator list by the normal closure of its finite relator list. [[def-group-presentation]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Orient the projection plane by the viewing normal and the ambient orientation. At an oriented crossing let $o$ be the over-arc, and let $n_o$ be its positive in-plane normal: the ordered pair consisting of the over-tangent and $n_o$ is positive. Call the under-side from which $n_o$ points the source $s$, and the side toward which it points the target $t$. A positive meridian is the oriented boundary of a small normal disk whose orientation, preceded by the oriented knot tangent, is the ambient orientation. With the common upper-collar basing paths, the based positive meridians satisfy
$$m_t=m_o^{-1}m_s m_o.$$
This side-based equation is independent of the direction of the understrand. In an oriented chart with over-tangent rightward, the target is the upper side $L$ and source the lower side $R$, so equivalently $m_R=m_o m_Lm_o^{-1}$. In incoming/outgoing notation, the outgoing under-meridian is $m_o^{-1}m_{\rm in}m_o$ if the under-tangent points along $n_o$, and is $m_om_{\rm in}m_o^{-1}$ otherwise. Reversing a chosen meridian loop inverts its class. Changing every common access path by the same based loop conjugates all three classes simultaneously.

facts:
**Given:** The oriented local crossing, the positive-meridian disk convention in the Statement, and common upper-collar access paths.

[F1] The crossing has the annular attachment and meridian-region paths of the crossing-ball construction. [[lem-wirtinger-crossing-ball-cover]]

[F2] Fundamental-group multiplication is represented by loop concatenation; inverse paths give inverses and homotopic based loops give the same element. [[def-based-loops-and-fundamental-group]], [[thm-fundamental-group-laws]]

[F3] Attaching the contractible crossing region kills the image of its annular core normally. [[thm-seifert-van-kampen]], [[thm-group-pushout-as-an-amalgamated-quotient]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot, let $D$ be a valid finite planar code for a regular diagram of $K$, choose a basepoint $b$ in the complement, and designate a starting under-arc. The finite procedure $\mathsf{Wirtinger}(D,a_0)$ terminates and returns a presentation with one positive-meridian generator for each under-arc and one crossing conjugacy relator for each crossing. For the based meridians determined by the diagram's common upper-collar paths from $b$, the homomorphism from the presented group to $\pi_1(S^3\setminus K,b)$ that sends each generator to its corresponding based positive meridian is an isomorphism. Changing the designated starting under-arc only relabels the same finite cyclic arc set and gives an isomorphic presentation. If all basing paths are changed by prepending the same based loop, every generator image is conjugated by the same element, so the isomorphism type is unchanged.

facts:
**Given:** A smooth oriented knot, its valid finite diagram code, a basepoint in the complement, and a designated base under-arc.

[F1] For $c>0$, the exterior retracts to a cover by the meridian region and contractible crossing regions with annular overlaps; the meridian region retracts to the free meridian wedge. For $c=0$, the Euclidean complement has homotopy type $S^1\vee S^2$, with the circle represented by the positive meridian; its fundamental group is infinite cyclic on that meridian. [[lem-wirtinger-crossing-ball-cover]]

[F2] The annular core at each crossing imposes exactly the local conjugacy relation read by the constructor; reversed meridian orientation gives the inverse, and common basing-path change conjugates all generators simultaneously. [[lem-wirtinger-local-meridian-conjugacy]]

[F3] The open-cover fundamental group is the pushout of the inclusion maps. [[thm-seifert-van-kampen]]

[F4] The pushout with a trivial crossing-piece group kills the normal closure of the annular-core image. [[thm-group-pushout-as-an-amalgamated-quotient]]

[F5] The fundamental group of the meridian-region wedge is free on its standard loops. [[thm-fundamental-group-of-finite-wedge-of-circles]]

[F6] A free group is the free object on its declared generator set. [[def-free-group]]

[F7] The returned presentation is the free group on its generators modulo the normal closure of its relators. [[def-group-presentation]]

[F8] A quotient by the relator normal closure has the presentation's universal property. [[thm-quotient-group-universal-property]]

[F9] The inclusion from the Euclidean knot complement into the three-sphere complement induces an isomorphism. [[lem-knot-group-infinity-collar]]

[F10] The constructor makes one finite scan of under-arcs and crossings and returns the specified meridian assignment. [[alg-knot-wirtinger-presentation-from-code]]

[F11] The fundamental group of a circle is infinite cyclic on its once-around loop. [[thm-fundamental-group-of-the-circle]]

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $D^2$ be the oriented closed disk and give $C=D^2\times[0,1]$ the product orientation. An $r$-component string link is an ordered family of pairwise disjoint smooth proper embeddings $\tau_i:[0,1]\to C$, for $1\le i\le r$, with fixed distinct endpoints $\tau_i(0)=(p_i,0)$ and $\tau_i(1)=(p_i,1)$ and fixed product collars at the endpoints. Orient each interval from bottom to top. The exterior $X_\tau$ is obtained by removing the relative interiors of chosen pairwise disjoint product tubes around the intervals. The bottom and top punctured disks $P_-$ and $P_+$ are the copies of $D^2$ with the interiors of the endpoint tube disks removed.

Choose a basepoint on the outer boundary of $P_-$, a path in the side boundary of $C$ to the corresponding top basepoint, and basing paths from these points to the component meridians. Each end inclusion, with the chosen connecting path for the top end, induces a based homomorphism $\iota_\pm:\pi_1(P_\pm)\to\pi_1(X_\tau)$. For each string component choose a parallel path on its tube boundary from the bottom endpoint to the top endpoint, and choose access paths that close it to a based loop using the fixed side connector. The resulting element of $\pi_1(X_\tau)$ is its based string-link longitude; the parallel and access paths are part of the peripheral datum. The positively oriented boundaries of the endpoint tube disks are the designated meridian loops. Stacking two string links means rescaling them into the lower and upper halves of $C$ and identifying their matching endpoint collars; closure joins each top endpoint to the matching bottom endpoint outside $C$ and retains the component labels.

For a nonempty labeled oriented link $L=K_1\cup\cdots\cup K_r$ in the oriented three-sphere, choose pairwise disjoint closed product tubes $N(K_i)$, put $E_L=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}\bigl(\bigcup_iN(K_i)\bigr)$, and write $T_i=\partial N(K_i)$. A positive meridian $\mu_i$ is the oriented boundary of a normal disk, with the disk orientation fixed by the rule that the oriented tangent of $K_i$ followed by the disk orientation gives the ambient orientation. A degree-one parallel is a simple closed curve on $T_i$ whose projection to $K_i$ has degree $+1$. A based longitude is the class of such a parallel transported to the common basepoint by a specified path. When the positive meridians form a basis of $H_1(E_L;\mathbb Z)$, the self-meridian coordinate of a longitude is its coefficient on $[\mu_i]$. A preferred zero-self-meridian longitude is a chosen degree-one parallel whose self-meridian coordinate is zero. The choice, when it exists, is part of the peripheral datum; this definition asserts neither existence nor uniqueness. Changing a common basing path conjugates the peripheral group elements simultaneously.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
For any group $G$, define its lower-central series by $\Gamma_1G=G$ and
$\Gamma_{q+1}G=[G,\Gamma_qG]$, where $[G,H]$ is the subgroup generated by
$ghg^{-1}h^{-1}$ for $g\in G$ and $h\in H$. For $r\ge1$, let
$F_r=\langle x_1,\ldots,x_r\rangle$ be the free group on the formal meridian
symbols $x_i$, with the free-group convention of its stated generators.

Let $\mathcal A_r=\mathbb Z\langle\!\langle X_1,\ldots,X_r\rangle\!\rangle$
be the ring of formal integer sums $\sum_w a_wX_w$ over all finite words $w$
in the letters $X_i$, with multiplication given by concatenation of words.
This is the degree-complete ring for the word-length filtration; a series with
invertible constant coefficient is a unit, with inverse determined recursively
degree by degree.
Filter it by total degree (word length), and let $\mathfrak m$ be the ideal of
series with zero constant term.
The Magnus expansion is the group homomorphism
$$
E:F_r\longrightarrow
\mathbb Z\langle\!\langle X_1,\ldots,X_r\rangle\!\rangle^\times,
\qquad E(x_i)=1+X_i.
$$
It sends $x_i^{-1}$ to $(1+X_i)^{-1}=\sum_{k\ge0}(-1)^kX_i^k$. For an
integer $d\ge0$, calculations through degree $d$ use the truncated ring
$R_d=\mathbb Z\langle X_1,\ldots,X_r\rangle/\mathfrak m^{d+1}$. As a
$\mathbb Z$-module it has the finite monomial basis of words of length at most
$d$. In $R_d$, the inverse of $1+A$ for $A\in\mathfrak m$ is the finite sum
$1-A+A^2-\cdots+(-A)^d$.

For a based string link, $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ may be used as formal symbols
corresponding to the positive bottom-end meridians. No freeness or
lower-central quotient isomorphism is asserted here; those properties require
separate proofs.
