contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $\mathbb N=\{1,2,3,\ldots\}$. For each positive noise level $\epsilon$, let $\Pi_{0,\epsilon}$ be a proper Borel prior on $\ell^2(\mathbb N,\mathbb R)$ in the Gaussian sequence inverse experiment, and let $\mathbb P_{\Pi_{0,\epsilon}}$ be the resulting prior-predictive joint law of parameter and data. A posterior kernel is a data-measurable assignment $y\mapsto\Pi_\epsilon(\cdot\mid y)$ of Borel probability measures on $\ell^2$ satisfying
$$\mathbb P_{\Pi_{0,\epsilon}}(\theta\in A,\,Y\in B)=\int_B\Pi_\epsilon(A\mid y)\,\mathbb P_{\Pi_{0,\epsilon}}^Y(dy)$$
for every Borel $A\subseteq\ell^2$ and every product-Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R^{\mathbb N}$, where $\mathbb P_{\Pi_{0,\epsilon}}^Y$ is the prior-predictive data marginal. Fix a truth $\theta^\dagger\in\ell^2$ and write $\mathbb P_{\theta^\dagger}^\epsilon$ for its data law. Since a conditional-law version is specified only up to a prior-predictive null set, any contraction claim under $\mathbb P_{\theta^\dagger}^\epsilon$ refers to the stated version. A positive function $r_\epsilon\to0$ is a posterior contraction rate in the $\ell^2$ norm at $\theta^\dagger$ if, for every positive function $M_\epsilon\to\infty$,
$$\mathbb E_{\theta^\dagger}^\epsilon\!\left[\Pi_\epsilon\!\left(\{\theta\in\ell^2:\|\theta-\theta^\dagger\|_2>M_\epsilon r_\epsilon\}\mid Y\right)\right]\longrightarrow0\quad\text{as }\epsilon\downarrow0.$$

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $0<\epsilon$, let $(s_j)_{j\ge1}$ be the positive singular values in the Gaussian sequence inverse model, and let a fixed truth $\theta^\dagger=(\theta^\dagger_j)_{j\ge1}$ belong to $\ell^2(\mathbb N,\mathbb R)$. Let $\tau_j>0$ satisfy $\sum_{j\ge1}\tau_j^2<\infty$, and let the prior be a Borel probability on $\ell^2$ whose coordinates are independent $N(0,\tau_j^2)$ variables, independent of the observation noise. Under the prior-predictive law the observations are $Y_j=s_j\theta_j+\epsilon\xi_j$; under the fixed truth they are $Y_j=s_j\theta^\dagger_j+\epsilon\xi_j$, where the $\xi_j$ are independent $N(0,1)$ variables. Define $v_j=(\tau_j^{-2}+s_j^2/\epsilon^2)^{-1}$ and $\lambda_j=\tau_j^2s_j^2/(\epsilon^2+\tau_j^2s_j^2)$. For fixed-truth-almost every data sequence, a posterior version on $\ell^2$ is the restriction of $\bigotimes_{j\ge1}N(\lambda_jY_j/s_j,v_j)$. Its expected posterior squared distance from the truth is
$$S_\epsilon(\theta^\dagger):=\mathbb E_{\theta^\dagger}\!\left[\int_{\ell^2}\|\theta-\theta^\dagger\|_2^2\,\Pi_\epsilon(d\theta\mid Y)\right]=\sum_{j\ge1}\left[(1-\lambda_j)^2(\theta^\dagger_j)^2+\frac{v_j^2s_j^2}{\epsilon^2}+v_j\right].$$
The identity holds in $[0,+\infty]$; under the stated trace condition its right side is finite. For every $R>0$, the expected posterior mass outside the radius-$R$ ball is at most $S_\epsilon(\theta^\dagger)/R^2$. In particular, if $S_\epsilon(\theta^\dagger)\le C r_\epsilon^2$ for a constant $C$ and a positive $r_\epsilon\to0$, then $r_\epsilon$ is a posterior contraction rate in the sense of the preceding definition.

facts:
**Given:** AC and Countable Choice; the positive-noise Gaussian sequence inverse experiment; a fixed truth $\theta^\dagger\in\ell^2$; an independent-coordinate Gaussian prior with $\tau_j>0$ and $\sum_j\tau_j^2<\infty$; and prior/noise independence.

[A1] The Axiom of Choice states that every family of nonempty sets has a choice function. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[A2] Countable Choice supplies a choice function for every countable family of nonempty sets; this is the branch assumed by the compact-SVD coordinate model. [[def-countable-choice]]

[F1] The Gaussian sequence inverse model has parameter $\theta\in\ell^2$, product-Borel data $Z\in\mathbb R^{\mathbb N}$, and coordinates $Z_j=\theta_j+\epsilon s_j^{-1}\xi_j$ with independent standard normal $\xi_j$. Multiplying by $s_j>0$ gives $Y_j=s_j\theta_j+\epsilon\xi_j$. [[def-ip-gaussian-sequence-inverse-model]]

[F2] In a finite linear Gaussian model with Gaussian prior covariance $C_0$ and positive-definite observation-noise covariance $\Gamma$, the posterior covariance is $C_0-C_0A^T(AC_0A^T+\Gamma)^{-1}AC_0$ and the posterior mean is $m_0+C_0A^T(AC_0A^T+\Gamma)^{-1}(y-Am_0)$. [[thm-ip-finite-linear-gaussian-posterior]]

[F3] Under AC, a consistent family of finite Gaussian laws on countably many real coordinates has a unique probability law on the product cylinder sigma-algebra. [[thm-gaussian-process-exists-from-mean-and-positive-semidefinite-covariance-kernel]]

[F4] Independence of random elements is independence of their generated sigma-algebras; the assumed independent prior and noise coordinates give independent coordinate pairs. [[def-independent-random-elements]]

[F5] Finite measures that agree on a generating $\pi$-system and on the whole space agree on its generated sigma-algebra. [[lem-finite-measure-uniqueness-on-a-pi-system]]

[F6] A $\pi$-system contained in a Dynkin system has its generated sigma-algebra contained in that Dynkin system. [[thm-dynkin-pi-lambda]]

[F7] Increasing nonnegative measurable functions satisfy convergence of their integrals to the integral of their pointwise limit. [[thm-monotone-convergence-for-the-integral]]

[F8] For a nonnegative measurable function $f$ and $t>0$, $\mu\{f\ge t\}\le t^{-1}\int f\,d\mu$. [[thm-chebyshev-markov-inequality-for-the-integral]]

[F9] A posterior contraction rate is defined by the expected fixed-truth posterior tail condition in the Statement. [[def-ip-posterior-contraction-rate]]

**Given:** The hypotheses of the Statement.

contract.heading: Example
contract.text: Assume AC and Countable Choice. Fix $\alpha,\beta,p,L>0$. For each $0<\epsilon\le1$, use the centered Gaussian Borel prior on $\ell^2$ with independent coordinates $\theta_j\sim N(0,j^{-1-2\alpha})$, independent of the observation noise. Under the fixed-truth law, observe $Y_j=j^{-p}\theta^\dagger_j+\epsilon\xi_j$ with independent $N(0,1)$ noise and a fixed truth $\theta^\dagger$ in the power ellipsoid $\{\theta\in\ell^2:\sum_{j\ge1}j^{2\beta}(\theta_j)^2\le L^2\}$. Then the posterior contracts in the $\ell^2$ norm at rate $r_\epsilon=\epsilon^{2\min(\alpha,\beta)/(1+2\alpha+2p)}$, meaning that for every $M_\epsilon\to\infty$ the expected posterior mass outside radius $M_\epsilon r_\epsilon$ tends to zero as $\epsilon\downarrow0$.

[F7] The standard coordinate basis makes $H=\ell^2$ a separable real Hilbert space. For the diagonal covariance, positivity and self-adjointness follow from $\langle\Gamma x,x\rangle=\sum_j\tau_j^2x_j^2\ge0$ and $\langle\Gamma x,y\rangle=\langle x,\Gamma y\rangle$. Finite-rank truncations converge in operator norm, so $\Gamma$ is compact; its diagonal rank-one expansion has nuclear sum $\sum_j\tau_j^2<\infty$, so it is trace class. [[thm-hilbert-space-with-a-given-orthonormal-basis-is-ell-two-of-the-index-set]], [[def-separable-space]], [[lem-finite-rank-operators-are-compact]], [[thm-norm-limit-of-compact-operators-is-compact]], [[lem-nuclear-series-characterizes-trace-norm]]

[F8] A positive self-adjoint trace-class covariance on a separable real Hilbert space defines a Borel centered Hilbert-valued Gaussian random element with that covariance. [[lem-positive-trace-class-covariance-defines-hilbert-gaussian]]

[F9] A finite vector is multivariate normal when all its linear projections are normal. [[def-multivariate-normal-law]]

[F10] Finite jointly Gaussian blocks with zero cross-covariance are independent, including for singular covariance matrices. [[lem-uncorrelated-jointly-gaussian-blocks-are-independent]]

[F11] The notation $N(m,\sigma^2)$ denotes the law of a normal variable with mean $m$ and variance $\sigma^2$. [[def-standard-normal-and-normal-laws]]

**Given:** The hypotheses of the Example and facts [A1], [F1]–[F10].

contract.heading: Statement refuted
contract.text: Assume AC and Countable Choice. In every positive-noise Gaussian sequence inverse experiment, every proper centered Gaussian prior on $\ell^2$ yields posterior contraction at some rate $r_\epsilon\to0$ about every truth $\theta^\dagger\in\ell^2$, including truths for which the prior gives zero mass to every ball of radius less than $1$ centered at $\theta^\dagger$.

facts:
**Given:** AC and Countable Choice; the positive-noise sequence inverse experiment; its standard basis vector $e_1=(1,0,0,\ldots)$; and the posterior contraction definition.

[A1] AC and Countable Choice are assumed by the Gaussian sequence model and its product-law theorem. [[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]

[F1] The data coordinates are $Y_j=s_j\theta_j+\epsilon\xi_j$ with positive $s_j$ and independent standard-normal noise. [[def-ip-gaussian-sequence-inverse-model]]

[F2] The conjugate contraction theorem assumes $\tau_j>0$ and $\sum_j\tau_j^2<\infty$; its conclusion is not stated for every Gaussian prior without those hypotheses. [[thm-ip-conjugate-gaussian-sequence-contraction]]

[F3] The law $N(0,0)$ is the point mass $\delta_0$. [[def-standard-normal-and-normal-laws]]

[F4] A nondegenerate finite-dimensional Gaussian with covariance $\epsilon^2 I$ has density proportional to $\exp(-\|y-m\|_2^2/(2\epsilon^2))$. [[thm-nondegenerate-multivariate-normal-law-has-density]]

[F5] Finite measures agreeing on a generating cylinder $\pi$-system and on the whole space agree on the generated product Borel sigma-algebra. [[lem-finite-measure-uniqueness-on-a-pi-system]]

[F6] The real exponential is strictly positive. [[cor-exponential-reciprocal-and-positivity]]

[F7] The posterior contraction condition requires the expected posterior mass outside every diverging multiple of a rate to tend to zero under the fixed-truth data law. [[def-ip-posterior-contraction-rate]]

contract.heading: Open problem
contract.text:
Assume AC and Countable Choice. Fix $p>0$, $C\ge1$, $0<\beta_-<\beta_+<A<\infty$, $R\ge1$, $L_0\ge1$, an integer $N_0\ge1$, $\rho\ge2$, $m\in(0,R]$, and $0<\gamma<1$. Let a known positive singular-value sequence satisfy $C^{-2}i^{-2p}\le\kappa_i^2\le C^2i^{-2p}$, and observe $X_i=\kappa_i\theta_i+n^{-1/2}\xi_i$ for $i\ge1$, where the fixed truth $\theta=(\theta_i)\in\ell^2(\mathbb N,\mathbb R)$ and the $\xi_i$ are independent $N(0,1)$ variables. For $\alpha>0$, use the product prior $\Pi_\alpha=\bigotimes_{i\ge1}N(0,i^{-1-2\alpha})$ and its product Gaussian posterior with coordinate mean $n\kappa_iX_i/(i^{1+2\alpha}+n\kappa_i^2)$ and variance $(i^{1+2\alpha}+n\kappa_i^2)^{-1}$. Select $\widehat\alpha_n$ as a Borel global maximizer over $[0,A]$ of the marginal log-likelihood score
$$\ell_n(\alpha;X)=-\frac12\sum_{i\ge1}\left[\log\left(1+\frac{n\kappa_i^2}{i^{1+2\alpha}}\right)-\frac{n^2\kappa_i^2X_i^2}{i^{1+2\alpha}+n\kappa_i^2}\right],$$
assuming the score series is finite on a Borel data domain of probability one for the truths below and is upper semicontinuous in $\alpha$ there. The $\widehat\alpha_n=0$ branch uses the whole space $\ell^2$ and asserts no posterior probability on $\ell^2$.

For $\theta\in\ell^2$, write $\|\theta\|_2=(\sum_{i\ge1}\theta_i^2)^{1/2}$. For $B\subseteq\ell^2$, define $\operatorname{diam}_{\ell^2}(B)=\sup_{u,v\in B}\|u-v\|_2$, with $\operatorname{diam}_{\ell^2}(\varnothing)=0$.

For $\beta\in[\beta_-,\beta_+]$, let $\Theta_\beta(R)=\{\theta\in\ell^2:\sum_{i\ge1}i^{2\beta}\theta_i^2\le R^2\}$ and let $\Theta_{\mathrm{pt}}(L_0,N_0,\rho)$ consist of those $\theta\in\ell^2$ satisfying $\sum_{i=N}^{\infty}\theta_i^2\le L_0\sum_{i=N}^{\lfloor\rho N\rfloor}\theta_i^2$ for every integer $N\ge N_0$. Put $\mathcal G_\beta=\Theta_\beta(R)\cap\Theta_{\mathrm{pt}}(L_0,N_0,\rho)\cap\{\theta:\theta_1=0,\ \|\theta\|_2\ge m\}$ and assume the fixed constants make each $\mathcal G_\beta$ nonempty. Does there exist a single graph-measurable data-indexed set rule $C_{n,\gamma}(X)\subseteq\ell^2$, depending only on the known model and class constants and not on $\theta$ or $\beta$, such that on $\widehat\alpha_n>0$ it has posterior mass $\Pi_{\widehat\alpha_n}(C_{n,\gamma}(X)\mid X)\ge1-\gamma$, its uniform frequentist coverage satisfies
$$\sup_{\beta\in[\beta_-,\beta_+]}\sup_{\theta\in\mathcal G_\beta}\left|P_\theta^{(n)}\{\theta\in C_{n,\gamma}(X)\}-(1-\gamma)\right|\longrightarrow0,$$
and its $\ell^2$-diameter has the no-log rate $n^{-\beta/(1+2\beta+2p)}$ uniformly in the following sense: for every $\eta>0$ there is $K_\eta<\infty$ such that
$$\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{\beta\in[\beta_-,\beta_+]}\sup_{\theta\in\mathcal G_\beta}P_\theta^{(n)}\left\{\operatorname{diam}_{\ell^2}(C_{n,\gamma}(X))>K_\eta n^{-\beta/(1+2\beta+2p)}\right\}\le\eta?$$

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $H$ be a separable real Hilbert space, let
$\mu_0$ be a centered Borel Gaussian probability measure on $H$, let
$D\subseteq H$ be Borel with $\mu_0(D)=1$, and let
$\Phi_D:D\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ be Borel. Assume the evidence
$$
Z:=\int_D e^{-\Phi_D(u)}\,\mu_0(du)
$$
satisfies $0<Z<\infty$. Extend the potential to all of $H$ by setting
$\bar\Phi(u)=\Phi_D(u)$ for $u\in D$ and $\bar\Phi(u)=+\infty$ for
$u\notin D$, and define the target probability
$\mu(du)=Z^{-1}e^{-\bar\Phi(u)}\mu_0(du)$. For a scale $\beta\in[0,1]$,
write $\rho=\sqrt{1-\beta^2}$. At state $u\in H$, draw $\xi\sim\mu_0$
independently and propose $v=\rho u+\beta\xi$. Set the acceptance probability
to $0$ if either $\bar\Phi(u)$ or $\bar\Phi(v)$ is $+\infty$, and otherwise set
$$
\alpha(u,v)=\min\{1,\exp(\bar\Phi(u)-\bar\Phi(v))\}.
$$
Draw an independent uniform random variable on $[0,1]$ and move to $v$ if it
is at most $\alpha(u,v)$; otherwise remain at $u$. The resulting one-step
transition rule is the prior-preserving Crank–Nicolson, or pCN, rule
$P_\beta$. States with infinite potential are absorbing under this total
definition; they have $\mu$-measure zero.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $H$ be a separable real Hilbert space and let
$\mu_0$ be a centered Borel Gaussian probability measure on $H$. Let
$\Phi:H\to[0,\infty)$ be finite-valued and Borel measurable. Suppose that
there are constants $p,K>0$ such that
$$0\le\Phi(u)\le K(1+\|u\|^p)\qquad(u\in H),$$
and for every $R>0$ there is a finite $L_R$ such that
$$|\Phi(u)-\Phi(v)|\le L_R\|u-v\|\quad\text{whenever }\max\{\|u\|,\|v\|\}<R.$$
Set $Z=\int_H e^{-\Phi(u)}\,\mu_0(du)$ and
$\mu(du)=Z^{-1}e^{-\Phi(u)}\mu_0(du)$. For $\beta\in[0,1]$, let
$U\sim\mu$ and $\xi\sim\mu_0$ be independent, put
$V_\beta=\sqrt{1-\beta^2}U+\beta\xi$, and define
$$\alpha_\beta=\min\{1,\exp(\Phi(U)-\Phi(V_\beta))\}.$$
Then $0<Z<\infty$, $\mu$ is a probability measure, and the stationary mean
acceptance satisfies
$$\lim_{\beta\downarrow0}\mathbb E[\alpha_\beta]=1.$$

facts:
**Given:** The hypotheses in the Statement.

[A1] AC is assumed, as required by the centered Borel Gaussian interface and the pCN algorithm. [[def-axiom-of-choice]] [[alg-ip-prior-preserving-crank-nicolson]]

[F1] The pCN proposal is $V_\beta=\sqrt{1-\beta^2}U+\beta\xi$, and its acceptance for finite potential values is $\min\{1,\exp(\Phi(U)-\Phi(V_\beta))\}$. [[alg-ip-prior-preserving-crank-nicolson]]

[F2] A prior on a full-mass Borel forward domain and a finite continuous potential with a common integrable lower envelope have positive finite evidence and a normalized posterior. [[def-ip-prior-on-a-forward-domain]] [[def-ip-misfit-evidence-and-posterior-law]] [[thm-ip-function-space-posterior-propriety]]

[F3] A centered Borel Gaussian random element in a separable Banach space has $\mathbb E e^{a\|X\|^2}<\infty$ for some $a>0$; a centered Borel Gaussian probability on $H$ is realized by the identity random element on $(H,\mathcal B(H),\mu_0)$. [[def-borel-gaussian-random-element-on-a-separable-banach-space]] [[thm-fernique-integrability-for-separable-banach-gaussian-law]]

[F4] If a nonnegative measurable function has integral zero, it vanishes almost everywhere; integrating on a measurable set is integrating its indicator times the function. [[thm-nonnegative-integral-zero-iff-zero-almost-everywhere]] [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]]

[F5] If measurable functions converge pointwise and are dominated in absolute value by one integrable function, their integrals converge to the integral of the pointwise limit. [[thm-dominated-convergence]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the inputs of the prior-preserving
Crank–Nicolson algorithm: a separable real Hilbert space $H$, centered Borel
Gaussian reference probability $\mu_0$, full-mass Borel domain $D$, Borel
potential $\Phi_D:D\to(-\infty,+\infty]$, positive finite evidence $Z$, and
scale $\beta\in[0,1]$. Let $\mu$ be the normalized target on $H$ obtained by
extending $\Phi_D$ by $+\infty$ off $D$, and let $P_\beta$ be the algorithm's
accept-reject transition. Then $P_\beta$ is reversible with respect to $\mu$:
its joint flow
$$\Lambda_\beta(C):=\int_H P_\beta(u,C_u)\,\mu(du),\qquad C_u:=\{v\in H:(u,v)\in C\},$$
is unchanged by $(u,v)\mapsto(v,u)$ for every Borel
$C\subseteq H\times H$. Consequently, $\mu$ is invariant:
$$\int_H P_\beta(u,A)\,\mu(du)=\mu(A)\qquad(A\in\mathcal B(H)).$$
This conclusion gives invariance only; it does not assert uniqueness,
convergence, mixing, an effective-sample-size bound, mesh-independent cost,
or correctness of an approximate forward solver.

facts:
**Given:** The algorithm inputs in the Statement.

[A1] The Axiom of Choice and the algorithm's full-mass domain, potential extension, evidence, target density, proposal, and acceptance convention. [[def-axiom-of-choice]] [[alg-ip-prior-preserving-crank-nicolson]]

[F1] The proposal rule $Q_\beta$ and accept-reject rule $P_\beta$ are Borel probability kernels; for each $u$,
$$Q_\beta(u,B)=\int_H\mathbf1_B(\rho u+\beta z)\,\mu_0(dz),\qquad P_\beta(u,A)=\int_A\alpha(u,v)Q_\beta(u,dv)+\mathbf1_A(u)(1-a(u)),$$
where $a(u)=\int_H\alpha(u,v)Q_\beta(u,dv)$. [[lem-ip-pcn-transition-kernel-is-measurable]]

[F2] If $w(u)=e^{-\bar\Phi(u)}$, then $\mu(du)=Z^{-1}w(u)\mu_0(du)$, $w(u)=0$ when $\bar\Phi(u)=+\infty$, and $\alpha(u,v)=0$ if either potential is infinite. [[alg-ip-prior-preserving-crank-nicolson]] [[def-ip-misfit-evidence-and-posterior-law]]

[F3] For $U_0,\xi$ independent with law $\mu_0$ and $V_0=\rho U_0+\beta\xi$, the joint Borel law of $(U_0,V_0)$ is symmetric under coordinate swap; on the separable Hilbert product, the Borel sigma-algebra equals the product sigma-algebra. [[lem-ip-pcn-reference-pair-law-is-symmetric]] [[lem-borel-product-of-second-countable-spaces]]

[F4] A prior and probability kernel define a joint flow probability measure with the rectangle formula and nonnegative iterated-integral identity. [[lem-prior-and-model-kernel-define-joint-law]] [[def-measure-kernel-and-probability-kernel]] [[def-probability-measure]]

[F5] Equality of probability laws is preserved under measurable changes of variables, and integration against a law equals expectation of the corresponding random-element function. [[def-law-or-distribution-of-a-random-element]] [[thm-change-of-variables-for-expectation]]

[F6] The product of two probability measures exists and has the rectangle formula; the rectangle criterion then makes its coordinate projections independent random elements. [[thm-sigma-finite-product-measure-exists-is-rectangular-and-is-unique]] [[thm-rectangle-criterion-for-independent-random-elements]] [[def-independent-random-elements]] [[def-product-sigma-algebra-and-finite-product-sigma-algebras]]

[F7] A probability kernel is reversible with respect to a probability measure when its joint flow equals its coordinate transpose; this definition requires no density. [[def-general-state-reversibility-by-symmetric-flow-measure]]

[F8] Reversibility with respect to a probability measure implies its invariance. [[thm-general-state-reversibility-implies-invariance]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Let $H=\ell^2(\mathbb N,\mathbb R)$ with its canonical real inner product, and for each $j\in\mathbb N$ let $e_j$ be the sequence whose $j$th coordinate is $1$ and whose other coordinates are $0$. Then $(e_j)_{j\in\mathbb N}$ is a complete orthonormal basis of $H$. For every $x=(x_j)\in H$, the truncations $\sum_{j=1}^N x_je_j$ converge in $H$ to $x$, and $\|x\|_2^2=\sum_{j\in\mathbb N}|x_j|^2$.

facts:
**Given:** The real sequence Hilbert space $H=\ell^2(\mathbb N,\mathbb R)$ and the coordinate vectors $(e_j)$.

[F1] Square summability means $\sum_j|x_j|^2<\infty$, the norm squared is that sum, and finite tails of the sum can be made arbitrarily small. [[def-square-summable-family-on-an-arbitrary-index-set]]

[F2] The canonical inner product makes real $\ell^2(\mathbb N)$ a complete real Hilbert space. [[lem-square-summable-sequences-form-a-hilbert-space]]

[F3] An orthonormal family is a Hilbert basis when its closed linear span is the whole Hilbert space. [[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]

contract.heading: Statement refuted
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and fix $\beta\in(0,1]$. Let
$H=\ell^2(\mathbb N,\mathbb R)$ with its canonical basis $(e_j)$. Take
mutually independent standard normal variables $(X_j,Y_j)_{j\ge1}$ and set
$$U=\sum_{j\ge1}2^{-j/2}X_je_j,\qquad \xi=\sum_{j\ge1}2^{-j/2}Y_je_j.$$
These series converge almost surely in $H$ and define independent centered
Borel Gaussian random elements with the same law $\mu_0$. Define the Gaussian
random-walk proposal $V=U+\beta\xi$, its probability kernel
$$Q_\beta(u,B)=\mu_0(\{z\in H:u+\beta z\in B\}),$$
its forward flow $\eta(du,dv)=\mu_0(du)Q_\beta(u,dv)$, and its transpose
$\eta^\top(C)=\eta(\{(u,v):(v,u)\in C\})$. Then $\eta$ and $\eta^\top$ are
mutually singular: a Borel set $A_\beta\subseteq H\times H$ satisfies
$$\eta(A_\beta)=1,\qquad \eta^\top(A_\beta)=0.$$
For the same reference law and scale, the pCN proposal flow is symmetric.

facts:
**Given:** AC, $\beta\in(0,1]$, and the Gaussian sequence and Hilbert-space notation of the Statement.

[A1] AC implies both Dependent Choice and Countable Choice. [[def-axiom-of-choice]] [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]

[F1] Under Countable Choice and Dependent Choice, a countable independent sequence with the standard normal law exists. [[def-countable-choice]] [[def-dependent-choice]] [[cor-countable-independent-copies-exist]]

[F2] The coordinate vectors form a complete orthonormal basis of $H$, and the norm squared is the sum of coordinate squares. [[lem-ip-coordinate-vectors-form-a-basis-of-ell-two]]

[F3] For independent standard normal coordinates and weights $\lambda_j=2^{-j}$, the series $\sum_j\sqrt{\lambda_j}X_je_j$ converges almost surely in $H$ and defines a centered Borel Gaussian random element. Its coordinates are $2^{-j/2}X_j$. [[lem-ip-gaussian-series-prior-regularity]] [[lem-ip-coordinate-vectors-form-a-basis-of-ell-two]]

[F4] Disjoint subfamilies of an independent family generate independent sigma-algebras, and measurable functions of independent random elements remain independent. [[def-independent-random-elements]] [[thm-grouping-independent-sigma-algebras]] [[lem-measurable-functions-preserve-independence]]

[F5] A $N(0,1)$ variable has mean zero, second moment one, and fourth moment three. [[lem-normal-location-scale-mean-and-variance]] [[lem-standard-normal-fourth-moment]]

[F6] Expectations of integrable products of independent variables factor. [[thm-factorization-of-expectations-for-independent-variables]]

[F7] IID square-integrable real variables satisfy the strong law of large numbers. [[def-identically-distributed-and-iid-random-variables]] [[cor-iid-finite-variance-strong-law]]

[F8] For a probability measure and a probability kernel, the associated joint flow is a probability measure with the iterated-integral identity. [[def-measure-kernel-and-probability-kernel]] [[lem-prior-and-model-kernel-define-joint-law]]

[F9] Integrating a Borel function against a random-element law equals its expectation; independent random elements have product joint law. [[def-law-or-distribution-of-a-random-element]] [[thm-change-of-variables-for-expectation]] [[thm-independent-random-elements-have-product-joint-law]]

[F10] The Borel sigma-algebra of a topological space is generated by its open sets; Borel measurable functions are closed under finite arithmetic operations. [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]] [[thm-arithmetic-and-lattice-operations-preserve-measurability]]

[F11] The Borel sigma-algebra on a product of second-countable spaces is the product sigma-algebra, and integrating a nonnegative product-measurable function against a probability kernel gives a measurable function of its source point. [[lem-borel-product-of-second-countable-spaces]] [[thm-measurability-of-integration-against-a-kernel]] [[thm-continuous-preimages-of-borel-sets-are-borel]]

[F12] For the same Gaussian reference law and $\beta\in[0,1]$, the pCN proposal pair law is symmetric. [[lem-ip-pcn-reference-pair-law-is-symmetric]]

[F13] Under Countable Choice, Borel probability laws on a separable Hilbert space with the same finite coordinate laws in a complete orthonormal basis are equal. [[def-countable-choice]] [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]] [[lem-ip-separable-hilbert-borel-laws-determined-by-orthonormal-coordinates]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\pi$ be a probability measure on $\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^m$, where $d,m\ge1$, and let $\pi_Y(B):=\pi(\mathbb R^d\times B)$ be its second marginal. Let $\eta$ be a probability measure on $\mathbb R^d$, and let $y\mapsto\pi_y$ be a probability kernel satisfying
$$\pi(A\times B)=\int_B\pi_y(A)\,\pi_Y(dy)$$
for all Borel $A\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ and $B\subseteq\mathbb R^m$. Suppose $T:\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^m$ is Borel and triangular, $T(x,y)=(T_y(x),y)$, with each $T_y$ a Borel bijection, and define the image measure by $T_{\#}\mu(E):=\mu(T^{-1}(E))$. If
$$T_{\#}(\eta\otimes\pi_Y)=\pi,$$
then $T_y{}_{\#}\eta=\pi_y$ as probability measures for $\pi_Y$-almost every $y$. By disintegration on standard Borel spaces, such a kernel $\pi_y$ exists and is unique outside one $\pi_Y$-null set. In a proper Bayesian model, when $\pi$ is the joint parameter/data law, this conditional kernel is the posterior kernel; the conclusion says an exact triangular transport maps the reference law to the data-conditioned posterior for almost every datum.

For the triangular terminal flow in the preceding ODE lemma, joint continuity supplies the Borel map and each fiber is a bijection. The theorem requires only the exact joint pushforward identity; it does not require a density or a Jacobian formula.

facts:
**Given:** The Axiom of Choice, the joint law $\pi$, its second marginal $\pi_Y$, the reference probability $\eta$, the supplied probability kernel $\pi_y$, and the Borel triangular map and exact joint pushforward identity in the Statement.

[A1] Assume the Axiom of Choice for standard-Borel disintegration existence and simultaneous almost-everywhere uniqueness. [[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[thm-disintegration-of-a-joint-law-on-standard-borel-spaces]]

[F1] Finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces with their Borel sigma-algebras are standard Borel. [[lem-finite-euclidean-space-is-standard-borel]]

[F2] For a probability measure on a product of standard-Borel spaces, a probability-kernel disintegration satisfies the rectangle identity and is unique outside one common marginal-null set. The theorem also gives the corresponding iterated-integral identity for nonnegative product-measurable functions. [[thm-disintegration-of-a-joint-law-on-standard-borel-spaces]]

[F3] A probability kernel has a probability-measure section at every parameter, and each fixed-set evaluation is measurable in the parameter. [[def-measure-kernel-and-probability-kernel]]

[F4] Borel coordinate maps and finite coordinate permutations are measurable for the relevant finite-product Borel sigma-algebras, which agree with the product sigma-algebras. [[def-product-sigma-algebra-and-finite-product-sigma-algebras]], [[def-measurable-function-between-measurable-spaces]], [[lem-coordinate-maps-and-permutations-are-measurable-on-finite-products]]

[F5] Integrating a nonnegative product-measurable function against a probability kernel gives a measurable function of the parameter. [[thm-measurability-of-integration-against-a-kernel]]

[F6] The product of probability measures has the rectangle formula, and Tonelli identifies its nonnegative integral with either iterated integral. [[thm-sigma-finite-product-measure-exists-is-rectangular-and-is-unique]], [[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]

[F7] Under Countable Choice and Dependent Choice, the stated ODE hypotheses give a jointly continuous triangular terminal flow with bijective fibers; the optional C$^1$ density clause is separate. [[lem-ip-lipschitz-ode-triangular-flow-and-c1-density]]

[F8] In a proper Bayesian model on standard-Borel parameter and data spaces, the data-indexed conditional posterior kernel is a version of the posterior and is unique as a probability measure outside one data-marginal-null set. [[def-ip-misfit-evidence-and-posterior-law]]

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $d,m,n,B\ge1$, let $\eta$ be a reference probability on $\mathbb R^d$, and let $\pi$ be the proper joint law of an unknown $X_1\in\mathbb R^d$ and data $Y\in\mathbb R^m$ in a specified Bayesian inverse model. Write $\pi_Y$ for the data marginal and $\pi_y$ for a posterior-kernel version of the conditional law of $X_1$ given $Y=y$. Assume
$$\int_{\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^m}|x_1|^2\,\pi(dx_1,dy)+\int_{\mathbb R^d}|x_0|^2\,\eta(dx_0)<\infty.$$

Choose a jointly measurable parameterized vector-field family $v_\theta:[0,1]\times\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^d$ whose candidates have finite population squared loss. For $i=1,\ldots,n$, draw independent triples
$$(t_i,X_{0i},(X_{1i},Y_i))\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\otimes\eta\otimes\pi,$$
where $\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]$ is Lebesgue probability on the unit interval, and set
$$X_{t_i}=(1-t_i)X_{0i}+t_iX_{1i},\qquad V_i=X_{1i}-X_{0i}.$$
Fit the field by minimizing, over the chosen model class, the empirical squared regression loss
$$\widehat{\mathcal L}_n(\theta)=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\bigl|v_\theta(t_i,X_{t_i},Y_i)-V_i\bigr|^2.$$
Declare a finite maximum optimizer-step budget $M$, a tolerance $\varepsilon_{\rm opt}>0$, and a named stopping statistic $S$ computed from the finite training objective. Stop with status **converged** when $S\le\varepsilon_{\rm opt}$; return **budget-exhausted** if $M$ steps are used first and **failed** if the objective or optimizer becomes nonfinite. The optimizer returns the fitted field $\widehat v$, achieved training loss, value of $S$, tolerance, step budget and status; this finite-data stopping rule does not certify $\widehat v=v^*$.
The population least-squares target is the conditional-expectation class
$$v^*(t,x,y)=\mathbb E[X_1-X_0\mid\sigma(t,X_t,Y)]$$
coordinatewise, evaluated at $(t,x,y)$ through a chosen measurable representative. A conditional expectation is only an almost-sure equivalence class, so this formula does not specify an off-support pointwise extension.

For a query datum $y$, check all hypotheses of the cited ODE flow lemma, including joint continuity of the fitted field and its integrable global spatial-Lipschitz and origin-growth bounds on compact data-parameter sets containing $y$. If this check fails, return a field-regularity failure status. Otherwise draw $B$ independent initial states $Z_0^j\sim\eta$ and give each to a declared numerical ODE solver with a finite step or tolerance budget for
$$\dot Z_t^j=\widehat v(t,Z_t^j,y),\qquad Z_0^j\sim\eta.$$
Return terminal approximations only for successful integrations, together with the field, optimizer and solver statuses and any certified solver error estimate. Return a failure status for an integration that does not meet its declared stopping rule. If the exact triangular flow of $\widehat v$ were known to satisfy $T_{\#}(\eta\otimes\pi_Y)=\pi$, the exact transport theorem would imply $T_y{}_{\#}\eta=\pi_y$ for $\pi_Y$-almost every $y$; finite regression loss, optimizer termination, and solver success alone do not establish this joint pushforward identity or exact posterior sampling.

Record posterior model, discretization, kernel, burn-in, Monte Carlo and solver components under the declared posterior-computation error budget when applicable. The budget does not supply a learned-flow regression or optimizer-error estimate; report those as separate measured or certified quantities, and mark unavailable quantities unquantified rather than zero.

facts:
**Given:** AC; proper joint posterior law $\pi$ on finite-dimensional unknown/data spaces; independent reference law $\eta$; finite second moments; a chosen measurable vector-field family with finite squared population loss; finite optimizer and ODE budgets; and a numerical solver that returns either an endpoint or an explicit status.

[A1] AC is assumed for the conditional-expectation projection and standard-Borel posterior-kernel interfaces. Its implications include Countable Choice and Dependent Choice for the flow lemma. [[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]], [[thm-conditional-expectation-is-the-l2-orthogonal-projection]], [[def-ip-misfit-evidence-and-posterior-law]]

[F1] In a proper Bayesian model, $\pi$ is the joint unknown/data law and $\pi_y$ is a version of the posterior conditional law; values on a $\pi_Y$-null set are not fixed by the conditional identity. [[def-ip-misfit-evidence-and-posterior-law]], [[def-conditional-law-given-a-random-element]]

[F2] For a square-integrable target, the conditional expectation given $\sigma(t,X_t,Y)$ is the unique $L^2$ minimizer of the population squared prediction loss, coordinatewise. [[def-conditional-expectation-given-a-sigma-algebra]], [[thm-conditional-expectation-is-the-l2-orthogonal-projection]]

[F3] Under AC, a conditional expectation given a random element in a standard Borel space has a measurable representative as a function of that conditioning element; the identity with the conditional expectation holds almost surely. [[cor-conditional-expectation-as-a-measurable-function-of-the-conditioning-variable]], [[lem-finite-euclidean-space-is-standard-borel]]

[F4] Independent sampling from $\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]$, $\eta$, and $\pi$ gives the stated product training law; product probabilities have the rectangle formula, and the expectation of a finite sum of integrable losses is the sum of their expectations. [[thm-sigma-finite-product-measure-exists-is-rectangular-and-is-unique]], [[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]]

[F5] A fitted field satisfying the integrable spatial-Lipschitz and origin-growth assumptions has a unique global flow and a continuous terminal map; these facts do not certify that its output law is the target. [[lem-ip-lipschitz-ode-triangular-flow-and-c1-density]]

[F6] If the exact triangular terminal map has joint pushforward $\pi$, its exact conditional fibers push $\eta$ to $\pi_y$ for $\pi_Y$-almost every datum; this needs the joint identity as a separate hypothesis. [[thm-ip-exact-triangular-transport-disintegrates-to-posterior]]

[F7] The six-term posterior-computation budget is a telescoping ledger and supplies no learned-flow regression or optimizer bound. [[def-ip-posterior-computation-error-budget]]

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Fix a measurable space $(E,\mathcal E)$ and a bounded measurable functional
$f:E\to\mathbb R$, with $\|f\|_\infty:=\sup_{x\in E}|f(x)|<\infty$. All
target laws below are probability measures on this same space. If a model or
discretization originally uses another state space, specify its measurable
embedding into $E$ and compare its pushforward law; no identification of
different state spaces is implicit. A **posterior law** here is the probability
law for the unknown at the specified computation stage, conditional on the same
fixed observed data. For a probability law $\mu$, write
$\mu(f):=\int_E f\,d\mu$.

Name the successive posterior laws as follows: $\mu_\star$ is the intended
target; $\mu_{\rm model}$ is the posterior under the selected statistical or
physical model; $\mu_{\rm solver}$ is the posterior after replacing the exact
forward or PDE solution by the declared numerical solver output; and
$\mu_{\rm disc}$ is the posterior after the declared finite-dimensional
discretization. These labels refer to the exact adjacent laws recorded for the
computation, even when two stages happen to agree.

Let $K$ be the implemented probability kernel on $(E,\mathcal E)$. An
**invariant law** $\pi_K$ for $K$ is a probability measure satisfying
$$\int_E K(x,A)\,\pi_K(dx)=\pi_K(A)\qquad(A\in\mathcal E).$$
Choose and report which invariant law is used if $K$ has more than one. If no
invariant law has been established, the invariant-kernel and burn-in terms
below are unavailable; they are not set to zero. Let $(X_n)_{n\ge0}$ be a
time-homogeneous Markov chain with transition kernel $K$ relative to its
natural filtration, with initial probability law $\lambda$. For burn-in length
$b\ge0$ and retained sample size $N\ge1$, set
$$\bar f_{b,N}:=\frac1N\sum_{j=1}^N f(X_{b+j}),$$
and let $\mathbb E_\lambda$ denote expectation under this initial law and the
chain's transition randomness.

When all stages are present, define the component errors
$$\begin{aligned}\delta_{\rm model}&:=|\mu_\star(f)-\mu_{\rm model}(f)|,\\ \delta_{\rm solver}&:=|\mu_{\rm model}(f)-\mu_{\rm solver}(f)|,\\ \delta_{\rm disc}&:=|\mu_{\rm solver}(f)-\mu_{\rm disc}(f)|,\\ \delta_K&:=|\mu_{\rm disc}(f)-\pi_K(f)|,\\ \delta_{\rm burn}&:=|\pi_K(f)-\mathbb E_\lambda\bar f_{b,N}|,\\ \delta_{\rm MC}&:=|\mathbb E_\lambda\bar f_{b,N}-\bar f_{b,N}|.\end{aligned}$$
The last component is random and the earlier components are fixed for the
declared data and computation. The **posterior computation error budget** is
$$\mathcal B_f:=\delta_{\rm model}+\delta_{\rm solver}+\delta_{\rm disc}+\delta_K+\delta_{\rm burn}+\delta_{\rm MC}.$$
If a computation stops before one of these stages, report the shorter reference
chain and its component terms. The term $\delta_K$ measures the invariant-law
discrepancy induced by the implemented transition rule; it is not a one-step
distance between kernels. A one-step kernel error cannot replace it without a
separate perturbation theorem with its own hypotheses.

The successive scalar references are arranged as this directed error chain;
each arrow is labelled by the absolute difference of its endpoints.

```tikzcd
\mu_\star(f) \arrow[r, "\delta_{\rm model}"] &
\mu_{\rm model}(f) \arrow[r, "\delta_{\rm solver}"] &
\mu_{\rm solver}(f) \arrow[r, "\delta_{\rm disc}"] &
\mu_{\rm disc}(f) \arrow[r, "\delta_K"] &
\pi_K(f) \arrow[r, "\delta_{\rm burn}"] &
\mathbb E_\lambda\bar f_{b,N} \arrow[r, "\delta_{\rm MC}"] &
\bar f_{b,N}
```

The budget is a bookkeeping bound only when its components are supplied with
estimators or verified bounds; an unavailable component is reported as
unquantified rather than silently set to zero. In particular, invariance alone
does not provide a burn-in estimate, a mixing rate, or a Monte Carlo error
estimate.

contract.heading: Open problem
contract.text:
Let $\mathcal H$ be a separable real Hilbert space, let $K\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be compact, and let $y\mapsto\Pi^y$ be the pointwise potential posterior of a proper Bayesian inverse model, with positive finite evidence and finite second moment for every $y\in K$. Let $P_n$ be finite-rank orthogonal projections on $\mathcal H$ with $P_nx\to x$ for every $x\in\mathcal H$, let $\mathcal H_n=P_n\mathcal H$, and let $\Pi_n^y$ be proper posteriors defined by declared finite-rank forward/potential approximations on $\mathcal H_n$, with finite second moments for every $y\in K$. Write $i_n:\mathcal H_n\hookrightarrow\mathcal H$ for inclusion and define the posterior model error
$$e_{\mathrm{post},n}:=\sup_{y\in K}W_{2,\mathcal H}(i_{n\#}\Pi_n^y,\Pi^y),$$
where $W_{2,\mathcal H}(\mu,\nu)$ is the infimum, over joint laws with marginals $\mu,\nu$, of the square root of the expected squared Hilbert distance. This term includes both posterior-potential and finite-rank model error; the known Hellinger potential/discretization estimates would need an explicit moment or tail argument to control it in $W_2$.

Let $\pi$ be the prior-predictive joint law of $(X_1,Y)$, let $\eta$ be an independent reference probability on $\mathcal H$ with finite second moment, and use the product training law $\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\otimes\eta\otimes\pi$. Let $X_t=(1-t)X_0+tX_1$ and let $v^*(t,X_t,Y)=\mathbb E[X_1-X_0\mid\sigma(t,X_t,Y)]$ be a chosen continuum conditional regression version. For projected endpoints, define
$$v_n^*(t,P_nX_t,Y)=\mathbb E[P_n(X_1-X_0)\mid\sigma(t,P_nX_t,Y)]$$
and the finite-rank conditional-target discrepancy
$$e_{\mathrm{target},n}:=\sup_{y\in K}\left(\int_0^1\mathbb E\!\left[\left\|P_nv^*(t,X_t,y)-v_n^*(t,P_nX_t,y)\right\|_{\mathcal H}^2\mid Y=y\right]dt\right)^{1/2}.$$
The conditional expectation versions at $Y=y$ must be chosen on all $y\in K$ for these suprema. For a measurable vector field $v:\,[0,1]\times\mathcal H_n\times K\to\mathcal H_n$, define its pointwise conditional population loss by
$$\mathcal L_{n,y}(v):=\int_0^1\mathbb E\!\left[\left\|v(t,P_nX_t,y)-P_n(X_1-X_0)\right\|_{\mathcal H}^2\mid Y=y\right]dt,$$
using the selected conditional-law version. For a finite training sample of size $N$, let $\bar v_{n,N}$ be an empirical-risk minimizer in the specified vector-field class, when it exists, and let $\widehat v_{n,N}$ be the output of the declared optimizer. Define the uniform conditional statistical and optimizer excess-risk terms by
$$e_{\mathrm{stat},n,N}^2:=\sup_{y\in K}\left[\mathcal L_{n,y}(\bar v_{n,N})-\inf_{v\in\mathcal V_n}\mathcal L_{n,y}(v)\right],\qquad e_{\mathrm{opt},n,N}^2:=\sup_{y\in K}\left[\mathcal L_{n,y}(\widehat v_{n,N})-\mathcal L_{n,y}(\bar v_{n,N})\right]_+$$
where $\mathcal V_n$ is the chosen class and $\mathcal L_{n,y}$ is its population conditional squared regression loss at datum $y$. Let $e_{\mathrm{solver},n,N,h}$ be a certified $W_2$ coupling bound between the numerical endpoint law at solver budget $h$ and the exact learned-flow endpoint law. Finally, let $\Lambda$ be a proposed bound, uniform in $n$ and $y\in K$, for the time-integrated spatial Lipschitz constants of the learned drifts.

Find checkable assumptions under which the learned finite-rank flow defines a posterior sampler $\widehat\Pi_{n,N,h}^y$ and, for each training realization satisfying explicit risk certificates (or with a stated probability over training data), satisfies a dimension-uniform bound of the form
$$\sup_{y\in K}W_{2,\mathcal H}(i_{n\#}\widehat\Pi_{n,N,h}^y,\Pi^y)\le e_{\mathrm{post},n}+e_{\mathrm{solver},n,N,h}+C e^{\Lambda}\bigl(e_{\mathrm{target},n}+e_{\mathrm{stat},n,N}+e_{\mathrm{opt},n,N}\bigr),$$
with $C$ independent of $n$. The result should derive usable bounds for the posterior model term from the Bayesian potential and discretization hypotheses, establish the uniform-in-$y$ training terms from prior-predictive data, and state the required flow regularity and numerical coupling assumptions. It must not assume that a finite-sample learned field or numerical solver already has the exact joint pushforward property; that property is the conclusion to be certified through the displayed error terms.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $(E,\mathcal E)$ be a measurable space, let $\mu,\nu$ be probability
measures on it, and let $f:E\to\mathbb R$ be measurable with
$|f|\le M$ for some $0\le M<\infty$. Use the library convention
$$\|\mu-\nu\|_{\rm TV}:=\sup_{A\in\mathcal E}|\mu(A)-\nu(A)|.$$
Then
$$|\mu(f)-\nu(f)|\le2M\|\mu-\nu\|_{\rm TV}.$$

For the complete posterior computation error budget defined above, the
pathwise total error satisfies
$$|\mu_\star(f)-\bar f_{b,N}|\le\mathcal B_f.$$
This is a telescoping bound; it does not estimate any component.

Separately, let $(X_n)_{n\ge0}$ be a stationary time-homogeneous Markov chain
with transition kernel $K$, invariant law $\pi_K$, and initial law
$X_0\sim\pi_K$, and use the same bounded functional $f$. Put
$$\gamma_k:=\operatorname{Cov}(f(X_0),f(X_k))\qquad(k\ge0).$$
If $\sum_{k=1}^\infty|\gamma_k|<\infty$, then for every burn-in $b\ge0$ and
sample size $N\ge1$,
$$\mathbb E\left[|\bar f_{b,N}-\pi_K(f)|^2\right]=\frac{1}{N^2}\left[N\gamma_0+2\sum_{k=1}^{N-1}(N-k)\gamma_k\right]\le\frac{\gamma_0+2\sum_{k=1}^\infty|\gamma_k|}{N}.$$
The sample bound assumes stationarity; for a nonstationary start, the budget
keeps $|\pi_K(f)-\mathbb E_\lambda\bar f_{b,N}|$ as a separate burn-in term.
This finite-$N$ variance bound is not a central limit theorem or a confidence
interval.

facts:
**Given:** The hypotheses in the Statement, the complete error budget when its pathwise bound is used, and a stationary Markov chain in the separate sample-error branch.

[F1] Total variation is the event supremum $\sup_{A\in\mathcal E}|\mu(A)-\nu(A)|$; it has no half-factor. [[def-total-variation-distance-for-probability-laws]]

[F2] If $\mu,\nu$ are probability measures and $|f|\le M$, then $|\mu(f)-\nu(f)|\le2M\|\mu-\nu\|_{\rm TV}$. [[thm-total-variation-bounds-for-expectations]]

[F3] The error budget consists of the six absolute adjacent differences from $\mu_\star(f)$ through $\bar f_{b,N}$, and its Monte Carlo component is pathwise. [[def-ip-posterior-computation-error-budget]]

[F4] A stationary chain has marginal law $\pi_K$ at every time, and the covariance of $f(X_i),f(X_j)$ depends only on the lag $|j-i|$. [[def-invariant-and-stationary-distribution-for-a-markov-kernel]] [[def-stationary-process-and-canonical-shift]]

[F5] For square-integrable real random variables, variance is the expected squared centered value and covariance is the expected product of centered values. [[def-moments-variance-and-covariance]]

[F6] For a finite scalar reference chain, the total signed error telescopes and its absolute value is bounded by the sum of absolute adjacent errors. [[thm-pathwise-error-ledger-decomposition]]

[A1] AC is assumed only for the library time-homogeneous Markov-chain interface; this proposition assumes stationarity and makes no chain-existence claim. [[def-axiom-of-choice]] [[def-time-homogeneous-markov-chain-with-transition-kernel]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let a proper prior and forward simulator define a joint prior-predictive law $\pi$ for an unknown $X_1$ and data $Y$. Suppose the available interface can draw independent pairs $(X_1,Y)\sim\pi$ and reference states $X_0\sim\eta$, but supplies neither an evaluable likelihood density $L(x_1;y)$ nor an auxiliary nonnegative random estimate $\widehat L(x_1;y,U)$ with $\mathbb E_U\widehat L(x_1;y,U)=L(x_1;y)$, where the expectation is over auxiliary randomness $U$. Conditional flow matching can train from these joint and reference samples and an independent $t\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]$ using the linear path $X_t=(1-t)X_0+tX_1$ and target velocity $X_1-X_0$, without evaluating $L$. For a fixed query datum, suppose the finite-dimensional prior has density $p_0$ with respect to Lebesgue measure $\lambda$ on $\mathbb R^d$, the reference law $\eta$ has a Lebesgue density, and the learned flow satisfies the separate C$^1$ hypotheses of the ODE lemma, so its proposal has the available density $q_y$ with respect to $\lambda$. Write $\widetilde p_y(x)=p_0(x)L(x;y)$ for the unnormalized posterior density. For pairs with positive forward proposal-flow density $\widetilde p_y(x)q_y(z)$, the density-based independent-Metropolis–Hastings acceptance probability is
$$\alpha_y(x,z)=\min\!\left\{1,\frac{\widetilde p_y(z)q_y(x)}{\widetilde p_y(x)q_y(z)}\right\}.$$
The stated sampling interface does not in general supply this ratio, so it does not by itself give an evaluable density-based correction. In a specified special model the likelihood ratio may cancel or be otherwise known without separate likelihood evaluations; such a case needs no missing likelihood oracle. This example concerns the general limitation of the specified density-based correction; it does not rule out pseudo-marginal correction if an appropriate likelihood estimator is supplied, nor other correction methods with different inputs.

facts:
**Given:** A proper prior-predictive simulator for $\pi$, independent reference sampling from $\eta$, no evaluable likelihood density and no unbiased nonnegative likelihood estimator, and the density-based independent-MH correction specified in the Statement.

[A1] Assume the Axiom of Choice for the posterior-kernel and density-based Metropolis–Hastings interfaces. [[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[lem-metropolis-hastings-density-ratio]]

[F1] Blechschmidt et al. specify that conditional flow matching trains from prior-predictive joint samples and reference draws using a conditional velocity regression objective without evaluating the likelihood. [Blechschmidt et al., §3.2 and Remark 3.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.02377)

[F2] The density-based independent-MH correction requires the unnormalized target posterior density in its target/proposal ratio. [[lem-metropolis-hastings-density-ratio]], [Owen, Chapter 11 §11.4](https://artowen.su.domains/mc/Ch-MCMC.pdf)

[F3] Under the stated dominated model, the unnormalized posterior density is prior density times likelihood; evidence normalization does not remove the likelihood from an MH ratio. [[def-ip-misfit-evidence-and-posterior-law]]

[F4] The C$^1$ flow clause can supply a proposal density by the Jacobian formula, independently of whether the likelihood density is available. [[lem-ip-lipschitz-ode-triangular-flow-and-c1-density]]

[F5] If a distinct exact triangular map satisfies the joint pushforward identity, conditional transport can yield the posterior without evaluating that density; the identity is a separate exactness hypothesis. [[thm-ip-exact-triangular-transport-disintegrates-to-posterior]]

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be real Hilbert spaces and let $U\subseteq X$ be a nonempty open set in the norm topology. A **nonlinear forward model on Hilbert spaces** is a map $F:U\to Y$; no linearity is assumed, and linear maps are allowed as special cases. For $y\in Y$, its exact solution set is

$$S_F(y):=\{x\in U:F(x)=y\}.$$

A point $x^\dagger\in U$ generates the exact datum $y=F(x^\dagger)$. When $F$ is Fréchet differentiable at $x\in U$, write $F'(x):X\to Y$ for its unique bounded real-linear derivative.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text: Let $X$ and $Y$ be real Hilbert spaces, let $D\subseteq X$ be nonempty, and let $F:D\to Y$ be a forward map. The domain $D$ is **weakly closed** when it is closed in the weak topology $\sigma(X,X^*)$, the coarsest topology making every bounded real-linear functional on $X$ continuous. The graph of $F$ is **sequentially weak-to-weak closed** when, for every sequence $(x_n)$ in $D$ and every $x\in X$ and $z\in Y$, the conditions $x_n\rightharpoonup x$ and $F(x_n)\rightharpoonup z$ imply $x\in D$ and $F(x)=z$; here weak convergence means convergence under every bounded real-linear functional on the corresponding Hilbert space. We call $F$ a **weakly closed forward map** when its domain is weakly closed and its graph is sequentially weak-to-weak closed. No linearity, norm continuity, Fréchet differentiability, or convexity is assumed; linear maps are allowed as special cases.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be real Hilbert spaces, let $D\subseteq X$ be a nonempty domain, and let $F:D\to Y$ be a forward map. For a regularization parameter $\alpha>0$, reference element $x_0\in X$, and datum $y\in Y$, the **nonlinear Tikhonov functional** is the map $J_{\alpha,y,x_0}:D\to[0,\infty)$ defined by

$$
J_{\alpha,y,x_0}(x):=\frac12\|F(x)-y\|_Y^2+\frac{\alpha}{2}\|x-x_0\|_X^2\qquad(x\in D).
$$

A **global minimizer** is a point $x_\alpha\in D$ such that $J_{\alpha,y,x_0}(x_\alpha)\le J_{\alpha,y,x_0}(x)$ for every $x\in D$. This definition asserts neither existence nor uniqueness.

contract.heading: Example
contract.text:
Let $X=Y=\mathbb R$ with the usual inner product, let $U=\mathbb R$, and define $F:U\to Y$ by $F(t)=t^2$. Take $x_0=0$, $y=1$, and $\alpha=1$. The domain $U$ is weakly closed and, whenever $t_n$ converges weakly to $t$ and $F(t_n)$ converges weakly to $z$, one has $z=F(t)$; weak convergence means convergence under every bounded real-linear functional. The Tikhonov functional is

$$
J(t)=\frac12(t^2-1)^2+\frac12t^2\qquad(t\in\mathbb R).
$$

It has exactly two distinct global minimizers, $t=1/\sqrt2$ and $t=-1/\sqrt2$.

facts:
**Given:** $X=Y=\mathbb R$ with the standard real inner product and norm, $U=\mathbb R$, $F(t)=t^2$, $x_0=0$, $y=1$, and $\alpha=1$.

[F1] The standard real inner product induces the usual norm, and $\mathbb R$ is complete for it; hence it is a real Hilbert space ([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]], [[thm-reals-cauchy-complete]], [[def-hilbert-space]]).

[F2] Weak convergence is convergence under every bounded real-linear functional; in particular the identity functional shows that weak convergence in $\mathbb R$ implies ordinary convergence ([[def-weak-convergence-of-nets-and-sequences]]).

[F3] A weakly closed forward map has weakly closed domain and sequentially weak-to-weak closed graph ([[def-ip-weakly-closed-nonlinear-forward-map]]).

[F4] The nonlinear Tikhonov functional is $\frac12\|F(t)-y\|^2+\frac{\alpha}{2}\|t-x_0\|^2$ ([[def-ip-nonlinear-tikhonov-functional]]).

[F5] A nonlinear forward map is a map from a nonempty norm-open subset of a real Hilbert space to a real Hilbert space; no linearity is assumed ([[def-ip-nonlinear-forward-map]]).

contract.heading: Example
contract.text:
Assume the ultrafilter lemma, dependent choice, and HB. Give $\Omega=\{0,1\}$ its full sigma-algebra and probability measure $\mu(A)=|A|/2$. For each $s\in\mathbb R$, let $g_s:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be the simple function $g_s(0)=s$, $g_s(1)=s^2$, and define $F(s)=\int_\Omega g_s\,d\mu=(s+s^2)/2$. With $X=Y=D=\mathbb R$ and the usual real Hilbert structure, $D$ is weakly closed and $F$ is nonlinear; if $s_n\rightharpoonup s$ and $F(s_n)\rightharpoonup z$, then $z=F(s)$, where weak convergence in $\mathbb R$ means convergence under every bounded real-linear functional. For every $\alpha>0$, $x_0,y\in\mathbb R$, its Tikhonov functional

$$
J_{\alpha,y,x_0}(s)=\frac12|F(s)-y|^2+\frac{\alpha}{2}|s-x_0|^2
$$

has a global minimizer on $\mathbb R$.

facts:
**Given:** The ultrafilter lemma, DC, and HB; the finite set $\Omega=\{0,1\}$ with $\mu(A)=|A|/2$; the maps $g_s(0)=s$, $g_s(1)=s^2$; and $X=Y=D=\mathbb R$ with the usual real Hilbert structure.

[A1] The ultrafilter lemma extends every filter to an ultrafilter ([[def-ultrafilter-extension-principle]]).

[A2] DC supplies an infinite sequence following an everywhere-extendible relation ([[def-dependent-choice]]).

[A3] HB is the real dominated-extension principle ([[def-hahn-banach-extension-principle-relative]]).

[F1] A measure is zero on the empty set and countably additive on disjoint measurable sets ([[def-measure]]); a measure space consists of a set, sigma-algebra, and measure ([[def-measure-space]]).

[F2] A measurable simple Banach-valued function $g=\sum_jx_j\mathbf1_{A_j}$ with finite-measure nonzero level sets is integrable and has integral $\int g\,d\mu=\sum_j\mu(A_j)x_j$ ([[def-banach-valued-simple-function-and-integral]]).

[F3] An integrable simple Banach-valued function is Bochner integrable, with its Bochner integral equal to the simple integral ([[def-bochner-integrable-function]], [[lem-banach-valued-simple-integral-is-well-defined]]).

[F4] The real numbers with their standard inner product form a real Hilbert space ([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]], [[thm-reals-cauchy-complete]], [[def-hilbert-space]]).

[F5] Weak convergence in a normed space is convergence under every bounded real-linear functional ([[def-weak-convergence-of-nets-and-sequences]]).

[F6] The open-domain nonlinear forward-map interface permits any map $F:U\to Y$ on a nonempty norm-open set, without assuming linearity ([[def-ip-nonlinear-forward-map]]).

[F7] Under the assumptions of [A1]–[A3], a real-Hilbert weakly closed forward map on a nonempty weakly closed domain has a global minimizer for every positive parameter and datum ([[thm-ip-nonlinear-tikhonov-minimizer-exists]]).

[F8] The Tikhonov functional is $\frac12\|F(s)-y\|^2+\frac{\alpha}{2}\|s-x_0\|^2$ on the domain ([[def-ip-nonlinear-tikhonov-functional]]).

[F9] DC implies countable choice, the principle that every countable family of nonempty sets admits a choice function ([[lem-dependent-choice-implies-countable-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]).

[F10] A weakly closed forward map has a weakly closed domain and sequentially weak-to-weak closed graph ([[def-ip-weakly-closed-nonlinear-forward-map]]).

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $X,Y$ be real Banach spaces, $D(F)\subseteq X$, and $F:D(F)\to Y$. Let $R:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ be proper and convex, let $x^\dagger\in D(F)\cap\operatorname{dom}R$, set $y=F(x^\dagger)$, and choose $\xi^\dagger\in\partial R(x^\dagger)$. Fix $1\le p<\infty$, $0\le\beta<1$, and a level $R_0>R(x^\dagger)$. Let $\psi:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ be continuous, nondecreasing and concave, with $\psi(0)=0$ and $\psi(t)>0$ for $t>0$, and assume the variational source inequality

$$-\langle\xi^\dagger,x-x^\dagger\rangle_{X^*,X}\le\beta D_R^{\xi^\dagger}(x,x^\dagger)+\psi\!\left(\|F(x)-F(x^\dagger)\|_Y^p\right)\qquad\left(x\in L_{R_0}:=\{x\in D(F):R(x)\le R_0\}\right),$$

where $D_R^{\xi^\dagger}(x,x^\dagger):=R(x)-R(x^\dagger)-\langle\xi^\dagger,x-x^\dagger\rangle_{X^*,X}$. Extend $-\psi$ by $+\infty$ on negative arguments and write $H(q):=(-\psi)^*(-q)=\sup_{s\ge0}(\psi(s)-qs)$; assume $H(q)$ is finite for sufficiently large $q$ and $H(q)\to0$ as $q\to\infty$. For sufficiently small noise levels $\delta>0$ and data $y^\delta\in Y$ with $\|y^\delta-y\|_Y\le\delta$, define $J_\alpha^\delta(x):=p^{-1}\|F(x)-y^\delta\|_Y^p+\alpha R(x)$. Suppose $\alpha=\alpha(\delta)>0$ tends to zero, $0\le\varepsilon_\delta\le C_\varepsilon\delta^p$, and $x_\alpha^{\delta,\varepsilon}\in D(F)$ is an $\varepsilon_\delta$-minimizer, meaning $J_\alpha^\delta(x_\alpha^{\delta,\varepsilon})\le\inf_{z\in D(F)}J_\alpha^\delta(z)+\varepsilon_\delta$. Set $c_p:=2^{1-p}/p$ and $\rho_\delta:=H(c_p/\alpha(\delta))$. Assume that for constants $c_-,c_+,C_H>0$ independent of $\delta$,

$$c_-\delta^p\le\alpha(\delta)\rho_\delta\le c_+\delta^p,\qquad H(c_p/(2\alpha(\delta)))\le C_H\rho_\delta$$

for all sufficiently small $\delta$. Then for all sufficiently small $\delta$, $x_\alpha^{\delta,\varepsilon}\in L_{R_0}$ and

$$D_R^{\xi^\dagger}(x_\alpha^{\delta,\varepsilon},x^\dagger)=O(\rho_\delta),\qquad \|F(x_\alpha^{\delta,\varepsilon})-y^\delta\|_Y=O(\delta).$$

If, in addition, $\psi(C_0\delta^p)=O(\rho_\delta)$ for a fixed $C_0$ such that $T_\delta:=\|F(x_\alpha^{\delta,\varepsilon})-F(x^\dagger)\|_Y^p\le C_0\delta^p$ for all sufficiently small $\delta$, then $|R(x_\alpha^{\delta,\varepsilon})-R(x^\dagger)|=O(\rho_\delta)$. If also $D_R^{\xi^\dagger}(x,x^\dagger)\ge c_R\|x-x^\dagger\|_X^s$ on $L_{R_0}$ for constants $c_R,s>0$, then $\|x_\alpha^{\delta,\varepsilon}-x^\dagger\|_X^s=O(\rho_\delta)$.

In the Hilbert special case, set $p=2$ and suppose $X,Y$ are real Hilbert spaces, $F:U\to Y$ has the real open-domain interface of a nonlinear forward map, $x^\dagger$ is an $x_0$-minimum-norm exact solution, $R(x)=\frac12\|x-x_0\|_X^2$, and the source inequality on a regularizer sublevel contained in $U$ is

$$\langle x^\dagger-x_0,x^\dagger-x\rangle_X\le\beta_1\frac12\|x-x^\dagger\|_X^2+\beta_2\|F(x)-F(x^\dagger)\|_Y$$

with $0\le\beta_1<1$ and $\beta_2\ge0$. For exact global minimizers of the nonlinear Tikhonov functional with $\alpha(\delta)\asymp\delta$, the theorem gives $\|x_{\alpha(\delta)}^\delta-x^\dagger\|_X=O(\sqrt\delta)$ and $\|F(x_{\alpha(\delta)}^\delta)-y^\delta\|_Y=O(\delta)$. The assertion is conditional on such a global minimizer being supplied; it does not assert existence or cover local numerical minima.

facts:
**Given:** All hypotheses in the Statement hold. Write $x_\delta:=x_\alpha^{\delta,\varepsilon}$, $T_\delta:=\|F(x_\delta)-F(x^\dagger)\|_Y^p$, and $r_\delta:=\|F(x_\delta)-y^\delta\|_Y$.

[A1] $\delta>0$, $x_\delta$ is an $\varepsilon_\delta$-minimizer of $J_\alpha^\delta$, and $\|y^\delta-y\|_Y\le\delta$, with $0\le\varepsilon_\delta\le C_\varepsilon\delta^p$.

[A2] The VSC holds on $L_{R_0}$ with the chosen $\xi^\dagger$, $\beta$, and $\psi$.

[A3] $\alpha\rho_\delta\asymp\delta^p$, $H(c_p/(2\alpha))\le C_H\rho_\delta$, $\alpha\to0$, and $\rho_\delta\to0$.

[A4] For the optional penalty conclusion, $\psi(C_0\delta^p)=O(\rho_\delta)$ for a fixed $C_0$ that bounds $T_\delta/\delta^p$ for small $\delta$.

[A5] For the optional norm conclusion, $D_R^{\xi^\dagger}(x,x^\dagger)\ge c_R\|x-x^\dagger\|_X^s$ on $L_{R_0}$ for constants $c_R,s>0$.

[F6] [[def-ip-x0-minimum-norm-solution]]: the Hilbert specialization assumes the exact solution globally minimizes distance to $x_0$ over its exact solution set.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $X,Y$ be real Hilbert spaces, let $U\subseteq X$ be a nonempty open set, let $F:U\to Y$ be a forward map, let $y\in Y$, and let $x_0\in X$. A point $x^\dagger\in U$ is an **$x_0$-minimum-norm solution** of $F(x)=y$ on $U$ if $F(x^\dagger)=y$ and

$$\|x^\dagger-x_0\|\le\|x-x_0\|\qquad\text{for every }x\in U\text{ with }F(x)=y.$$

This definition asserts no existence or uniqueness; it describes the minimizing property of a supplied exact solution. The minimum is global over the exact solution set on $U$, with distance measured from the specified reference point $x_0$.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $X,Y$ be real Hilbert spaces, let $U\subseteq X$ be open, and let $F:U\to Y$ be Fréchet differentiable at every point with a derivative map $F':U\to\mathcal B(X,Y)$ that is continuous in operator norm. This is the real-Hilbert forward-map convention. Assume Countable Choice, so every bounded derivative $F'(x)$ has the Hilbert adjoint $F'(x)^*:Y\to X$ characterized by $\langle F'(x)u,v\rangle_Y=\langle u,F'(x)^*v\rangle_X$.

An **admissible local instance** consists of an initial point $x_0\in U$, a radius $r>0$, an exact solution $x^\dagger\in\overline B_r(x_0):=\{x\in X:\|x-x_0\|_X\le r\}$ with exact datum $y=F(x^\dagger)$, a noise level $\delta\ge0$, noisy datum $y^\delta\in Y$ with $\|y^\delta-y\|_Y\le\delta$, a constant $0\le\eta<1/2$, a discrepancy parameter $\tau>2(1+\eta)/(1-2\eta)$, and a finite update budget $M\in\mathbb N_0$. The closed outer ball $\overline B_{2r}(x_0)$ is contained in $U$; $\|F'(x)\|\le1$ for every $x\in\overline B_{2r}(x_0)$; and the uniform two-point tangential-cone inequality

$$
\|F(x)-F(\widetilde x)-F'(x)(x-\widetilde x)\|_Y\le\eta\|F(x)-F(\widetilde x)\|_Y
$$

holds for every $x,\widetilde x\in\overline B_{2r}(x_0)$. This is the uniform family of the one-basepoint local tangential-cone inequality; the shared constant and pair domain are part of the admissibility hypothesis. The exact solution and the bounds are analysis data and need not be available to the computational loop.

**Inputs:** $F$, $x_0$, $y^\delta$, $\delta$, $\tau$, and $M$ from an admissible local instance.

**Output:** Either `stopped` with an index $k$, iterate $x_k^\delta$, and residual $\|y^\delta-F(x_k^\delta)\|_Y$, or `budget_exhausted` with the last iterate and its residual.

**Procedure:** Set $x_0^\delta:=x_0$. For $k=0,1,\ldots,M$, compute $r_k^\delta:=\|y^\delta-F(x_k^\delta)\|_Y$. If $r_k^\delta\le\tau\delta$, return `stopped` with $(k,x_k^\delta,r_k^\delta)$. If $k=M$, return `budget_exhausted` with $(k,x_k^\delta,r_k^\delta)$. Otherwise set

$$
x_{k+1}^\delta:=x_k^\delta+F'(x_k^\delta)^*(y^\delta-F(x_k^\delta))
$$

and continue at the next index. Each update is evaluated at a current point in $U$, where the derivative and its Hilbert adjoint are defined.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $X,Y$ be real Hilbert spaces, let $U\subseteq X$ be open, and let $F:U\to Y$ be Fréchet differentiable at $x\in U$. For $\delta>0$ such that the closed ball

$$\overline B_\delta(x):=\{x+h:h\in X,\ \|h\|_X\le\delta\}$$

is contained in $U$, the **local tangential cone condition at $x$ on radius $\delta$ with constant $\eta$** holds if $0\le\eta<1$ and

$$\|F(x+h)-F(x)-F'(x)h\|_Y\le\eta\,\|F(x+h)-F(x)\|_Y\qquad(\|h\|_X\le\delta).$$

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $X,Y$ be real Hilbert spaces, let $U\subseteq X$ be open, and let $F:U\to Y$ be Fréchet differentiable at every point with $F':U\to\mathcal B(X,Y)$ continuous in operator norm. Fix $x_0\in U$ and $r>0$ such that $\overline B_{2r}(x_0)\subseteq U$, and suppose an exact solution $x^\dagger\in\overline B_r(x_0)$ satisfies $y=F(x^\dagger)$. Assume $\|F'(x)\|\le1$ for every $x\in\overline B_{2r}(x_0)$ and that, for some $0\le\eta<1/2$,

$$
\|F(x)-F(\widetilde x)-F'(x)(x-\widetilde x)\|_Y\le\eta\|F(x)-F(\widetilde x)\|_Y
$$

for every $x,\widetilde x\in\overline B_{2r}(x_0)$. This is a uniform two-point hypothesis with the derivative based at the first point. Assume Countable Choice so that the bounded derivatives have Hilbert adjoints. For $\delta\ge0$ and $y^\delta\in Y$ with $\|y^\delta-y\|_Y\le\delta$, set $x_0^\delta=x_0$ and define the ideal Landweber sequence by

$$
x_{n+1}^\delta=x_n^\delta+F'(x_n^\delta)^*(y^\delta-F(x_n^\delta)).
$$

Let $\tau>2(1+\eta)/(1-2\eta)$. For $\delta>0$, let $N(\delta,y^\delta)$ denote the first $n\in\mathbb N_0$ with $\|y^\delta-F(x_n^\delta)\|_Y\le\tau\delta$, if it exists. Put $d_0=\|x_0-x^\dagger\|_X$ and $c_\tau=1-2\eta-2(1+\eta)/\tau>0$. Then the following hold.

1. For every update before the first discrepancy stop, writing $R_n^\delta=\|y^\delta-F(x_n^\delta)\|_Y$, the squared-error estimate is

   $$
   \|x_{n+1}^\delta-x^\dagger\|_X^2-\|x_n^\delta-x^\dagger\|_X^2\le R_n^\delta\bigl(2(1+\eta)\delta-(1-2\eta)R_n^\delta\bigr).
   $$

   In particular, the iterates are Fejér monotone relative to $x^\dagger$ up to the stop: their distance to $x^\dagger$ does not increase. Here Fejér monotonicity means exactly this nonincrease of distance to the stated solution.

2. If $\delta>0$, the first discrepancy index exists and

   $$
   N(\delta,y^\delta)<C\delta^{-2},\qquad C:=1+\frac{d_0^2}{c_\tau\tau^2}.
   $$

   A run of the finite-budget algorithm with budget $M\ge N(\delta,y^\delta)$ returns `stopped` at this first index; if $M<N(\delta,y^\delta)$, it returns `budget_exhausted` at $M$.

3. For exact data ($\delta=0$ and $y^\delta=y$), the ideal sequence is defined for every $n$, satisfies

   $$
   (1-2\eta)\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\|F(x_n)-y\|_Y^2\le d_0^2,
   $$

   and converges strongly to some $\bar x\in\overline B_{2r}(x_0)$ with $F(\bar x)=y$. No finite stopping index is claimed in the exact-data case.

4. For noisy data ($\delta>0$), the ideal stopped iterates converge uniformly over the admissible noise ball to that same exact-data limit:

   $$
   \lim_{\delta\downarrow0}\ \sup_{\|y^\delta-y\|_Y\le\delta}\|x_{N(\delta,y^\delta)}^\delta-\bar x\|_X=0.
   $$

   For finite-budget runs this conclusion concerns outputs only when their budgets reach the first discrepancy indices. The theorem asserts neither a convergence rate nor that $\bar x$ is an $x_0$-minimum-norm solution.

facts:
**Given:** All hypotheses in the Statement. For any current iterate $u$ in the outer ball, write $A=F'(u)$ and $q=y^\delta-F(u)$. The update is $u^+=u+A^*q$.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: the Axiom of Countable Choice, $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is assumed. No stronger form of choice is assumed.

[A2] The data satisfy $y=F(x^\dagger)$ and $\|y^\delta-y\|_Y\le\delta$.

[A3] The closed outer ball lies in $U$, $x^\dagger$ is within distance $r$ of $x_0$, $F'$ is continuous in operator norm on $U$, and the derivative bound and uniform two-point tangential-cone inequality in the Statement hold on that ball.

[F1] [[alg-ip-nonlinear-landweber-discrepancy]]: the iteration is $x_{n+1}^\delta=x_n^\delta+F'(x_n^\delta)^*(y^\delta-F(x_n^\delta))$ and the discrepancy check is made before the finite-budget check.

[F2] [[def-ip-tangential-cone-condition]]: at a base point $x$, the local TCC bounds $\|F(x+h)-F(x)-F'(x)h\|_Y$ by $\eta\|F(x+h)-F(x)\|_Y$. The theorem assumes this exact orientation uniformly for pairs in the outer ball.

[F3] [[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]] and [[thm-hilbert-adjoint-properties]]: $\langle Au,v\rangle_Y=\langle u,A^*v\rangle_X$ and $\|A^*\|=\|A\|$ for every bounded Hilbert-space operator $A$.

[F4] [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]: the real inner product is symmetric and $\|u\|_X^2=\langle u,u\rangle_X$; the corresponding expansion is $\|u+v\|_X^2=\|u\|_X^2+2\langle u,v\rangle_X+\|v\|_X^2$.

[F5] [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-in-an-inner-product-space]]: $|\langle u,v\rangle|\le\|u\|\,\|v\|$.

[F6] [[cor-inner-product-induces-a-norm]]: $\|u+v\|\le\|u\|+\|v\|$ in each real Hilbert space.

[F7] [[def-hilbert-space]]: every Cauchy sequence in $X$ for the induced norm converges in $X$.

[F8] [[def-series]] and [[thm-nonnegative-series-bounded-partial-sums]]: a series with nonnegative real terms and bounded partial sums converges, and its tails tend to zero.

[F9] [[thm-reals-cauchy-complete]] and [[thm-of-archimedean]]: the real field is complete and its natural numbers are unbounded above.

[F10] [[thm-well-ordering-principle]]: every nonempty set of natural indices has a least member.

[F11] [[def-operator-norm]]: for every bounded linear $T$, $\|Tu\|\le\|T\|\,\|u\|$.

[F12] [[def-ip-nonlinear-forward-map]]: a real-Hilbert forward map is $F:U\to Y$ on an open domain, and exact solutions satisfy $F(x^\dagger)=y$.

[F13] [[def-frechet-derivative-between-banach-spaces]]: each Fréchet derivative is a bounded real-linear operator, and differentiability on $U$ defines the derivative map $F':U\to\mathcal B(X,Y)$.

contract.heading: Example
contract.text: Take $X=Y=\mathbb R$ with the usual real Hilbert structure, $U=\mathbb R$, $F(x)=x$, $x_0=x^\dagger=0$, $y=F(x^\dagger)=0$, noise level $\delta=1$, noisy datum $y^\delta=1$, discrepancy parameter $\tau>2$, and update budget $M=0$. The local Landweber assumptions hold with any radius $r>0$ and $\eta=0$, and the initial residual is $1\le\tau\delta$. The algorithm therefore returns `stopped` at index zero with iterate $0$ and residual $1$, before consulting the zero update budget.

[F1] [[alg-ip-nonlinear-landweber-discrepancy]]: the algorithm tests $\|y^\delta-F(x_k^\delta)\|_Y\le\tau\delta$ before testing whether $k=M$.

[F2] [[def-ip-tangential-cone-condition]]: the local TCC remainder is $F(x+h)-F(x)-F'(x)h$ and its required bound is relative to $\|F(x+h)-F(x)\|$.

contract.text: Exact solvability by itself is enough for exact-data nonlinear Landweber to converge from every initial point; no local tangential-cone or initial-ball hypothesis is needed.

**Given:** The real Hilbert line $X=Y=\mathbb R$, $U=\mathbb R$, $F(x)=x^2-1$, exact solution $x^\dagger=1$, exact datum $y=0$, and initial point $x_0=0$.

[F1] [[alg-ip-nonlinear-landweber-discrepancy]]: at exact data, $x_{n+1}=x_n+F'(x_n)^*(y-F(x_n))$; a zero derivative gives a zero update.

[F3] [[thm-ip-nonlinear-landweber-fejer-and-finite-stopping]]: its exact-data convergence conclusion assumes the specified outer ball, derivative bound, and uniform TCC on that ball.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $X,Y$ be real Hilbert spaces, let $U\subseteq X$ be open, and let
$F:U\to Y$ be continuously Fréchet differentiable, meaning that $F$ is
Fréchet differentiable at each point of $U$ and $x\mapsto F'(x)$ is continuous
in operator norm. For a subset $V\subseteq U$ and a constant $c>0$, the
**product-type tangential cone condition on $V$ with constant $c$** is the
requirement that, for every $x,\tilde x\in V$,

$$\|F(x)-F(\tilde x)-F'(x)(x-\tilde x)\|_Y\le c\|x-\tilde x\|_X\|F(x)-F(\tilde x)\|_Y.$$

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $X,Y$ be real Hilbert spaces, let $U\subseteq X$ be open, and let
$F:U\to Y$ be Fréchet differentiable at every point of $U$ with
$x\mapsto F'(x)$ continuous in operator norm. Let $V\subseteq U$ and let
$c>0$ be such that, for every $u,\tilde u\in V$,
$$\|F(u)-F(\tilde u)-F'(u)(u-\tilde u)\|_Y\le c\|u-\tilde u\|_X\|F(u)-F(\tilde u)\|_Y.$$
Suppose
$x^\dagger,x\in V$, $F(x^\dagger)=y$, $\|y^\delta-y\|_Y\le\delta$ with
$\delta\ge0$, $\tau>0$, and $\|x-x^\dagger\|_X\le e$. If
$R:=\|F(x)-y^\delta\|_Y>\tau\delta$, then

$$\|F'(x)(x^\dagger-x)+F(x)-y^\delta\|_Y\le\frac{1+ce(1+\tau)}{\tau}R.$$

In particular, if $\sigma\in(0,1)$, $e\le e_0$, and
$$\gamma:=\frac{\sigma\tau}{1+ce_0(1+\tau)}>1,$$
then
$$\|F'(x)(x^\dagger-x)+F(x)-y^\delta\|_Y\le\frac{\sigma}{\gamma}R.$$

facts:
**Given:** The spaces, map, set, constant, exact solution, datum, noise bound, $\tau$, and points in the Statement.

[F1] For $x,\tilde x\in V$, the product condition gives
$$\|F(x)-F(\tilde x)-F'(x)(x-\tilde x)\|_Y\le c\|x-\tilde x\|_X\|F(x)-F(\tilde x)\|_Y$$
([[def-ip-product-tangential-cone-condition]]).

[F2] The exact-data convention is $F(x^\dagger)=y$ ([[def-ip-nonlinear-forward-map]]); the noise bound $\|y^\delta-y\|_Y\le\delta$ is an additional hypothesis in the Statement.

[F3] The induced real Hilbert norm satisfies the triangle inequality ([[cor-inner-product-induces-a-norm]]).

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $X,Y$ be real Hilbert spaces, let $U\subseteq X$
be open, and let $F:U\to Y$ be continuously Fréchet differentiable, meaning
that $F$ is Fréchet differentiable at each point of $U$ and
$x\mapsto F'(x)$ is continuous in operator norm. The input consists of an
initial point $x_0\in U$, a datum $y^\delta\in Y$, a positive noise bound
$\delta>0$, a discrepancy factor $\tau>1$, a forcing fraction $\sigma\in(0,1)$,
a range-approximation margin $\gamma>1$, and a finite update budget
$N_{\max}\in\mathbb N_0:=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$. Assume an exact solution $x^\dagger\in U$ exists
with $F(x^\dagger)=y$ and $\|y^\delta-y\|_Y\le\delta$. At every state
$x_n^\delta$ before the discrepancy stop, the admissible local range condition
is
$$\|F'(x_n^\delta)(x^\dagger-x_n^\delta)+F(x_n^\delta)-y^\delta\|_Y\le\frac{\sigma}{\gamma}\|F(x_n^\delta)-y^\delta\|_Y.$$

For $x_n^\delta\in U$ and $\alpha>0$, define $h_{n,\alpha}$ to be the unique
global minimizer over $h\in X$ of the regularized linearized least-squares
objective
$$J_{n,\alpha}(h):=\frac12\|F'(x_n^\delta)h+F(x_n^\delta)-y^\delta\|_Y^2+\frac\alpha2\|h\|_X^2.$$
Equivalently, it is the unique solution of
$$\bigl(F'(x_n^\delta)^*F'(x_n^\delta)+\alpha I_X\bigr)h_{n,\alpha}=F'(x_n^\delta)^*(y^\delta-F(x_n^\delta)).$$
Here $I_X$ is the identity operator on $X$.
The forcing rule selects any $\alpha_n>0$ for which
$$\|F'(x_n^\delta)h_{n,\alpha_n}+F(x_n^\delta)-y^\delta\|_Y=\sigma\|F(x_n^\delta)-y^\delta\|_Y,$$
and sets $x_{n+1}^\delta=x_n^\delta+h_{n,\alpha_n}$. The displayed range
condition is a sufficient condition for the forcing rule to have such a
parameter; it is not an input to either linearized minimization problem.

For a finite run, inspect $n=0,1,\ldots,N_{\max}$ in order. If
$x_n^\delta\notin U$, return $(x_n^\delta,n,\texttt{domain-failure})$. If
$\|F(x_n^\delta)-y^\delta\|_Y\le\tau\delta$, return
$(x_n^\delta,n,\texttt{discrepancy})$. If $n=N_{\max}$, return
$(x_n^\delta,n,\texttt{budget-exhausted})$. Otherwise request the exact
regularized minimizer and a positive parameter satisfying the forcing rule.
If the exact minimizer cannot be certified, return
$(x_n^\delta,n,\texttt{solve-unverified})$; if the parameter selector cannot
return a positive parameter satisfying the displayed equality, return
$(x_n^\delta,n,\texttt{forcing-unavailable})$. After both exact calls succeed,
set $x_{n+1}^\delta=x_n^\delta+h_{n,\alpha_n}$ and continue. Each return is a
triple of state, index, and status. No convergence claim is attached to the
failure statuses or to a budget-exhausted state.
