contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $X,Y$ be real Hilbert spaces, let $U\subseteq X$
be open, and let $F:U\to Y$ be Fréchet differentiable everywhere with
$x\mapsto F'(x)$ continuous in operator norm. For $s>0$, write
$$B_s(x_0):=\{x\in X:\|x-x_0\|_X<s\}.$$
Suppose $B_{2r}(x_0)\subseteq U$ for some $r>0$, $x^\dagger\in B_r(x_0)$,
and $F(x^\dagger)=y$. Assume there are constants $M,c>0$ such that, for every
$x,\tilde x\in B_{2r}(x_0)$,
$$\|F'(x)\|\le M,$$
$$\|F(x)-F(\tilde x)-F'(x)(x-\tilde x)\|_Y\le c\|x-\tilde x\|_X\|F(x)-F(\tilde x)\|_Y.$$
Fix $\sigma\in(0,1)$ and $\tau>1/\sigma$. Put
$$e_0:=\|x_0-x^\dagger\|_X$$
and assume
$$e_0<\min\left\{r,\frac{\sigma\tau-1}{c(1+\tau)},\frac{1-\sigma}{2c}\right\}.$$
Set
$$\gamma:=\frac{\sigma\tau}{1+ce_0(1+\tau)};$$
the hypotheses give $\gamma>1$. For each exact iteration, use this $\gamma$ in
the range-approximation margin of the regularized LM procedure and select any
positive parameter satisfying its residual-forcing equality.
For every $\delta>0$ and $y^\delta\in Y$ satisfying
$\|y^\delta-y\|_Y\le\delta$, start at $x_0^\delta=x_0$ and, at each state
before stopping, let $h_n$ minimize
$$h\longmapsto\frac12\|F'(x_n^\delta)h+F(x_n^\delta)-y^\delta\|_Y^2+\frac{\alpha_n}{2}\|h\|_X^2$$
for a selected $\alpha_n>0$ satisfying
$$\|F'(x_n^\delta)h_n+F(x_n^\delta)-y^\delta\|_Y=\sigma\|F(x_n^\delta)-y^\delta\|_Y,$$
and set $x_{n+1}^\delta=x_n^\delta+h_n$. Let $N_\delta$ be the first
$n\in\mathbb N_0:=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$ such that
$$\|F(x_n^\delta)-y^\delta\|_Y\le\tau\delta.$$
Then this exact iteration is well-defined up to a finite first discrepancy
index $N_\delta$. Set
$$q:=\frac{\sigma+ce_0}{1-ce_0},\qquad K:=1+\|F(x_0)-y\|_Y,\qquad
\delta_0:=\min\left\{1,\frac K\tau\right\}.$$
Here $q\in(0,1)$ and $\log$ denotes the natural logarithm. For
$0<\delta\le\delta_0$,
$$N_\delta\le1+\frac{\log(K/(\tau\delta))}{-\log q}.$$
Consequently $N_\delta=O(1+|\log\delta|)$ as $\delta\downarrow0$, with
constants depending only on the fixed problem and displayed parameters. A
finite run with update budget at least $N_\delta$ and successful exact calls
returns this first crossing; a shorter budget may return
`budget-exhausted`. No convergence rate for $x_{N_\delta}^\delta$ is asserted.

facts:
**Given:** Countable Choice; real Hilbert spaces $X,Y$; an open domain $U$; a continuously Fréchet differentiable map $F:U\to Y$; $B_{2r}(x_0)\subseteq U$; an exact solution $x^\dagger\in B_r(x_0)$ with $F(x^\dagger)=y$; constants $M,c>0$; $\sigma\in(0,1)$; $\tau>1/\sigma$; the stated smallness bound on $e_0$; and positive noise $\delta$ with $\|y^\delta-y\|\le\delta$.

[A1] Countable Choice is the sole choice axiom assumed for Hilbert adjoints and the shifted normal equations ([[def-countable-choice]]).

[F1] On the local ball, the product remainder is bounded by $c\|x-\tilde x\|\|F(x)-F(\tilde x)\|$ ([[def-ip-product-tangential-cone-condition]]).

[F2] If $\|x-x^\dagger\|\le e_0$ and $\|F(x)-y^\delta\|>\tau\delta$, then the linearized residual at $x^\dagger$ is at most $[1+ce_0(1+\tau)]/\tau$ times the current residual; when $\gamma=\sigma\tau/[1+ce_0(1+\tau)]>1$, this is at most $\sigma/\gamma$ times the current residual ([[lem-ip-lm-product-condition-implies-range-approximation]]).

[F3] The algorithm checks discrepancy before updates, uses the exact regularized linearized minimizer and the residual-forcing equality, and returns the first crossing when exact calls and its finite cap permit ([[alg-ip-regularized-levenberg-marquardt]]).

[F4] Under the range-approximation condition, the exact step obeys
$$\|e_n\|^2-\|e_n+h_n\|^2\ge\|h_n\|^2+\frac{2(\gamma-1)\sigma^2}{\gamma\alpha_n}\|F(x_n)-y^\delta\|^2,$$
and if $\|F'(x_n)\|\le M$, then $\alpha_n\le\sigma M^2/(1-\sigma)$ ([[lem-ip-lm-fejer-decrease-and-parameter-bound]]).

[F5] The natural logarithm is strictly increasing, satisfies the quotient law, and is negative on $(0,1)$ ([[def-natural-logarithm]], [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]]).

[F6] For every real bound $b$, some natural number exceeds $b$ ([[lem-cauchy-reals-archimedean]]).

[F7] The real Hilbert norm satisfies the triangle inequality ([[cor-inner-product-induces-a-norm]]).

[F8] A Fréchet derivative is a bounded linear map, and its norm is the operator norm defined on bounded linear maps ([[def-frechet-derivative-between-banach-spaces]], [[def-operator-norm]]).

[F9] For a nonzero residual and a vector meeting the range-approximation margin, the regularized linearized least-squares problem has a unique minimizer and some positive parameter attains the residual-forcing equality ([[lem-ip-lm-step-existence-and-residual-forcing]]).

contract.text: Assume Countable Choice. Let $K:X\to Y$ be compact between real or complex Hilbert spaces over the same scalar field, let $\psi$ be a bounded nonnegative spectral index with $\psi(0)=0$, and let $x=\psi(|K|)w$ for some $w\in X$. Then $x\in N(K)^\perp$; consequently, among all $z\in X$ satisfying $Kz=Kx$, $x$ is the unique vector of minimum norm.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: Countable Choice is the hypothesis of the compact norm-limit theorem, Hilbert adjoint, and compact square-root results used below.

[F1] [[def-square-summable-family-on-an-arbitrary-index-set]] and [[lem-square-summable-sequences-form-a-hilbert-space]]: $\ell^2(\mathbb N,\mathbb R)$ has norm squared $\sum_j|x_j|^2$, unit coordinate vectors $e_j$, and is a complete real Hilbert space.

[F2] [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-in-an-inner-product-space]] and [[def-operator-norm]]: The inner product satisfies Cauchy–Schwarz and the operator norm is the supremum of $\|Tx\|$ over $\|x\|\le1$.

[F3] [[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]], [[thm-hilbert-adjoint-properties]], and [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]: Every bounded operator on a Hilbert space has a unique adjoint satisfying $\langle Tx,y\rangle=\langle x,T^*y\rangle$; self-adjointness is $T^*=T$, and positivity is $\langle Tx,x\rangle\ge0$ for every $x$.

[F4] [[lem-finite-rank-operators-are-compact]] and [[thm-norm-limit-of-compact-operators-is-compact]]: Bounded finite-rank maps are compact, and a norm limit of compact maps into a Banach space is compact under Countable Choice.

[F5] [[lem-positive-square-root-of-a-compact-positive-operator]] and [[def-compact-spectral-filter-and-qualification]]: The positive square root of a compact positive operator is unique and acts on an eigenvector of eigenvalue $\lambda$ by $\sqrt{\lambda}$; compact spectral multipliers act eigenvalue by eigenvalue.

[F6] [[def-ip-index-source-ball]] and [[def-ip-power-source-set]]: The source ball is the image of the radius-$\rho$ vector ball under its spectral index multiplier; the power index is $t^\nu$, and the logarithmic candidate defines a source ball once it is bounded on the compact spectrum.

[F7] [[thm-ip-source-ball-modulus-of-continuity]]: The centered power-source modulus is at most $\delta^{\nu/(\nu+1)}\rho^{1/(\nu+1)}$ and attains this value at the radii $\rho s_j^{\nu+1}$.

[F8] [[def-natural-logarithm]], [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]], [[def-real-power]], [[def-real-exponential-function-and-e]], [[cor-exponential-reciprocal-and-positivity]], [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]], [[cor-mean-value-theorem]], [[thm-real-power-laws]], [[cor-archimedean-reciprocal]], [[lem-of-inverse-positive]], and [[def-complete-ordered-real-field]]: The real field is complete and ordered; $\log 1=0$, $\exp(0)=1$, and positive-base real powers are positive. For every $\varepsilon>0$, choose $N$ with $1/N<\varepsilon$ by the reciprocal Archimedean property; if $j\ge N$, reciprocal order gives $1/j\le1/N<\varepsilon$.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $X$, $Y$, and $Z$ be real Banach spaces, let $U\subseteq X$ be nonempty, let $x_0\in U$, and let $F:U\to Y$ be a map. A **differential range-invariance factorization at $x_0$ on $U$** consists of a bounded linear map $K:Z\to Y$ and a map $r:U\to Z$ such that

$$F(x)-F(x_0)=Kr(x)\qquad(x\in U).$$

Thus every data increment lies in the range of the fixed operator $K$. The factorization alone does not assert that $K$ is injective, that $r$ is unique, or that a tangential-cone inequality holds. If $U$ is open and $F$ and $r$ are Fréchet differentiable, differentiating this identity gives $F'(x)=Kr'(x)$ at every $x\in U$; no converse is asserted without further hypotheses.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $X$ be a real Banach space and let $X^*$ be its continuous real dual. The dual pairing is evaluation, written $\langle \xi,x\rangle_{X^*,X}:=\xi(x)$ for $\xi\in X^*$ and $x\in X$. Let $R:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ be a proper convex functional: $R$ never takes the value $-\infty$, its effective domain $\operatorname{dom}R:=\{x\in X:R(x)<+\infty\}$ is nonempty, and $R((1-t)x+tz)\le (1-t)R(x)+tR(z)$ for $x,z\in X$ and $t\in[0,1]$, with $0\cdot(+\infty):=0$ for this convex-combination formula. For $x\in\operatorname{dom}R$, its subdifferential is

$$\partial R(x):=\{\xi\in X^*:R(z)\ge R(x)+\langle\xi,z-x\rangle_{X^*,X}\text{ for every }z\in X\}.$$

An element of $\partial R(x)$ is a subgradient of $R$ at $x$. Set $\partial R(x):=\varnothing$ when $x\notin\operatorname{dom}R$. The subdifferential may be empty at a point of $\operatorname{dom}R$; no nonemptiness assertion is part of this definition.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $X,Y,Z$ be real Banach spaces, let $X_0$ be a closed linear subspace of $X$, and let $D\subseteq X$ contain $X_0$ and a nonempty set $U$. Fix $x_0\in X_0\cap U$, a map $F:D\to Y$, a bounded linear map $K:Z\to Y$, and a map $r:D\to Z$ such that $F(x)-F(x_0)=Kr(x)$ for every $x\in D$. Assume that $r|_U$ is a bijection from $U$ onto a set $\widetilde U\subseteq Z$, and that $(I-P)r^{-1}(\widehat r)\in X_0\cap D$ for every $\widehat r\in\widetilde U$ admitted below. Here $I$ is the identity on $X$ and $P:X\to X$ is a bounded linear projection with $P^2=P$, $P|_{X_0}=0$, and $(I-P)(X)\subseteq X_0$. Let $\check R:X_0\to[0,+\infty]$ be a proper convex regularizer, let $R_P:P(X)\to[0,+\infty]$ be a nonnegative penalty, and let $Q:Z\times Z\to[0,+\infty]$ satisfy $Q(a,b)=Q(b,a)$ and $Q(a,b)=0$ exactly when $a=b$. For $\widehat r\in\widetilde U$, set

$$\mathcal R(\widehat r):=\check R\big((I-P)r^{-1}(\widehat r)\big)+R_P\big(Pr^{-1}(\widehat r)\big).$$

For $p\in[1,\infty)$, data $y^\delta\in Y$, and parameters $\alpha,\beta>0$, the **joint relaxed objective** is

$$\mathcal J_{\alpha,\beta}^\delta(\widehat r,x):=\|K\widehat r+F(x_0)-y^\delta\|_Y^p+\alpha\mathcal R(\widehat r)+\beta Q(r(x),\widehat r)^p+\|Px\|_X^p,\qquad (\widehat r,x)\in\widetilde U\times U.$$

The joint source-condition objective takes $R_P=0$. The term $\beta Q(r(x),\widehat r)^p$ ties the relaxed range variable to the physical variable, while $\|Px\|_X^p$ penalizes the component outside $X_0$.

If $r$ is Gâteaux differentiable at a current iterate $x_n\in U$, the **frozen-Newton objective** with parameters $\alpha_n,\beta_n>0$ is

$$\mathcal J_n^\delta(\widehat r,x):=\|K\widehat r+F(x_0)-y^\delta\|_Y^p+\alpha_n\mathcal R(\widehat r)+\beta_n Q\big(r(x_n)+r'(x_n)(x-x_n),\widehat r\big)^p+\|Px\|_X^p.$$

Here $r'(x_n)$ is the bounded linear Gâteaux derivative used to form the affine range proxy; no minimizer existence or uniqueness is part of either definition.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $1\le p<\infty$. Let $X,Y,Z$ be real Banach spaces, $X_0\subseteq X$ a closed linear subspace, $D\subseteq X$ a domain containing $X_0$ and $U$, and $x_0\in U\cap X_0$. Let $F:D\to Y$, $K\in\mathcal L(Z,Y)$, and $r:D\to Z$ satisfy $F(x)-F(x_0)=Kr(x)$ on $D$, with $r|_U:U\to\widetilde U$ bijective and $r$ Lipschitz with constant $L_r$ on $D$. Let $P:X\to X$ be a bounded linear projection such that $P|_{X_0}=0$, $(I-P)(X)\subseteq X_0$, and $P(x_0)=P(x^\dagger)=0$ for an exact solution $x^\dagger\in U\cap X_0$; put $y:=F(x^\dagger)$. Assume the projected points $(I-P)r^{-1}(\widehat r)$ belong to $D\cap X_0$ for all admitted $\widehat r\in\widetilde U$.

Let $\check R:X_0\to[0,+\infty]$ be proper and convex, choose $\xi^\dagger\in\partial\check R(x^\dagger)\subseteq X_0^*$, and suppose that for some $R_0\ge\check R(x^\dagger)$, $b\in[0,1)$, and continuous nondecreasing concave $\psi:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ with $\psi(0)=0$, the variational source inequality

$$-\langle\xi^\dagger,\check x-x^\dagger\rangle\le bD_{\check R}^{\xi^\dagger}(\check x,x^\dagger)+\psi\big(\|F(\check x)-F(x^\dagger)\|_Y^p\big)$$

holds whenever $\check x\in D\cap X_0$ and $\check R(\check x)\le R_0$, where $D_{\check R}^{\xi^\dagger}(\check x,x^\dagger):=\check R(\check x)-\check R(x^\dagger)-\langle\xi^\dagger,\check x-x^\dagger\rangle$. Set $R_P=0$ in the joint objective. Let $Q:\widetilde U\times\widetilde U\to[0,\infty]$ satisfy $Q(a,b)=Q(b,a)$ and $Q(a,b)=0$ exactly when $a=b$, and assume there is a constant $C_Q\ge0$ such that

$$\|P(r^{-1}(a))-P(r^{-1}(b))\|_X\le C_Q Q(a,b)\qquad(a,b\in\widetilde U).$$

For $\delta>0$, let $y^\delta\in Y$ satisfy $\|y^\delta-y\|_Y\le\delta$. Let $\alpha,\beta>0$, $C_\eta\ge0$, and let $(\widehat r_\delta,x_\delta)\in\widetilde U\times U$ be an $\eta_\delta$-minimizer of the joint objective, meaning

$$\mathcal J_{\alpha,\beta}^\delta(\widehat r_\delta,x_\delta)\le\mathcal J_{\alpha,\beta}^\delta(\widehat r,x)+\eta_\delta\qquad((\widehat r,x)\in\widetilde U\times U),\qquad 0\le\eta_\delta\le C_\eta\delta^p.$$

Assume $\check x_\delta:=(I-P)r^{-1}(\widehat r_\delta)$ lies in the stated VSC sublevel. Define

$$s_\delta:=2^{1-p}\|K(\widehat r_\delta-r(x^\dagger))\|_Y^p+\beta Q(r(x_\delta),\widehat r_\delta)^p+\|Px_\delta\|_X^p,\qquad e_\delta:=D_{\check R}^{\xi^\dagger}(\check x_\delta,x^\dagger),$$

and

$$C_*:=2^{2p-2}\max\left\{1,\|K\|^pL_r^p,\frac{\|K\|^pL_r^pC_Q^p}{\beta}\right\},\qquad d_\delta:=(2+C_\eta)\delta^p.$$

Then

$$s_\delta+(1-b)\alpha e_\delta\le d_\delta+\alpha\psi(C_*s_\delta).$$

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $X$ be a real Banach space, let $R:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ be proper and convex, choose $x^\dagger\in\operatorname{dom}R$, and choose $\xi^\dagger\in\partial R(x^\dagger)$. For $x\in\operatorname{dom}R$, the **Bregman distance** generated by $\xi^\dagger$ from the reference point $x^\dagger$ to $x$ is

$$D_R^{\xi^\dagger}(x,x^\dagger):=R(x)-R(x^\dagger)-\langle\xi^\dagger,x-x^\dagger\rangle_{X^*,X}.$$

The subgradient inequality makes this quantity nonnegative, and $D_R^{\xi^\dagger}(x^\dagger,x^\dagger)=0$. The definition fixes the orientation: the first argument is the comparison point and the second is the reference point carrying the chosen subgradient.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $X,Y$ be real Banach spaces, let $F:D(F)\subseteq X\to Y$, let $x^\dagger\in D(F)$ with exact datum $y=F(x^\dagger)$, and let $R:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ be proper and convex with $x^\dagger\in\operatorname{dom}R$. Fix $\xi^\dagger\in\partial R(x^\dagger)$, an exponent $1\le p<\infty$, a continuous nondecreasing concave function $\psi:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ with $\psi(0)=0$ and $\psi(t)>0$ for $t>0$, a coefficient $0\le\beta<1$, and a level $R_0\ge R(x^\dagger)$. The **variational source condition** with these data holds on the named regularizer sublevel $L_{R_0}:=\{x\in D(F):R(x)\le R_0\}$ when

$$-\langle\xi^\dagger,x-x^\dagger\rangle_{X^*,X}\le\beta D_R^{\xi^\dagger}(x,x^\dagger)+\psi\!\left(\|F(x)-F(x^\dagger)\|_Y^p\right)\qquad(x\in L_{R_0}).$$

The condition is an assumption on the selected subgradient and the stated sublevel; it makes no assertion that a subgradient exists at every point or that a regularized minimizer exists.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $1\le p<\infty$. Let $X,Y,Z$ be real Banach spaces, let $X_0$ be a closed linear subspace of $X$, and let $D,U\subseteq X$. Let $x_0,x^\dagger\in D\cap U\cap X_0$, let $F:D\to Y$, $K\in\mathcal L(Z,Y)$, and $r:D\to Z$ satisfy $F(x)-F(x_0)=Kr(x)$ for all $x\in D$. Assume $r|_U:U\to\widetilde U$ is a bijection, $r$ is Lipschitz on $D$ with constant $L_r$, and $r$ has bounded linear Gâteaux derivatives on $U$. Let $P:X\to X$ be a bounded linear projection with $P^2=P$, $P|_{X_0}=0$, and $(I-P)(X)\subseteq X_0$. Assume $P(x^\dagger)=0$ and $(I-P)r^{-1}(\widehat r)\in D\cap X_0$ for each admitted $\widehat r\in\widetilde U$.

Let $\check R:X_0\to[0,+\infty]$ be proper and convex, choose $\xi^\dagger\in\partial\check R(x^\dagger)$, and write

$$D_{\check R}^{\xi^\dagger}(z,x^\dagger):=\check R(z)-\check R(x^\dagger)-\langle\xi^\dagger,z-x^\dagger\rangle_{X_0^*,X_0}.$$

Suppose that, on the stated sublevel $\check R(z)\le R_0$, the variational source inequality

$$-\langle\xi^\dagger,z-x^\dagger\rangle_{X_0^*,X_0}\le bD_{\check R}^{\xi^\dagger}(z,x^\dagger)+\psi\!\left(\|F(z)-F(x^\dagger)\|_Y^p\right)$$

holds for some $R_0\ge\check R(x^\dagger)$ and $0\le b<1$. Assume that $\psi:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ is continuous, nondecreasing and concave, with $\psi(0)=0$, and that for a constant $C_\psi>0$,

$$\psi(a+b)\le C_\psi\bigl(\psi(a)+\psi(b)\bigr)\qquad(a,b\ge0).$$

Let $H(q):=\sup_{s\ge0}(\psi(s)-qs)$, and assume the values of $H$ used below are finite. Let $\gamma>C_\psi$, $C_P\ge2^{p-1}\|K\|^pL_r^p$, and $\widetilde C_Q>0$. Let $R_P:P(X)\to[0,+\infty]$ satisfy $R_P(0)=0$ and

$$R_P(z)\ge\gamma\psi(C_P\|z\|_X^p)\qquad(z\in P(X)).$$

For each admitted $\widehat r\in\widetilde U$, put $u(\widehat r):=r^{-1}(\widehat r)$ and $\check x(\widehat r):=(I-P)u(\widehat r)$. Assume the compatibility bound

$$\|\widehat r-r(x^\dagger)\|_Z^p\le\widetilde C_Q\left(D_{\check R}^{\xi^\dagger}(\check x(\widehat r),x^\dagger)+\psi(C_P\|Pu(\widehat r)\|_X^p)\right).$$

Choose $c_{\beta\alpha}>0$ with $c_{\beta\alpha}\le\min\{1-b,\gamma-C_\psi\}/(4\widetilde C_Q)$, and set

$$m:=\min\{1-b,\gamma-C_\psi\},\quad a:=2^{1-p},\quad \lambda:=2^{1-p},\quad t:=2^{2-2p}-2^{p-1}c_{\rm tcr}^p,\quad v:=(1+2^{p-1})c_{\rm tcr}^p,\quad \overline C:=C_\psi 2^{2p-2}.$$

Assume $0<c_{\rm tcr}<1$ and $t>0$, and for all $x_1,x_2\in U$ assume

$$\|r(x_1)-r(x_2)-r'(x_2)(x_1-x_2)\|_Z\le c_{\rm tcr}\|r(x_1)-r(x_2)\|_Z.$$

Assume the candidate projected point satisfies $\check R(\check x(\widehat r_{n+1}))\le R_0$.

Let $Q(a,b):=\|a-b\|_Z$. Fix $\delta>0$, $y^\delta\in Y$ with $\|y^\delta-F(x^\dagger)\|_Y\le\delta$, and $\alpha_n>0$, with $\beta_n:=c_{\beta\alpha}\alpha_n$. Suppose $(\widehat r_{n+1},x_{n+1})\in\widetilde U\times U$ satisfies, for some $\eta_n\ge0$,

$$\mathcal J_n^\delta(\widehat r_{n+1},x_{n+1})\le\mathcal J_n^\delta(\widehat r,x)+\eta_n\qquad((\widehat r,x)\in\widetilde U\times U),$$

where $\mathcal J_n^\delta$ is the frozen objective in the Joint and frozen-Newton objectives definition, with regularizer $\mathcal R(\widehat r)=\check R(\check x(\widehat r))+R_P(Pu(\widehat r))$ and distance $Q$.

Define

$$E_{n+1}:=\frac{c_{\beta\alpha}}{C_\psi}\left(\lambda\|\widehat r_{n+1}-r(x^\dagger)\|_Z^p+t\|r(x_{n+1})-r(x^\dagger)\|_Z^p\right),$$

$$S_{n+1}:=\frac{1}{C_\psi}\left(2^{1-p}\|K(\widehat r_{n+1}-r(x^\dagger))\|_Y^p+\|Px_{n+1}\|_X^p\right),$$

and

$$d_n:=\frac{c_{\beta\alpha}}{C_\psi}\alpha_n v\|r(x_n)-r(x^\dagger)\|_Z^p+\frac{2\delta^p+\eta_n}{C_\psi}.$$

Then

$$S_{n+1}+\alpha_nE_{n+1}\le d_n+\alpha_n\psi(\overline C S_{n+1}).$$

Consequently,

$$E_{n+1}\le\frac{d_n}{\alpha_n}+H\!\left(\frac{1}{\overline C\alpha_n}\right),\qquad S_{n+1}\le2\left(d_n+\alpha_nH\!\left(\frac{1}{2\overline C\alpha_n}\right)\right).$$

facts:
**Given:** All spaces, maps, penalties, parameters, source inequalities, compatibility inequalities, and the approximate frozen step satisfy the hypotheses in the Statement.

[A1] The projected point $\check x(\widehat r_{n+1})$ belongs to the regularizer sublevel where the VSC holds.

[F1] [[def-ip-differential-range-invariance]]: $F(x)-F(x_0)=Kr(x)$ on the specified domain, and $r|_U$ is invertible onto $\widetilde U$.

[F2] [[def-ip-relaxed-range-invariance-objective]]: the frozen objective has data term $\|K\widehat r+F(x_0)-y^\delta\|^p$, regularizer $\alpha_n\mathcal R(\widehat r)$, coupling $\beta_n\|\ell_n(x)-\widehat r\|^p$, and penalty $\|Px\|^p$, where $\ell_n(x)=r(x_n)+r'(x_n)(x-x_n)$.

[F3] [[def-ip-banach-convex-subgradient-and-dual-pairing]]: $\xi^\dagger\in\partial\check R(x^\dagger)$ means $\check R(z)\ge\check R(x^\dagger)+\langle\xi^\dagger,z-x^\dagger\rangle$ for every $z\in X_0$.

[F4] [[def-ip-bregman-distance]]: $D_{\check R}^{\xi^\dagger}(z,x^\dagger)=\check R(z)-\check R(x^\dagger)-\langle\xi^\dagger,z-x^\dagger\rangle$.

[F5] [[def-ip-variational-source-condition]]: $-\langle\xi^\dagger,z-x^\dagger\rangle\le bD_{\check R}^{\xi^\dagger}(z,x^\dagger)+\psi(\|F(z)-F(x^\dagger)\|^p)$ on the stated sublevel.

[F6] [[lem-ip-index-function-young-conjugate-bound]]: if $r+\alpha e\le d+\alpha\psi(Cr)$, then $e\le d/\alpha+H(1/(C\alpha))$ and $r\le2(d+\alpha H(1/(2C\alpha)))$.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the hypotheses of the joint range-invariance VSC estimate lemma, with the same notation, with fixed $\beta>0$, and with $R_P=0$ in the joint objective. Define

$$H(q):=\sup_{s\ge0}\bigl(\psi(s)-qs\bigr)\qquad(q>0),\quad \rho_\delta:=H\!\left(\frac{1}{C_*\alpha(\delta)}\right).$$

Assume $H(1/(C_*\alpha(\delta)))$ and $H(1/(2C_*\alpha(\delta)))$ are finite, $\alpha(\delta)\to0$, $\rho_\delta\to0$, $\eta_\delta\le C_\eta\delta^p$, and there are constants $c_-,c_+,C_H>0$ independent of $\delta$ such that

$$c_-\delta^p\le\alpha(\delta)\rho_\delta\le c_+\delta^p,\qquad H\!\left(\frac{1}{2C_*\alpha(\delta)}\right)\le C_H\rho_\delta.$$

Then the approximate joint reconstructions satisfy, as $\delta\downarrow0$,

$$D_{\check R}^{\xi^\dagger}(\check x_\delta,x^\dagger)=O(\rho_\delta),\qquad S_\delta=O(\delta^p),$$

where $S_\delta$ is the scalar residual, coupling, and projection error defined in the joint range-invariance VSC estimate lemma. In particular,

$$\|K(\widehat r_\delta-r(x^\dagger))\|_Y=O(\delta),\quad \|Px_\delta\|_X=O(\delta),\quad Q(r(x_\delta),\widehat r_\delta)=O(\delta),$$

and the data residual $\|K\widehat r_\delta+F(x_0)-y^\delta\|_Y$ is $O(\delta)$.

For the following three-dimensional EIT specialization, assume the Axiom of Choice, Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Let $\Omega=B_1\subset\mathbb R^3$, let the known background be $1$ outside $B_\rho\Subset B_1$, and impose fixed bounds $0<m<1<M$ and $m\le\sigma\le M$. Let $s_1\in(5/2,7/2)$, use the intrinsic quadratic penalty $\frac12\|\sigma\|_{H^{s_1}(\Omega)}^2$ on this admissible class, and let $\sigma^\dagger\in B^{s_2}_{2,\infty}(\Omega)$ with $s_2\in(s_1,2s_1-1)$. The Sobolev norm is the exact intrinsic Hilbert norm in the EIT compatibility lemma. Use centered mean-zero Neumann voltage data $(\mathscr N_\sigma-\mathscr N_1)Y_{\ell k}$ in $Y=\ell^2(L^2(S^2))$, its observation-augmentation range coordinates, and admitted approximate joint minimizers in the set $U$ specified by that lemma. The artificial voltage is $z\in Y$ and the projection is $P(\sigma-\sigma_0,z)=(0,z)$. Put

$$\nu=\frac{(s_2-s_1)(2s_1-3)}{s_2-1},\qquad L_\delta=\log(1/\delta).$$

For fixed $\beta>0$, noise bounded by $\delta$, and $\eta_\delta=O(\delta^2)$, the balanced choice $\alpha\asymp\delta^2L_\delta^\nu$ gives

$$\|\sigma_\delta-\sigma^\dagger\|_{H^{s_1}(\Omega)}=O(L_\delta^{-\nu/2}),\qquad \|z_\delta\|_Y=O(\delta),\qquad S_\delta=O(\delta^2).$$

Every pure power $\alpha\asymp\delta^k$ with $0<k<2$ gives the same conductivity norm rate and $S_\delta=O(\delta^kL_\delta^{-\nu})$, hence $\|z_\delta\|_Y=O(\delta^{k/2}L_\delta^{-\nu/2})$. At the nominal endpoint $\alpha\asymp\delta^2$, the same conductivity norm rate holds under the explicit actual-noise and tolerance condition

$$2\|y^\delta-y\|_Y^2+\eta_\delta=O(\delta^2L_\delta^{-\nu});$$

then $S_\delta=O(\delta^2L_\delta^{-\nu})$ and $\|z_\delta\|_Y=O(\delta L_\delta^{-\nu/2})$. In each case the coupling distance and relaxed data residual have order $O(\sqrt{S_\delta}+\|y^\delta-y\|_Y)$. In particular the sum of the conductivity norm error and the artificial-voltage norm is $O(L_\delta^{-\nu/2})$ in all three stated regimes.

facts:
**Given:** For the generic assertion, the joint estimate lemma and parameter-index bounds in the first part of the Statement apply. For each EIT regime, use that regime's own stated parameter and noise conditions in the same joint comparison.

[A1] For the generic assertion, the parameter coupling satisfies $c_-\delta^p\le\alpha\rho_\delta\le c_+\delta^p$.

[A2] For the generic assertion, the conjugate values at $1/(C_*\alpha)$ and $1/(2C_*\alpha)$ are finite, and $H(1/(2C_*\alpha))\le C_H\rho_\delta$.

[F1] [[lem-ip-joint-range-invariance-vsc-estimate]]: $S_\delta+(1-b)\alpha e_\delta\le(2+C_\eta)\delta^p+\alpha\psi(C_*S_\delta)$.

[F2] [[lem-ip-index-function-young-conjugate-bound]]: if $c_1r+c_2\alpha e\le d+\alpha\psi(C_3r)$, then $e\le c_2^{-1}(d/\alpha+H(c_1/(C_3\alpha)))$ and $r\le2c_1^{-1}(d+\alpha H(c_1/(2C_3\alpha)))$.

[F3] [[def-ip-differential-range-invariance]]: $F(x)-F(x_0)=Kr(x)$, so $K r(x^\dagger)+F(x_0)=F(x^\dagger)$.

[A3] The EIT clauses use the Axiom of Choice, Countable Choice and Dependent Choice only at their local elliptic, Fourier, trace and Hilbert suppliers; the generic implication above retains its original assumptions.

[F4] [[lem-ip-eit-centered-range-invariance-vsc-and-frozen-compatibility]] verifies the centered EIT structural hypotheses with $p=2$, exact quadratic Bregman distance, $b=3/4$, and logarithmic source exponent $\nu$ displayed in the Statement.

[F5] [[lem-ip-logarithmic-index-conjugate-and-parameter-rates]] gives $H(q)\sim C(\log q)^{-\nu}$ and the balanced and strict-power scalar comparison rates.

[F6] [[lem-ip-logarithmic-endpoint-under-effective-noise-control]] gives the endpoint scalar rates with the explicitly strengthened actual noise and tolerance term.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the structural hypotheses of the frozen Newton one-step error lemma hold with fixed constants and notation. Let the initial pair be $(\widehat r_0,x_0)\in\widetilde U\times U$, where $x_0$ is the basepoint from the range-invariance factorization. At step $n\ge1$, freeze the objective at the previous iterate $x_{n-1}$, use parameters $\alpha_n$ and $\beta_n=c_{\beta\alpha}\alpha_n$, and let $(\widehat r_n,x_n)$ satisfy the resulting approximate-minimum inequality. Let $E_n$ and $S_n$ be the error and residual quantities from the one-step lemma for this step, with its input iterate relabeled $x_{n-1}$ and output iterate relabeled $x_n$. Define $E_0:=\frac{c_{\beta\alpha}}{C_\psi}\bigl(\lambda\|\widehat r_0-r(x^\dagger)\|_Z^p+t\|r(x_0)-r(x^\dagger)\|_Z^p\bigr)$. The parameter sequence $(\alpha_n)_{n\ge1}$ and the associated $h_n,\rho_n$ are fixed independently of $\delta$. Write

$$H(q):=\sup_{s\ge0}(\psi(s)-qs),\quad h_n:=H\!\left(\frac{1}{2\overline C\alpha_n}\right),\quad \rho_n:=\alpha_n h_n,\quad q:=\frac{v}{t},$$

where $t,v,\overline C$ are as in that lemma. Let $\alpha_n>0$ decrease strictly to zero, suppose $h_n$ is finite and positive, $\rho_n$ decreases strictly to zero, and assume for some $C_H\ge1$ that

$$h_n\le C_Hh_{n+1}\quad(n\ge1),\qquad qC_H<1.$$

Assume each step through $N$ satisfies the one-step lemma, has tolerance $\eta_n\le C_\eta\rho_n$, and the initial error $E_0$ is finite. Assume also that for every sufficiently small $\delta>0$ there is an index $N=N(\delta)\ge2$ such that

$$\rho_N\ge\tau\delta^p,\qquad \rho_N\le M\tau\delta^p,\qquad \rho_n\ge\tau\delta^p\quad(1\le n\le N),$$

for constants $\tau,M>0$ independent of $\delta$. This bounded crossing condition is satisfied, for example, if $N$ is the last index with $\rho_N\ge\tau\delta^p$ and $\rho_n/\rho_{n+1}\le M$ for all $n$.

Then the stopping iterate $(\widehat r_N,x_N)$ satisfies

$$E_N=O(h_N),\qquad S_N=O(\delta^p),$$

and therefore

$$\|\widehat r_N-r(x^\dagger)\|_Z^p+\|r(x_N)-r(x^\dagger)\|_Z^p=O(h_N),$$

$$\|K(\widehat r_N-r(x^\dagger))\|_Y=O(\delta),\qquad \|Px_N\|_X=O(\delta),\qquad \|K\widehat r_N+F(x_0)-y^\delta\|_Y=O(\delta).$$

If $\Phi(a):=aH(1/(2\overline C a))$ has a strictly increasing inverse $\phi$ on the relevant range, then

$$h_N\le H\!\left(\frac{1}{2\overline C\,\phi(M\tau\delta^p)}\right),$$

which gives the corresponding source-index rate for the range-variable and nonlinear-range errors.

For the following three-dimensional EIT specialization, assume the Axiom of Choice, Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Let $\Omega=B_1\subset\mathbb R^3$, let the known conductivity be $1$ outside $B_\rho\Subset B_1$, impose fixed positive upper and lower conductivity bounds, use the exact intrinsic quadratic $H^{s_1}(\Omega)$ penalty with $s_1\in(5/2,7/2)$, and assume $\sigma^\dagger\in B^{s_2}_{2,\infty}(\Omega)$ for $s_2\in(s_1,2s_1-1)$. Use the centered mean-zero Neumann voltage map in $Y=\ell^2(L^2(S^2))$ and the explicit observation augmentation, admitted neighborhood $U$, penalty $R_P$, and linked-parameter constants in the EIT compatibility lemma. Choose the initial conductivity sufficiently close to the truth that its radius condition $LR<c_{\rm tcr}<1/\sqrt{20}$ holds, and choose a fixed initial range variable in $r(U)$, independently of noise. Put

$$\nu=\frac{(s_2-s_1)(2s_1-3)}{s_2-1},\qquad L_\delta=\log(1/\delta).$$

Take a fixed geometric parameter sequence, starting sufficiently far down its tail that the conjugate growth condition above holds, set $\beta_n=c_{\beta\alpha}\alpha_n$, and use admitted approximate steps with $\eta_n\le C_\eta\rho_n$. For a positive target $w_\delta$, stop at the last index $N$ with $\rho_N\ge\tau w_\delta$. If the actual squared data noise is $O(w_\delta)$, then

$$\|\sigma_N-\sigma^\dagger\|_{H^{s_1}(\Omega)}=O(L_\delta^{-\nu/2}),\qquad \|z_N\|_Y=O(\sqrt{w_\delta}),\qquad \|K\widehat r_N+F(x_0)-y^\delta\|_Y=O(\sqrt{w_\delta})$$

in each of the following regimes: $w_\delta=\delta^2$ for the balanced choice $\alpha_N\asymp\delta^2L_\delta^\nu$ and ordinary noise bounded by $\delta$; $w_\delta=\delta^kL_\delta^{-\nu}$ for every $0<k<2$, giving $\alpha_N\asymp\delta^k$ under the same ordinary noise bound; and $w_\delta=\delta^2L_\delta^{-\nu}$ for the nominal endpoint $\alpha_N\asymp\delta^2$, under the explicit stronger actual-noise condition $\|y^\delta-y\|_Y^2=O(\delta^2L_\delta^{-\nu})$. All tolerances remain bounded by $C_\eta\rho_n$ through the stopping index. Thus the total conductivity and artificial-voltage norm error has logarithmic exponent $\nu/2$ in every stated regime.

facts:
**Given:** For the generic assertion, every $n\le N$ satisfies the stated one-step and stopping hypotheses. For the EIT regimes, use their own stated actual-noise upper bound in those same hypotheses, with fixed structural constants and a fixed parameter sequence.

[A1] $\rho_n=\alpha_nh_n\ge\tau\delta^p$ for $1\le n\le N$ and $\rho_N\le M\tau\delta^p$.

[A2] The tolerances satisfy $\eta_n\le C_\eta\alpha_nh_n$.

contract.heading: Example
contract.text: Let $U=(-6,6)^2\subset\mathbb R^2$, let $\phi(s):=s+9\int_0^s e^{-u^2}\,du$, and define the partially observed map $F:U\to\mathbb R$ by $F(s,t):=\phi(s)$. With basepoint $x_0=(0,0)$, set $Z=\mathbb R^2$, $K(a,b):=10a$, and $r(s,t):=(\phi(s)/10,t)$. Then $F(x)-F(x_0)=Kr(x)$ for every $x\in U$, and $r$ is bi-Lipschitz on $U$. Nevertheless, the local tangential cone condition at $x_0$ fails on radius $5$ for every allowed constant $0\le\eta<1$. The second parameter $t$ is unobserved: all points $(0,t)$ give the datum $0$.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open and let $u\in L^1(\Omega;\mathbb R)$, where elements of $L^1$ are almost-everywhere equivalence classes. For each $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, its distributional derivative $D_i u$ acts on $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ by
$$\langle D_i u,\varphi\rangle:=-\int_\Omega u\,\partial_i\varphi\,dx.$$
The function $u$ is in $BV(\Omega)$ when each $D_i u$ is represented by a finite signed Radon measure and the resulting vector-valued measure $Du=(D_1u,\ldots,D_nu)$ has finite total variation. Here a finite vector-valued Radon measure means that its partition variation is a finite Radon measure. For a Borel set $A\subseteq\Omega$, define
$$|Du|(A):=\sup\left\{\sum_{j=1}^\infty |Du(A_j)|:\ (A_j)_{j\ge1}\text{ is a Borel partition of }A\right\},$$
using the Euclidean norm on each vector value. Define the spatial total variation by $TV(u;\Omega):=|Du|(\Omega)$. A Lebesgue-measurable set $E\subseteq\Omega$ of finite measure has finite perimeter relative to $\Omega$ when $\chi_E\in BV(\Omega)$; its relative perimeter is $P(E;\Omega):=TV(\chi_E;\Omega)$.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ be open and let $X=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$. Every $u\in X$ is integrable on compact subsets by Cauchy–Schwarz. Define its extended distributional total variation by
$$TV_2(u;\Omega):=\sup\left\{\int_\Omega u\,\operatorname{div}\varphi\,dx:\ \varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^2),\ \sup_{x\in\Omega}|\varphi(x)|\le1\right\}\in[0,+\infty],$$
where $C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^2)$ denotes smooth compactly supported vector fields, $|\cdot|$ is the Euclidean norm, and $\operatorname{div}\varphi=\partial_1\varphi_1+\partial_2\varphi_2$. This definition treats $L^2$ functions as almost-everywhere classes and does not require $u\in L^1(\Omega)$.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $u\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^2)$, with functions identified when they agree almost everywhere. For full-space TV, use $u$ itself. For a bounded-domain Dirichlet or Neumann problem, use the zero extension $\widetilde u$ only to define the geometric level sets; this does not change the selected regularizer, and for each nonzero level the resulting set lies inside $\Omega$. For $t>0$, the positive $t$-level class is the measurable-set class of $E_t^+(u):=\{x\in\mathbb R^2:u(x)>t\}$; for $t<0$, the negative $t$-level class is the class of $E_t^-(u):=\{x\in\mathbb R^2:u(x)<t\}$. These classes do not depend on the representative of $u$. For any measurable set $E\subseteq\mathbb R^2$, its density-one representative is

$$E^{(1)}:=\left\{x\in\mathbb R^2:\lim_{r\downarrow0}\frac{|E\cap B(x,r)|}{|B(x,r)|}=1\right\}.$$

This representative depends only on the almost-everywhere class of $E$. The canonical level set $U_u^{(t)}$ is $(E_t^+(u))^{(1)}$ when $t>0$ and $(E_t^-(u))^{(1)}$ when $t<0$. Its canonical boundary is the ordinary topological boundary $\partial U_u^{(t)}$ in $\mathbb R^2$. For two nonempty boundary sets, use the usual extended Hausdorff distance induced by Euclidean distance; set $d_H(\varnothing,\varnothing)=0$ and $d_H(E,F)=+\infty$ if exactly one set is empty. Hausdorff convergence uses this convention and is invariant under changes to a function on a null set.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text: Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain, meaning a bounded open set whose boundary has a finite cover by coordinate neighborhoods in which it is the graph of a Lipschitz function and $\Omega$ lies on one side of that graph. For $u\in BV(\Omega)$ define the Neumann total variation by $TV_N(u;\Omega):=|Du|(\Omega)$. Define its zero extension $\widetilde u\in L^1(\mathbb R^n)$ by $\widetilde u=u$ almost everywhere on $\Omega$ and $\widetilde u=0$ almost everywhere on $\mathbb R^n\setminus\Omega$. Define the Dirichlet total variation by $TV_D(u;\Omega):=TV(\widetilde u;\mathbb R^n)$ when $\widetilde u\in BV(\mathbb R^n)$ and by $TV_D(u;\Omega):=+\infty$ otherwise. For $v\in BV(\mathbb R^n)$ define the full-space total variation by $TV_F(v):=TV(v;\mathbb R^n)$. Thus Neumann variation counts only the distributional derivative inside $\Omega$, while Dirichlet variation also counts any jump created by zero extension across $\partial\Omega$.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $\Omega=\mathbb R^2$ or let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain. Choose one of three perimeter functionals for measurable $E\subseteq\Omega$: full-space perimeter $P_R(E)=P(E;\mathbb R^2)$ when $\Omega=\mathbb R^2$; Neumann relative perimeter $P_N(E)=P(E;\Omega)$ on a bounded domain; or Dirichlet perimeter $P_D(E)=P(\widetilde E;\mathbb R^2)$, where $\widetilde E$ is $E$ extended by the empty set outside $\Omega$. Require finite measure and finite selected perimeter, and let $\kappa$ be measurable with $\int_F|\kappa|<\infty$ for every set considered. The set $E$ has **variational curvature** $\kappa$ for the selected model if its selected perimeter minus $\int_E\kappa\,dx$ is no greater than the same quantity for every finite-measure finite-selected-perimeter competitor $F\subseteq\Omega$ whose symmetric difference $F\mathbin\triangle E$ has compact closure in $\Omega$. In the full-space model, this means compact closure in $\mathbb R^2$.

For bounded Dirichlet TV, a separate **obstacle curvature** condition on $\Omega$ means that $\Omega$, viewed as a finite-perimeter set in $\mathbb R^2$, minimizes $F\mapsto P(F;\mathbb R^2)-\int_F\kappa_\Omega\,dx$ over all finite-measure finite-perimeter $F\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ whose symmetric difference with $\Omega$ has compact closure in $\mathbb R^2$.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $\Omega=\mathbb R^2$, or let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain. Set $X=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ and let $Y=L^2(\Sigma,\mu;\mathbb R)$ for a measure space $(\Sigma,\mu)$, using the real integral inner products. Let $A:X\to Y$ be bounded and real-linear, and let $A^*:Y\to X$ be its Hilbert adjoint, characterized by $\langle Au,p\rangle_Y=\langle u,A^*p\rangle_X$. Define $R:X\to[0,+\infty]$ as follows. If $\Omega=\mathbb R^2$, take $R(u)=TV_2(u;\mathbb R^2)$, the supremum of $\int u\,\operatorname{div}\varphi$ over smooth compactly supported vector fields of Euclidean norm at most one. For bounded $\Omega$, either take Neumann TV, $R(u)=TV(u;\Omega)$ when $u\in BV(\Omega)$ and $+\infty$ otherwise, or Dirichlet TV, $R(u)=TV(\widetilde u;\mathbb R^2)$ when the zero extension $\widetilde u$ belongs to $BV(\mathbb R^2)$ and $+\infty$ otherwise. Thus the bounded-domain choices count, respectively, only the interior derivative or also the jump of the zero extension across the boundary. In the full-space case finite $R$ does not require global $L^1$ integrability.

Identify each $q\in X$ with the continuous linear functional $h\mapsto\langle q,h\rangle_X$ by the real Hilbert-space Riesz representation. For exact data $f=Au^\dagger$, a **minimum-TV exact solution** is a point $u^\dagger\in X$ satisfying $Au^\dagger=f$ and $R(u^\dagger)\le R(u)$ for every $u\in X$ with $Au=f$. A vector $p^\dagger\in Y$ is a **dual source certificate** for $u^\dagger$ if $A^*p^\dagger\in\partial R(u^\dagger)$, where $\partial R$ is the convex subdifferential on the real Banach space $X$. The **TV source condition** at $u^\dagger$ is that such a certificate exists; it does not assert uniqueness of the truth or of the certificate. For a chosen certificate, the associated Bregman distance is

$$D_R^{A^*p^\dagger}(u,u^\dagger):=R(u)-R(u^\dagger)-\langle A^*p^\dagger,u-u^\dagger\rangle_X,$$

for $u\in\operatorname{dom}R$.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume Countable Choice. If $u\in L^2(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb R)$ and $TV_2(u;\mathbb R^2)<\infty$, there exist smooth cutoffs $\chi_k$ with $0\le\chi_k\le1$, $\chi_k=1$ on $B(0,k)$, support in $B(0,2k)$, and $\sup_{k\ge1}k\|\nabla\chi_k\|_\infty<\infty$. For every family satisfying these four conditions, $v_k:=\chi_ku$ belongs to $BV(\mathbb R^2)\cap L^1(\mathbb R^2)$, has support in $B(0,2k)$, converges to $u$ in $L^2(\mathbb R^2)$, and
$$\limsup_{k\to\infty}TV(v_k;\mathbb R^2)\le TV_2(u;\mathbb R^2).$$

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $X=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ and $Y=L^2(\Sigma,\mu;\mathbb R)$ be real Hilbert spaces, let $A:X\to Y$ be bounded and real-linear, and let $R:X\to[0,+\infty]$ be one of the full-space, Dirichlet, or Neumann TV functionals. Assume that $R$ is proper, convex, lower semicontinuous, and positively one-homogeneous, and that $u^\dagger$ is a minimum-$R$ exact solution of $Au=f$ with a dual source certificate $p^\dagger\in Y$, so $A^*p^\dagger\in\partial R(u^\dagger)$. Define $K:=\{p\in Y:A^*p\in\partial R(0)\}$ and $D_{\alpha,w}(p):=\langle f+w,p\rangle_Y-\frac{\alpha}{2}\|p\|_Y^2$ for $\alpha>0$ and $w\in Y$.

For each $\alpha>0$ and $w\in Y$, $D_{\alpha,w}$ has a unique maximizer $p_{\alpha,w}=\operatorname{Proj}_K((f+w)/\alpha)$. If $u_{\alpha,w}$ is any supplied global minimizer of $u\mapsto\frac12\|Au-(f+w)\|_Y^2+\alpha R(u)$, then $p_{\alpha,w}=(f+w-Au_{\alpha,w})/\alpha$, $A^*p_{\alpha,w}\in\partial R(u_{\alpha,w})$, and $A^*p_{\alpha,w}\in\partial R(0)$. For every such supplied minimizer, the correctly normalized primal-dual value identity is

$$\min_u\{\tfrac12\|Au-(f+w)\|_Y^2+\alpha R(u)\}=\alpha D_{\alpha,w}(p_{\alpha,w}).$$

Let $P_0:=\{p\in K:\langle f,p\rangle_Y=R(u^\dagger)\}$ and let $p_0$ be its unique minimum-norm element. For every sequence $\alpha_n>0$ with $\alpha_n\to0$, $p_{\alpha_n,0}\to p_0$ strongly in $Y$ and $A^*p_{\alpha_n,0}\to A^*p_0$ strongly in $X$. For every $\alpha>0$ and $w\in Y$,

$$\|p_{\alpha,w}-p_{\alpha,0}\|_Y\le\frac{\|w\|_Y}{\alpha},\qquad \|A^*p_{\alpha,w}-A^*p_{\alpha,0}\|_X\le\frac{\|A^*\|\,\|w\|_Y}{\alpha}.$$

Moreover, for any $R_0>R(u^\dagger)$ the certificate yields a variational source condition on $\{u:R(u)\le R_0\}$ with exponent $2$, coefficient $\beta=0$, and index function $\psi(s)=(1+\|p^\dagger\|_Y)\sqrt{s}$. Consequently, if $\delta_n\downarrow0$, $\|w_n\|_Y\le\delta_n$, $\alpha_n\asymp\delta_n$, and exact global minimizers $u_n$ are supplied, then the variational-source rate theorem gives

$$D_R^{A^*p^\dagger}(u_n,u^\dagger)=O(\delta_n),\qquad \|Au_n-(f+w_n)\|_Y=O(\delta_n).$$

facts:
**Given:** Countable Choice, the real Hilbert spaces and map in the Statement, a minimum-TV exact solution, a dual source certificate, and (where specified) supplied global minimizers.

[A1] Countable Choice supplies the nearest-point minimizing sequences and weakly convergent subsequences used below. ([[def-countable-choice]])

[F1] [[def-ip-tv-dual-source-certificate]]: $u^\dagger$ is an exact minimum-TV solution and $A^*p^\dagger\in\partial R(u^\dagger)$; the Hilbert adjoint satisfies $\langle Au,p\rangle_Y=\langle u,A^*p\rangle_X$.

[F2] [[def-ip-banach-convex-subgradient-and-dual-pairing]]: $\xi\in\partial R(u)$ exactly when $R(z)\ge R(u)+\langle\xi,z-u\rangle$ for every $z\in X$.

[F3] [[def-ip-bregman-distance]]: $D_R^{\xi^\dagger}(u,u^\dagger)=R(u)-R(u^\dagger)-\langle\xi^\dagger,u-u^\dagger\rangle_X$.

[F4] [[lem-ip-banach-fenchel-duality-for-regularization]]: $R(u)+R^*(\xi)=\langle\xi,u\rangle$ if and only if $\xi\in\partial R(u)$.

[F5] [[def-ip-variational-source-condition]]: on a named sublevel, $-\langle\xi^\dagger,u-u^\dagger\rangle\le\beta D_R^{\xi^\dagger}(u,u^\dagger)+\psi(\|Au-Au^\dagger\|_Y^2)$.

[F6] [[thm-ip-vsc-nonlinear-regularization-rate]]: when the exact global minimizer, noise bound, sublevel VSC, and conjugate parameter coupling hold, the Bregman distance and noisy residual have the displayed rates.

[F7] [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-in-an-inner-product-space]]: $|\langle u,v\rangle|\le\|u\|\,\|v\|$ in a real Hilbert space.

[F8] [[thm-bolzano-weierstrass]]: every bounded real sequence has a convergent subsequence.

[F9] [[thm-riesz-representation-for-hilbert-space]]: every bounded linear functional on a real Hilbert space is inner product with a vector in that space.

[F10] [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]: the real Hilbert norm satisfies $\|y\|_Y^2=\langle y,y\rangle_Y$.

contract.text:
Let $X$ be a real Banach space, let $R:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ be proper and convex, and define its Fenchel conjugate $R^*:X^*\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ by $R^*(\xi):=\sup_{z\in X}(\langle\xi,z\rangle_{X^*,X}-R(z))$. For every $x\in\operatorname{dom}R$ and $\xi\in X^*$, the Fenchel–Young inequality and its equality characterization are

$$R(x)+R^*(\xi)\ge\langle\xi,x\rangle_{X^*,X},\qquad R(x)+R^*(\xi)=\langle\xi,x\rangle_{X^*,X}\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \xi\in\partial R(x).$$

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, let $u\in BV(\Omega)$, and for $t>0$ set $E_t^+:=\{x\in\Omega:u(x)>t\}$ while for $t<0$ set $E_t^-:=\{x\in\Omega:u(x)<t\}$. Then for almost every applicable $t$ these sets have finite perimeter relative to $\Omega$, and $$TV(u;\Omega)=\int_0^\infty P(E_t^+;\Omega)\,dt+\int_{-\infty}^0P(E_t^-;\Omega)\,dt.$$

contract.text:

$$TV_2(u;\mathbb R^2)=\int_0^\infty P(E_t^+;\mathbb R^2)\,dt+\int_{-\infty}^0P(E_t^-;\mathbb R^2)\,dt.$$

[F5] [[thm-fatou-lemma]] and [[thm-monotone-convergence-for-the-integral]]: Fatou bounds the limiting perimeter integrals, and increasing truncations of nonnegative level integrals converge to the full integral.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $X=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ and let $Y=L^2(\Sigma,\mu;\mathbb R)$ be real Hilbert spaces. Let $A:X\to Y$ be bounded and real-linear, let $f=Au^\dagger$, and assume $u^\dagger$ is an exact solution minimizing a proper, convex, lower semicontinuous, positively one-homogeneous TV functional $R:X\to[0,+\infty]$ with a source certificate $p^\dagger\in Y$, so $A^*p^\dagger\in\partial R(u^\dagger)$. Use full-space $R=TV_2(\cdot;\mathbb R^2)$ if $\Omega=\mathbb R^2$; for a bounded connected Lipschitz $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^2$, use either Neumann $R(u)=TV(u;\Omega)$ or Dirichlet $R(u)=TV(\widetilde u;\mathbb R^2)$ for the zero extension $\widetilde u$, assigning $+\infty$ outside the respective finite-variation domain. A bounded connected Lipschitz domain here is a bounded open set with a finite Lipschitz graph cover of its boundary, with the domain on one side of each graph, and it has no separation into two disjoint nonempty relatively open sets.

Let $\alpha_n>0$ tend to zero, let $w_n\in Y$, and suppose $\|A^*\|\,\|w_n\|_Y/\alpha_n\le\eta$ for some finite $\eta$. For each $n$, suppose a supplied global minimizer $u_n\in X$ minimizes
$$J_n(u)=\tfrac12\|Au-(f+w_n)\|_Y^2+\alpha_nR(u).$$
In the Neumann case, if $A\mathbf1_\Omega=0$, take $u_n$ after subtracting its mean $|\Omega|^{-1}\int_\Omega u_n$; this leaves $J_n$ unchanged. Then a subsequence converges weakly in $L^2(\Omega)$ and, in addition, strongly in $L^1(\Omega)$ when $\Omega$ is bounded or strongly in $L^1$ on every bounded ball when $\Omega=\mathbb R^2$. Its limit $u_0$ is an exact solution $Au_0=f$ minimizing $R$ among exact solutions, and $A^*p^\dagger\in\partial R(u_0)$.

facts:
**Given:** The objects and hypotheses in the Statement, including supplied global minimizers of $J_n$.

[A1] Countable Choice supplies the countable diagonal selections in the compactness and weak-subsequence arguments. ([[def-countable-choice]])

[F1] [[def-ip-tv-dual-source-certificate]]: $Au^\dagger=f$, $R(u^\dagger)$ is minimal over exact solutions, and $A^*p^\dagger\in\partial R(u^\dagger)$; the Hilbert adjoint satisfies $\langle Au,p\rangle_Y=\langle u,A^*p\rangle_X$.

[F2] [[lem-ip-tv-dual-attainment-and-certificate-limit]]: every supplied global minimizer has $p_{\alpha,w}=(f+w-Au_{\alpha,w})/\alpha$, the exact-data fields $p_{\alpha,0}$ remain bounded as $\alpha\to0$, and $\|p_{\alpha,w}-p_{\alpha,0}\|_Y\le\|w\|_Y/\alpha$.

[F3] [[lem-ip-bv-compactness-lower-semicontinuity]]: bounded-domain BV sequences with bounded $L^1$ norm and variation have an $L^1$-convergent subsequence, and TV is lower semicontinuous under $L^1$ convergence.

[F4] [[lem-ip-bv-sobolev-inequality]]: in two dimensions, $\|v\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^2)}\le TV(v;\mathbb R^2)$ for $v\in BV(\mathbb R^2)$.

[F5] [[lem-ip-tv-l2-sobolev-inequality]]: the same estimate holds for $u\in L^2(\mathbb R^2)$ with finite extended variation: $\|u\|_2\le TV_2(u;\mathbb R^2)$.

[F6] [[lem-ip-bv-zero-gradient-constant-on-connected-domain]]: a locally integrable function with zero distributional gradient on a connected open domain is a.e. constant.

[F7] [[def-ip-boundary-tv-conventions]]: Neumann TV is unchanged by adding constants; Dirichlet TV is the full-space TV of the zero extension and dominates the interior variation.

[F8] [[lem-ip-bv-test-field-characterization-and-lsc]]: spatial TV is lower semicontinuous in $L^1$ and finite whenever the extended test-field variation is finite under Countable Choice.

[F9] [[lem-ip-tv-l2-finite-variation-has-radon-derivative]]: finite $TV_2$ gives a finite vector Radon derivative measure, whose restriction to bounded balls has variation at most $TV_2(u;\mathbb R^2)$.

[F10] [[thm-bolzano-weierstrass]]: bounded scalar real sequences have convergent subsequences.

[F11] [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-in-an-inner-product-space]]: $|\langle x,y\rangle|\le\|x\|\|y\|$.

[F12] [[thm-riesz-representation-for-hilbert-space]]: bounded linear functionals on a real Hilbert space are inner products with vectors in that space.

[F13] [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]: two locally integrable functions that define the same distribution are equal almost everywhere.

[F14] [[lem-ip-neumann-bv-sobolev-poincare]]: on a bounded connected Lipschitz domain, $\|u-u_\Omega\|_2\le C_\Omega TV(u;\Omega)$ for a fixed finite $C_\Omega$.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $A:L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)\to L^2(\Sigma,\mu;\mathbb R)$ be bounded and real-linear, let $f=Au^\dagger$, and suppose $u^\dagger$ is a minimum-TV exact solution with a source certificate $p^\dagger$. For $\alpha_n>0$ tending to zero and noises $w_n\in L^2(\Sigma,\mu;\mathbb R)$, assume $\|A^*\|\|w_n\|_2/\alpha_n\le\eta$ and let $u_n$ be supplied global minimizers of $\frac12\|Au-(f+w_n)\|_2^2+\alpha_n TV(u)$. Define $p_n=(f+w_n-Au_n)/\alpha_n$ and $v_n=A^*p_n$. Use $TV_2$ on $L^2(\mathbb R^2)$ for full-space TV, zero-extension Dirichlet TV on a bounded Lipschitz domain, and relative Neumann TV on a bounded connected Lipschitz domain; for bounded-domain geometry use the ambient zero-extended level sets and their topological boundaries in $\mathbb R^2$.

For full-space or Dirichlet TV, assume $\eta<2\sqrt\pi$; in the bounded Dirichlet case also assume $\Omega$ has global obstacle curvature $\kappa_\Omega\in L^1(\mathbb R^2)$ with $\kappa_\Omega\ge g$ almost everywhere outside $\Omega$ for some $g\in L^2(\mathbb R^2\setminus\Omega)$. For Neumann TV, let $C_\Omega$ be a constant from the BV Sobolev–Poincaré inequality $\|u-u_\Omega\|_2\le C_\Omega TV(u;\Omega)$ and assume $\eta<1/C_\Omega$.

For almost every nonzero $t$, the level set $E_n(t)$ has finite measure and perimeter, minimizes the branch-specific perimeter minus $\int_{E}\operatorname{sgn}(t)v_n$ under compactly supported perturbations, and satisfies $P(E_n(t))=\operatorname{sgn}(t)\int_{E_n(t)}v_n$. There are constants $c>0$ and $r_0>0$, independent of $n$ and almost every such $t$, such that for every $x\in\partial E_n(t)$ and $0<r<r_0$,
$$|B(x,r)\cap E_n(t)|\ge c|B(x,r)|,\qquad |B(x,r)\setminus E_n(t)|\ge c|B(x,r)|.$$
In the full-space branch all these level sets are contained in one common ball; in the bounded branches they lie in $\overline\Omega$. The same density and support conclusions are asserted for any selected minimum-TV exact limit that carries the inherited source certificate, using zero noise. Whenever the corresponding level sets converge in measure, their canonical boundaries converge in Hausdorff distance.

facts:
**Given:** Countable Choice, the linear map and TV branch, a minimum-TV exact source-certified truth, the noise condition, and supplied global regularized minimizers as in the Statement.

[A1] Countable Choice is used by the coarea, BV representation, and compactness suppliers. ([[def-countable-choice]])

[F1] [[lem-ip-tv-dual-attainment-and-certificate-limit]]: each supplied minimizer has $p_n=(f+w_n-Au_n)/\alpha_n$, $v_n=A^*p_n\in\partial TV(u_n)\cap\partial TV(0)$, the exact-data fields $v_{\alpha_n,0}$ converge strongly in $L^2$ to $v_0$, and $\|v_n-v_{\alpha_n,0}\|_2\le\|A^*\|\|w_n\|_2/\alpha_n\le\eta$.

[F2] [[def-ip-tv-dual-source-certificate]]: the initial exact truth is minimum-TV and the source certificate supplies a subgradient in the real Hilbert pairing.

[F3] [[def-ip-tv-level-set-representatives-and-boundaries]]: for $t>0$ use the density-one representative of $\{u>t\}$; for $t<0$ use that of $\{u<t\}$; bounded-domain sets are viewed by zero extension solely for their ambient geometry.

[F4] [[lem-ip-tv-l2-coarea-formula]] and [[lem-ip-bv-coarea-formula]]: full-space finite-variation $L^2$ functions and bounded-domain BV functions have the corresponding positive-superlevel/negative-sublevel coarea identities.

[F5] [[def-ip-tv-variational-curvature]]: variational curvature means minimization of the branch-specific perimeter minus the signed integral of its curvature over compactly supported symmetric-difference perturbations.

[F6] [[lem-ip-planar-isoperimetric-inequality-for-finite-perimeter-sets]]: $4\pi|E|\le P(E;\mathbb R^2)^2$ for finite-area finite-perimeter planar sets.

[F10] Actual ball-cut and obstacle comparisons, uniform two-sided density in all three branches, and a common full-space support bound follow from distributional ball products and radial-tail extinction. [[lem-ip-tv-finite-perimeter-ball-cut-calculus]], [[lem-ip-tv-uniform-density-and-radial-support-for-curvature-minimizers]]

[F12] The distributional L2 TV is proper, convex, lower semicontinuous and positively one-homogeneous, and agrees with BV TV on integrable functions. [[lem-ip-tv-l2-functional-properties]]

[F11] A bounded Lipschitz-domain BV indicator has a BV zero extension, so its ambient perimeter is finite even in the Neumann branch. Completed Fubini and Tonelli apply to the signed layer-cake integrals when their absolute integral is finite. [[lem-ip-bv-lipschitz-trace-and-zero-extension]], [[thm-tonelli-and-fubini-for-completed-product-measures]]

[F13] The real Hilbert pairing satisfies Cauchy–Schwarz. [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-in-an-inner-product-space]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume Countable Choice. Here $\mathcal H^m$ on a boundary denotes normalized Hausdorff measure: the repository's unnormalised $m$-dimensional Hausdorff measure divided by $c_m=H^m((0,1]^m)$ for $m\ge1$, and counting measure for $m=0$. Let $n\ge2$ and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain, meaning a bounded open set whose boundary has a finite cover by coordinate neighborhoods in which it is the graph of a Lipschitz function and $\Omega$ lies on one side of the graph. There is a unique bounded linear trace operator $T:BV(\Omega)\to L^1(\partial\Omega,\mathcal H^{n-1})$ such that for every $u\in BV(\Omega)$ and $\phi\in C_c^1(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb R^n)$, $$\int_\Omega u\,\operatorname{div}\phi\,dx=-\int_\Omega\phi\cdot dDu+\int_{\partial\Omega}Tu\,\phi\cdot\nu\,d\mathcal H^{n-1},$$ where $\nu$ is the outward unit normal defined almost everywhere on $\partial\Omega$. The zero extension $\widetilde u$ belongs to $BV(\mathbb R^n)$ and satisfies $$TV(\widetilde u;\mathbb R^n)=TV(u;\Omega)+\|Tu\|_{L^1(\partial\Omega)}\le C_\Omega\bigl(\|u\|_{L^1(\Omega)}+TV(u;\Omega)\bigr)$$ for a finite constant $C_\Omega$ depending only on the domain. The same conclusions hold in dimension one for a bounded open set with a finite one-sided graph cover, with the two one-sided endpoint traces and counting measure on its finite boundary.

facts:
**Given:** Countable Choice, a bounded Lipschitz domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, and $u\in BV(\Omega)$.

[F1] Every smaller Lipschitz graph chart has a linear one-sided $L^1$ trace, its local norm estimate, and the local BV Green formula. Traces agree on overlapping charts. The same result supplies the endpoint case in dimension one. ([[lem-ip-bv-one-sided-trace-on-lipschitz-graph]])

[F2] Normalized Hausdorff measure on a Lipschitz graph has density $\sqrt{1+|Dh|^2}$, with its almost-everywhere unit outward normal. ([[lem-ip-lipschitz-graph-area-and-calculus-under-countable-choice]])

[F3] Compact sets admit finite smooth cutoff covers, and finite signed Radon measures are determined by smooth compactly supported tests. ([[lem-smooth-bump-between-concentric-euclidean-balls]], [[lem-ip-distributional-radon-representation-unique]])

[F4] A finite vector of signed Radon measures has finite Radon partition variation. ([[lem-ip-vector-radon-variation-is-radon]])

contract.heading: Statement refuted
contract.text: The claim that every minimum-TV exact truth in a two-dimensional Neumann model has an $L^2$ source certificate is false. Let $\Omega=(-1,1)^2$, let $X=Y=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$, let $A:X\to Y$ be the identity, let $f=u^\dagger$ with $u^\dagger(x_1,x_2)=|x_1|$, and let the regularizer be the Neumann total variation $R(u)=|Du|(\Omega)$ on $BV(\Omega)\cap L^2(\Omega)$ and $R(u)=+\infty$ otherwise. The exact equation $Au=f$ has the unique solution $u^\dagger$, so it is a minimum-TV exact truth. Nevertheless, there is no $p\in L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ such that $A^*p=p\in\partial R(u^\dagger)$, where $p\in\partial R(u^\dagger)$ means $R(v)\ge R(u^\dagger)+\int_\Omega p(v-u^\dagger)\,dx$ for every $v\in L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$.

facts:
**Given:** $\Omega=(-1,1)^2$, $X=Y=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$, $A=I$, $u^\dagger(x_1,x_2)=|x_1|$, $f=u^\dagger$, and $R=TV_N$ as specified in the Statement.

[F1] [[def-ip-spatial-bv-and-distributional-tv]]: $Du$ is the vector of distributional derivatives and $TV(u;\Omega)$ is the partition variation $|Du|(\Omega)$.

[F2] [[def-ip-boundary-tv-conventions]]: in the Neumann convention, $R(u)=TV(u;\Omega)$ for $u\in BV(\Omega)$.

[F3] [[def-ip-banach-convex-subgradient-and-dual-pairing]]: $p\in\partial R(u)$ exactly when $R(v)\ge R(u)+\langle p,v-u\rangle_{L^2}$ for every $v\in L^2(\Omega)$.

[F4] [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]: the real $L^2$ inner product is $\langle p,v\rangle=\int_\Omega pv\,dx$; Cauchy–Schwarz bounds its absolute value by $\|p\|_2\|v\|_2$. ([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-in-an-inner-product-space]])

[F5] [[thm-tonelli-and-fubini-for-completed-product-measures]]: integrable functions on this rectangle may be integrated by iterated one-dimensional integration.

[F6] [[thm-lebesgue-measure-is-a-radon-measure-on-rn]]: Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb R^2$ is Radon; an integrable density gives a finite Radon measure on the bounded domain.

[F7] [[lem-ip-vector-radon-variation-is-radon]]: the partition variation of a finite vector Radon measure is a finite positive Radon measure.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Let $0<a<b$, let $\phi\in C_c^\infty((a,b))$ be nonnegative and not identically zero, define $U(r)=\int_r^b\phi(s)\,ds$ for $r\ge0$, and set $u^\dagger(x)=U(|x|)$ on $\mathbb R^2$. Choose $h\in C_c^\infty((a/2,2b))$ with $0\le h\le1$ and $h=1$ on $\operatorname{supp}\phi$, put $z(x)=h(|x|)x/|x|$ extended by zero at the origin, and let $q=\operatorname{div}z$. On real $L^2(\mathbb R^2)$ define the Bessel blur $A=\mathcal F_2^{-1}M_m\mathcal F_2$, where $\mathcal F_2$ is the unitary Fourier transform with phase $e^{-2\pi i x\cdot\xi}$ and $M_m$ multiplies by $m(\xi)=(1+4\pi^2|\xi|^2)^{-1/2}$. Let $f=Au^\dagger$ and define $p=\mathcal F_2^{-1}\bigl((1+4\pi^2|\xi|^2)^{1/2}\widehat q(\xi)\bigr)$. Then $A$ is bounded, self-adjoint, and injective, $p\in L^2(\mathbb R^2)$, and $A^*p\in\partial TV_2(u^\dagger)$. Thus $u^\dagger$ is the unique minimum-TV exact solution satisfying the full-space source condition; for zero noise the parameter ratio $\|A^*\|\|w_n\|_2/\alpha_n$ is zero.

facts:
**Given:** The nonzero nonnegative radial profile $\phi$, the radial truth $u^\dagger$, the Fourier multiplier $m$, and full-space $TV_2$.

[A1] Countable Choice is assumed by the Plancherel supplier. ([[def-countable-choice]])

[F1] [[thm-plancherel]]: $\mathcal F_2$ is a unitary map on complex $L^2(\mathbb R^2)$ and preserves inner products.

[F2] [[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]]: for integrable $q$, $\widehat q(\xi)=\int q(x)e^{-2\pi i x\cdot\xi}\,dx$; integration by parts gives the displayed derivative transform.

[F3] [[lem-schwartz-space-is-dense-in-l-two]]: complex Schwartz functions are dense in complex $L^2$; taking real parts gives density of real Schwartz functions in real $L^2$.

[F4] [[def-ip-tv-functional-on-l2-distributional-variation]]: $TV_2(v)$ is the supremum of $\int v\operatorname{div}y$ over compactly supported smooth vector fields with $\|y\|_\infty\le1$.

[F5] [[def-ip-banach-convex-subgradient-and-dual-pairing]] and [[def-ip-tv-dual-source-certificate]]: $q\in\partial TV_2(u)$ when $TV_2(v)\ge TV_2(u)+\langle q,v-u\rangle$ for all $v\in L^2$, using the real Hilbert pairing.

[F6] [[lem-smooth-bump-between-concentric-euclidean-balls]]: a smooth cutoff can equal one on the compact radial support of $\phi$ and vanish near the origin.

[F7] [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]: on real-valued functions, the complex $L^2$ inner product equals the real Hilbert pairing.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $m,n\in\mathbb N$ with $m,n\ge1$, and let
$A\in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb R)=\mathbb R^{m\times n}$.
Put $[m]:=\{1,\ldots,m\}$ and $[n]:=\{1,\ldots,n\}$. The library indexes
vector coordinates and matrix columns by $n=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ and matrix rows
by $m=\{0,\ldots,m-1\}$. Throughout this item use the canonical relabeling
$j\mapsto j-1$ from $[n]$ to the library's coordinate and column indices, and
similarly from $[m]$ for rows. Thus write
$u_j:=u(j-1)$ and $A_{ij}:=A(i-1,j-1)$. For $u\in\mathbb R^n$, define
the matrix-vector product by
$$(Au)_i:=\sum_{j=1}^n A_{ij}u_j \qquad (i\in[m]),$$
and define
$$\ker A:=\{h\in\mathbb R^n:Ah=0\}.$$
For $h\in\mathbb R^n$ and $S\subseteq[n]$, let $h_S\in\mathbb R^n$ be the
vector whose $j$th coordinate is $h_j$ for $j\in S$ and $0$ for $j\notin S$;
write $S^c:=[n]\setminus S$. For $u\in\mathbb R^n$, write
$$\|u\|_1:=\sum_{j=1}^n|u_j|,$$
the same $p=1$ norm as the library's finite-dimensional norm under this
coordinate relabeling.
For $s\in\mathbb N$ with $1\le s\le n$, the matrix $A$ satisfies the **strict
nullspace property of order $s$** if
$$\|h_S\|_1<\|h_{S^c}\|_1$$
for every nonzero $h\in\ker A$ and every $S\subseteq[n]$ with $|S|\le s$.
This condition concerns exact kernel vectors only and says nothing about vectors
with $Ah\ne0$.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $n,s\in\mathbb N$ with $n\ge1$ and $1\le s\le n$, and let $x\in\mathbb R^n$. Use one-based labels $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, identifying label $j$ with library coordinate $j-1$. For $T\subseteq[n]$, let $x_{T^c}$ retain the coordinates outside $T$ and vanish on $T$, where $T^c=[n]\setminus T$. Define the best $s$-term $\ell^1$ approximation error by
$$\sigma_s(x)_1:=\min\{\|x_{T^c}\|_1:T\subseteq[n],\ |T|\le s\}.$$
The indexing family is finite and nonempty, so the displayed minimum exists and is attained.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $m,n,s\in\mathbb N$ with $m,n\ge1$ and $1\le s\le n$, let $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$, and let $0<\rho<1$ and $\tau>0$. In real scalar expressions, a natural number denotes its canonical real image. Use one-based coordinate labels $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, identifying coordinate label $j$ with library coordinate $j-1$. For $h\in\mathbb R^n$ and $S\subseteq[n]$, let $h_S$ agree with $h$ on $S$ and vanish on $S^c=[n]\setminus S$. The matrix $A$ satisfies the **$\ell^2$ robust nullspace property of order $s$ with constants $(\rho,\tau)$** if
$$\|h_S\|_2\le \frac{\rho}{\sqrt{s}}\|h_{S^c}\|_1+\tau\|Ah\|_2$$
for every $h\in\mathbb R^n$ and every $S\subseteq[n]$ with $|S|\le s$. This condition applies to all vectors, including vectors with $Ah\ne0$.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $m,n\in\mathbb N$ with $m,n\ge1$, let $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ act in the standard finite coordinate bases, with labels $j=1,\ldots,n$ corresponding to library coordinates $j-1$, $y\in\mathbb R^m$, and $\epsilon\ge0$. If
$$F:=\{z\in\mathbb R^n:\|Az-y\|_2\le\epsilon\}$$
is nonempty, then $z\mapsto\|z\|_1$ attains a minimum on $F$.

facts:
**Given:** Integers $m,n\ge1$, a real matrix $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$, a vector $y\in\mathbb R^m$, a radius $\epsilon\ge0$, and a nonempty set $F=\{z:\|Az-y\|_2\le\epsilon\}$.

[F1] [[def-ip-nullspace-property]]: $(Au)_i=\sum_{j=1}^n A_{ij}u_j$ under the one-based labels identified with library coordinate $j-1$.

[F2] [[def-p-norms-on-rn]]: $\|u\|_1=\sum_{j=1}^n|u_j|$ and $\|u\|_2=(\sum_{j=1}^n|u_j|^2)^{1/2}$.

[F3] [[lem-p-norms-are-norms-and-induce-the-published-metrics]] and [[lem-every-norm-on-rn-is-continuous-for-the-euclidean-metric]]: for $n\ge1$, $\|\cdot\|_2$ is a positive-definite norm, and every norm $N$ satisfies $|N(u)-N(v)|\le N(u-v)$, $\|u\|_1\le\sqrt{\iota(n)}\|u\|_2$, and $\|u\|_2\le\|u\|_1$.

[F4] [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-and-the-euclidean-norm]]: for finite real coordinate lists, $|\sum_j a_jb_j|\le(\sum_j a_j^2)^{1/2}(\sum_j b_j^2)^{1/2}$.

[F5] [[lem-finite-sum-laws]]: finite sums preserve termwise inequalities and sums of nonnegative terms are nonnegative.

[F6] [[lem-of-square-monotone]]: for nonnegative reals $a,b$, $a^2\le b^2$ implies $a\le b$.

[F7] [[thm-euclidean-heine-borel-pseudocompactness-and-extreme-values]]: in $\mathbb R^n$ with $n\ge1$, closed bounded sets are compact, and every continuous real-valued function on a nonempty compact set attains its minimum and maximum; this is a ZF theorem.

[F8] [[def-canonical-natural]]: $\iota(n)$ is the canonical real image of the natural $n$ in scalar expressions.

[F9] [[lem-of-naturals-positive]]: because $n\ge1$, $\iota(n)>0$.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $n,s\in\mathbb N$ with $n\ge1$ and $1\le s\le n$, and let $h\in\mathbb R^n$ use one-based coordinate labels $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, with label $j$ corresponding to library coordinate $j-1$. In real scalar expressions, a natural number denotes its canonical real image. Order the coordinates by decreasing $|h_j|$, breaking ties by increasing $j$. Let $S$ consist of the first $s$ indices, and partition $S^c$ in this same order into consecutive nonempty blocks $T_1,\ldots,T_q$ of size $s$, with only the last block possibly smaller; if $S^c=\varnothing$, take $q=0$. Then
$$\|h_{S^c}\|_2\le \|h_S\|_2+\frac{\|h_{S^c}\|_1}{\sqrt{s}}.$$

[F1] [[def-ip-nullspace-property]]: $h_S$ agrees with $h$ on $S$ and is zero on $S^c$; the coordinate labels are one-based with label $j$ identified with library coordinate $j-1$.

[F3] [[lem-p-norms-are-norms-and-induce-the-published-metrics]]: $\|\cdot\|_2$ is a norm and obeys the triangle inequality.

[F4] [[lem-finite-sum-laws]]: finite sums preserve termwise inequalities and a sum of nonnegative terms is nonnegative.

[F5] [[lem-of-square-monotone]]: for nonnegative $a,b$, $a^2\le b^2$ implies $a\le b$.

[F7] [[lem-of-naturals-positive]]: the canonical real image $\iota(s)$ is positive for $s\ge1$, and $k\le s$ implies $\iota(k)\le\iota(s)$.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be real vector spaces, let $U\subseteq X$ be nonempty, and let $A:X\to Y$ be linear. The corresponding inverse-problem model has admissible truths $U$ and forward map $A|_U$. An **admissible constraint class** is a nonempty subset $C\subseteq U$; its constrained forward map is the restriction $A|_C:C\to Y$. The class $C$ is **identifiable for $A$** if $A|_C$ is injective, meaning $Ax=Ax'$ for $x,x'\in C$ implies $x=x'$. Define the difference set and kernel by

$$C-C:=\{x-x':x,x'\in C\},\qquad \ker A:=\{x\in X:Ax=0_Y\}.$$

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
For integers $1\le p\le n$, define the real Stiefel constraint set

$$\operatorname{St}(n,p):=\{X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}:X^{\mathsf T}X=I_p\}.$$

Equip $\mathbb R^{n\times p}$ with the Frobenius inner product $\langle U,V\rangle_F=\operatorname{tr}(U^{\mathsf T}V)$ and norm $\|U\|_F=\sqrt{\langle U,U\rangle_F}$. Let $H=\mathbb R^{n\times p}$, let $Y$ be a real Hilbert space, let $U\subseteq H$ be open and contain $\operatorname{St}(n,p)$, and let $F:U\to Y$ be continuously Fréchet differentiable. Given data $y\in Y$, a reference matrix $X_{\rm ref}\in H$, and $\lambda\ge0$, define the residual and regularized objective by

$$r(X):=\|F(X)-y\|_Y,\qquad \Phi(X):=\tfrac12\|F(X)-y\|_Y^2+\tfrac\lambda2\|X-X_{\rm ref}\|_F^2.$$

Supply an ambient gradient oracle $G:U\to H$ satisfying $D\Phi(X)[Z]=\langle G(X),Z\rangle_F$ for every $X\in U$ and $Z\in H$, an initial frame $X_0\in\operatorname{St}(n,p)$, a residual tolerance $\tau\ge0$, a finite integer budget $K\ge0$, and a step schedule $\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_{K-1}$ with every $\alpha_k>0$. For a square matrix $M$, put $\operatorname{sym}(M):=(M+M^{\mathsf T})/2$. The procedure is:

1. Set the current frame to $X_0$ and the schedule index to $k=0$. If $r(X)\le\tau$, return $(X,r(X),\texttt{target-met})$.
2. While $k<K$, compute $G(X)$ and the Stiefel gradient $g:=G(X)-X\operatorname{sym}(X^{\mathsf T}G(X))$. If $g=0$, return $(X,r(X),\texttt{stationary})$.
3. Set $\eta:=-\alpha_k g$ and form the polar-retracted candidate

   $$X_{\rm trial}:=(X+\eta)\bigl((X+\eta)^{\mathsf T}(X+\eta)\bigr)^{-1/2}.$$

4. Evaluate $\Phi(X_{\rm trial})$ and $r(X_{\rm trial})$. If $\Phi(X_{\rm trial})>\Phi(X)$, return $(X,r(X),\texttt{objective-rejected})$. Otherwise accept $X_{\rm trial}$ as the current frame. If its residual is at most $\tau$, return $(X,r(X),\texttt{target-met})$; otherwise increment $k$ by one and repeat the loop.
5. When $k=K$, return $(X,r(X),\texttt{budget-exhausted})$.

This procedure is restricted to the stated finite-dimensional real Stiefel constraint and the displayed polar retraction. It gives no convergence, global-optimality, or noisy-data stability guarantee, and it makes no finite-precision claim. It does not apply to positivity constraints or other nonlinear manifolds without a separately specified compatible retraction and proof.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Write $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb C)$ for the complex-valued smooth functions of compact support on the Euclidean plane. For $u\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb C)$, $n=1$ or $2$, use the compact-support Riemann Fourier transform
$$\widehat u(\xi)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}u(x)e^{-2\pi i x\cdot\xi}\,dx.$$
For $\theta=(\theta_1,\theta_2)\in S^1:=\{x\in\mathbb R^2:|x|=1\}$ put $\theta^\perp=(-\theta_2,\theta_1)$. The line with normal $\theta$ and signed offset $s$ is $\{x\in\mathbb R^2:x\cdot\theta=s\}$. Its **Euclidean Radon transform** is
$$Rf(\theta,s):=\int_{\mathbb R}f(s\theta+t\theta^\perp)\,dt,\qquad f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb C),\ (\theta,s)\in S^1\times\mathbb R.$$
The line integral is a compact-support Riemann integral.
The full data set uses every oriented normal $\theta\in S^1$ and every $s\in\mathbb R$; the same unoriented line is represented by $(\theta,s)$ and $(-\theta,-s)$.
For a one-dimensional function $h$ with integrable Fourier transform, define
$$|D_s|h(s):=\int_{\mathbb R}2\pi|\sigma|\,\widehat h(\sigma)e^{2\pi i s\sigma}\,d\sigma.$$
For $f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb C)$ define the Riesz potential notation used here by
$$|D|^{-1}f(x):=\int_{\mathbb R^2}e^{2\pi i x\cdot\xi}\frac{\widehat f(\xi)}{2\pi|\xi|}\,d\xi.$$
The quotient in the last integral is assigned value $0$ at $\xi=0$. These integrals are absolutely convergent on the stated classes: compact-support integration by parts gives rapid decay of $\widehat f$ and $\widehat h$, while $\widehat f$ is bounded near $0$ and $|\xi|^{-1}$ is locally integrable in two dimensions. Here the multiplier for $|D_s|$ is $2\pi|\sigma|$, corresponding to the $e^{-2\pi i s\sigma}$ Fourier convention.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Let $f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb C)$ and, for $z=(z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb C^2$, define $F(z)=\int_{\mathbb R^2}f(x)e^{-2\pi i(x_1z_1+x_2z_2)}\,dx$ using the compact-support Riemann integral on any rectangle containing $\operatorname{supp}f$. This value is independent of the containing rectangle. Each coordinate slice of $F$ is entire, with $\frac{\partial F}{\partial z_j}(z)=\int_{\mathbb R^2}(-2\pi ix_j)f(x)e^{-2\pi i x\cdot z}\,dx$ for $j=1,2$, and the restriction of $F$ to $\mathbb R^2$ is the compact-support Fourier transform in the stated line-normal convention. The proof uses no Countable Choice.

facts:
**Given:** A compactly supported smooth complex function $f$ on $\mathbb R^2$, a rectangle containing its support, and a complex frequency $z\in\mathbb C^2$.

[F1] [[def-ip-2d-radon-transform]]: the compact-support Fourier transform uses $e^{-2\pi i x\cdot\xi}$ and is defined by a compact-support Riemann integral.

[F2] [[thm-continuous-on-a-rectangle-is-riemann-integrable]]: each continuous real function on a nondegenerate closed rectangle is Riemann integrable; apply this to real and imaginary parts.

[F3] [[thm-complex-exponential-is-entire-with-derivative-itself]]: the complex exponential is entire with derivative itself, so $(e^w-1)/w\to1$ as $w\to0$.

[F4] [[thm-multidimensional-integral-properties]]: the Riemann integral is linear and its absolute-value estimate bounds an integral by the rectangle volume times a uniform bound; for complex functions apply the real estimate to both components.

[F5] [[def-complex-differentiability-holomorphic-and-entire]]: a function complex differentiable at every point of $\mathbb C$ is entire.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $\Theta\subset S^1$ be a nonempty proper open set of line normals, assume $\theta\in\Theta$ if and only if $-\theta\in\Theta$, and assume $S^1\setminus\overline{\Theta}$ contains a nonempty open arc. The measured line with normal $\theta$ and signed offset $s$ is $\ell_{\theta,s}=\{y\in\mathbb R^2:y\cdot\theta=s\}$. Identify the nonzero cotangent vectors of the Euclidean plane with pairs $(x,\xi)\in\mathbb R^2\times(\mathbb R^2\setminus\{0\})$. Such a covector is visible from $\Theta$ when $\xi/|\xi|\in\Theta$, and invisible when $\xi/|\xi|\notin\Theta$. The associated measured Fourier wedge is

$$W_\Theta=\{\sigma\theta:\theta\in\Theta,\ \sigma\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}\}.$$

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text: For $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^2)$, $\theta=(\theta_1,\theta_2)\in S^1$, $s\in\mathbb R$, and $\theta^\perp=(-\theta_2,\theta_1)$, define $R_{\mathcal S}f(\theta,s)=\int_{\mathbb R}f(s\theta+t\theta^\perp)\,dt$, where the absolutely convergent integral is with respect to one-dimensional Lebesgue measure. Here $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^2)$ is the space of smooth complex functions for which every seminorm $\sup_{x\in\mathbb R^2}|x^\alpha\partial^\beta f(x)|$, for multi-indices $\alpha,\beta$, is finite. The parameter $\theta$ is the unit normal to the line, so $(\theta,s)$ and $(-\theta,-s)$ represent the same unoriented line. Under the Axiom of Countable Choice, the Lebesgue integral in this definition agrees on compactly supported smooth inputs with the compact-support Riemann line integral, so the normalization is the same.
