contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
For every $f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb C)$, every unit normal $\theta\in S^1$, and every $\sigma\in\mathbb R$, the compact-support Fourier transform of the line data in the offset variable equals the restriction of the two-dimensional Fourier transform to the line in frequency space with direction $\theta$:
$$\widehat{Rf}(\theta,\sigma)=\widehat f(\sigma\theta).$$

facts:
**Given:** $f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb C)$, $\theta\in S^1$, and $\sigma\in\mathbb R$.

[F1] [[def-ip-2d-radon-transform]]: $Rf(\theta,s)=\int_{\mathbb R}f(s\theta+t\theta^\perp)\,dt$, and the compact-support Fourier transform uses the phase $e^{-2\pi i x\cdot\xi}$.

[F2] [[thm-continuous-functions-on-compact-jordan-sets-are-integrable]]: a continuous real function on a compact Jordan set is Riemann integrable; apply this to real and imaginary parts on a bounding rectangle.

[F3] [[thm-riemann-fubini-on-product-rectangles]]: for a Riemann-integrable function on a product of closed rectangles, the iterated Riemann integrals equal the product-rectangle integral when the sections are integrable.

[F4] [[cor-change-of-variables-for-compactly-supported-functions]]: an injective $C^1$ change of variables with nonvanishing Jacobian carries a compactly supported Riemann integral to the integral multiplied by the absolute Jacobian.
scope: Literal contract/Facts extraction only; accepted proof body not inspected.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Let $\Theta\subset S^1$ be a nonempty open set of unit line normals and let $f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb C)$. If the line integral $Rf(\theta,s)$ is zero for every $\theta\in\Theta$ and $s\in\mathbb R$, then $f$ is zero everywhere. The assertion holds without Countable Choice.

facts:
**Given:** A nonempty open set $\Theta\subset S^1$, a compactly supported smooth complex function $f$, and the hypothesis $Rf(\theta,s)=0$ for every measured normal and offset.

[F1] [[def-ip-visible-covector-for-limited-angle-data]]: the measured Fourier wedge is $W_\Theta=\{\sigma\theta:\theta\in\Theta,\ \sigma\ne0\}$.

[F2] [[thm-ip-fourier-slice-identity]]: for compactly supported smooth input and the line-normal convention, $\widehat{Rf}(\theta,\sigma)=\widehat f(\sigma\theta)$ for all real $\sigma$; the supplier proof uses no Countable Choice.

[F3] [[lem-ip-compact-support-fourier-laplace-is-entire]]: the compact-support Riemann Fourier-Laplace transform of a smooth compactly supported function is entire in each coordinate, with coordinate derivatives given by integrals with polynomial factors; the proof is choice-free.

[F4] [[thm-multidimensional-integral-properties]]: the real Riemann integral is linear, monotone, and bounded by volume times a uniform absolute bound; apply it componentwise to complex functions.

[F5] [[thm-identity-theorem-holomorphic-functions]]: a holomorphic function on a connected domain that vanishes on a set with an accumulation point in the domain vanishes everywhere.

[F6] [[thm-real-stone-weierstrass-for-compact-metric-spaces]]: real polynomials on a compact subset of $\mathbb R^2$ are dense in its real continuous functions because they form a unital point-separating algebra.
scope: Literal contract/Facts extraction only; accepted proof body not inspected.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $\Theta\subset S^1$ be a nonempty proper open antipodally symmetric set whose complement contains a nonempty open arc, and let $W_\Theta=\{\sigma\theta:\theta\in\Theta,\ \sigma\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}\}$. For $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^2)$ and every measured normal $\theta\in\Theta$, the one-dimensional Fourier transform in the offset variable obeys $\widehat{R_{\mathcal S}f}(\theta,\sigma)=\widehat f(\sigma\theta)$ for all $\sigma\in\mathbb R$. In particular, zero restricted data imply that $\widehat f$ vanishes on $W_\Theta$. If in addition $f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2)$, zero restricted data imply $f=0$ everywhere; this compact-support implication is proved separately from the choice-free compact-support Fourier-slice theorem and uses no Countable Choice.

facts:
**Given:** The set $\Theta$, $W_\Theta$, and a function $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^2)$; in the compact-support conclusion also $f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2)$ and $R_{\mathcal S}f(\theta,s)=0$ for every $\theta\in\Theta$ and $s\in\mathbb R$.

[F1] [[def-ip-visible-covector-for-limited-angle-data]]: the measured Fourier wedge is $W_\Theta=\{\sigma\theta:\theta\in\Theta,\ \sigma\ne0\}$.

[F2] [[def-ip-schwartz-radon-transform]]: $R_{\mathcal S}f(\theta,s)=\int_\mathbb R f(s\theta+t\theta^\perp)\,dt$.

[F3] [[lem-ip-fourier-slice-identity-on-schwartz]]: for $f\in\mathcal S$, $\widehat{R_{\mathcal S}f}(\theta,\sigma)=\widehat f(\sigma\theta)$.

[F4] [[thm-ip-fourier-slice-identity]]: for $f\in C_c^\infty$ and the IP-36 normalization, the same compact-support Fourier-slice identity holds.

[F5] [[cor-ip-limited-angle-compact-support-uniqueness]]: compactly supported smooth functions with zero data on a nonempty open set of line normals vanish everywhere; the proof uses the Riemann Fourier-Laplace transform and no Countable Choice.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: Countable Choice is required by [F3] for the general Schwartz Fourier-slice formula; the compact-support uniqueness branch below instead uses [F4] and no choice axiom.

contract.heading: Open problem
contract.text:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^2$ be any bounded open set with nonempty interior, and let $\Theta\subset S^1$ be any nonempty proper open antipodally symmetric set whose complement contains a nonempty open arc. Write $\theta^\perp=(-\theta_2,\theta_1)$ and define $R_\Theta f(\theta,s)=\int_{\mathbb R}f(s\theta+t\theta^\perp)\,dt$ for $\theta\in\Theta$, $s\in\mathbb R$. Equip $L^2(\Theta\times\mathbb R)$ with the norm $\|g\|_2=(\int_\Theta\int_{\mathbb R}|g(\theta,s)|^2\,ds\,d\theta)^{1/2}$, where $ds$ is Lebesgue measure and $d\theta$ is arc-length measure, and equip $L^2(\mathbb R^2)$ with Lebesgue measure. The line data of every compactly supported smooth input are regarded as elements of this data space. For $M>0$ define $\mathcal K_M(\Omega)=\{f\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb C):\|f\|_{H^1}\le M\}$ with $\|f\|_{H^1}^2=\|f\|_2^2+\|\partial_1f\|_2^2+\|\partial_2f\|_2^2$. For deterministic noise radius $\delta>0$, define the worst-case reconstruction error $\mathcal E_{\Omega,\Theta,M}(\delta)=\inf_{\Phi:L^2(\Theta\times\mathbb R)\to L^2(\mathbb R^2)}\sup_{\substack{f\in\mathcal K_M(\Omega),\ \eta\in L^2(\Theta\times\mathbb R)\\\|\eta\|_2\le\delta}}\|\Phi(R_\Theta f+\eta)-f\|_2$.
Determine the sharp asymptotic order of $\mathcal E_{\Omega,\Theta,M}(\delta)$ as $\delta\downarrow0$, with matching upper and lower bounds and a deterministic reconstruction rule attaining the upper bound, for every such $\Omega$ and $\Theta$. In particular, determine the dependence of the sharp modulus on the geometry and aperture of the measured normal set.

contract.heading: Example
contract.text: Let $\Theta\subset S^1$ be a nonempty proper open antipodally symmetric set whose complement contains a nonempty open arc. Write $\theta^\perp=(-\theta_2,\theta_1)$ and define the line Radon integral by $Rg(\theta,s)=\int_{\mathbb R}g(s\theta+t\theta^\perp)\,dt$ using Lebesgue measure $dt$. Choose a smooth function $\psi$ supported in $B_1(0)$ and equal to one on $\overline B_{1/2}(0)$. For every $h\in C_c^\infty(B_1(0);\mathbb C)$, equality of the restricted line data $Rh(\theta,s)=R\psi(\theta,s)$ for all $\theta\in\Theta$ and $s\in\mathbb R$ forces $h=\psi$. The Fourier-Laplace transforms of these compactly supported functions are entire in each complex frequency coordinate, so their agreement on the measured open wedge determines their values at every real frequency. In particular, $R\psi$ is not identically zero.

facts:
**Given:** The set $\Theta$, a smooth bump $\psi$ supported in $B_1(0)$ and equal to one on $\overline B_{1/2}(0)$, and a compactly supported smooth function $h$ with the same restricted line data as $\psi$.

[F1] [[def-ip-visible-covector-for-limited-angle-data]]: the Fourier wedge of measured line normals is $W_\Theta=\{\sigma\theta:\theta\in\Theta,\ \sigma\ne0\}$, a nonempty open sector when $\Theta$ is nonempty and open.

[F2] [[lem-smooth-bump-between-concentric-euclidean-balls]]: a smooth compactly supported function equal to one on a smaller concentric ball and supported in a larger ball exists.

[F3] [[lem-ip-compact-support-fourier-laplace-is-entire]]: the compact-support Riemann Fourier-Laplace transform is entire in each coordinate and restricts to the usual compact-support Fourier transform on real frequencies.

[F4] [[thm-ip-fourier-slice-identity]]: the Fourier transform of compact-support Radon data equals the object Fourier transform on the ray $\sigma\theta$.

[F5] [[cor-ip-limited-angle-compact-support-uniqueness]]: zero limited-angle data for a compactly supported smooth function force that function to vanish everywhere, by the choice-free analytic-continuation argument.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $(X,d_X)$, $(Y,d_Y)$, and $(Q,d_Q)$ be metric spaces, let $U\subseteq X$ be a nonempty admissible truth class, let $F:U\to Y$ be a forward map, and let $q:U\to Q$ assign each truth its target class. Let $x_0,x_1\in U$, let $\delta\ge0$, and suppose a single datum $y\in Y$ satisfies

$$d_Y(y,F(x_0))\le\delta\quad\text{and}\quad d_Y(y,F(x_1))\le\delta.$$

For every deterministic data-only estimator, meaning every function $\widehat q:Y\to Q$, the two target-class losses at that datum satisfy

$$\max\{d_Q(\widehat q(y),q(x_0)),d_Q(\widehat q(y),q(x_1))\}\ge\frac12d_Q(q(x_0),q(x_1)).$$

In particular, if $F(x_0)=F(x_1)$ but $q(x_0)\ne q(x_1)$, no data-only estimator exactly recovers both truths. The quantitative bound also holds whenever the radius-$\delta$ data balls around the two forward data share the observed datum $y$.

facts:
**Given:** Metric spaces $(X,d_X)$, $(Y,d_Y)$, and $(Q,d_Q)$; a nonempty set $U\subseteq X$; a map $F:U\to Y$; a target-class map $q:U\to Q$; truths $x_0,x_1\in U$; a radius $\delta\ge0$; a datum $y\in Y$ within distance $\delta$ of both $F(x_0)$ and $F(x_1)$; and an estimator $\widehat q:Y\to Q$.

[F1] [[def-ip-forward-map-and-solution-classes]]: the recovery target has a metric $d_Q$, and $q(x)$ is the target class of truth $x$.

[F2] [[def-ip-identifiability-and-stability-modulus]]: a deterministic data-only estimator is a function $Y\to Q$ and exact recovery requires $\widehat q(F(x))=q(x)$ for every admissible truth.

[F3] [[def-metric-space]]: the target metric satisfies separation and the triangle inequality.

[F4] [[lem-metric-nonnegativity]]: every metric distance is nonnegative.

contract.heading: Example
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $\Theta\subset S^1$ be a nonempty proper open antipodally symmetric set such that $S^1\setminus\overline\Theta$ contains a nonempty open arc. Choose an open arc $J$ with $\overline J\subset S^1\setminus\overline\Theta$, put $V=\{r\omega:1<r<2,\ \omega\in J\}$, choose a nonzero smooth function $q\in C_c^\infty(V;\mathbb C)$, and define $f(x)=\int_{\mathbb R^2}q(\xi)e^{2\pi i x\cdot\xi}\,d\xi$. For $\theta=(\theta_1,\theta_2)$ write $\theta^\perp=(-\theta_2,\theta_1)$ and, for a Schwartz function $g$, define $R_{\mathcal S}g(\theta,s)=\int_{\mathbb R}g(s\theta+t\theta^\perp)\,dt$ using Lebesgue measure $dt$. Let $Y=L^2(\Theta\times\mathbb R,d\theta\,ds)$, where $d\theta$ is arc-length measure and $ds$ is Lebesgue measure. Then $f$ is a nonzero Schwartz function in $L^2(\mathbb R^2)$ with Lebesgue measure, its Fourier transform is $q$, and $R_{\mathcal S}f(\theta,s)=0$ for every $\theta\in\Theta$ and $s\in\mathbb R$, so both $0$ and $f$ give datum $0$ in $Y$ without either truth being required to have compact support. For the two-truth class $\{0,f\}$ with target loss $\|g-h\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^2)}$, every deterministic estimator $\Phi:Y\to L^2(\mathbb R^2)$ satisfies $\max\{\|\Phi(0)\|_2,\|\Phi(0)-f\|_2\}\ge \|f\|_2/2>0$.

facts:
**Given:** The Axiom of Countable Choice, the normal set $\Theta$, the blind arc $J$, the annular sector $V$, and the nonzero smooth function $q$ supported in $V$ from the Example.

[F1] [[def-ip-visible-covector-for-limited-angle-data]]: $W_\Theta=\{\sigma\theta:\theta\in\Theta,\ \sigma\ne0\}$, while the directions in $S^1\setminus\overline\Theta$ are unmeasured.

[F2] [[lem-smooth-bump-between-concentric-euclidean-balls]]: every nonempty open ball contains a nonzero smooth compactly supported function, by translating and rescaling a concentric bump.

[F3] [[thm-fourier-transform-maps-schwartz-space-continuously-to-itself]]: under Countable Choice the negative-sign, $2\pi$-normalized Fourier transform maps Schwartz functions to Schwartz functions.

[F4] [[thm-fourier-inversion-on-schwartz-space]]: under Countable Choice, $g(x)=\int\widehat g(\xi)e^{2\pi i x\cdot\xi}\,d\xi$ for every Schwartz function $g$.

[F5] [[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]]: $\widehat g(\eta)=\int g(x)e^{-2\pi i x\cdot\eta}\,dx$ for integrable $g$.

[F6] [[cor-c-one-change-of-variables-for-l-one-functions]]: under Countable Choice, the reflection $x\mapsto-x$ preserves Lebesgue integrals because its absolute determinant is one.

[F7] [[lem-schwartz-functions-and-all-derivatives-are-integrable]]: under Countable Choice every Schwartz function belongs to $L^p$ for each $1\le p\le\infty$.

[F8] [[lem-ip-fourier-slice-identity-on-schwartz]]: under Countable Choice, $\widehat{R_{\mathcal S}g}(\theta,\sigma)=\widehat g(\sigma\theta)$ for Schwartz $g$.

[F9] [[lem-ip-schwartz-radon-well-defined]]: for fixed $\theta$, $R_{\mathcal S}g(\theta,\cdot)$ is a Schwartz function.

[F10] [[thm-the-l-p-norm-descends-to-the-quotient-and-makes-l-p-a-normed-space]]: the $L^2$ quotient norm is a norm and gives the triangle inequality and separation.

[F11] [[thm-ip-kernel-directions-preclude-unrestricted-recovery]]: if two truths share one exact datum, every deterministic data-only estimator has maximum target loss at least half their target distance.

[F12] [[def-ip-forward-map-and-solution-classes]]: the truth class may be any nonempty subset of a metric parameter space, and exact recovery may use the truth itself as the target class.

[F13] [[def-metric-space]]: a metric is nonnegative, symmetric, separates distinct points, and satisfies the triangle inequality; the metric induced by an $L^2$ norm is $d(g,h)=\|g-h\|_2$.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: Countable Choice is assumed by the Fourier transform, inversion, Lp integrability, Fourier-slice, and Lebesgue substitution suppliers [F3], [F4], [F6]–[F9].

contract.heading: Example
contract.text:
Let $\Theta\subset S^1$ be a nonempty proper open set of line normals, invariant under $\theta\mapsto-\theta$, and suppose $S^1\setminus\overline{\Theta}$ contains an open arc. Restrict the Euclidean Radon incidence relation to
$$
Z_\Theta=\{(\theta,s,x)\in(\Theta\times\mathbb R)\times\mathbb R^2:s=x\cdot\theta\}.
$$
Give $Z_\Theta$ the standard nowhere vanishing analytic total density $|d\theta\,ds\,dt|$, with $x=s\theta+t\theta^\perp$, and constant weight $1$. This is a properly supported analytic double fibration.
For any $x_0\in\mathbb R^2$ and any nonzero covector $\xi_0\in T^*_{x_0}\mathbb R^2$ with $\xi_0/|\xi_0|\notin\Theta$, there are no $(\theta,s)\in\Theta\times\mathbb R$ and no data covector $\eta$ such that $(\theta,s,\eta;x_0,\xi_0)\in C_{Z_\Theta}$. In particular, this object covector has no data-side canonical pair for the restricted-angle transform.

facts:
**Given:** The open antipodally symmetric set $\Theta$, the incidence submanifold $Z_\Theta$, and the invisible covector $(x_0,\xi_0)$.

[F1] [[def-ip-2d-radon-transform]]: the line with normal $\theta$ and signed offset $s$ is given by $s=x\cdot\theta$.

[F2] [[def-ip-visible-covector-for-limited-angle-data]]: a nonzero plane covector is visible exactly when its unit direction lies in $\Theta$; $\Theta$ is antipodally symmetric.

[F3] [[def-ip-distributions-conormal-kernels-and-cotangent-relation]]: $(\theta,s,\eta;x,\xi)$ belongs to the incidence relation exactly when $(\theta,s,x;\eta,-\xi)$ is a nonzero conormal to $Z_\Theta$.

[F4] [[lem-ip-double-fibration-conormal-kernel]]: if $F(\theta,s,x)=0$ defines the incidence hypersurface, its conormal covectors are scalar multiples of $dF$.

[F5] [[def-ip-analytic-double-fibration-transform]]: both incidence projections must be analytic submersions and the support condition is properness over compact object supports.

[F6] [[thm-real-analytic-inverse-and-implicit-function-theorems]]: a regular zero of a real-analytic scalar function is locally an analytic hypersurface.

contract.heading: Example
contract.text:
Let $X=\mathbb R^2$, $G=S^1\times\mathbb R$, and
$$
Z=\{(\theta,s,x):s=x\cdot\theta\}.
$$
Write $x=s\theta+t\theta^\perp$ on $Z$, use the analytic total density $|d\theta\,ds\,dt|$ and constant weight $1$, so $R$ is the full Euclidean Radon transform. This is a properly supported analytic double fibration. Its canonical relation satisfies the global Bolker condition. Using the Euclidean metric to identify covectors with vectors and its associated norm, for every $x\in\mathbb R^2$ and every $\xi\in T_x^*\mathbb R^2\setminus0$, set
$$
\theta=\xi/|\xi|,\qquad \tau=|\xi|,\qquad s=x\cdot\theta,\qquad \eta_s=\tau,\quad \eta_\theta=-\tau\,x\cdot\theta^\perp.
$$
Then $(\theta,s;\eta_\theta,\eta_s;x,\xi)$ is a canonical pair. Thus every nonzero Euclidean covector is visible. In particular, for a compactly supported distribution $f$, the analytic wavefront recovery theorem implies that if $(x,\xi)\in\operatorname{WF}_A(f)$, then this data covector belongs to $\operatorname{WF}_A(Rf)$.

facts:
**Given:** The full Euclidean Radon incidence, its constant analytic weight and line density, and a nonzero covector $(x,\xi)$.

[F1] [[def-ip-2d-radon-transform]]: lines are parameterized by $s=x\cdot\theta$, with $\theta^\perp=(-\theta_2,\theta_1)$.

[F2] [[lem-ip-double-fibration-conormal-kernel]]: the defining function $F(\theta,s,x)=s-x\cdot\theta$ gives conormal components by differentiating $F$, with the relation sign $(\eta,-\xi)$.

[F3] [[def-ip-bolker-condition]]: the Bolker condition requires a singleton left fiber and injective differential at its point.

[F4] [[thm-ip-analytic-wavefront-recovery-under-bolker]]: data-side analytic regularity at a Bolker pair implies object-side analytic regularity.

[F5] [[def-ip-analytic-double-fibration-transform]]: both incidence projections must be analytic submersions and the support condition is properness over compact object supports.

[F6] [[thm-real-analytic-inverse-and-implicit-function-theorems]]: a regular zero of a real-analytic scalar function is locally an analytic hypersurface.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $X,Y$ be real or complex Hilbert spaces over the same scalar field, let
$A:X\to Y$ be a compact linear forward map (the closure of $A(B)$ is compact
in $Y$ for every bounded set $B\subseteq X$), and let $A_h:X\to Y$ be a
bounded linear discretized map with finite-dimensional range. For a datum
$b\in Y$, let $\lambda>0$ be the coefficient of $\|x\|_X^2$ in the Tikhonov
objective $\|Ax-b\|_Y^2+\lambda\|x\|_X^2$. Supply adjoints $A^*:Y\to X$ and
$A_h^*:Y\to X$ satisfying
$\langle Ax,y\rangle_Y=\langle x,A^*y\rangle_X$ and
$\langle A_hx,y\rangle_Y=\langle x,A_h^*y\rangle_X$, where the inner products
are linear in their first arguments. Assume the shifted normal operators
$A^*A+\lambda I_X$ and $A_h^*A_h+\lambda I_X$ are bijective, and define
$$R_\lambda=(A^*A+\lambda I_X)^{-1}A^*,\qquad R_{\lambda,h}=(A_h^*A_h+\lambda I_X)^{-1}A_h^*.$$

For a truth $x^\dagger\in X$, data perturbation $e\in Y$, and $\delta\ge0$
with $\|e\|\le\delta$, put
$$y=Ax^\dagger,\qquad y_\delta=y+e,\qquad y_{h,\delta}=A_hx^\dagger+e,\qquad d_h=(A-A_h)x^\dagger=y_\delta-y_{h,\delta}.$$
For any returned output $\widetilde x_h\in X$, define its exact discrete
normal-equation residual by
$$r_{h,h}=(A_h^*A_h+\lambda I_X)\widetilde x_h-A_h^*y_{h,\delta}.$$
The five-channel error budget is the ordered tuple
$(b_{\mathrm{bias}},b_{\mathrm{data}},b_{\mathrm{operator}},b_{\mathrm{pre}},b_{\mathrm{solve}})$, where
$$\begin{aligned}b_{\mathrm{bias}}&=x^\dagger-R_\lambda y,\qquad b_{\mathrm{data}}=R_\lambda y-R_\lambda y_\delta,\\b_{\mathrm{operator}}&=(R_\lambda-R_{\lambda,h})y_{h,\delta},\qquad b_{\mathrm{pre}}=R_\lambda d_h,\\b_{\mathrm{solve}}&=R_{\lambda,h}y_{h,\delta}-\widetilde x_h.\end{aligned}$$
The five entries are, in order, the truth-bias, data-perturbation,
regularized-operator, pre-inversion, and algebraic-solve error vectors.
The scalar total budget is the sum of the five channel norms. The raw
pre-inversion forward residual is $d_h$; its reconstruction contribution is
$b_{\mathrm{pre}}$. The operator channel measures the difference between the
regularized exact and discretized operators. The solve channel measures the
returned output's difference from the exact discrete Tikhonov output. The
definition supplies no rate or arithmetic residual certificate.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $(M,g)$ be a compact, connected, nonempty smooth two-dimensional Riemannian manifold with smooth boundary. For $x\in\partial M$, let $\nu_{\mathrm{out}}(x)$ be the outward unit normal. The boundary is **strictly convex** if
$$
g(\nabla_w\nu_{\mathrm{out}},w)>0
$$
for every $x\in\partial M$ and every nonzero $w\in T_x\partial M$. A **Jacobi field** along a unit-speed geodesic $\gamma$ is a smooth vector field $J$ along $\gamma$ satisfying
$$
D_t^2J+R(J,\dot\gamma)\dot\gamma=0,
$$
where $R(X,Y)Z=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z$. The manifold has **no conjugate points** if, on every unit-speed geodesic segment $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$, a Jacobi field with $J(a)=J(b)=0$ must be identically zero. It is **nontrapping** if every maximal unit-speed geodesic starting in $M^\circ$ reaches $\partial M$ in finite forward and backward time. The pair $(M,g)$ is a **simple surface** if its boundary is strictly convex, it has no conjugate points, and it is nontrapping.

The unit tangent bundle is $SM=\{(x,v):x\in M,\ v\in T_xM,\ g_x(v,v)=1\}$. Write $\nu_{\mathrm{in}}=-\nu_{\mathrm{out}}$ and
$$
\partial_+SM=\{(x,v)\in SM:x\in\partial M,\ g_x(v,\nu_{\mathrm{in}})>0\}
$$
for inward-pointing unit boundary vectors. For $(x,v)\in\partial_+SM$, let $\gamma_{x,v}$ be the unit-speed geodesic with $\gamma_{x,v}(0)=x$ and $\dot\gamma_{x,v}(0)=v$, and let $\tau_+(x,v)$ be its first positive exit time from $M$. For $f\in C^\infty(M)$, its scalar **geodesic X-ray transform** is the function on $\partial_+SM$ defined by
$$
I_0f(x,v)=\int_0^{\tau_+(x,v)} f(\gamma_{x,v}(t))\,dt.
$$
The geodesic equation is interpreted up to first boundary exit; local smooth extensions of the metric are used only to solve the coordinate ODE at boundary initial data.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $n\ge2$ and let $(M,g)$ be a compact, connected, nonempty smooth $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifold with smooth boundary. Let $\nu_{\mathrm{out}}$ be the outward unit normal and let $\nabla$ be the Levi–Civita connection of $g$. The boundary is **strictly convex** when
$$
g(\nabla_w\nu_{\mathrm{out}},w)>0
$$
for every boundary point and every nonzero boundary-tangent vector $w$. Use the curvature convention
$$
R(X,Y)Z=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z.
$$
A Jacobi field along a unit-speed geodesic $\gamma$ is a smooth vector field $J$ satisfying $D_t^2J+R(J,\dot\gamma)\dot\gamma=0$, where $D_tJ=\nabla_{\dot\gamma}J$. The manifold has **no conjugate points** if every positive-length unit-speed geodesic segment $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ has no nonzero Jacobi field with $J(a)=J(b)=0$. It is **nontrapping** if every maximal unit-speed geodesic starting in $M^\circ$ reaches $\partial M$ in finite forward and backward time. The pair $(M,g)$ is a **simple Riemannian background** if its boundary is strictly convex, it has no conjugate points, and it is nontrapping.

When $n=2$, this is the simple-surface convention used for the scalar geodesic X-ray transform on the required inverse-problems page.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume Countable Choice. Let $(M,g)$ be a compact, connected, nonempty simple two-dimensional Riemannian background with smooth boundary. Suppose $L_*<\infty$ bounds the lengths of all maximal unit-speed geodesics in $M$, and let $T>L_*$. For real static potentials $q_1,q_2\in C_c^\infty(M^\circ;\mathbb R)$, if the full time-dependent Dirichlet-to-Neumann maps for $\partial_t^2-\Delta_g+q_1$ and $\partial_t^2-\Delta_g+q_2$ agree for every smooth boundary input compactly supported in $(0,T)\times\partial M$, then $q_1=q_2$ on $M$. This equality statement asserts no stability modulus or recovery in the presence of noisy data.

[F1] Equal wave DN maps on a simple background imply that the integral of $q_1-q_2$ over every maximal unit-speed geodesic of length less than $T$ is zero. ([[thm-ip-wave-data-determine-light-ray-integrals]])

[F2] The scalar geodesic X-ray transform integrates a real interior function over each incoming maximal unit-speed boundary geodesic. ([[def-ip-simple-surface-and-geodesic-xray-transform]])

[F3] On a compact simple surface, zero unweighted scalar geodesic X-ray data for a real smooth interior function imply that the function vanishes. ([[thm-ip-2d-simple-surface-xray-injectivity]])

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $(M,g)$ be a compact, connected, nonempty simple two-dimensional Riemannian manifold with smooth boundary. Suppose $L_*<\infty$ is an upper bound for the lengths of all maximal unit-speed geodesics in $M$. Let $T>L_*$ and let $q_1,q_2\in C_c^\infty(M^\circ;\mathbb R)$ be static interior potentials. If their full time-dependent Dirichlet-to-Neumann maps agree for every smooth boundary input compactly supported in $(0,T)\times\partial M$, then $q_1=q_2$ throughout $M$.

This gives a concrete observation-time condition: observing longer than a uniform upper bound on the maximal geodesic lengths suffices for coefficient uniqueness in the simple-surface case.

**Given:** Countable Choice; a simple compact Riemannian surface; a finite uniform upper bound $L_*$ on all maximal geodesic lengths; $T>L_*$; two real smooth interior potentials with equal full time-dependent DN maps.

[F1] In dimension two, the wave coefficient-uniqueness corollary applies on a simple background when the observation time exceeds the longest relevant maximal geodesic length and the corresponding light-ray integrals vanish. ([[cor-ip-wave-coefficient-uniqueness-under-simple-geometry]])

[F2] The unweighted scalar geodesic X-ray transform is injective on a compact simple surface. ([[thm-ip-2d-simple-surface-xray-injectivity]])

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice.

Let $M\Subset\mathbb R\times M_0^\circ$ be a three-dimensional transversally anisotropic product domain with compact connected simple surface transversal $(M_0,g_0)$. For every $p\in M_0^\circ$ choose two nontangential unit-speed geodesic segments $\gamma_1,\gamma_2$ meeting transversely at $p$ and nowhere else. For every $\xi\in\mathbb R$ and every $Q\in C^\infty(\overline M)$, there are four exact harmonic solutions $u_{\tau,1}^+,u_{\tau,1}^-,u_{\tau,2}^+,u_{\tau,2}^-\in H^1(M)$, with no prescribed boundary values, such that
$$\lim_{\tau\to\infty}\int_MQ(x_1,x')u_{\tau,1}^+u_{\tau,1}^-u_{\tau,2}^+u_{\tau,2}^-\,dV_g =c(p,\gamma_1,\gamma_2)\int_{I_p}e^{-i\xi x_1}Q(x_1,p)\,dx_1,$$
where $I_p=\{x_1\in\mathbb R:(x_1,p)\in M^\circ\}$ and $c(p,\gamma_1,\gamma_2)>0$ is the nonzero Gaussian normalization divided by $|\sin\angle(\dot\gamma_1(p),\dot\gamma_2(p))|$.

facts:
[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]] is inherited from the CGO solver supplier [F2].

[A2] [[def-countable-choice]] is inherited from the CGO solver supplier [F2].

**Given:** the simple surface product, an interior transversal point, two crossing nontangential geodesics, a longitudinal frequency $\xi$, and $Q\in C^\infty(\overline M)$.

[F1] [[def-ip-simple-surface-and-geodesic-xray-transform]]: strict convexity and unique geodesic segments define the simple surface convention.

[F2] [[thm-ip-cgo-solvability-and-remainder-bound]]: the intended supplier constructs exact harmonic solutions from transport amplitudes and controls the correction in $L^2$.

[F3] **External input:** Lassas--Liimatainen--Lin--Salo, Proposition 5.1, arXiv:1903.12562v1, PDF p. 14: on a compact oriented transversally anisotropic manifold of dimension at least three, if $f\in C^1(M)$ satisfies $\int_M f v_1\cdots v_m\,dV=0$ for all smooth harmonic $v_j$, with $m\ge4$, then $f=0$. We import this density statement. The statement and proof through PDF p. 20 were inspected; the remaining proof through p. 22 is not claimed read or reconstructed here. The simple surface is diffeomorphic to a disk, hence oriented, so its product and $M$ meet the source orientation hypothesis.

[F4] The literal quantifiers in the statement permit the four witnesses to depend on $Q$. They impose no uniformity in $Q$, no nonzero-solution requirement, and no quantitative remainder or beam-profile estimate. The proof below uses density to obtain smooth witnesses constant in $\tau$; it does not assert a uniform Gaussian-beam family. The Gaussian calculation fixes the allowed positive geometric normalization.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice.

Let $(M,g)$ be a three-dimensional transversally anisotropic product domain with compact connected simple surface transversal $(M_0,g_0)$. Let $q_1,q_2\in C^\infty(\overline M,\mathbb R)$. Suppose that for every finite family of smooth boundary directions, the corresponding small-data nonlinear Dirichlet-to-Neumann maps for
$$-\Delta_g u+q_j u^3=0$$
agree for all sufficiently small real parameter values. Then $q_1=q_2$ on $\overline M$.

facts:
[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]] is inherited from the small-data, third-linearization, and four-factor suppliers [F1]--[F3].

[A2] [[def-countable-choice]] is inherited from the small-data, third-linearization, and four-factor suppliers [F1]--[F3].

**Given:** the CTA product with simple surface transversal, real smooth cubic coefficients, and equality of the finite-parameter nonlinear DN maps for every finite list of smooth boundary directions.

[F1] [[lem-ip-cubic-dn-small-data-differentiability]]: each finite-parameter solution and its nonlinear DN data are $C^3$ in the real parameters near zero.

[F2] [[lem-ip-cubic-dn-third-linearization-identity]]: the third DN derivative determines $6\int_Mq\,v_1v_2v_3\overline{v_4}\,dV_g$ for any four harmonic boundary solutions.

[F3] [[lem-ip-intersecting-gaussian-beam-four-factor-limit]]: the claimed four-factor limit at any transversal intersection is a nonzero constant times the longitudinal Fourier transform of the coefficient difference.

[F4] [[cor-uniqueness-of-the-l-one-fourier-transform]]: an $L^1(\mathbb R)$ function with identically zero Fourier transform vanishes almost everywhere.

[F5] The four-factor supplier uses the external smooth harmonic-product density theorem, Lassas--Liimatainen--Lin--Salo, Proposition 5.1, PDF p. 14 (source hypotheses: compact oriented CTA manifold of dimension at least three, $C^1$ coefficient, four or more smooth harmonic factors). Its actual witnesses are smooth on $\overline M$, depend on the coefficient being tested, and are constant in $\tau$. Thus the smooth-boundary identity [F2] applies directly; no extension of that identity to arbitrary $H^1$ boundary traces is required. The source statement and Section 5 through p. 20 were inspected, not the entire proof through p. 22. Theorem 1.3, pp. 5--6, is the corresponding nonlinear uniqueness theorem, not a replacement local proof here.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice.

Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded smooth domain whose Euclidean metric is isometric to the product metric $dx_1^2\oplus g_0$ on a compact subdomain of $\mathbb R\times D^\circ$, where $(D,g_0)$ is a compact connected simple Riemannian surface with smooth boundary. Let $\gamma_1,\gamma_2\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega,\mathbb R)$ be strictly positive. If their full physical scalar conductivity Dirichlet-to-Neumann maps agree on every boundary datum, then $\gamma_1=\gamma_2$ in $\overline\Omega$.

facts:
[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]] is inherited from the boundary determination and Euclidean potential uniqueness suppliers [F1]--[F3].

[A2] [[def-countable-choice]] is inherited from the boundary determination and Euclidean potential uniqueness suppliers [F1]--[F3].

**Given:** the Euclidean CTA product domain, a compact simple transversal surface, two positive smooth conductivities, and equality of their full physical DN maps.

[F1] [[thm-ip-boundary-determination-of-scalar-conductivity]]: equal full conductivity DN maps imply equality of every inward boundary-normal derivative of the two conductivities.

[F2] [[lem-ip-conductivity-liouville-transform-and-dn-conjugacy]]: for $\rho_j=\sqrt{\gamma_j}$, $q_j=\Delta_g\rho_j/\rho_j$, the conductivity equation is conjugated by $u=\rho_jv$ to $(-\Delta_g+q_j)u=0$, and $\Lambda_{\gamma_j}f=\rho_{j,b}\Lambda_{q_j}(\rho_{j,b}f)-\rho_{j,b}(\partial_\nu\rho_j)f$.

[F3] [[thm-ip-euclidean-schrodinger-calderon-uniqueness]]: on a bounded smooth Euclidean domain in dimension at least three, equality of the full Schrödinger DN maps for real smooth nonresonant potentials implies equality of the potentials.

contract.heading: Example
contract.text:
Let $D=\{x'\in\mathbb R^2:|x'|\leq1\}$ with its Euclidean metric and let
$$M=\{(x_1,x')\in\mathbb R\times D:x_1^2+4|x'|^2\leq1\}$$
with the restricted Euclidean product metric. Then $M$ is a compact smooth three-dimensional product subdomain compactly contained in $\mathbb R\times D^\circ$, and the transversal $D$ is a simple surface whose unweighted scalar geodesic ray transform is injective on real-valued compactly supported smooth functions.

**Given:** the disk $D$, the ellipsoid $M$, and the Euclidean product metric in the statement.

[F1] [[def-ip-transversally-anisotropic-product-domain]]: a compact smooth three-dimensional domain compactly contained in a product $\mathbb R\times M_0^\circ$ with product metric is transversally anisotropic.

[F2] [[def-ip-simple-surface-and-geodesic-xray-transform]]: a compact surface is simple when its boundary is strictly convex, there are no conjugate points, and geodesics exit in finite time.

[F3] [[thm-ip-2d-simple-surface-xray-injectivity]]: for a real $f\in C_c^\infty(D^\circ)$, zero integrals over all nontangential boundary-to-boundary geodesics on a simple surface imply $f=0$.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Assume Countable Choice.

Let $(M,g)$ be a compact smooth Riemannian manifold with smooth boundary, with no orientability assumption. Fix a finite smooth atlas of interior and boundary charts and a smooth partition of unity subordinate to it. For an integer $k\geq0$, define $H^k(M)$ as the completion of $C^\infty(M)$ in the sum of the Euclidean $W^{k,2}$ norms of the localized coordinate representatives; derivatives in a boundary chart are taken on the corresponding half-space. Define $H_0^1(M)$ as the closure of $C_c^\infty(M^\circ)$ in $H^1(M)$. Define $H^{1/2}(\partial M)$ by the fixed finite boundary atlas and partition of unity, using the Euclidean fractional Slobodeckij space $W^{1/2,2}(\mathbb R^{n-1})$ for each localized representative. Define $H^{-1/2}(\partial M)$ as the continuous dual of $H^{1/2}(\partial M)$ with the Riemannian boundary density pairing. These are the fixed-atlas norms used on this page; no atlas-independence assertion is part of this definition.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $n\ge2$, let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a bounded connected domain with smooth nonempty boundary, and regard $\overline\Omega$ as a compact smooth manifold with the Euclidean metric. Write $H^1_{\rm E}(\Omega)=W^{1,2}(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ and let $H^1_{0,\rm E}(\Omega)$ be the closure of $C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ in that norm; put $\mathcal B_{\rm E}:=H^1_{\rm E}(\Omega)/H^1_{0,\rm E}(\Omega)$. Let $H^1_{\rm fix}(\overline\Omega)$ and $H^1_{0,\rm fix}(\overline\Omega)$ be the fixed-atlas spaces on $\overline\Omega$ and let $H^{1/2}_{\rm fix}(\partial\Omega)$ be the fixed-atlas boundary space using localized Euclidean $W^{1/2,2}$ norms. The identity on smooth functions extends to bounded linear isomorphisms between $H^1_{\rm E}(\Omega)$ and $H^1_{\rm fix}(\overline\Omega)$, and between their zero-boundary subspaces. Classical boundary restriction extends to a bounded linear trace $T:H^1_{\rm fix}(\overline\Omega)\to H^{1/2}_{\rm fix}(\partial\Omega)$ with kernel $H^1_{0,\rm fix}(\overline\Omega)$. The induced quotient map is a bounded linear isomorphism

$$H^1_{\rm E}(\Omega)/H^1_{0,\rm E}(\Omega)\;\cong\;H^1_{\rm fix}(\overline\Omega)/H^1_{0,\rm fix}(\overline\Omega)\;\cong\;H^{1/2}_{\rm fix}(\partial\Omega).$$

Thus the Euclidean trace quotient and the fixed-atlas $H^{1/2}$ boundary space are canonically equivalent.

facts:
**Given:** The Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice; the bounded connected smooth Euclidean domain and fixed-atlas conventions in the statement.

[A1] The Axiom of Choice. ([[def-axiom-of-choice]])

[A2] Countable Choice. ([[def-countable-choice]])

[F1] $H^1_{\rm fix}$ is the completion of smooth functions in the fixed finite chartwise $W^{1,2}$ norm; $H^1_{0,\rm fix}$ is the closure of interior compactly supported smooth functions; $H^{1/2}_{\rm fix}$ is the fixed finite sum of localized Euclidean $W^{1/2,2}$ boundary norms. ([[def-ip-sobolev-spaces-on-compact-riemannian-domain]])

[F2] The compact-boundary fractional space consists of $L^2$ classes with finite chartwise Slobodeckij norm, and different finite atlases and subordinate partitions give equivalent norms. ([[def-fractional-sobolev-space-on-a-compact-c-one-boundary]], [[lem-fractional-boundary-norm-is-independent-of-atlas]])

[F3] Smooth flattening-chart compositions and multiplication by the fixed smooth cutoffs are bounded in $W^{1,2}$; restrictions of ambient smooth functions are dense in Euclidean $W^{1,2}(\Omega)$, which is complete. ([[lem-c-k-boundary-flattening-preserves-wkp-locally]], [[lem-weak-leibniz-rule-with-a-smooth-factor]], [[thm-smooth-up-to-the-boundary-density-on-smooth-domains]], [[thm-sobolev-spaces-are-banach-spaces]])

[F4] For $p=2$, the half-space trace extends classical restriction to a bounded map $W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^n_+)\to W^{1/2,2}(\mathbb R^{n-1})$. ([[lem-half-space-trace-has-the-fractional-slobodeckij-bound]])

[F5] The usual trace from Euclidean $H^1(\Omega)$ to $L^2(\partial\Omega)$ is bounded and agrees with classical restriction on continuous Sobolev functions. ([[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]])

[F6] The kernel of that $L^2$ trace is exactly the Euclidean $H^1$-closure of $C_c^\infty(\Omega)$, namely $H^1_{0,\rm E}(\Omega)$. ([[thm-kernel-of-the-trace-is-w-one-p-zero]], [[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]])

[F7] For a bounded smooth Euclidean domain, the $L^2$ trace has a bounded right inverse from the compact-boundary $W^{1/2,2}$ space to Euclidean $H^1(\Omega)$. ([[thm-bounded-right-inverse-for-the-sobolev-trace]])

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice.

Let $(M,g)$ be a nonempty compact connected smooth Riemannian domain with nonempty smooth boundary. For a real-valued $\gamma\in C^\infty(M)$ with $\gamma(x)>0$ at every $x\in M$, let $v_f\in H^1(M)$ be the unique weak solution of $\operatorname{div}_g(\gamma\nabla_gv_f)=0$ with trace $f\in H^{1/2}(\partial M)$, whose existence is supplied by the positive-conductivity solvability lemma. Define the full-data physical conductivity Dirichlet-to-Neumann map $\Lambda_\gamma:H^{1/2}(\partial M)\to H^{-1/2}(\partial M)$ by
$$\langle\Lambda_\gamma f,h\rangle=\int_M\gamma\,g(\nabla_gv_f,\nabla_g\overline{V_h})\,dV_g,$$
where $V_h\in H^1(M)$ is any extension of $h\in H^{1/2}(\partial M)$. The weak equation makes this value independent of the extension. For smooth data, $\Lambda_\gamma f=\gamma\partial_{\nu_{\rm out}}v_f|_{\partial M}$; this is the full physical flux convention. When $M=\overline\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ with the Euclidean metric, this is the scalar Euclidean conductivity DN map.

For a real $q\in C^\infty(M)$ such that the only $w\in H_0^1(M)$ satisfying $(-\Delta_g+q)w=0$ weakly is $w=0$, let $u_f\in H^1(M)$ be the unique weak solution of $(-\Delta_g+q)u_f=0$ with trace $f$, whose existence follows from the nonresonant regularity lemma. Define the Schrödinger DN map $\Lambda_q:H^{1/2}(\partial M)\to H^{-1/2}(\partial M)$ by
$$\langle\Lambda_qf,h\rangle=\int_M\big(g(\nabla_gu_f,\nabla_g\overline{V_h})+qu_f\overline{V_h}\big)\,dV_g.$$
For smooth data this is $\partial_{\nu_{\rm out}}u_f|_{\partial M}$. Equality of these operators means equality on all of $H^{1/2}(\partial M)$, not equality for a restricted set of boundary inputs.

facts:
**Given:** AC and Countable Choice; the compact smooth Riemannian domain; positive smooth $\gamma$; a real smooth nonresonant $q$; and the weak solutions in the Definition.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]] is assumed by the Euclidean trace-kernel and Gauss-Green suppliers [F2, F5].

[A2] [[def-countable-choice]] is assumed by the local weak-solution, trace-lift, and collar suppliers [F3, F4, F6, F8].

[F1] [[def-ip-sobolev-spaces-on-compact-riemannian-domain]]: $H_0^1(M)$ is the closure of interior compactly supported smooth functions in a fixed finite chartwise $H^1$ norm; the trace is defined chartwise and the fixed finite atlas admits a smooth partition of unity.

[F2] [[thm-kernel-of-the-trace-is-w-one-p-zero]]: on a bounded Euclidean $C^1$ domain, an $H^1$ function has zero trace if and only if it belongs to the $H^1$ closure of compactly supported interior smooth functions.

[F3] [[lem-ip-conductivity-map-wellposedness]]: for each $H^{1/2}$ boundary value, the positive-conductivity weak solution exists uniquely, its weak equation vanishes on every $H_0^1$ test, and smooth boundary data with smooth forcing give a solution smooth up to the boundary.

[F4] [[lem-ip-smooth-manifold-elliptic-nonresonant-regularity]]: under the stated trivial Dirichlet-kernel condition, the Schrödinger weak solution is unique and smooth for smooth boundary data.

[F5] [[thm-sobolev-gauss-green-formula-on-c-one-domains]]: for smooth functions on a bounded Euclidean $C^1$ domain, integration by parts produces the outward-normal boundary term.

[F6] [[thm-bounded-right-inverse-for-the-sobolev-trace]]: each $H^{1/2}$ boundary datum has an $H^1$ extension in a smooth Euclidean chart; finite chart localization supplies such extensions on $M$.

[F7] [[lem-trace-commutes-with-smooth-boundary-cutoffs-and-charts]]: multiplying by a smooth cutoff multiplies the trace by its boundary restriction, and flattening charts transport the trace to the Euclidean chart trace.

[F8] [[thm-collar-neighborhood-theorem]]: smooth boundary data extend smoothly into a collar by constant normal extension and a cutoff.

[F9] [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]]: the trace is a bounded map on $H^1$ and agrees with restriction for smooth functions.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $n\ge2$ and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a bounded connected open set with smooth boundary. Write $H^1(\Omega)=W^{1,2}(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ and let $H_0^1(\Omega)$ be the $H^1$-closure of $C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R)$. Define the boundary trace-data space $\mathcal B_\Omega:=H^1(\Omega)/H_0^1(\Omega)$ with quotient norm; the trace-quotient lemma identifies this quotient with the fixed-atlas $H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega)$ boundary data convention of the scalar conductivity map. Let $\gamma\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega;\operatorname{Sym}_n(\mathbb R))$ be uniformly positive definite, so some $0<c\le C<\infty$ satisfy $c|\xi|^2\le \xi^T\gamma(x)\xi\le C|\xi|^2$ for all $x\in\overline\Omega$ and $\xi\in\mathbb R^n$. For $f=[U]\in\mathcal B_\Omega$, a weak solution with boundary datum $f$ is a class $u_{\gamma,f}\in H^1(\Omega)$ with $[u_{\gamma,f}]=f$ and

$$\int_\Omega \gamma\nabla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\nabla\varphi\,dx=0\qquad(\varphi\in H_0^1(\Omega)).$$

The weak anisotropic Dirichlet-to-Neumann map is the bilinear-form candidate $\Lambda_\gamma:\mathcal B_\Omega\times\mathcal B_\Omega\to\mathbb R$ given, whenever the weak solution exists, by

$$\langle\Lambda_\gamma f,h\rangle:=\int_\Omega\gamma\nabla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\nabla V_h\,dx,$$

where $V_h\in H^1(\Omega)$ is any representative of $h$. The local anisotropic conductivity well-posedness lemma proves existence and uniqueness for every boundary class, independence of the representative $V_h$, and boundedness on $\mathcal B_\Omega\times\mathcal B_\Omega$; it therefore makes this candidate a bounded bilinear map. The map is the boundary energy form for the equation $\operatorname{div}(\gamma\nabla u)=0$. Under the trace-quotient isomorphism and the local boundedness result, this form gives the usual weak map into the dual $H^{-1/2}(\partial\Omega)$ with the scalar convention.

contract.heading: Open problem
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice, and let $n\ge3$. Let $M$ be a compact connected smooth $n$-manifold with nonempty smooth boundary and no orientability assumption, and let $\Gamma\subsetneq\partial M$ be a nonempty relatively open patch. Use a fixed finite smooth atlas and subordinate smooth partition of unity. Define $H^1(M)$ as the completion of $C^\infty(M)$ under the sum of localized Euclidean $W^{1,2}$ norms. For each integer $k\ge0$, $H^k(M)$ uses the same completion convention with localized $W^{k,2}$ norms. Let $H_0^1(M)$ be the closure of $C_c^\infty(M^\circ)$ in $H^1(M)$. Define $H^{1/2}(\partial M)$ by the same fixed boundary atlas and partition, using localized Euclidean $W^{1/2,2}$ Slobodeckij norms. Let $\operatorname{Tr}:H^1(M)\to H^{1/2}(\partial M)$ be the Sobolev trace, the continuous extension of classical boundary restriction. For a smooth Riemannian metric $g$, write $dV_g=\sqrt{\det(g_{ij})}\,|dx^1\cdots dx^n|$ in coordinates and let $dS_g$ be its induced boundary density; $\langle du,dv\rangle_g$ is the cotangent inner product induced by $g^{-1}$. For $f\in C_c^\infty(\Gamma)$ extended by zero on $\partial M\setminus\Gamma$, let $u_{g,f}\in H^1(M)$ be the unique weak solution with $\operatorname{Tr}u_{g,f}=f$ and

$$\int_M\langle du_{g,f},dv\rangle_g\,dV_g=0\qquad(v\in H_0^1(M)).$$

The zero-boundary kernel is trivial by uniqueness of the positive scalar Dirichlet problem, so the nonresonant elliptic regularity interface applies; for smooth $f$, the solution lies in every integer-order Sobolev space. This is the positive scalar conductivity Dirichlet problem at $\gamma\equiv1$. Define its local zero-frequency energy map, with the same patch for inputs and observations, by

$$\mathcal E_{g,\Gamma}(f,h):=\int_M\langle du_{g,f},du_{g,h}\rangle_g\,dV_g\qquad(f,h\in C_c^\infty(\Gamma)).$$

The displayed energy is the weak scalar DN pairing with the second extension chosen as $u_{g,h}$. If two smooth metrics $g_1,g_2$ on this same manifold satisfy $\mathcal E_{g_1,\Gamma}(f,h)=\mathcal E_{g_2,\Gamma}(f,h)$ for every such pair, must there be a smooth diffeomorphism $\Phi:M\to M$ with $\Phi|_\Gamma=\operatorname{id}$ and $g_2=\Phi^*g_1$, where $(\Phi^*g_1)_p(v,w):=(g_1)_{\Phi(p)}(D\Phi_pv,D\Phi_pw)$?

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $(M,g)$ be a compact smooth Riemannian domain with smooth boundary and no orientability assumption, let $q\in C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$, and suppose the only $w\in H_0^1(M)$ satisfying $(-\Delta_g+q)w=0$ weakly is $w=0$. For every $F\in L^2(M)$ and $f\in H^{1/2}(\partial M)$ there is a unique weak solution $u\in H^1(M)$ of $(-\Delta_g+q)u=F$ with trace $f$. If $f=0$, $F\in H^m(M)$ and $m\geq0$ is an integer, then $u\in H^{m+2}(M)$ and $\|u\|_{H^{m+2}}\leq C_m\|F\|_{H^m}$. If $F$ and $f$ are smooth, this solution belongs to $H^m(M)$ for every integer $m\geq0$.

facts:
[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: every family of nonempty sets has a choice function; this is assumed by the Rellich compactness and abstract Fredholm suppliers used in steps 1.2 and 2.1.

[A2] [[def-countable-choice]]: every countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function; this is assumed by the Lax--Milgram, partition, and trace suppliers used in steps 1.1 and 2.2.

**Given:** AC and Countable Choice; the compact smooth Riemannian domain; a real smooth potential with trivial Dirichlet kernel; $F\in L^2(M)$; and $f\in H^{1/2}(\partial M)$.

[F1] [[def-ip-sobolev-spaces-on-compact-riemannian-domain]]: $H_0^1(M)$ is the closure of compactly supported interior smooth functions in $H^1(M)$; the boundary space $H^{1/2}$ is defined by finite chartwise Euclidean $W^{1/2,2}$ norms.

[F2] [[thm-lax-milgram]]: a bounded coercive sesquilinear form on a Hilbert space has a unique weak solution.

[F3] [[thm-rellich-compactness-from-w-one-p-zero-to-lp]]: on a bounded Euclidean open set, $W_0^{1,2}$ is compactly embedded in $L^2$.

[F4] [[thm-fredholm-alternative-for-identity-minus-compact]]: for compact $K$ on a Banach space, $I-K$ is injective if and only if it is surjective, and then it is boundedly invertible.

[F5] [[thm-bounded-right-inverse-for-the-sobolev-trace]]: a smooth bounded Euclidean domain has a bounded right inverse from its $H^{1/2}$ boundary space to $H^1$.

[F6] [[thm-higher-order-boundary-regularity-for-dirichlet-problems]]: a zero-trace weak solution of a uniformly elliptic divergence-form equation on a bounded smooth Euclidean domain gains two derivatives, with the stated $H^{m+2}$ estimate.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K:X\to Y$ be a compact linear map
between real or complex Hilbert spaces, with Hilbert adjoint $K^*:Y\to X$.
Write $\mathbb N_{>0}:=\{1,2,3,\ldots\}$. If $R(K)$ has finite dimension
$r\in\mathbb N$, put $J=\{1,\ldots,r\}$, interpreted as empty when $r=0$;
if $R(K)$ is infinite-dimensional, put $J=\mathbb N_{>0}$. Thus $J$ indexes
exactly the positive singular values $s_j>0$ in nonincreasing order. Let
$(v_j)_{j\in J}$ and $(u_j)_{j\in J}$ be complete
orthonormal families in $N(K)^\perp$ and $\overline{R(K)}$, respectively,
with $Kv_j=s_ju_j$ and $K^*u_j=s_jv_j$. The empty sum is zero, finite $J$
uses a finite sum, and infinite $J$ uses the norm-convergent series whenever
the stated square-summability condition holds. Use inner products linear in the
first argument. Define the Picard sum
$$P_K(y):=\sum_{j\in J}\frac{|\langle y,u_j\rangle_Y|^2}{s_j^2},\qquad y\in Y.$$
Then:

1. The exact equation $Kx=y$ is solvable if and only if
   $y\perp N(K^*)$ and $P_K(y)<\infty$.

2. The domain of the Hilbert-space Moore–Penrose inverse is
   $$D(K^\dagger)=R(K)\oplus R(K)^\perp=\{y\in Y:P_K(y)<\infty\},$$
   and for every $y\in D(K^\dagger)$,
   $$K^\dagger y=\sum_{j\in J}\frac{\langle y,u_j\rangle_Y}{s_j}v_j.$$
   Thus the orthogonal component in $R(K)^\perp=N(K^*)$ is discarded by
   $K^\dagger$; exact range membership additionally requires that component
   to be zero.

facts:
**Given:** Countable Choice, the compact Hilbert-space model $K:X\to Y$, its adjoint $K^*$, and the positive singular system described in the statement.

[F1] The model supplies real or complex Hilbert parameter/data spaces and a compact linear forward map ([[def-ip-compact-linear-inverse-model]]).

[F2] The compact SVD supplies the positive singular values, complete orthonormal right and left singular families, the singular relations, and the operator expansion ([[thm-singular-value-decomposition-for-compact-operators]]).

[F3] $(R(K))^\perp=N(K^*)$ and $\overline{R(K)}=(N(K^*))^\perp$ ([[lem-kernel-range-orthogonality-for-hilbert-adjoints]]).

[F4] $\langle Kx,y\rangle_Y=\langle x,K^*y\rangle_X$ ([[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]]).

[F5] Finite Bessel inequality: $\sum_{j\in F}|\langle x,e_j\rangle|^2\le\|x\|^2$ for every finite orthonormal family ([[lem-finite-bessel-inequality]]).

[F6] Finite orthogonal sums satisfy Pythagoras ([[lem-pythagorean-theorem-and-finite-orthogonal-sums]]).

[F7] On a complete orthonormal family, the finite Fourier sums converge in norm to each vector in its closed span ([[thm-hilbert-space-fourier-expansion]]).

[F8] Every closed subspace of a Hilbert space has an orthogonal decomposition ([[thm-orthogonal-decomposition-by-a-closed-subspace]]).

[F9] Hilbert spaces are complete and Cauchy–Schwarz makes the inner product continuous in either argument ([[def-hilbert-space]], [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-in-an-inner-product-space]]).

[F10] For $r+z$ with $r\in R(K)$ and $z\in R(K)^\perp$, the inverse returns the minimum-norm preimage of $r$ and annihilates $z$ ([[def-ip-unbounded-hilbert-moore-penrose-inverse]]).

[F11] A compact linear operator is bounded and hence continuous in norm ([[def-compact-linear-operator]]).

[A1] Countable Choice is the hypothesis in the compact SVD and Hilbert Fourier expansion used here ([[def-countable-choice]]).

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
**Inputs and admissible conditions.** Fix the domain $D$, wavenumber $k>0$, and library Fourier convention from the fixed-frequency data definition. Give nonempty finite lists of incident directions $d_1,\ldots,d_s\in S^2$ and observation directions $\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_r\in S^2$. Give a finite measurable partition $D=\bigsqcup_{n=1}^N E_n$ with $|E_n|>0$, complex Born-data samples $y=(y_{ba})\in\mathbb C^{rs}$, a discrepancy threshold $\delta\ge0$, and an iteration budget $B\in\mathbb N_0:=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$. The sample frequency for pair $(\theta_b,d_a)$ is $\xi_{ba}:=k(\theta_b-d_a)/(2\pi)$. The declared finite discrete Born Fourier matrix $F\in\mathbb C^{rs\times N}$ has entries
$$F_{(b,a),n}:=\frac1{4\pi}\int_{E_n}e^{-2\pi i x\cdot\xi_{ba}}\,dx.$$
For a piecewise-constant contrast $q_c:=\sum_{n=1}^N c_n1_{E_n}$, its sampled first Born data vector is exactly $Fc$.
The input also declares a reduced singular-value decomposition
$$Fc=\sum_{j=1}^{p}\sigma_j\langle c,v_j\rangle u_j\qquad(c\in\mathbb C^N),$$
where $p=\operatorname{rank}F$, the positive singular values $\sigma_j$ have orthonormal right vectors $v_j$ and orthonormal left vectors $u_j$, and the empty sum is used when $F=0$. Give a scalar filter $g:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb C$ whose values at the $\sigma_j$ are finite and with $g(0)=0$. The threshold filter $g_\tau(\sigma)=1/\sigma$ for $\sigma>\tau$ and $g_\tau(\sigma)=0$ for $0\le\sigma\le\tau$ is the truncated singular-value pseudoinverse at threshold $\tau\ge0$.

**Instructions and outputs.**

1. If $B=0$, return no estimate, no residual, and status **budget-exhausted**, with zero filter applications.
2. If $B\ge1$, form the coefficient estimate
   $$\widehat c:=\sum_{j:\sigma_j>0}g(\sigma_j)\langle y,u_j\rangle v_j,$$
   where $\langle z,w\rangle=\sum_\ell z_\ell\overline{w_\ell}$ is linear in its first argument. Return the piecewise-constant reconstruction $\widehat q:=\sum_{n=1}^{N}\widehat c_n1_{E_n}$ after exactly one filter application.
3. Compute the finite data residual $R:=\|F\widehat c-y\|_2$, where $\|z\|_2=(\sum_\ell|z_\ell|^2)^{1/2}$. Return status **discrepancy** when $R\le\delta$, and **residual-above-threshold** when $R>\delta$; in either case also return $\widehat q$, $R$, and the application count $1$.

This procedure only defines one filtered finite-dimensional Born reconstruction and a residual status. The residual is not an exact-range test for an infinite-dimensional compact forward operator and does not establish a nonlinear solution, identifiability, stability, convergence, or correctness of the reconstructed contrast.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Fix an integer $d\ge2$, a bounded polyhedral open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$, a finite matching affine simplicial mesh $\mathcal T_h$ of $\Omega$, and unisolvent reference finite elements assembled on that mesh. Thus the mesh is a finite face-to-face cover by nondegenerate affine simplices with disjoint interiors, and each local finite-element degree-of-freedom map is bijective on its polynomial space. Fix coefficient spaces $\Theta_h=\mathbb R^m$, $V_h=\mathbb R^n$, and $Y_h=\mathbb R^s$ with their standard Euclidean inner products, where $m,n,s\ge1$. Let $Q_h\subseteq\Theta_h$ be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let $O_h\subseteq\Theta_h$ be open with $Q_h\subseteq O_h$.

A **finite-element PDE model** in this contract consists of a continuously differentiable residual map $R_h:O_h\times V_h\to V_h$ and a continuously differentiable observation map $G_h:O_h\times V_h\to Y_h$. It must supply a continuously differentiable state branch $S_h:O_h\to V_h$ satisfying $R_h(q,S_h(q))=0$ for every $q\in O_h$. For every $q\in Q_h$, this branch must be the specified unique admissible state and the matrix $D_uR_h(q,S_h(q))$ must be invertible. The discrete forward map is $F_h(q):=G_h(q,S_h(q))$. The unisolvent finite-element degrees of freedom identify $V_h$ with its coefficient space; all matrix transposes below are in the fixed Euclidean coefficient inner products.

For data $y^\delta\in Y_h$, reference parameter $q_0\in\Theta_h$, and $\alpha>0$, the discrete nonlinear Tikhonov objective is
$$
\Phi_h(q):=\frac12\|F_h(q)-y^\delta\|_{Y_h}^2+\frac\alpha2\|q-q_0\|_{\Theta_h}^2\qquad(q\in Q_h).
$$
Define the finite-dimensional objective before eliminating the state by
$$
J_h(q,u):=\frac12\|G_h(q,u)-y^\delta\|_{Y_h}^2+\frac\alpha2\|q-q_0\|_{\Theta_h}^2.
$$
The symbols $\nabla_uJ_h$ and $\nabla_qJ_h$ denote the Euclidean gradient vectors representing the two partial derivative functionals. At an admissible $q$, the **exact discrete adjoint** $p_h(q)\in V_h$ is the unique solution of
$$
\bigl(D_uR_h(q,S_h(q))\bigr)^T p_h(q)=\nabla_uJ_h(q,S_h(q)).
$$
The associated discrete-adjoint gradient vector is
$$
g_h(q):=\nabla_qJ_h(q,S_h(q))-\bigl(D_qR_h(q,S_h(q))\bigr)^T p_h(q).
$$
The next lemma proves that this vector is the gradient of $\Phi_h$; the definition itself asserts no minimizer exists and no gradient iteration converges.

An **admissibility predicate** is a specified finite-time test $\operatorname{adm}_h(q)$ that decides whether $q\in Q_h$ and checks the model's stated coefficient, boundary, mesh, and time-step hypotheses before a PDE solve. For an explicit time discretization, a Courant–Friedrichs–Lewy condition (CFL condition) is a method-specific bound relating the time step to the mesh and the discrete evolution operator; no universal CFL threshold is part of this definition. A true predicate result certifies that the declared model hypotheses hold for that input, not merely that a heuristic check passed.

The model must also supply an exact finite-dimensional projection routine which returns $P_{Q_h}(z)$ for a queried $z\in\Theta_h$ in finite time or reports failure only when its declared finite call budget is exhausted. The unique nearest point exists because $Q_h$ is nonempty, closed, and convex, but an operational routine for computing it is an additional part of this contract.

A solver routine with declared nonnegative state and adjoint tolerances $\tau_u,\tau_p$ and a finite solve budget must return either `failure` or approximate state and adjoint vectors $\widetilde u,\widetilde p$ together with certified finite bounds $\rho_u,\rho_p,\eta_u,\eta_p,P,L_{J,u},L_{R,u},M_q,L_{G,u}$. The residual bounds have the exact-system meaning $\|R_h(q,\widetilde u)\|_{V_h}\le\rho_u$ and $\|(D_uR_h(q,u))^T\widetilde p-\nabla_uJ_h(q,u)\|_{V_h}\le\rho_p$, where $u=S_h(q)$; both must satisfy $\rho_u\le\tau_u$ and $\rho_p\le\tau_p$. In particular, an adjoint residual evaluated at $\widetilde u$ alone does not certify $\rho_p$ unless the model also bounds the resulting state and derivative-data defects. With $u=S_h(q)$ and $p=p_h(q)$, the model must certify
$$
\|u-\widetilde u\|_{V_h}\le\eta_u,\qquad \|p-\widetilde p\|_{V_h}\le\eta_p,\qquad \|p\|_{V_h}\le P,
$$
$$
\|\nabla_qJ_h(q,u)-\nabla_qJ_h(q,\widetilde u)\|_{\Theta_h}\le L_{J,u}\eta_u,
$$
$$
\|(D_qR_h(q,u))^T-(D_qR_h(q,\widetilde u))^T\|\le L_{R,u}\eta_u,\qquad \|(D_qR_h(q,\widetilde u))^T\|\le M_q,
$$
and $\|G_h(q,u)-G_h(q,\widetilde u)\|_{Y_h}\le L_{G,u}\eta_u$. It then returns
$$
\widetilde g:=\nabla_qJ_h(q,\widetilde u)-(D_qR_h(q,\widetilde u))^T\widetilde p,\qquad \widetilde F:=G_h(q,\widetilde u),
$$
All constants and state/adjoint error bounds must be justified for the chosen model with every derivative-data, geometry, quadrature, and algebraic-solve defect retained. Certified residual bounds $\rho_u,\rho_p$ do not by themselves imply $\eta_u,\eta_p$; a separate model-valid stability estimate is required. The proposition below derives the resulting $\varepsilon_g$ and $\varepsilon_F$ bounds. An objective-evaluation routine must return in its finite budget either `failure` or an interval $[\ell_h(q),u_h(q)]$ containing the exact value $\Phi_h(q)$; `failure` is permitted only when a required state/adjoint solve fails its contract or the evaluation-call budget is exhausted. Exact evaluation is the degenerate-interval case. Projection and objective-evaluation calls consume the algorithm's finite evaluation budget. Each routine must return within its declared budget or report failure.

If a continuous model $F$ is also supplied, an optional mesh certificate $\varepsilon_{\rm mesh}$ must separately bound the claimed continuous-to-discrete error, such as $\|F_h(q)-F(q)\|$ or $\|\nabla\Phi_h(q)-\nabla\Phi(q)\|$. The state and adjoint algebraic residual certificates do not imply this mesh certificate.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Assume a finite-element PDE model satisfying the admissibility and certificate contract, with nonempty closed convex coefficient set $Q_h$, discrete Tikhonov objective $\Phi_h$ using reference coefficient $q_0$, a state/adjoint solve routine, an exact projection routine, an objective interval routine, and finite solve and evaluation budgets. Let the input be an initial coefficient $q_{\rm init}\in Q_h$, data $y^\delta\in Y_h$, noise bound $\delta\ge0$, penalty $\alpha>0$, state and adjoint residual tolerances $\tau_u,\tau_p\ge0$, discrepancy factor $\kappa\ge1$, stationarity tolerance $\tau_g\ge0$, scaling parameter $L>0$, and positive integer budgets $N_{\rm iter}$, $N_{\rm solve}$, $N_{\rm eval}$, and $N_{\rm backtrack}$. The global budget $N_{\rm solve}$ counts state and adjoint solves; $N_{\rm eval}$ counts exact projections and objective-interval evaluations. The scaling parameter $L$ is only a positive step-size scale; it is not assumed to be a Lipschitz constant. The algorithm returns a coefficient, one status from `converged`, `discrepancy-stopped`, `linear-solve-failed`, `inadmissible`, or `budget-exhausted`, and any diagnostics certified at that coefficient.

1. If $q_{\rm init}\notin Q_h$ or the model's exact admissibility predicate is false at $q_{\rm init}$, return status `inadmissible` without solving a PDE. Otherwise set $q:=q_{\rm init}$.

2. For $k=0,\ldots,N_{\rm iter}$, first check the finite-time admissibility predicate, which includes membership in $Q_h$. If it is false, return `inadmissible`. If no global solve or evaluation budget remains, return `budget-exhausted`.

3. Call the state/adjoint solver at $q$ with tolerances $\tau_u,\tau_p$ and the remaining solve budget. If it returns `failure`, if either certified residual bound exceeds its declared tolerance, or if any required state/adjoint error estimate or derivative bound is missing or invalid, return `linear-solve-failed`. Otherwise receive $\widetilde g_h$, $\widetilde F_h$, $\eta_u,\eta_p,P,L_{J,u},L_{R,u},M_q,L_{G,u}$ and set $\varepsilon_g=(L_{J,u}+L_{R,u}P)\eta_u+M_q\eta_p$ and $\varepsilon_F=L_{G,u}\eta_u$.

4. Use the exact projection routine to compute $P_{Q_h}(q-\widetilde g_h/L)$. If the routine fails or the evaluation budget is exhausted, return `budget-exhausted`. Set $\widetilde\rho:=L\|q-P_{Q_h}(q-\widetilde g_h/L)\|_2$. If $\widetilde\rho+\varepsilon_g\le\tau_g$, return `converged` with stationarity upper bound $\widetilde\rho+\varepsilon_g$. This status means only that the exact projected-gradient residual of the discrete objective is within tolerance; it is not a claim that an iterate sequence converges or that $q$ is a global minimizer.

5. Compute $d^+:=\|\widetilde F_h-y^\delta\|_{Y_h}+\varepsilon_F$. If $d^+\le\kappa\delta$, return `discrepancy-stopped` with data-residual upper bound $d^+$. This status certifies only the discrete model's data discrepancy.

6. If $k=N_{\rm iter}$, return `budget-exhausted` at the current coefficient with its current diagnostics. Otherwise, evaluate the current objective using its certified interval $[\ell_h(q),u_h(q)]$. If the evaluation fails because a required state or adjoint solve fails its contract, return `linear-solve-failed`; if the global solve or evaluation budget is exhausted, return `budget-exhausted`.

7. For $j=0,\ldots,N_{\rm backtrack}-1$, set $t_j=2^{-j}/L$ and use the exact projection routine to compute $q_j=P_{Q_h}(q-t_j\widetilde g_h)$. If projection fails or the evaluation budget is exhausted, return `budget-exhausted`. Reject this trial and continue to the next $j$ if $q_j=q$ or its admissibility predicate is false. Otherwise evaluate a certified interval $[\ell_h(q_j),u_h(q_j)]$. If evaluation fails because a required linear solve fails its contract, return `linear-solve-failed`; if it only exhausts the finite evaluation budget, return `budget-exhausted`. Accept the first trial with $u_h(q_j)\le\ell_h(q)$, set $q:=q_j$, and continue to the next outer iteration. This interval test guarantees $\Phi_h(q_j)\le\Phi_h(q)$.

8. If no trial is accepted within the backtracking budget, return `budget-exhausted` at the current coefficient. Each accepted trial uses one of the at most $N_{\rm iter}$ updates; the inclusive outer loop evaluates the final coefficient before returning budget exhaustion.

The global solve budget counts all primal and adjoint solves used both at iterates and in objective trials. The evaluation budget counts every projection and objective-interval call. Each status is returned after finitely many tests because all four budgets are finite and every model routine returns in finite time or reports failure. Any continuous-to-discrete mesh bound is reported separately by the model contract and is never inferred from the algebraic state or adjoint residuals.

contract.heading: Example

facts:
**Given:** The unit square, the four-cell mesh, the specified bilinear form and forcing functional, the scalar control coefficient space $\Theta_h=\mathbb R$ with $Q_h=[0,1]$, Countable Choice, the piecewise-affine state space, observation $F(\gamma)=\int_\Omega u(\gamma)$, the data and penalty, and the exact algorithm routines and tolerances specified in the Example.

[A1] Countable Choice means that every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-countable-choice]]).

[F1] For the bounded Lipschitz domain and bounded coercive form, the state and adjoint equations have unique solutions under Countable Choice ([[def-linear-elliptic-pde-constrained-control-problem]], [[thm-linear-elliptic-control-state-and-adjoint-wellposedness]]).

[F2] A continuous piecewise polynomial with zero boundary facet traces on a bounded polyhedral matching mesh lies in $W^{1,2}_0$ under Countable Choice ([[thm-zero-boundary-piecewise-polynomials-in-w10p]]).

[F3] On each cell the mesh is affine and the local nodal degree-of-freedom map is unisolvent ([[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]], [[def-reference-finite-element-and-unisolvent-dofs]]).

[F4] For $\alpha>0$, the Tikhonov objective is one half squared data misfit plus $\alpha/2$ times the squared distance from the reference parameter ([[def-ip-nonlinear-tikhonov-functional]]).

[F5] The algorithm's `converged` status tests the exact discrete projected-gradient residual, not the continuous-to-discrete mesh error ([[alg-ip-finite-element-pde-tikhonov]], [[def-ip-pde-solver-admissibility-contract]]).

[F6] In any real inner-product space, $|\langle v,z\rangle|\le\|v\|\|z\|$ ([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-in-an-inner-product-space]]).

[F7] The algorithm's `converged` status is sound for the exact discrete projected-gradient residual but asserts no mesh convergence or continuous-model accuracy ([[thm-ip-finite-element-pde-tikhonov-status-soundness-and-termination]]).

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Fix an integer $d\ge2$. Let $\Omega\subset(0,1)^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected open domain with $C^\infty$ boundary, and let $\Omega'\subset\Omega$ be an open domain whose closure is compact and contained in $\Omega$. Fix real parameters $m>0$, $M\ge\max\{1,m\}$, $R>0$, and $0<\alpha<1$. Define
$$\Gamma_{m,M}(\Omega):=\{\gamma\in L^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R):m\le\gamma(x)\le M\text{ for almost every }x\in\Omega\}$$
and
$$\Gamma'_{m,M}(\Omega,\Omega'):=\{\gamma\in\Gamma_{m,M}(\Omega):\gamma=1\text{ almost everywhere on }\Omega\setminus\Omega'\}.$$
For $\gamma\in BV(\Omega)$ set $\|\gamma\|_{BV(\Omega)}:=\max\{\|\gamma\|_{L^1(\Omega)},TV(\gamma;\Omega)\}$. For a continuously differentiable function on $\overline\Omega$ whose first derivatives are $\alpha$-Hölder continuous, set
$$\|\gamma\|_{C^{1,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}:=\max\left\{\max_{|\beta|\le1}\sup_{x\in\overline\Omega}|\partial^\beta\gamma(x)|,\ \max_{|\beta|=1}\sup_{\substack{x,y\in\overline\Omega\\x\ne y}}\frac{|\partial^\beta\gamma(x)-\partial^\beta\gamma(y)|}{|x-y|^\alpha}\right\}.$$
Define
$$X_d(R):=\begin{cases}\{\gamma\in\Gamma'_{m,M}(\Omega,\Omega')\cap BV(\Omega):\|\gamma\|_{BV(\Omega)}\le R\},&d=2,\\[2mm]\{\gamma\in\Gamma'_{m,M}(\Omega,\Omega')\cap C^{1,\alpha}(\overline\Omega):\|\gamma\|_{C^{1,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}\le R\},&d\ge3.\end{cases}$$
For $\gamma\in\Gamma'_{m,M}(\Omega,\Omega')$, define its measurable background extension $\gamma_e:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ by $\gamma_e=\gamma$ almost everywhere on $\Omega$ and $\gamma_e=1$ on $\mathbb R^d\setminus\Omega$. Then $\gamma_e-1$ vanishes almost everywhere outside $\Omega'$. No pointwise continuity of $\gamma_e$ is asserted. The classes $X_d(R)$ are not assumed nonempty.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $x_0\in\mathbb R^2$, $r>0$, $E=B(x_0,r)$, and let $D\subset\mathbb R^2$ be open with $\overline E\subset D$. Then $\chi_E\in BV(\mathbb R^2)$, its distributional derivative is
$$D\chi_E=-\nu_E\,\mathcal H^1|_{\partial E},\qquad \nu_E(x)=\frac{x-x_0}{r},$$
and
$$TV(\chi_E;\mathbb R^2)=TV(\chi_E;D)=2\pi r.$$

facts:
**Given:** Countable Choice, $x_0\in\mathbb R^2$, $r>0$, $E=B(x_0,r)$, and an open $D$ with $\overline E\subset D$.

[F1] For $u\in L^1$, $\langle Du,\phi\rangle=-\int u\,\operatorname{div}\phi$ on smooth compactly supported tests; if $Du$ is a vector measure, $|Du|(A)$ is the supremum of $\sum_j|Du(A_j)|$ over Borel partitions of $A$, and $TV(u;G)=|Du|(G)$. ([[def-ip-spatial-bv-and-distributional-tv]])

[F2] On an epigraph of a locally Lipschitz graph, a smooth vector field supported away from the chart sides has divergence integral $\int\psi(y,h(y))\cdot(Dh(y),-1)\,dy$; the sign reverses for a subgraph. For smooth graphs, [F4] identifies this with outward-normal surface flux. ([[lem-ip-lipschitz-graph-area-and-calculus-under-countable-choice]])

[F3] For a $C^1$ diffeomorphism $T$, the change-of-variables identity holds for every nonnegative Lebesgue-measurable integrand; additivity gives the corresponding identity for an integrable signed integrand by applying it to its positive and negative parts. ([[thm-c-one-change-of-variables-for-nonnegative-lebesgue-measurable-functions]], [[cor-additivity-of-the-nonnegative-lebesgue-integral]])

[F4] Surface measure on a compact $C^1$ hypersurface is the chart integral; the regular chart density is the square root of the Gram determinant, so a circle parametrization has density equal to its speed. ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]], [[lem-surface-integral-is-independent-of-c-one-boundary-charts]])

[F5] The derivative of a $C^1$ composition is the product of the derivative matrices. ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]])

[A1] Countable Choice is assumed at the graph-calculus, surface-integral, and change-of-variables interfaces. ([[def-countable-choice]])

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $m\ge1$, let $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, and let $h:Q\to\mathbb R$ be locally Lipschitz. Then $h$ is differentiable almost everywhere, its partial derivatives are measurable and are its weak derivatives. On every open region where $h$ is $L$-Lipschitz, $|Dh|\le L$ almost everywhere. Let $H^m$ denote the repository's unnormalised Hausdorff measure, put $c_m=H^m((0,1]^m)$, and write $\sigma_m=c_m^{-1}H^m$ also on Euclidean spaces containing $m$-dimensional subsets. The graph map $F(y)=(y,h(y))$ satisfies, for every nonnegative Borel $a$,
$$\int_{F(Q)}a(x)\,d\sigma_m(x)=\int_Qa(F(y))\sqrt{1+|Dh(y)|^2}\,dy.$$
For the epigraph $G=\{(y,z):y\in Q,\ z>h(y)\}$, a smooth vector field compactly supported away from the chart sides satisfies
$$\int_G\operatorname{div}\phi\,dx=\int_Q\phi(y,h(y))\cdot(Dh(y),-1)\,dy.$$
Thus its outward normal is $(Dh,-1)/\sqrt{1+|Dh|^2}$ almost everywhere. The sign reverses for a subgraph. The graph surface measure is locally finite and Radon on $F(Q)$ with its relative topology, and its null sets coincide with graph images of Lebesgue-null subsets of the base.

facts:
**Given:** Countable Choice and the locally Lipschitz graph in the Statement.

[F1] A Lipschitz interval function is absolutely continuous and has a derivative almost everywhere; these conclusions assume at most Countable Choice. ([[thm-c1-lipschitz-ac-bv-hierarchy]], [[thm-absolutely-continuous-functions-have-integrable-derivatives]])

[F2] Completed Euclidean Fubini and Tonelli hold under Countable Choice. ([[thm-tonelli-and-fubini-for-completed-product-measures]], [[thm-euclidean-lebesgue-measure-is-the-completion-of-the-product-of-lebesgue-measures]])

[F3] Lebesgue differentiation of locally integrable functions holds under Countable Choice. ([[thm-lebesgue-differentiation-theorem-for-locally-integrable-functions-on-r-n]])

[F4] Hausdorff measure on an $m$-plane, divided by $c_m$, is Euclidean $m$-volume; isometries preserve it and $K$-Lipschitz maps increase it by at most $K^m$. Invertible linear maps scale Euclidean volume by the absolute determinant. ([[thm-hausdorff-n-measure-is-proportional-to-lebesgue-measure]], [[cor-hausdorff-measure-under-similarities]], [[thm-hausdorff-measure-under-lipschitz-maps]], [[thm-linear-change-of-variables-for-lebesgue-measure]])

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $n\ge2$ and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a nonempty bounded connected open set whose boundary is covered by finitely many $C^1$ graph charts. Give $H^1(\Omega;\mathbb K)=W^{1,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ its Sobolev norm, let $H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ be the $H^1$-closure of $C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$, and let $W^{1/2,2}(\partial\Omega;\mathbb K)$ have the finite-chart Slobodeckij norm. Define $\mathcal D(\Omega):=H^1(\Omega;\mathbb K)/H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with its quotient norm. The trace induces a bounded linear bijection $\overline T:\mathcal D(\Omega)\to W^{1/2,2}(\partial\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with bounded inverse, so these two norms are equivalent under the induced identification. The induced map after quotienting by constants is also a bounded linear bijection $\mathcal D(\Omega)/\mathbb K\mathbf1\to W^{1/2,2}(\partial\Omega;\mathbb K)/\mathbb K$, with equivalent quotient norms. A continuous linear functional on $W^{1/2,2}(\partial\Omega;\mathbb K)$ descends to the constant quotient exactly when it annihilates constants, and its descended functional has the quotient dual norm.

facts:
**Given:** The Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice; the bounded $C^1$ domain; the trace operator $T$; and the quotient spaces in the statement.

[F1] The trace is bounded from $H^1(\Omega)$ into $W^{1/2,2}(\partial\Omega)$ and is onto. ([[thm-sharp-trace-theorem-for-w-one-p]])

[F2] The kernel of the trace is exactly $H_0^1(\Omega)$, the closure of compactly supported smooth functions. ([[thm-kernel-of-the-trace-is-w-one-p-zero]], [[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]])

[F3] There is a bounded right inverse $R:W^{1/2,2}(\partial\Omega)\to H^1(\Omega)$ with $TRf=f$. ([[thm-bounded-right-inverse-for-the-sobolev-trace]])

[F4] The trace-page boundary norm is a finite-chart Slobodeckij norm on almost-everywhere boundary classes. ([[def-fractional-sobolev-space-on-a-compact-c-one-boundary]])

[A1] The Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice are assumed at the cited trace and boundary-space interfaces. ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]])

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected smooth domain, and let $\gamma\in\Gamma_{m,M}(\Omega)$ be a real almost-everywhere class with $0<m\le\gamma\le M<\infty$. Set $\mathcal D(\Omega):=H^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)/H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)$ with quotient norm $\|[U]\|_{\mathcal D}:=\inf_{w\in H_0^1(\Omega)}\|U+w\|_{H^1(\Omega)}$, and let $\mathcal D(\Omega)^*$ be its continuous conjugate-linear dual. For $f=[U]\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$, let $u_{\gamma,f}$ be the unique element of the coset $f$ satisfying
$$\int_\Omega\gamma\,\nabla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\overline{\nabla z}\,dx=0\qquad(z\in H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)).$$
Define the weak Dirichlet-to-Neumann map $\Lambda_\gamma:\mathcal D(\Omega)\to\mathcal D(\Omega)^*$ by
$$\bigl(\Lambda_\gamma f\bigr)(g):=\int_\Omega\gamma\,\nabla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\overline{\nabla V_g}\,dx,$$
where $V_g$ is any representative of $g\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$. The trace quotient identification makes $\mathcal D(\Omega)$ the $H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega)$ boundary data space with its trace quotient norm. Constants lie in the kernel of $\Lambda_\gamma$, and its range functionals annihilate constants; hence $\Lambda_\gamma$ induces $\dot\Lambda_\gamma:\mathcal D(\Omega)/\mathbb C\mathbf1\to(\mathcal D(\Omega)/\mathbb C\mathbf1)^*$, the quotient Dirichlet-to-Neumann map used for Calderón stability. Well-posedness, independence from the representative $V_g$, boundedness and the induced quotient map are established by the well-posedness result cited below.
