contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For an oriented smooth knot
$K:S^1\hookrightarrow S^3$, its normal bundle is
$\nu K=TS^3|_K/TK$, oriented so that a positive tangent to $K$ followed by a
positive basis of a normal fibre gives the ambient orientation. A **framing**
of $K$ is a homotopy class through smooth nowhere-zero sections of $\nu K$.
The normal bundle is made a smooth vector bundle under this axiom; a framed
knot includes the section class as data, not a choice made afterwards. For the
relative integer use the round metric transferred from the unit sphere in
$\mathbb R^4$ by the explicit diffeomorphism
$$x\longmapsto\left(\frac{2x}{1+\lVert x\rVert^2},\frac{\lVert x\rVert^2-1}{1+\lVert x\rVert^2}\right),\qquad\infty\longmapsto(0,0,0,1).$$
It induces a smooth bundle metric on $\nu K$. The resulting winding number is
independent of the metric: any two smooth fibre metrics interpolate through
positive metrics and the corresponding angle maps are homotopic.

Given a reference framing $[s_0]$ and another framing $[s_1]$, use a bundle
metric and the positive quarter-turn $J$ on each oriented normal plane to write
the normalized representative of $s_1$ as
$$s_1(x)=\cos\theta(x)s_0(x)+\sin\theta(x)Js_0(x).$$
The resulting map $S^1\to S^1$ has a continuous angle lift along a parameter
interval $[0,1]$: subdivide into finitely many intervals whose images lie in
open semicircles and choose consecutive local arguments agreeing at endpoints.
Since the map is closed, the lift changes by $2\pi m$ for some $m\in\mathbb Z$;
different lifts differ by a constant multiple of $2\pi$, and homotopies keep
$m$ fixed. This integer $m$ is the **relative framing integer** of $[s_1]$
with respect to $[s_0]$. Thus, once a reference framing is supplied, the
framing classes are an integer torsor; no absolute integer is assigned before
choosing a reference.

The **self-linking number** of a framed knot $(K,[s])$ is the linking number
of $K$ with a sufficiently small push-off along $s$, oriented parallel to $K$.
The push-off and its integer are independent of the representative section,
small radius, and normalized tubular chart by the preceding well-definedness
result.

If a compact oriented surface $\Sigma$ is supplied with boundary $K$, its
**Seifert framing relative to $\Sigma$** is the homotopy class of the inward
unit conormal to $K$ in $\Sigma$, viewed as a nonzero normal section to $K$ in
$S^3$. This definition is relative to the supplied surface; it neither asserts
that every knot bounds such a surface nor asserts the self-linking-zero result.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $F\subset S^3$ be a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface whose oriented boundary is $K$. The normal framing along $K$ given by the inward unit conormal to $K$ in $F$ has self-linking number zero. Here self-linking is the linking number of $K$ with a sufficiently small disjoint push-off along that framing. In the framing-class parameterization by relative winding from the surface framing, this class has integer zero.

facts:
**Given:** The Axiom of Choice, a smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$, and a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface $F$ whose oriented boundary is $K$.

[A1] The Axiom of Choice implies the Axiom of Countable Choice through dependent choice. ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]])

[F1] A Seifert surface is a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface whose oriented boundary is the specified knot; its genus formula assumes $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. ([[def-oriented-seifert-surface]])

[F2] For a knot with a supplied oriented spanning surface, the inward unit surface conormal is a reference normal framing, and relative winding identifies its framing class with zero. ([[thm-oriented-knot-framing-classes-form-z-torsor]])

[F3] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the inward unit conormal defines the Seifert framing; its self-linking is the linking number with a sufficiently small push-off along that section. ([[def-framed-knot-self-linking-and-seifert-framing]])

[F4] The linking number of a framed knot is unchanged when its normal section is replaced by a homotopic nowhere-zero section and the push-off radius is sufficiently small. ([[lem-framed-knot-push-off-self-linking-well-defined]])

[F5] For disjoint oriented circles $J,K$ and an oriented spanning surface $\Sigma$ with $\partial\Sigma=K$, if $J$ is transverse to $\Sigma$ and $D$ is a regular oriented diagram of $J\cup K$, the diagram linking number equals the signed intersection number $J\cdot\Sigma$. The theorem assumes the Axiom of Choice. ([[thm-linking-number-equals-signed-intersection]])

[F6] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, every oriented link in $\mathbb R^3$ has a dense set of directions giving a regular diagram with finitely many crossings. ([[lem-every-oriented-link-admits-a-regular-projection]])

[F7] A regular oriented diagram is a projection with only finitely many transverse double points and no triple points. ([[def-regular-oriented-link-diagram]])

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K:S^1\hookrightarrow S^3$ be an
oriented smooth embedded circle and let $s$ be a smooth nowhere-zero section of
its normal bundle. For any tubular neighbourhood chart that is the inclusion
on the zero section and identifies each vertical normal fibre with the ambient
normal quotient by the identity, the curve $K_{\varepsilon s}$ obtained by
mapping the graph of $\varepsilon s$ into $S^3$ is an embedded oriented circle
disjoint from $K$ for every sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$. The integer
linking number of $K$ with $K_{\varepsilon s}$ is independent of the sufficiently
small radius, of the representative section in its homotopy class, and of the
normalized tubular chart. It therefore defines a self-linking integer of the
framing class $[s]$.

facts:
**Given:** The Axiom of Countable Choice, an oriented smooth embedded circle
$K\subset S^3$, and a smooth nowhere-zero normal section $s$.

[A1] The Axiom of Countable Choice, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]).

[F1] The normal bundle is the quotient $TS^3|_K/TK$; under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ it is a smooth vector bundle, and a tubular neighbourhood is a diffeomorphism from an open neighbourhood of its zero section onto an ambient neighbourhood of $K$ ([[def-normal-and-conormal-bundles-of-an-embedded-submanifold]], [[prop-normal-and-conormal-bundles-are-smooth-vector-bundles]], [[def-tubular-neighbourhood-of-an-embedded-submanifold]], [[thm-tubular-neighbourhood-theorem-in-a-smooth-ambient-manifold]]).

[F2] Normalized tubular neighbourhood charts of the same closed embedded submanifold induce isotopic push-off embeddings after shrinking, with an ambient isotopy fixing the zero section near compact $K$ ([[cor-tubular-neighbourhoods-are-unique-up-to-ambient-isotopy]]).

[F3] The integer half-sum of mixed crossing signs is invariant under ambient isotopy of two-component oriented links ([[lem-linking-number-even-sum-and-reidemeister-invariance]], [[thm-oriented-linking-number-scan-terminates-and-is-correct]]).

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text: Let $X,Y,Z$ be real or complex Hilbert spaces over one scalar field, let $F:X\to Y$ and $G:Y\to Z$ be compact linear maps, and set $A:=G\circ F:X\to Z$. For spectral regularization families $R^G_\alpha:Z\to Y$ for $G^\dagger$ and $R^F_\gamma:Y\to X$ for $F^\dagger$, and a parameter rule $(\alpha,\gamma):(0,\infty)\times Z\to(0,\infty)^2$, define $T_\delta(z^\delta):=R^F_{\gamma(\delta,z^\delta)}(R^G_{\alpha(\delta,z^\delta)}z^\delta)$ for $z^\delta\in Z$. The order is fixed by the factorization: first regularize $G$, then $F$; no general identity $A^\dagger=F^\dagger G^\dagger$ is part of this definition.

facts:
**Given:** Countable Choice; compact real or complex Hilbert maps $F:X\to Y$ and $G:Y\to Z$ with the common positive singular system in the Statement; $A=G\circ F$; $x^\dagger=|A|^\nu w$, $\|w\|\le\rho$, $z=Ax^\dagger\ne0$; the compatible minimum-norm factorization; spectral filters with the stated residual, norm, and qualification bounds; the two geometric first-crossing rules; and noisy data $\|z^\delta-z\|\le\delta$ for a sequence $\delta\downarrow0$.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: Every sequence of nonempty sets admits a choice function selecting one member from each set.

[F1] [[def-ip-composite-double-regularization]]: The forward map is $A=G\circ F$ and the reconstruction applies $R^G_\alpha$ first, then $R^F_\gamma$.

[F2] [[def-ip-compact-linear-inverse-model]]: A compact Hilbert inverse model has a compact linear forward map and exact data $z=Ax^\dagger$ for a truth $x^\dagger$.

[F3] [[def-ip-power-source-set]]: $X_{\nu,\rho}(A)=\{|A|^\nu w:\|w\|\le\rho\}$, where $|A|=(A^*A)^{1/2}$; source elements lie in $(\ker A)^\perp$ and are minimum-norm representatives.

[F4] [[def-ip-unbounded-hilbert-moore-penrose-inverse]]: The inverse domain is $R(A)\oplus R(A)^\perp$, and on exact range data it returns the unique minimum-norm solution.

[F5] [[thm-singular-value-decomposition-for-compact-operators]]: A compact Hilbert operator has a positive singular system with orthonormal right and left singular families and the corresponding operator expansion.

[F6] [[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]]: The adjoint is characterized by $\langle Tx,y\rangle=\langle x,T^*y\rangle$.

[F7] [[def-compact-spectral-filter-and-qualification]]: For a filter family, the residual multiplier is $1-tf(t)$ and qualification bounds positive spectral powers times the absolute residual.

[F8] [[lem-ip-spectral-interpolation-for-power-source-balls]]: If $e=|H|^\nu v$, then $\|e\|\le\|He\|^{\nu/(\nu+1)}\|v\|^{1/(\nu+1)}$.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For an oriented smooth knot $K\subset S^3$, define

$$\mathcal G(K):=\{n\in\mathbb N_0: \text{there is a Seifert surface }F\text{ for }K\text{ with }g(F)=n\}.$$

Every element of $\mathcal G(K)$ is the genus of a connected compact oriented surface. The existence theorem makes $\mathcal G(K)$ nonempty, and the well-ordering of $\mathbb N_0$ gives its least element. The **smooth knot genus** is $g(K):=\min\mathcal G(K)$. This genus is the minimum over embedded spanning surfaces; it is not the number of Seifert circles or the genus of every surface produced from a diagram.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in $S^3$, and let $r:S^3\to S^3$ be an orientation-reversing reflection. Give $r(K)$ the image orientation, and let $-K$ denote reversal of the knot orientation. Then $g(K)=g(r(K))=g(-K)=g(-r(K))$.

facts:
**Given:** AC$_\omega$, a smooth oriented knot $K$, and a smooth reflection $r$ of $S^3$.

[F1] Knot genus is the minimum genus among connected compact smooth oriented surfaces whose oriented boundary is the knot. ([[def-oriented-seifert-surface-and-knot-genus]])

[F2] For a connected compact orientable surface with one boundary component, reversing its orientation or applying a diffeomorphism preserves its genus. ([[lem-finite-chart-surface-normal-forms-supply-jordan-disks-and-torsion-free-groups]])

[A1] AC$_\omega$ is the sequence-choice principle. ([[def-countable-choice]])

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For any smooth oriented knots $K,J\subset S^3$, the Seifert genus of their oriented connected sum satisfies $g(K\#J)=g(K)+g(J)$.

facts:
**Given:** AC$_\omega$ and smooth oriented knots $K,J$.

[F1] The minimum genus surfaces for $K$ and $J$ exist by the definition of genus and the nonempty spanning-surface theorem. ([[def-oriented-seifert-surface-and-knot-genus]])

[F2] Under AC$_\omega$, a connected compact oriented surface with $b$ boundary circles satisfies $\chi=2-2g-b$. ([[lem-finite-chart-surface-normal-forms-supply-jordan-disks-and-torsion-free-groups]])

[F3] A compact spanning surface can be isotoped rel its boundary to be transverse to the standard connected-sum sphere when its boundary is already transverse to that sphere. ([[lem-relative-transversality-for-embedded-surfaces]])

[F4] Every smooth embedded circle in the standard sphere is nullhomotopic and bounds an embedded disk there under AC$_\omega$. ([[thm-higher-dimensional-spheres-are-simply-connected]], [[lem-finite-chart-surface-normal-forms-supply-jordan-disks-and-torsion-free-groups]])

[F5] The connected-sum model supplies a standard separating sphere meeting the sum knot in two points and separating the two summand pieces. ([[def-knot-connected-sum-and-prime-knot]])

[L1] Cutting at a decomposing sphere and capping on its boundary recovers the oriented connected-sum factors. ([[lem-knot-decomposing-sphere-realizes-connected-sum]])

[A1] AC$_\omega$ is the sequence-choice principle used by the genus and transversality suppliers. ([[def-countable-choice]])

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the full Axiom of Choice. For the standard right-handed trefoil in $S^3$, the minimum genus among its connected compact smooth oriented spanning surfaces is exactly $1$.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC and the standard right-handed trefoil $T$.

[F1] Oriented smoothing replaces a crossing by its orientation-compatible noncrossing pairing; the Seifert algorithm records one disk per resulting circle and one band per crossing. Under AC$_\omega$, the bands realize a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface with the original knot as boundary, and its genus is $(1-s+c)/2$ for $s$ circles and $c$ crossings. ([[def-seifert-smoothing-and-seifert-circles-of-an-oriented-link-diagram]], [[alg-seifert-surface-from-diagram]], [[lem-seifert-bands-embedded-orientable-boundary-correct]], [[thm-seifert-algorithm-boundary-euler-and-genus]])

[F2] Under full AC, $T$ does not bound a smooth properly embedded disk in $B^4$. ([[lem-the-trefoil-does-not-bound-a-smooth-proper-disk-in-the-four-ball]])

[F3] A genus-zero connected compact orientable surface with one boundary component is topologically a disk. For smooth input the disk-and-band normal-form construction gives a smooth disk parametrization: steps 7.1–12.1 use smooth circle extensions and smooth disk/band collar moves. ([[lem-finite-chart-surface-normal-forms-supply-jordan-disks-and-torsion-free-groups]], [[lem-finite-c2-surface-carriers-have-smooth-normal-forms-and-relative-cap-approximations]])

[F4] A smooth disk in the boundary $S^3$ can be pushed through a collar into $B^4$, fixing its boundary, to give a smooth proper disk. ([[thm-collar-neighborhood-theorem]])

[F5] Knot genus is the minimum nonnegative integer among the genera of spanning surfaces. ([[def-oriented-seifert-surface-and-knot-genus]])

[A1] Full AC is the choice-function axiom. ([[def-axiom-of-choice]])

[A2] Full AC implies AC$_\omega$. ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]])

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. If a connected compact oriented disk-and-band surface $F$ is built from $s$ disjoint disks by attaching $c$ rectangular bands along boundary intervals and has one boundary component, then $\chi(F)=s-c$ and $g(F)=(1-s+c)/2$. In particular, if the Seifert algorithm on an oriented knot diagram $D$ has $s$ Seifert circles and $c$ crossings, its output surface has genus $(1-s+c)/2$ and the knot genus satisfies $g(K)\le (1-s+c)/2$. This is an upper bound from one spanning surface, not a minimality assertion.

facts:
**Given:** $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, a connected disk-and-band surface made from $s$ disks and $c$ bands with one boundary component; for the final clause, $F$ is the output for an oriented knot diagram $D$ representing $K$.

[F1] The finite-cell Euler characteristic is the alternating sum of the numbers of cells. ([[def-euler-characteristic-of-a-finite-cw-complex]])

[F2] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, a connected compact oriented surface with $b>0$ boundary circles has $\chi=2-2g-b$. ([[lem-finite-chart-surface-normal-forms-supply-jordan-disks-and-torsion-free-groups]])

[F3] A connected compact oriented embedded surface with boundary $K$ is admissible in the set defining $g(K)$. ([[def-oriented-seifert-surface-and-knot-genus]])

[F4] For a one-component regular diagram with $s$ smoothed circles and $c$ crossings, the algorithm uses $s$ disk records and one band record per crossing. ([[alg-seifert-surface-from-diagram]])

[F5] For such a knot diagram, the realized disk-and-band surface is connected, oriented, embedded, and has boundary the represented knot. ([[lem-seifert-bands-embedded-orientable-boundary-correct]])

[A1] The Axiom of Countable Choice is the sequence principle stated in the item. ([[def-countable-choice]])

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Every nontrivial smooth oriented knot in $S^3$ is ambient isotopic to a finite connected sum of prime knots, and the prime factors are unique up to permutation and orientation-preserving ambient isotopy of the oriented factors.

facts:
**Given:** AC$_\omega$ and a nontrivial smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$.

[F1] Nontrivial knots have positive integer genus, genus is additive under connected sum, and the unknot has genus zero. ([[def-oriented-seifert-surface-and-knot-genus]], [[thm-knot-genus-additive-under-connected-sum]], [[lem-knot-genus-zero-iff-unknot]])

[F2] A twice-transverse sphere realizes the oriented connected-sum factors; two prime sphere systems determine the same unordered list by the marked cut-and-paste lemma. ([[lem-knot-decomposing-sphere-realizes-connected-sum]], [[lem-knot-decomposing-sphere-systems-cut-and-paste]])

[F3] Connected sum is associative and commutative with unknot identity, and a prime knot is a nontrivial knot that cannot split into two nontrivial factors. ([[def-knot-connected-sum-and-prime-knot]], [[thm-oriented-knot-connected-sum-is-a-commutative-monoid]])

[A1] The stated countable choice hypothesis supplies exactly the hypothesis of these surface, isotopy, and sphere suppliers. ([[def-countable-choice]])

contract.heading: Statement refuted
contract.text: Assume the full Axiom of Choice. For an oriented Seifert surface $F\subset S^3$ with boundary $K$ and ordered basis $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$, let $V$ be the Seifert matrix with entries $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. Here $\operatorname{lk}$ is the integer linking number of disjoint oriented cycles in $S^3$, and $a_i^+$ is a small push-off in the positive normal direction, chosen so that the positive normal followed by the oriented basis of $F$ gives the orientation of $S^3$. Use the standard knot-invariant conventions $\Delta_K(t)=\det(V-tV^T)$ up to units $\pm t^k$ and $\sigma_{-1}(K)=\operatorname{sign}(2(V+V^T))$, where the matrix sign is the number of positive eigenvalues minus the number of negative eigenvalues; independence of the chosen surface and basis is part of the Seifert-form invariance theorems. Let $T$ be the standard right-handed trefoil, let $T^*$ be its image under a fixed orientation-reversing reflection of $S^3$, and let $-T^*$ be that image with reversed knot orientation. Define $G=T\#T$ and $Q=T\#(-T^*)$. Then $\Delta_G(t)\doteq\Delta_Q(t)\doteq(t^2-t+1)^2$, and $|\sigma_{-1}(G)|=4$ while $\sigma_{-1}(Q)=0$. The oriented prime-factor multisets of $G$ and $Q$ are different. Thus equality of Alexander polynomials does not determine the prime knot summands.

facts:
**Given:** The full AC, knots $T,T^*,-T^*,G,Q$, positive-push and invariant conventions of the original Statement.

[A1] Full AC implies countable choice, as required by the prime and smooth knot suppliers. [[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]

[F1] The actual right-handed trefoil bounds the standard positive two-Hopf-band plumbing, whose positive-push matrix in its ordered core basis is $V=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}-1&0\\-1&-1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. The handedness and negative diagonal signs are the established geometric convention, not the differently labeled positive matrix in the source-specific KT06 example. [[lem-positive-hopf-plumbing-has-trefoil-seifert-matrix]], [[lem-canonical-positive-three-crossing-braid-has-negative-trefoil-form]]

[F2] For every knot Seifert surface with the same positive normal and positive-meridian convention, $\Delta_K(t)\doteq\det(V-tV^T)$. The actual boundary connected-sum surface has block matrix $V_K\oplus V_J$: the old bases lie in separated balls and both cross-linking blocks vanish. [[thm-seifert-determinant-is-the-knot-alexander-polynomial]], [[cor-alexander-polynomial-multiplies-under-connected-sum]], Proof2.1–4.1.

[F3] At every nonroot point $\omega$, the signature of $(1-\omega)V+(1-\bar\omega)V^T$ is an oriented knot invariant independent of surface and basis. The full knot-surface S-equivalence and stabilization proofs now establish this actual interface. [[def-levine-tristram-hermitian-form-and-signature]], [[lem-seifert-matrices-of-a-knot-are-s-equivalent]], [[lem-seifert-stabilization-preserves-levine-tristram-signature]]

[F4] The right trefoil is prime, reflection preserves nontriviality and primality, and the oriented prime decomposition is unique up to ordering and insertion/deletion of unknot factors. [[lem-right-trefoil-is-prime]], [[lem-mirroring-preserves-primality-of-a-knot]], [[thm-schubert-prime-decomposition-for-knots]], [[def-knot-connected-sum-and-prime-knot]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the oriented standard three-sphere, let $F$ be a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface with boundary orientation equal to that of $K$, let $g$ satisfy $\chi(F)=1-2g$, and choose an ordered integral basis $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$. Use the positive normal convention $(n,u,v)>0$ and define $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. Let $A_K=H_1(\widetilde X_K;\mathbb Z)$ be the one-variable Alexander module of the knot complement $X_K=S^3\setminus K$, where the cover is classified by the total-linking homomorphism and $t$ acts by the deck transformation corresponding to the positive meridian. Then there is an isomorphism of $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$-modules
$$
A_K\cong\operatorname{coker}\bigl(V-tV^T:\Lambda^{2g}\to\Lambda^{2g}\bigr).
$$

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, a smooth oriented knot $K$, a connected compact smooth oriented spanning surface $F$, an integral homology basis, and the positive-push convention.

[A1] Full AC implies the countable-choice hypothesis used by the tubular-neighborhood and surface normal-form suppliers, and is the stated hypothesis of Alexander duality and the one-variable module convention. [[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]

[F1] The knot normal bundle admits an orientation-preserving framing, and a tubular map gives a compact exterior $E$ whose inclusion into $X_K=S^3\setminus K$ is a homotopy equivalence. [[lem-knot-normal-circle-bundle-trivialization]], [[lem-knot-tubular-exterior-and-boundary]], [[thm-tubular-neighbourhood-theorem-in-a-smooth-ambient-manifold]], [[def-tubular-neighbourhood-of-an-embedded-submanifold]]

[F2] The positive meridian generates $H_1(E;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z$, and the boundary longitude is the unique degree-one class in the kernel of its map into the exterior. [[thm-knot-exterior-homology-and-longitude]]

[F3] For a tube compatible with the surface collar, the cut-open cover has Alexander-module presentation $V-tV^T$ under the stated positive seam and linking-dual convention. [[lem-knot-infinite-cyclic-cover-cut-and-paste-presentation]]

[F4] The one-variable module is $H_1$ of the connected cover classified by the kernel of total linking, with $t$ acting by the deck transformation for $+1$; the positive meridian maps to $+1$. [[def-one-variable-alexander-module-of-an-oriented-link]]

[F5] Connected covers are classified by subgroups of $\pi_1$, normal kernels give regular covers with quotient deck group, and degree-one Hurewicz identifies total linking on $H_1$ with the corresponding homomorphism on $\pi_1$. [[thm-classification-of-connected-covering-spaces]], [[thm-regular-covering-characterizations]], [[cor-deck-group-of-a-regular-covering]], [[def-deck-transformation-and-deck-group]], [[prop-the-first-hurewicz-map-in-degree-one-is-abelianization]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(K,F)$ and $(K',F')$ be oriented knot and spanning-surface pairs in the oriented standard three-sphere, and let $h_t:S^3\to S^3$ be a smooth ambient isotopy with $h_0$ the identity, $h_1(K)=K'$, and $h_1(F)=F'$, preserving the given orientations. If $V$ and $V'$ are their Seifert matrices in any integral bases, then the basis transported by $h_1$ has matrix $V$, and any other target basis with transition matrix $P$ has matrix $V'=P^TVP$. Hence $V$ and $V'$ are S-equivalent, meaning they are related by a finite sequence of integral unimodular congruences and the two elementary rank-two enlargement moves or their reverses.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, two oriented knot-surface pairs and an orientation-preserving smooth ambient isotopy carrying the first pair to the second.

[A1] Full AC supplies the Alexander-duality linking convention used by the Seifert pairing. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] The Seifert pairing is bilinear on homology classes and is computed by linking positive normal push-offs. [[def-knot-seifert-pairing-and-matrix]], [[lem-seifert-pairing-well-defined]]

[F2] An orientation-preserving ambient isotopy induces homology isomorphisms on complements and carries positive meridians to positive meridians; naturality of Alexander duality preserves the total-linking coefficient. [[def-oriented-link-in-s-three-and-ambient-isotopy]], [[prop-singular-chains-and-homology-are-covariantly-functorial]], [[def-one-variable-alexander-module-of-an-oriented-link]]

[F3] The positive normal is fixed by the ambient and surface orientations, so an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism carrying the oriented surface carries positive normal levels to positive normal levels. [[def-knot-seifert-pairing-and-matrix]]

[F4] S-equivalence is generated by integral unimodular congruences, the two elementary rank-two enlargements, and their reverses. [[def-seifert-matrix-s-equivalence]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $K,J\subset S^3$ be smooth oriented knots, and let $K\#J$ be their oriented connected sum for a connected-sum datum using the fixed gluing convention. Then

$$\Delta_{K\#J}(t)\doteq \Delta_K(t)\Delta_J(t),$$

where each $\Delta$ is the generator of the zeroth elementary ideal of the one-variable Alexander module and $\doteq$ means equality up to multiplication by a unit $\pm t^k$ of $\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$. The statement is independent of the local connected-sum choices and of the Seifert surfaces and bases used to compute the polynomials.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, two smooth oriented knots $K,J\subset S^3$, and a connected-sum datum as in the Definition.

[A1] Full AC is the choice-function axiom used by the Alexander-module and knot-surface conventions. ([[def-axiom-of-choice]])

[F1] The connected sum is formed by cutting each knot in a trivial-arc ball and gluing along the fixed orientation-matching boundary map. ([[def-knot-connected-sum-and-prime-knot]])

[F2] Changing the local balls, subarcs, local frames, or oriented knot representatives does not change the oriented ambient-isotopy class of the connected sum. ([[lem-knot-connected-sum-well-defined]])

[F3] Full AC implies DC and hence the Axiom of Countable Choice. ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]])

[F4] A Seifert surface is a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface with the given knot as its oriented boundary; under AC$_\omega$, every smooth oriented knot bounds one. ([[def-oriented-seifert-surface]], [[thm-every-oriented-knot-bounds-a-seifert-surface]])

[F5] A connected compact knot surface has free fundamental group of rank $2g(F)$, and the first Hurewicz map identifies its first homology with the abelianization. Thus an ordered integral homology basis exists for each summand surface. ([[lem-finite-chart-surface-normal-forms-supply-jordan-disks-and-torsion-free-groups]], [[prop-the-first-hurewicz-map-in-degree-one-is-abelianization]])

[F6] The Seifert matrix uses $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$ with the positive normal. ([[def-knot-seifert-pairing-and-matrix]])

[F7] The one-variable Alexander module is the positive-meridian module, $\Delta_K$ is its zeroth-elementary-ideal generator, and for each connected knot Seifert surface and basis the module is presented by $V-tV^T$, whose determinant generates that ideal up to a unit. ([[def-one-variable-alexander-module-of-an-oriented-link]], [[def-alexander-polynomial-from-the-first-elementary-ideal]], [[thm-seifert-matrix-presents-knot-alexander-module]], [[lem-square-seifert-presentation-and-alexander-normalization]], [[thm-seifert-determinant-is-the-knot-alexander-polynomial]])

[F8] Ambient isotopies preserve the Alexander polynomial up to a unit, and transported/basis-changed Seifert matrices have the stated congruence relation. ([[thm-the-alexander-polynomial-is-an-oriented-link-invariant]], [[lem-seifert-matrix-s-equivalence-under-isotopy]])

[F9] A standard closed 3-ball is contractible, so its first singular homology is that of a point and vanishes. The singular chain complex of a point has $\partial_1=0$ and $\partial_2=1$, hence $H_1(\ast;\mathbb Z)=0$. ([[cor-contractible-nonempty-spaces-have-the-homology-of-a-point]])

[F10] Under AC$_\omega$, every smooth manifold with boundary, including each summand Seifert surface, has a smooth collar of its boundary. ([[thm-collar-neighborhood-theorem]], [[def-smooth-collar-of-a-manifold-boundary]])

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Assume full AC. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot and $F$ a connected compact smooth oriented spanning surface of genus $g$. The Seifert matrix $V$ defines a function on $H_1(F;\mathbb F_2)$ by
$$q_F([x])=\operatorname{lk}(x^+,x)\pmod2=x^TVx\pmod2,$$
where an integral lift of the mod-two homology class is used in the last expression. Its polarization is the mod-two intersection form. A symplectic basis is an ordered basis $(a_1,b_1,\ldots,a_g,b_g)$ with $a_i\cdot b_j=\delta_{ij}$ and all other pairings zero. Define
$$\operatorname{Arf}(q_F)=\sum_{i=1}^g q_F(a_i)q_F(b_i)\pmod2.$$
The quadratic-enhancement lemma proves that this value is independent of symplectic basis; the S-equivalence and Conway bridge proves independence of $F$, so the resulting knot invariant is denoted $\operatorname{Arf}(K)$. For $g=0$ the empty sum is $0$.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, a smooth oriented knot, a connected compact oriented spanning surface, and its Seifert matrix.

[A1] Full AC is the ambient choice hypothesis of the Seifert pairing. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Assume full AC. For an even-order integral matrix $V$ that is the Seifert matrix of a knot, **S-equivalence** means the equivalence relation generated by integral unimodular congruences $V\mapsto P^TVP$ with $\det P=\pm1$, where $x,y\in\mathbb Z^n$ and $z\in\mathbb Z$, and the two enlargements
$$E_0(V;x,y,z)=\begin{pmatrix}V&x&0\\y^T&z&0\\0^T&1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad E_1(V;x,y,z)=\begin{pmatrix}V&x&0\\y^T&z&1\\0^T&0&0\end{pmatrix},$$
and their reverses. For an assignment $P$ of an integer polynomial in $z$ to each ambient-isotopy class of oriented links, call $P$ **Conway-normalized** when $P_U(z)=1$ for the unknot $U$ and
$$P_{L_+}(z)-P_{L_-}(z)=z\,P_{L_0}(z)$$
whenever the three oriented links agree outside one crossing ball and inside it are respectively the positive crossing, negative crossing, and orientation-compatible smoothing; positive means $\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})>0$, where $v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under}$ are the projected oriented tangent vectors and $P$ is oriented so the viewing normal followed by a positive basis of $P$ is ambient-positive. The smoothing reconnects the four oriented half-arcs in the unique noncrossing way compatible with their directions. No existence of such an assignment is presupposed: the Seifert-determinant lemma constructs a unique assignment and denotes it by $\nabla_L(z)$. For a knot, let $\Delta_K^\#(t)$ be the unique associate of its Alexander polynomial satisfying $\Delta_K^\#(1)=1$ and $\Delta_K^\#(t^{-1})=\Delta_K^\#(t)$; existence and uniqueness follow from the Alexander-normalization corollary. Set $z=t^{1/2}-t^{-1/2}$, with $t^{1/2}$ a formal Laurent variable, and use $\Delta_K^\#(t)=\nabla_K(z)$ as the normalization convention.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere $S^3$. A **Seifert surface** for $K$ is a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface $F\subset S^3$ with boundary set equal to $K$. Orient each boundary component so that an outward-pointing conormal in $F$, followed by a positive boundary tangent, is a positive basis of $TF$; the oriented boundary of $F$ must agree with the given orientation of $K$. For such a surface, its genus $g(F)$ is the unique nonnegative integer satisfying $\chi(F)=2-2g(F)-b$, where $b$ is the number of boundary components; here $b=1$, so $\chi(F)=1-2g(F)$. The compact-surface normal-form result supplies this integer under the stated choice axiom.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Every smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$ bounds a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface $F\subset S^3$ whose oriented boundary is $K$.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the oriented standard three-sphere and let $F$ be a connected compact smooth oriented surface with boundary $K$. Choose a sufficiently small oriented product tubular neighborhood $N(K)$ compatible with the inward conormal of $F$, set $E=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$ and $T=\partial E$, and put $S=F\cap E$. Thus $S$ is a connected properly embedded surface in $E$ and its boundary on $T$ projects to $K$ with degree $+1$. Choose a product bicollar of $S$ in $E$ and let $Y$ be the compact cut-open complement, with boundary copies $S_+$ and $S_-$. Form a space $\widetilde E_F$ from copies $Y_n$ ($n\in\mathbb Z$) by gluing $S_-(Y_n)$ to $S_+(Y_{n+1})$ for every $n$, with the remaining boundary faces glued by the inherited product collar. Let $t$ be the deck shift $Y_n\to Y_{n+1}$ and let $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$. Then $Y$ is connected, $\partial S$ is the preferred longitude, linking defines an isomorphism $H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(H_1(F;\mathbb Z),\mathbb Z)$, and there is an exact sequence of $\Lambda$-modules
$$
H_1(F;\mathbb Z)\otimes\Lambda\xrightarrow{i_- -t i_+}H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)\otimes\Lambda\longrightarrow H_1(\widetilde E_F;\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow0,
$$
where $i_\pm:H_1(F;\mathbb Z)\to H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)$ are the inclusions of the two collar copies. Thus $H_1(\widetilde E_F;\mathbb Z)$ is the cokernel of the displayed map.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, an oriented knot $K$, a connected compact oriented spanning surface $F$, an adapted tubular neighborhood, a proper cut surface $S$, and a product bicollar used to form $Y$.

[A1] Full AC supplies Alexander duality, the universal-coefficient theorem, and the countable-choice hypotheses inherited by the surface and tubular-neighborhood suppliers. [[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]

[F2] The exterior has $H_1(E;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z$ generated by the positive meridian, and its kernel on the boundary torus has a unique degree-one class, the preferred longitude. [[thm-knot-exterior-homology-and-longitude]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume countable choice. For every smooth oriented knot $K$ in $S^3$, there are an oriented normal-bundle trivialization, a tubular map $\Phi$ defined on an open neighbourhood containing $S^1\times D^2_{2\epsilon}$ for some $\epsilon>0$, and a closed tubular neighbourhood $N(K)=\Phi(S^1\times D^2_\epsilon)$. This $N(K)$ is diffeomorphic to $S^1\times D^2$, its boundary $T_K$ is diffeomorphic to $S^1\times S^1$, and its exterior $E_K=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$ is a compact smooth oriented three-manifold with boundary $T_K$. The open complement $S^3\setminus K$ strongly deformation retracts onto $E_K$.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K:S^1	o S^3$ be a smooth oriented embedding and write its quotient normal bundle as $
u_K=K^*TS^3/dK(TS^1)$. Choose an orientation-preserving trivialization $
u_K\cong S^1	imes\mathbb R^2$ and a tubular map $\Phi:\Omega	o S^3$, meaning a smooth embedding from an open neighbourhood $\Omega\subseteq
u_K$ of the zero section onto an open neighbourhood of $K(S^1)$ with $\Phi(s,0)=K(s)$, such that in these product coordinates $\Omega$ contains $S^1	imes D^2_{2\epsilon}$ for some $\epsilon>0$. Here $D^2_r=\{z\in\mathbb R^2:\|z\|\le r\}$. Set $N(K)=\Phi(S^1	imes D^2_\epsilon)$, $E_K=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$, $T_K=\partial E_K$, and let $i:T_K\hookrightarrow E_K$ be inclusion, $p:T_K	o S^1$ the product projection, and $\mu$ the positive boundary of a normal disk, using the normal-plane orientation determined by the orientations of $K$ and $S^3$. A class is primitive if it is not $m$ times another class for any integer $|m|>1$. Then $H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z$ is generated by $[\mu]$. The kernel of $i_*:H_1(T_K;\mathbb Z)	o H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)$ is a primitive rank-one direct summand generated by a unique class $[\lambda]$ with $p_*[\lambda]=1\in H_1(S^1;\mathbb Z)$. It has a simple closed representative, is the preferred longitude, and $([\mu],[\lambda])$ is a basis of $H_1(T_K;\mathbb Z)$.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot, let $F\subset S^3$ be a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface with oriented boundary $K$, and let $\chi(F)=1-2g$ with $g\ge0$. Choose an ordered integral basis $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$, use the positive normal convention, and set $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. Let $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$, let $A_K$ be the first homology of the infinite cyclic cover classified by total linking with $t$ acting by the positive-meridian deck transformation, and let $\Delta_K$ be a generator of the zeroth elementary ideal $E_0(A_K)$. Then the square matrix $M(t)=V-tV^T$ generates that ideal:

$$E_0(A_K)=(\det M(t)).$$

For $g=0$, the matrix is empty and its determinant is $1$. In every genus, $\det(V-V^T)=\pm1$, so every generator $\Delta_K$ satisfies $\Delta_K(1)=\pm1$. The ideal and determinant assertions are compatible with integral basis changes and with orientation-preserving ambient isotopies of knot-surface pairs.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, an oriented knot $K\subset S^3$, a connected compact oriented Seifert surface $F$ with $\partial F=K$, and an ordered integral basis of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$.

[A1] Full AC is the assertion that every family of nonempty sets has a choice function. It is the stated hypothesis of the Alexander-module and Seifert-matrix presentation conventions used here. ([[def-axiom-of-choice]])

[F8] Full AC implies DC and hence the Axiom of Countable Choice, which is the stated choice hypothesis of the Seifert-surface and finite surface-normal-form suppliers. ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]])

[F1] A Seifert surface is connected, compact, smooth, oriented and embedded with the given knot as oriented boundary; in the chosen basis the positive-push matrix has entries $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. ([[def-oriented-seifert-surface]], [[def-knot-seifert-pairing-and-matrix]])

[F2] The one-variable Alexander module is defined over $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$; $\Delta_K$ is a greatest common divisor of $E_0(A_K)$ and is determined up to a unit $\pm t^k$. ([[def-one-variable-alexander-module-of-an-oriented-link]], [[def-alexander-polynomial-from-the-first-elementary-ideal]], [[def-elementary-ideals-of-a-finitely-presented-module]], [[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]], [[lem-units-and-powers-of-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]])

[F3] The elementary ideal $E_0$ is independent of the finite presentation and depends only on the module's isomorphism class. ([[lem-elementary-ideals-are-independent-of-the-presentation]])

[F4] The positive-meridian convention gives an isomorphism $A_K\cong\operatorname{coker}(V-tV^T)$ over $\Lambda$. ([[thm-seifert-matrix-presents-knot-alexander-module]])

[F5] The skew part of the matrix is the surface intersection matrix: $V-V^T=J_F$, and $J_F$ is unimodular. ([[lem-seifert-matrix-skew-part-is-surface-intersection]])

[F6] Under an orientation-preserving ambient isotopy, a transported basis has the same Seifert matrix; a target basis change gives $V'=P^TVP$ for $P\in\mathrm{GL}_{2g}(\mathbb Z)$. ([[lem-seifert-matrix-s-equivalence-under-isotopy]])

[F7] An orientation-preserving ambient isotopy induces an isomorphism of Alexander modules and preserves $E_0(A_K)$ and $\Delta_K$ up to a unit. ([[thm-the-alexander-polynomial-is-an-oriented-link-invariant]])

contract.heading: Example
contract.text:
Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $T$ and $E$ be the oriented boundaries of the standard one-boundary square plumbings of two positive Hopf bands and of one positive with one negative Hopf band, respectively; these are the right-handed trefoil and the figure-eight knot. A positive Hopf band is an oriented annulus whose induced boundary components have linking number $+1$; its core, the central simple closed curve, has self-pairing $-1$. a negative Hopf band has boundary linking number $-1$ and core self-pairing $+1$. A square plumbing identifies a square in the boundary collars of the two annuli so that its edges alternate between them, then smooths the corners; use the gluing for which the resulting boundary is one component. Order the two cores $a,b$ with the positive Hopf core first, orient them so $a\cdot_F b=+1$, and use the standard plumbing side for which $a^+$ bounds a disk disjoint from $b$. In the positive-push convention $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$, their Seifert matrices are

$$V_T=\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\-1&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad V_E=\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\-1&1\end{pmatrix}.$$

Their determinant representatives are $\Delta_T(t)=1-t+t^2$ and $\Delta_E(t)=-1+3t-t^2$. They both evaluate to $1$ at $t=1$; at $t=-1$ the displayed representatives evaluate to $3$ and $-5$, so the unit-invariant absolute values are $3$ and $5$. These determinant classes are unchanged up to units by oriented ambient isotopy and integral basis changes. The connected sum satisfies

$$\Delta_{T\#E}(t)\doteq(1-t+t^2)(-1+3t-t^2)=-t^4+4t^3-5t^2+4t-1.$$

This displayed representative has values $1$ at $t=1$ and $-15$ at $t=-1$.

facts:

[A1] Full AC is the choice-function axiom assumed by the Alexander-module and Seifert-matrix definitions. ([[def-axiom-of-choice]])

[F1] The positive-push matrix is $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. ([[def-knot-seifert-pairing-and-matrix]])

[F2] For every ordered integral homology basis, $V-V^T=J_F$, and the surface intersection matrix $J_F$ is unimodular. ([[lem-seifert-matrix-skew-part-is-surface-intersection]])

[F3] A Seifert surface is connected, compact, smooth, oriented and embedded with its given knot as oriented boundary; a connected compact surface with one boundary has free fundamental group of rank $2g(F)$, and its first homology is the free abelianization. For genus one, this gives a free rank-two group. ([[def-oriented-seifert-surface]], [[lem-finite-chart-surface-normal-forms-supply-jordan-disks-and-torsion-free-groups]], [[prop-the-first-hurewicz-map-in-degree-one-is-abelianization]])

[F4] The positive-meridian module is presented by $V-tV^T$, its $E_0$ ideal is generated by the determinant, and that determinant is associated to the polynomial generator. ([[def-one-variable-alexander-module-of-an-oriented-link]], [[def-alexander-polynomial-from-the-first-elementary-ideal]], [[thm-seifert-matrix-presents-knot-alexander-module]], [[lem-square-seifert-presentation-and-alexander-normalization]], [[thm-seifert-determinant-is-the-knot-alexander-polynomial]])

[F7] The connected sum uses the fixed oriented gluing convention and represents a one-component knot. ([[def-knot-connected-sum-and-prime-knot]])

[F8] Full AC implies the Axiom of Countable Choice, the surface-normal-form hypothesis. ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]])

[F9] Ambient isotopy transports a Seifert matrix by unimodular congruence and preserves the Alexander polynomial up to a unit. ([[lem-seifert-matrix-s-equivalence-under-isotopy]], [[thm-the-alexander-polynomial-is-an-oriented-link-invariant]])

contract.heading: Statement refuted
contract.text: Assume the full Axiom of Choice and the existing knot convention $D_K(t)=\Delta_K(t)/(1-t)$. The fraction $D_K(t)$ is a Laurent polynomial in $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$ for every smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC and the standard unknot $U$ in the oriented three-sphere.

[A1] Full AC is the choice-function axiom used by the Alexander-module and Seifert-matrix conventions. ([[def-axiom-of-choice]])

[F1] The standard unknot is the oriented unit circle in a fixed coordinate two-plane of $S^3\subset\mathbb R^4$. ([[def-knot-connected-sum-and-prime-knot]])

[F2] A Seifert surface is a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface with the given knot as oriented boundary; a disk has Euler characteristic $1$ and genus $0$. ([[def-oriented-seifert-surface]])

[F3] A nonempty contractible space has the singular homology of a point. The singular chain complex of a point has $\partial_1=0$ and $\partial_2=1$, so $H_1(\ast;\mathbb Z)=0$. ([[cor-contractible-nonempty-spaces-have-the-homology-of-a-point]])

[F4] The positive-push Seifert matrix is defined on an ordered basis of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$, and the determinant of the empty $0\times0$ matrix is $1$. ([[def-knot-seifert-pairing-and-matrix]])

[F5] The positive-meridian module is presented by $V-tV^T$, the square presentation generates $E_0(A_K)$ by its determinant, and that determinant is associated to $\Delta_K(t)$. ([[def-one-variable-alexander-module-of-an-oriented-link]], [[thm-seifert-matrix-presents-knot-alexander-module]], [[lem-square-seifert-presentation-and-alexander-normalization]], [[thm-seifert-determinant-is-the-knot-alexander-polynomial]])

[F6] For a knot, the separate knot-normalized fraction is $D_K(t)=\Delta_K(t)/(1-t)$. ([[def-alexander-polynomial-from-the-first-elementary-ideal]])

[F7] The assignment $t\mapsto1$ extends to a ring homomorphism $\operatorname{ev}_1:\Lambda\to\mathbb Z$, since $1$ is invertible in the Laurent ring. ([[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]])

[F8] Connected-sum multiplicativity gives $\Delta_{K\#J}\doteq\Delta_K\Delta_J$. ([[cor-alexander-polynomial-multiplies-under-connected-sum]])

[F9] Full AC implies the Axiom of Countable Choice, the stated hypothesis of the Seifert-surface definition. ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]])

[F10] Every generator $\Delta_K$ satisfies $\Delta_K(1)=\pm1$. ([[cor-knot-alexander-normalization-symmetry-and-genus-bound]])

[F11] The Alexander polynomial is unchanged up to a unit under oriented ambient isotopy, and a transported Seifert matrix is related by unimodular congruence. ([[thm-the-alexander-polynomial-is-an-oriented-link-invariant]], [[lem-seifert-matrix-s-equivalence-under-isotopy]])

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For a nonempty oriented link $L$, the diagram quandle presentations from any two regular oriented diagrams of $L$ are isomorphic by the local quandle Tietze transformations for R1, R2 and R3. If $L=K$ has one component and $D$ is its diagram, let
$$W(D)=\langle g_a\ (a\in A(D))\mid g_v=g_o^{-1}g_ug_o\text{ at every crossing with source }u,\text{ target }v,\text{ and overarc }o\rangle.$$
Then the positive-meridian Wirtinger constructor uses these same under-arcs and crossing relations, and
$$\operatorname{Adj}(Q(D))\cong W(D)\cong\pi_1(S^3\setminus K).$$
No completeness or knot-classification assertion is made.

facts:
**Given:** A nonempty oriented link $L$, its diagrams, and, for the group comparison, a one-component link $L=K$; also the diagram quandle, $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, and the common positive-normal crossing convention.

[F1] [[def-rack-fundamental-quandle-and-adjoint-group]]: $Q(D)$ is generated by the under-arcs with crossing relations, and $\operatorname{Adj}(Q)$ has relations $e_{q*r}=e_r^{-1}e_qe_r$.

[F2] [[def-group-presentation]]: $\langle X\mid S\rangle$ is the quotient of the free group on $X$ by the normal closure of the relator words $S$.

[F3] [[thm-oriented-reidemeister-equivalence-theorem]]: assuming $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, equivalent oriented diagrams are related by finitely many planar isotopies and oriented R1, R2, and R3 moves.

[F4] [[def-knot-planar-code]]: the finite code records the oriented knot's under-arcs, over/under data, and edge orientations; an under-arc is maximal between consecutive underpasses, and the code stores no algebraic crossing sign.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is the axiom that every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function.

[F5] The constructor names source and target by the positive over-normal and emits $g_o^{-1}g_ug_og_v^{-1}$; its correctness theorem identifies this presented group with the knot complement group. [[alg-knot-wirtinger-presentation-from-code]], [[thm-knot-wirtinger-presentation-correctness]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the smooth framing statements. Let $R$ be a rack and let $\pi(x)=x*x$ be its kink map. Rack-coloring sets
are in bijection across every oriented R2 or R3 move and planar isotopy.
Across a single oriented R1 curl, the label transported along the affected
strand changes by $\pi$ or $\pi^{-1}$ according to the curl orientation.
Consequently, an opposite-kink pair on the same component whose two signed framing changes cancel
induces a bijection on colorings. A single unframed R1 move has a unique
extension for every boundary color exactly when $\pi$ is the identity, which
is the quandle idempotency axiom. Thus finite rack coloring counts are
invariant under R2, R3, planar isotopy, and framing-preserving opposite-kink
compensation; the unframed R1 move is covered when the rack is a quandle.

facts:
**Given:** A rack $R$, its kink map $\pi$, the positive-normal crossing convention, and $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ when smooth framings are used.

[F1] [[def-rack-fundamental-quandle-and-adjoint-group]]: every right translation is bijective, right self-distributivity holds, and the coloring relation uses the overarc action.

[F2] [[lem-rack-kink-map-is-bijective]]: the map $\pi(x)=x*x$ is bijective with inverse $\pi^{-1}(z)=R_z^{-1}(z)$.

[F3] [[def-oriented-reidemeister-moves]]: oriented R2 and R3 moves have all local orientation and height-order variants.

[F4] The crossing sign is $\operatorname{sgn}\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})$; blackboard self-linking equals self-writhe. Therefore an R1 creation with sign $\epsilon$ changes blackboard self-linking by $\epsilon$. [[def-oriented-crossing-sign-writhe-and-blackboard-framing]], [[thm-blackboard-framing-self-linking-is-writhe]]

[A1] $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is used only for the supplied smooth-framing/self-linking results. [[def-countable-choice]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $D$ be a regular oriented diagram
of a knot $K$ with blackboard framing $b_D$. The self-linking number of the
framed knot $(K,b_D)$ equals the diagram writhe:
$$\operatorname{sl}(K,b_D)=\operatorname{wr}(D).$$
For a link component $K_i$, the corresponding self-linking number is its
self-writhe $\operatorname{wr}_i(D)$. Total writhe of a link still includes
the signs of mixed crossings, while the sum of component self-linking numbers
uses only self-crossings.

facts:
**Given:** The Axiom of Countable Choice and a regular oriented diagram $D$ of
a knot $K$.

[A1] The Axiom of Countable Choice, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]).

[F1] The self-linking number of a framed knot is the linking number with a sufficiently small embedded push-off along its framing section ([[lem-framed-knot-push-off-self-linking-well-defined]], [[def-framed-knot-self-linking-and-seifert-framing]]).

[F2] For a two-component diagram the algorithmic linking number is one half of the signed sum of its mixed crossing signs ([[alg-oriented-linking-number-from-diagram]], [[thm-oriented-linking-number-scan-terminates-and-is-correct]]).

[F3] The blackboard push-off has exactly two mixed crossings of the original sign for each original self-crossing and no other mixed crossings ([[lem-blackboard-push-off-has-two-mixed-crossings-per-crossing]]).

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $L=K_1\cup\cdots\cup K_r\subset S^3$ be a nonempty oriented smooth link with $r\ge1$ components, and let $X_L=S^3\setminus L$ be its open complement. For each component choose a smooth fibrewise norm on its normal plane bundle $\nu(K_i)$ and a tubular map $\Phi_i$ from an open neighborhood of the zero section, fixing the zero section, together with a radius $\epsilon_i>0 whose closed disk subbundle lies in that neighborhood. Require the resulting closed tubes $N(K_i)=\Phi_i(D_{\epsilon_i}\nu(K_i))$ to be pairwise disjoint, and put $N(L)=\bigcup_{i=1}^rN(K_i)$ and $E_L=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}_{S^3}N(L)$, the resulting compact smooth $3$-manifold with boundary. The tube choices are part of the input. Choose a basepoint $b\in E_L\subset X_L$. Orient each normal disk so that the positive tangent to $K_i$ followed by its positive normal basis agrees with the fixed orientation of $S^3$. A **positive meridian** $\mu_i$ of $K_i$ is the oriented boundary of the radius-$\epsilon_i$ normal disk in one fibre of $\nu(K_i)$; it lies on $\partial E_L$, meets $K_i$ once, and misses every other component. Alexander duality identifies $H_1(X_L;\mathbb Z)$ with $\mathbb Z^r$ and identifies the classes of $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_r$ with its standard basis. Write $G=\pi_1(X_L,b)$ and let $\phi:G\to H_1(X_L;\mathbb Z)$ be the first Hurewicz homomorphism, equivalently abelianization. The subgroup $\ker\phi$ is normal. The connected covering $p:X_L^{\mathrm{ab}}\to X_L$ classified by $\ker\phi$ is the **maximal abelian cover**; it is regular and its deck group is identified with $G/\ker\phi\cong H_1(X_L;\mathbb Z)$. Put $\Lambda_r=\mathbb Z[H_1(X_L;\mathbb Z)]\cong\mathbb Z[t_1^{\pm1},\ldots,t_r^{\pm1}]$, where $t_i$ is the deck transformation corresponding to $[\mu_i]$. The isomorphism sends each variable to its group-ring basis element; monomials $t_1^{n_1}\cdots t_r^{n_r}$ correspond bijectively to the basis elements indexed by $n_1[\mu_1]+\cdots+n_r[\mu_r]$. Define the absolute multivariable Alexander module by

$$
A_L=H_1(X_L^{\mathrm{ab}};\mathbb Z),
$$

as a left $\Lambda_r$-module under the deck action. “Absolute” means this is ordinary homology of the covering space, not relative homology with respect to a fibre over the basepoint.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $K$ and $J$ be disjoint oriented smooth embedded circles in the oriented
three-sphere. Choose a closed product tube $N(K)$ disjoint from $J$, let
$E_K=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$, and let $\mu_K$ be the positive
meridian. Since $H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z[\mu_K]$, define the topological
linking number relative to this tube by the unique integer $a$ satisfying
$$[J]=a[\mu_K]\quad\text{in }H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z).$$
The chosen tube is part of the data for this definition.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice as in the maximal-abelian-cover convention. Let $L=K_1\cup\cdots\cup K_r\subset S^3$ be a nonempty oriented smooth link, with $r\ge1$, compact exterior $E_L$ formed by deleting the interiors of pairwise-disjoint chosen closed normal-disk tubes, and basepoint $b\in E_L$. For a knot, $r=1$ and $E_L=E_K$. The full meridian abelianization group is $H_L=H_1(E_L;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^r$, with the positive normal-disk meridians as its ordered basis. Choose a finite-rank free abelian group $H$ of positive rank and an epimorphism $\chi:H_L\to H$; write $\psi=\chi\circ\mathrm{ab}:G\to H$ for the induced map from $G=\pi_1(E_L,b)$. The identity choice $H=H_L$ is the full multivariable deck map; a coloring may identify its variables only through the explicitly stated map $\chi$. Let $\mathbb F$ be a field, let $d\ge1$, and let $\rho:G\to\mathrm{GL}_d(\mathbb F)$ be a representation. Put $\Lambda=\mathbb F[H]$, the commutative Laurent-polynomial ring with monomial basis $H$, and $Q=\operatorname{Frac}(\Lambda)$. On row vectors define the right $\mathbb F[G]$ action by $v\cdot g=v\rho(g)\psi(g)$, where $\psi(g)$ is central multiplication by its monomial in $\Lambda$. For a chosen finite based CW structure $X$ on $E_L$, orient and order its cells and choose one lift of each cell to the universal cover $\widetilde X$. The twisted cellular complex is

$$C_*^{\rho,\psi}(X;\Lambda^d)=\Lambda^d\otimes_{\mathbb F[G]}C_*(\widetilde X;\mathbb F),$$

and its fraction-field complex is $C_*^{\rho,\psi}(X;Q^d)=Q\otimes_{\Lambda}C_*^{\rho,\psi}(X;\Lambda^d)$. The lifted cell bases and the standard coordinate basis of $\mathbb F^d$ give the based $Q$-vector-space bases. If this fraction-field complex is not acyclic, define its twisted torsion to be $0$. If it is acyclic, choose in each degree a basis $\mathbf b_i$ of $B_i=\operatorname{im}\partial_{i+1}$ and lifts $\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{i-1}$ of $\mathbf b_{i-1}$ under $\partial_i$; with $\mathbf c_i$ the based cellular basis, set

$$\tau(C_*,\mathbf c)=\prod_i[\mathbf b_i,\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{i-1}/\mathbf c_i]^{(-1)^{i+1}}\in Q^\times,$$

where brackets denote the determinant of the change-of-basis matrix. The twisted Reidemeister torsion is this value modulo the subgroup $\mathcal U_{\rho,\psi}=\{\pm\det(\rho(g))\psi(g)^d:g\in G\}\subset Q^\times$. This exact determinant image is contained in the commonly used coarser unit subgroup $\{\pm a h:a\in\det(\rho(G)),\ h\in H\}$. The choice-free statement uses the full abelianization chain model first and specializes it only by the declared coefficient map $\chi$.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the data in the definition of the maximal-abelian-cover Alexander module for a nonempty oriented smooth link $L$. Let $i:E_L\hookrightarrow X_L$ be the inclusion of the compact exterior into the open complement, and let $p:X_L^{\mathrm{ab}}\to X_L$ be the maximal abelian cover. Then $E_L$ is a strong deformation retract of $X_L$, the restricted covering $p^{-1}(E_L)\to E_L$ is the connected maximal abelian cover of $E_L$, and the lifted deformation retract is equivariant under the deck group. The inclusion identifies $H_1(E_L;\mathbb Z)$ with $H_1(X_L;\mathbb Z)$ and preserves the positive-meridian classes. In particular, inclusion induces a $\Lambda_r$-module isomorphism

$$
H_1(p^{-1}(E_L);\mathbb Z)\cong A_L.
$$

facts:
**Given:** AC; the link, its chosen pairwise-disjoint closed normal disk tubes $N(K_i)=\Phi_i(D_{\epsilon_i}\nu(K_i))$, the compact exterior $E_L$, the open complement $X_L$, a basepoint $b\in E_L$, and the maximal abelian cover $p:X_L^{\mathrm{ab}}\to X_L$.

[A1] AC is assumed in the maximal-abelian-cover definition and its link-complement supplier ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

[F1] The cover $p$ is the connected regular cover classified by the kernel of abelianization, and its deck group is $H_1(X_L;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^r$ ([[def-maximal-abelian-cover-alexander-module]]).

[F2] A homotopy of maps into a base of a covering, together with an initial lift, has a unique homotopy lift ([[thm-homotopy-lifting-for-covering-maps]]).

[F3] Paths lift uniquely from a prescribed point of a covering fibre ([[thm-path-lifting-for-covering-maps]]).

[F4] Connected covers of a path-connected, locally path-connected, semilocally simply connected space are classified by their induced fundamental-group subgroups ([[thm-classification-of-connected-covering-spaces]]).

[F5] A map defined continuously on the members of a finite closed cover, with agreeing restrictions on overlaps, is continuous ([[lem-continuity-is-local-and-pastes]]).

[F6] The link complement is a connected smooth three-manifold under AC ([[lem-the-complement-of-an-oriented-link-is-a-connected-smooth-three-manifold]]).

[F7] In a connected regular covering, the deck group acts transitively on each fibre ([[thm-regular-covering-characterizations]]).

[F8] A deformation retract is fixed pointwise by a homotopy from the identity to the retraction-inclusion composite ([[def-retraction-and-deformation-retract]]).

[F9] Inclusion of a deformation retract induces an isomorphism on fundamental groups at every basepoint in the retract ([[prop-retracts-inject-fundamental-groups]]).

[F10] Homotopic maps induce the same homomorphism on singular homology ([[cor-homotopic-maps-induce-the-same-map-on-singular-homology]]).

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Choice convention of the twisted-chain definition. Let $L$ be a nonempty oriented link, let $E_L$ be its chosen compact exterior, and let $X$ be a finite based two-dimensional CW complex with one $0$-cell, $n\ge2$ oriented $1$-cells $x_1,\ldots,x_n$, and $n-1$ oriented $2$-cells attached by based words $r_1,\ldots,r_{n-1}$. The supplied data include a based cellular spine certificate: a finite sequence of elementary cellular expansions and collapses identifying the simple-homotopy type of $X$ with the selected finite CW structure on $E_L$. Thus an abstract group isomorphism $\pi_1(X)\cong\pi_1(E_L)$ alone is not a spine certificate. Let $G=\pi_1(E_L)$, let $\rho:G\to\mathrm{GL}_d(\mathbb F)$ and $\psi:G\twoheadrightarrow H$ be the representation and declared free-abelian deck map, and put $Q=\operatorname{Frac}(\mathbb F[H])$. The associated deficiency-one presentation is $\langle x_1,\ldots,x_n\mid r_1,\ldots,r_{n-1}\rangle$ through the certified spine map. For $w\in F_n$, define Fox derivatives recursively by $\partial x_k/\partial x_j=\delta_{kj}$, $\partial(uv)/\partial x_j=\partial u/\partial x_j+u\,\partial v/\partial x_j$, and $\partial x_k^{-1}/\partial x_j=-x_k^{-1}\delta_{kj}$. Extend them linearly to the group ring and let $\Phi:\mathbb F[F_n]\to M_d(Q)$ be the ring homomorphism induced by $x_k\mapsto\rho(x_k)\psi(x_k)$. Form the block Fox matrix $J=(\Phi(\partial r_i/\partial x_k))_{i,k}$, of size $(n-1)d$ by $nd$. For a chosen column index $j$, let $J_{\widehat j}$ be obtained by deleting its entire $d$-column block and let $D_j=\det(\rho(x_j)\psi(x_j)-I_d)$. The Wada quotient for this column is defined only when $D_j\ne0$, and then is $W_j=\det(J_{\widehat j})/D_j\in Q$; a zero denominator makes that column inadmissible even when another column is valid. No abstract deficiency-one presentation is assigned exterior torsion unless its presentation complex is the stated based spine.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $L$ be a nonempty oriented smooth $r$-component link with $r\ge1$, compact exterior $E_L=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(L)$ obtained from pairwise-disjoint closed normal disk tubes, a finite oriented simplicial triangulation $K$ of $E_L$ with ordered vertices and simplices, with least vertex $v_0$ as the basepoint used in the cover definition, and one certified positive-meridian edge loop $\mu_i$ per component. Orient each normal disk so the positive tangent to its component followed by the positive disk basis agrees with the orientation of $S^3$, and assume the resulting classes form the standard basis of $H_1(E_L;\mathbb Z)$. If an integer-vector edge labeling is antisymmetric under edge reversal, sums to zero on every oriented 2-simplex, and evaluates to the $i$th standard basis vector on $\mu_i$, then the chain procedure returns a finite free chain complex over $\Lambda_r=\mathbb Z[t_1^{\pm1},\ldots,t_r^{\pm1}]$. The first homology of this complex is the absolute maximal-abelian-cover Alexander module $A_L$. Its Fitting ideals are independent of the triangulation and cell lifts, and its order is defined up to multiplication by a unit $\pm t_1^{k_1}\cdots t_r^{k_r}$.

facts:
**Given:** AC; a nonempty oriented smooth $r$-component link; its chosen compact exterior and finite ordered oriented simplicial triangulation; certified positive-meridian edge loops forming the basis of $H_1(E_L;\mathbb Z)$; and an edge labeling accepted by the chain procedure.

[A1] AC is assumed in the maximal-abelian-cover definition and its link-complement supplier ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

[F1] The module $A_L$ is $H_1(X_L^{\mathrm{ab}};\mathbb Z)$ with Laurent variables acting by positive-meridian deck transformations ([[def-maximal-abelian-cover-alexander-module]]).

[F2] Inclusion of the compact exterior into the open complement lifts to a deck-equivariant homotopy equivalence of maximal abelian covers and preserves the positive-meridian basis ([[lem-maximal-abelian-cover-link-exterior-retraction]]).

[F3] The procedure checks edge reversal, all oriented 2-simplex sums and the marked meridian images, returning invalid-labeling upon any failed check ([[alg-abelian-cover-chain-model-from-triangulated-exterior]]).

[F4] On each encoded admissible input the procedure terminates and rejects exactly inputs that fail one of its three label checks ([[thm-abelian-cover-chain-model-from-triangulated-exterior-procedure-properties]]).

[F5] A finite CW structure on $E_L$ lifts to a finite-rank free $\Lambda_r$ cellular chain complex whose first homology is $A_L$ ([[lem-maximal-abelian-cover-cellular-chain-model]]).

[F6] For every CW complex, cellular homology agrees naturally with singular homology and the comparison is natural for cellular maps ([[thm-cellular-homology-computes-singular-homology]]).

[F7] The first Hurewicz homomorphism identifies $\pi_1(E_L,b)^{\mathrm{ab}}$ with $H_1(E_L;\mathbb Z)$ ([[prop-the-first-hurewicz-map-in-degree-one-is-abelianization]]).

[F8] The Fitting ideals of $A_L$ and its order are independent of finite triangulation and cell lifts; the order has the signed Laurent-monomial unit ambiguity ([[lem-multivariable-alexander-order-and-specialization]]).

[F9] Connected covers of a path-connected, locally path-connected, semilocally simply connected space are classified by their induced subgroups ([[thm-classification-of-connected-covering-spaces]]).

[F10] For each lifted face incidence, the procedure inserts the signed incidence number times the deck monomial of its lift displacement ([[alg-abelian-cover-chain-model-from-triangulated-exterior]]).

facts:
**Given:** AC; the actual compatible based spine and filling certificates; the full positive-meridian abelianization followed by the explicit color map; a field-valued representation of $\pi_1(X)$; and $D\ne0$.

[A1] The maximal-abelian-cover and twisted-chain conventions explicitly assume AC. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]; [[def-knot-twisted-chain-complex-and-reidemeister-torsion]]

[F1] For a based acyclic twisted complex, torsion is the alternating determinant product in the cellular bases; nonacyclic torsion is defined to be zero. [[def-knot-twisted-chain-complex-and-reidemeister-torsion]]

[F2] For a certified deficiency-one exterior spine with torsion degree-one homology over the Laurent ring and an admissible deleted column, the Fox minor divided by its boundary determinant equals the based torsion class. [[thm-wada-deleted-minor-equals-twisted-reidemeister-torsion]]

[F3] The finite braid procedure fixes the positive Artin convention, the cumulative meridians $g_i$, the closure relators, the reduced Fox block $\overline B_\rho(\beta)$, and the numerator and denominator $N,D$. [[alg-twisted-burau-determinant-for-colored-braid-closure]]

[F4] The closure and axis exteriors, their meridian generators, and the Artin action use the stated geometric braid and punctured-disk conventions; the standard positive puncture meridians form a free basis. [[def-closure-of-a-geometric-braid]]; [[def-artin-automorphisms-of-the-free-group]]; [[def-standard-meridians-of-a-punctured-disk]]; [[thm-the-punctured-disk-fundamental-group-is-free-on-standard-meridians]]

[F5] The based Fox block matrix is the cellular boundary matrix of the based presentation complex under the row-coefficient convention. [[lem-twisted-fox-jacobian-is-cellular-boundary]]

[F6] The full positive-meridian abelianization chain model is formed before applying the declared map $\chi$; it computes the maximal-abelian-cover module. [[thm-abelian-cover-chain-model-computes-alexander-module]]

[F7] Filling the axis torus kills its meridian in the fundamental group, and the gluing fundamental group is determined by the inclusions of the common boundary torus. [[thm-seifert-van-kampen]]; [[def-knot-exterior]]

[F8] The Laurent coefficient ring is an integral domain embedded in its fraction field, so clearing a nonzero denominator in a free module is valid. [[def-field-of-fractions]]; [[thm-field-of-fractions-is-a-field-and-the-domain-embeds]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Choice convention of the twisted-chain definition. Let a finite colored geometric braid, a field with exact arithmetic, a representation of the closure exterior group, the full positive-meridian abelianization followed by a declared surjective color map, and compatible based spine and axis-filling certificates satisfy all input conditions of the colored twisted Burau procedure. Assume its designated denominator $D=\det(\rho(g_n)\psi(g_n)-I_d)$ is nonzero, so the procedure is applicable, and assume the representation and deck map extend over the filling with the axis meridian acting trivially. Then the procedure returns the class of the twisted Reidemeister torsion of the closure exterior. If the fraction-field complex is acyclic, the returned value is $N/D$, where $N=\det(\overline B_\rho(\beta)-I_{(n-1)d})$; if it is nonacyclic, the procedure returns $0$ and $N=0$, in agreement with the declared zero-torsion convention. The geometric certificates are essential hypotheses: matching a group presentation alone does not certify an exterior spine or the axis-filling decomposition.

facts:
**Given:** AC; all finite encoded procedure inputs; a nonzero designated denominator; the actual based spine and compatible axis-filling certificates; and the stated coefficient extension across filling.

[A1] AC is inherited from the full abelianization and twisted-chain convention. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]; [[def-knot-twisted-chain-complex-and-reidemeister-torsion]]

[F1] The finite procedure checks its declared input conditions, evaluates $D$ before the acyclicity branch, returns zero for a nonacyclic complex, and otherwise returns $N/D$. [[alg-twisted-burau-determinant-for-colored-braid-closure]]

[F2] For the certified closure and axis exteriors with $D\ne0$, the braid-axis torsion product identifies the exterior torsion with $N/D$ on the acyclic branch and proves $N=0$ on the nonacyclic branch. [[thm-twisted-burau-axis-torsion-product]]

[F3] The twisted torsion convention assigns zero to a nonacyclic fraction-field complex and takes acyclic torsion modulo the determinant and deck-unit subgroup. [[def-knot-twisted-chain-complex-and-reidemeister-torsion]]

[F4] The full positive-meridian abelianization chain model precedes every declared color specialization. [[thm-abelian-cover-chain-model-computes-alexander-module]]

contract.heading: Statement refuted
contract.text: The assertion that every generator-column deletion gives a defined Wada quotient for a based deficiency-one spine is false. Let $X$ be the standard unknot exterior, with its circle spine generated by a positive meridian $y$, and form a based simple expansion by adding a $1$-cell $x$ and a $2$-cell attached by the word $r=x$. This gives the based deficiency-one presentation $\langle x,y\mid x\rangle$. Use the trivial one-dimensional representation over $\mathbb Q$ and the full abelianization deck map $\psi(x)=1$, $\psi(y)=t$ into $H=\langle t\rangle\cong\mathbb Z$. For the $x$ column, the Fox minor is $0$ and the denominator is $0$, so that column's Wada quotient is undefined; for the $y$ column, the denominator is $t-1\ne0$ and the quotient is $1/(t-1)$. Thus the invalidity of one designated column does not imply that another column is inadmissible.

facts:
**Given:** AC; the standard solid-torus model of the unknot exterior; the based circle spine; the elementary expansion adding the pair $(x,r=x)$; the trivial representation; and the specified full abelianization map.

[A1] AC is inherited from the twisted-chain convention. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] The Wada quotient for a selected generator column is defined only when its denominator $\det(\rho(x_j)\psi(x_j)-I)$ is nonzero; its numerator is the determinant of the Fox matrix with that block column deleted. [[def-knot-wada-quotient-for-deficiency-one-presentation]]

[F2] The based twisted differential for a generator $z$ is multiplication by $\rho(z)\psi(z)-1$, and acyclic based torsion is computed by the alternating determinant product. [[def-knot-twisted-chain-complex-and-reidemeister-torsion]]

[F3] The compact unknot exterior is a solid torus and retracts onto its core circle. [[def-knot-exterior]]

[F4] The positive meridian generates the first homology of a knot exterior. [[thm-knot-exterior-homology-and-longitude]]; [[def-knot-meridian-and-preferred-longitude]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot, let $X_K=S^3\setminus K$, and let $q\ge2$. Let $A_K=H_1(\widetilde X_K;\mathbb Z)$ be the one-variable Alexander module with the positive-meridian deck action $t$. Then, as abelian groups,
$$
H_1(\Sigma_q(K);\mathbb Z)\cong A_K/(t^q-1)A_K.
$$

facts:
**Given:** The Axiom of Choice, a smooth oriented knot $K$, its chosen exterior $E_K$, positive meridian $\mu$, and an integer $q\ge2$.

[A1] Full AC is the choice-function axiom. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] The connected cover $E_q\to E_K$ is classified by the positive-meridian homomorphism modulo $q$; its filling kills the closed lift of $\mu^q$. [[def-cyclic-branched-cover-of-a-knot]]

[F2] The inclusion $E_K\hookrightarrow X_K$ is a strong deformation retraction equivalence and carries the positive meridian to the positive meridian. [[lem-knot-tubular-exterior-and-boundary]]

[F3] The module $A_K$ is $H_1$ of the connected infinite cyclic cover of $X_K$ classified by total linking, with $t$ acting by the positive-meridian deck transformation. [[def-one-variable-alexander-module-of-an-oriented-link]]

[F4] For a path-connected space, the first Hurewicz map identifies $H_1$ with the abelianization of its fundamental group. [[prop-the-first-hurewicz-map-in-degree-one-is-abelianization]]

[F5] Connected covers of a path-connected, locally path-connected, semilocally simply connected base are classified by subgroups of its fundamental group. [[thm-classification-of-connected-covering-spaces]]

[F6] Mayer–Vietoris is exact for an open cover, and a deformation retraction induces an isomorphism on singular homology. [[thm-mayer-vietoris-sequence-in-singular-homology]], [[prop-singular-homology-is-invariant-under-deformation-retracts]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot, let $F$ be a connected compact oriented Seifert surface of genus $g$, and choose any ordered integral basis $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$ with positive-push Seifert matrix $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. For an integer $q\ge2$, let $M_q(V)$ be the symmetric block matrix of size $2g(q-1)$ whose $2g\times2g$ block in position $(k,\ell)$, for $1\le k,\ell\le q-1$, is $V+V^T$ if $k=\ell$, $-V^T$ if $\ell=k+1$, $-V$ if $k=\ell+1$, and $0$ if $|k-\ell|\ge2$. Then
$$
H_1(\Sigma_q(K);\mathbb Z)\cong\operatorname{coker}(M_q(V)).
$$
For $q=2$ this presentation matrix is $V+V^T$; when $g=0$ the empty matrix has trivial cokernel.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, the oriented knot $K$, a connected compact oriented Seifert surface $F$, an ordered integral basis of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$, its positive-push matrix $V$, and $q\ge2$.

[A1] Full AC is the choice-function axiom used by the cyclic-cover and duality suppliers. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] The cover $\Sigma_q(K)$ is the boundary of the $q$-fold branched cover of $B^4$ along a push-in of $F$. [[def-cyclic-branched-cover-of-a-knot]], [[lem-branched-cover-surgery-presentation-from-seifert-surface]]

[F2] For the disk-band basis, that 4-manifold has one $0$-handle and $2g(q-1)$ $2$-handles, with intersection matrix $M_q(V)$. [[lem-branched-cover-surgery-presentation-from-seifert-surface]]

[F3] Poincaré–Lefschetz duality identifies $H^2(W;\mathbb Z)$ with $H_2(W,\partial W;\mathbb Z)$ by capping with the relative fundamental class. [[thm-poincare-lefschetz-duality]]

[F4] The homology long exact sequence of the pair $(W,\partial W)$ is exact. [[thm-long-exact-sequence-of-a-pair-in-singular-homology]]

[F5] The Seifert pairing is bilinear on homology classes; changing an integral basis by $P\in\operatorname{GL}_{2g}(\mathbb Z)$ changes its matrix to $P^TVP$. [[def-knot-seifert-pairing-and-matrix]], [[lem-seifert-pairing-well-defined]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot, let $F$ be a connected compact oriented Seifert surface of genus $g$, and let $V$ be its positive-push Seifert matrix in any ordered integral basis of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$. Then
$$
H_1(\Sigma_2(K);\mathbb Z)\cong\operatorname{coker}(V+V^T).
$$
For $g=0$, the matrix is empty and the cokernel is trivial.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, a smooth oriented knot $K$, a connected compact oriented Seifert surface $F$, an ordered integral basis of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$, and its positive-push matrix $V$.

[A1] Full AC is the choice-function axiom used by the cyclic-cover construction. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] The double branched cover is $\Sigma_2(K)$ from the connected meridian-mod-$2$ exterior cover with its lifted meridian filled. [[def-cyclic-branched-cover-of-a-knot]]

[F2] For every $q\ge2$, $H_1(\Sigma_q(K);\mathbb Z)\cong\operatorname{coker}(M_q(V))$, with diagonal blocks $V+V^T$ and adjacent blocks $-V$ and $-V^T$. [[lem-cyclic-branched-cover-seifert-block-matrix]]
