contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot, let $F$ be a connected compact oriented Seifert surface of genus $g$, and let $V$ be its positive-push Seifert matrix in an ordered integral basis of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$. Write $\Delta_K(t)$ for the Alexander polynomial normalized up to multiplication by $\pm t^k$, and let $q\ge2$ with $\zeta_q$ a primitive $q$-th root of unity. Then $H_1(\Sigma_q(K);\mathbb Z)$ is finite if and only if $\Delta_K(\zeta_q^j)\ne0$ for every $1\le j<q$, and, when it is finite,
$$
|H_1(\Sigma_q(K);\mathbb Z)|=\prod_{j=1}^{q-1}|\Delta_K(\zeta_q^j)|.
$$
The same criterion and order hold when $\Delta_K(t)$ is replaced by $\det(V-tV^T)$.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, $K,F,V,q$, and the primitive root $\zeta_q$ in the Statement.

[A1] Full AC is the choice-function axiom required by the cyclic-cover definition and coinvariant lemma. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] $H_1(\Sigma_q(K);\mathbb Z)\cong A_K/(t^q-1)A_K$, where $A_K$ is the infinite-cyclic-cover Alexander module with positive-meridian deck action $t$. [[lem-cyclic-branched-cover-homology-is-alexander-module-coinvariants]]

[F2] $A_K$ has presentation $\operatorname{coker}(V-tV^T)$ over $\mathbb Z[t,t^{-1}]$. [[thm-seifert-matrix-presents-knot-alexander-module]]

[F3] $V-V^T$ is the matrix of the integral intersection form on $F$, hence has determinant $\pm1$. [[lem-seifert-matrix-skew-part-is-surface-intersection]]

[F4] $\det(V-tV^T)$ represents $\Delta_K(t)$ up to multiplication by $\pm t^k$. [[thm-seifert-determinant-is-the-knot-alexander-polynomial]]

[F5] The cokernel of a square integer matrix is finite exactly when its determinant is nonzero, and then its order is the absolute determinant. [[lem-square-integer-cokernel-finiteness-and-order]]
scope: Literal contract/Facts extraction only; accepted proof body not inspected.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot with Alexander polynomial $\Delta_K(t)$ normalized up to multiplication by $\pm t^k$. Then $H_1(\Sigma_2(K);\mathbb Z)$ is finite if and only if $\Delta_K(-1)\ne0$, and in that case
$$
|H_1(\Sigma_2(K);\mathbb Z)|=|\Delta_K(-1)|.
$$
Moreover, $\Delta_K(-1)$ is odd, so the first homology of every double branched cover is finite.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC and a smooth oriented knot $K$.

[A1] Full AC is the choice-function axiom required by the cyclic branched-cover definition and Seifert determinant presentation. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] For a positive-push Seifert matrix $V$, $H_1(\Sigma_2(K);\mathbb Z)\cong\operatorname{coker}(V+V^T)$. [[lem-double-branched-cover-homology-from-seifert-matrix]]

[F2] The cokernel of a square integer matrix is finite exactly when its determinant is nonzero, and then its order is the absolute determinant. [[lem-square-integer-cokernel-finiteness-and-order]]

[F3] $\det(V-tV^T)$ represents $\Delta_K(t)$ up to multiplication by $\pm t^k$. [[thm-seifert-determinant-is-the-knot-alexander-polynomial]]

[F4] $\Delta_K(t)$ is an integer Laurent polynomial and $\Delta_K(1)=\pm1$. [[def-alexander-polynomial-from-the-first-elementary-ideal]], [[lem-square-seifert-presentation-and-alexander-normalization]]

contract.heading: Example
contract.text:
For the right-handed trefoil and figure-eight knot, use their standard genus-one Seifert surfaces and the ordered bases whose positive-push Seifert matrices are, respectively,
$$V_T=\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\1&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad V_8=\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\1&1\end{pmatrix}.$$
Their double branched covers have first homology $\mathbb Z/3\mathbb Z$ and $\mathbb Z/5\mathbb Z$, respectively. The double branched cover of the unknot is $S^3$.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC and the matrices and knots specified in the Example.

[A1] Full AC is the choice-function axiom required by the double-cover presentation. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] For a positive-push Seifert matrix $V$, $H_1(\Sigma_2(K);\mathbb Z)\cong\operatorname{coker}(V+V^T)$. [[lem-double-branched-cover-homology-from-seifert-matrix]]

[F2] A square integer matrix with nonzero determinant has finite cokernel of order the absolute determinant; unimodular row and column operations preserve the cokernel. [[lem-square-integer-cokernel-finiteness-and-order]]

contract.heading: Statement refuted
contract.text: Every cyclic branched cover of a smooth oriented knot has finite first homology.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, the right-handed trefoil matrix $V_T=\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}$, and the primitive sixth root $\zeta_6=e^{i\pi/3}$.

[A1] Full AC is the choice-function axiom required by the cyclic-cover and Alexander-polynomial theorems. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] The Seifert determinant $\det(V-tV^T)$ represents the Alexander polynomial up to a unit $\pm t^k$. [[thm-seifert-determinant-is-the-knot-alexander-polynomial]], [[def-alexander-polynomial-from-the-first-elementary-ideal]]

[F2] The cyclic-cover order theorem states that a zero at any nontrivial $q$-th root makes the first homology infinite. [[thm-knot-cyclic-cover-order-from-alexander-polynomial]]

[F3] The Alexander normalization gives $\Delta_K(1)=\pm1$, and the double-cover theorem gives finiteness when $|\Delta_K(-1)|$ is this nonzero odd integer. [[lem-square-seifert-presentation-and-alexander-normalization]], [[thm-knot-determinant-is-order-of-double-cover-homology]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $L$ be a nonempty smooth oriented link in the oriented $3$-sphere, and let $F_0,F_1$ be connected compact smooth oriented embedded surfaces with the same oriented boundary $L$. There is a finite sequence of such spanning surfaces from $F_0$ to $F_1$ in which each consecutive pair differs either by an ambient isotopy fixed on $L$ or by one embedded arc surgery or its reverse.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, a nonempty oriented link $L\subset S^3$, and connected compact oriented spanning surfaces $F_0,F_1$ with boundary $L$.

[A1] Full AC implies dependent choice and countable choice. [[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]

[F1] The one-variable cover of $S^3\setminus L$ is the connected cover classified by the kernel of the total-linking homomorphism, which sends every positive meridian to $1$. [[def-one-variable-alexander-module-of-an-oriented-link]]

[F2] Under [A1], relative transversality gives arbitrarily small smooth perturbations fixed on a closed good region. The dimension-general isotopy extension theorem applies to a compact smooth surface, possibly with boundary, embedded in the boundaryless three-sphere. Its velocity construction fixes $L$ when the prescribed surface velocity is zero there. Smooth tubular neighborhoods exist for the link. [[thm-transversality-homotopy-theorem]], [[prop-relative-transversality-preserves-a-map-on-a-closed-good-region]], [[thm-isotopy-extension]], [[thm-tubular-neighbourhood-theorem-in-a-smooth-ambient-manifold]], [[thm-transverse-preimage-theorem]]

[F3] A compact smooth manifold with corners has a finite triangulation relative to its already triangulated boundary faces. [[thm-compact-smooth-manifolds-with-corners-admit-relative-finite-triangulations]]

[F4] The arc-surgery operation removes two disks and replaces them with the lateral annulus of an embedded product cylinder, leaving the boundary link fixed. [[def-seifert-surface-arc-surgery]]

[F5] For a compact locally contractible subset of $S^3$, Alexander duality identifies its second integral cohomology with the reduced zeroth homology of its complement. [[thm-alexander-duality-for-compact-locally-contractible-subsets-of-a-sphere]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume full AC. Let $L$ be a nonempty smooth oriented link in the oriented $3$-sphere, and let $F$ be a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface with oriented boundary $L$. For disjoint oriented embedded circles $C,D\subset S^3$, define $\operatorname{lk}(C,D)$ as the coefficient of the positive meridian of $D$ in $H_1(S^3\setminus D;\mathbb Z)$, and extend it bilinearly to finite integral sums of oriented circles. This linking number is symmetric on disjoint circle cycles. Every class of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$ has a representative that is a finite integral sum of pairwise disjoint smooth oriented embedded circles in $F$. The positive push-off $x^+$ of such a representative is a sufficiently small copy in the positive normal direction determined by the ambient and surface orientations. For representatives $x$ and $y$, the sum of the pairwise linking numbers between $x^+$ and $y$ depends only on $[x]$ and $[y]$, is independent of the sufficiently small positive push-off level, and is bilinear. Hence it defines the positive-push Seifert pairing on $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, a nonempty oriented link $L$, and a connected compact oriented spanning surface $F$ with boundary $L$.

[A1] Full AC implies dependent choice and countable choice, supplying the compact-surface normal form and Alexander-duality conventions. [[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]], [[def-one-variable-alexander-module-of-an-oriented-link]]

[F1] The compact surface has a finite cellulation, and its first homology is finitely generated and represented by integral cellular cycles. [[lem-finite-chart-surface-normal-forms-supply-jordan-disks-and-torsion-free-groups]]

[F2] Linking of disjoint oriented circles is the meridian coefficient; when a regular diagram and spanning surface are supplied it agrees with the signed intersection and mixed-crossing half-sum. [[def-one-variable-alexander-module-of-an-oriented-link]], [[thm-linking-number-equals-signed-intersection]]

[F3] After moving a finite oriented link off infinity, it has a regular projection, a finite decorated immersion with finitely many mixed crossings. [[def-oriented-link-in-s-three-and-ambient-isotopy]], [[def-regular-oriented-link-diagram]], [[lem-every-oriented-link-admits-a-regular-projection]]

[F4] Every smooth oriented circle has a supplied connected compact oriented spanning surface, so the link-intersection theorem applies to it. [[thm-every-oriented-knot-bounds-a-seifert-surface]]

[F5] A smooth loop can be homotoped in the complement of a disjoint circle to meet a supplied spanning surface transversely. [[thm-transversality-homotopy-theorem]], [[prop-relative-transversality-preserves-a-map-on-a-closed-good-region]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume full AC. Let $L$ be a nonempty smooth oriented link with $r$ components, let $F$ be a connected compact smooth oriented spanning surface of genus $g$, and let $F'$ be obtained by choosing an embedded solid cylinder $[0,1]\times D^2$ that meets $F$ exactly in its two end disks and lies on the same local side at both disks, then replacing those disks by the cylinder's lateral annulus with the compatible orientation. This surgery preserves $L$. Put $m=2g+r-1$, choose an ordered integral basis of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$ represented away from the two end disks, and let $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$ be its positive-push Seifert matrix. The surviving classes of that basis extend by two classes to an integral basis of $H_1(F';\mathbb Z)$, and for some column vectors $x,y\in\mathbb Z^m$ and integer $z$, the new Seifert matrix is one of
$$
\begin{pmatrix}V&x&0\\y^T&z&0\\0^T&1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
\begin{pmatrix}V&x&0\\y^T&z&1\\0^T&0&0\end{pmatrix}.
$$

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, a nonempty oriented link $L$, a connected compact oriented spanning surface $F$, an ordered basis of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$, and one embedded arc surgery producing $F'$.

[A1] Full AC implies dependent choice and countable choice, supplying the Alexander-duality convention and compact-surface normal form. [[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]

[F1] The positive-push Seifert pairing is well-defined and bilinear on the homology of every connected link surface. [[lem-link-seifert-pairing-well-defined]]

[F2] An arc surgery replaces two disks by the lateral annulus of an embedded product cylinder, leaving the oriented boundary unchanged. [[def-seifert-surface-arc-surgery]]

[F3] Mayer–Vietoris computes the homology of two surfaces glued along a common boundary circle. [[thm-mayer-vietoris-sequence-in-singular-homology]]

[F4] Linking is the signed intersection with a supplied spanning surface; linking of disjoint circles is symmetric. [[thm-linking-number-equals-signed-intersection]], [[lem-link-seifert-pairing-well-defined]], [[def-regular-oriented-link-diagram]], [[lem-every-oriented-link-admits-a-regular-projection]]

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $V$ be an even-order square matrix with integer entries, of size $n=2g$. A unimodular congruence replaces $V$ by $P^TVP$ for an integer matrix $P$ with determinant $+1$ or $-1$. For $x,y\in\mathbb Z^n$ as column vectors and $z\in\mathbb Z$, the two elementary enlargements of $V$ are
$$
E_0(V;x,y,z)=\begin{pmatrix}V&x&0\\y^T&z&0\\0^T&1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
E_1(V;x,y,z)=\begin{pmatrix}V&x&0\\y^T&z&1\\0^T&0&0\end{pmatrix}.
$$
Two even-order integral matrices are **S-equivalent** if one can be obtained from the other by a finite sequence of unimodular congruences, elementary enlargements, and reverse elementary enlargements.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume full AC. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the oriented standard $3$-sphere, and let $F,F'$ be any connected compact smooth oriented spanning surfaces for $K$. For any ordered integral bases of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$ and $H_1(F';\mathbb Z)$, the matrices of the positive-push Seifert pairing are related by a finite sequence of integral unimodular congruences and the two rank-two elementary Seifert enlargements or their reverses.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, a smooth oriented knot $K$, two connected smooth oriented spanning surfaces $F,F'$, and ordered integral bases for their first homology groups.

[A1] Full AC is the choice-function axiom assumed by the knot Seifert-pairing interface. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] The positive-push pairing is $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$ and is bilinear on integral homology classes. [[def-knot-seifert-pairing-and-matrix]], [[lem-seifert-pairing-well-defined]]

[F2] If an ambient isotopy carries one oriented knot-surface pair to another, the transported basis has the same Seifert matrix; changing an integral basis gives a unimodular congruence. [[lem-seifert-matrix-s-equivalence-under-isotopy]]

[F3] An arc surgery replaces two disks by the lateral annulus of a product cylinder while preserving the oriented boundary knot. [[def-seifert-surface-arc-surgery]]

[F4] The two elementary enlargement matrices are $E_0(V;x,y,z)$ and $E_1(V;x,y,z)$ as defined in S-equivalence. [[def-seifert-matrix-s-equivalence]]

[F6] For disjoint oriented knots, linking is the signed intersection with a spanning surface and is symmetric in the two components; the mixed-crossing formula gives the same half-sum after the components are interchanged. [[thm-linking-number-equals-signed-intersection]]

[F7] The skew part of the positive-push Seifert matrix is the oriented intersection form on the surface. [[lem-seifert-matrix-skew-part-is-surface-intersection]]

[L1] Any two such surfaces are connected by finitely many ambient isotopies fixing the boundary and embedded arc surgeries or their reverses. [[lem-seifert-surfaces-of-same-link-are-related-by-arc-surgeries]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume full AC. For a knot Seifert surface $F$ with Seifert matrix $V$, the function $q_F(x)=x^TVx\pmod2$ is well-defined on $H_1(F;\mathbb F_2)$ and satisfies
$$q_F(x+y)=q_F(x)+q_F(y)+x\cdot_F y.$$
Its polarization is nondegenerate. For any symplectic basis $(a_1,b_1,\ldots,a_g,b_g)$, the sum $\sum_iq_F(a_i)q_F(b_i)$ is independent of that basis. It is unchanged by either elementary Seifert enlargement, so it depends only on the knot.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, an oriented knot, a connected genus-$g$ spanning surface, and its Seifert matrix $V$.

[A1] Full AC supplies the chosen integral homology basis and Seifert pairing. [[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-knot-seifert-pairing-and-matrix]]

[F1] $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$ is free of rank $2g$, and reduction modulo two identifies $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)\otimes\mathbb F_2$ with $H_1(F;\mathbb F_2)$. [[lem-finite-chart-surface-normal-forms-supply-jordan-disks-and-torsion-free-groups]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume full AC. Every nonempty smooth oriented link $L\subset S^3$ bounds a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface. If $F$ is any such surface with Seifert matrix $V$, and $u$ is a formal Laurent variable, then
$$D_L(u)=\det(u^{-1}V-uV^T)$$
is independent of the surface and integral basis, belongs to $\mathbb Z[u-u^{-1}]$, equals $1$ for the unknot, and satisfies
$$D_{L_+}(u)-D_{L_-}(u)=(u-u^{-1})D_{L_0}(u)$$
for every oriented skein triple. Thus $D_L(u)=
abla_L(u-u^{-1})$ for the unique Conway polynomial normalized by $
abla_U=1$ and $
abla_+-
abla_-=z
abla_0$.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, a nonempty oriented link, the positive crossing convention, and a connected spanning surface with its Seifert matrix.

[A1] Full AC implies the countable-choice hypotheses for regular projection, Jordan disks, and the Seifert construction. [[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]

[F1] A regular oriented diagram has finitely many crossings; oriented smoothing yields finitely many disjoint circles, each bounding a disk in the projection sphere. [[def-regular-oriented-link-diagram]], [[lem-every-oriented-link-admits-a-regular-projection]], [[def-seifert-smoothing-and-seifert-circles-of-an-oriented-link-diagram]], [[lem-finite-chart-surface-normal-forms-supply-jordan-disks-and-torsion-free-groups]]

[F2] The positive-push matrix is $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$ on integral homology classes, with the pairing independent of representatives and push-off level. [[def-link-seifert-pairing-and-matrix]], [[lem-link-seifert-pairing-well-defined]]

[F3] One link-level embedded arc surgery changes the positive-push matrix by one of the two displayed two-row/two-column block enlargements. [[lem-link-seifert-matrix-enlargement-under-arc-surgery]]

[F6] Any two connected oriented spanning surfaces of the same oriented link are related by finitely many ambient isotopies fixing the boundary and embedded arc surgeries. [[lem-seifert-surfaces-of-same-link-are-related-by-arc-surgeries]]

[F4] The positive crossing is the right-handed half-twist in the declared diagram convention; linking is the half-sum of mixed crossing signs for a supplied regular diagram. [[def-oriented-crossing-sign-writhe-and-blackboard-framing]], [[thm-linking-number-equals-signed-intersection]], [[def-regular-oriented-link-diagram]], [[lem-every-oriented-link-admits-a-regular-projection]]

[F7] Alexander duality identifies reduced complement homology with reduced cohomology of a compact locally contractible subset; finite-dimensional parametric transversality applies to a smooth transverse evaluation family (fixed endpoint neighborhoods are preserved by choosing perturbations supported away from them). [[thm-alexander-duality-for-compact-locally-contractible-subsets-of-a-sphere]], [[thm-parametric-transversality]]

[F5] An embedded arc surgery replaces two disks by the lateral annulus of an embedded product cylinder and preserves the boundary link. [[def-seifert-surface-arc-surgery]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the hypotheses and conventions of the Levine–Tristram form definition. At every root $\omega_0\in S^1\setminus\{1\}$ of $\Delta_K$, each one-sided limit of the nonroot signature as the parameter moves along the unit circle to $\omega_0$ exists and is an integer.

facts:

[A1] Full AC and the chosen surface/basis supply a finite real Seifert matrix. [[def-knot-seifert-pairing-and-matrix]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] $H_{e^{i\theta}}$ is a continuous Hermitian matrix family, and its singular parameters away from $1$ are exactly the zeros of a nonzero Alexander polynomial. [F3] A continuous real function on an interval cannot take both positive and negative values without vanishing between them. [[thm-intermediate-value]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume full AC. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot of genus $g$, let $V$ be a Seifert matrix in an integral symplectic basis, and let $\Delta_K^\#(t)$ be the unique symmetric Alexander normalization with $\Delta_K^\#(1)=1$. In the quotient ring $\mathbb F_2[t,t^{-1}]/(1+t)^4$,
$$\Delta_K^\#(t)=1+\operatorname{Arf}(K)\frac{(1+t)^2}{t}.$$

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, an oriented knot, a genus-$g$ Seifert surface, and its positive-push Seifert matrix $V$.

[A1] Full AC supplies the Seifert pairing and Alexander conventions. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] $V-V^T$ is the standard integral symplectic intersection matrix in a handle basis, and changes of integral symplectic basis preserve the Arf value. [[lem-seifert-matrix-skew-part-is-surface-intersection]], [[lem-arf-quadratic-enhancement-from-seifert-form]]

[F2] In a symplectic basis, $\operatorname{Arf}(K)=\sum_i v_{2i-1,2i-1}v_{2i,2i}\pmod2$, equivalently $\sum_{x\in H_1(F;\mathbb F_2)}(-1)^{q_F(x)}=2^g(-1)^{\operatorname{Arf}(K)}$. [[def-knot-arf-invariant-from-seifert-form]], [[lem-arf-quadratic-enhancement-from-seifert-form]]

[F3] The determinant $\det(uV-u^{-1}V^T)$ is $\nabla_K(u-u^{-1})=\Delta_K^\#(u^2)$. [[lem-conway-polynomial-from-seifert-determinant]], [[def-seifert-s-equivalence-and-conway-normalization]]

[F4] $\det(V-V^T)=1$ in a positively oriented symplectic basis, so the centered determinant is the unique normalized symmetric Alexander generator. [[thm-seifert-determinant-is-the-knot-alexander-polynomial]], [[cor-knot-alexander-normalization-symmetry-and-genus-bound]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume full AC. The stable isometry class of the Seifert quadratic enhancement and its Arf value are independent of the spanning surface and integral symplectic basis of an oriented knot $K$. Stable isometry means isometry after orthogonally adjoining finitely many hyperbolic planes $q_H(s,t)=st$ on either side. Under the convention $\Delta_K(t)=
abla_K(t^{1/2}-t^{-1/2})$ with $\Delta_K(1)=1$, the coefficient $a_2(
abla_K)$ of $z^2$ satisfies
$$\operatorname{Arf}(K)\equiv a_2(
abla_K)\pmod2.$$

facts:
**Given:** Full AC and a smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$.

[A1] Full AC supplies the Alexander and Seifert-pairing conventions. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] Any two spanning-surface Seifert matrices are S-equivalent. [[lem-seifert-matrices-of-a-knot-are-s-equivalent]]

[F2] The quadratic enhancement is well-defined, has basis-independent Arf value, and each enlargement orthogonally adds a hyperbolic plane up to isometry; hence its stable isometry class and Arf value are unchanged. [[lem-arf-quadratic-enhancement-from-seifert-form]]

[F3] The normalized Conway determinant is independent of surface and basis and has the declared skein normalization. [[lem-conway-polynomial-from-seifert-determinant]]

[F4] In the symmetric normalized variable, $\Delta_K^\#(t)=\nabla_K(t^{1/2}-t^{-1/2})$. [[def-seifert-s-equivalence-and-conway-normalization]]

[F5] The Seifert determinant near $t=-1$ is $1+\operatorname{Arf}(K)(1+t)^2/t$ modulo $(2,(1+t)^4)$. [[lem-arf-seifert-determinant-congruence-near-minus-one]]

contract.heading: Statement refuted
contract.text: Assume full AC. The false statement is: “For every $\omega\in S^1\setminus\{1\}$, the Levine–Tristram Hermitian matrix of every knot is nonsingular.” The positive trefoil matrix at a primitive sixth root is singular. At that root the nondegenerate signature calculation does not apply; the defined knot invariant is the one-sided-average value.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, the positive trefoil matrix $V_T=\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\-1&-1\end{pmatrix}$, and a primitive sixth root $\omega=e^{i\pi/3}$.

[A1] Full AC supplies the positive-push Seifert matrix and signature conventions. [[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-levine-tristram-hermitian-form-and-signature]]

[F1] $V_T$ is the positive-push trefoil matrix and its Alexander polynomial is $1-t+t^2$. [[ex-knot-kt-07-worked-cases]]

[F2] A root of the Alexander polynomial is exactly a singular parameter for $H_\omega$, and the invariant at such a root is the average of one-sided signatures. [[lem-levine-tristram-hermitian-form-singular-set]], [[def-levine-tristram-hermitian-form-and-signature]]

[F3] Each one-sided limit at this root exists as an integer, so the arithmetic mean prescribed by the definition is defined. [[lem-levine-tristram-one-sided-averages-exist]]

contract.heading: Example
contract.text:
Assume full AC. Use the positive-push Seifert matrices
$$V_T=\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\-1&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad V_F=\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\-1&1\end{pmatrix}$$
for the positive trefoil and the figure-eight knot, respectively. At $\omega=-1$, their Levine–Tristram signatures are $-2$ and $0$. In the displayed symplectic bases both quadratic forms have $q(a)=q(b)=1$, so both Arf invariants are $1$. Their normalized Conway polynomials are $1+z^2$ and $1-z^2$, respectively.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC and the two displayed oriented knot Seifert matrices in the positive-push convention.

[A1] Full AC is the ambient hypothesis for the Seifert pairing. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] The trefoil matrix $V_T$ is the positive-push matrix for the positive trefoil. [[ex-knot-kt-07-worked-cases]]

[F2] The figure-eight matrix $V_F$ is a positive-push Seifert matrix; its skew part is the standard symplectic block. [[def-knot-seifert-pairing-and-matrix]], [[lem-seifert-matrix-skew-part-is-surface-intersection]]

[F3] The Arf invariant is $q(a)q(b)$ for a genus-one symplectic basis and equals $a_2$ modulo two. [[def-knot-arf-invariant-from-seifert-form]], [[thm-arf-equals-second-conway-coefficient-mod-two]]

[F4] For a Seifert matrix $V$, the determinant substitution gives the normalized Conway polynomial $D_K(u)=\det(uV-u^{-1}V^T)=\nabla_K(u-u^{-1})$. [[lem-conway-polynomial-from-seifert-determinant]]

[F5] The Levine–Tristram signature of the knot is independent of the chosen surface and basis, including the one-sided-average value at an Alexander root. [[lem-seifert-stabilization-preserves-levine-tristram-signature]]

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the oriented $3$-sphere, let $N(K)$ be a chosen closed tubular solid-torus neighborhood, let $E_K=\overline{S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)}$, and let $T_K=\partial E_K=\partial N(K)$. Let $\mu$ be the positive oriented meridian, meaning the boundary of a positive normal disk in $N(K)$, and let $\lambda$ be a preferred longitude, meaning a degree-one parallel of the core $K$ in $N(K)$ that is null-homologous in $E_K$. Assume that $[\mu],[\lambda]$ are an ordered basis of $H_1(T_K;\mathbb Z)$, with the boundary-orientation convention $\mu\cdot\lambda=-1$. A slope is the unoriented isotopy class of an essential simple closed curve on $T_K$ whose homology class is $p[\mu]+q[\lambda]$ for coprime integers $p,q$ not both zero; $(p,q)$ and $(-p,-q)$ represent the same slope. For a slope represented by $p[\mu]+q[\lambda]$, the Dehn filling $E_K(p/q)$ is obtained by gluing an oriented solid torus $D^2\times S^1$ to $E_K$ by an orientation-reversing boundary homeomorphism that sends $[\partial D^2\times\{1\}]$ to that slope; the filled orientation agrees with the fixed orientation on $E_K$. If $q\ne0$, the coefficient is written $p/q$; the meridional slope is $1/0$, and integer $n$-framed filling means slope $n[\mu]+[\lambda]$. The oriented homeomorphism type is independent of the gluing map once its meridian image is fixed.

facts:
**Given:** A marked oriented knot exterior $(E_K,T_K,\mu,\lambda)$ satisfying the hypotheses in Definition, and two orientation-reversing gluing maps with the same unoriented meridian slope.

[A1] $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is the stated axiom [[def-countable-choice]]. The marked data include the chosen exterior [[def-knot-exterior]], its boundary torus, and the meridian–preferred-longitude basis [[def-knot-meridian-and-preferred-longitude]]. The batch-57 definitions specify this interface; the basis is an explicit hypothesis here, not an assertion that those definitions prove its existence.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the oriented $3$-sphere with a chosen connected exterior $E_K$ and boundary torus $T_K$. Let $(\mu,\lambda)$ be its positive meridian and preferred longitude, assume $([\mu],[\lambda])$ is a basis of $H_1(T_K;\mathbb Z)$, and assume $[\mu]$ generates $H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)$ and $[\lambda]=0$. For coprime integers $p,q$ not both zero, let $E_K(p/q)$ be the filling whose attached solid-torus meridian maps to $p[\mu]+q[\lambda]$. Then
$$H_1(E_K(p/q);\mathbb Z)\cong\begin{cases}\mathbb Z/|p|\mathbb Z,&p\ne0,\\[2pt]\mathbb Z,&p=0.\end{cases}$$

facts:
**Given:** A smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$, its exterior $E_K$, tubular neighborhood $N(K)$, boundary torus $T_K$, meridian $\mu$, preferred longitude $\lambda$, and coprime integers $p,q$ not both zero.

[F1] [[thm-mayer-vietoris-sequence-in-singular-homology]]: for an open cover $X=U\cup V$, the singular-homology Mayer–Vietoris sequence is exact.

[F2] [[cor-homology-of-spheres]]: for $n\ge1$, the reduced singular homology of $S^n$ is $\mathbb Z$ in degree $n$ and zero in all other degrees; in particular $H_1(S^3;\mathbb Z)=H_2(S^3;\mathbb Z)=0$ and $H_1(S^1;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z$.

[F3] [[ex-mayer-vietoris-computation-of-the-torus-first-homology]]: $H_1(T^2;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z\oplus\mathbb Z$, generated by the two factor circles.

[F4] [[prop-singular-homology-is-invariant-under-deformation-retracts]]: a deformation-retract inclusion induces an isomorphism on singular homology.

[F5] [[def-oriented-slope-and-knot-dehn-filling]]: the filling glues a solid torus to $E_K$ with its meridian identified with the class $p[\mu]+q[\lambda]$.

[A1] $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is the stated axiom [[def-countable-choice]]. The chosen meridian bounds a disk in $N(K)$ and the degree-one preferred longitude maps to a generator of $H_1(N(K);\mathbb Z)$ [[def-knot-meridian-and-preferred-longitude]]. These are the batch-57 peripheral definitions' hypotheses; their bodies are present and were checked. This argument assumes the exterior generator and longitude-zero conditions stated above and does not invoke the separate full-AC exterior-homology theorem.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the oriented $3$-sphere with a chosen exterior $E_K$ and peripheral basis $(\mu,\lambda)$, where $\lambda$ is preferred. For $n\in\mathbb Z$, attach one smooth $4$-dimensional $2$-handle $D^2\times D^2$ to the $4$-ball $B^4$ along $S^1\times D^2$ in $\partial B^4=S^3$ by the standard orientation-compatible handle attachment, using a product framing whose attaching parallel on $\partial E_K$ has slope $n[\mu]+[\lambda]$. Denote the resulting oriented trace by $X_n(K)$. After rounding corners, its oriented boundary is the filling $E_K(n/1)$. This theorem covers integer framings only: a rational $p/q$ filling has a trace only after specifying an integral continued-fraction handle chain or a separately defined rational-surgery cobordism; an arbitrary rational coefficient is not the framing of a single smooth $2$-handle.

facts:
**Given:** The oriented $4$-ball, a framed attaching knot $K\subset S^3$, the specified product identification of its tubular neighborhood, and the slope convention for $E_K(n/1)$.

[F1] [[def-oriented-slope-and-knot-dehn-filling]]: the filling replaces the knot neighborhood by $D^2\times S^1$ whose meridian maps to $n[\mu]+[\lambda]$, and its orientation agrees with the exterior orientation.

[A1] $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is included for the chosen exterior and peripheral-system interface [[def-countable-choice]]. The product framing is part of the handle-attachment data; after those data are supplied, the boundary decomposition makes no further choice.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $T$ be the closure of the positive geometric two-strand braid $\sigma_1^3$, with orientation given by increasing braid parameter. In the chart $(x,y,t)$ with ambient orientation $(x,y,t)$, view along $+y$, put increasing $t$ downward, and orient the projection plane by $(\partial_t,\partial_x)$. The right-starting strand passes over the left-starting strand at each positive crossing. Let $E_T$ be its chosen exterior. For the positive meridian $\mu=a$ at the first left arc and the preferred degree-one longitude $\lambda$, the fundamental group of $+1$ filling, with slope $[\mu]+[\lambda]$, has presentation
$$\pi_1(E_T(1/1))\cong\langle a,b\mid aba=bab,\;bab^{-1}aba^{-2}=1\rangle.$$
In these based coordinates the blackboard parallel is $w=bac$ with $c=b^{-1}ab$, and
$$w a^3=(ab)^3,\qquad\lambda=w a^{-3}=(ab)^3a^{-6}.$$
Thus the same filling relation is $(ab)^3=a^5$. In particular the positive trefoil and the sign of the filling are both fixed; no mirror substitution is implicit.

facts:
**Given:** The fixed positive braid, its oriented closure, the chosen exterior, and $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$.

[F1] In the positive elementary motion the left point travels below the midpoint and the right point above. The closure identifies equal disk positions at the ends and follows increasing parameter. [[def-elementary-geometric-half-twist]], [[prop-stacking-of-geometric-braids-is-well-defined]], [[def-closure-of-a-geometric-braid]]

[F2] In the designated viewing chart the crossing sign is the determinant sign of the over and under tangents in coordinates $(t,x)$. [[def-oriented-crossing-sign-writhe-and-blackboard-framing]]

[F3] With common upper-collar basing paths, positive meridians satisfy $g_{\rm out}=g_o^{-1}g_{\rm in}g_o$ when the under-tangent follows the positive over-normal; the Wirtinger meridian map is an isomorphism. [[lem-wirtinger-local-meridian-conjugacy]], [[thm-knot-wirtinger-presentation-correctness]]

[F4] Blackboard self-linking equals self-writhe. [[thm-blackboard-framing-self-linking-is-writhe]], [[def-framed-knot-self-linking-and-seifert-framing]]

[F5] The degree-one preferred longitude has zero image in exterior first homology. The positive meridian is the normal-disk boundary. [[def-knot-meridian-and-preferred-longitude]]

[F6] First homology is the abelianization of the fundamental group. [[prop-the-first-hurewicz-map-in-degree-one-is-abelianization]]

[F7] Filling kills the specified primitive boundary slope, by the open-collar van Kampen pushout. [[def-oriented-slope-and-knot-dehn-filling]], [[thm-seifert-van-kampen]]

contract.heading: Statement refuted
contract.text: Every connected closed oriented $3$-manifold $M$ with $H_1(M;\mathbb Z)=0$ is simply connected, meaning that $\pi_1(M)$ is trivial.

[F2] [[lem-trefoil-plus-one-surgery-group-presentation]]: $\pi_1(M)$ has presentation $\langle a,b\mid aba=bab,\;bab^{-1}aba^{-2}=1\rangle$.

[F3] [[def-oriented-slope-and-knot-dehn-filling]]: filling glues an oriented solid torus to the knot exterior along the specified meridian slope.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Choice. It supplies countable choice for the chosen tubular data: for any sequence of nonempty sets, apply full choice to its range and compose with the index map. Let $L=\bigcup_{i\in I}K_i$ be a finite oriented link in the standard oriented $3$-sphere, where $I$ is a finite index set. For each component $K_i$, include a chosen closed tubular neighbourhood $N(K_i)$, its exterior $E_{K_i}=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K_i)$, the positive meridian $\mu_i$, and the preferred longitude $\lambda_i$; the longitude is the degree-one parallel class in $H_1(\partial E_{K_i};\mathbb Z)$ that maps to zero in $H_1(E_{K_i};\mathbb Z)$. For each $i\in I$, choose an integer $n_i$. The resulting **integral framed-link surgery diagram** is this link and integer family, with the surgery result defined by removing the interiors of all $N(K_i)$ and gluing an oriented solid torus to each boundary torus so that its meridian maps to $n_i[\mu_i]+[\lambda_i]$. If $I=\varnothing$, the surgery result is $S^3$. A diagram is considered up to orientation-preserving ambient isotopy carrying each component framing; a planar projection is only a way of drawing the link.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Choice. If two integral framed-link surgery diagrams are related by one ambient isotopy, handle slide, or split $\pm1$-unknot stabilization or destabilization as defined for this page, then their oriented surgery results are orientation-preservingly diffeomorphic. The same holds for any finite sequence of these moves.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, two integral framed-link diagrams, and one allowed Kirby move between them.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: every family of nonempty sets has a choice function. Applying it to the range of any sequence of nonempty sets gives the countable-choice axiom required by the framed handle-slide and surgery-trace interfaces.

[F1] [[def-integral-framed-link-surgery-diagram]]: component $K_i$ is filled with a solid torus whose meridian maps to $n_i[\mu_i]+[\lambda_i]$.

[F2] [[def-kirby-moves-on-integral-framed-links]]: a handle slide replaces a component by the band sum with a framed parallel of another component, and stabilization adds or removes a split unknot with coefficient $+1$ or $-1$.

[F3] [[def-handle-slide-of-one-k-handle-over-another]]: the slid attaching sphere is the band sum of the first attaching sphere with a signed framed parallel copy of the second, with the full framing carried across the band.

[F4] [[lem-handle-slides-preserve-the-relative-diffeomorphism-type]]: for $1\le k\le n-2$, a handle slide gives a diffeomorphism of the handle attachments relative to the incoming boundary.

[F5] [[def-surgery-trace-cobordism]]: a framed surgery trace is the cylinder with a handle attached along the framed sphere.

[F6] [[thm-upper-boundary-of-the-surgery-trace-is-the-surged-manifold]]: the outgoing face of a framed surgery trace is the corresponding surgered manifold, with compatible orientation.

[F7] [[def-oriented-slope-and-knot-dehn-filling]]: the integer $r$ filling slope is $r[\mu]+[\lambda]$.

[F8] [[def-countable-choice]]: $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ says that every sequence of nonempty sets $(X_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ has a choice function $f$ with $f(n)\in X_n$.
scope: Literal contract/Facts extraction only; accepted proof body not inspected.

contract.heading: Example
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Choice. The empty integral surgery diagram gives the standard oriented $S^3$. Surgery on the standard unknot with framing $0$ gives $S^1\times S^2$. For every integer $p>0$, surgery on the standard unknot with framing $p$ gives the oriented lens space $L(p,1)$ in the convention $L(p,q)=E_U(p/q)$.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, the empty link, and the standard oriented unknot $U(t)=(e^{2\pi i t},0)$ in $S^3\subset\mathbb C^2$.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: every family of nonempty sets has a choice function; full AC also supplies the countable-choice hypotheses in the chosen tubular data.

[A2] [[def-countable-choice]]: $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ says that every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function.

[F1] [[def-integral-framed-link-surgery-diagram]]: each component with integer $n$ is filled along $n[\mu]+[\lambda]$, and the empty link has surgery result $S^3$.

[F2] [[def-oriented-slope-and-knot-dehn-filling]]: the integer $n$ filling attaches a solid torus whose meridian maps to $n[\mu_U]+[\lambda_U]$.

[F3] [[def-lens-space-surgery-orientation-convention]]: for $p>0$, $L(p,q)$ is the oriented filling of the unknot exterior with meridian slope $p[\mu_U]+q[\lambda_U]$.

[F4] [[def-knot-meridian-and-preferred-longitude]]: a preferred longitude is a degree-one parallel curve whose homology class maps to zero in the chosen exterior.

[F5] [[thm-knot-exterior-homology-and-longitude]]: under full AC the positive meridian and unique preferred longitude form the peripheral basis of the unknot exterior.

contract.heading: Statement refuted
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice.

The false claim is that if two integral framed-link surgery diagrams in $S^3$ have orientation-preservingly diffeomorphic surgery results, then the framed links are ambient isotopic.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, the empty surgery diagram $D_0$, and the diagram $D_1$ consisting of a single $+1$-framed standard unknot.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: every family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

[A2] [[def-countable-choice]]: $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ says that every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function. Full AC [A1] implies this by applying its choice function to the range of the sequence and composing with the index map.

[F1] [[def-integral-framed-link-surgery-diagram]]: the empty diagram has surgery result $S^3$, and the integer $n$ filling uses meridian slope $n[\mu]+[\lambda]$.

[F2] [[def-knot-meridian-and-preferred-longitude]]: $\mu$ is the positive meridian and $\lambda$ is the degree-one preferred longitude that maps to zero in the knot exterior.

[F3] [[thm-knot-exterior-homology-and-longitude]]: under full AC the preferred longitude is the unique degree-one class in the kernel of the exterior inclusion.

[F4] [[def-kirby-moves-on-integral-framed-links]]: adding a split $+1$-framed unknot is a Kirby stabilization.

[F5] [[def-oriented-link-in-s-three-and-ambient-isotopy]]: ambient isotopy identifies links by a diffeomorphism of their component domains, so it preserves the number of components.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Identify the standard oriented three-sphere with $S^3=\{(z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb C^2:|z_1|^2+|z_2|^2=1\}$ and choose $0<r<1$. The standard unknotted Heegaard torus is $T_r=\{|z_1|=r,\ |z_2|=\sqrt{1-r^2}\}$; its two sides are solid tori. In the angular coordinates $(u,v)\in(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^2$ given by $(u,v)\mapsto(r e^{2\pi i u},\sqrt{1-r^2}e^{2\pi i v})$, let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be the first and second coordinate classes in $H_1(T_r;\mathbb Z)$. For coprime nonzero integers $p,q$, the **oriented torus knot** $T(p,q)$ is the image of $s\mapsto(r e^{2\pi i p s},\sqrt{1-r^2}e^{2\pi i q s})$, for $s\in\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$, oriented by increasing $s$; it represents the primitive slope $p\alpha+q\beta$. The mirror convention is the reflection $(z_1,z_2)\mapsto(z_1,\overline{z_2})$, which sends $T(p,q)$ to $T(p,-q)$ with image orientation, and reversing the knot orientation gives $T(-p,-q)$. For nonzero $p,q$ with $d=\gcd(|p|,|q|)>1$, the corresponding torus link is the union of $d$ disjoint parallel copies of the primitive slope $(p/d,q/d)$; it is not a single embedded curve of class $p\alpha+q\beta$. The exterior is $E_K=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$ for a chosen closed tubular neighborhood. A positive meridian is the oriented boundary of a normal disk, and a preferred longitude is a degree-one class on $\partial E_K$ whose image in $H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)$ is zero; this definition alone asserts neither existence nor uniqueness.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. If $p,q$ are coprime nonzero integers and $|p|=1$ or $|q|=1$, then the oriented torus knot $T(p,q)$ is ambient isotopic in $S^3$ to the standard unknot with its standard orientation.

facts:
**Given:** Countable Choice, coprime nonzero integers $p,q$, and $|p|=1$ or $|q|=1$.

[F1] [[def-coprime-torus-knot]] realizes $T(p,q)$ as the primitive slope curve on the standard Heegaard torus, with the two coordinate circles bounding disks on opposite sides.

[F2] [[def-knot-connected-sum-and-prime-knot]] fixes the standard unknot as the standard oriented unit circle and uses orientation-preserving ambient isotopy for knot equivalence.

[F3] [[thm-isotopy-extension]] extends a smooth isotopy of a compact embedded circle to an ambient isotopy of the surrounding smooth manifold.

[A1] Countable Choice is the hypothesis of the torus-knot, unknot, and isotopy-extension interfaces ([[def-countable-choice]]).

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $p,q\ge2$ be coprime integers. There is a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface $F_{p,q}\subset S^3$ whose oriented boundary is $T(p,q)$ and whose genus is $(p-1)(q-1)/2$. It can be constructed from a disk by plumbing $(p-1)(q-1)$ positive Hopf bands: a positive Hopf band is the oriented annulus spanning the positively linked Hopf link, and plumbing along a square glues square neighborhoods of properly embedded arcs in two surfaces on opposite sides of a 3-ball, with the four boundary edges alternating between the surfaces and with orientations agreeing on the square. For a connected compact oriented surface with one boundary component, genus is defined by $\chi(F)=1-2g(F)$.

facts:
**Given:** Countable Choice and coprime integers $p,q\ge2$.

[A1] Countable Choice is the choice-function principle for sequences of nonempty sets ([[def-countable-choice]]).

[F1] [[def-coprime-torus-knot]] parameterizes $T(p,q)$ on the standard Heegaard torus by the primitive slope $p\alpha+q\beta$.

[F2] [[def-oriented-seifert-surface]] defines a Seifert surface as a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface with the knot as its oriented boundary, and gives $\chi(F)=1-2g(F)$ for a one-boundary-component surface.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $p,q$ be coprime nonzero integers, let $K=T(p,q)$ be the oriented primitive slope curve in the standard Heegaard torus, and let $\rho_t(z_1,z_2)=(e^{2\pi i p t}z_1,e^{2\pi i q t}z_2)$ be the weighted circle action on the unit $S^3\subset\mathbb C^2$. Choose $N(K)$ to be a sufficiently small closed metric tube around the orbit $K$ for the round metric; this tube is invariant because $\rho_t$ is isometric and preserves $K$. Set $E_K=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$. Let $x$ and $y$ be based generators of the fundamental groups of the two solid-torus pieces obtained by cutting $E_K$ along the annulus left on the Heegaard torus, oriented so that the annulus core maps to $x^p$ and $y^q$. Then

$$\pi_1(E_K)=\langle x,y\mid x^p=y^q\rangle.$$

The common element $h=x^p=y^q$ is central and represents a regular fiber of a Seifert fibration of $E_K$ over a disk. The fibration has two distinguished core fibers of multiplicities $|p|$ and $|q|$; a fiber of multiplicity one is regular, and a fiber of multiplicity greater than one is exceptional. Thus there are exactly two exceptional fibers when $|p|,|q|>1$, and one is regular when one absolute parameter is $1$.

For any integers $\alpha,\beta$ with $p\alpha+q\beta=1$, compatible based paths identify the positive normal-disk meridian and preferred longitude in the peripheral system as

$$\mu=y^\alpha x^\beta,\qquad \lambda=h\mu^{-pq}.$$

Here the positive meridian is the oriented boundary of a normal disk, and the preferred longitude has degree one around $K$ and maps to zero in $H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)$. Their homology classes form a basis of $H_1(\partial E_K;\mathbb Z)$, so both classes are primitive.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, coprime nonzero integers $p,q$, the chosen knot exterior and based paths, and the specified Heegaard torus.

[A1] Full AC is the axiom that every family of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

[L1] Full AC implies the Axiom of Countable Choice, which is the hypothesis of the exterior and peripheral-system definitions ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]).

[F1] [[def-coprime-torus-knot]] identifies $K$ with the oriented primitive slope $p\alpha+q\beta$ on the standard unknotted Heegaard torus.

[F2] [[def-knot-exterior]] sets $E_K=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$ with its boundary torus, and [[def-knot-meridian-and-preferred-longitude]] defines the positive meridian by the normal-disk boundary and the preferred longitude by degree one and zero exterior homology.

[F3] Under full AC, [[thm-knot-exterior-homology-and-longitude]] proves $H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z$ generated by the positive meridian, proves existence and uniqueness of the preferred-longitude class, and proves that their boundary classes form a basis of $H_1(\partial E_K;\mathbb Z)$.

[F4] [[thm-seifert-van-kampen]] identifies the fundamental group of a union from a path-connected open cover with the pushout of the two inclusion-induced maps from the intersection.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $p,q$ be coprime nonzero integers and let $K=T(p,q)$. Choose generators $x,y$ for the two-generator presentation $\pi_1(E_K)=\langle x,y\mid x^p=y^q\rangle$. Let $P_{p,q}$ be the two-dimensional presentation complex with one vertex, oriented edges $x,y$, and one two-cell attached along $r=x^py^{-q}$. The assignment $\phi(x)=q$, $\phi(y)=p$ defines an epimorphism $\phi:\pi_1(P_{p,q})\to\mathbb Z$; let $\widetilde P_\phi$ be its connected cyclic cover classified by $\ker\phi$. Let $A_K=H_1(\widetilde{S^3\setminus K};\mathbb Z)$ be the one-variable Alexander module for the infinite cyclic cover classified by total linking, with $t$ acting by the deck transformation of the positive meridian. Put $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$ and define
$$\delta_{p,q}(t)=\frac{(t^{pq}-1)(t-1)}{(t^p-1)(t^q-1)}.$$
Then $\delta_{p,q}(t)$ is a Laurent polynomial, $A_K\cong\Lambda/(\delta_{p,q})$, and the Alexander polynomial $\Delta_K$, defined as a generator of the zeroth elementary ideal $E_0(A_K)$, satisfies $\Delta_K(t)\doteq\delta_{p,q}(t)$, where $f\doteq g$ means $f=\pm t^k g$ for some integer $k$.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, coprime nonzero integers $p,q$, the torus knot $K=T(p,q)$, its exterior, and the total-linking cover.

[A1] Full AC is the choice-function axiom used by the one-variable Alexander-module and polynomial definitions ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

[L1] Full AC implies Countable Choice, the hypothesis of the tubular-exterior retraction supplier ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]).

[F1] [[thm-torus-knot-group-presentation]] gives $\pi_1(E_K)=\langle x,y\mid x^p=y^q\rangle$ and a positive meridian $\mu=y^\alpha x^\beta$ with $p\alpha+q\beta=1$.

[F2] [[thm-knot-exterior-homology-and-longitude]] says $H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)$ is generated by $[\mu]$ and the positive meridian maps to $1$ in total linking.

[F3] [[lem-knot-tubular-exterior-and-boundary]] says the open complement $S^3\setminus K$ strongly deformation retracts onto the compact exterior $E_K$.

[F4] [[def-one-variable-alexander-module-of-an-oriented-link]] defines $A_K$ as the first homology of the connected infinite cyclic cover with positive meridian deck action.

[F5] [[thm-cellular-homology-computes-singular-homology]] identifies cellular-chain homology with singular homology, and [[prop-the-first-hurewicz-map-in-degree-one-is-abelianization]] identifies first homology with the abelianization of the fundamental group.

[F6] [[def-elementary-ideals-of-a-finitely-presented-module]] defines $E_0$ by the maximal minors of a presentation matrix, [[def-alexander-polynomial-from-the-first-elementary-ideal]] defines $\Delta_K$ as its gcd generator up to units $\pm t^k$, and [[lem-the-laurent-polynomial-ring-is-noetherian-and-a-unique-factorisation-domain]] supplies unique factorization in $\Lambda$.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $p,q$ be coprime nonzero integers, let $K=T(p,q)$, and put $a=|p|$, $b=|q|$. For $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$, define
$$\delta_{a,b}(t)=\frac{(t^{ab}-1)(t-1)}{(t^a-1)(t^b-1)}.$$
Then $\delta_{a,b}(t)$ is a polynomial in $\mathbb Z[t]$, the Alexander polynomial $\Delta_K$ defined as a generator of the zeroth elementary ideal of the positive-meridian infinite-cyclic-cover module satisfies $\Delta_K(t)\doteq\delta_{a,b}(t)$, and the knot genus is $g(K)=(a-1)(b-1)/2$. Here $f\doteq g$ means $f=\pm t^k g$ for some integer $k$.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, coprime nonzero integers $p,q$, and $K=T(p,q)$.

[A1] Full AC means every family of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

[L1] Full AC implies Countable Choice, the hypothesis of the spanning-surface and genus definitions ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]).

[F1] [[def-coprime-torus-knot]] defines the oriented primitive-slope knot $T(p,q)$ and identifies sign changes with the stated mirror and orientation conventions.

[F2] [[thm-torus-knot-group-presentation]] gives $\pi_1(E_K)=\langle x,y\mid x^p=y^q\rangle$ with the positive meridian word determined by $p\alpha+q\beta=1$.

[F3] [[lem-torus-knot-alexander-polynomial-from-presentation]] proves that the positive-meridian Alexander module is cyclic with order $\delta_{p,q}(t)=(t^{pq}-1)(t-1)/((t^p-1)(t^q-1))$, a Laurent polynomial, and hence $\Delta_K\doteq\delta_{p,q}$.

[F4] [[lem-torus-knot-unit-slope-is-unknot]] says $T(p,q)$ is ambient isotopic to the standard unknot whenever $|p|=1$ or $|q|=1$.

[F5] [[lem-torus-knot-sign-changes-give-mirror-or-reversal]] identifies the mirror and reversed-orientation curves obtained by changing parameter signs; [[lem-knot-genus-invariant-under-mirror-and-reversal]] proves that these operations preserve genus.

[F6] [[lem-positive-torus-knot-hopf-plumbing-surface]] constructs a positive Hopf-plumbed Seifert surface of genus $(a-1)(b-1)/2$ for $T(a,b)$ when $a,b\ge2$.

[F7] [[def-oriented-seifert-surface-and-knot-genus]] defines $g(K)$ as the minimum genus of a connected compact oriented spanning surface under Countable Choice.

[F8] [[thm-seifert-determinant-is-the-knot-alexander-polynomial]] identifies the Alexander polynomial with the Seifert determinant under the positive-push convention; [[cor-knot-alexander-normalization-symmetry-and-genus-bound]] gives $\operatorname{width}(\Delta_K)\le2g(K)$.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text: Let $V=S^1\times D^2$ be the standard oriented solid torus, with oriented core $S^1\times\{0\}$. A **pattern** is a smooth oriented knot $P$ contained in the interior of $V$, together with a chosen closed tubular neighbourhood $N(P)$ contained in the interior of $V$. Its **winding number** $w(P)$ is the integer by which the homology class $[P]$ maps to $H_1(V;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z$ under the isomorphism that sends the oriented core to $1$. The **pattern exterior** is $X_P=V\setminus\operatorname{int}N(P)$; its **outer torus** is $\partial V$ and its **inner torus** is $\partial N(P)$. A **companion** is a smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$ with a specified orientation-preserving tubular embedding $e:V\to S^3$ that sends the core to $K$ and identifies the solid-torus meridian and product longitude with the positive meridian and preferred longitude of $K$. The **satellite knot** $P(K)$ is $e(P)$, with chosen exterior $E_{P(K)}=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}e(N(P))$; the image $e(\partial V)$ is its **companion torus**. The outer torus is **incompressible** when it bounds no properly embedded disk in $X_P$ with essential boundary on $\partial V$. It is **product-parallel** to the inner torus when $X_P$ is a product $T^2\times[0,1]$ with those tori as its ends. This definition alone asserts neither incompressibility nor essentiality of the companion torus.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text: Let $M$ be a compact smooth $3$-manifold. A properly embedded surface is **two-sided** if it has a product neighbourhood $F\times[-1,1]$ in $M$. A **compressing disk** for a two-sided surface $F$ is an embedded disk $D\subset M$ with $\operatorname{int}(D)\cap F=\varnothing$ and $\partial D$ an essential simple closed curve in $F$; $F$ is **incompressible** if it has no compressing disk. A **boundary-compressing disk** is an embedded disk $D$ with $\partial D=\alpha\cup\beta$, where $\alpha=D\cap F$ is an arc not cutting off a disk in $F$, $\beta=D\cap\partial M$, and $\operatorname{int}(D)$ misses $F\cup\partial M$; $F$ is **boundary-incompressible** if it has no such disk. A surface is **boundary-parallel** if it cobounds a product with a subsurface of $\partial M$, and it is **essential** if it is incompressible, boundary-incompressible, and not boundary-parallel. $M$ is **irreducible** if every embedded $2$-sphere in its interior bounds an embedded $3$-ball in $M$. An incompressible torus is boundary-parallel if it cobounds a product $T^2\times[0,1]$ with a component of $\partial M$; $M$ is **atoroidal** if every incompressible torus is boundary-parallel. A **Seifert fibration** is a decomposition into circles with local models given by fibered solid tori; in the model $(D^2\times S^1)/\langle(z,w)\mapsto(e^{2\pi i/q}z,e^{2\pi ip/q}w)\rangle$, where $\gcd(p,q)=1$, the core fiber has multiplicity $q$. Fibers of multiplicity $1$ are **regular** and those of multiplicity greater than $1$ are **exceptional**. A finite family of pairwise disjoint incompressible tori is a **JSJ system** if every component obtained by cutting $M$ along the family is atoroidal or Seifert-fibered. It is **inclusion-minimal** if no proper subfamily is a JSJ system. Atoroidal does not mean hyperbolic.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $M$ be a compact connected orientable piecewise linear three-manifold with a given finite compatible manifold triangulation and with boundary a subcomplex. Let $F\subset\partial M$ be a connected compact piecewise linear subsurface and $N\trianglelefteq\pi_1(F)$ a normal subgroup. Suppose there is a continuous map $f:(D^2,\partial D^2)\to(M,F)$ whose boundary lies in the relative interior of $F$ and has class outside $N$. Then there is a properly embedded piecewise linear disk in $M$, with boundary in the relative interior of $F$, whose boundary class is outside $N$.

In particular, if a connected boundary component has noninjective induced fundamental-group map into $M$, it contains an essential simple closed curve bounding a properly embedded piecewise linear disk in $M$. Boundary classes outside $N$ are understood up to conjugation by a basepath in $F$.

facts:
**Given:** $M,F,N,f$ as in the Statement.

[F1] Continuous maps of finite polyhedral pairs admit simplicial approximations homotopic as maps of pairs; PL maps admit compatible finite subdivisions ([[thm-finite-simplicial-approximation-for-maps-of-pairs]]).

[F2] A finite subpolyhedron in a finitely triangulated PL three-manifold has a compact PL manifold neighborhood strongly retracting onto it, with controlled trace in a marked boundary subsurface ([[lem-finite-subpolyhedra-have-compact-pl-manifold-neighborhoods]]).

[F3] Compact locally collared PL subpolyhedra have PL collars; in particular this applies to the boundary of a compact PL manifold and to boundary curves of a compact PL surface ([[lem-compact-locally-collared-pl-subpolyhedron-has-pl-collar]]).

[F4] A disk map lifts to any covering after fixing its initial lift ([[thm-covering-space-lifting-criterion]]). Pulling back finitely many triangulation simplices gives a finite compatible PL structure on a twofold cover. Its deck involution sends each point to the other point in the same fiber; its continuity follows by interchanging the two sheets on every evenly covered neighborhood. It has no fixed point.

[F5] If a compact connected orientable finite PL three-manifold has no connected twofold cover, its boundary components are PL spheres. This has a local proof using explicit twofold covers from finite edge cocycles, dual-cell boundary matrices, finite pivots, and finite polygonal surface reduction, with no choice assumption ([[lem-no-twofold-cover-forces-spherical-boundary-in-finite-pl-three-manifold]]).

[F6] On a PL two-sphere, a simple polygonal circle bounds polygonal disks on its two sides. Finite polygonal disk parametrizations and their boundary extensions are supplied by [[lem-finite-polygonal-disk-and-collar-surgery]] after using a standard two-disk sphere model. A connected compact subsurface is planar; its finitely many boundary components bound the complementary disk regions, as follows by applying the same polygonal separation successively.

[F7] A proper PL disk immersion with only regular double arcs and circles and no values of multiplicity greater than two has an essential embedded disk with respect to any prescribed normal boundary subgroup ([[lem-two-sheeted-pl-disk-immersion-has-essential-embedded-disk]]).

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume full AC. Let $V=S^1\times D^2$ be a solid torus. Every connected, two-sided, properly embedded incompressible and boundary-incompressible surface $F\subset V$ with nonempty boundary is a disk, either a meridian disk or a boundary-parallel disk. In particular, if $F$ is not boundary-parallel, it is a meridian disk. Any two smooth meridian disks with the same boundary admit a smooth isotopy of embeddings relative to that boundary, with a boundary-fixing topological ambient extension. If both disks are neat, this can be a smooth ambient isotopy relative to the boundary. In addition, every two-sided embedded torus $T\subset\operatorname{int}V$ has a compressing disk in $V$.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, the standard smooth solid torus $V$, the connected two-sided proper surface $F$ with nonempty boundary and the two disk-obstruction hypotheses; and, for the last assertion, an embedded two-sided torus $T$ in its interior.

[A1] Full AC is [[def-axiom-of-choice]] and implies countable choice ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]], Statement; [[def-countable-choice]]).

[F1] The disk obstructions and product definition of boundary-parallelity are [[def-incompressibility-seifert-fibration-and-jsj-system]], Definition.

[F2] Every smooth sphere in $S^3$ bounds smooth balls on both sides ([[thm-smooth-schoenflies-for-embedded-two-sphere-in-s-three]], Statement).

[F3] A smooth sphere boundary map extends over parametrized balls, as a product in their smaller boundary collars ([[lem-smooth-sphere-diffeomorphisms-extend-over-balls]], Statement). Smooth disk boundary maps extend retaining prescribed collars ([[lem-smooth-jordan-disk-boundary-maps-extend-to-diffeomorphisms]], Statement).

[F4] Essential torus circles in the same primitive class admit smooth finite bigon reductions and parallel-strip parameters ([[lem-relative-smooth-mapping-classes-of-annulus-and-torus]], Proof 1.1–2.1). Disk pushes across a ball have a smooth cap sweep with fixed boundary circle, explicitly parametrized in [[lem-gluing-irreducible-smooth-three-manifolds-across-injective-annuli]], Proof 3.1.

[F5] Finite relative general position and smooth ambient extension are [[lem-relative-transversality-for-embedded-surfaces]] and [[thm-isotopy-extension]], Statements.

[F6] For a compact two-sided neat surface in a compact orientable smooth three-manifold, geometric incompressibility is equivalent to injectivity on fundamental groups ([[thm-smooth-loop-theorem-and-incompressibility-criterion-in-orientable-three-manifolds]], Statement).

[F9] Boundary-fixed smooth embedding neatification, its explicit topological ambient extension and the smooth disk-obstruction transport retain both classification hypotheses. A neat input admits a smooth ambient extension; a broad input has only the stated topological ambient extension at its original tangencies. [[lem-compact-smooth-boundary-preimage-surfaces-admit-neat-embedding-isotopies]] [[lem-angular-boundary-neatification-preserves-smooth-disk-obstructions]]

[F10] Full AC gives a finite PL triangulation of every compact TOP cut piece, with its entire boundary triangulated. The finite PL Loop theorem applies to a connected boundary component with nontrivial inclusion kernel; transporting its proper disk through that triangulation gives a TOP disk in the original piece. [[thm-compact-topological-three-manifolds-admit-finite-pl-triangulations]] [[thm-loop-theorem-for-finitely-triangulated-orientable-pl-three-manifolds]]

[F11] Connected-overlap van Kampen and amalgam normal form embed an injected common torus group. For a connected cut piece with two faces, the same collar van Kampen calculation gives the HNN presentation; its normal form embeds the vertex group and its associated subgroups, with transversals supplied by full AC. The torus group is $\mathbb Z^2$ and the standard solid-torus group is $\mathbb Z$. contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $F$ be a compact smooth surface with boundary, let $M$ be a smooth three-manifold without boundary, and let $S\subset M$ be a closed embedded smooth surface. If $i:F\to M$ is a smooth embedding whose boundary restriction $i|_{\partial F}$ is transverse to $S$, then there is a smooth isotopy $i_t:F\to M$ through embeddings, fixed on a neighbourhood of $\partial F$, such that $i_1(F)$ is transverse to $S$.

facts:
**Given:** AC$_\omega$, a compact smooth surface with boundary $F$, a smooth three-manifold $M$, a closed embedded surface $S\subset M$, and an embedding $i:F\to M$ with $i|_{\partial F}\pitchfork S$.

[F1] For a smooth map from a boundaryless manifold to a boundaryless target, there is a finite-dimensional smooth perturbation family through that map whose parameter map is a submersion at every source point. ([[lem-a-tubular-target-produces-a-submersive-finite-dimensional-perturbation-family]])

[F2] If a smooth family $G:X\times B\to M$ is transverse to $S$, then the parameters for which the slice $G_a:X\to M$ is not transverse to $S$ form a null subset of $B$. ([[thm-parametric-transversality]])

[F3] Every smooth manifold with boundary has a smooth collar. ([[thm-collar-neighborhood-theorem]])

[F4] Under AC$_\omega$, every smooth isotopy of embeddings of a compact source with boundary into a boundaryless target extends to an ambient isotopy. ([[thm-isotopy-extension]])

[F5] A smooth map transverse to an embedded submanifold has the tangent-space spanning property in the transversality definition; invertible differentials give local diffeomorphisms in charts. ([[def-a-smooth-map-transverse-to-an-embedded-submanifold]], [[thm-euclidean-inverse-function-theorem]])

[F6] Under AC$_\omega$, every smooth manifold, including one with boundary, admits a Riemannian metric compatible with its manifold topology. ([[thm-every-smooth-manifold-admits-a-riemannian-metric]])

[A1] AC$_\omega$ is the sequence-choice principle used by [F1], [F2], and [F4]. ([[def-countable-choice]])

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume countable choice. Let $M$ be a compact connected irreducible orientable smooth $3$-manifold with nonempty boundary, and fix a finite triangulation of $M$ with $t$ triangular faces. If $\mathcal T$ is any finite family of pairwise disjoint, two-sided, incompressible tori in $M$ such that no component obtained by cutting $M$ along $\mathcal T$ is homeomorphic to $T^2\times[0,1]$, then
$$
|\mathcal T|\le 4t+\dim_{\mathbb Z_2}H_2(M;\mathbb Z_2)-1.
$$
Consequently, any iterative process that cuts along tori and for which every finite stage satisfies this no-product condition terminates after finitely many cuts.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume full AC. Let $B$ be a compact piecewise linear $3$-ball with a finite compatible triangulation, and let $T\subset\operatorname{int}B$ be a two-sided embedded torus, where two-sided means that $T$ has a product neighborhood with its given central inclusion. Then there is an embedded compressing disk $D\subset\operatorname{int}B$ with $D\cap T=\partial D$ and $\partial D$ essential on $T$. The disk is properly embedded in the closure of one component of $B\setminus T$: its boundary lies on that component's copy of $T$ and its interior lies in the interior of the component.

[F1] Two-sidedness and a compressing disk have the geometric product-neighborhood and essential-boundary conventions of [[def-incompressibility-seifert-fibration-and-jsj-system]]. A torus with a topological product neighborhood is locally flat, by its intrinsic surface charts crossed with the interval.

[F2] Under full AC every compact TOP3-manifold, boundary allowed, has a finite compatible PL triangulation with its boundary a subcomplex. contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume full AC. Let $M$ be a compact connected irreducible Seifert-fibered $3$-manifold, and let $F\subset M$ be a connected, two-sided essential annulus or torus, neatly embedded at its boundary (the condition is vacuous for a torus). Then $F$ is ambient isotopic to either a vertical surface, meaning a union of regular fibers, or a horizontal surface, meaning a surface transverse to every fiber. For a horizontal surface $F$ with $n$ sheets over the base orbifold $B$ and exceptional-fiber multiplicities $q_1,\ldots,q_m$, the Euler characteristics satisfy
$$
\frac{\chi(F)}{n}=\chi(B)-\sum_{i=1}^m\left(1-\frac1{q_i}\right).
$$
If $F$ is two-sided and horizontal, cutting $M$ along $F$ gives an interval bundle over a surface.

For a smooth boundary-preimage embedding without the neatness condition, the same vertical-or-horizontal normal form is attained by a smooth isotopy of embeddings, fixed on the original boundary during its preliminary neatification, and by a topological ambient isotopy. The Euler count and interval-bundle conclusions apply to the resulting horizontal representative. A smooth ambient isotopy is asserted for the neat inputs above.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, the compact connected irreducible smooth Seifert-fibered three-manifold $M$ and the connected two-sided essential annulus or torus $F$, neat for the smooth ambient conclusion and otherwise a smooth boundary-preimage embedding for the final broader variant. The ambient manifold is not assumed orientable.

[A1] Full AC implies countable choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]], [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]).

[F1] Essentiality, the geometric disk obstructions and the fibered solid-torus models are [[def-incompressibility-seifert-fibration-and-jsj-system]], Definition.

[F2] In a solid torus an incompressible boundary-incompressible proper surface is a meridian disk or a boundary-parallel disk; an embedded torus compresses there ([[lem-incompressible-surface-in-solid-torus-is-meridian-or-boundary-parallel]], Statement). Its Proof 1.1 gives the actual smooth ball/disk push with marked rim collars. A two-sided torus in a parametrized smooth ball also compresses there: otherwise [[thm-smooth-loop-theorem-and-incompressibility-criterion-in-orientable-three-manifolds]], Statement, would inject $\mathbb Z^2$ into the trivial group. This is the compact orientable smooth-ball application of that criterion, not an unproved category change for a PL ball.

[F3] An incompressible proper surface in an irreducible orientable manifold with torus boundary is either boundary-incompressible or a boundary-parallel annulus ([[lem-incompressible-surface-torus-boundary-essential-or-parallel-annulus]], Statement).

[F4] Smooth torus circles and annulus arcs have the finite strip normalizations of [[lem-choice-free-smooth-torus-curves-and-annulus-strips]], Statement. Essential two-sided Klein-bottle circles have the vertical or horizontal normal forms of [[lem-smooth-two-sided-klein-bottle-curves-have-vertical-or-horizontal-normal-forms]], Statement.

[F5] Finite disk systems in a ball or solid torus, primitive vertical-boundary annulus systems, and horizontal meridian-boundary disk systems admit simultaneous smooth normalization, fixing a smaller already common boundary collar ([[lem-simultaneous-smooth-disk-and-primitive-annulus-normalization]], Statement).

[F6] Relative surface general position is [[lem-relative-transversality-for-embedded-surfaces]], Statement; general embedded-submanifold parametric transversality is [[thm-parametric-transversality]], Statement. For boundary faces apply the former in the double of the supplied neat collars. The latter also applies to the one-dimensional fiber cores.

[F7] Compact-source isotopies extend smoothly ([[thm-isotopy-extension]]; [[lem-choice-free-isotopy-extension-for-a-compact-smooth-source]]). The latter's Proof 2.1–4.1 also gives the finite-chart bump and compact-time flow construction. Smooth Euclidean flows and parameter dependence are [[thm-picard-lindelof-local-existence-and-uniqueness]] and [[thm-smooth-dependence-of-ode-solutions-on-parameters]], Statements.

[F8] Compact smooth surfaces with boundary have compatible finite triangulations ([[thm-compact-smooth-manifolds-with-corners-admit-relative-finite-triangulations]], Statement in dimension two).

[F9] Boundary-fixed smooth embedding neatification has an explicit topological ambient extension and preserves absence of smooth compressing and boundary-compressing disks. Boundary-parallelity is invariant under that extension: a product for the final surface pulls back to a product for the original surface, and conversely. Hence essentiality in the original product sense is retained. [[lem-compact-smooth-boundary-preimage-surfaces-admit-neat-embedding-isotopies]] [[lem-angular-boundary-neatification-preserves-smooth-disk-obstructions]]

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
A compact orientable three-manifold $M$ is **irreducible** if every embedded $2$-sphere in its interior bounds an embedded $3$-ball in $M$. A properly embedded surface is **incompressible** if it admits no embedded disk whose interior misses the surface and whose boundary is an essential simple closed curve in it. A boundary subsurface is **$\pi_1$-injective** if the inclusion of each component induces an injection on fundamental groups. A **pared pair** is a pair $(M,P)$ in which $M$ is compact, orientable and irreducible, and $P$ is a possibly empty compact subsurface of $\partial M$ whose pairwise disjoint components are $\pi_1$-injective annuli or tori, every noncyclic abelian subgroup of $\pi_1(M)$ is conjugate into $\pi_1$ of a component of $P$ up to base-path conjugacy, and every map of pairs
$$
(S^1\times I,S^1\times\partial I)\longrightarrow(M,P)
$$
that induces injections on fundamental groups is homotopic through maps of pairs into $P$, so its boundary remains in $P$ during the homotopy. Write $\partial_0M=\partial M\setminus\operatorname{int}P$. A **horoball** is a region bounded by a horosphere, a Euclidean plane or sphere tangent to the ideal boundary at one point. The **peripheral subgroup** for a component of $P$ is the image of its fundamental group in $\pi_1(M)$, recorded up to conjugacy. A **hyperbolic structure** on $(M,P)$ is a curvature $-1$ metric on $\operatorname{int}M$ described by an atlas of charts into $\mathbb H^3$ whose transition maps are in $\operatorname{Isom}^+(\mathbb H^3)$. Its developing map $\operatorname{dev}$ from the universal cover and holonomy homomorphism $\rho:\pi_1(M)\to\operatorname{Isom}^+(\mathbb H^3)$ satisfy $\operatorname{dev}(gx)=\rho(g)\operatorname{dev}(x)$. The metric is **complete** when it is geodesically complete. A **cusp** corresponding to a component of $P$ is a quotient of a horoball by the associated peripheral subgroup. The hyperbolic volume is the integral of the Riemannian volume density over $\operatorname{int}M$; the structure has **finite volume** when this integral is finite.

The definition asserts no existence.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume countable choice. For a smooth oriented knot with a chosen product tubular neighbourhood $N(K)\cong S^1\times D^2$, let $\mu$ be the positive fibre meridian and let $\sigma$ be the product section $s\mapsto(s,1)$ of $T_K=\partial N(K)\cong S^1\times S^1$. Then $T_K=\partial E_K$ is a torus and $[\mu],[\sigma]$ form a basis of $H_1(T_K;\mathbb Z)$. The curve $\sigma$ is a product section; this statement does not assert that it is the preferred zero-homology longitude.

contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K:S^1\to S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot with a chosen product tubular neighbourhood $N(K)$, and set $E_K=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$ and $T_K=\partial E_K$. contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $E_K$ be the compact connected orientable exterior of a smooth knot in $S^3$, with one torus boundary component. If $E_K$ is irreducible, its boundary is incompressible, $E_K$ is atoroidal, and $E_K$ is not Seifert-fibered, then $\operatorname{int}(E_K)$ admits a complete finite-volume Riemannian metric of constant sectional curvature $-1$ with one torus cusp. No conclusion is asserted for a torus or satellite knot unless its exterior satisfies all four topological hypotheses.

facts:
**Given:** The smooth knot exterior $E_K$ and all hypotheses in the Statement, including full AC. Atoroidality here has the embedded-torus meaning of [[def-incompressibility-seifert-fibration-and-jsj-system]].

[F1] **External input — Loop Theorem.** If a subsurface $F$ of the boundary of a compact $3$-manifold $N$ has noninjective $\pi_1(F)\to\pi_1(N)$, an essential simple closed curve in $F$ bounds a properly embedded disk in $N$. Source: Aschenbrenner–Friedl–Wilton, *3-Manifold Groups*, arXiv:1205.0202, Theorem 1.2, p.7.

[F2] **External input — comparison of atoroidality conventions.** For compact orientable irreducible $3$-manifolds with empty or toroidal boundary, the condition that every incompressible embedded torus is boundary-parallel and the condition that every $\pi_1$-injective torus map is homotopic into the boundary agree outside certain Seifert-fibered manifolds. In particular they agree for a manifold which is not Seifert-fibered. Source: the same survey, §1.4, p.9, immediately after its definition of atoroidal. This is the torus-theorem consequence expressly recorded there; it is imported, not reconstructed here.

[F3] **External input — Hyperbolization Theorem.** If $N$ is compact, orientable, irreducible, has empty or toroidal boundary, is atoroidal in the torus-map convention, and has infinite fundamental group, then its interior admits a complete hyperbolic metric. For this empty-or-toroidal-boundary theorem the metric has finite volume. Source: the same survey, Theorem 1.13, p.13, with the definition on p.11 and finite-volume statement/convention on p.12. This imports the complete established hyperbolization result, covering both fibered and nonfibered cases; it does not invoke a conditional deformation theorem to create an initial representation.

[F4] **External input — finite-volume cusp decomposition.** A complete oriented hyperbolic $3$-manifold of finite volume is a compact submanifold bounded by tori together with finitely many horoballs modulo rank-two free abelian parabolic actions. Source: Thurston, *The Geometry and Topology of Three-Manifolds*, Chapter 5, Proposition 5.11.1, printed p.116 (PDF p.34). Thus its noncompact ends are exactly its torus cusps.

The cited statements, their indicated conventions and the short proof of [F4] were read in the actual source PDFs. The full proofs of the Loop Theorem, the torus theorem and general hyperbolization are external inputs; they have not been locally reconstructed or fully reread for this application.
