contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Define the standard figure-eight knot $K_8$ to be the oriented closure of the three-strand geometric braid $(\sigma_1\sigma_2^{-1})^2$. Its endpoint permutation is a $3$-cycle, so this closure has one component.

Let $\Delta_0=[0,1,2,3]$ and $\Delta_1=[0',1',2',3']$ be oriented ideal tetrahedra with orientation-reversing affine face maps
$$
[0,1,2]\to[3',1',2'],\quad
[0,1,3]\to[0',1',2'],\quad
[0,2,3]\to[0',1',3'],\quad
[1,2,3]\to[0',2',3'].
$$
This is the two-tetrahedron ideal triangulation obtained from the standard four-crossing figure-eight diagram by cutting along crossing arcs, identifying upper and lower polyhedron faces with equal region labels, and collapsing the two bigon faces. Its edge classes are
$$
\{01,02,23,0'1',1'3',2'3'\},\qquad
\{12,03,13,1'2',0'2',0'3'\};
$$
each has valence six, and the unique ideal vertex link is a torus. Put shape $z_1$ on $01,23$, shape $z_2$ on $03,12$, and shape $z_3$ on $02,13$ in $\Delta_0$; put shape $w_1$ on $0'1',2'3'$, shape $w_2$ on $0'3',1'2'$, and shape $w_3$ on $0'2',1'3'$ in $\Delta_1$. Unfold the eight cusp-link triangles by the face maps into the standard rectangular strip, and label them $a,b,c,d,e,f,g,h$ from left to right; identify the strip boundary sides as prescribed by those same maps. Let $\alpha$ be the edge path across the strip from the left side of $a$ on the left boundary to the left side of $a$ on the right boundary, and let $\beta$ be the edge path on the left boundary from the base of $a$ to the top of $h$. Their ordered corner factors are respectively $z_3,w_2^{-1},z_2,w_3^{-1},z_3,w_2^{-1},z_2,w_3^{-1}$ and $z_2^{-1},w_1$. The face-pairing incidence check gives one positive transverse intersection, so their homology classes form a basis of $H_1$ and the loops form a basis of $\pi_1$ of the torus link. The two edge products are $z_1^2z_3w_1^2w_3$ and $z_2^2z_3w_2^2w_3$, while
$$
H(\alpha)=\left(\frac{z_2z_3}{w_2w_3}\right)^2,\qquad H(\beta)=\frac{w_1}{z_2}.
$$
For $\omega=e^{i\pi/3}$, assigning $z_1=z_2=z_3=w_1=w_2=w_3=\omega$ makes both edge products and both cusp multipliers equal to $1$ and gives total angle $2\pi$ around each edge. The gluing therefore gives the figure-eight complement a complete finite-volume curvature $-1$ metric with one peripheral torus cusp.

facts:
**Given:** The stated face-paired ideal triangulation of the complement of the standard figure-eight knot, with positive tetrahedron shapes as specified.

[F1] [[def-ideal-tetrahedron-shape-and-cusp-holonomy]] defines the normalized ideal-tetrahedron shapes, corner factors, upper half-space metric, and cusp multiplier.

[F2] [[lem-ideal-tetrahedron-shape-parameter-relations]] proves that setting $z=\omega=e^{i\pi/3}$ makes all three shapes equal to $\omega$ and each dihedral angle equal to $\pi/3$.

[F3] [[lem-ideal-torus-cusp-holonomy-criterion]] says that edge products $1$, edge angle sums $2\pi$, and cusp multipliers $1$ on a torus basis imply completeness at that cusp.

[F4] [[lem-horocusp-truncation-has-finite-volume]] computes the volume of a rank-two horocusp quotient as half the area of its Euclidean cross-section.

[F5] [[thm-regular-ideal-tetrahedron-volume]] gives the finite volume $v_3=3\Lambda(\pi/3)$ of a regular ideal tetrahedron.

[F6] [[def-knot-exterior]] fixes the chosen compact knot exterior, and [[lem-knot-exterior-has-peripheral-torus]] identifies its boundary as the peripheral torus.

[F7] [[def-elementary-geometric-half-twist]] defines $\sigma_1,\sigma_2$ as the positive adjacent geometric half twists and their opposites as their group inverses; [[thm-geometric-braids-form-a-group]] gives the endpoint-permutation homomorphism.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth knot in $S^3$ that is not ambient isotopic to the standard unknot, and assume its compact exterior $E_K$ is atoroidal and not Seifert-fibered. Then every smoothly embedded $2$-sphere in $\operatorname{int}E_K$ bounds an embedded $3$-ball in $E_K$, and there is no smoothly embedded disk in $E_K$ whose interior misses $\partial E_K$ and whose boundary is essential in $\partial E_K$.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, a nontrivial smooth knot exterior $E_K$, and the assumptions that it is atoroidal and not Seifert-fibered.

[A1] Full AC is [[def-axiom-of-choice]].

[F1] [[def-incompressibility-seifert-fibration-and-jsj-system]] defines irreducible to mean every interior $2$-sphere bounds a $3$-ball, incompressible boundary to mean no compressing disk with essential boundary, atoroidal to mean every incompressible torus is boundary-parallel, and Seifert-fibered to mean decomposed into circles with the specified fibered-solid-torus local models.

[L1] Full AC implies the countable-choice assumption of [F1] by applying a choice function to the countable family of nonempty smooth-manifold data. [[def-countable-choice]]

[F2] [[lem-knot-exterior-irreducible-and-boundary-incompressible-kt18-local]] proves that every knot exterior with non-unknot core is irreducible and has incompressible boundary under AC.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ and $N$ be interiors of compact connected oriented knot exteriors carrying complete finite-volume hyperbolic metrics. Every isomorphism $\pi_1(M)\to\pi_1(N)$, considered up to the conjugacy induced by basepoint changes, is realized by a unique isometry in the corresponding proper homotopy class. If the isomorphism is induced by an orientation-preserving proper homotopy equivalence, the isometry preserves orientation. In particular, the two metrics have equal volume, where volume is the integral of their Riemannian volume densities.

facts:
**Given:** AC, the two connected oriented knot-exterior interiors with their complete finite-volume hyperbolic metrics, and the stated outer fundamental-group isomorphism.

[A1] Full choice is [[def-axiom-of-choice]] and supplies the countable-choice hypothesis in [[def-countable-choice]].

[F1] [[thm-mostow-prasad-rigidity-for-standard-finite-volume-cusped-three-manifolds]] proves that every isomorphism between the fundamental groups of connected oriented complete finite-volume curvature-$-1$ three-manifolds is induced by a unique isometry, properly homotopic to every proper homotopy equivalence inducing the same outer isomorphism. It proves orientation agreement and equality of volume integrals. Its quotient presentation and finite torus-cusp decomposition are proved consequences of its metric hypotheses, not extra assumptions.

contract.heading: Statement refuted
contract.text: Every compact exterior of a smooth knot in $S^3$ is non-Seifert-fibered.

facts:
**Given:** $S^3=\{(z,w)\in\mathbb C^2:|z|^2+|w|^2=1\}$, the weighted circle action $g_\theta(z,w)=(e^{3i\theta}z,e^{2i\theta}w)$, its orbit $K(t)=2^{-1/2}(e^{3it},e^{2it})$, the orbit map $q:S^3\to S^3/S^1$, a small closed disk $D$ around $q(K)$ disjoint from the two axis orbits, and the invariant tube $N(K)=q^{-1}(D)$ with exterior $E_K=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$.

[F1] [[def-knot-exterior]] defines the compact exterior by removing the interior of the chosen closed tube.

[F2] [[def-incompressibility-seifert-fibration-and-jsj-system]] defines a Seifert fibration by local fibered-solid-torus models; multiplicity $1$ fibers are regular, while multiplicity $q>1$ fibers are exceptional of order $q$.

[F3] [[thm-thurston-hyperbolization-for-atoroidal-knot-exteriors]] explicitly requires that the exterior not be Seifert-fibered.

contract.heading: Example
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be the standard figure-eight knot and $E_K$ its compact exterior. Its interior admits a complete finite-volume hyperbolic metric obtained by gluing two regular ideal tetrahedra; each edge class has total angle $2\pi$, both generators of the peripheral torus have trivial rotation-and-scale cusp multiplier, and its complete hyperbolic volume is $6\Lambda(\pi/3)=2v_3\approx2.02988$.

facts:
**Given:** AC and the standard figure-eight knot exterior.

[F1] [[lem-figure-eight-ideal-gluing-and-cusp-completeness]] constructs the complete finite-volume metric from the specified two-tetrahedron face gluing and verifies both edge classes and a basis of cusp multipliers.

[F2] [[thm-regular-ideal-tetrahedron-volume]] gives the volume of each regular ideal tetrahedron as $v_3=3\Lambda(\pi/3)$.

[F4] [[thm-mostow-prasad-rigidity-and-knot-volume]] proves uniqueness and volume preservation for complete finite-volume hyperbolic metrics on this knot exterior.

[F3] [[lem-lobachevsky-fourier-expansion-and-pi-third-bound]] gives the positive series for $\Lambda(\pi/3)$ and bounds the tail after the first $N+1$ terms by $\sqrt3/(72N^2)$.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice for the chosen smooth knot-exterior data. Let $K_8$ be the standard figure-eight knot, presented as the boundary of the square plumbing of one positive and one negative Hopf band, with one boundary component. A positive Hopf band is an oriented annulus whose positive normal push-off of its core has linking number $+1$ with the core; a negative Hopf band has linking number $-1$. A square plumbing identifies a square in the boundary collars of the annuli with the four boundary edges alternating between the annuli, then smooths corners. Let $F$ be this plumbed surface, and choose the compact exterior by deleting the interior of the binding neighborhood $N(K_8)\cong\partial F\times D^2$ supplied by the open book; on every page this neighborhood meets the page in an annular collar of $\partial F$. Let $a,b$ be the core curves, ordered so that $a$ is the positive-band core and $a\cdot_F b=+1$. The exterior $E_{K_8}$ fibers over $S^1$ with fiber $F$. With the twist convention that the positive twist $R_a$ sends $a\mapsto a$, $b\mapsto a+b$, and the negative twist $L_b$ sends $a\mapsto a+b$, $b\mapsto b$, the monodromy is $R_a\circ L_b$. After capping $\partial F$ by a disk, its action on the ordered homology basis $([a],[b])$ is represented by $\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$.

facts:
**Given:** The explicitly plumbed oriented knot $K_8$, the chosen compact exterior $E_{K_8}$, and the square-plumbing surface with ordered core curves $a,b$.

[A1] The Axiom of Countable Choice, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the hypothesis of the smooth exterior convention [[def-countable-choice]].

[F1] [[def-knot-exterior]]: the chosen exterior is $S^3$ with the interior of the supplied closed tubular neighborhood removed.

[F2] [[def-oriented-link-in-s-three-and-ambient-isotopy]]: a knot is a smooth oriented circle embedded in the standard oriented $S^3$, considered up to orientation-preserving ambient isotopy.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume AC. Every nonempty connected oriented complete Riemannian three-manifold of constant sectional curvature $-1$ is isometric to $\Gamma\backslash\mathbb H^3$ for a discrete torsion-free subgroup $\Gamma\le\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb C)$. The covering is a universal Riemannian covering and identifies $\Gamma$ with the fundamental group up to the usual basepoint conjugacies. Its completeness and quotient presentation are conclusions from the stated metric hypotheses. The orientation-preserving isometry group of the model is $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb C)$ with its usual Möbius boundary action.

facts:
**Given:** AC and the nonempty connected oriented complete curvature-$-1$ three-manifold $(M,g)$.

[A1] Full choice is [[def-axiom-of-choice]] and supplies all the stated countable-choice hypotheses.

[F1] Cartan–Hadamard makes $\exp_p:(T_pM,\exp_p^*g)\to M$ a universal Riemannian covering, with complete source. [[thm-cartan-hadamard]]

[F2] Differentials of exponential maps are Jacobi fields with the specified initial data. The constant-curvature tensor is $R(X,Y)Z=-(g(Y,Z)X-g(X,Z)Y)$; supplied vectors have unique parallel extensions, these preserve inner products, and Jacobi fields are uniquely determined by their initial value and covariant derivative. [[thm-differential-of-the-exponential-map-in-terms-of-jacobi-fields]], [[prop-curvature-tensor-of-constant-sectional-curvature]], [[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-parallel-sections]], [[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-jacobi-fields-from-initial-data]], [[prop-levi-civita-parallel-transport-preserves-lengths-angles-and-volume]]

[F3] The upper half-space distance, ball model, complete-geodesic uniqueness, and isometric extension of every Möbius transformation are calculated locally in the boundary-extension supplier. [[lem-hyperbolic-three-space-quasi-isometry-has-quasiconformal-boundary]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M=\Gamma\backslash\mathbb H^3$ be a connected oriented complete finite-volume hyperbolic three-manifold with a compact smooth core and $k\ge1$ disjoint standard torus cusp ends. Choose positively oriented peripheral bases $(\mu_i,\lambda_i)$. Let $\rho_u$, for $u$ near $0$ in $\mathbb C^k$, be the augmented holonomy family supplied by the augmented holonomy-coordinate theorem, based at the complete holonomy $\rho_0$. Thus the logarithms satisfy $v_i(u)=\tau_i(u)u_i$ with $\operatorname{Im}\tau_i(u)>0$.

After shrinking this neighborhood, there are smooth hyperbolic metrics $g_u$ on $M$, possibly incomplete, with holonomy $\rho_u$. They depend smoothly on the real and imaginary parts of $u$ on every compact subset, and $g_0$ is the given complete metric. Each end with $u_i=0$ is a complete finite-volume translation cusp. Each end with $u_i\ne0$ has an explicit developing map onto the punctured tube about its peripheral axis, with the angular and axial periods specified by $u_i,v_i$.

Suppose $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,k\}$ and, for every $i\in J$, a primitive integral pair $(p_i,q_i)$ satisfies
$$p_i u_i+q_i v_i(u)=2\pi i,$$
while $u_i=0$ for $i\notin J$. Then $g_u$ extends across all ends in $J$ to a smooth complete finite-volume hyperbolic metric on the ordinary Dehn filling whose meridians are $p_i\mu_i+q_i\lambda_i$. For arbitrary supplied orientation-reversing boundary homeomorphisms realizing these same slopes, the resulting topological filling is orientation-preservingly and core-preservingly homeomorphic to this realization, by a homeomorphism equal to the identity on the truncated original manifold. Transporting the realization's smooth structure and metric through this homeomorphism gives the asserted smooth hyperbolic metric on that supplied filling. No assertion is made about a separately prescribed smooth structure for an arbitrary topological gluing. The added cores are ordinary smooth geodesics, with no cone or orbifold singularity. Their lengths are
$$\ell_i=\frac{|u_i|^2\operatorname{Im}\tau_i(u)}{2\pi}>0.$$
Along such filling parameters tending to zero, the metrics converge smoothly to $g_0$ on every compact subset of $M$, the core lengths tend to zero, and the filled volumes tend to $\operatorname{Vol}(M,g_0)$. No ideal triangulation is assumed. This theorem realizes given small holonomy solutions; it does not assert their existence for specified slopes.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, the complete quotient, the compact core and standard cusp models, the peripheral bases, and the augmented representation family in the Statement.

[A1] AC supplies Countable Choice for smooth partitions of unity and for the holonomy supplier. The supplier also uses AC in its Hilbert-space and recursive formal-extension arguments. [[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]

[F1] There are holomorphic representatives $\rho_u$ and holomorphically varying peripheral eigenlines. On each end a holomorphic change of frame sends that line to $\infty$, and the peripheral maps become $Z\mapsto e^{u_i}Z+a_i(u)$ and $Z\mapsto e^{v_i}Z+b_i(u)$, with $a_i(0)\ne0$, $v_i=\tau_i u_i$ and $\operatorname{Im}\tau_i>0$. On $u_i=0$, $v_i=0$ and $b_i/a_i=\tau_i$. [[thm-augmented-finite-volume-hyperbolic-holonomy-coordinates]]

[F2] A smooth open manifold has smooth partitions subordinate to an open cover under Countable Choice. A smooth map with invertible differential is a local diffeomorphism. [[thm-smooth-partitions-of-unity-exist-on-manifolds]], [[thm-smooth-inverse-function-theorem-on-manifolds]]

[F3] The curvature-$-1$ model is the upper half-space $(Z,Y)\in\mathbb C\times(0,\infty)$, with its orientation-preserving projective matrix isometries. Its metric and volume formula are computed directly in step 1.1. [[lem-complete-curvature-minus-one-manifolds-are-kleinian-quotients]]

[F4] Ordinary filling attaches a solid torus by an orientation-reversing boundary homeomorphism sending its meridian to the specified slope. Here equality of slopes means equality of unoriented ambient-isotopy classes of embedded curves on the torus, the standard ordinary-slope convention. A boundary homeomorphism between product solid tori extends core-preservingly, with the same orientation sign, if an ambient isotopy of the target boundary moves the image meridian to its target meridian. [[def-multicusped-dehn-filling]], [[lem-meridian-preserving-torus-homeomorphism-extends-over-solid-torus]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K_8$ be the standard figure-eight knot with compact exterior obtained by deleting the binding neighborhood from its open-book presentation and peripheral basis $(\mu,\lambda)$, where $\mu$ is the positive meridian and $\lambda$ is the preferred zero-homology longitude. The exterior fibers over $S^1$ with fiber a once-punctured torus and monodromy fixing its boundary pointwise. Filling along the slope $\lambda$ produces a torus bundle over $S^1$. For the fiber and ordered core basis in the figure-eight plumbing convention, the induced action on the capped torus homology is $\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$.

facts:
**Given:** The chosen exterior of the standard figure-eight knot, its positive meridian and preferred longitude, and the square-plumbed fiber and monodromy convention.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: every family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

[F1] [[def-countable-choice]]: $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ selects from every countable family of nonempty sets.

[F2] [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]: in ZF, $\mathrm{AC}\Rightarrow\mathrm{DC}\Rightarrow\mathrm{AC}_\omega$.

[F3] [[def-oriented-slope-and-knot-dehn-filling]]: with the stated peripheral basis, the integer coefficient $0$ is the unoriented slope represented by $\lambda$; ordinary filling attaches a solid torus whose meridian is that slope.

[F4] [[thm-knot-exterior-homology-and-longitude]]: under AC the preferred longitude is the unique primitive boundary class that maps to zero in $H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)$, and $(\mu,\lambda)$ is a basis.

[F5] [[lem-figure-eight-complement-punctured-torus-bundle]]: the exterior is the mapping torus of a once-punctured torus, with boundary-fixing monodromy whose capped homology matrix is $\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$.

[F6] [[def-multicusped-dehn-filling]]: a filling along a selected boundary slope is obtained by attaching an oriented solid torus with the specified meridian slope.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. If $M$ is a closed connected orientable three-manifold with a complete Riemannian metric of constant sectional curvature $-1$, then its fundamental group contains no subgroup isomorphic to $\mathbb Z^2$.

facts:
**Given:** A closed connected three-manifold $M$ with a complete metric of constant sectional curvature $-1$ and the inherited $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ selects from every countable family of nonempty sets.

[F1] [[def-pared-hyperbolic-structures-and-volume]]: a hyperbolic structure is a curvature $-1$ metric described by charts into $\mathbb H^3$.

[F2] [[thm-cartan-hadamard]]: the complete simply connected universal cover of a connected complete manifold with $K\le0$ is identified with its tangent space by the exponential map.

[F3] [[ex-jacobi-fields-in-constant-sectional-curvature]]: along a unit-speed geodesic in curvature $-1$, a normal Jacobi field with $J(0)=0$ and $D_tJ(0)=w$ is $J(t)=\sinh(t)P_t w$, where $P_t$ is parallel transport.

[F4] [[def-universal-covering-space]] and [[def-deck-transformation-and-deck-group]]: the universal cover is a covering and its deck group acts freely; [[thm-deck-group-of-a-universal-cover-is-the-fundamental-group]] identifies that group with $\pi_1(M)$. The lifted metric makes the covering a local isometry by [[def-riemannian-isometry-and-local-isometry]], local isometries send geodesics to geodesics by [[lem-local-isometries-send-geodesics-to-geodesics]], and covering paths lift by [[thm-path-lifting-for-covering-maps]].

[F5] Gongopadhyay and Kulkarni, *z-Classes of Isometries of the Hyperbolic Space*, §1 and Appendix A.1: orientation-preserving isometries of $\mathbb H^3$ are Möbius transformations of the boundary sphere, with hyperbolic/parabolic/elliptic types identified by their fixed-point behavior.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Let an oriented finite ideal triangulation of the interior of a compact connected orientable three-manifold have $k\ge1$ ideal vertices, each with torus link. Assign a positive ideal-tetrahedron shape to every tetrahedron. Suppose that around every finite edge the product of its incident complex shape parameters is $1$ and the sum of its dihedral angles is $2\pi$. For each ideal vertex $v$, choose a basis $(\alpha_v,\beta_v)$ of the fundamental group of its torus link and suppose the cusp multipliers satisfy $H(\alpha_v)=H(\beta_v)=1$. Then the face gluings define a complete finite-volume hyperbolic metric on the manifold interior, with one rank-two cusp for each ideal vertex.

facts:
**Given:** The finite face-paired ideal triangulation, its positive shapes, all edge equations and angle sums, and a homology basis on each torus vertex link.

[F1] [[def-ideal-tetrahedron-shape-and-cusp-holonomy]]: a positive shape determines a nondegenerate ideal tetrahedron in $\mathbb H^3$, its corner factors, and the cusp multiplier $H(\gamma)$ along a path in a torus vertex link.

[F2] [[lem-ideal-tetrahedron-shape-parameter-relations]]: the argument of each positive shape parameter is the corresponding dihedral angle.

[F3] [[lem-ideal-torus-cusp-holonomy-criterion]]: for one torus vertex, edge products $1$, angle sums $2\pi$, and cusp multipliers $1$ on a fundamental-group basis imply a complete hyperbolic cusp.

[F4] [[lem-horocusp-truncation-has-finite-volume]]: a rank-two translation-lattice horocusp with Euclidean cross-section area $A$ has volume $A/2$.

[F5] [[def-pared-hyperbolic-structures-and-volume]]: a hyperbolic structure is a curvature $-1$ metric on the manifold interior, and a torus cusp is a horoball quotient by its peripheral subgroup.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Use the upper half-space model
$$
\mathbb H^3=\{(x+iy,t):x,y\in\mathbb R,\ t>0\},\qquad
ds^2=t^{-2}(dx^2+dy^2+dt^2),
$$
whose ideal boundary is $\mathbb C\cup\{\infty\}$. An oriented ideal tetrahedron in normalized position has ideal vertices $0,1,\infty,z$, where $\operatorname{Im}z>0$. Its three edge-shape parameters are
$$
z,\qquad z'=\frac1{1-z},\qquad z''=\frac{z-1}{z},
$$
each assigned to one pair of opposite edges; the parameter at a corner of a truncated ideal vertex triangle is the parameter of the incident edge. For an oriented path $\gamma$ in a triangulated torus link of ideal vertices, its cusp multiplier $H(\gamma)$ is the product of the corner parameters encountered along $\gamma$, using the parameter when the path cuts off that corner on its left and its reciprocal when it cuts off the corner on its right.

scope: Literal contract/Facts extraction only; accepted proof body not inspected.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: For an oriented ideal tetrahedron with normalized vertices $0,1,\infty,z$ and $\operatorname{Im}z>0$, its three edge-shape parameters are $z$, $z'=1/(1-z)$, and $z''=(z-1)/z$. They satisfy $zz'z''=-1$, and their arguments in $(0,\pi)$ are the three dihedral angles, whose sum is $\pi$. For $\omega=e^{i\pi/3}$, the choice $z=\omega$ gives $z=z'=z''=\omega$ and all six dihedral angles equal to $\pi/3$.

facts:
**Given:** A positively oriented ideal tetrahedron in normalized upper half-space position with shape $z$, $\operatorname{Im}z>0$.

[F1] [[def-ideal-tetrahedron-shape-and-cusp-holonomy]] defines its edge parameters as $z$, $1/(1-z)$ and $(z-1)/z$, one for each opposite-edge pair.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Let an orientable finite ideal triangulation have exactly one ideal vertex, whose link is a torus. Suppose its tetrahedra carry positive shapes whose edge products equal $1$ and whose dihedral angles sum to $2\pi$ around every edge. If the cusp multipliers $H(\alpha)$ and $H(\beta)$ are $1$ for a basis $\alpha,\beta$ of the torus fundamental group, then the glued hyperbolic metric is complete at that cusp.

facts:
**Given:** The finite face-glued ideal triangulation, its positive shapes, the edge equations, and a basis of loops on the torus vertex link.

[F1] [[def-ideal-tetrahedron-shape-and-cusp-holonomy]] defines the upper half-space metric, the shape at each corner of a truncated ideal vertex, and the product $H(\gamma)$ recording the linear scale and rotation accumulated around a cusp path.

[F2] [[lem-ideal-tetrahedron-shape-parameter-relations]] identifies the argument of each positive shape with its dihedral angle.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $\Gamma\subset\mathbb C$ be a rank-two lattice acting on $\mathbb H^3$ by horizontal translations, and let
$$
C=\{(x+iy,t):t\ge1\}/\Gamma
$$
be the quotient of the horoball $t\ge1$. If $A$ is the Euclidean area of a fundamental parallelogram for $\Gamma$, then the end is at infinite hyperbolic distance and $\operatorname{Vol}(C)=A/2$.

facts:
**Given:** The upper half-space metric and a rank-two translation lattice $\Gamma$.

[F1] [[def-ideal-tetrahedron-shape-and-cusp-holonomy]] gives $ds^2=t^{-2}(dx^2+dy^2+dt^2)$ and its volume density $dx\,dy\,dt/t^3$.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text: Let $M$ be the interior of a compact connected orientable three-manifold with a complete finite-volume hyperbolic metric and torus cusps $C_1,\ldots,C_k$. For a chosen cusp $C_i$, choose a horospherical section $T_i$ and identify its Euclidean universal cover with $\mathbb R^2$ so its deck group is a rank-two translation lattice. A slope on $T_i$ is represented by a primitive lattice vector $v$ modulo sign. Its **Euclidean slope length on the chosen section** is $\ell_{T_i}(v)=\lVert v\rVert$ in the induced Euclidean metric. In upper half-space coordinates, if the section is the quotient of the horosphere of height $h>0$ by lattice $\Lambda$, then $\ell_{T_i}(p,q)=|p u+q w|/h$, where $u,w$ are the translation vectors representing the chosen basis. Replacing height $h$ by $h'>0$ multiplies every slope length by $h/h'$; therefore the length depends on the chosen section and is not an intrinsic number until that section is fixed.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Let $N$ be the complement of finitely many disjoint open solid tori in a connected oriented three-manifold, and suppose its interior has a hyperbolic metric. Fix one boundary torus $T$ with primitive peripheral basis $(\mu,\lambda)$. Assume that a neighborhood of this end, after developing into $\mathbb H^3$, is isometric to a punctured radius-$\varepsilon$ tube about a geodesic axis, modulo a translation of length $L>0$ along that axis. Assume that $\lambda$ is the axial translation direction and that $\mu$ is the angular direction making one full turn of angle $2\pi$ about the axis; equivalently, its peripheral holonomy is the identity isometry with the full-turn lift. Then the hyperbolic metric extends smoothly over the ordinary Dehn filling along $\mu$, adding the axis quotient as the core geodesic of length $L$. The same conclusion holds simultaneously for any finite set of ends satisfying these conditions.

facts:
**Given:** The hyperbolic metric on the complement of the stated tubes, the peripheral basis on each selected torus, and the explicit developed tube model with meridional angle $2\pi$ and positive axial translation length.

[F1] [[def-multicusped-dehn-filling]]: ordinary Dehn filling attaches a solid torus whose meridian disk boundary is the specified primitive slope.

[F2] [[def-pared-hyperbolic-structures-and-volume]]: a hyperbolic metric has curvature $-1$ in local charts into $\mathbb H^3$.

[F3] [[lem-ideal-triangulation-gluing-equations-and-peripheral-holonomy]]: edge products $1$ and angle sums $2\pi$ give a smooth hyperbolic metric away from ideal vertices; the cusp equations are additional conditions used to obtain completeness at those ends.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be the interior of a compact connected orientable three-manifold with $k\ge1$ torus cusps and a complete finite-volume hyperbolic metric. Choose a peripheral basis $(\mu_i,\lambda_i)$ on each cusp. On the augmented holonomy space obtained by selecting one common invariant line on each peripheral subgroup, near the complete structure write $u_i$ and $v_i$ for the logarithms of the eigenvalue ratios of the peripheral holonomies of $\mu_i$ and $\lambda_i$, with branches chosen so $u_i=v_i=0$ at the complete structure. There is a neighborhood of the complete point in the $k$ generalized parameter spheres such that primitive integral filling data $(p_i,q_i)$ in that neighborhood satisfying $p_i u_i+q_i v_i=2\pi i$ at every filled cusp produce a complete finite-volume hyperbolic structure on the ordinary filled manifold. The peripheral full-turn equations are solved simultaneously across the $k$ cusps; unfilled cusps retain their complete parabolic holonomy. No universal numeric length threshold is asserted.

facts:
**Given:** AC, the full finite-volume $k$-cusped metric, the ordered peripheral bases and the primitive filling data.

[A1] AC supplies DC and countable choice. [[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]], [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]

[F1] The given metric has a Kleinian quotient description and a compact smooth core with standard torus cusps. [[lem-complete-curvature-minus-one-manifolds-are-kleinian-quotients]], [[lem-finite-volume-hyperbolic-three-manifolds-have-finite-standard-cusp-decompositions]]

[F2] The augmented deformation germ is smooth of complex dimension $k$, with independent logarithms $u_i$ and $v_i=u_i\tau_i(u)$, where the complete $\tau_i$ are nonreal; for positive bases their imaginary parts are positive. [[thm-augmented-finite-volume-hyperbolic-holonomy-coordinates]]

[F3] These factors admit a product neighborhood of the complete generalized parameters with unique simultaneous small full-turn solutions, continuous also at partially unfilled tuples. [[lem-simultaneous-peripheral-full-turn-equations-have-small-solutions]]

[F4] Given such primitive solutions, the explicit developed ends extend to smooth solid-torus cores; the resulting metric is complete and has finite volume. Coordinates $u_i=0$ remain complete cusps. [[thm-small-augmented-holonomy-deformations-have-smooth-geometric-fillings]]

[F5] Ordinary fillings use primitive slopes modulo sign, and cusp lengths use chosen-section Euclidean norms. [[def-multicusped-dehn-filling]], [[def-cusp-slope-length]], [[def-pared-hyperbolic-structures-and-volume]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume AC. Let $M$ be a nonempty connected oriented complete Riemannian three-manifold of constant curvature $-1$ and finite volume. Then $M$ is a compact core together with finitely many pairwise disjoint standard torus cusp ends. Each end is an embedded quotient $\{y>R_i\}/\Lambda_i$ of a horoball by a rank-two translation lattice, and the complement of these open ends is compact. The number of cusps may be zero. In particular, the standard cusp decomposition in the general rigidity construction follows from the complete finite-volume metric, with no knot or triangulation assumption.

facts:
**Given:** AC and the complete finite-volume manifold of the Statement.

[A1] Full choice is [[def-axiom-of-choice]].

[F1] The metric gives a quotient $M=\Gamma\backslash\mathbb H^3$ by a discrete torsion-free subgroup of $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb C)$. The model's point stabilizer $K=\mathrm{SO}(3)$ is compact and its isometry group is a smooth frame bundle over $\mathbb H^3$. [[lem-complete-curvature-minus-one-manifolds-are-kleinian-quotients]]

[F2] Centralizers and discrete abelian subgroups of the Möbius group are computed explicitly in the horocusp supplier: parabolic centralizers are translations, discrete diagonal torsion-free groups are cyclic, and discrete translation groups have rank at most two. [[lem-rank-two-kleinian-subgroups-give-proper-embedded-horocusps]]

[F3] The complete quotient is a proper metric space, by Hopf–Rinow. [[thm-hopf-rinow]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be the interior of a compact connected orientable three-manifold with one torus cusp and a complete finite-volume hyperbolic metric. In a neighborhood of its complete holonomy, the representation deformation space modulo conjugacy is a complex one-dimensional manifold, with local coordinate $s=\operatorname{tr}^2\rho(\mu)$ near $s=4$ for a chosen peripheral basis $(\mu,\lambda)$.

Augment a representation by choosing a common invariant line of its peripheral holonomy. The augmented deformation space is a smooth complex curve, with holomorphic eigenvalue-ratio logarithm coordinate $u$ vanishing at the complete point. The forgetful map to the ordinary conjugacy quotient is $s=4\cosh^2(u/2)$. The corresponding logarithm $v(u)$ for $\lambda$ satisfies $v(0)=0$ and $v(u)=\tau u+O(u^2)$. Here $\operatorname{Im}\tau\ne0$; it is positive for a positively oriented basis of the oriented horotorus, and changes sign if the basis orientation is reversed. In particular the eigenvalue logarithm is a coordinate on the augmented space, rather than a single-valued holomorphic coordinate on the ordinary quotient.

The pair $(u,v)$ records the local generalized filling parameters. The primitive slope equation $p u+q v(u)=2\pi i$ has its full-turn holonomy meaning for ordinary smooth filling when $\gcd(p,q)=1$; sufficiently large primitive coefficients admit such small solutions and smooth complete hyperbolic fillings. Nonprimitive ray parameters are not ordinary slopes.

facts:
**Given:** AC, the complete one-cusped metric and the chosen ordered peripheral basis.

[A1] AC supplies DC and countable choice for the analytic and geometric suppliers. [[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]], [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]

[F1] A complete oriented curvature-minus-one manifold is a Kleinian quotient, and finite volume supplies a compact smooth core with finitely many standard rank-two cusps. [[lem-complete-curvature-minus-one-manifolds-are-kleinian-quotients]], [[lem-finite-volume-hyperbolic-three-manifolds-have-finite-standard-cusp-decompositions]]

[F2] For any such finite-volume quotient, the ordinary conjugacy quotient has independent trace-squared coordinates; its augmented space has independent eigenvalue-ratio logarithms, the stated branched forgetful map and peripheral factorization. [[thm-augmented-finite-volume-hyperbolic-holonomy-coordinates]]

[F3] Holomorphic peripheral factors with nonreal complete values admit unique simultaneous small full-turn solutions for all sufficiently large real coefficient tuples, including the partially unfilled coordinates. [[lem-simultaneous-peripheral-full-turn-equations-have-small-solutions]]

[F4] Small augmented solutions with primitive full-turn meridians give smooth complete finite-volume ordinary fillings. [[thm-small-augmented-holonomy-deformations-have-smooth-geometric-fillings]]

[F5] Ordinary slopes are primitive pairs modulo sign, and the chosen-section length is a lattice norm up to a fixed invertible real-linear map. [[def-multicusped-dehn-filling]], [[def-cusp-slope-length]], [[def-pared-hyperbolic-structures-and-volume]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be the interior of a compact connected orientable three-manifold with $k\ge1$ torus cusps and a complete finite-volume hyperbolic metric. Choose an ordered peripheral basis on each cusp. For cusp $i$, let the generalized filling parameter sphere be $S_i=\mathbb R^2\cup\{\infty\}$, with $\infty$ denoting the complete cusp and primitive integral pairs modulo sign denoting ordinary slopes. There is a neighborhood $U$ of $(\infty,\ldots,\infty)$ in $\prod_{i=1}^k S_i$ such that every tuple in $U$ whose finite coordinates are primitive integral slopes determines a complete finite-volume hyperbolic metric on the corresponding ordinary Dehn filling; coordinates equal to $\infty$ remain unfilled complete cusps. Consequently, one may choose neighborhoods $U_i$ of $\infty$ with $\prod_i U_i\subseteq U$, and only finitely many primitive integral pairs at each cusp lie outside $U_i$. Thus every simultaneous filling whose slopes all lie in their respective $U_i$ is hyperbolic. Nonprimitive ray parameters may describe cone or orbifold completions but are not ordinary smooth fillings. No universal numeric length threshold or universal bound on the number of exceptional slopes is asserted.

facts:
**Given:** AC, the complete finite-volume metric with $k\ge1$ torus cusps and the chosen ordered peripheral bases.

[A1] AC and its countable-choice consequence are retained. [[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]], [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]

[F1] The full $k$-cusped local deformation-and-completeness theorem gives a product neighborhood of the complete generalized parameters and smooth complete finite-volume ordinary fillings for every primitive tuple therein, with the other cusps unfilled. [[lem-dehn-filling-deformation-and-completeness]]

[F2] Slopes and arbitrary supplied ordinary gluing maps have the stated primitive-pair convention. [[def-multicusped-dehn-filling]]

[F3] The input metric and volume convention are [[def-pared-hyperbolic-structures-and-volume]]. Each chosen-section cusp length is a norm on its rank-two peripheral lattice; changing section rescales it by a positive constant. [[def-cusp-slope-length]]

contract.heading: Example
contract.text: Let $K_8$ be the standard figure-eight knot, let $E_{K_8}$ be the exterior obtained by deleting the binding neighborhood from its open-book presentation, and use the positive meridian $\mu$ and preferred longitude $\lambda$. The exterior admits a complete finite-volume hyperbolic metric obtained by gluing two regular ideal tetrahedra, of total volume $2v_3=6\Lambda(\pi/3)\approx2.02988$, where $v_3=3\Lambda(\pi/3)$ is the volume of one regular ideal tetrahedron and $\Lambda$ is the Lobachevsky function. The ordinary zero filling along $\lambda$ is a torus bundle over $S^1$ with monodromy matrix $\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$ on the capped fiber homology, and the filled manifold admits no complete hyperbolic metric.

facts:
**Given:** The standard figure-eight knot with chosen compact exterior and peripheral basis $(\mu,\lambda)$, with $\lambda$ the preferred longitude.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: AC selects from every family of nonempty sets.

[F1] [[def-countable-choice]]: $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ selects from every countable family of nonempty sets.

[F2] [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]: in ZF, $\mathrm{AC}\Rightarrow\mathrm{DC}\Rightarrow\mathrm{AC}_\omega$.

[F3] [[lem-figure-eight-ideal-gluing-and-cusp-completeness]]: the standard two-tetrahedron gluing gives the figure-eight exterior a complete finite-volume hyperbolic metric, with total volume $2v_3$.

[F4] [[lem-zero-filling-of-fibered-knot-is-a-torus-bundle]]: filling the figure-eight exterior along $\lambda$ caps its once-punctured torus fiber and gives the torus bundle whose homology matrix is $\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$.

[F5] [[lem-closed-hyperbolic-three-manifold-has-no-z2-subgroup]]: a closed connected three-manifold with a complete curvature $-1$ metric has fundamental group with no subgroup isomorphic to $\mathbb Z^2$.

[F6] [[def-multicusped-dehn-filling]]: ordinary filling along $\lambda$ attaches a solid torus with meridian disk boundary in that slope.

[F7] [[def-covering-map-and-evenly-covered-neighbourhoods]]: the explicit pullback of a bundle along $\mathbb R\to S^1$ is a covering map.

[F8] [[thm-covering-maps-inject-fundamental-groups]]: every covering map induces an injective homomorphism on fundamental groups.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text: Fix the orientation-reversing reflection $r:S^3\to S^3$ chosen for the mirror convention in the oriented connected-sum definition. If $K$ is a smooth oriented knot, its mirror $r(K)$ carries the orientation induced from $K$ by $r$. The reverse mirror of $K$, denoted $K^\dagger$, is the image $r(K)$ with its knot orientation reversed. Thus $K^\dagger$ changes both the ambient orientation convention and the orientation of the knot.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For every smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$, let $B^4=\{x\in\mathbb R^4:\lVert x\rVert^2\le1\}$ with boundary $S^3$. The oriented connected sum $K\#K^\dagger$ bounds a smooth properly embedded disk $D\subset B^4$ for which the squared radial function $\rho(x)=\lVert x\rVert^2$ restricts to a Morse function on the interior of $D$ with all critical points of index $0$ or $1$.

facts:
**Given:** $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and a smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$.

[F1] A knot is a smooth embedding of an oriented circle in the standard oriented $S^3$; a small ball meeting it in a short trivial arc leaves a properly embedded smooth arc in the complementary ball. ([[def-oriented-link-in-s-three-and-ambient-isotopy]])

[F2] The connected sum uses the fixed reflection and orientation-reversing boundary gluing, and changing the local trivial arcs and ball charts does not change its oriented knot type under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. ([[def-knot-connected-sum-and-prime-knot]], [[lem-knot-connected-sum-well-defined]])

[F3] If a smooth family of maps is transverse as a total map to $\{0\}\subset\mathbb R$, then outside a null set of parameters its slice is transverse to $0$. ([[thm-parametric-transversality]])

[F4] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, an isotopy of embeddings of a compact source with boundary into the boundaryless manifold $S^3$ extends to an ambient isotopy supported in any prescribed neighborhood of its track. ([[thm-isotopy-extension]])

[F5] The reverse mirror is obtained by applying the fixed orientation-reversing reflection and reversing the knot orientation. ([[def-reverse-mirror-of-oriented-knot]])

[F6] A proper surface embedding has boundary preimage equal to its surface boundary; smooth surface charts give the required boundary behavior in the unit four-ball. ([[def-locally-flat-proper-surface-and-concordance-collars]])

[F7] A Morse function has nondegenerate critical points, and the index is the maximal dimension of a subspace on which its Hessian is negative definite. ([[def-morse-function-and-excellent-morse-function]], [[def-nondegenerate-critical-point-nullity-index-and-coindex]])

[A1] The Axiom of Countable Choice is the sequence-choice principle stated in the extension and transversality suppliers. ([[def-countable-choice]])

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. A smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere bounds a smooth properly embedded disk in the unit four-ball $B^4=\{x\in\mathbb R^4:\lVert x\rVert^2\le1\}$ if and only if it is smoothly concordant to the standard unknot.

facts:
**Given:** $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, a smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$, and one of the two asserted geometric objects.

[F1] A smooth concordance is a proper smooth annulus in $S^3\times I$ with product collars and oriented boundary $-K_0\times\{0\}\sqcup K_1\times\{1\}$. ([[def-smooth-knot-concordance]])

[F2] A smooth proper surface has smooth boundary charts and product collars; removing an interior disk from a disk leaves a smooth annulus. ([[def-locally-flat-proper-surface-and-concordance-collars]])

[F3] The standard unknot bounds its standard disk in the standard four-ball. ([[def-knot-connected-sum-and-prime-knot]])

[F4] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, an isotopy of compact smooth embeddings into $\mathbb R^4$ extends to an ambient isotopy supported in any prescribed neighborhood of its track. ([[thm-isotopy-extension]])

[A1] The Axiom of Countable Choice is the sequence-choice principle in [F4]. ([[def-countable-choice]])

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. If $K_0$ and $K_1$ are concordant in the smooth category and $J_0$ and $J_1$ are concordant in the same category, then $K_0\#J_0$ and $K_1\#J_1$ are smoothly concordant. The same implication holds when both given concordances and the resulting concordance are required to be locally flat and topological.

facts:
**Given:** $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, concordance annuli $A$ from $K_0$ to $K_1$ and $B$ from $J_0$ to $J_1$ in one of the two categories.

[F1] Each annulus is proper, has product collars at its endpoint knots, and has boundary orientation $-K_0\sqcup K_1$ or $-J_0\sqcup J_1$. ([[def-smooth-knot-concordance]], [[def-locally-flat-topological-knot-concordance]])

[F2] The oriented connected sum is obtained by deleting short trivial arcs and gluing with the fixed orientation-reversing boundary map; its class is independent of the local choices under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. ([[def-knot-connected-sum-and-prime-knot]], [[lem-knot-connected-sum-well-defined]])

[F3] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, $S^3$ is simply connected, continuous homotopies into a smooth manifold can be smoothly approximated relative to a closed region where they are already smooth, finite-dimensional smooth perturbations can be chosen transverse, compact smooth isotopies extend ambiently, and smooth submanifolds have tubular neighborhoods. ([[thm-higher-dimensional-spheres-are-simply-connected]], [[thm-relative-whitney-approximation-for-manifold-valued-maps]], [[thm-parametric-transversality]], [[thm-isotopy-extension]], [[thm-tubular-neighbourhood-theorem-in-a-smooth-ambient-manifold]], [[def-countable-choice]])

[F4] Ambient-isotopic oriented knot representatives may be changed by smooth families of orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms of $S^3$. A chosen point on a knot can be moved to any prescribed point by an isotopy of embeddings of that point, which extends ambiently under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. ([[def-oriented-link-in-s-three-and-ambient-isotopy]], [[thm-isotopy-extension]], [[def-countable-choice]])

[F5] Bare locally flat proper arcs with specified product end collars can be straightened by [[thm-locally-flat-codimension-three-arc-unknotting]]. This retained local result is not being strengthened into a relative transverse pair-tube or complement theorem.

[F6] **External TOP input, initially in ordinary ZFC:** connected sum is well-defined on the concordance classes of smooth oriented knots represented by proper locally flat annuli in $S^3\times I$. In particular, the two given annulus concordances imply an oriented locally flat annulus concordance between their endpoint connected sums, in the usual collared-end convention of [F1]. This is the TOP connected-sum operation in Ray, §3, Definition 3.1, Definition 3.5 and the discussion through Proposition 3.6, printed II–11–II–12. It is imported here, not presented as a locally reconstructed pair-tube/complement proof.

[F7] **External set-theoretic input:** for a real $r\subseteq\omega$, the relativized constructible class $L[r]$ is a transitive inner model of ZFC containing $r$ and all natural numbers. Karagila, §8.3, closing remarks, printed p.42, gives the $L[A]$ construction and its inner-ZFC conclusion; for a real parameter, $r\subseteq\omega\subseteq L[r]$, so the parameter belongs to that model. No ambient full AC is assumed by this input. The compact coding argument below, rather than an implication from ambient full AC, supplies the Countable Choice specialization of [F6].

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For every smooth oriented knot $K$ in the standard oriented three-sphere, let $\mathcal S_{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$ be the set of genera $g(F)\in\mathbb N_0$ of connected compact orientable smooth properly embedded surfaces $F\subset B^4$ with oriented boundary $K$, and let $\mathcal S_{\mathrm{top}}(K)$ be the corresponding set for locally flat topologically properly embedded surfaces. For each surface, $g(F)$ is the nonnegative integer determined by $\chi(F)=1-2g(F)$. Both sets are nonempty and have least elements.

facts:
**Given:** $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and a smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$.

[F1] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, $K$ bounds a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface $\Sigma\subset S^3$ with oriented boundary $K$. ([[thm-every-oriented-knot-bounds-a-seifert-surface]])

[F2] For a connected compact orientable surface with one boundary component, $g(\Sigma)\in\mathbb N_0$ is determined by $\chi(\Sigma)=1-2g(\Sigma)$. ([[def-oriented-seifert-surface-and-knot-genus]])

[F3] A smooth boundary has a smooth collar; in the standard unit ball the boundary collar is $(x,u)\mapsto(1-u)x$ for $x\in S^3$ and sufficiently small $u\ge0$. ([[thm-collar-neighborhood-theorem]], [[def-euclidean-spheres-and-closed-balls]])

[F4] A proper surface is locally flat when it has the stated plane-pair charts at interior and boundary points; a smooth proper surface has such topological charts. ([[def-locally-flat-proper-surface-and-concordance-collars]])

[A1] The Axiom of Countable Choice is the sequence-choice principle stated in the supplier. ([[def-countable-choice]])

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. The set of smooth oriented knot concordance classes in the standard three-sphere is an abelian group under connected sum, with identity the standard unknot and inverse of $[K]$ represented by the reverse mirror $K^\dagger$. Separately, the set of locally flat topological oriented knot concordance classes is an abelian group under connected sum, with the same identity and inverse convention.

facts:
**Given:** $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the smooth and topological concordance relations, and their oriented connected-sum operation.

[F1] Smooth and locally flat topological concordance are equivalence relations on oriented ambient-isotopy classes. ([[lem-smooth-and-topological-knot-concordance-is-an-equivalence-relation]])

[F2] Concordance respects connected sum in both categories under the stated $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. The smooth implication is the retained local annulus construction. The TOP implication uses the explicitly imported classical operation and the compact real-code/$L[r]$ specialization in the compatibility supplier; it is not inferred from bare-core straightening. ([[lem-knot-concordance-compatible-with-connected-sum]])

[F3] On oriented ambient-isotopy classes, connected sum is associative and commutative and has the standard unknot as two-sided identity under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. ([[thm-oriented-knot-connected-sum-is-a-commutative-monoid]])

[F4] For every smooth oriented knot $K$, $K\#K^\dagger$ bounds a smooth properly embedded disk in $B^4$; the disk is locally flat as a topological proper surface. ([[lem-general-knot-reverse-mirror-sum-is-ribbon]], [[def-locally-flat-proper-surface-and-concordance-collars]])

[F5] A knot bounds a smooth proper disk in $B^4$ if and only if it is smoothly concordant to the standard unknot. ([[lem-smooth-slice-iff-concordant-to-unknot]])

[A1] The Axiom of Countable Choice is used by the actual connected-sum and isotopy-extension supplier branches cited in this theorem; the TOP external input is specialized to the required compact data under that same hypothesis in [F2], rather than assuming ambient full Choice. ([[def-countable-choice]], [[thm-oriented-knot-connected-sum-is-a-commutative-monoid]], [[lem-knot-connected-sum-well-defined]])

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere and let $B^4$ be the standard four-ball with boundary $S^3$. Let $\mathcal S_{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$ be the set of genera of connected compact orientable smooth properly embedded surfaces $F\subset B^4$ with oriented boundary $K$. Let $\mathcal S_{\mathrm{top}}(K)$ be the set of genera of connected compact orientable locally flat topologically properly embedded surfaces $F\subset B^4$ with oriented boundary $K$. For each such surface, its genus $g(F)$ is the nonnegative integer determined by $\chi(F)=1-2g(F)$. Define the smooth slice genus and the locally flat topological slice genus by

$$
g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K):=\min\mathcal S_{\mathrm{sm}}(K),\qquad g_4^{\mathrm{top}}(K):=\min\mathcal S_{\mathrm{top}}(K).
$$

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be disjoint finite rational $1$-cycles in the boundary $S^3$ of the standard oriented $4$-ball $B^4$, each represented as a finite rational linear combination of oriented knots. Let $P$ and $Q$ be finite rational $2$-chains in $B^4$ with $\partial P=\alpha$ and $\partial Q=\beta$, with common standard product collars at their respective boundaries and with their interiors in general position. Then the signed interior intersection number $P\cdot Q$ equals the bilinear extension of the linking number $\operatorname{lk}(\alpha,\beta)$ defined by positive meridians in $S^3$.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, disjoint oriented boundary cycles in $S^3$, collared rational bounding chains in $B^4$, and general position for their interiors.

[A1] The Axiom of Choice is assumed in the supplied topological linking-number convention. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] For disjoint oriented knots, linking is the signed intersection of the first knot with an oriented Seifert surface spanning the second. [[thm-linking-number-equals-signed-intersection]]

[F5] Every oriented knot in $S^3$ bounds a compact oriented smooth Seifert surface. [[thm-every-oriented-knot-bounds-a-seifert-surface]]

[F2] A compact oriented $1$-manifold has signed boundary count zero. [[lem-oriented-boundary-of-a-compact-oriented-one-manifold-has-zero-signed-count]]

[F3] The standard $4$-ball is contractible, so its interior has zero second rational homology. [[cor-contractible-nonempty-spaces-have-the-homology-of-a-point]]

[F4] The local sign of a transverse intersection is determined by the ordered tangent bases and ambient orientation; boundary orientations use the outward-normal-first convention and product orientations preserve the stated factor order. [[def-oriented-intersection-number]], [[def-local-oriented-intersection-sign]], [[def-induced-boundary-orientation]], [[def-product-orientation]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume full AC. Let $D$ be a locally flat properly embedded disk in the standard four-ball $B^4$ with boundary an oriented knot $K\subset S^3$, and let $F\subset S^3$ be a connected oriented Seifert surface for $K$. After matching product collars and pushing the interior of $F$ slightly into $B^4$, the closed locally flat surface $\Sigma=F\cup_KD$ bounds a compact connected oriented locally flat three-manifold $R\subset B^4$. The conclusion includes an oriented ambient product neighborhood of $R$ on both sides, with the positive normal push-off along the $F$ portion of $\partial R=\Sigma$ lying on the complementary side of $R$.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, the locally flat disk and surface of the Statement and their matching boundary collars. The first part additionally assumes that the disk is smooth; the final part proves the TOP branch using the explicitly cited external normal-bundle and transversality inputs.

[A1] Full AC implies the countable-choice hypotheses of the smooth approximation, ODE and transversality suppliers. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] A locally flat surface has the pair charts and prescribed boundary collars in the Definition. For a smooth surface these are smooth charts. The Definition alone does not assert a global TOP normal disk bundle. [[def-locally-flat-proper-surface-and-concordance-collars]]

[F2] Local smooth ODEs, the inverse-function theorem and Euclidean smooth approximation apply with compact parameters. Parametric transversality applies to finite smooth perturbation families. [[thm-time-dependent-vector-fields-have-local-smooth-evolution-operators]], [[thm-smooth-inverse-function-theorem-on-manifolds]], [[thm-whitney-approximation-for-euclidean-valued-maps]], [[thm-parametric-transversality]]

[F3] Boundary linking equals the intersection of collared bounding chains in the four-ball. Smooth compact manifolds have finite CW homotopy models under countable choice. [[lem-linking-number-equals-four-dimensional-intersection-number]], [[lem-compact-smooth-manifolds-have-finite-cw-models-under-countable-choice]]

[F4] Mayer–Vietoris computes the actual collared decomposition homology; the oriented meridian is dual to a Seifert surface. [[thm-excision-and-mayer-vietoris-with-local-coefficients]], [[thm-linking-number-equals-signed-intersection]]

[F5] Alexander duality gives the meridional complement class for the capped locally flat surface, but it supplies no regular fiber or collar at that surface. [[thm-alexander-duality-for-compact-locally-contractible-subsets-of-a-sphere]]

[F6] **External input — relative TOP normal bundle.** Freedman–Quinn, Theorem 9.3A, printed137–141, supplies an actual rank-two normal vector bundle for a locally flat proper surface in a TOP four-manifold, relative to a supplied normal bundle near a closed subset, including a boundary collar. Its neighborhood embedding agrees with that germ after restriction. This is only the normal-bundle input; it does not assert a circle-map fiber or a Seifert hypersurface. The usual full-AC setting of the Statement is retained.

[F7] **External input — strongly relative TOP transversality.** Quinn1988, Theorem printed145: for proper submanifolds $M,X\subset Y$, a specified normal microbundle $\xi$ of $X$, and closed $C\subset D\subset Y$, if $M$ is transverse to $\xi$ near $C$, an isotopy of $M$, supported in any prescribed neighborhood of $(D\setminus C)\cap M\cap X$, makes it transverse near $D$. Boundary properness is part of the theorem. Transversality means that the intersection is a manifold whose normal microbundle in $M$ is the restriction of the specified $\xi$. The theorem includes the dimensions used below, namely $4$-submanifolds of a $5$-manifold with intersection dimension $3$. This theorem is imported, not reconstructed locally.

[F8] **External input — circle representatives on TOP manifolds.** Metrizable TOP manifolds have CW homotopy type by the ANR/CW-type criterion of Milnor1959. On that homotopy type, Hatcher Proposition1B.9 for $S^1=K(\mathbb Z,1)$ represents every integral first-cohomology class by a continuous map to $S^1$; two such maps with the same induced integer homomorphism are homotopic. These classification inputs are used only to construct a continuous meridian map. They are not transversality assertions.


[F9] An actual compact TOP manifold with boundary has a TOP product collar of its entire boundary. Apply this only after the exterior has been constructed as such a manifold. [[thm-topological-collaring-for-manifold-boundaries]]

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Assume the full Axiom of Choice when a knot's Seifert pairing is formed. An integral Seifert lattice is a pair $(H,V)$ in which $H$ is a free abelian group of rank $2g$ for some $g\geq0$, and $V:H\times H\to\mathbb Z$ is bilinear with $V-V^T$ unimodular. The rank-zero lattice is allowed, with the determinant of its empty skew matrix equal to $1$. A metabolizer is a primitive direct summand $M\subset H$ of rank $g$ such that $V(x,y)=0$ for every $x,y\in M$; the lattice is metabolic when it has a metabolizer. A chosen Seifert surface of an oriented knot gives such a lattice through the positive-push pairing. Its form is algebraically slice when that lattice is metabolic.

An isomorphism of integral Seifert lattices $(H,V)$ and $(H',V')$ is an integral group isomorphism $P:H\to H'$ satisfying $V'(Px,Py)=V(x,y)$ for all $x,y\in H$. Let $\mathcal S$ be the commutative monoid of these isomorphism classes under orthogonal direct sum, where $(H,V)\oplus(H',V')$ has underlying group $H\oplus H'$ and pairing $V\oplus V'$, with the rank-zero lattice as identity. The integral algebraic concordance group $G_{\mathbb Z}$ is the abelian group generated by symbols $[V]$ for $[V]\in\mathcal S$, subject to $[V\oplus W]=[V]+[W]$ and $[M]=0$ for every metabolic lattice $M$. Two selected Seifert forms are algebraically concordant when they represent the same element of $G_{\mathbb Z}$. This form relation does not assert the existence of a smooth or locally flat topological concordance annulus between the knots.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume full AC. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the oriented standard $3$-sphere, let $F\subset S^3$ be a connected compact smooth oriented Seifert surface of genus $g$, and let $D\subset B^4$ be a locally flat properly embedded disk with oriented boundary $K$. Then the positive-push Seifert lattice $(H_1(F;\mathbb Z),V)$ is metabolic: it has a rank-$g$ primitive direct summand on which $V$ vanishes identically.

**Given:** Full AC, a Seifert surface $F$ of genus $g$, and a locally flat slice disk $D$ with the same oriented boundary knot.

[A1] Full AC is the family-of-nonempty-sets choice axiom used by the Seifert-pairing convention. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] For an ordered integral basis of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$, the matrix entries are $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$, and $V$ is bilinear on homology. [[def-knot-seifert-pairing-and-matrix]], [[lem-seifert-pairing-well-defined]]

[F2] Poincaré–Lefschetz duality for a compact oriented $3$-manifold $R$ with boundary $\Sigma$ identifies $H_i(R,\Sigma;\mathbb Q)$ with $H^{3-i}(R;\mathbb Q)$. [[thm-poincare-lefschetz-duality]]

[F3] The linking number of disjoint rational boundary cycles in $S^3=\partial B^4$ is the signed intersection number of collared rational $2$-chains in $B^4$ that bound them. [[lem-linking-number-equals-four-dimensional-intersection-number]]

[F4] A $g$-dimensional rational subspace on which $V$ vanishes saturates to a rank-$g$ direct summand of the integral lattice, still with vanishing restriction. [[lem-rational-isotropic-subspace-saturates-to-integral-metabolizer]]

[F5] For the given locally flat slice disk the hypersurface supplier constructs the compact oriented locally flat Seifert three-manifold with an actual two-sided product and positive-push alignment. Its pre-collar-push model meets the outer sphere in $F$, with the stated product corners at $K$. Its smooth branch remains the previously supplied smooth construction; its TOP branch explicitly imports separate relative normal-bundle and microbundle-transversality theorems. [[lem-locally-flat-slice-surface-bounds-seifert-hypersurface]]

[F6] Smooth chains compute continuous real homology, including for a smooth manifold with boundary. This is invoked below only in smooth ambient neighborhoods, not by treating a locally flat $R$ as an already smooth submanifold. [[thm-smooth-singular-chains-compute-singular-homology]]

[F7] Under full AC a compact TOP three-manifold has a finite compatible PL triangulation, with boundary a subcomplex. In particular its Betti numbers and Euler characteristic are finite. This is intrinsic to the three-manifold and does not smooth its embedding in the four-ball. [[thm-compact-topological-three-manifolds-admit-finite-pl-triangulations]]

contract.heading: Statement refuted
contract.text: Every abstract oriented cobordism between two oriented knot circles in the standard three-sphere can be realized by a smoothly embedded concordance annulus in $S^3\times[0,1]$.

facts:
**Given:** The standard unknot $U$, the standard right-handed trefoil $T$, and the claim in the Statement refuted.

[F1] An abstract oriented cobordism is a compact oriented surface with boundary $-C_0\sqcup C_1$ and contains no ambient embedding data. ([[def-abstract-oriented-knot-cobordism]])

[F2] The Seifert matrix convention in the library is $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$ for a chosen oriented surface and basis; the surface and basis are part of the data until invariance is proved. ([[def-knot-seifert-pairing-and-matrix]])

[F3] A trefoil Seifert surface admits a rank-two Seifert matrix whose symmetric sum is $\begin{pmatrix}-2&1\\1&-2\end{pmatrix}$; if the cited convention uses the transpose matrix, the symmetric sum is unchanged. For a real symmetric matrix, its signature is the number of positive eigenvalues minus the number of negative eigenvalues. (Collins, Theorem 2.2.9 and Example 2.2.13, https://era.ed.ac.uk/bitstream/handle/1842/5034/Collins2011.pdf?sequence=4)

[F4] The standard unknot bounds a disk in $S^3$; the disk is contractible, so its first homology is zero and its symmetrized Seifert form has signature $0$. ([[def-knot-connected-sum-and-prime-knot]])

[F5] A metabolizer for a rank-two integral Seifert form is a rank-one direct summand $L$ with $V(x,y)=0$ for $x,y\in L$. Thus every nonzero $x\in L$ satisfies $x^T(V+V^T)x=2V(x,x)=0$. This is immediate from the defining bilinear relation, with no signature-invariance or general signature-vanishing theorem. ([[def-metabolic-seifert-form-and-algebraic-knot-concordance]])

[F6] Under the Axiom of Countable Choice, a knot is smoothly slice if and only if it is smoothly concordant to the standard unknot. ([[lem-smooth-slice-iff-concordant-to-unknot]])

[A1] Full Axiom of Choice is assumed by the supplied Seifert-pairing definition. ([[def-axiom-of-choice]])

[A2] Full Axiom of Choice implies the countable-choice hypothesis used by [F6]. ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]])

[F7] For a smooth slice disk, the actual smooth branch of [[lem-slice-disk-induces-seifert-metabolizer]] constructs a metabolizer for every specified smooth Seifert surface: its Proof1.1–2.2 uses the actual smooth hypersurface and positive product constructed in Proof1.1–7.1 of [[lem-locally-flat-slice-surface-bounds-seifert-hypersurface]]. The separate unresolved TOP branches are not used here. This direct finite-form obstruction needs neither surface-choice invariance nor a general signature-vanishing theorem.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Assume the full Axiom of Choice when an integral Seifert lattice comes from a knot's positive-push pairing. For an integral Seifert lattice $(H,V)$, its integral Witt class is its class in $G_{\mathbb Z}$ from the definition of metabolic Seifert form and algebraic knot concordance. An isomorphism $(W,B,T)\to(W',B',T')$ of rational isometric structures is a rational-linear bijection $P:W\to W'$ such that $B'(Px,Py)=B(x,y)$ and $PT=T'P$. A rational isometric structure is a triple $(W,B,T)$ in which $W$ is a finite-dimensional even-dimensional $\mathbb Q$-vector space, $B:W\times W\to\mathbb Q$ is a nonsingular symmetric bilinear form, $T:W\to W$ is an invertible linear map satisfying $B(Tx,Ty)=B(x,y)$ for all $x,y\in W$, and $I-T$ is invertible. Such a structure is metabolic if it has a $T$-invariant subspace $L\subset W$ with $\dim_{\mathbb Q}L=\frac12\dim_{\mathbb Q}W$ and $B|_{L\times L}=0$. Define the rational Witt group $G_{\mathbb Q}$ by direct sum of isomorphism classes, with metabolic structures set equal to zero. For a nonsingular integral Seifert matrix $V$, the associated matrix pair is $(B,T)=(V+V^T,V^{-1}V^T)$; whether this pair is a rational isometric structure is established separately.

The definition concerns finite-rank bilinear forms and isometry data. It does not identify the unrelated Witt Lie algebra with either $G_{\mathbb Z}$ or $G_{\mathbb Q}$.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the full Axiom of Choice. A positive Hopf band is an oriented annulus whose two boundary components, with their induced orientations, have linking number $+1$. Let $F$ be the genus-one Seifert surface obtained by plumbing two positive Hopf bands in a square, with oriented core curves $a,b$ forming a positive handle basis, and choose the plumbing side so that $a^+$ bounds a disk in $S^3$ disjoint from $b$. The oriented boundary of this standard positive two-band plumbing is the right-handed trefoil. In the positive-push convention $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$ with ordered basis $(a,b)$, the Seifert matrix is
$$
V=\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\-1&-1\end{pmatrix}.
$$

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the full Axiom of Choice for knot Seifert pairings. Let $G_{\mathbb Q}$ be the rational Witt group of finite-dimensional even-dimensional nonsingular symmetric rational forms equipped with an invertible isometry $T$ for which $I-T$ is invertible, modulo metabolic $T$-invariant subspaces, and let $G_{\mathbb Z}$ be the integral algebraic concordance group of Seifert lattices. The rational algebraic concordance classification due to Levine and the integral classification completed by Stoltzfus identify each of these abelian groups, as an abstract group, with
$$
\mathbb Z^{(\mathbb N)}\oplus(\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z)^{(\mathbb N)}\oplus(\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z)^{(\mathbb N)}.
$$
Here $A^{(\mathbb N)}$ denotes the direct sum of countably infinitely many copies of the abelian group $A$; the statement does not identify Levine's rational classification with the distinct integral group or claim that their defining objects are the same.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC and the two groups in the Statement, with their original defining objects and metabolic relations.

[A1] Full AC is assumed as stated. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] The integral group uses finite integral Seifert lattices with unimodular skew part, and the rational group uses the even-dimensional rational isometric structures in the Statement. [[def-metabolic-seifert-form-and-algebraic-knot-concordance]], [[def-integral-witt-and-seifert-isometric-structures]]

[F2] Integral Seifert classes admit invertible representatives, and the associated rational structure defines an injective homomorphism $\iota:G_{\mathbb Z}\hookrightarrow G_{\mathbb Q}$. This includes singular-matrix reduction and saturation of rational metabolizers. [[thm-integral-seifert-witt-group-injects-into-rational-isometric-group]]

[F3] Rational isometric classes split as the direct sum of their self-reciprocal primary groups. For each irreducible $p\ne t+1$ the primary group is the hermitian Witt group of the number field $E=\mathbb Q[t]/(p)$ with involution $t\mapsto t^{-1}$, and the $t+1$ group is the even-dimensional symmetric Witt group over $\mathbb Q$. [[thm-rational-isometric-witt-group-has-reciprocal-primary-decomposition]], [[thm-rational-primary-isometric-classes-are-hermitian-witt-classes]]

[F4] The kernel of all hermitian signatures over each quadratic number-field extension is killed by four. The rational symmetric signature kernel is also killed by four, including on its even-dimensional subgroup. [[thm-hermitian-number-field-signature-kernel-is-killed-by-four]], [[thm-rational-symmetric-signature-kernel-is-killed-by-four]]

[F5] The explicit integral matrices $F_b=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&b\end{pmatrix}$, $P_n=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&-n^2\end{pmatrix}$, and $Q_q=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&-(3q-1)/4\end{pmatrix}$, for $b,n\ge1$ and primes $q\equiv3\pmod4$, $q\ne3$, lie in distinct quadratic primary components. The first family is independent of infinite order, the second has exact order two, and the third exact order four. The $P_n$ have independent images in $G_{\mathbb Z}/2G_{\mathbb Z}$. [[lem-integral-algebraic-concordance-has-independent-free-two-and-four-torsion-families]]

[F6] A countable abelian group mapping to a countable direct sum of copies of $\mathbb Z$ with exponent-four kernel splits into countably many free, order-two, and order-four summands. The three multiplicities are infinite under the precise independent-family tests in that lemma. [[lem-countable-signature-groups-with-exponent-four-kernel-split]]

contract.text: Assume full AC. Let $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sm}}$ and $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{top}}$ denote, respectively, the smooth and locally flat topological concordance groups of smooth oriented knots in the standard oriented $3$-sphere, with connected sum as operation. Let $G_{\mathbb Z}$ be the integral algebraic concordance group generated by integral Seifert lattices modulo direct-sum and metabolic relations. In either category $\mathcal C$, the rule $[K]\mapsto[(H_1(F;\mathbb Z),V_F)]$, where $F$ is any connected oriented Seifert surface of $K$ and $V_F$ is its positive-push Seifert pairing, defines a surjective group homomorphism $\Phi_{\mathcal C}:\mathcal C\to G_{\mathbb Z}$.

Transporting an oriented surface under an oriented ambient isotopy preserves its matrix in the transported basis. [[lem-seifert-matrices-of-a-knot-are-s-equivalent]], [[lem-seifert-matrix-s-enlargement-preserves-algebraic-concordance-class]], [[lem-seifert-matrix-s-equivalence-under-isotopy]]

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text: Let $K_0,K_1$ be smooth oriented knots in the standard oriented three-sphere $S^3$, and let $I=[0,1]$. They are locally flat topologically concordant if there is a topological proper embedding $f:S^1\times I\to S^3\times I$ whose image is a locally flat annulus, whose boundary circles are $K_0\times\{0\}$ and $K_1\times\{1\}$, and whose annulus orientation induces the boundary $-K_0\times\{0\}\sqcup K_1\times\{1\}$. The annulus must have product collars at both ends. No differentiability of the annulus is assumed.

contract.heading: Statement refuted
contract.text: Assume full AC. The false claim is: every positive-rank integral Seifert lattice with unimodular alternating part is metabolic. The right-handed trefoil's positive-push Seifert lattice has $V=\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\-1&-1\end{pmatrix}$ and $V-V^T=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix}$. Its invertible matrix gives the rational isometric structure with $B=V+V^T=\begin{pmatrix}-2&-1\\-1&-2\end{pmatrix}$, which is negative definite; the rational extension of $V$ has no isotropic line, so the rational-to-integral saturation lemma has no input. No rank-one integral subgroup has zero Seifert self-pairing, so the lattice is not metabolic.

[F2] A metabolic rank-two lattice must have a rank-one subgroup on which $V$ vanishes, and hence every vector in that subgroup has zero self-pairing. [[def-metabolic-seifert-form-and-algebraic-knot-concordance]]

[F3] Since $V$ is invertible, $(V+V^T,V^{-1}V^T)$ satisfies the rational isometric-structure definition. [[def-integral-witt-and-seifert-isometric-structures]], [[lem-invertible-seifert-matrix-gives-rational-isometric-structure]]

[F4] A rational isotropic line for an integral bilinear form saturates to a rank-one integral direct summand with zero restriction. [[lem-rational-isotropic-subspace-saturates-to-integral-metabolizer]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Let $H$ be a free abelian group of rank $2g$ and let $V:H\times H\to\mathbb Z$ be a bilinear form. Write $H_{\mathbb Q}=H\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$ and extend $V$ $\mathbb Q$-bilinearly to $H_{\mathbb Q}$. If $L\subset H_{\mathbb Q}$ is a $\mathbb Q$-subspace of dimension $g$ and $V(x,y)=0$ for all $x,y\in L$, then $M=H\cap L$ is a rank-$g$ direct summand of $H$ and $V|_{M\times M}=0$.

facts:
**Given:** A finite-rank free abelian group $H$, an integral bilinear form $V$, and a $g$-dimensional rational isotropic subspace $L\subset H_{\mathbb Q}$, where $\operatorname{rank}H=2g$.

[A1] The displayed hypotheses are the complete input; no choice axiom is used.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot, let $F\subset S^3$ be a connected compact smooth oriented Seifert surface of genus $g$, and let $V$ be its positive-push Seifert matrix, with entries $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$ in an ordered integral basis of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$. Let $\Delta_K(t)$ be the Alexander polynomial normalized by $\Delta_K(t)\doteq\det(V-tV^T)$, where $p\doteq q$ means $p=\pm t^kq$ for some $k\in\mathbb Z$. If the integral Seifert lattice is metabolic, then there is an $f(t)\in\mathbb Z[t]$ such that $\Delta_K(t)\doteq f(t)f(t^{-1})$. The same factorization is necessary if $K$ bounds a locally flat properly embedded disk in the standard four-ball $B^4$. This is a necessary condition for either algebraic or locally flat sliceness, not a sufficient condition. The factorization concerns the Alexander polynomial $\Delta_K$, not the separate knot-normalized fraction $D_K(t)=\Delta_K(t)/(1-t)$.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, an oriented knot $K$, a connected oriented Seifert surface $F$, its positive-push matrix $V$, and either a metabolizer for $V$ or a locally flat proper slice disk for $K$.

[A1] Full AC is the family-of-nonempty-sets choice axiom used by the knot Seifert-pairing convention. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] The positive-push matrix represents the integral Seifert pairing, with the stated linking convention. [[def-knot-seifert-pairing-and-matrix]]

[F2] The generator of the zeroth Alexander elementary ideal satisfies $\Delta_K(t)\doteq\det(V-tV^T)$ in this convention. [[thm-seifert-determinant-is-the-knot-alexander-polynomial]]

[F3] A metabolic Seifert lattice has a rank-$g$ direct summand on which the pairing vanishes. [[def-metabolic-seifert-form-and-algebraic-knot-concordance]]

[F4] For any integral rank-$2g$ bilinear form with unimodular skew part and a rank-$g$ direct-summand metabolizer, its determinant is $t^gf(t)f(t^{-1})$ for some $f\in\mathbb Z[t]$. [[lem-metabolic-seifert-form-implies-fox-milnor-factorization]]

[F5] Under full AC the actual slice-metabolizer supplier proves that every locally flat proper slice disk induces the required integral rank-$g$ primitive metabolizer. Its TOP branch uses the explicitly sourced geometric inputs of the Seifert-hypersurface supplier and retains the local duality, isotropy and integral-saturation argument. [[lem-slice-disk-induces-seifert-metabolizer]]
