contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume full AC. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot, let $F$ be a connected compact smooth oriented Seifert surface of genus $g$, and let $V$ be the positive-push Seifert matrix in an ordered integral basis. Suppose the integral Seifert lattice has a rank-$g$ direct summand $M$ on which $V$ vanishes identically. For every $\omega\in S^1\setminus\{1\}$ with $\Delta_K(\omega)\ne0$, the Levine–Tristram signature $\sigma_\omega(K)$ is zero. The assertion concerns only points away from Alexander roots; no value at a root is asserted here.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, a knot Seifert matrix $V$ of size $2g$, a rank-$g$ direct-summand metabolizer $M$, and $\omega\in S^1\setminus\{1\}$ with $\Delta_K(\omega)\ne0$.

[A1] Full AC is the choice axiom stated by the knot Seifert-pairing convention; the finite-dimensional Hermitian argument below is choice-free. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] In an ordered integral basis, $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. [[def-knot-seifert-pairing-and-matrix]]

[F2] A metabolizer is a rank-$g$ direct summand $M$ with $V(x,y)=0$ for every $x,y\in M$. [[def-metabolic-seifert-form-and-algebraic-knot-concordance]]

[F3] The determinant $d_V(t)=\det(V-tV^T)$ differs from $\Delta_K(t)$ by a Laurent unit. [[thm-seifert-determinant-is-the-knot-alexander-polynomial]]

[F4] The matrix $H_\omega(V)=(1-\omega)V+(1-\bar\omega)V^T$ is Hermitian, and its signature is the value $\sigma_\omega(K)$. [[def-levine-tristram-hermitian-form-and-signature]]

[F5] The nonroot Levine–Tristram signature is independent of the chosen surface and basis. [[lem-seifert-stabilization-preserves-levine-tristram-signature]]

contract.heading: Example
contract.text: Assume full AC. Let $T$ be the right-handed trefoil obtained by plumbing two positive Hopf bands, with positive-push Seifert matrix $V=\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\-1&-1\end{pmatrix}$. Let $T^\dagger$ be its reverse mirror and set $S=T\#T^\dagger$. Then $S$ bounds a smooth proper disk in $B^4$ for which the squared radial function has only index-$0$ and index-$1$ interior critical points. A Seifert matrix for $S$ is $W=\operatorname{diag}(V,-V^T)$, the rank-$2$ direct summand $M=\langle e_1+e_4,e_2+e_3\rangle\subset\mathbb Z^4$ is a metabolizer for $W$, and $\Delta_S(t)\doteq (t^2-t+1)^2$. In particular, with $f(t)=t^2-t+1$, the determinant is a Laurent-unit multiple of $f(t)f(t^{-1})$.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, the positive Hopf-plumbed trefoil $T$, its reverse mirror $T^\dagger$, and the connected sum $S=T\#T^\dagger$.

[A1] Full AC is the family-of-nonempty-sets choice axiom used by the Seifert-pairing convention. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] Full AC implies the Axiom of Countable Choice required by the ribbon-disk supplier. [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]

[F2] In the stated positive-push basis, the trefoil matrix is $V=\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\-1&-1\end{pmatrix}$. [[lem-positive-hopf-plumbing-has-trefoil-seifert-matrix]]

[F3] The reverse mirror is obtained by the fixed orientation-reversing reflection and reversal of the knot orientation. [[def-reverse-mirror-of-oriented-knot]]

[F4] The connected sum uses the fixed oriented ball-gluing convention, independent of the allowed local choices. [[def-knot-connected-sum-and-prime-knot]], [[lem-knot-connected-sum-well-defined]]

[F5] Every smooth knot $K$ has a smooth proper disk for $K\#K^\dagger$ with only index-$0$ and index-$1$ interior radial critical points, under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. [[lem-general-knot-reverse-mirror-sum-is-ribbon]]

[F6] The Alexander polynomial satisfies $\Delta_S(t)\doteq\det(W-tW^T)$ for this positive-push matrix. [[thm-seifert-determinant-is-the-knot-alexander-polynomial]]

contract.heading: Statement refuted
contract.text: Assume full AC, and let $T$ be the right-handed trefoil whose positive-push Seifert matrix in the ordered Hopf-core basis is $V=\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\-1&-1\end{pmatrix}$. The claim refuted is that $T$ bounds a locally flat properly embedded disk in the standard four-ball $B^4$.

contract.text: Assume AC. Let $D\subset B^4$ be a smooth proper disk with boundary $K\subset S^3$. The positive meridian is the oriented circle $\{x\}\times\partial D^2$ in the overlap $D^2\times S^1$, oriented by the ambient and disk orientations.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $S_0,S_1$ be compact connected oriented smooth surfaces with nonempty smooth boundary. Supply finite smooth triangle presentations: face-to-face triangular disks, with circular interior vertex links and interval boundary links, whose parametrizations are smooth nonsingular maps in surface charts through each closed triangle. Suppose the two presentations have the same Euler characteristic and the same positive number $b$ of boundary components.

For any bijection of their boundary components, any orientation-preserving smooth circle maps on the paired components, and any prescribed inward collar germs, there is an orientation-preserving smooth diffeomorphism $B:S_0\to S_1$ realizing those circle maps and their collar identifications. In particular one may prescribe one marked point on each boundary circle. The diffeomorphism can additionally agree with finitely many prescribed orientation-preserving interior diffeomorphism germs at distinct points with distinct target points, while retaining the boundary collars.

All surface presentations are supplied finite data. No triangulation-existence, arbitrary topological smoothing, three-dimensional smoothing or unproved smooth classification result is assumed.

facts:
**Given:** The finite smooth surface data, equal Euler characteristics, paired boundary components and their oriented maps and collars, and optional finite interior germs.

[F1] A closed finite triangulated oriented surface has a one-polygon presentation. Finite polygon subdivisions, diagonal cuts/merges, inverse-pair cancellation and interlaced-handle extraction give its oriented commutator normal form. These are finite constructions without choice; the supplied smooth realizations are handled explicitly below rather than assuming that a topological homeomorphism is smooth. ([[lem-finite-triangulated-surface-reduces-to-a-one-polygon-schema]], [[lem-polygonal-schema-reduction-moves]])

[F2] Smooth Jordan disks have actual smooth parametrizations. Every oriented boundary diffeomorphism extends over such a disk with prescribed boundary collar and one prescribed positive interior germ. ([[lem-smooth-jordan-disk-boundary-maps-extend-to-diffeomorphisms]])

[F3] A boundary connected sum with a standard disk, rounded in actual collar coordinates, preserves smooth diffeomorphism type. Compact-source embedding isotopies, with support in a specified neighborhood, extend to ambient isotopies. Both statements hold under Countable Choice. ([[lem-boundary-connected-sum-with-a-disk-does-not-change-the-diffeomorphism-type]], [[lem-isotopy-extension-for-a-compact-source-with-boundary]])

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text: Assume countable choice as required by the chosen tubular-neighborhood and peripheral-system data. Let K be a smooth oriented knot with compact exterior E_K, positive meridian mu_K, and preferred longitude lambda_K on the boundary torus. The zero-framed surgery manifold M(K) is the closed oriented 3-manifold obtained by gluing D²×S¹ to E_K so that the meridian boundary circle of D²×{1} is identified with lambda_K and the core {0}×S¹ is identified with mu_K. The orientation extends the orientation of E_K across the filling. Thus the filling slope is the preferred zero-linking longitude; the definition asserts no 4-manifold bounded by M(K).

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text: Assume AC. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot, let $q\ge2$, and let $M=\Sigma_q(K)$ be its $q$-fold cyclic branched cover. A character is a homomorphism $\chi:H_1(M;\mathbb Z)\to\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z$. Its order is its order in $\operatorname{Hom}(H_1(M;\mathbb Z),\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)$; it is finite-order when this order is finite and has prime-power order when its order is $p^e$ for a prime $p$ and $e\ge1$. It vanishes on a subgroup $P$ when $\chi(x)=0$ for every $x\in P$.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Assume full AC, matching the chosen finite twisted-chain and maximal-abelian-cover conventions. Let K be a smooth oriented knot, M(K) its preferred-longitude zero-framed surgery, W a compact connected oriented smooth 4-manifold with boundary M(K), and π=π₁(W). Put π^(0)=π and π^(j+1)=[π^(j),π^(j)]. A right Zπ-chain complex with coefficients in a left Z[π/π^(j)]-module is formed by tensoring over Zπ with that module.

For n≥0, W is an integral n-solution for K when H₁(M(K);Z)→H₁(W;Z) is an isomorphism, H₂(W;Z) is free of rank 2r for some finite r, and there are classes x₁,…,x_r,y₁,…,y_r in H₂(W;Z[π/π^(n)]) whose equivariant intersection pairings satisfy λ_n(x_i,x_j)=0 and λ_n(x_i,y_j)=δ_ij. It is an integral (n+1/2)-solution when, in addition, each x_i is the image of a class x̃_i in H₂(W;Z[π/π^(n+1)]) and λ_{n+1}(x̃_i,x̃_j)=0 for all i,j. Here λ_j is the equivariant intersection pairing induced by the orientation of W.

For a commutative ring R with 1≠0, a group G belongs to Strebel's class D(R) if every homomorphism between projective RG-modules is injective whenever its tensor with the trivial G-module R is injective. In this page R is Q or F_p for a prime p. For a countable discrete group G, its group von Neumann algebra N G is the weak-operator closure of CG in the left regular representation on ℓ²(G), with trace τ_G(T)=⟨Tδ_e,δ_e⟩. The von Neumann dimension of a finitely generated projective N G-module represented by a projection E is τ_G(E); for an arbitrary module it is the supremum of the dimensions of its finitely generated projective submodules.

For a compact oriented 4-manifold W with boundary, sign(W) is the inertia difference of the symmetric intersection form on H₂(W;R) modulo its radical (the subspace pairing to zero with every class), equivalently on the image of H₂(W;R)→H₂(W,∂W;R). Given a closed oriented 3-manifold M, a homomorphism φ:π₁(M)→G, a compact oriented 4-manifold W with ∂W=M, and an extension ψ:π₁(W)→G of φ, the L²-signature sign_G^(2)(W,ψ) is the von Neumann signature of the nonsingular part of the N G-coefficient intersection form. When such a W and extension exist, the signature defect is sign_G^(2)(W,ψ)−sign(W). It is called the rho invariant of (M,φ) only after its independence of the bounding data is established by a separate bordism argument.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text: Assume AC. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot bounding a smooth proper disk $D\subset B^4$, and let $q\ge2$. Write $X_D$ for the compact disk exterior and let the positive meridian induce $\pi_1(X_D)\to H_1(X_D;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z\to\mathbb Z/q$. Let $X_{D,q}$ be the connected cover classified by the kernel of this map. Attach $D^2\times D^2$ to $X_{D,q}$ along the connected cover of $D^2\times S^1$ using the normal-disk map $z\mapsto z^q$. The resulting compact oriented $4$-manifold $W_{D,q}$ is the $q$-fold cyclic cover of $B^4$ branched along $D$; its boundary is $\Sigma_q(K)$, and the local branched model is $(x,z)\mapsto(x,z^q)$.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $M$ be a closed oriented three-manifold with a specified coefficient homomorphism $\phi:\pi_1(M_j)\to\Gamma$ on each component, where $\Gamma$ is PTFA. The integral coefficient ring is $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[\Gamma]$ with its fraction division ring $K\Gamma$. More generally let $k$ be $\mathbb Z$ or a commutative field, let $K$ be the fraction division ring of $k[\Gamma]$, and let $k[\Gamma]\subseteq R\subseteq K$ be an involution-stable unital intermediate ring. The involution fixes $k$ and sends $g$ to $g^{-1}$; on fractions it is the involutive anti-automorphism extending this formula. Taking $k=\mathbb Z$ and $R=\Lambda$ recovers the integral convention.

If $H_1(M;K)=0$, the coefficient Bockstein, oriented Poincaré duality and evaluation define the Blanchfield linking pairing
$$B_{M,\phi,R}:TH_1(M;R)\times TH_1(M;R)\longrightarrow K/R.$$
Here $T$ denotes the submodule of elements with a nonzero right annihilator, the first variable is conjugate-linear, and the second is right-linear. Nonsingularity means that the adjoint
$$\overline{TH_1(M;R)}\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_R(TH_1(M;R),K/R)$$
is an isomorphism of left $R$-modules, where $r\cdot\bar x=\overline{x\bar r}$ on the conjugate module. This is equivalent to the conjugate-dual formulation in the right-module convention. For $\Gamma=\mathbb Z$ with generator $t$, $R=\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$ and $K=\mathbb Q(t)$ give the classical coefficient convention. Nonsingularity is a separate property of the defined pairing, with its coefficient hypotheses supplied by the nonsingularity theorem.

For a homomorphism φ:π₁(M)→G and an extension ψ:π₁(W)→G over a compact oriented 4-manifold W with ∂W=M, define the signature defect by ρ(M,φ;W,ψ)=sign_G^(2)(W,ψ)−sign(W). It is an invariant of (M,φ) only when a separate bordism-independence theorem applies.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume AC. For every smooth oriented knot $K$ and $q\ge2$, the first homology of the $q$-fold cyclic cover $M_{0,q}$ of zero surgery has an isomorphism of abelian groups
$$H_1(M_{0,q};\mathbb Z)\cong H_1(\Sigma_q(K);\mathbb Z)\oplus\mathbb Z,$$
where the free summand is generated by $\widetilde\mu$, the closed lift of the $q$-fold meridian loop $\mu^q$.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, a smooth oriented knot $K$, the integer $q\ge2$, the exterior cover $E_q$, its meridional filling $\Sigma_q(K)$, and its zero-surgery filling $M_{0,q}$.

[A1] Full AC is assumed wherever the cover and orientation conventions use the choice axiom. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] The zero-surgery cover is obtained by filling the common exterior cover $E_q$ along a lift of the preferred longitude. Its filling solid torus has core represented by the closed lift $\widetilde\mu$ of $\mu^q$. [[def-cyclic-zero-surgery-cover]]

[F2] The branched cover $\Sigma_q(K)$ is obtained by filling the same $E_q$ along the closed lift of $\mu^q$. [[def-cyclic-branched-cover-of-a-knot]]

[F3] The exterior homology is generated by the meridian; the preferred longitude is a degree-one peripheral curve nullhomologous in the exterior. The induced homomorphism $\ell_K:\pi_1(E_K)\to\mathbb Z$ sends $\mu$ to $1$ and is the meridian-coordinate map. [[thm-knot-exterior-homology-and-longitude]] [[def-knot-meridian-and-preferred-longitude]]

[F4] Every smooth oriented knot bounds a connected compact smooth oriented Seifert surface. Full AC supplies the countable-choice hypothesis of this supplier. [[thm-every-oriented-knot-bounds-a-seifert-surface]] [[def-countable-choice]] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F5] For a one-component knot, the total-linking homomorphism is the meridian-coordinate map $\ell_K$ from [F3]; it equals signed intersection with a Seifert surface. [[lem-total-linking-equals-intersection-with-link-seifert-surface]] [[thm-knot-exterior-homology-and-longitude]]

[F6] Mayer–Vietoris computes the first homology of each filling from the common boundary torus, and the H0 map is injective because all three spaces are connected. [[thm-mayer-vietoris-sequence-in-singular-homology]]

[F7] The unbranched exterior cover is classified by the kernel of $\ell_K\bmod q$; a connected surface whose fundamental-group image lies in this subgroup lifts to the cover. [[def-cyclic-branched-cover-of-a-knot]] [[thm-classification-of-connected-covering-spaces]]

[L1] Conway's Lemma 2.31 states the same splitting and gives a Mayer–Vietoris proof. The complete proof in the retrieved §2.6 was read; the explicit meridian retraction below makes the splitting step transparent. [Anthony Conway, *Algebraic Concordance and Casson–Gordon Invariants*, §2.6, Lemma 2.31, pp. 23–24](https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000id_/https://www.unige.ch/math/folks/conway/Notes/AlgebraicConcordanceCassonGordon.pdf)

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume full AC. Let $L=K_1\cup\cdots\cup K_r\subset S^3$ be a nonempty smooth oriented link, let $F$ be a compact smooth oriented embedded surface with oriented boundary $L$, and put $X=S^3\setminus L$. For each component $K_i$, let $\mu_i$ be the positive meridian, oriented as the boundary of a small normal disk so that a positive tangent to $K_i$ followed by the disk's positive basis gives the ambient orientation. Alexander duality identifies $H_1(X;\mathbb Z)$ with the free abelian group on $[\mu_1],\ldots,[\mu_r]$. Define the total-linking homomorphism $\varphi:H_1(X;\mathbb Z)\to\mathbb Z$ by $\varphi(\sum_i m_i[\mu_i])=\sum_i m_i$. If a smooth oriented loop $J\subset X$ is transverse to the interior of $F$, define its signed intersection number $J\cdot F$ by counting $+1$ when $J$ crosses from the negative to the positive side of the oriented normal of $F$ and $-1$ for the reverse crossing. Then $J\cdot F=\varphi([J])$.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, a nonempty smooth oriented link $L$, a compact oriented spanning surface $F$ with boundary $L$, and a smooth loop $J$ in $X=S^3\setminus L$ transverse to the interior of $F$.

[A1] Full AC is the ambient choice hypothesis for the Alexander-duality convention. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] The link complement $X$ is connected, and Alexander duality identifies $H_1(X;\mathbb Z)$ with $\mathbb Z^r$ on the positive meridian basis; total linking is the sum of the component coordinates. [[lem-the-complement-of-an-oriented-link-is-a-connected-smooth-three-manifold]], [[def-one-variable-alexander-module-of-an-oriented-link]]

[F2] Smooth loops and homotopies in $X$ can be perturbed to be transverse to the interior of $F$, while a prescribed closed region on which the map is already suitable is kept fixed. [[thm-transversality-homotopy-theorem]], [[prop-relative-transversality-preserves-a-map-on-a-closed-good-region]]

[F3] The degree-one Hurewicz map sends $\pi_1(X,x_0)$ onto $H_1(X;\mathbb Z)$ and factors through abelianization. [[prop-the-first-hurewicz-map-in-degree-one-is-abelianization]]

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text: Assume AC. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot, $q\ge2$, and $M=\Sigma_q(K)$ oriented as the boundary of the positive-meridian branched cover. When $H_1(M;\mathbb Z)$ is finite, its torsion linking form is the oriented pairing $\lambda_M:H_1(M;\mathbb Z)\times H_1(M;\mathbb Z)\to\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z$ given by $\lambda_M(x,y)=(C\cdot y)/n\bmod\mathbb Z$ for any integer $n>0$ and integral $2$-chain $C$ in $M$ with $\partial C=nx$; reversing the orientation negates $\lambda_M$. For a prime-power-order character $\chi$ of order $d$, the standard splitting $H_1(M_{0,q};\mathbb Z)\cong H_1(M;\mathbb Z)\oplus\mathbb Z\langle\widetilde\mu\rangle$ of the $q$-fold cyclic cover $M_{0,q}$ of zero surgery extends $\chi$ to $\eta:H_1(M_{0,q};\mathbb Z)\to\mathbb Z/d\oplus\mathbb Z$ by identifying its cyclic image with $\mathbb Z/d$ and using the free-summand projection in the second factor. A Casson–Gordon bordism datum is a positive integer $r$ and a compact oriented $4$-manifold $W$ with a map to $K(\mathbb Z/d\oplus\mathbb Z,1)$ whose boundary represents $r$ copies of $(M_{0,q},\eta)$.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume AC. If a smooth oriented knot $K$ bounds a smooth proper disk $D$ in $B^4$ and $q$ is a prime power, then
$$P_D=\ker\bigl(H_1(\Sigma_q(K);\mathbb Z)\to H_1(W_{D,q};\mathbb Z)\bigr)$$
is a metabolizer for the torsion linking form of $\Sigma_q(K)$.

facts:

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text: Let $X$ be a compact connected oriented topological $4$-manifold with nonempty boundary, let $x_0\in X$, and put $G=\pi_1(X,x_0)$. A **finite relative disk-embedding datum** consists of proper generic immersions $f_i:(D^2,S^1)\looparrowright(X,\partial X)$, $1\le i\le n$, whose boundary circles are embedded and pairwise disjoint, together with framed immersed spheres $g_i:S^2\looparrowright\operatorname{int}X$ that are algebraically dual to the disks. Here a generic immersion is locally a topological embedding except at finitely many double points, each with exactly two preimages whose image sheets are the coordinate planes $\mathbb R^2\times\{0\}$ and $\{0\}\times\mathbb R^2$ in a chart of $X$; proper means that the inverse image of $\partial X$ is exactly the domain boundary; and framed means that the normal microbundle has a chosen trivialization extending the specified boundary framing. Choose paths from $x_0$ to the immersed surfaces and orient the surfaces. Each transverse intersection $p$ of two surfaces contributes $\epsilon(p)g_p$ to $\lambda$, where $\epsilon(p)\in\{1,-1\}$ compares their induced local orientation with the chosen orientation of $X$, and $g_p\in G$ is the loop that travels along the chosen path to the first surface, then to $p$, and returns along the second surface and its chosen path. Thus $\lambda$ is a signed equivariant intersection sum in $\mathbb Z[G]$. Wall's self-intersection sum $\mu$ is the signed sum over self-double points in $\mathbb Z[G]/\langle g-g^{-1}:g\in G\rangle$, because interchanging the two sheets replaces a label by its inverse. The normal framing is a separate datum; its relative normal Euler or boundary-framing obstruction is zero precisely when the specified framing extends over the immersion. The spheres are **algebraically dual** when $\lambda(f_i,g_j)=\delta_{ij}$, $\lambda(g_i,g_j)=0$ for every $i,j$, and $\mu(g_i)=0$ for every $i$. The disk data are **algebraically unobstructed** when also $\lambda(f_i,f_j)=0$ for $i\ne j$ and $\mu(f_i)=0$ for every $i$.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Let $X$ be a compact oriented topological $4$-manifold with nonempty boundary. A **kinky handle** is a standard $2$-handle whose core disk has finitely many transverse self-plumbings; a **framed Casson-handle tower** is a nested sequence of such stages in which each self-plumbing point of one stage is replaced by a framed kinky handle at the next stage, with the attaching regions matching the preceding stage. Suppose a finite family of these tower $4$-neighborhoods is embedded pairwise disjointly in $X$, with attaching circles in $\partial X$, and carries the algebraic dual data of a disk-embedding datum. If each embedded tower has a homeomorphism of pairs to the standard open $2$-handle $D^2\times\mathbb R^2$ with attaching region $S^1\times\mathbb R^2$, then the inverse images of the cores $D^2\times\{0\}$ form a pairwise disjoint family of locally flat properly embedded disks in $X$, with the prescribed framed boundary circles.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $V$ be an integral Seifert matrix in the positive-push convention $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. Two integral Seifert forms are **S-equivalent** when they are related by a finite sequence of integral unimodular basis changes and algebraic tube additions or their inverses. A basis change replaces $V$ by $P^T V P$ for $P\in\operatorname{GL}_m(\mathbb Z)$. A tube addition replaces $V$ by
$$
\begin{pmatrix}
V&0&\rho\\
0&0&1\\
\rho^T&0&0
\end{pmatrix},\qquad \rho\in\mathbb Z^m,
$$
where the two new basis elements are the short and long curves of the added tube. The **empty Seifert form** is the unique bilinear form on the zero module, represented by the $0\times0$ matrix.

contract.text:
Assume full AC. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot with $\Delta_K(t)\doteq1$, where $\doteq$ denotes equality up to multiplication by a unit $\pm t^k$ of $\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$. Then $K$ has a connected compact smooth oriented Seifert surface $F$ and an ordered geometric basis, represented by embedded simple closed curves $s_1,\ldots,s_g,\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_g$ for $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$, such that $s_i\cdot_Fs_j=0=\ell_i\cdot_F\ell_j$ and $s_i\cdot_F\ell_j=\delta_{ij}$, and the Seifert matrix in this basis has block form
$$V=\begin{pmatrix}0&I_g+U\\U^T&W\end{pmatrix},$$
where $U$ is strictly upper triangular and $W$ is symmetric with zero diagonal. Such a geometric symplectic basis and block matrix are called a trivial Alexander basis.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume full AC. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot with $\Delta_K(t)\doteq1$. There is a connected compact smooth Seifert surface $F$ with a geometric symplectic basis $s_1,\ldots,s_g,\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_g$ whose positive-push matrix is
$$V=\begin{pmatrix}0&I_g+U\\ U^T&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad U\text{ strictly upper triangular}.$$
Place $F$ on the unit sphere in the literal radius-$3/2$ ball and join its boundary to the outer copy of $K$ by the radial product collar, rounding the inner junction away from that outer collar. Write $\Sigma$ for this proper surface. Its actual smooth normal thickening can be chosen so that the rounded complement
$$N=B^4_{3/2}\setminus\operatorname{int}\nu\Sigma$$
is compact, connected and smooth, with $\pi_1(N)\cong\mathbb Z$ generated by the positive normal meridian of $\Sigma$.

The fixed negative normal pushoffs of the short curves give disjoint framed circles $\delta_i\subset\partial N$. They bound proper framed smooth generic disks $\Delta_i$ in $N$ admitting framed smooth immersed spheres $f_i$ such that
$$\lambda(\Delta_i,f_j)=\delta_{ij},\quad \lambda(\Delta_i,\Delta_j)=0\ (i\ne j),\quad \mu(\Delta_i)=0,\quad \lambda(f_i,f_j)=0,\quad\mu(f_i)=0$$
in $\mathbb Z[\mathbb Z]$ with the specified Wall conventions. Along the fixed annuli from $\delta_i$ to $s_i\subset\Sigma$, their boundary framings agree with the normal directions of $s_i$ within $\Sigma$. Thus the data retain the actual ambient ball, complement, attaching circles and compression framings. The group is good when the infinite-cyclic good-group theorem is supplied. For $g=0$ the disk and sphere families are empty and the geometric complement assertion remains valid.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume full AC. Let $T$ be the right-handed trefoil and let $S=T\#T^\dagger$ be the square knot in the fixed oriented connected-sum convention. The universal converse assertion “if a knot has nonunit Alexander polynomial, then it is not topologically slice” is false: $S$ bounds a smooth properly embedded disk in the standard unit four-ball $B^4\subset\mathbb R^4$ whose squared radial function has only index-$0$ and index-$1$ interior critical points, while $\Delta_S(t)\doteq(t^2-t+1)^2$. Here $\doteq$ means equality up to a unit of $\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$; those units are exactly $\pm t^k$, and the displayed polynomial has nonzero terms in degrees $0$ through $4$, so it is not a unit. A knot is topologically slice when it bounds a locally flat disk in $B^4$, and every smooth proper disk is locally flat. The trefoil itself also has nonunit Alexander polynomial, but this fact alone only places it outside the hypothesis of the Alexander-one sufficient theorem and proves no nonsliceness claim about the trefoil.

[F2] [[def-knot-seifert-pairing-and-matrix]]: In the positive-push convention, the Seifert matrix is $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$ in the chosen integral basis.

[F3] [[lem-seifert-matrix-of-reverse-mirror-is-negative-original]]: The reverse-mirror matrix in the image basis is $-V$.

[F7] [[lem-general-knot-reverse-mirror-sum-is-ribbon]]: Under AC$_\omega$, $T\#T^\dagger$ bounds a smooth properly embedded ribbon disk in $B^4$.

contract.heading: Statement

Let $Wh^+(T)$ denote the satellite of the right-handed trefoil $T$ by the positive-clasped, untwisted Whitehead pattern, embedded using the preferred longitude. This knot has Alexander polynomial $1$; by topologically slice we mean that it bounds a locally flat embedded disk in $B^4$. The established theorem gives that topological conclusion, not a smooth slice disk.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume full AC, using Sobolev norms formed from the $L^p$ norms of Euclidean ordered derivative tensors. There exist constants $\varepsilon,C,C_3>0$ with the following property. Let $A$ be a smooth $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued one-form on the closed Euclidean ball $B_r(0)\subset\mathbb R^4$, with Frobenius target norm and curvature $F_A=dA+A\wedge A$. If $\|F_A\|_{L^2(B_r)}\le\varepsilon$, then there exists $g:B_r\to SU(2)$ belonging to $W^{2,p}$ for every finite $p\ge2$ such that
$$a=A^g=g^{-1}dg+g^{-1}Ag,\qquad d^*a=0,$$
and $a$ belongs to the $W^{1,3}$ closure $Y_3$ of smooth one-forms with zero normal component on the sphere. In particular the normal condition is valid in the weak integration identity. The form $a$ belongs to every $W^{1,p}$ with finite $p\ge2$ and satisfies
$$r^{-1}\|a\|_2+\|\nabla a\|_2+\|a\|_4\le C\|F_A\|_2,\qquad r^{-1}\|a\|_3+\|\nabla a\|_3\le C_3\|F_A\|_3.$$
The constants are independent of $r$ and $A$; no uniform bound on the gauge's higher norms in terms of the critical curvature norm alone is asserted.

If a fixed finite $\Gamma\le O(4)$ acts on the ball and $\tau$ is an action of $\Gamma$ on $SU(2)$ by constant unitary conjugations, assume $\gamma^*A=d\tau_\gamma(A)$. Then $g$ may be chosen with $g(\gamma x)=\tau_\gamma(g(x))$. This includes prescribed conjugation actions coming from $PU(2)$ representations, without choosing a lift to an $SU(2)$ representation.

For a finite collection of balls with smooth local connection forms $A_i$ and given smooth $SU(2)$ transition maps $t_{ij}$ satisfying $A_j=A_i^{t_{ij}}$ and $t_{ij}t_{jk}=t_{ik}$, apply the construction on each ball where its curvature bound holds. The transformed maps $h_{ij}=g_i^{-1}t_{ij}g_j$ are continuous $W^{2,3}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ transition maps on the overlaps, satisfy the cocycle identities pointwise, and identify the transformed connection forms by $a_j=a_i^{h_{ij}}$.

facts:
[F1] On $B_1$ the constructed normal-boundary Hodge estimate applies to the closure classes $Y_p$ and, for $p=2,3$, absorbs the curvature nonlinearity when $\|a\|_4\le\rho_p$. It then bounds $\|a\|_{W^{1,p}}$ by $C_p\|F_a\|_p$ for Coulomb forms ([[lem-normal-boundary-hodge-estimate-on-four-dimensional-balls]]).

[F2] For $a\in Y_3$ Coulomb with $\|a\|_4\le\rho_c$, and $\lambda\in Y_3$ with sufficiently small $W^{1,3}$ norm, the proved contraction constructs a Neumann gauge $h=e^u$ with $b=(a+\lambda)^h\in Y_3$ Coulomb, and $\|b-a\|_{W^{1,3}}\le C_c(1+\|a\|_{W^{1,3}})\|\lambda\|_{W^{1,3}}$. It preserves given finite constant-conjugation equivariance. Its Neumann gauge class is the $W^{2,3}$ closure $\mathcal G_N$ of smooth $SU(2)$ maps with zero normal derivative ([[lem-neumann-coulomb-gauge-correction-by-contraction]]).

[F3] The constructed strong Neumann inverse supplies the unique mean-zero weak solution in $W^{2,p}$ for every finite $p\ge2$ and preserves normal polynomial approximation ([[lem-strong-lp-neumann-inverse-on-four-dimensional-balls]]).

[F4] On the ball, $W^{1,2}\hookrightarrow L^4$, $W^{1,3}\hookrightarrow L^{12}$, and $W^{2,3}\hookrightarrow L^\infty$. Also $W^{2,6}$ has bounded first derivatives. These follow from the proved first- and higher-order embeddings and the ball's extension property ([[thm-sobolev-embedding-on-bounded-extension-domains-for-p-less-than-n]], [[thm-higher-order-sobolev-embedding]], [[thm-extension-theorem-for-bounded-smooth-domains]]).

[F5] Holder gives the product estimates below, and smooth approximation gives weak product rules. In particular the embeddings in [F4] prove continuity of multiplication $W^{2,3}\times W^{2,3}\to W^{2,3}$ and $W^{2,3}\times W^{1,3}\to W^{1,3}$: second-derivative cross terms use $L^6\cdot L^6\subset L^3$, and first derivatives of mixed products use $L^{12}\cdot L^4\subset L^3$ ([[thm-holder-inequality-for-integrals]], [[thm-meyers-serrin-density-on-an-arbitrary-open-set]]).

[F6] Full AC is inherited from these analytic suppliers ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume full AC. Let $X$ be a closed oriented Riemannian four-manifold, let $P$ be a fixed principal $SU(2)$-bundle with charge $k=-\langle c_2(P),[X]\rangle$, and let $(A_j)$ be smooth connections satisfying $F_{A_j}^-=0$ and $\sup_j\int_X|F_{A_j}|^2\,d\mathrm{vol}<\infty$. Then a subsequence, bundle isomorphisms, and a finite set $S\subset X$ exist such that the transported connections converge in local Sobolev gauge on compact subsets of $X\setminus S$ to a self-dual connection on a possibly lower-charge bundle of charge $k_\infty$. For each $p\in S$ there is a positive integer bubble charge $m_p$, and $k=k_\infty+\sum_{p\in S}m_p$. The limiting connection extends smoothly across every puncture after gauge transformation, and the compactified moduli space is obtained by adjoining the lower-charge limits together with the finite bubble points and their integer charge labels.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, the fixed closed oriented smooth Riemannian four-manifold, the smooth $SU(2)$ bundle and the self-dual sequence in the Statement. Use the real Frobenius form on $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ for coefficient energy. Changing this norm by a fixed positive convention factor changes only the displayed energy unit, not the integer charges.

[F1] The actual smooth-ball small-curvature theorem constructs Euclidean Coulomb gauges with $\|a\|_4+\|a\|_{W^{1,2}}\le C\|F\|_2$ on a unit ball. It applies to arbitrary smooth connections, with exact unitary curvature covariance. ([[lem-small-critical-curvature-coulomb-gauges-on-four-balls]])

[F2] For a smooth metric sufficiently $C^0$ close to Euclidean, the new curved-metric weak Coulomb theorem proves smoothness, uniform interior coefficient bounds for small $L^4$ potential, and the actual estimate $r^2\|F\|_\infty\le C\|F\|_2$. Its constants are uniform on the rescalings of finitely many fixed compact coordinate charts. It covers either Hodge sign. ([[lem-weak-coulomb-asd-connections-for-smooth-four-metrics-are-interior-smooth]])

[F3] The annular transport proof gives a frame bounded by the uniform annular curvature, using two spherical path families and quaternionic normalization. The punctured critical-gauge proof aligns adjacent frames by constants and sums a dyadic annular $L^4$ bound. The point-removal proof retains the full quadratic cutoff curvature and constructs a limiting gauge after Coulomb extraction. Their Euclidean-ASD Statements are NOT invoked for a curved metric: the required extensions of these actual arguments are supplied below with [F2]. ([[lem-small-uniform-curvature-gauges-on-four-dimensional-annuli]], [[lem-finite-energy-punctured-euclidean-asd-connections-have-l-four-gauges]], [[lem-finite-energy-euclidean-asd-point-singularity-is-removable]])

[F4] Close $SU(2)$ cocycles are intertwined by the explicitly proved normalized quaternionic average. Its finite algebra works on any finite chart cover with compactly supported smooth scalar weights; below it is written again for the present smooth data. A countable smooth matrix cocycle glues a smooth vector bundle. For $SU(2)$ transitions its preserved metric, complex structure and determinant give the corresponding principal $SU(2)$ frame bundle. ([[lem-close-su-two-cocycles-admit-constructed-sobolev-isomorphisms]], [[thm-vector-bundle-construction-from-a-smooth-cocycle]])

[F5] The second Chern form is $c_2(A)=\operatorname{tr}(F_A\wedge F_A)/(8\pi^2)$ for the trace-zero rank-two connection and represents the integral topological class over the reals. Closed exact top forms integrate to zero. On a coordinate ball, the divergence theorem gives zero integral for the derivative of a smooth three-form with zero tangential boundary trace. Thus, for the sign $F_A^-=0$, $\int|F_A|^2=-8\pi^2\langle c_2(P),[X]\rangle$. These signs follow from the given Frobenius norm and the stated determinant normalization. ([[thm-chern-weil-forms-represent-the-at-characteristic-classes-over-the-reals]], [[def-chern-pontryagin-and-euler-characteristic-forms]], [[lem-finite-chart-localization-defines-choice-free-integration-and-compact-stokes]], [[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-c-one-euclidean-domains]])

[F6] Arzela–Ascoli, smooth cutoffs, Holder and absolute continuity hold in the stated finite-dimensional smooth charts. Countable diagonal extractions and choices are permitted by full AC. ([[cor-arzela-ascoli-subsequence-theorem-for-proper-metric-targets]], [[lem-smooth-bump-between-concentric-euclidean-balls]], [[thm-holder-inequality-for-integrals]], [[thm-absolute-continuity-of-the-integral]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]])

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume AC. Let $Y$ be a compact oriented Hausdorff topological five-manifold with supplied boundary collar, and let $X=\partial Y$ have its boundary orientation. Supply a based homomorphism $\psi:\pi_1Y\to G$ on each component, where $G$ is an arbitrary discrete group, with the standard unitary regular coefficient systems. Then
$$\operatorname{sign}^{(2)}_G(X,\psi|_X)=0,\qquad \operatorname{sign}(X)=0.$$
In particular, when $X=X_1\sqcup(-X_0)$, the ordinary and $L^2$ signatures of these closed oriented four-manifolds agree across this actual coefficient-extending TOP bordism. The equality is unchanged under embedding the target group in a larger group. This theorem asserts bordism invariance and does not assert existence of a bordism between arbitrary closed coefficient manifolds.

facts:
**Given:** AC, the actual collared oriented $Y$, its boundary $X$, and the compatible regular coefficient maps in the Statement.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]] is the standing spectral and projective-comparison hypothesis of the finite-projective supplier.

[F1] For compact collared TOP manifolds in every dimension, bounded finite-projective coefficient chain models and their pair diagrams transfer actual cap duality to bounded isomorphisms on completed reduced homology and cohomology. Pair sequences are weakly exact; algebraic harmonic parts are dense. Cap-boundary and restriction identities hold after completion. For a closed oriented four-manifold its middle Hermitian operator is boundedly invertible. Model independence and coefficient-subgroup induction hold by finite matrices and identical coset operator blocks. [[thm-topological-finite-projective-l2-duality-and-boundary-gluing]]

[F2] Restriction of a boundedly invertible Hermitian form on a finite Hilbert von Neumann module to a closed coisotropic submodule preserves its signature; a zero form has zero signature. [[lem-von-neumann-inertia-and-coisotropic-reduction]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume full AC. Let $X$ be a compact connected smooth simply connected oriented four-manifold. If its integral intersection form is positive definite, then there is an integral basis of $H_2(X;\mathbb Z)/\operatorname{Tor}$ in which the form is the identity matrix. Equivalently, the integral intersection lattice is isometric to the standard diagonal lattice $\mathbb Z^{b_2(X)}$ with dot product.

facts:
[F1] The integral intersection pairing is a symmetric integral unimodular form on the free finite-rank group $H_2(X;\mathbb Z)/\operatorname{Tor}$. [[def-integral-intersection-lattice-of-a-simply-connected-four-manifold]] [[lem-integral-intersection-pairing-is-unimodular]]

[F2] The equation is $F_A^-=0$, with charge $c_2=-1$. Its actual compatible reducible preparation, middle regularization, complete inverse small-instanton end and smooth cut bordism are supplied by [[lem-donaldson-reducible-ends-and-one-instanton-compactification]]. The actual reducible orbits inject into mutually orthogonal unordered integral norm-one pairs, so their number is at most $b_2(X)$. [[lem-reducible-charge-one-su-two-connections-admit-controlled-projective-links]]

[F3] The ordinary signature of the full boundary of an actual compact oriented five-manifold is zero. This follows from the explicitly proved self-annihilating image of restriction in the boundary intersection form; no closed four-dimensional index theorem is used. [[thm-topological-five-bordisms-preserve-ordinary-and-l2-signatures]]

[F4] The integral cohomology ring of $\mathbb{CP}^2$ is $\mathbb Z[x]/(x^3)$, with $x^2$ a generator. Thus its middle form has rank one and signature $1$ or $-1$, according to orientation. [[lem-integral-cohomology-ring-of-complex-projective-space-by-splitting]]

[A1] Full AC is inherited from the gauge, compactness, characteristic-class and duality suppliers. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot such that its double branched cover $M=\Sigma_2(K)$ is a rational homology sphere. Let $D\subset B^4$ be a smooth proper embedded disk with boundary $K$, and let $B_D$ be the connected double cover of $B^4$ branched over $D$. Let $W$ be a compact connected smooth simply connected oriented four-manifold with boundary identified orientation-compatibly with $M$, and assume its boundary intersection form is positive definite. Assume also that the image of $\pi_1(M)\to\pi_1(B_D)$ normally generates $\pi_1(B_D)$, meaning its normal closure is the whole group. Then the oriented gluing $X=W\cup_M(-B_D)$ is a closed smooth simply connected positive-definite four-manifold, and inclusion induces an isometric full-rank embedding $Q_W\hookrightarrow Q_X$ of integral intersection lattices with $b_2(X)=b_2(W)$.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC; the knot, slice disk, rational-homology-sphere boundary, positive-definite simply connected filling, boundary identification, and normal-generation hypothesis in the statement.

[F1] For a smooth proper disk, the double cover branched over the disk is a compact connected oriented smooth four-manifold with rational homology of a point, and its boundary is the double branched cover of the boundary knot. The result does not assert a fundamental-group conclusion. [[lem-double-cover-branched-over-a-slice-disk-is-a-rational-homology-ball]]

[F2] The double branched cover is defined by the connected cover of the knot exterior classified by the positive-meridian map to $\mathbb Z/2$, filled along the closed lift of the squared meridian. [[def-cyclic-branched-cover-of-a-knot]]

[F3] Smooth four-ball genus is the minimum genus of a smooth proper oriented surface in $B^4$; a smooth slice disk is the genus-zero case. [[def-smooth-and-topological-slice-genus]]

[F4] The boundary form is the signed intersection pairing on the torsion-free quotient, and is rationally nondegenerate when the boundary is a rational homology sphere. [[def-intersection-lattice-of-a-four-manifold-with-boundary]] [[lem-boundary-intersection-pairing-well-defined-and-nondegenerate]]

[F5] Seifert–van Kampen computes the fundamental group of a union along a path-connected collar as the pushout of the two inclusion homomorphisms. [[thm-seifert-van-kampen]]

[F6] Mayer–Vietoris gives the singular-homology exact sequence for the collar-thickened decomposition along $M$. [[thm-mayer-vietoris-sequence-in-singular-homology]]

[F7] Smooth collars on the two boundaries allow the orientation-compatible gluing and its collar-thickened open cover. [[thm-collar-neighborhood-theorem]]

[F8] For any abelian group $A$, $A\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$ is its positive-integer localization, and $a\otimes1=0$ exactly when some positive integer kills $a$. The natural coefficient map identifies $H_j(Y;\mathbb Z)\otimes\mathbb Q$ with $H_j(Y;\mathbb Q)$. [[lem-rationalization-is-exact-and-commutes-with-singular-homology]]

[A1] For this particular branched cover $B_D$, the boundary inclusion normally generates $\pi_1(B_D)$. This is an explicit additional hypothesis; it is not a consequence of the rational-homology-ball supplier [F1].

[A2] Full AC is assumed by the branched-cover and homology suppliers in [F1]–[F3].

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $M$ be a compact connected Hausdorff manifold, $o\in M$, and $R$ a unital ring. One can construct paths $\gamma_x$ from $o$ to every $x\in M$, with $\gamma_o$ constant, by fixed rules from one finite atlas and finitely many connecting paths. Let $\mathcal R$ be a right-$R$ local system with a supplied identification $\mathcal R_o=R$ and transport given by left multiplication by units, with monodromy image $H\le R^\times$. Its twisted singular complex has an explicit chain decomposition $C_*(M;\mathcal R)=C'_*\oplus Q_*$ after a change of free bases, where $C'_0=R$, $C'_* $ is free, and $Q_*$ is contractible with its only nonzero differential an identity from degree one to degree zero. Moreover
$$\operatorname{im}(d'_1)=\sum_{h\in H}(h-1)R.$$
The decomposition and its dual cochain homotopy equivalences require no choice principle. In particular this image is principal if $H$ is cyclic, if it equals $R$, or if every right ideal of $R$ is principal.

facts:
**Given:** The compact connected manifold, point, coefficient system, and base fiber identification.

[F1] A right-$R$ local system here means a functor from the fundamental groupoid to unital right-$R$ modules with right-linear transport isomorphisms. Forgetting the right action gives an abelian-group local system; the intrinsic first-vertex construction of [[def-singular-and-cellular-chain-complexes-with-local-coefficients]] applies with commutative base ring $\mathbb Z$. The additional arbitrary-ring linearity and square-zero calculation are supplied directly in step 1.1 below.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $M$ be a compact connected Hausdorff manifold with a basepoint, and let $0\to\mathcal A\xrightarrow{i}\mathcal B\xrightarrow{q}\mathcal C\to0$ be a short exact sequence of local systems of abelian groups on $M$. There is a natural coefficient Bockstein making the sequence
$$H^1(M;\mathcal B)\xrightarrow{q_*}H^1(M;\mathcal C)\xrightarrow{\beta}H^2(M;\mathcal A)\xrightarrow{i_*}H^2(M;\mathcal B)$$
exact at its two middle terms. In particular $\beta$ is an isomorphism if $H^1(M;\mathcal B)=H^2(M;\mathcal B)=0$. No choice principle is assumed. If the local systems and maps have a commuting coefficient-ring action, the sequence and Bockstein respect it.

facts:
**Given:** The based manifold and the fiberwise exact coefficient sequence.

[F1] Based paths $\gamma_x$ to all points can be specified from finite atlas data, with $\gamma_o$ constant; the fundamental group has a finite generating list. [[lem-compact-manifold-twisted-singular-chains-admit-one-vertex-reduction]], [[lem-compact-connected-manifold-fundamental-group-has-finite-generators-in-zf]]

[F2] Intrinsic local cochains take values in the fiber over the first vertex, and their coboundary uses inverse transport along the first edge. [[def-homology-and-cohomology-with-local-coefficients]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Let $M$ be a compact connected Hausdorff topological manifold and $o\in M$. There is a finite based graph mapped continuously into $M$ such that its induced fundamental-group map is onto. Consequently $\pi_1(M,o)$ has a finite generating list, without a choice principle. No triangulation or smooth structure on $M$ is assumed.

facts: **Given:** The compact connected manifold and specified basepoint.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Every compact Hausdorff topological manifold $M$, with boundary allowed, admits an embedding $e:M\hookrightarrow\mathbb R^N$, an open neighborhood $U$ of $e(M)$ and a retraction $r:U\to e(M)$. Moreover there is a finite Euclidean cubical complex $L$ with $e(M)\subseteq L\subseteq U$, so that $r|_L$ makes $M$ an actual retract of a finite CW complex. No choice principle, smooth or PL structure, triangulation of $M$, or general locally contractible-space retraction theorem is assumed.

facts:
**Given:** The compact Hausdorff manifold.

[F1] A finite union of closed Euclidean cubes together with all their faces is a finite CW complex: the open faces are its cells, their characteristic maps are the closed cubes, and the finite closed-cover topology gives the weak topology. [[def-cw-complex-with-closure-finiteness-and-weak-topology]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $M$ be a compact connected Hausdorff manifold, with boundary allowed, and $o\in M$. Supply any finite list of based loops $\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_\ell$. There is a finite connected two-dimensional CW complex $K$ with one vertex $v$, a based map $f:(K,v)\to(M,o)$ inducing an isomorphism on fundamental groups, and marked oriented one-cells which $f$ parametrizes by the specified loops. In particular $\pi_1(M,o)$ is finitely presented without a choice axiom.

For any normal subgroup $N\triangleleft\pi_1(M,o)$ and commutative unital ring $k$, use on $M$ the associated right $k[\pi_1(M)/N]$ normal-cover system and on $K$ its pullback. The actual induced map on $H_1$ with these coefficients is an isomorphism. No finite CW type, triangulation or smoothing of $M$ is asserted.

facts:
**Given:** The based compact manifold and finite marked loop list.

[F1] A compact Hausdorff manifold is a strict retract $M\xrightarrow{i}L\xrightarrow{r}M$ of a finite geometric polyhedron, with $ri=\mathrm{id}$. [[thm-compact-manifolds-are-retracts-of-finite-polyhedra-without-choice]]

[F2] Fundamental groups of connected collared open gluings are their actual group pushouts, without an overlap-injectivity assumption or global choice of loop representatives. [[thm-seifert-van-kampen]]

[F3] Normal-cover right local first homology is naturally the abelianized covering subgroup tensored with $k$, for actual based maps and induced coefficient maps, without choice. The supplied contractible-neighborhood-basis scope includes finite polyhedra. [[lem-normal-cover-local-homology-detects-mixed-derived-kernels-without-choice]]

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
A group G is poly-torsion-free abelian (PTFA) if it admits a finite subnormal series
1=G_0 ◁ G_1 ◁ ⋯ ◁ G_m=G
in which every quotient G_{j+1}/G_j is torsion-free abelian. The trivial group is PTFA, using the length-zero series. The term “subnormal” means each G_j is normal in G_{j+1}; normality in all of G is not required.

scope: Literal contract/Facts extraction only; accepted proof body not inspected.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $k$ be a commutative field and $G$ a PTFA group. For every homomorphism $f:P\to Q$ between projective right-$k[G]$ modules, if
$$f\otimes1:P\otimes_{k[G]}k\longrightarrow Q\otimes_{k[G]}k$$
is injective under the augmentation $k[G]\to k$, then $f$ is injective. Projective means the lifting property for surjections, applied to right modules; it does not mean a supplied free basis. Thus this is the right-module defining property of Strebel's class $D(k)$. The left-module version holds too.

Moreover, if $k[G]\subseteq K$ is a supplied division ring of Ore fractions, every finite matrix $T$ over $k[G]$ satisfies
$$\operatorname{rank}_K(T\otimes K)\ge\operatorname{rank}_k(\varepsilon T).$$
Both assertions require no choice axiom. The group need not be finitely generated, its series need not be normal in all of $G$, and its successive extensions need not split.

facts:
**Given:** The field, PTFA group, augmentation and, for the matrix consequence, the supplied Ore fraction division ring.

[F1] PTFA means a finite subnormal series with torsion-free abelian successive quotients. A torsion-free abelian group has a commutative group ring with no zero divisors over $k$: apply the nonsplit-extension domain theorem with trivial kernel. [[def-poly-torsion-free-abelian-group]], [[lem-torsion-free-abelian-extensions-preserve-group-ring-domains]]

[F2] Projectivity is the lifting property against each individual surjection; for right modules use the opposite-ring version of that definition. Tensor relations preserve compositions and split identities. [[def-projective-module]], [[def-opposite-ring]], [[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]

[F3] Ore fraction extension is exact on arbitrary right modules, hence preserves each injection of finite free modules. [[lem-ore-localization-is-flat-and-detects-module-torsion]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Let $k$ be a commutative field and let $H\trianglelefteq G$ be a normal subgroup with torsion-free abelian quotient $G/H$. If $k[H]$ has no zero divisors, then $k[G]$ has no zero divisors. The group extension need not split; neither finite generation of $G/H$ nor an order on all of $G$ is assumed.

facts:
**Given:** The field $k$, normal subgroup $H\trianglelefteq G$, and torsion-free abelian quotient $A=G/H$.

[F1] Group-ring elements have unique finite expansions, multiplication is $k$-bilinear with $[g][h]=[gh]$, and each $[g]$ is a unit ([[def-group-ring]], [[thm-group-ring-is-a-unital-algebra-with-basis-g]]).

[F2] Every finitely generated torsion-free abelian group is isomorphic to $\mathbb Z^r$ for some finite $r$ ([[lem-finitely-generated-torsion-free-abelian-freeness-without-choice]]).

[A1] The ring $k[H]$ has no zero divisors.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text: Let knots be smooth oriented knots in the standard oriented S³ and let I=[0,1]. Let C_sm be their smooth concordance classes, where equivalence is witnessed by a smooth proper annulus in S³×I. Let C_top be their locally flat topological concordance classes in that product. Let C_ex be their exotic-smooth concordance classes: equivalence is witnessed by a smooth proper annulus in a compact smooth oriented 4-manifold W together with an orientation-preserving homeomorphism of pairs (W,∂W)≅(S³×I,S³×{0,1}) matching the endpoint knots. For a nonzero integer n set R_n=Z[1/|n|]. Let C^{1/n} be the classes under equivalence witnessed by a smooth proper annulus in a compact smooth oriented 4-manifold W with boundary the two standard endpoint 3-spheres such that each boundary inclusion induces an isomorphism H_i(S³;R_n)→H_i(W;R_n) for every i. A knot is pseudo-slice if it bounds a smooth proper disk in a compact smooth oriented 4-manifold homeomorphic to B⁴, with its oriented boundary identified with the standard oriented S³. A knot is Z[1/|n|]-slice if it bounds a smooth proper disk in a compact smooth oriented 4-manifold B with its oriented boundary identified with the standard oriented S³ and with H_i(B;R_n)≅H_i(B⁴;R_n) for every i; such a B is an R_n-homology 4-ball. These are sets of equivalence classes; this definition alone asserts no group structure.

scope: Literal contract/Facts extraction only; accepted proof body not inspected.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $\Gamma$ be PTFA and let $k$ be either $\mathbb Z$ or a commutative field. The group ring $A=k[\Gamma]$ has no zero divisors, satisfies both Ore conditions, and has a fraction division ring $K$ in which every element is both a right and a left fraction of elements of $A$. The involution $\overline{\sum c_g g}=\sum c_g g^{-1}$ extends uniquely to an involutive anti-automorphism of $K$.

Every intermediate unital ring $A\subseteq R\subseteq K$ has no zero divisors, satisfies both Ore conditions, and has this same $K$ as its fraction division ring. If $R$ is stable under the extended involution, that involution restricts to $R$ and descends to its additive quotient $K/R$. None of these assertions requires a choice principle.

facts:
**Given:** The coefficient ring, PTFA series and indicated intermediate ring when used.

[F1] Nonsplit extensions by torsion-free abelian quotients preserve absence of group-ring zero divisors over every commutative field. [[lem-torsion-free-abelian-extensions-preserve-group-ring-domains]]

[F2] PTFA groups have finite left Folner sets, and a group ring without zero divisors over a commutative field with these sets satisfies both Ore conditions and has a constructed right-fraction division ring. [[lem-ptfa-groups-have-finite-folner-sets]], [[lem-folner-group-ring-domains-have-ore-fractions]]
scope: Literal contract/Facts extraction only; accepted proof body not inspected.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $k$ be a commutative field, let $G$ be PTFA and let $H\le G$. Put $A=k[H]$, $B=k[G]$ and let $F\subseteq K$ be their Ore fraction division rings, with the compatible standard involutions fixing $k$. Let $M$ be a closed oriented three-manifold, with a supplied homomorphism $\pi_1(M_j)\to H$ on each component. Use the canonical based coefficient systems, with base vector $1$ and the standard transported Hermitian structure. Suppose $H_1(M;F)=0$.

Then $H_1(M;K)=0$, and there is the natural isomorphism
$$H_1(M;B)\cong H_1(M;A)\otimes_A B.$$
The maps $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ are injective. The coefficient Bockstein, oriented duality and evaluation define linking pairings $B_A$ with target $F/A$ and $B_B$ with target $K/B$, and their values satisfy
$$B_B(x\otimes1,y\otimes1)=j(B_A(x,y)),\qquad j:F/A\hookrightarrow K/B.$$
In particular a nonzero self-pairing remains nonzero after subgroup extension. Neither pairing is asserted nonsingular without its additional coefficient hypotheses. No choice principle is assumed.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $(M,o)$ be a compact connected based Hausdorff manifold, let $R$ be an involutive unital ring, and supply a rank-one right-$R$ local system $\mathcal R$ with an identification $\mathcal R_o=R$. Assume every based-loop monodromy is left multiplication by a unit $u$ satisfying $\bar u=u^{-1}$. Equip the base fiber with the standard Hermitian form $h_o(a,b)=\bar a b$. Transport extends this to a path-independent parallel Hermitian form $h$ on $\mathcal R$. Put $C_*=C_*(M;\mathcal R)$. For a right $R$-module $P$, write $\overline P$ for its conjugate left module, with $r\cdot\bar p=\overline{p\bar r}$.

The left-$R$ cochain complex $\operatorname{Hom}_R(C_*,R)$ is the intrinsic cochain complex of the left-$R$ local system with fiber $R$ and transport $a\mapsto au^{-1}$. Relative to the supplied parallel Hermitian form, that local system is naturally isomorphic to $\overline{\mathcal R}$ by $\bar v\mapsto[w\mapsto h(v,w)]$. The identifications are independent of unitary fiber frames; an arbitrary change of Hermitian structure is not asserted to preserve them. If $M$ is oriented, boundaryless and of dimension $n$, cap duality therefore gives
$$H^p(\operatorname{Hom}_R(C_*,R))\cong\overline{H_{n-p}(C_*)}.$$
If $R\subseteq K$ is an embedding into an involutive division ring extending the involution, the same conclusion is valid for $K$, with $C_*\otimes_R K$ in the homology target. If $R$ is involution-stable in $K$, the complex $\operatorname{Hom}_R(C_*,K/R)$ is the corresponding intrinsic left-$R$ cochain complex with fiber $K/R$ and transport by right multiplication by $u^{-1}$. These identifications require no choice principle and commute with the coefficient maps $R\to K\to K/R$.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $M$ be a compact oriented boundaryless Hausdorff topological $n$-manifold and let $\mathcal L$ be a local system of abelian groups. Cap with its integral orientation class induces isomorphisms
$$H^p(M;\mathcal L)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{n-p}(M;\mathcal L)$$
for every integer $p$, without a choice principle. The maps respect any coefficient-ring action commuting with transport, and in particular apply to local systems of modules over a noncommutative ring by forgetting to abelian groups and retaining that action. No smoothness, triangulation or prescribed finite CW structure is assumed.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $W$ be a compact oriented Hausdorff topological $n$-manifold with boundary $A$ and a supplied boundary collar $c:A\times[0,1)\to W$. Let $\mathcal L$ be a local system of abelian groups. Cap with the integral relative orientation class $z=[W,A]$ gives isomorphisms in every integer degree:
$$H^p(W,A;\mathcal L)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{n-p}(W;\mathcal L),\qquad H^p(W;\mathcal L)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{n-p}(W,A;\mathcal L).$$
The maps commute with every coefficient action commuting with transport, including noncommutative ring actions on the underlying abelian-group systems. No choice principle, smoothness, triangulation or finite CW structure is assumed.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $P\cup\eta$ be a smooth oriented two-component link in $S^3$ with unknotted axis $\eta$, and let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot. Supply disjoint closed product tubes and positive meridian/preferred zero-linking-longitude peripheral data for the knots and axis. Write $P(K)$ for infection along $\eta$ with the untwisted companion $K$. For a knot $L$, write $M(L)$ for its actual chosen zero-longitude filling, with the orientation extending its exterior. Let $w=\operatorname{lk}(P,\eta)$.

There is a compact oriented smooth cobordism $E$ with
$$\partial E=M(P)\sqcup M(K)\sqcup(-M(P(K))).$$
For any commutative unital coefficient ring $R$, it has $H_1(E;R)=R$ and $H_2(E;R)=R^2$. The two first boundary components induce the displayed basis in degree two. If $s_L=\alpha_L\cap[M(L)]$ where $\alpha_L\in H^1(M(L);R)$ evaluates as $1$ on the positive meridian, then, in those coordinates,
$$i_*s_{P(K)}=i_*s_P+w\,i_*s_K.$$
In degree one the meridians of $P$, $K$ and $P(K)$ map to $1,w,1$, respectively.

Likewise, for any finite nonempty list of knots $K_1,\ldots,K_q$ with the same supplied peripheral data, there is a compact oriented smooth cobordism $C$ from $\bigsqcup_j M(K_j)$ to $M(K_1\#\cdots\#K_q)$, with $H_1(C;R)=R$ and $H_2(C;R)=R^q$. The incoming degree-two classes are its coordinate basis and the outgoing class maps to their sum. In particular, for $X=E$ or $C$, the outgoing inclusions are injective on $H_1,H_2$ and the union of incoming components surjects onto $H_2(X;R)$.

The peripheral and framing data are supplied, rather than selected by an existence theorem. Their subsequent construction and the homology assertions use no additional choice principle. This is an ordinary-coefficient assertion; arbitrary twisted-coefficient boundary generation is not asserted.

facts:

[F2] Oriented cap duality and its boundary formula hold for compact collared manifolds and their closed boundaries, retaining constant $R$ actions by forgetting to abelian groups. contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $W$ be a compact connected oriented topological four-manifold with a supplied boundary collar. Supply a unital involution-stable inclusion $R\subseteq K$ into an involutive division ring and a based rank-one right-$R$ coefficient system on $W$, with unitary monodromy and the transported standard Hermitian form. Suppose
$$H_2(W;K)=\operatorname{im}\{H_2(\partial W;K)\longrightarrow H_2(W;K)\}.$$
Let $N$ be a finite union of connected boundary components, each satisfying $H_1(N_j;K)=0$, with its induced boundary orientation and coefficient system. On each component define the linking form by inverse coefficient Bockstein, inverse oriented cap duality and evaluation; let $B_N$ be their orthogonal sum. Then
$$B_N(x,y)=0\quad\text{whenever }x,y\in\ker\{H_1(N;R)\longrightarrow H_1(W;R)\}.$$
No choice axiom or finite CW structure is assumed. No vanishing condition is imposed on the unselected boundary components.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $M$ be a closed connected oriented Hausdorff topological three-manifold, with a specified based loop $\mu$ freely generating $H_1(M;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z$. Use the associated right infinite-cyclic coefficient system, with first-loop-first convention and transport around $a$ given by left multiplication by $t^{-\phi(a)}$, where $\phi(\mu)=1$. Put $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[t,t^{-1}]$, $\Lambda_{\mathbb Q}=\mathbb Q[t,t^{-1}]$, and $\Lambda_p=\mathbb F_p[t,t^{-1}]$. All systems have their based standard parallel Hermitian structure with involution $t^*=t^{-1}$. Define $B_{\mathbb Z}$, $B_{\mathbb Q}$ and $B_p$ on the respective first local homology modules by inverse coefficient Bockstein, inverse oriented cap duality and evaluation, with targets $\mathbb Q(t)/\Lambda$, $\mathbb Q(t)/\Lambda_{\mathbb Q}$ and $\mathbb F_p(t)/\Lambda_p$.

These forms are defined on the whole respective first homology modules. There is a primitive annihilator $\Delta\in\mathbb Z[t]$, $\Delta(1)=1$, for $H_1(M;\Lambda)$. Put $\delta=\Delta^*$. For the actual coefficient images $x_{\mathbb Q},x_p,y_{\mathbb Q},y_p$ of any $x,y\in H_1(M;\Lambda)$,
$$B_{\mathbb Q}(x_{\mathbb Q},y_{\mathbb Q})=j\bigl(B_{\mathbb Z}(x,y)\bigr),\qquad B_p(x_p,y_p)=\rho_{p,\delta}\bigl(B_{\mathbb Z}(x,y)\bigr).$$
Here $j$ is the natural integral-to-rational quotient map, and $\rho_{p,\delta}$ is the well-defined fraction reduction on the $\delta$-annihilated subgroup, $[a/\delta]\mapsto[a_p/\delta_p]$. Its denominator is nonzero modulo every prime. Consequently, if $B_{\mathbb Z}(x,x)\ne0$, then $B_{\mathbb Q}(x_{\mathbb Q},x_{\mathbb Q})\ne0$ and $B_p(x_p,x_p)\ne0$ for all primes outside a finite explicit set. No choice principle, finite CW model, smoothness, Seifert presentation, or global rational-function reduction map is assumed.

facts:
**Given:** The closed oriented manifold, marked integral homology generator and the explicit right coefficient convention.

[[thm-compact-betti-one-manifolds-have-primitive-alexander-annihilators-without-choice]]

[F2] For a primitive Laurent polynomial $\delta$, the integral-to-rational quotient map is injective on its annihilated subgroup, and the reductions $[a/\delta]\mapsto[a_p/\delta_p]$ are well-defined and preserve each nonzero class outside finitely many explicitly bounded primes. [[lem-primitive-laurent-annihilators-preserve-nonzero-values-under-rational-and-prime-reduction]]

[F3] Localization into the fraction field is exact and commutes with arbitrary chain homology. [[lem-ore-localization-is-flat-and-detects-module-torsion]]

[F4] Closed oriented cap duality holds without choice for arbitrary underlying abelian-group local systems and commuting scalar actions. The supplied Hermitian structure identifies intrinsic dual systems with conjugate right systems, naturally under the stated coefficient maps. [[thm-compact-oriented-manifold-local-coefficient-duality-in-zf]], [[lem-involutive-twisted-chain-duals-realize-local-coefficient-duality]]

[F5] Compact-manifold right singular chains have a free basis prescribed from one finite atlas and finite path data, with an explicit one-vertex reduction. The low-degree coefficient Bockstein is natural and exact without an infinite-product lifting premise. [[lem-compact-manifold-twisted-singular-chains-admit-one-vertex-reduction]], [[lem-choice-free-low-degree-coefficient-bockstein-on-compact-manifolds]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $W$ be a compact connected oriented topological four-manifold with a supplied boundary collar, and put $M=\partial W$. Let $R\subseteq K$ be a unital involution-stable subring of an involutive division ring. Supply a based rank-one right-$R$ coefficient system $\mathcal R$ on $W$, with its base fiber identified with $R$, unitary monodromy and the transported standard Hermitian form. Write $H_*(W;R)$ and $H_*(W;K)$ for its homology and scalar-extended homology.

Define the equivariant intersection pairing $\lambda_R$ by sending $\bar p\in\overline{H_2(W;R)}$ through inverse relative cap duality to $H^2(W,M;\mathcal R^\vee)$, then into $H^2(W;\mathcal R^\vee)$, then evaluating on $q\in H_2(W;R)$. Here $\mathcal R^\vee$ is the intrinsic dual coefficient system, identified with the conjugate system by the supplied Hermitian form. Thus $\lambda_R(p,q)$ is conjugate-linear in $p$ and right-linear in $q$. Define $\lambda_K$ by the same construction over $K$.

Suppose $m\ge0$ and classes $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_m,d_1,\ldots,d_m\in H_2(W;R)$ satisfy
$$\lambda_R(\ell_i,\ell_j)=0,\qquad\lambda_R(\ell_i,d_j)=\lambda_R(d_j,\ell_i)=\delta_{ij},$$
and suppose
$$\dim_K\bigl(H_2(W;K)/\operatorname{im}H_2(M;K)\bigr)\le2m.$$
Let $M_0$ be one connected boundary component with $H_1(M_0;K)=0$. Its coefficient Bockstein, oriented cap duality and evaluation define the linking form $B_0$ with values in $K/R$. Then
$$B_0(x,y)=0\quad\text{for all }x,y\in\ker\{H_1(M_0;R)\longrightarrow H_1(W;R)\}.$$
No vanishing condition on the other boundary components is imposed. No choice axiom, finite CW structure, or general noncommutative universal-coefficient theorem is assumed.

The cochain identification is simplexwise, so restriction to a subspace and the relative cochain subcomplex preserve it. [[lem-involutive-twisted-chain-duals-realize-local-coefficient-duality]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Let A be a proper annulus in a compact oriented 4-manifold W, with boundary knots K₀ and K₁ in the two boundary 3-spheres. Assume A has an oriented normal disk neighborhood A×D² whose endpoint framings are the preferred zero-linking longitudes. Let R be Z or R_n=Z[1/|n|], and assume each end S³→W is an R-homology isomorphism. Removing A×D² and attaching D²×S¹×I along the annular side, with ∂D² matched to the annulus longitude and the core matched to the normal meridian, produces a cobordism V from M(K₀) to M(K₁). The statement predicts that the boundary inclusions M(K_i)→V are R-homology isomorphisms. If W is simply connected, it also predicts that π₁(V) is normally generated by either endpoint knot-group image.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let V=S¹×D² be the standard oriented solid torus, with oriented core, meridional disk and product longitude. A pattern is a smooth oriented knot P in the interior of V. Its winding number w(P) is its algebraic intersection with an oriented meridional disk, equivalently the coefficient of the core in [P]∈H₁(V;Z). For a smooth oriented knot K in S³, let e_K:V→S³ be a zero-framed tubular embedding carrying the core to K and carrying the meridian and product longitude to the positive meridian and preferred longitude of K. The satellite knot P(K) is e_K(P).

When concordance preservation has been established, the formula [K]↦[P(K)] defines a set map on each of C_sm, C_top, C_ex and C^{1/n}. The solid-torus meridian is strong winding number ±1 for P if, after V is embedded as the standard unknotted solid torus and P(U) denotes the resulting closure, that meridian normally generates π₁(S³\P(U)). Normal generation means that the smallest normal subgroup containing the element is the whole group. Strong winding number ±1 is a separate condition from ordinary winding number ±1. No additivity or homomorphism property is part of this definition.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $L$ be a finite geometric simplicial complex with an ordered vertex set, and let $\mathcal R$ be a local system of rank-one free right modules over an arbitrary unital ring $R$. Its finite simplicial chain complex $F_*(L;\mathcal R)$ and intrinsic singular chain complex $C_*(L;\mathcal R)$ admit $R$-linear chain maps
$$P:C_*(L;\mathcal R)\to F_*(L;\mathcal R),\qquad J:F_*(L;\mathcal R)\to C_*(L;\mathcal R)$$
with $PJ=1$ and an explicitly constructed chain homotopy $JP\simeq1$. Choices of bases at its finitely many vertices make $F_*$ bounded finite-free.

Consequently, for every compact connected Hausdorff topological manifold $M$, with boundary allowed, and every such local system supplied with a base-fiber identification with $R$, its nonnegative singular chain complex is free with a formula-specified basis and is $R$-linearly chain-homotopy dominated by a bounded finite-free complex. No choice principle, triangulation of $M$, or assertion of finite CW type for $M$ is assumed.

facts:

Applied to underlying abelian-group systems it respects any commuting right-$R$ action, since all coefficient transports are right-linear. [[thm-excision-and-mayer-vietoris-with-local-coefficients]]

[F2] A compact Hausdorff manifold with boundary is a retract of a finite Euclidean cubical complex, without choice. [[thm-compact-manifolds-are-retracts-of-finite-polyhedra-without-choice]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Work in ZF. Let $A$ be any associative unital ring and let $C$ be a chain complex of unital right $A$-modules with $C_n=0$ for $n<0$. Supply a chain complex $F$ with $F_n=0$ outside $0\le n\le m$, each $F_n$ supplied as a finite free right $A$-module, chain maps $f:C\to F$ and $g:F\to C$, and right $A$-linear maps $h_n:C_n\to C_{n+1}$ such that
$$1_C-gf=d_Ch+hd_C.$$
Then there is a chain complex $E$ of finitely generated projective right $A$-modules, zero outside $0\le n\le N$ for some finite $N$, together with explicitly constructed chain maps $a:C\to E$, $b:E\to C$ and chain homotopies
$$1_C-ba=dH+Hd,\qquad 1_E-ab=dL+Ld.$$
The modules of $E$ below its top degree can be taken finite free, and its top module is the image of an explicit idempotent on $\bigoplus_{j=0}^mF_j$.

Neither freeness nor projectivity nor finite generation of the modules of $C$ is required. Thus the result applies in particular to the nonnegative singular or cellular free chain complexes with specified bases. More generally it applies after reindexing whenever $C$ and $F$ have a common finite lower bound. It makes no assertion for inputs unbounded below and no assertion that $E$ is finite free or that any underlying space has finite CW type. No form of the Axiom of Choice is assumed.

facts:
**Given:** The ring, nonnegative complexes and explicit domination data in the Statement. Maps are composed from right to left; $d=d_C$ and $\partial=d_F$. A composition containing a zero degree module is zero. A power $h^s$ denotes the specified successive degree-one maps, and $h^0=1$.

[F1] Chain maps commute with differentials. A degree-one homotopy has boundary $dH+Hd$; mutually inverse maps up to these boundaries are a chain homotopy equivalence. These conventions are [[def-chain-map]], [[def-chain-homotopy]] and [[def-chain-homotopy-equivalence]], applied to right module homomorphisms.

[F2] Projectivity means the lifting property for surjective module homomorphisms. The left-module convention of [[def-projective-module]] is applied to $A^{\mathrm{op}}$ for right modules. Only finite free modules and their explicit summands will be used; their lifting property is proved below.

[F3] A finite list of nonempty sets admits a simultaneous choice in ZF. [[lem-finite-choice]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume AC_ω. Under connected sum, each of C_sm, C_top, C_ex and C^{1/n} is an abelian group. The identity is the class of the unknot, and the inverse of [K] is the class of the reverse mirror of K. Each category retains the ambient and coefficient conditions in its definition.

facts:
**Given:** The four concordance sets with their specified concordance relations.

[F1] The ambient and coefficient conditions defining the four concordance relations ([[def-cdr-satellite-concordance-categories]]).

[F2] The mirror-reverse connected sum K#−K bounds a ribbon disk in the standard 4-ball ([[lem-general-knot-reverse-mirror-sum-is-ribbon]]).

[F3] Connected sum is associative and commutative on oriented knot types, with the unknot identity ([[thm-oriented-knot-connected-sum-is-a-commutative-monoid]]).

[F4] Connected sum of knot concordances is the operation on concordance classes ([[def-knot-connected-sum-and-prime-knot]]).

[A1] AC_ω supplies the countable choice used by the cited ribbon and concordance constructions ([[def-countable-choice]]).

[F5] **External TOP/exotic input.** In the category conventions of [F1], connected sum descends to an abelian group on $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{top}}$ and $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{ex}}$, with unknot identity and reverse-mirror inverse. This is the group assertion in Cochran–Davis–Ray Section1, printed1–2. Its underlying TOP ambient gluing and relative-collar conclusion are imported under the run-specific external-source boundary; no new local proof of those unresolved ambient identifications is claimed. The cited CDR definitions and group assertion on printed1–2 were read directly.

[F6] **Compact finite-input convention.** The classical external results are initially used in ordinary ZFC, not assumed choice-free from their citations. For this one application take finitely many charts covering the given compact manifolds and finitely many pair charts covering each given compact disk or annulus, shrinking to closed inner charts inside open outer charts. Such finite subcovers exist by compactness; selecting this finite list uses no axiom of choice. Include the actual boundary/product collars and all supplied homeomorphisms in the list. Encode chart domains and overlaps by their rational balls, continuous maps and their inverses by dense rational data with moduli on the closed inner charts, and smooth maps by all finite-order derivative and Taylor-remainder data. The modulus at each integer scale is the least integer satisfying its uniform-continuity bound; restrictions to rational compact boxes use the least box index. These are uniquely defined choices from subsets of $\mathbb N$, not a countable family of freely selected charts. Include positive open-image and overlap margins, inverse identities, finite cover/Lebesgue bounds, and the pair-section identities with positive separation from the compact outside-patch remainder. On the standard disk/annulus parameters the latter certify the actual plane section, not merely a continuous embedding. One real $r$ codes these finitely many maps and their canonical countable data. The external relative-constructibility input is that $L[r]$ is an inner model of ZFC containing $r$ (Karagila, §8.3, p.42); no ambient choice hypothesis is required. An internally produced compact witness is exported with the same certificates, and hence is an actual ambient compact witness. contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $W$ be a compact connected oriented Hausdorff topological four-manifold and put $M=\partial W$, allowing $M$ empty. Let $k$ be a commutative field, $G$ a PTFA group, and $\phi:\pi_1(W)\to G$ a supplied coefficient homomorphism. Write $K$ for the fraction division ring of $k[G]$, with its standard involution, and use the induced rank-one right-coefficient systems. Suppose $\dim_kH_1(M_j;k)=1$ for each connected component $M_j$ of $M$. Then
$$\dim_K\operatorname{coker}\{H_2(M;K)\to H_2(W;K)\}\le\dim_k\operatorname{coker}\{H_2(M;k)\to H_2(W;k)\}.$$
All dimensions in the formula are finite. No choice axiom, smoothness, triangulation, or supplied finite CW model of $W$ is assumed.

facts:
**Given:** The compact oriented manifold, field, group, coefficient homomorphism and boundary first-Betti hypothesis.

[F1] Singular right-coefficient chains of a compact manifold, with boundary allowed, have an actual basis and explicit domination by a bounded finite-free complex. The choice-free Wall construction converts that domination into a nonnegative bounded finitely generated projective chain model, with maps and homotopies. [[thm-finite-geometric-complex-chains-dominate-compact-manifold-chains-in-zf]], [[lem-choice-free-wall-chain-finiteness-from-explicit-domination]]

[F2] Finite projective PTFA base change preserves Euler characteristic and gives $b_1^K\le b_1^k-1$ when $b_0^k=1$ and $b_0^K=0$. The group-ring fractions and standard involution exist for the stated fields. [[lem-ptfa-finite-projective-basechange-preserves-euler-characteristic]], [[lem-ptfa-integral-and-field-group-rings-have-compatible-ore-involutions]]

[F3] Compact boundaries have collars, without choice. Relative and closed cap duality apply to arbitrary underlying abelian-group local systems with commuting actions. The standard unitary structure identifies dual cochains with conjugate chains; its simplexwise formula respects boundary subcomplexes. [[thm-topological-collaring-for-manifold-boundaries]], [[thm-compact-collared-manifold-local-coefficient-lefschetz-duality-in-zf]], [[thm-compact-oriented-manifold-local-coefficient-duality-in-zf]], [[lem-involutive-twisted-chain-duals-realize-local-coefficient-duality]]

[F4] The homology pair sequence is exact with its actual inclusion and boundary maps. [[thm-pair-long-exact-sequences-with-local-coefficients]]
