contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Let P be a pattern and let K be a knot. Choose a transverse meridional disk for P and a short product slab about it. Form a pattern P_K by replacing all strands of P across that slab by parallel untwisted copies of a long-knot representative of K, with the individual strand orientations inherited from P; this is simultaneous companion insertion, rather than tying K into just one arc. For every knot J, the satellite P(K#J) is isotopic as an oriented knot to P_K(J). The pattern P_K has the same winding number as P.

facts:
**Given:** The pattern $P$, knots $K,J$, the transverse meridional disk and product slab specified in the Statement, and the preferred zero framings.

[F1] A satellite inserts the complete pattern into the companion's zero-framed tubular neighborhood, matching its meridian and preferred longitude. [[def-satellite-induced-concordance-operator]], [[def-satellite-pattern-companion-and-winding-number]]

[F2] Connected sum joins two long-knot representatives end to end with their endpoint product coordinates matched. [[def-knot-connected-sum-and-prime-knot]]

[F3] Coordinate disks have smooth cutoffs, and an everywhere invertible derivative gives a smooth local inverse. [[lem-smooth-bump-between-concentric-euclidean-balls]], [[thm-euclidean-inverse-function-theorem]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Let P be a pattern of strong winding number ±1. For every oriented knot K, regard P(K) as the pattern obtained by tying K into each strand of P in the companion solid torus. Then this new pattern P(K) also has strong winding number ±1. A pattern obtained from any strong-winding pattern by taking connected sum with a local knot also has strong winding number ±1.

facts:
**Given:** A pattern P, its unknotted-solid-torus closure P(U), strong-winding meridian η, and a knot K inserted as companion.

[F1] Strong winding means the axis meridian normally generates the closure complement group ([[def-satellite-induced-concordance-operator]]).

[F2] The knot exterior has meridian μ_K and preferred longitude λ_K on its boundary torus ([[def-knot-exterior]], [[def-knot-meridian-and-preferred-longitude]]).

[F3] The knot-group meridian normally generates π₁(S³\K): meridional filling gives S³, and van Kampen quotients by the normal closure of μ_K to π₁(S³)=1 ([[def-knot-exterior]], [[def-knot-meridian-and-preferred-longitude]]).

[F4] Connected sum is formed by joining the two knot exteriors along a meridional annulus ([[def-knot-connected-sum-and-prime-knot]]).

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $W,X$ be compact oriented topological four-manifolds with supplied boundary collars and decompositions $\partial W=A\sqcup D$, $\partial X=A\sqcup B$. Glue their copies of $A$ by a supplied orientation-reversing identification, obtaining $Y=W\cup_A X$ with $\partial Y=D\sqcup B$. Supply one ambient rank-one right-$R$ local system on $Y$, where $R$ is an involutive unital ring. On each connected component supply a base-fiber identification with $R$ and unitary monodromy, and use its transported standard Hermitian form. Use its restrictions and the induced orientations on $W,X$.

For the intersection pairings defined by inverse relative cap duality, passage to absolute cohomology and evaluation,
$$\lambda_Y(i_*p,i_*q)=\lambda_W(p,q)\qquad(p,q\in H_2(W;R)).$$
In particular all isotropic and dual-pair identities for homology classes in $W$ persist under their inclusion in $Y$. The result applies to topological manifolds and requires no geometric surface transversality or choice principle.

facts:
**Given:** The collared gluing, compatible orientations, single ambient coefficient system and parallel form.

[F1] Relative duality identifies $\overline{H_2(W;R)}$ with $H^2(W,\partial W;\mathcal R^\vee)$, and likewise for $Y$. The dual-system identification is relative to the supplied form and is compatible with restriction. [[thm-compact-collared-manifold-local-coefficient-lefschetz-duality-in-zf]], [[lem-involutive-twisted-chain-duals-realize-local-coefficient-duality]]

[F2] Local excision holds with actual small-chain homotopy inverses. Support and relative cap commute with those maps by their face formulas, and orientation classes are characterized by their local images. These facts apply to the underlying abelian-group systems at base ring $\mathbb Z$, retaining the right or left actions commuting with transport. [[thm-excision-and-mayer-vietoris-with-local-coefficients]], [[def-cup-and-cap-products-with-local-coefficient-pairings]], [[lem-canonical-twisted-fundamental-classes-over-compact-subsets]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $V$ be a compact connected oriented topological four-manifold with boundary a chosen zero-longitude surgery $M(J)$. Suppose
$$H_1(V;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z,\qquad H_2(V;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^{2r}.$$
Put $\pi=\pi_1(V)$ and $\Pi_s=\pi/\pi^{(s)}$, where $s\ge0$ and the superscript denotes the ordinary derived series. Supply classes $x_1,\ldots,x_r,y_1,\ldots,y_r\in H_2(V;\mathbb Z[\Pi_s])$ satisfying
$$\lambda(x_i,x_j)=0,\qquad\lambda(x_i,y_j)=\delta_{ij}.$$
These are actual integral intersection-pair data; existence of such data is not asserted.

Form $W$ by finitely many oriented attachments of standard connected-sum or infection cobordisms, allowing their orientation reversals, along each piece's marked outgoing surgery component. Use the supplied peripheral models in those constructions. Let $\phi:\pi_1(W)\to G$ be a supplied homomorphism to a PTFA group whose restriction to $\pi_1(V)$ factors through $\Pi_s$. In particular the factorization is automatic if $G^{(s)}=1$. Let $k=\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb F_p$ for a prime $p$, put $A=k[G]$, and let $K$ be its fraction division ring with standard involution.

Then there are image classes $\ell_i,d_i\in H_2(W;A)$ with
$$\lambda_A(\ell_i,\ell_j)=0,\qquad\lambda_A(\ell_i,d_j)=\lambda_A(d_j,\ell_i)=\delta_{ij},$$
and both cokernel dimensions satisfy
$$\dim_K\operatorname{coker}\{H_2(\partial W;K)\to H_2(W;K)\}\le\dim_k\operatorname{coker}\{H_2(\partial W;k)\to H_2(W;k)\}\le2r.$$
For every boundary component $M_0$ with nontrivial restricted homomorphism, $H_1(M_0;K)=0$ and its Bockstein-duality pairing has
$$B_0(a,b)=0\quad\text{for all }a,b\in\ker\{H_1(M_0;A)\to H_1(W;A)\}.$$
Consequently every boundary class with nonzero self-pairing has nonzero image in $H_1(W;A)$. The theorem applies to locally flat topological bordisms as well as smooth ones and introduces no choice principle.

facts:
**Given:** The actual integral homology and lifted pairing data, finite framed cobordism attachments, coefficient homomorphism and field in the Statement.

[F1] Standard infection and connected-sum pieces have outgoing injections on ordinary $H_1,H_2$ and incoming degree-two surjectivity. A collared gluing with outgoing $H_1$ injection and remaining-boundary $H_2$ surjection induces a surjection on boundary homology cokernels. [[lem-standard-infection-cobordisms-have-boundary-generated-second-homology]], [[lem-boundary-homology-cokernels-surject-under-excisive-bordism-gluing]]

[F2] Ambient unitary coefficients preserve intersection pairings under collared gluing, and the pairings are Hermitian. [[lem-equivariant-intersection-pairings-are-preserved-by-collared-bordism-gluing]], [[lem-relative-unitary-equivariant-intersection-pairing-is-hermitian]]

[F3] A compact oriented four-manifold with boundary components of ordinary first Betti number one has localized boundary-cokernel dimension at most the ordinary one. A nontrivial PTFA coefficient system on a compact Betti-one manifold kills localized first homology. [[thm-ptfa-localized-boundary-intersection-rank-is-no-larger-than-ordinary-rank]], [[lem-ptfa-localization-kills-first-homology-of-betti-one-manifolds]]

[F4] Integral pairs and the localized cokernel bound force each selected acyclic boundary kernel to be isotropic for the Bockstein-duality form. [[thm-unimodular-intersection-pairs-force-boundary-blanchfield-kernel-isotropy]]

[F5] Relative cap duality holds with arbitrary underlying abelian-group local systems. Constant rational localization is exact; compact manifold boundaries have collars without choice. [[thm-compact-collared-manifold-local-coefficient-lefschetz-duality-in-zf]], [[lem-ore-localization-is-flat-and-detects-module-torsion]], [[thm-topological-collaring-for-manifold-boundaries]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $W$ be a compact connected oriented topological four-manifold with supplied boundary collar, and let $R$ be an involutive unital ring. Supply a based rank-one right-$R$ local system $\mathcal R$, a base-fiber identification with $R$, unitary monodromy and its parallel standard Hermitian form. For $p\in H_2(W;\mathcal R)$ let $a_p\in H^2(W,\partial W;\mathcal R^\vee)$ be the inverse cap-duality image of $\bar p$, using the form to identify the intrinsic dual system with $\overline{\mathcal R}$. Define
$$\lambda(p,q)=\langle j(a_p),q\rangle,$$
where $j$ forgets the relative condition and the last pairing is intrinsic cochain evaluation. Then
$$\lambda(p,q)=\overline{\lambda(q,p)}$$
for all $p,q$. In particular $\lambda(\ell_i,d_j)=\delta_{ij}$ implies $\lambda(d_j,\ell_i)=\delta_{ij}$. No choice axiom, triangulation or geometric transversality of surfaces in dimension four is required.

facts:
**Given:** The compact collared manifold, ring, unitary local system and its supplied standard Hermitian structure.

[F1] Relative cap duality holds for arbitrary abelian-group local systems and commuting scalar actions; unitary Hermitian structures identify intrinsic dual systems with conjugate systems. [F2] Cup and cap are given by front/back faces and coefficient transport, and their associativity identity is checked on these faces. The relative orientation class is represented by a finite integral chain with boundary in $\partial W$. contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Let P be an oriented pattern of winding n≠0 and K an oriented knot. If P(U) bounds a smooth proper disk in a compact smooth oriented 4-manifold B whose oriented boundary is identified with the standard oriented S³ and H_i(B;R_n)≅H_i(B⁴;R_n) for every i, then for every K the zero surgeries M(P(K)) and M(K) are smoothly R_n-homology cobordant. For the positive meridians determined by the supplied orientations, their images in the cobordism satisfy [mu_K]=n[mu_{P(K)}]; in particular they differ by a unit of R_n. This is a winding-unit meridian comparison, not a claim of literal equality for arbitrary winding. If P has strong winding number ±1 and P(U) is pseudo-slice (respectively locally flat topologically slice), then M(P(K)) and M(K) are smoothly (respectively topologically) homology cobordant through a 4-manifold whose fundamental group is normally generated by the image of the fundamental group of either boundary component. The category and closure hypotheses are separate and cannot be inferred from winding alone.

The pseudo-slice convention likewise includes this orientation. No orientability is inferred solely from localized homology.

Consequently this gives exactly the boundary-compatible product tube required by the TOP clauses of steps1.1–4.1. The modulus at each integer scale is the least integer satisfying its uniform-continuity bound; restrictions to rational compact boxes use the least box index. These are uniquely defined choices from subsets of $\mathbb N$, not a countable family of freely selected charts. Include positive open-image and overlap margins, inverse identities, finite cover/Lebesgue bounds, and the pair-section identities with positive separation from the compact outside-patch remainder. On the standard disk/annulus parameters the latter certify the actual plane section, not merely a continuous embedding. One real $r$ codes these finitely many maps and their canonical countable data. The external relative-constructibility input is that $L[r]$ is an inner model of ZFC containing $r$ (Karagila, §8.3, p.42); no ambient choice hypothesis is required. All compact maps are decoded using these same moduli, so the inverse identities, covers, pair sections and collar equalities are checked on dense rational sets with their displayed buffers and remain valid in the ambient universe $V$. contract.text: Let P be a winding-zero pattern whose image consists of topologically slice knots, and let C_sm be the smooth knot concordance group. For n≥0, let Pⁿ be the n-fold composition of the induced satellite map, with P⁰ the identity, and let ⟨S⟩ denote the subgroup generated by S. contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Let G be a countable discrete amenable group. For every right CG-module M and every integer q>0, the N G-von Neumann dimension of Tor_q^{CG}(M,N G) is zero. This dimension-flatness statement does not say that the Tor module itself is zero.

facts:
**Given:** A countable discrete amenable group $G$, a right $\mathbb CG$-module $M$, and $q>0$. Work in the standing full-AC convention of the L2-signature definitions; the spectral and Hilbert-module arguments below use that existing convention, not an additional group-theoretic hypothesis.

[F1] The group von Neumann algebra, its canonical trace and the extended projective-submodule dimension have the stated meanings. The defining page fixes full AC as its foundational convention. [[def-integral-half-solutions-strebel-and-l2-signatures]]

[F2] In a finite von Neumann projection module, Hilbert-dense submodules have dimension-zero quotient; zero-dimensional modules are closed under submodules, quotients, extensions and filtered colimits. [[lem-finite-von-neumann-module-dimension-and-dense-quotients]]

[F3] For a finite matrix over $\mathbb CG$, its algebraic kernel is Hilbert-dense in its full Hilbert kernel, and the quotient of its $\mathcal N G$-kernel by the right $\mathcal N G$-span of that algebraic kernel has dimension zero. [[lem-amenable-folner-kernel-approximation]]

[F4] Tensor products consist of finite sums of elementary tensors and preserve cokernels over arbitrary rings. Apply the stated left-module version to the opposite ring and flip elementary tensors to obtain the right-module version used here. [[lem-tensoring-with-a-right-module-is-additive-right-exact-and-preserves-direct-sums]]

[F5] Tor is homology after tensoring a projective resolution of the right module. Canonical free covers iterated on kernels give a free resolution; apply the left-module construction to the opposite ring for right modules. Under the standing AC convention it is projective. Any two projective resolutions are homotopy equivalent over the resolved module, under DC, which follows from this standing AC convention. [[def-tor-by-resolving-the-right-module]], [[prop-the-iterated-free-module-resolution-is-canonical-in-zf]], [[thm-projective-resolutions-of-the-same-object-are-homotopy-equivalent-over-that-object]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume AC. Let $G$ be a discrete group, let $A=\mathcal N G\subseteq\mathcal B(\ell^2(G))$ have its canonical faithful normal trace $\tau$, and give matrices the unnormalized trace $\tau_r((a_{ij}))=\sum_{i=1}^r\tau(a_{ii})$. For a projection $p\in M_r(A)$ put $\dim_A(pA^r)=\tau_r(p)$; for any right $A$-module take the supremum of dimensions of its finitely generated projective submodules. These dimensions are independent of the projective representation. If $L\subseteq pA^r$ is any submodule and $q$ is the projection onto its Hilbert closure in $p\ell^2(G)^r$, then $q\in M_r(A)$, $q\le p$, and
$$\dim_A L=\tau_r(q),\qquad \dim_A(pA^r/L)=\tau_r(p)-\tau_r(q).$$
In particular a Hilbert-dense submodule has dimension-zero quotient. Modules of dimension zero are closed under submodules, quotients, extensions and filtered colimits. For any matrix $B\in M_{r,s}(A)$, its kernel and Hilbert-closed image are projection modules, its algebraic image is isomorphic to its support projection module, and
$$\tau_s(P_{\ker B})+\tau_r(P_{\overline{\operatorname{im}B}})=s.$$

facts:
**Given:** AC, the group algebra von Neumann closure $A$, its canonical trace and the dimension convention in the Statement. Vectors in $A^r$ are columns and matrices act on the left, so their maps are right $A$-linear.

[F1] The canonical group trace is faithful, normal and tracial. Matrix traces inherit these properties by finite summation. [[def-tracial-state-and-faithful-normal-trace-on-a-von-neumann-algebra]]

[F2] A generated concrete von Neumann algebra is strongly closed and equals its double commutant. [[thm-double-commutant-theorem-for-concrete-von-neumann-algebras]]

[F3] Bounded self-adjoint operators have spectral projections and bounded Borel functional calculus. [[thm-spectral-theorem-for-bounded-normal-operators-pvm-form]]

[F4] A bounded operator has polar decomposition, with initial and final spaces the closures of its adjoint range and range. [[thm-polar-decomposition-for-bounded-operators]]

[A1] AC is the standing hypothesis of [F2]–[F4]. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let X be a closed oriented smooth 4-manifold, Γ a discrete group, and φ:π₁(X)→Γ a homomorphism. Then the von Neumann signature of the NΓ-coefficient intersection form equals the ordinary signature:
sign_Γ^(2)(X,φ)=sign(X).

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, the closed oriented smooth four-manifold $X$, the discrete group $\Gamma$, and the homomorphism $\phi$ of the Statement. AC is the standing convention of the coefficient Definition and the supplied smooth realization proof.

[A1] Full AC is already assumed by the coefficient Definition. [[def-integral-half-solutions-strebel-and-l2-signatures]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F2] The smooth group-signature theorem constructs a coefficient-preserving smooth five-bordism after an injective acyclic-envelope enlargement, proves signature invariance across that actual bordism, and proves induction under group inclusion. Its closed smooth conclusion applies to arbitrary discrete target groups. [[thm-smooth-group-signature-defects-are-independent-and-uniformly-bounded]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Let R be Q or F_p, let Γ be a countable discrete amenable group in Strebel's class D(R), and let C_* be a bounded-below chain complex of right ZΓ-modules whose C_i are finitely generated free for i≤n. Give R the trivial Γ-action. If H_i(C_*⊗_{ZΓ}R)=0 for every i≤n, then H_i(C_*⊗_{ZΓ}NΓ) has von Neumann dimension zero for every i≤n. This is a dimension-zero conclusion and does not assert that the L²-homology module vanishes.

Dimension-zero modules have dimension-zero quotients. [[lem-finite-von-neumann-module-dimension-and-dense-quotients]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let P be a pattern of nonzero winding n. If P(U) is smoothly slice in an R_n-homology 4-ball, then P is weakly injective on C^{1/n}, meaning P(K)=P(U) implies K=U in that category. If P has strong winding number ±1 and P(U) is pseudo-slice (respectively locally flat topologically slice), then P is weakly injective on C_ex (respectively C_top). In ordinary smooth concordance, if P(U) is smoothly slice in standard B⁴ and P has strong winding number ±1, then P is weakly injective on C_sm provided the smooth 4-dimensional Poincaré conjecture holds.

For any pattern P and knots K,J with P(K)=P(J) in one of these concordance groups, the connected-sum reduction constructs a pattern R for which R(−K#J) is concordant to U, whose closure R(U)=−P(K)#P(K) is ribbon, and whose winding w(R)=w(P). If P is strong winding ±1, then R is strong winding ±1. This reduction turns injectivity of P into weak injectivity of R; it does not assert that P itself is weakly injective without the closure hypotheses above.

[F2] The zero-surgery comparison has a smooth R_n branch and category-specific exotic/topological branches with their closure hypotheses ([[lem-cdr-zero-surgery-pattern-homology-cobordism]]).

[F3] The definitions of C_ex, C_top and C^{1/n} specify the ambient 4-manifold and coefficient conditions ([[def-cdr-satellite-concordance-categories]]).

[F4] Only finite connected-sum, inverse and compatibility instances for the actual supplied knots and concordances are used here. Their choice-free compact-input specialization is established in step0.1. The general AC_omega group theorem records the same operations ([[thm-cdr-concordance-categories-form-abelian-groups]]); its stronger choice premise is not invoked in $V$ for this unqualified Statement.

[F5] The ordinary smooth branch uses the special smooth S⁴-complement assertion ([[lem-cdr-smooth-s4-complement-is-standard-ball]]).

[F6] Satellite insertion rewrites P(K#J) as P_K(J) for the simultaneous companion-insertion pattern P_K ([[lem-satellite-connected-sum-substitution]]).

[F7] The satellite rule descends to the specified concordance classes only after concordance preservation ([[lem-satellite-operator-preserves-concordance]]).

[F8] A concordance annulus with a compatible zero-framed normal neighborhood gives a zero-surgery cobordism ([[lem-concordance-annulus-induces-zero-surgery-cobordism]]).

[F9] Strong winding survives companion insertion and local connected sum ([[lem-strong-winding-stable-under-companion-insertion]]).

[F11] **External TOP input.** A compact contractible topological four-manifold with boundary homeomorphic to the standard $S^3$ is homeomorphic to $B^4$. This is the Freedman consequence invoked explicitly in Cochran–Davis–Ray, Proposition3.2 and its proof, printed7–8; it is imported, not locally reconstructed. A supplied boundary marking is respected: if $h:B\to B^4$ is any such homeomorphism and $k:\partial B\to S^3$ is the required marking, extend $k\circ(h|_{\partial B})^{-1}$ radially over $B^4$ by the Alexander extension and postcompose $h$. Thus the co-core boundary knot retains its actual endpoint marking. This fact applies to the underlying TOP manifold of a smooth contractible $B$ as well; it asserts no smooth standardness. The cited application in CDR printed7–8 was read directly; the original Freedman paper is cited as its authoritative source, not claimed read in full here.

[F12] **External remaining concordance input.** Zero-framed surgery on a concordance annulus descends to a homology cobordism of the zero-surgery manifolds in the same category; the coefficient ring is $R_n$ for localized concordance, and in the TOP/exotic categories the fundamental group is normally generated by either boundary knot-group image. The meridians are the normal-circle factors along the framed annulus and are identified by its product coordinate. This is the zero-surgery descent in CDR Section3, printed7, paragraph preceding Definition3.1 and diagram3.1, read directly. The local normal-GIVEN construction [F8] is retained; this explicit external input supplies its needed conclusion where an unresolved general annulus-neighborhood/descent interface would otherwise be required. No local reconstruction of that missing interface is asserted.

[F13] **Compact finite-input convention.** The classical external results are initially used in ordinary ZFC, not assumed choice-free from their citations. For this one application take finitely many charts covering the given compact manifolds and finitely many pair charts covering each given compact disk or annulus, shrinking to closed inner charts inside open outer charts. Such finite subcovers exist by compactness; selecting this finite list uses no axiom of choice. Include the actual boundary/product collars and all supplied homeomorphisms in the list. Encode chart domains and overlaps by their rational balls, continuous maps and their inverses by dense rational data with moduli on the closed inner charts, and smooth maps by all finite-order derivative and Taylor-remainder data. The modulus at each integer scale is the least integer satisfying its uniform-continuity bound; restrictions to rational compact boxes use the least box index. These are uniquely defined choices from subsets of $\mathbb N$, not a countable family of freely selected charts. Include positive open-image and overlap margins, inverse identities, finite cover/Lebesgue bounds, and the pair-section identities with positive separation from the compact outside-patch remainder. On the standard disk/annulus parameters the latter certify the actual plane section, not merely a continuous embedding. One real $r$ codes these finitely many maps and their canonical countable data. The external relative-constructibility input is that $L[r]$ is an inner model of ZFC containing $r$ (Karagila, §8.3, p.42); no ambient choice hypothesis is required. All compact maps are decoded using these same moduli, so the inverse identities, covers, pair sections and collar equalities are checked on dense rational sets with their displayed buffers and remain valid in the ambient universe $V$. An internally produced compact witness is exported with the same certificates, and hence is an actual ambient compact witness. This uses the peer-checked compact annulus coding pattern of the standard connected-sum compatibility supplier only at its geometric scope; it does not assert that arbitrary homology or fundamental-group hypotheses are absolute.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $M$ be a closed oriented three-manifold, with a specified coefficient homomorphism $\phi:\pi_1(M_j)\to\Gamma$ on each component $M_j$, where $\Gamma$ is PTFA. Let $k=\mathbb Z$ or a commutative field, put $A=k[\Gamma]$, and let $K$ be its fraction division ring with the involution fixing $k$ and inverting group elements. Let $A\subseteq R\subseteq K$ be an involution-stable unital intermediate ring, and assume $H_1(M;K)=0$.

Then $H_1(M;R)$ is an $R$-torsion module and the coefficient Bockstein, oriented duality and evaluation define its Blanchfield pairing with target $K/R$. This pairing is nonsingular provided that on each component at least one of the following holds: every right ideal of $R$ is principal; $H_0(M_j;R)=0$; or the image of $\phi|_{\pi_1(M_j)}$ is cyclic. The last condition includes the usual integral infinite-cyclic coefficient case $R=\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$, without asserting that this ring is a principal ideal domain. No choice principle is assumed.

facts:
**Given:** The closed manifold, coefficient systems, coefficient rings and vanishing in the Statement; the additional alternative is imposed only for the nonsingularity conclusion.

[F1] The Blanchfield convention is the inverse coefficient Bockstein after oriented duality, followed by evaluation; its first argument is conjugate-linear and its second argument right-linear. [[def-blanchfield-pairing-and-higher-order-rho-invariant]]

[F2] Integral and field PTFA group rings and their intermediate rings have the asserted Ore fractions and compatible involutions. [[lem-ptfa-integral-and-field-group-rings-have-compatible-ore-involutions]]

[F3] Ore localization is exact, commutes with arbitrary chain homology, and annihilates exactly the elements with a nonzero right annihilator. [[lem-ore-localization-is-flat-and-detects-module-torsion]]

[F4] Twisted singular chains admit a choice-free one-vertex reduction with degree-zero boundary ideal $\sum_{h\in\operatorname{im}\phi}(h-1)R$. For a principal such ideal, degree-one evaluation with $K/R$ is an isomorphism. [[lem-compact-manifold-twisted-singular-chains-admit-one-vertex-reduction]], [[lem-principal-boundary-chain-evaluation-over-division-fractions]]

[F5] Involutive twisted-chain duals have the actual intrinsic local cochain models, and oriented duality identifies $H^p(\operatorname{Hom}_R(C_*,R))$ with $\overline{H_{3-p}(C_*)}$. [[lem-involutive-twisted-chain-duals-realize-local-coefficient-duality]]

[F6] The low-degree coefficient Bockstein is exact at $H^1(K/R)$ and $H^2(R)$ without an infinite product lifting assumption. [[lem-choice-free-low-degree-coefficient-bockstein-on-compact-manifolds]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let W₀ and W₁ be compact oriented smooth 4-manifolds with a common identified boundary M, and let Γ be a discrete group. Suppose coefficient homomorphisms ψ_i:π₁(W_i)→Γ agree on π₁(M), and let X=W₀∪_M(−W₁) be the resulting closed oriented 4-manifold with its glued coefficient map. Then
sign(X)=sign(W₀)−sign(W₁)
and
sign_Γ^(2)(X)=sign_Γ^(2)(W₀,ψ₀)−sign_Γ^(2)(W₁,ψ₁).

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume AC. For every closed oriented smooth four-manifold $Z$ and every based homomorphism $\theta:\pi_1Z\to G$ to an arbitrary discrete group,
$$\operatorname{sign}^{(2)}_G(Z,\theta)=\operatorname{sign}(Z).$$
Let $M$ be a closed oriented smooth three-manifold and $\phi:\pi_1M\to G$ any homomorphism. There exist an injective homomorphism $j:G\hookrightarrow\Gamma$ and a compact oriented smooth four-manifold $W$ with $\partial W=M$ and a homomorphism $\pi_1W\to\Gamma$ restricting to $j\phi$. For any such data put
$$\rho_{\mathrm{sm}}(M,\phi)=\operatorname{sign}^{(2)}_\Gamma(W)-\operatorname{sign}(W).$$
This number is independent of the smooth bound, its extending map and the injective target enlargement. The same value is obtained from $r$ copies of $M$ bounding a smooth $W$ by dividing its defect by $r>0$. Embedding the target group preserves the number. There is a finite constant $C_M$, depending only on the given smooth manifold $M$, such that
$$|\rho_{\mathrm{sm}}(M,\phi)|\le C_M$$
for all $G$ and $\phi$, including nononto homomorphisms and uncountable targets. For a disconnected compact $M$, use its finitely many components and the sum of these values, equivalently the free-product convention for its based fundamental groups. This is a signature-defect invariant among smooth bounds. No comparison with a nonsmooth TOP bound or an analytic eta definition is asserted.

A discrete group has a connected CW $K(G,1)$ model with contractible universal cover, obtained from Milnor's contractible principal total space. [F2] Smooth embedding, tubular collapse, compact finite-Grassmannian factorization, controlled smoothing near the zero section, relative transverse homotopies, normal-first orientation and linearization of a transverse map to its own collapse are proved in the point-target collapse carriers. [[thm-universal-pontryagin-thom-correspondence-for-unoriented-and-oriented-bordism]], [[lem-every-unoriented-and-oriented-bordism-class-is-realized-by-an-embedded-collapse]]

[F3] Integral cross-product Kunneth is natural, and a CW quotient induces the relative singular homology comparison. [[thm-topological-kunneth-short-exact-sequence-for-homology]], [[lem-cw-quotient-induces-relative-singular-homology-isomorphisms]]

The first possibly nonzero relative homotopy group of a CW pair with simply connected subspace is its relative homology, and a weak equivalence of CW complexes is a homotopy equivalence. contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume full AC. Let $M$ be a compact oriented Hausdorff topological manifold with supplied boundary collar, and supply a based homomorphism on each component to a discrete group $G$, with compatible paths when maps or gluings are considered. Use $R=\mathbb CG$, with involution conjugating complex scalars and sending $g$ to $g^{-1}$, and its based right regular local system with standard parallel Hermitian form. Let $A=\mathcal NG$ have the canonical group trace. Then its singular coefficient complex has an actual bounded finite-projective $R$ chain-homotopy model. Absolute, relative and finite whole-component gluing diagrams admit such models and finite matrix comparison maps.

After extending these finite projective matrices to $\ell^2(G)$, write $\mathscr H_i(M)$ for completed reduced homology, with boundaries replaced by their Hilbert closures. If $p_Z,p_B$ are the cycle and boundary-closure projections in a finite ambient projection module, the corresponding algebraic reduced module is $P_i=(p_Z-p_B)A^r$, and
$$H_i(M;A)\twoheadrightarrow P_i\hookrightarrow\mathscr H_i(M)=(p_Z-p_B)\ell^2(G)^r.$$
The first map has dimension-zero kernel, and the second is injective with dense image and need not be onto. Pair and whole-component Mayer–Vietoris sequences are weakly exact on the completed modules. Oriented cap duality gives bounded mutually inverse maps on their completed reduced homology and cohomology, with the cap-boundary and restriction identities. These structures and the resulting spectral signature do not depend on the finite-projective model.

For a four-manifold the middle intersection form is the bounded Hermitian form defined by inverse relative cap duality, restriction and evaluation. Its Hilbert radical is the kernel of its self-adjoint operator. Its signature is the trace of the positive spectral projection minus the trace of the negative projection; no closed range or bounded inverse is required for a manifold with boundary. For a closed four-manifold its middle intersection operator is boundedly invertible.

Let $W_0,W_1$ be compact oriented topological four-manifolds, let $N$ be a union of entire closed boundary components, and glue the two marked copies of $N$ by an orientation-reversing identification and the supplied collars. Put $W=W_0\cup_N W_1$ and supply one compatible regular coefficient system on $W$. Other boundary components may remain. Then
$$\operatorname{sign}^{(2)}_G(W)=\operatorname{sign}^{(2)}_G(W_0)+\operatorname{sign}^{(2)}_G(W_1),\qquad\operatorname{sign}(W)=\operatorname{sign}(W_0)+\operatorname{sign}(W_1).$$
Orientation reversal changes the corresponding sign. No finite CW type, triangulation, smoothing of a topological four-manifold, equality of ordinary and $L^2$ signatures on arbitrary closed manifolds, or analytic eta-to-defect comparison is asserted or assumed. For an arbitrary possibly uncountable $G$, the finite-matrix construction has the same dimensions and signatures as its countable coefficient image, so it agrees with the countable-group convention.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $n\ge1$. Supply a compact connected oriented topological four-manifold $V$ with boundary a marked knot zero surgery, $H_1(V;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z$ and $H_2(V;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z^{2r}$, and exactly $r$ integral pairs $x_i,y_i\in H_2(V;\mathbb Z[\pi/\pi^{(n)}])$, $\pi=\pi_1(V)$, satisfying $\lambda(x_i,x_j)=0$ and $\lambda(x_i,y_j)=\delta_{ij}$. Form $W$ by any finite sequence of the actual marked standard connected-sum and winding-zero infection cobordism adjunctions along outgoing knot-surgery components, including orientation reversals, using supplied smooth peripheral products and collars. Let $\phi:\pi_1(W)\to\Gamma$ have PTFA target and restrict on $V$ through $\pi/\pi^{(n)}$. Take $k=\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb F_p$ and put $A=k[\Gamma]$, with involutive Ore fraction division ring $K$ and the based standard parallel Hermitian structure.

The image pairs $\ell_i,d_i\in H_2(W;A)$ satisfy $\lambda(\ell_i,\ell_j)=0$ and $\lambda(\ell_i,d_j)=\lambda(d_j,\ell_i)=\delta_{ij}$. Their localized boundary-intersection cokernel has dimension at most $2r$. For each boundary component $M_0$ on which $\phi$ is nontrivial, $H_1(M_0;K)=0$, its coefficient Bockstein–duality linking form is defined, and its actual inclusion kernel is isotropic:
$$B_{M_0}(z,w)=0\quad\text{for all }z,w\in\ker\{H_1(M_0;A)\to H_1(W;A)\}.$$
Thus every boundary class with nonzero self-pairing survives in $H_1(W;A)$ and lies outside every isotropic submodule. If a component's coefficient image is cyclic, its form additionally has the nonsingularity furnished by the cyclic-image coefficient theorem; no unrestricted PTFA nonsingularity is asserted.

For a finite forest of iterated winding-zero infections with these initial data, suppose each top meridian generates $H_1(W_n;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z$ up to sign, and each pattern-axis integral classical self-pairing is nonzero. Use the actual intermediate $W_j$, rational mixed coefficients through index $n$, and one bottom field $\mathbb F_p$. For every odd prime outside the explicit finite exceptional set of the axis values, every branch meridian has a nonzero class in $P^{n-j}\pi_1(W_j)/P^{n-j+1}\pi_1(W_j)$, of infinite order when $j>0$ and order $p$ when $j=0$. All these conclusions hold for the supplied locally flat topological bordisms and smooth bordisms without a choice principle. Existence of the initial $V$ and its lifted pairs from a concordance relation is a separate hypothesis, as are analytic rho invariance and signature vanishing.

contract.text:
Assume AC. For every supplied finite smooth oriented disk-band Seifert surface $F$ with one-boundary knot $K$, ordered homology basis and first-variable positive-push matrix $V$, let $W_F$ and its meridional extension $\psi_d:\pi_1(W_F)\to\mathbb Z/d$ be the actual construction of the finite disk-band bounding-manifold construction. For every positive integer $d$, set $\zeta_d=\exp(2\pi i/d)$ and
$$D_d(F)=\operatorname{sign}^{(2)}_{\mathbb Z/d}(W_F,\psi_d)-\operatorname{sign}(W_F).$$
Then
$$D_d(F)=\frac1d\sum_{r=0}^{d-1}\operatorname{sign}\bigl((1-\zeta_d^r)V+(1-\zeta_d^{-r})V^T\bigr).$$
The sign is exactly the positive $L^2$ signature minus ordinary signature convention. The formula allows singular character forms and all $d$, including $d=1$ and even $d$. The term $r=0$ is defined by the zero Hermitian matrix and contributes zero; its equality to the trivial-character signature follows from the ordinary metabolic calculation, not from specialization of a localized homology basis.

The boundary is the actual oriented zero surgery and its positive meridian map, not the knot exterior or a simply connected trace. The displayed formula proves this **canonical bounding defect**. Whenever a separately proved applicable bordism-independence assertion identifies the rho invariant with the defect of this bounding extension, it consequently gives the same value for that rho invariant. No such general independence assertion, global signature invariance, rho identification, uniform bound, infinite-cyclic formula or arbitrary-group index theorem is asserted here.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $D^2$ be the oriented closed disk and let $K\subset S^3=\partial B^4$ be a smooth oriented knot, meaning the image of an orientation-preserving smooth embedding of a circle. A **ribbon immersion** for $K$ is a smooth immersion $f:D^2\to S^3$ whose boundary restriction is an embedding onto $K$ and whose only multiple points form finitely many pairwise disjoint transverse double arcs $\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_m$. For each $i$, the full preimage of $\gamma_i$ consists of two disjoint embedded arcs $\alpha_i$ and $\beta_i$ in $D^2$: $\alpha_i$ is properly embedded, with its two endpoints on $\partial D^2$ and its interior in $\operatorname{Int}D^2$, while $\beta_i$ is compact and lies in $\operatorname{Int}D^2$. There are no triple points or other self-intersections. A **ribbon disk** for $K$ is such a ribbon immersion, and $K$ is a **ribbon knot** if it admits a ribbon disk.

A **band** on a link in $S^3$ is the image of a smoothly embedded rectangle whose two opposite attaching edges lie on the link and whose remaining points are disjoint from it. A **band move** removes the attaching edges, inserts the other two edges, and rounds the corners; the embedded band, including its half-twist data, is part of the move. A **no-maximum disk movie** is the family of regular level links of a smooth proper disk $D\subset B^4$ for which the squared radial function $\rho(x)=\lVert x\rVert^2$ is Morse in the disk interior and has only index-$0$ minima and index-$1$ saddles. A minimum creates a split unknot and a saddle performs an oriented band move; there are no maxima. The no-maximum disk movie is a second presentation convention used by the design for explicit ribbon examples. This movie model and the ribbon-immersion definition above describe the same class of knots: a finite birth-and-band induction converts the movie to an immersion, and cutting the proper double-arc preimages converts an immersion to a disk-and-band movie. The local resolution lemma proves only that a ribbon immersion pushes rel boundary to a smooth proper disk in $B^4$. The slice-ribbon conjecture asks whether every smooth slice knot admits a ribbon immersion as defined above.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Let $f:D^2\to S^3$ be a smooth immersion of an oriented disk whose boundary is an embedded oriented knot $K$. Suppose that its only self-intersections are finitely many pairwise disjoint transverse double arcs, and that the two preimage arcs of each double arc are one properly embedded arc in $D^2$ and one compact arc contained in $\operatorname{Int}D^2$. Then there is a smooth proper embedding $\widetilde f:(D^2,\partial D^2)\to(B^4,S^3)$ with $\widetilde f|_{\partial D^2}=f|_{\partial D^2}$.

[F2] An embedding of a surface into a manifold with boundary is proper when the preimage of the ambient boundary is exactly the surface boundary; smooth proper surfaces have smooth boundary collars. ([[def-locally-flat-proper-surface-and-concordance-collars]])

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Every smooth oriented knot $K$ in the standard oriented three-sphere has its connected sum with its reverse mirror represented by the boundary of a smooth immersed disk in $S^3$ whose only multiple points are finitely many transverse double arcs, each having one proper preimage arc and one interior preimage arc. Consequently $K\#K^\dagger$ is ribbon in the ribbon-immersion sense.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $A$ be an indeterminate and let $D$ be a nonempty regular oriented link
diagram in an oriented $3$-sphere. Fix a unit viewing normal $n$ and orient its
projection plane $P$ so $(u,v)$ is positive exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is positive
in the ambient $3$-space. At each crossing define
$\operatorname{sgn}(c)=\operatorname{sgn}\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})$
from the oriented projected tangents, and set
$\operatorname{wr}(D)=\sum_c\operatorname{sgn}(c)$. With
$\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$, adding a positive type-I kink multiplies the
raw bracket by $-A^3$ and increases writhe by $1$; adding a negative type-I
kink multiplies it by $-A^{-3}$ and decreases writhe by $1$. Deleting either
kink multiplies by the reciprocal factor. Consequently
$$f_D(A):=(-A^3)^{-\operatorname{wr}(D)}\langle D\rangle$$
is unchanged by every oriented type-I, type-II, and type-III Reidemeister move
and by planar isotopy.

facts:
**Given:** A nonempty regular oriented link diagram $D$ and a type-I, type-II,
or type-III move applied to it.

[F1] In the positively oriented chart with over-strand southwest–northeast,
the A-smoothing pairs left endpoints and right endpoints, while the B-smoothing
pairs top endpoints and bottom endpoints. A crossing contributes $A$ for its
A-smoothing and $A^{-1}$ for its B-smoothing; a state with $k$ circles contributes the factor
$\delta^{k-1}$, and $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$
([[def-kauffman-bracket-smoothing-and-loop-value]]).

[F2] The total writhe is the sum of the signs
$\operatorname{sgn}(c)=\operatorname{sgn}\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})$;
the positive Artin half twist has sign $+1$
([[def-oriented-crossing-sign-writhe-and-blackboard-framing]]).

[F3] A type-I kink creates or deletes one crossing of either sign; type II
creates or deletes two crossings of opposite signs; type III preserves the
signs of its three crossings ([[def-oriented-reidemeister-moves]]).

[F4] The raw bracket is unchanged under every R2 and R3 local replacement
([[lem-kauffman-bracket-r2-r3-identities]]).

direction. Let $D_-$ be its mirror image, and let $U$ be the crossing-free
one-component unknot diagram. Fix a unit viewing normal $n$ and orient the

in the oriented ambient $3$-space. At each crossing use the local source chart
whose over-strand runs southwest to northeast; the A-smoothing joins the left
endpoints and right endpoints with weight $A$, and the B-smoothing joins the
top endpoints and bottom endpoints with weight $A^{-1}$. Transport these
labels by orientation-preserving changes of local coordinates. For a diagram
$D$, let $C(D)$ be its finite crossing set. Each state is a map
$S:C(D)\to\{A,B\}$; let $a(S)$ and $b(S)$ count the smoothing types and $|S|$
count its circles. Define
$\langle D\rangle=\sum_{S:C(D)\to\{A,B\}}
A^{a(S)-b(S)}(-A^2-A^{-2})^{|S|-1}$ and
$f_D(A)=(-A^3)^{-\operatorname{wr}(D)}\langle D\rangle$, where writhe is the
sum of determinant crossing signs, computed as
$\operatorname{sgn}\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})$ after fixing a unit
viewing normal $n$ and using the induced orientation of $P$ above. With
$t=A^{-4}$ and Jones polynomial
$V_D(t)=f_D(t^{-1/4})$, the values are
$$V_{D_+}(t)=t+t^3-t^4,\qquad V_{D_-}(t)=t^{-1}+t^{-3}-t^{-4},\qquad V_U(t)=1.$$

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let
$$R_D=\mathbb Z[a^{\pm1},z,d^{\pm1}]/(z(d-1)-(a-a^{-1})),$$
where $z$ is not inverted. A nonempty unoriented regular link diagram is a
finite generic planar projection of one or more circles with only transverse
double crossings and an over/under marking at each crossing. Use the crossing
chart in which the over-strand runs southwest to northeast. Its $D_0$
smoothing joins the left endpoints and the right endpoints (the through
pairing), and its $D_\infty$ smoothing joins the two top endpoints and the two
bottom endpoints (the cup-cap pairing). Thus $D_0$ is the orientation-preserving
smoothing when both crossing strands point downward and the displayed crossing
has positive determinant sign. These are respectively the $A$- and
$B$-smoothings in the stated bracket chart. A positive
curl is a type-I kink whose oriented crossing has determinant sign $+1$; a
negative curl has determinant sign $-1$. The sign is unchanged if the
orientation of the whole component is reversed.

The Dubrovnik regular-isotopy evaluation $P$ is normalized by
$P(\varnothing)=1$, $P(K\sqcup\bigcirc)=dP(K)$, positive and negative curl
factors $a$ and $a^{-1}$, and
$$P(D_+)-P(D_-)=z\bigl(P(D_0)-P(D_\infty)\bigr).$$
Here $D_+$ and $D_-$ differ only by switching the displayed crossing. For a
nonempty oriented link diagram $K$, let $c(K)$ be its number of components and
let $w(K)$ be the sum of the determinant crossing signs. Define
$$D_K(a,z)=d^{-1}P(K),$$
$$L_K(A,Z)=-i^{w(K)}(-1)^{c(K)}D_K(-iA,iZ),\qquad i^2=-1,$$
and
$$F_K(A,Z)=A^{-w(K)}L_K(A,Z).$$
Thus $D$ has unknot value $1$, and the universal relation defining $R_D$ is
retained even when $z$ is not invertible. These are conventions and
normalizations; ambient-isotopy invariance of $F$ is a separate theorem.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For each nonempty oriented regular link
diagram $K$, let $w(K)$ be its determinant writhe and $c(K)$ its number of
components, and define $D,L,F$ by the conventions stated for this page. Then
$$D_K(a,z)=-i^{-w(K)}(-1)^{c(K)}L_K(ia,-iz),\qquad i^2=-1.$$
The value assigned to $L$ is independent of reversing the orientation of any
whole component. The Dubrovnik value has the stated difference-skein, curl and
circle rules; the Kauffman value has the sum-skein, curl and circle rules; and
$F_K(A,Z)=A^{-w(K)}L_K(A,Z)$ is unchanged by planar isotopy and every oriented
Reidemeister move of types I, II, and III. The claim concerns these finite
diagram moves and uses the universal coefficient relations without dividing
by a skein variable.

facts:
**Given:** AC$_\omega$, a nonempty regular oriented link diagram, its determinant
crossing signs, and the Dubrovnik scalar evaluation.

[A1] The Axiom of Countable Choice, written AC$_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]), is the hypothesis of the mixed-crossing parity
supplier used below.

[F1] The Dubrovnik scalar $P$ is regular-isotopy invariant, has $P(\varnothing)=1$,
positive/negative curl factors $a,a^{-1}$, loop factor $d$, and skein
$P_+-P_-=z(P_0-P_\infty)$ over $z(d-1)=a-a^{-1}$
([[lem-framed-kauffman-link-evaluation]]).

[F2] The determinant writhe is the signed sum of crossing signs; reversing one
strand negates that crossing sign, while reversing both strands preserves it
([[def-oriented-crossing-sign-writhe-and-blackboard-framing]]).

[F3] The mixed crossing sum between two distinct oriented components is even
([[lem-linking-number-even-sum-and-reidemeister-invariance]]).

[F4] A type-I move changes one self-crossing, type II adds or removes two
opposite-sign crossings, and type III preserves its three crossing signs
([[def-oriented-reidemeister-moves]]).

[F5] In the stated polynomial convention, $D=P/d$ on nonempty diagrams,
$L_K(A,Z)=-i^{w(K)}(-1)^{c(K)}D_K(-iA,iZ)$, and $F=A^{-w}L$
([[def-kauffman-regular-isotopy-and-dubrovnik-conventions]]).

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let
$$S=\mathbb Z[a^{\pm1},z,d^{\pm1}]/(z(d-1)-(a-a^{-1}))$$
be the Dubrovnik coefficient ring, and let
$$T=S[q^{\pm1}]/(q-q^{-1}-z).$$
In $T$ put $\rho=a$, $\delta=d$, and $z_B=q-q^{-1}$. Then the natural
map $S\to T$ is injective and $T$ is a free $S$-module with basis $1,q$.
Moreover, the BMW coefficient relation
$$z_B(\delta-1)=\rho-\rho^{-1}$$
holds, and the substitution $a=\rho$, $z_D=z_B$, $d=\delta$ converts
the BMW skein, curl, adjacent untwisting, and loop coefficients to the
Dubrovnik relations in the specified chart: $D_+-D_-=z_D(D_0-D_\infty)$,
the curl factors are $a,a^{-1}$, and a disjoint trivial circle contributes
$d$. Here $D_0$ is through and $D_\infty$ is cup-cap. No skein parameter is
divided out.

facts:
**Given:** The BMW presentation over $R_B$, its units $q,\rho,\delta$, and the
Dubrovnik chart and parameters $a,z_D,d$.

[F1] The BMW relation is $g_i-g_i^{-1}=z_B(1-e_i)$, the coefficient relation is
$z_B(\delta-1)=\rho-\rho^{-1}$, and the local generators satisfy
$g_ie_i=e_ig_i=\rho^{-1}e_i$, $e_ig_{i\pm1}e_i=\rho e_i$, and
$e_i^2=\delta e_i$
([[def-bmw-algebra-with-fixed-kauffman-skein-convention]]).

[F2] In the chosen Dubrovnik chart, $D_0$ is the through smoothing,
$D_\infty$ is the cup-cap smoothing, the crossing rule is
$D_+-D_-=z_D(D_0-D_\infty)$, and the two curl factors are $a,a^{-1}$
([[def-kauffman-regular-isotopy-and-dubrovnik-conventions]]).

[F3] The bracket chart labels the left/right pairing as the A-smoothing and
the top/bottom pairing as the B-smoothing for an over-strand directed
southwest to northeast ([[def-kauffman-bracket-smoothing-and-loop-value]]).

[F4] The coefficient extension is $T=S[q^{\pm1}]/(q-q^{-1}-z)$, with
$z_B=q-q^{-1}$, $z_D=z_B$, $\rho=a$, and $\delta=d$
([[def-bmw-dubrovnik-coefficient-extension]]).

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Let $T$ be the coefficient extension and parameter substitution in the BMW-to-Dubrovnik dictionary, and let $\mathcal{KT}_n(T)$ be the ordinary Dubrovnik tangle skein algebra: its diagrams are finite generic projections of $n$ arcs with fixed ordered top and bottom endpoints and closed curves, modulo planar isotopy, Reidemeister II and III, the Dubrovnik skein relation, the two curl relations, and the free-circle relation with parameters $z_D,a,a^{-1},d$. In its fixed chart, $D_0$ is through left/right and $D_\infty$ is cup-cap top/bottom. For every $n\ge2$, send the BMW generator $g_i$ to the positive Artin crossing between strands $i,i+1$, its inverse to the negative crossing, and $e_i$ to the adjacent cup-cap tangle. This assignment extends to a unital $T$-algebra homomorphism $\Phi_n:BMW_n(T;q,\rho,\delta)\to\mathcal{KT}_n(T)$. For $n=0,1$, define the unital $T$-algebra homomorphism by sending each scalar to that scalar times the empty or straight tangle, respectively. This claim asserts well-definedness only; it does not assert surjectivity or injectivity.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Use the coefficient extension $T$ with $a=\rho$ and $d=\delta$. On input an integer $n\ge1$ and a finite signed Artin braid word
$$\beta=\sigma_{i_1}^{\varepsilon_1}\cdots\sigma_{i_m}^{\varepsilon_m},\qquad \varepsilon_j\in\{-1,1\},\quad 1\le i_j<n,$$
perform the following finite computation:

1. Form the BMW product $b_\beta=g_{i_1}^{\varepsilon_1}\cdots g_{i_m}^{\varepsilon_m}$.
2. Set $w=\sum_{j=1}^m\varepsilon_j$ and let $c$ be the number of cycles of the permutation $s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_m}$ of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, counting fixed points.
3. List the perfect matchings of the $2n$ tangle boundary endpoints and their standard descending representatives $T_m$. For each signed generator, form its finite left-multiplication matrix in this basis: its column at $T_m$ is obtained by reducing the tangle $g_i^{\pm1}T_m$ to the unique matching coordinates. In each reduction, use the standard endpoint traversal order, choose the first crossing whose first traversal branch is under, and with $\eta=1$ for the fixed $D_+$ chart and $\eta=-1$ for its crossing-switched $D_-$ chart replace
$$R(D)=R(D^{\mathrm{sw}})+\eta z_D\bigl(R(D_0)-R(D_\infty)\bigr).$$
The switched branch has one fewer non-descending crossing, and each smoothing has one fewer crossing; a descending leaf is reduced by the curl and free-circle rules to its standard matching representative. Starting with the coordinate vector of the identity tangle, apply the generator matrices from the rightmost braid letter to the leftmost to obtain the coordinate vector $v_\beta$ of $\Phi_n(b_\beta)$.
4. Form the trace row $t_m=d^{-n}P(\widehat{T_m})$ by closing each basis tangle and evaluating its scalar Dubrovnik value, and return
$$-(-1)^c a^{-w}d^{n-1}\tau_n(b_\beta).$$

Here $\tau_n(b_\beta)=t^{\mathsf T}v_\beta$. The output is the declared Kauffman ambient-isotopy value at $A=ia$, $Z=-iz$ in the Dubrovnik parameter convention. All matrices are finite and all coefficients lie in $T$; no division by the skein variable is used.

facts:
**Given:** A finite signed braid word, the BMW product, the oriented braid closure, the Dubrovnik scalar evaluation, and the normalized closure trace.

[F1] The positive Artin generator has determinant crossing sign $+1$, its inverse has sign $-1$, and writhe is the signed crossing sum ([[def-oriented-crossing-sign-writhe-and-blackboard-framing]]).

[F2] The closure of a braid word has one component for each cycle of its strand permutation ([[def-closure-of-a-geometric-braid]]).

[F3] The exponent sum of the word is the sum of its signed generator exponents ([[def-exponent-sum-of-a-braid]]).

[F4] The generator assignment extends to the algebra homomorphism $\Phi_n$ ([[lem-bmw-presentation-tangle-evaluation-is-well-defined]]).

[F5] The tangle algebra has a finite basis indexed by the perfect matchings of $2n$ endpoints; tangle skein reduction spans it and closure-pairing independence makes coordinates unique ([[lem-bmw-descending-tangle-spanning]], [[lem-bmw-closure-pairing-independence]]).

[F6] $\tau_n(b)=d^{-n}P(\widehat{\Phi_n(b)})$ and $P$ satisfies the stated skein, curl, and circle rules ([[lem-bmw-markov-trace-stabilization]], [[lem-framed-kauffman-link-evaluation]]).

[F7] On a fixed oriented diagram with writhe $w$ and component count $c$, the defining formulas are $L(A,Z)=-i^w(-1)^cD(-iA,iZ)$ and $F(A,Z)=A^{-w}L(A,Z)$, with $i^2=-1$ ([[def-kauffman-regular-isotopy-and-dubrovnik-conventions]]).

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $\mathcal A$ be a smooth planar
annulus and let $X=\mathcal A\times(-1,1)$, the interior of a solid torus.
A regular annular diagram is a finite immersed union of circles in
$\operatorname{int}(\mathcal A)$ with only finitely many transverse double
points, no triple points, and over/under data from the interval coordinate.
The **blackboard framing** is the normal strip lying in the annulus. A specified
framing differs from it on each component by an integer full-twist correction,
measured by the winding number of its normal direction relative to the
blackboard normal. Count the correction positively for an A-type full twist,
whose local curl has A-smoothing equal to the straight strip with one
contractible circle; count the opposite B-type twist negatively. Every framed
link in $X$ admits a regular annular diagram. The correction may be recorded
as signed full-twist marks on diagram arcs; its total is additive when arcs
are concatenated.

If two framed links in $X$ are ambient isotopic through links in $X$, their
regular annular diagrams are related by finitely many annular planar isotopies
and local oriented Reidemeister I, II, and III moves in disks contained in
$\operatorname{int}(\mathcal A)$. Reidemeister II and III and planar isotopy
preserve the blackboard framing; an A-type or B-type Reidemeister I move
changes it by one corresponding full twist, so the correction integer changes
by the opposite twist. For framed links in $S^3$, every link also admits a
regular planar diagram, and any two diagrams of ambient-isotopic framed links
are related by a finite planar-isotopy/Reidemeister sequence with the same
framing-correction rule.

facts:
**Given:** Countable choice, a framed link in $S^3$ or $X$, and a framed ambient isotopy between two such links.

[A1] Countable choice is the assertion that every countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-countable-choice]]).

[F1] A regular oriented link diagram is an immersion with finitely many transverse double points, no triple points, and over/under and orientation data; every oriented link in $S^3$ has a regular projection under countable choice ([[def-regular-oriented-link-diagram]], [[lem-every-oriented-link-admits-a-regular-projection]]).

[F2] Under countable choice, two regular oriented diagrams in $S^3$ represent equivalent oriented links exactly when a finite sequence of planar isotopies and oriented Reidemeister I, II, and III moves connects them ([[thm-oriented-reidemeister-equivalence-theorem]]).

[F3] Under countable choice, a smooth isotopy in $\mathbb R^3$ with regular endpoint projections can be perturbed, fixed near its endpoints, so its projection has finitely many isolated cusps, quadratic double tangencies, and transverse triple events; each event time is distinct ([[lem-a-smooth-isotopy-of-links-can-be-put-in-general-position]], [[lem-a-generic-isotopy-of-links-has-only-reidemeister-singular-times]]).

[F4] Parametric transversality gives generic parameter slices transverse to any fixed finite list of smooth strata, and a transverse preimage of codimension $c$ in a source of dimension $m<c$ is empty ([[thm-parametric-transversality]], [[thm-transverse-preimage-theorem]]).

[F5] R1, R2, and R3 are the local kink, two-strand cancellation, and strand-past-crossing replacements, with all sign and orientation variants; planar isotopy transports the diagram without creating or deleting a crossing ([[def-oriented-reidemeister-moves]], [[def-planar-isotopy-of-link-diagrams]]).

[F6] The A-smoothing is the left/right pairing with weight $A$, and the B-smoothing is the top/bottom pairing with weight $A^{-1}$ in the KT-29 source chart ([[def-kauffman-bracket-smoothing-and-loop-value]]).

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $M$ be a smooth oriented $3$-manifold and let $L$ be a framed unoriented
link in its interior with a specified component. A positive full framing twist is the local blackboard
curl whose $A$-smoothing is the straight strip with one additional
zero-framed trivial circle; a negative full framing twist is the curl whose
$B$-smoothing is the straight strip with one additional zero-framed trivial
circle. Write $L^+$ and $L^-$ for the links obtained by inserting these twists
on one component. With $R=\mathbb Z[A^{\pm1}]$ and
$\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$, the module classes satisfy
$$
[L^+]=-A^3[L],\qquad [L^-]=-A^{-3}[L].
$$

facts:
**Given:** A smooth oriented $3$-manifold $M$, a framed unoriented link $L$ in its interior, and the two local full-twist insertions from the Statement.

[F1] A crossing triple in $\mathcal K_A(M)$ satisfies $[L_\times]=A[L_A]+A^{-1}[L_B]$, and adjoining a zero-framed trivial circle multiplies a class by $\delta$ ([[def-kauffman-bracket-skein-module-of-a-three-manifold]]).

[F2] The loop value is $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$ and the coefficients of the two smoothings are $A$ and $A^{-1}$ ([[def-kauffman-bracket-smoothing-and-loop-value]]).

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $M$ and $N$ be smooth oriented $3$-manifolds, and let
$f:M\to N$ be an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism. Then
$[L]\mapsto[f(L)]$ induces an $R$-module isomorphism
$f_*:\mathcal K_A(M)\to\mathcal K_A(N)$. These maps respect identity
diffeomorphisms and composition.

Let $\Sigma$ be a compact oriented surface with a specified product collar
$\iota:\Sigma\times[0,1]\hookrightarrow M$ whose lower face lies in
$\partial M$. The stacking product on
$\mathcal K_A(\Sigma\times[0,1])$ and collar gluing define a unital left
action on $\mathcal K_A(M)$: a closed framed link in the surface product is
placed in a sufficiently thin outer subcollar and united with a framed link
in the interior of $M$. The action is independent of the thin-collar width,
associative, and natural under orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms that
respect the specified collars. Only closed framed links are glued; no relative
boundary endpoints are part of this action.

facts:
**Given:** Smooth oriented $3$-manifolds $M,N$, an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism $f:M\to N$, an oriented surface collar in $\partial M$, and the Kauffman bracket skein quotients defined above.

[F1] The free module is generated by framed unoriented link isotopy classes; its relation submodule is generated by the local crossing relation and the zero-framed trivial-circle relation with $R=\mathbb Z[A^{\pm1}]$ and $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$ ([[def-kauffman-bracket-skein-module-of-a-three-manifold]], [[def-kauffman-bracket-smoothing-and-loop-value]]).

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and let $R=\mathbb Z[A^{\pm1}]$ and
$\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$. For a nonempty framed unoriented link $L$ in $S^3$,
choose a regular planar diagram $D$ of its core. Let $m_j\in\mathbb Z$ be
the full-twist correction on the $j$th component from the blackboard framing
of $D$ to the specified framing of $L$, counting an A-type twist positively
and its inverse negatively as in the framed diagram calculus, and put
$m=\sum_jm_j$. For a state
$S$ of $D$, let $a(S)$ and $b(S)$ be its numbers of A- and B-smoothings and
$|S|$ its number of resulting circles. The assignment
$$
E(\varnothing)=1,\qquad
E(L)=\delta(-A^3)^m\sum_{S}A^{a(S)-b(S)}\delta^{|S|-1}
$$
is independent of the diagram and twist corrections and extends
$R$-linearly to a map $E:\mathcal K_A(S^3)\to R$ satisfying
$E([\varnothing])=1$.

facts:
**Given:** Countable choice, a framed unoriented link in $S^3$, and its regular diagram and framing corrections.

[A1] The Axiom of Countable Choice, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]).

[F1] For a nonempty regular diagram $D$, the Kauffman bracket is the finite sum $\langle D\rangle=\sum_S A^{a(S)-b(S)}\delta^{|S|-1}$ with $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$ ([[def-kauffman-bracket-smoothing-and-loop-value]]).

[F2] The raw bracket is unchanged by every local Reidemeister II and III replacement in the fixed source-chart convention ([[lem-kauffman-bracket-r2-r3-identities]]).

[F3] Framed isotopies in $S^3$ admit finite planar-isotopy/Reidemeister sequences; a type-I move changes the blackboard framing by one signed twist ([[lem-framed-link-diagram-calculus]]).

[F4] The skein module imposes $[L_\times]=A[L_A]+A^{-1}[L_B]$ and $[L\sqcup O]=\delta[L]$ for a zero-framed trivial circle ([[def-kauffman-bracket-skein-module-of-a-three-manifold]]).

contract.heading: Statement

facts:
**Given:** A regular link diagram with one of the local R2 or R3 replacements described in the statement.

[F1] In the source crossing chart, the A-smoothing has weight $A$, the B-smoothing has weight $A^{-1}$, and a closed trivial loop has value $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$ ([[def-kauffman-bracket-smoothing-and-loop-value]]).

[F2] The identity $I$ is the vertical through tangle; $e_i$ is the cap on top and cup on bottom, stacking removes loops with coefficient $\delta$, and the stacking product is associative and bilinear ([[def-temperley-lieb-diagram-category]], [[thm-temperley-lieb-diagram-category-laws]]).

[F3] The generators satisfy $e_i^2=\delta e_i$, $e_ie_{i+1}e_i=e_i$, $e_{i+1}e_ie_{i+1}=e_{i+1}$, and distant generators commute ([[lem-temperley-lieb-generators-satisfy-local-relations]]).

[F4] R2 creates or deletes two opposite crossings, and every allowed R3 has a strict height order with the cyclic over/under pattern excluded ([[def-oriented-reidemeister-moves]]).

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathcal A$ be a planar annulus
and identify the solid torus with $\mathcal A\times[-1,1]$. Let
$R=\mathbb Z[A^{\pm1}]$, $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$, and let $z$ be a formal
polynomial variable. For a regular annular diagram $D$, a state $S$ smooths
every crossing. Let $a(S)$ and $b(S)$ count its A- and B-smoothings, let
$u(S)$ count the resulting circles that bound disks in $\mathcal A$, and let
$e(S)$ count the resulting circles that do not bound disks in $\mathcal A$;
call a circle that does not bound a disk essential.
If $m$ is the total full-twist correction from the blackboard framing to the
specified framing, counting an A-type twist positively and its inverse
negatively as in the framed diagram calculus, set
$$
\Psi(D,m)=(-A^3)^m\sum_S A^{a(S)-b(S)}\delta^{u(S)}z^{e(S)}.
$$
This value is independent of the regular annular diagram and twist correction
of the framed link and induces an $R$-linear map
$$
\Psi:\mathcal K_A(\mathcal A\times[-1,1])\longrightarrow R[z].
$$
For the empty link, the empty diagram has its unique empty state and the
formula gives $\Psi(\varnothing)=1$.

The diagram below shows one essential core curve and one contractible circle
in an annular state; every smoothed component is classified by these two
types.

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.75,line cap=round]
  \draw[thick] (0,0) circle (1.6);
  \draw[thick] (0,0) circle (0.65);
  \draw[very thick] (0,0) circle (1.05);
  \draw[very thick] (1.30,0) circle (0.16);
  \node at (0,1.05) [above] {$z$};
  \node at (1.45,0.25) [right] {$\bigcirc$};
  \node at (0,-1.95) {essential core and contractible circle};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

facts:
**Given:** The Axiom of Choice, a framed link in the solid torus $\mathcal A\times[-1,1]$, and a regular annular diagram with its full-twist correction.

[A1] The Axiom of Choice, written $\mathrm{AC}$ ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

[A2] Countable choice, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, means every countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-countable-choice]]).

[A3] In ZF, $\mathrm{AC}$ implies $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]).

[F1] At a crossing, the Kauffman bracket state sum uses the A-smoothing with weight $A$, the B-smoothing with weight $A^{-1}$, and the loop value $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$ ([[def-kauffman-bracket-smoothing-and-loop-value]]).

[F2] The module is generated by framed-link classes modulo the crossing and trivial-circle relations ([[def-kauffman-bracket-skein-module-of-a-three-manifold]]).

[F3] Every framed link in the solid-torus product admits a regular annular diagram with signed full-twist correction marks, and framed isotopies of links are represented by annular planar isotopies and finitely many R1, R2, and R3 moves; R1 changes the blackboard twist correction by the opposite unit ([[lem-framed-link-diagram-calculus]]).

[F4] In the fixed source-chart convention, the crossing operators cancel under R2 and satisfy the three-strand braid relation under R3; these are equalities of local Temperley–Lieb tangles ([[lem-kauffman-bracket-r2-r3-identities]]).

[F5] For two disjoint smoothly embedded circles in $S^2$, the complement consists of two open disks and a unique open annulus bounded by the circles ([[lem-two-disjoint-circles-in-s-two-cobound-an-annulus]]).

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. An orientation-preserving diffeomorphism
between smooth oriented $3$-manifolds transports the full framing of every
link and induces an isomorphism of their Kauffman bracket skein modules. If
the diffeomorphism carries a specified product collar of a compact oriented
boundary surface productwise to another specified collar, the induced
isomorphism intertwines the two closed-link collar actions. A positive or
negative full framing twist on one link component multiplies its class by
$-A^3$ or $-A^{-3}$, respectively. In $\mathcal K_A(S^3)$, a positive twist
of a zero-framed trivial circle changes its class from
$\delta[\varnothing]$ to $-A^3\delta[\varnothing]$, with
$\delta[\varnothing]\ne -A^3\delta[\varnothing]$. In the solid-torus
module, a positive twist of the blackboard-framed core changes $[z]$ to
$-A^3[z]$, with $[z]\ne -A^3[z]$.

facts:

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Fix an even integer $p\ge4$ and a primitive $2p$-th root of unity $A\in\mathbb C$. Put

$$
\zeta=A^2,\qquad q=-\zeta,\qquad r=p/2,\qquad
\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}=q+q^{-1}.
$$

The coefficient field after specialization is $\mathbb C$, and the Kauffman bracket loop coefficient is $\delta$ in the framed-link relation $[L\sqcup O]=\delta[L]$. Define the quantum integers by $[0]=0$, $[1]=1$, and $[j+1]=\delta[j]-[j-1]$ for $j\ge1$. Since $q^2=A^4$ has order $r\ge2$, these quantum integers also satisfy

$$
[j]=\frac{q^j-q^{-j}}{q-q^{-1}}=(-1)^{j-1}\frac{A^{2j}-A^{-2j}}{A^2-A^{-2}}.
$$

The BHMV simple-label convention is the finite set

$$
\mathcal J_p=\{0,1,\ldots,r-2\}.
$$

The pivotal loop and coefficient conventions throughout this page are the displayed $\delta$ and $\mathbb C$; no zero quantum integer is inverted.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Fix a closed oriented marked surface $\Sigma$ with its Lagrangian and weighted anomaly data, and fix a marked handlebody $H$ with boundary $\Sigma$ and a complementary marked handlebody $H'$ so that their gluing is the standard oriented three-sphere. Specialize the framed-link Kauffman bracket skein module of $H$ to the coefficient field and root fixed above. For $x\in\mathcal K_A(H)$ and $y\in\mathcal K_A(H')$, define the handlebody pairing $B_\Sigma(x,y)$ by gluing the two framed skeins and evaluating the resulting closed marked three-manifold with the normalized root surgery invariant. Define

$$
\operatorname{Rad}(B_\Sigma)=\{x\in\mathcal K_A(H):B_\Sigma(x,y)=0\text{ for every }y\in\mathcal K_A(H')\},
\qquad
V_p(\Sigma)=\mathcal K_A(H)/\operatorname{Rad}(B_\Sigma).
$$

This is the radical-quotient handlebody state-space construction for the specified marking and anomaly data. Independence of the marking, finite generation, nondegeneracy, and the gluing maps are separate mathematical obligations.

**External normalization input.** In this Definition the closed marked evaluation is the BHMV TQFT normalization, not merely the raw signature-normalized closed invariant $\theta_p$ of the Kirby lemma. BHMV §2 pp.897–898 and Gilmer–Masbaum §11 pp.23–25 give
$$Z_p(M,w)=\eta^{b_0(M)+b_1(M)}(\kappa^3)^w\theta_p(M),\qquad \Delta_\pm=\eta^{-1}\kappa^{\pm3}.$$
Thus $Z_p(S^3,0)=\eta$ and $Z_p(S^2\times S^1,0)=1$. These nonzero normalizations and the registered Wall-sign weight are part of the pairing. BHMV Proposition1.9, p.891, identifies EXACTLY this radical quotient computed with two complementary handlebodies with its universal state space. This external identification supplies well-definedness of the presented model; its finite basis and gluing are the separate following lemmas. The selected $\kappa$ remains a sixth root, with one weight step acting by its cube. The source itself is only used at these located statements/constructions, not as a claimed locally reconstructed universal-construction proof.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $D_0$ and $D_1$ be finite integral framed-link surgery diagrams in the standard oriented $3$-sphere, with surgery results $M_0$ and $M_1$. Then $M_0$ and $M_1$ are orientation-preservingly diffeomorphic if and only if $D_0$ and $D_1$ are related by a finite sequence of ambient isotopies, framed handle slides, and additions or deletions of split $\pm1$-framed unknots.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, finite integral framed diagrams $D_0,D_1$ in the standard oriented $S^3$, and their oriented surgery results $M_0,M_1$.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]] is inherited by the suppliers below.

[F1] [[def-integral-framed-link-surgery-diagram]] and [[def-kirby-moves-on-integral-framed-links]] specify the integer-framing, ambient-isotopy, fully framed band-slide and split signed-unit-unknot conventions.

[F2] [[lem-kirby-moves-preserve-surgery-manifold]] proves that each allowed move, and hence each finite sequence, preserves the orientation-preserving diffeomorphism type of the surgery output.

[F3] [[lem-relative-three-bordism-surgery-presentation]] proves marked relative surgery completeness. In the empty-decoration, closed-boundary case with fixed base $N=S^3$, any prescribed orientation-preserving diffeomorphism of two surgery outputs is realized by a finite sequence of exterior framed isotopies, split signed-unit-unknot moves O1, framed slides O2, and moves O3 inserting or deleting a framed knot together with its small disk-zero-framed meridian. The proof supplies the signature-adjusted marked five-bordism, common middle trace, based descending handle movie and its full framed conversion; none of those constructions is inferred from a generic function path alone.

[F4] [[lem-zero-meridian-pairs-are-generated-by-kirby-moves-in-s-three]] proves that every such O3 move in $S^3$ is a finite sequence of the moves in [F1], with the full component framings retained.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume full AC. Fix even $p\ge4$, a primitive $2p$-th root $A$, and the BHMV Kauffman bracket convention with $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$. On the weighted Lagrangian extended bordism category built from the root semisimplified Temperley–Lieb data, the normalized Kirby-color surgery maps define a finite-dimensional skein TQFT: the handlebody state spaces are the radical quotients of their skein modules, gluing is given by the inverse normalized handlebody pairing, and the resulting closed value is unchanged under isotopy, framed handle slides, and split $\pm1$-blow-ups. Forgetting the weight and Lagrangian extension yields only the projective ordinary-oriented data unless a separate anomaly-cancellation result is proved.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and let $R=\mathbb Z[A^{\pm1}]$. Identify
the solid torus with $\mathcal A\times[-1,1]$, where $\mathcal A$ is a planar
annulus. A simple closed curve is called essential if it does not bound a disk
in $\mathcal A$. Every framed link in this product admits a regular annular
diagram and an integer framing correction from its blackboard framing. Let
$z$ be one blackboard-framed annular core curve, and for $n\geq1$ let $z^n$
denote $n$ parallel copies of that curve, with $z^0$ the empty link. In the polynomial
ring $R[z]$, $z$ is also the formal variable sent to the core class $[z]$.
Then the classes $[z^n]$, $n\geq0$, form an $R$-basis of
$\mathcal K_A(\mathcal A\times[-1,1])$. Equivalently, the map
$J:R[z]\to\mathcal K_A(\mathcal A\times[-1,1])$ sending $z^n$ to $[z^n]$ is
an $R$-module isomorphism.

facts:
**Given:** The Axiom of Choice, the annulus-product model of the solid torus, and its framed-link skein module.

[A1] The Axiom of Choice, written $\mathrm{AC}$ ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

[A2] Countable choice, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, means every countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-countable-choice]]).

[A3] In ZF, $\mathrm{AC}$ implies $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]).

[F1] The module quotient is generated by framed links and imposes the crossing and zero-framed trivial-circle relations ([[def-kauffman-bracket-skein-module-of-a-three-manifold]]).

[F2] Every framed link in $\mathcal A\times(-1,1)$ admits a regular annular diagram, with its framing correction recorded by signed full-twist marks ([[lem-framed-link-diagram-calculus]]).

[F3] The state expansion $\Psi$ is well-defined on the skein module and sends a diagram with twist correction $m$ to $(-A^3)^m\sum_S A^{a(S)-b(S)}\delta^{u(S)}z^{e(S)}$ ([[lem-annular-kauffman-bracket-state-expansion]]).

[F4] A positive or negative full framing twist on a component multiplies its skein class by $-A^3$ or $-A^{-3}$, respectively ([[lem-kauffman-bracket-module-framing-twist-factor]]).

contract.text: Use the BHMV convention $A$ primitive of order $2p$, $p$ even, $r=p/2$, and labels $0,\ldots,r-2$. At $p=4$ the label set is $\{0\}$ and the torus state space has dimension $1$. At $p=6$ the label set is $\{0,1\}$, the fusion rule is $1\otimes1\cong0$, and the torus state space has dimension $2$.
