contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $A$ be an indeterminate, $R_A=\mathbb Z[A^{\pm1},(A^{-4}+1)^{-1}]$,
$q=A^{-2}$, $t=q^2=A^{-4}$, $\delta=-(q+q^{-1})=-A^2-A^{-2}$, and
$z_0=-1/(t+1)$. For a nonempty regular diagram $D$, define
$\langle D\rangle$ by summing its crossing smoothings with weights $A$ and
$A^{-1}$ and the factor $\delta^{k-1}$ for a state with $k$ circles. Let
$B_n$ be the $n$-strand Artin braid group with positive geometric generators
$\sigma_i$ (label $i$ passes below the midpoint and label $i+1$ passes above),
drawn with braid parameter increasing from bottom to top; let
$e:B_n\to\mathbb Z$ be the homomorphism $e(\sigma_i)=1$. Let $H(n)$ be
the type-A Hecke algebra with generators $T_i$, quadratic relation
$T_i^2=(v-1)T_i+v$, braid relations, and distant commutation; let $\pi_n$
send $\sigma_i$ to $T_i$. Its normalized Markov trace $\operatorname{tr}_n$
satisfies $\operatorname{tr}_n(1)=1$, cyclicity, tower restriction, and
$\operatorname{tr}_{n+1}(xT_n)=z\operatorname{tr}_n(x)$. Let
$\mathrm{TL}_n$ be the noncrossing pairing algebra with loop value $\delta$,
and let $\operatorname{Tr}_n(D)=\delta^{c(D)}$ be the unnormalized trace,
where $c(D)$ is the number of circles after joining corresponding top and
bottom endpoints outside the rectangle; set
$\tau_n=\delta^{-n}\operatorname{Tr}_n$. For $\beta\in B_n$,
$n\ge1$, orient its closure in the braid direction. Under the specialization
$v\mapsto t$, $z\mapsto z_0$ of the Hecke tower, one has
$$\langle\widehat\beta\rangle =\delta^{n-1}(-A)^{e(\beta)}\operatorname{tr}_n(\pi_n(\beta))\big|_{v=t,\,z=z_0}.$$
The identity gives bracket value $1$ on the one-strand identity closure. Its
positive and negative Markov stabilizations multiply the raw bracket by
$-A^3$ and $-A^{-3}$, respectively.

facts:
**Given:** $n\ge1$, an $n$-strand braid $\beta$, the Laurent coefficient ring
$R_A$, and the definitions and relations named below.

[F1] A crossing in the source chart is the A-smoothing with coefficient $A$
plus the B-smoothing with coefficient $A^{-1}$, and the loop value is
$\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$
([[def-kauffman-bracket-smoothing-and-loop-value]]).

[F2] The positive geometric half twist has the explicit diamond path with label
$i$ passing below the midpoint and label $i+1$ above it; the reflected path is
its inverse ([[def-elementary-geometric-half-twist]]).

[F3] $B_n$ is generated by $\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_{n-1}$ with the Artin
braid and distant-commutation relations, and the closure joins corresponding
top and bottom endpoints with the strand orientations respected
([[def-braid-group-by-the-artin-presentation]],
[[def-closure-of-a-geometric-braid]]).

[F4] The vertical identity diagram has $n$ through strands; $e_i$ has a top
cap and bottom cup at positions $i,i+1$; stacking removes each closed loop
with coefficient $\delta$
([[def-temperley-lieb-diagram-category]]).

[F5] The generators satisfy $e_i^2=\delta e_i$,
$e_ie_{i+1}e_i=e_i$, $e_{i+1}e_ie_{i+1}=e_{i+1}$, and distant commutation
([[lem-temperley-lieb-generators-satisfy-local-relations]]).

[F6] The local crossing operators satisfy R2 cancellation and the R3 braid
identity in the declared source chart
([[lem-kauffman-bracket-r2-r3-identities]]).

[F7] The unnormalized diagram closure trace is cyclic,
$\operatorname{Tr}_{n+1}(x\otimes1)=\delta\operatorname{Tr}_n(x)$, and
$\operatorname{Tr}_{n+1}((x\otimes1)e_n)=\operatorname{Tr}_n(x)$;
when $\delta$ is a unit, $\tau_n=\delta^{-n}\operatorname{Tr}_n$
([[def-temperley-lieb-closure-trace-and-partial-trace]],
[[lem-temperley-lieb-closure-trace-component-identities]]).

[F8] The Hecke tower has quadratic relation
$T_i^2=(v-1)T_i+v$, and its Ocneanu trace satisfies the tower restriction,
cyclicity, and $\operatorname{tr}_{n+1}(xT_n)=z\operatorname{tr}_n(x)$
([[def-markov-trace-on-the-type-a-hecke-tower]],
[[thm-the-ocneanu-markov-trace-exists-and-is-unique]]).

[F9] The assignment $\sigma_i\mapsto T_i$ is a group homomorphism to Hecke
units, and $T_i^{-1}=v^{-1}T_i+(v^{-1}-1)$
([[lem-the-hecke-generators-satisfy-the-artin-relations-and-are-units]]).

[F10] The Hecke tower has the decomposition
$H(n+1)=H(n)\oplus H(n)T_nH(n)$ as an $H(n)$-bimodule
([[lem-the-hecke-tower-is-free-over-the-previous-level]]).

[F11] The exponent sum is a homomorphism $e:B_n\to\mathbb Z$ with
$e(\sigma_i)=1$ ([[def-exponent-sum-of-a-braid]]).

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $A$ be an indeterminate, $q_K=A^2$, $q_L=A^{-2}$, and $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$. Use the fundamental module, positive crossing, duality maps, and twist fixed in the preceding definition. For every $n\ge1$ and $\beta\in B_n$, let $t_n(\beta)$ be the categorical ribbon trace of its blackboard-framed closure and let $w(\beta)$ be its exponent sum. With $t=A^{-4}$ and $z_0=-1/(t+1)$, the exact identities are
$$t_n(\beta)=\delta\langle\widehat\beta\rangle=\delta^n(-A)^{w(\beta)}\operatorname{tr}_n(\pi_n(\beta))\big|_{v=t,\ z=z_0},$$
$$(-A^3)^{-w(\beta)}t_n(\beta)=\delta(-A^3)^{-w(\beta)}\langle\widehat\beta\rangle.$$
Here $\operatorname{tr}_n$ is the normalized type-A Hecke Markov trace with braid generator sent to $T_i$, and $\langle\widehat\beta\rangle$ is the Kauffman bracket in the fixed crossing chart. The second identity is a value-by-value normalization formula; it does not by itself assert a Jones-polynomial specialization.

facts:
**Given:** $A$ is indeterminate, $n\ge1$, $\beta\in B_n$, and the fundamental ribbon module with its stated basis, braiding, and duality maps.

[F1] The fundamental module has the displayed positive braiding matrix $c_{V,V}$ and scalar twist $-A^3\operatorname{id}_V$ ([[def-quantum-sl2-fundamental-ribbon-module]]).

[F2] Its self-dual evaluation and coevaluation are the maps $B,U$ whose closed-loop value is $\delta$ ([[def-quantum-sl2-fundamental-ribbon-module]]).

[F3] The ribbon evaluation of the $V$-colored closed braid is the left categorical trace $t_n(\beta)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(j_{V^{\otimes n}}\rho_n(\beta))$ ([[def-ribbon-evaluation-of-an-x-colored-closed-braid]]).

[F4] The Kauffman bracket chart has the over-strand from southwest to northeast, its A-smoothing joins left endpoints, its B-smoothing joins top endpoints, and the loop value is $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$ ([[def-kauffman-bracket-smoothing-and-loop-value]]).

[F5] The positive Artin half twist has label $i$ pass below the midpoint and label $i+1$ pass above, and its over/under projected tangents are $(1,-2h)$ and $(1,2h)$ in the stated projection coordinates ([[def-oriented-crossing-sign-writhe-and-blackboard-framing]]).

[F6] The Hecke–bracket trace dictionary states $\langle\widehat\beta\rangle=\delta^{n-1}(-A)^{e(\beta)}\operatorname{tr}_n(\pi_n(\beta))|_{v=t,z=z_0}$ for $q=A^{-2}$, $t=A^{-4}$, and $z_0=-1/(t+1)$ ([[lem-hecke-bracket-trace-dictionary-and-local-descent]]).

[F7] The braid exponent sum is a homomorphism with $w(\sigma_i^{\pm1})=\pm1$ ([[def-exponent-sum-of-a-braid]]).

[A1] The Axiom of Countable Choice, $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, selects an element from every countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable-choice]]).

[F8] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the framed tangle evaluator is monoidal, sends crossings to braidings and cups and caps to the chosen duality maps, and assigns equal values to framed-isotopic tangles ([[thm-a-ribbon-object-defines-a-unique-framed-tangle-evaluation-functor]]).

[F9] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the categorical ribbon trace $t_n(\beta)$ equals the framed tangle evaluation of the blackboard-framed closure ([[lem-ribbon-trace-equals-the-framed-closure-evaluation]]).

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $n\ge0$. In the unframed category, let $V$ be an $R$-valued invariant of type at most $n$. In the framed category assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and let $V$ be an $R$-valued framed invariant of type at most $n$. In either category, every degree-$n$ chord diagram $D$ has an $n$-singular representative $K$ with no framing zeroes in the framed case, and $w_V(D):=D_nV(K)$ is independent of the representative and of its zero-free framing class. For every degree-$n$ 4T generator $D_1-D_2+D_3-D_4$, the induced values satisfy $w_V(D_1)-w_V(D_2)+w_V(D_3)-w_V(D_4)=0$; this holds in the framed category with no 1T condition.

facts:
**Given:** A commutative ring $R$, an integer $n\ge0$, an $R$-valued ambient-isotopy invariant $V$ of oriented knots of type at most $n$, and the singular-knot and chord-diagram conventions below.

[F1] [[def-singular-knot-and-vassiliev-derivative]]: the finite difference is the alternating sum over all $2^m$ independent resolutions; in the framed case the $m$ singularities include double points and simple zeroes of the normal section.

[F2] [[def-framed-chord-diagram-and-four-term-relations]]: a degree-$n$ chord diagram is an oriented circle with $n$ paired endpoint sets; the 4T generator is $D_1-D_2+D_3-D_4$ from the endpoint-slide construction.

[F3] [[lem-each-oriented-reidemeister-move-is-realized-by-ambient-isotopy]]: each local oriented Reidemeister III replacement, with fixed outside lift, is an ambient isotopy supported over its move disk.

[F4] [[def-oriented-crossing-sign-writhe-and-blackboard-framing]]: a crossing has sign $\operatorname{sgn}\det(v_{\mathrm{over}},v_{\mathrm{under}})$ in the oriented projection plane, calibrated so the positive Artin half twist has sign $+1$.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: the framed normal-bundle and section clauses assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$; no choice axiom is used in the unframed crossing-change and 4T calculations.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $n\ge1$, and let $V$ be an $R$-valued invariant of unframed oriented knots of type at most $n$. Then $D_nV(K)=0$ whenever the degree-$n$ chord diagram of the $n$-singular knot $K$ has a chord that intersects no other chord. This is the 1T vanishing law for unframed symbols. In the framed category no universal 1T vanishing law holds: under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, integer-valued framed self-linking has type at most $1$ and has derivative $2$ on a one-chord diagram with blackboard framing.

facts:
**Given:** An unframed invariant $V$ of type at most $n$, its singular-knot finite-difference convention, and the chord-intersection convention in the statement. The separate framed witness assumes $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$.

[F1] [[def-singular-knot-and-vassiliev-derivative]]: the finite difference is the alternating sum over independent resolutions, and type at most $n$ means that every $(n+1)$-st finite difference vanishes; framed singularities may be double points or simple framing zeroes.

[F2] [[def-framed-chord-diagram-and-four-term-relations]]: two chords intersect when their endpoints alternate, a chord is isolated when it intersects no other chord, and 1T sets an unframed diagram with an isolated chord equal to zero.

[F3] [[def-oriented-crossing-sign-writhe-and-blackboard-framing]]: crossing sign is $\operatorname{sgn}\det(v_{\mathrm{over}},v_{\mathrm{under}})$, the writhe is the sum of crossing signs, and the positive Artin half twist has sign $+1$.

[F4] [[def-framed-knot-self-linking-and-seifert-framing]]: under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, framed self-linking is the linking number of the knot and a sufficiently small push-off along its framing section.

[F5] [[lem-framed-knot-push-off-self-linking-well-defined]]: under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, that push-off linking number is independent of the sufficiently small radius, framing representative, and normalized tubular chart.

[F6] [[thm-blackboard-framing-self-linking-is-writhe]]: under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the self-linking of the blackboard framing of a regular knot diagram equals its writhe.

[F7] [[alg-oriented-linking-number-from-diagram]]: for a two-component diagram, linking number is one half the signed sum of mixed crossing signs.

[F8] [[thm-oriented-linking-number-scan-terminates-and-is-correct]]: under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the finite scan returns the integer linking number.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ asserts that every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function; it is used only for the framed self-linking supplier branch, not for the finite unframed crossing-change argument.

contract.heading: Example
contract.text: For an oriented two-component link $L=L_1\cup L_2$, let $\operatorname{lk}(L_1,L_2)$ be one half the sum of the signs of all crossings between distinct components, using $\operatorname{sgn}\det(v_{\mathrm{over}},v_{\mathrm{under}})$ in the oriented projection plane with positive viewing normal. Extend the singular finite-difference formula to links by resolving marked crossings independently. At one marked mixed crossing, the positive-minus-negative derivative of $\operatorname{lk}$ is $+1$; reversing the order of those two resolutions gives $-1$. A marked self-crossing has derivative $0$. At any two distinct marked crossings, mixed or self, the second derivative is $0$, so linking number is a type-at-most-one invariant of two-component links and, by the nonzero first derivative, has exact type one. The total pairwise linking number of a one-component knot is $0$, because the defining sum over distinct component pairs is empty.

facts:
**Given:** The crossing-sign convention and the two-component oriented-link linking-number formula in the Example statement. The topological invariance of this quantity uses the separate $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ supplier branch.

[F1] [[def-singular-knot-and-vassiliev-derivative]]: link finite differences are the alternating sums over independent marked-crossing resolutions.

[F2] [[def-oriented-crossing-sign-writhe-and-blackboard-framing]]: a crossing sign is $\operatorname{sgn}\det(v_{\mathrm{over}},v_{\mathrm{under}})$; a positive crossing has sign $+1$ and a negative crossing has sign $-1$.

[F3] [[alg-oriented-linking-number-from-diagram]]: on a two-component diagram the linking-number algorithm returns one half of the signed sum of mixed crossings.

[F4] [[thm-oriented-linking-number-scan-terminates-and-is-correct]]: under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the finite diagram scan terminates and returns the integer linking number.

[F5] [[thm-linking-number-is-invariant-and-writhe-is-not]]: under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the algorithmic linking number is unchanged by oriented Reidemeister moves and hence is invariant under ambient isotopy.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ asserts that every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function; only the topological supplier chain [F4]–[F5] uses it.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For any two regular oriented diagrams
of ambient-isotopic two-component links, the algorithmic linking numbers
agree. Creating a positive type-I kink increases total writhe by $1$ and
deleting it decreases writhe by $1$; creating a negative kink decreases writhe
by $1$ and deleting it increases writhe by $1$. Types II and III leave total
writhe unchanged. For a knot
component, blackboard self-linking changes by the same amount under a type-I
move. Consequently writhe and blackboard self-linking are not invariants of
unframed ambient isotopy, although the integer linking number of two distinct
components is.

facts:
**Given:** The Axiom of Countable Choice, regular oriented link diagrams, and
the indicated ambient-isotopy relations.

[A1] The Axiom of Countable Choice, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]).

[F1] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, ambient-isotopic regular oriented link diagrams are connected by a finite sequence of planar isotopies and oriented Reidemeister moves ([[thm-oriented-reidemeister-equivalence-theorem]]).

[F2] A type-I move adds or removes a self-crossing; type II adds or removes two crossings of opposite signs; type III preserves the signs of its three crossings ([[def-oriented-reidemeister-moves]]).

[F3] Writhe is the signed sum over all crossings, and self-writhe is the signed sum over one component's self-crossings ([[def-oriented-crossing-sign-writhe-and-blackboard-framing]]).

[F4] Linking number is the integer half-sum of mixed crossing signs, invariant under all three Reidemeister moves ([[lem-linking-number-even-sum-and-reidemeister-invariance]]).

[F5] For a knot, blackboard self-linking equals diagram writhe ([[thm-blackboard-framing-self-linking-is-writhe]]).

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
For an oriented link type $L$ in $S^3$, the Conway polynomial is the polynomial $
abla_L(z)\in\mathbb Z[z]$ characterized by the normalization $
abla_U(z)=1$ for the unknot $U$ and the skein relation
$$
abla_{L_+}(z)-
abla_{L_-}(z)=z\,
abla_{L_0}(z).$$
Here $L_+$ and $L_-$ are identical oriented links outside a ball and have respectively a positive and negative crossing inside it, while $L_0$ is obtained in that ball by the orientation-preserving smoothing. For each integer $k\ge0$, the $k$th Conway coefficient is $c_k(L):=[z^k]
abla_L(z)$. This carrier records the conventional skein interface; existence and uniqueness of the invariant are a separate well-definedness obligation. The skein characterization is on nonempty oriented links. If the link domain also includes the empty link, extend the invariant by the separate conventional value $
abla_{\varnothing}(z)=0$; this empty-link value is not determined by the nonempty skein axioms.

facts:
**Given:** Finite diagrams of nonempty oriented links, with no ordering of their components, the declared positive/negative crossing convention and oriented smoothing. The link isotopy and diagram conventions are those of the Definition.

[F1] **External input — existence of the Conway coefficient invariants.** T. Garaev, *Elementary proof of existence of the Alexander-Conway polynomial*, arXiv:2012.03086v1 (5 December 2020), Section1, Theorem1, PDF p.2, with the equivalence and skein charts on p.1, supplies a sequence $c_{-1}=0,c_0,c_1,\ldots$ of invariants of oriented link diagrams with unordered components. They are invariant under all oriented Reidemeister moves and planar isotopies, have $c_0(U)=1$ and $c_j(U)=0$ for $j>0$, and satisfy
$$c_j(L_+)-c_j(L_-)=c_{j-1}(L_0),\qquad j\ge0.$$
This is an imported established coefficient-existence result, not a claim to reconstruct its Reidemeister-III argument. The source's crossing sign agrees with the declared convention: it is positive when the ordered over/under tangent pair has positive planar determinant. Its Figure2 is the oriented smoothing in this Definition. Polynomial finiteness, integrality and uniqueness are earned below rather than falsely attributed to the coefficient-sequence statement alone.

[F2] **External input — ambient-link interpretation and conventional normalization.** Chmutov–Duzhin–Mostovoy, *Introduction to Vassiliev Knot Invariants*, §1.2.1, printed p.11/PDF19, gives the Reidemeister diagram criterion with its oriented extension; §2.3.1, printed pp.35–36/PDF43–44, states the Conway invariant of ORIENTED LINKS with values in $\mathbb Z[t]$, normalized to one on the unknot and satisfying its displayed positive-minus-negative skein relation. It uses links with unnumbered components. These are the ambient-link interpretation and the standard skein convention of [F1]; the letter $t$ is renamed $z$. The book's §2.3.2 expressly notes that existence is nontrivial. Here existence is EXTERNALLY supplied, not inferred from that observation or from a formal definition. The empty link, if included in the ambient link domain, is assigned the separate conventional zero value in the Definition; the imported skein characterization is only for nonempty links.

Actual reading limits: the complete Garaev v1 Section1/Theorem1 statement and crossing-sign definitions on PDF pp.1–2, including visual inspection of Figures1–3; the coefficient-extension setup on p.3; CDM's complete §1.2.1 text and its oriented extension on printed p.11, and the complete §2.3.1 definition and displayed skein normalization plus the opening §2.3.2 text on printed pp.35–36. No full Garaev proof, Reidemeister-III reconstruction or full book reading is claimed. These exact established external inputs are used under the run-specific external-source permission.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Use coordinates $(z,t)\in\mathbb C\times\mathbb R$ on oriented $\mathbb R^3$, with $t$ increasing upward. A knot is a smooth embedding $K:S^1\hookrightarrow\mathbb C\times\mathbb R$ with the orientation of $S^1$. A strict Morse presentation is one for which $t|_K$ has nondegenerate critical points, meaning its second derivative in a local coordinate is nonzero there, and pairwise distinct critical values. Write $t_{\min}:=\min_{x\in K}t(x)$, $t_{\max}:=\max_{x\in K}t(x)$, and $r(K)$ for the number of local maxima. A parenthesized $q$-braid is a smooth braid with $q$ strands, each strictly increasing in $t$, together with an ordered binary parenthesization of its lower endpoints and an ordered binary parenthesization of its upper endpoints.

For $n\ge0$, a degree-$n$ chord diagram is an oriented circle with $n$ disjoint unordered pairs of distinct points, called chords. Let $\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{fr}}$ be the rational vector space on these diagrams modulo 4T, and let $\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{un}}$ be its quotient by 1T as well. A 4T relation fixes one chord $pq$ and another chord endpoint $r$, moves the other endpoint of the second chord to just before or after $p$ and just before or after $q$, and takes the alternating sum of those four diagrams. A chord is isolated when it intersects no other chord, where intersection means that chord endpoints alternate around the circle; 1T sets every such diagram to zero. Put $\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{fr/un}}_{\mathbb C}:=\prod_{n\ge0}(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{fr/un}}\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C)$, with multiplication induced by connected sum of diagrams and unit the empty diagram. For $q$ ordered upward strands, let $\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathbb C}(q)$ be the completion of the associative algebra generated by $t_{ij}=t_{ji}$ for $1\le i<j\le q$, with relations $[t_{ij},t_{kl}]=0$ when $i,j,k,l$ are distinct and $[t_{ij},t_{ik}+t_{jk}]=0$ when $i,j,k$ are distinct. The generator $t_{ij}$ is a horizontal chord joining strands $i$ and $j$; multiplication stacks diagrams from bottom to top.

More generally, a compact strict Morse tangle $T$ is a compact oriented smooth one-dimensional submanifold of $\mathbb C\times[a,b]$, with distinct boundary points on the planes $t=a$ and $t=b$, transverse to those planes, and with nondegenerate interior critical points of height having distinct critical values. A tangle chord diagram is a finite set of unordered pairs of distinct interior points on the oriented tangle skeleton. Its 4T relation is the same local alternating relation as above on the skeleton. The unframed tangle quotient also sets to zero any chord whose endpoints are consecutive in the order along the same skeleton component; for a circle the order is cyclic and for an arc it is linear. The completed degreewise tangle diagram space is denoted $\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C}(T)$.

The unframed configuration series of a strict Morse presentation $K$ is the formal degreewise series
$$
Z(K):=\sum_{m\ge0}\frac1{(2\pi i)^m}\int_{t_{\min}<t_m<\cdots<t_1<t_{\max}}\ \sum_{P}(-1)^{\downarrow(P)}[D_P]_{\mathrm{un}}\bigwedge_{j=1}^m\frac{dz_j-dz'_j}{z_j-z'_j}\ \in\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C}.
$$
The ordered simplex is divided into chambers by the critical values of $t|_K$. In each chamber, $P$ ranges over choices, at each level $t_j$, of an unordered pair of distinct points $(z_j,t_j),(z'_j,t_j)$ of $K$. The diagram $D_P$ joins the corresponding preimages on the oriented parameter circle. The integer $\downarrow(P)$ counts endpoints at which $t$ decreases along the orientation of $K$. The differential form is pulled back to the chamber by the selected local branches. The degree-zero term is the empty diagram with coefficient $1$; the displayed integrals are interpreted as improper integrals on each chamber.

For a compact strict Morse tangle $T$, $Z(T)$ is given by the same formula with $T$ in place of $K$, the interval $(a,b)$ in place of $(t_{\min},t_{\max})$, the chord diagrams on the tangle skeleton in place of circle diagrams, and the corresponding unframed tangle quotient in place of $\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C}$. A parenthesized braid is a special case with no interior critical points.

For a parenthesized braid path $\gamma$ in the configuration space of $q$ distinct complex points, define its Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov (KZ) series by the degreewise iterated-integral holonomy of
$$\Omega_q=\frac1{2\pi i}\sum_{1\le i<j\le q}t_{ij}\,d\log(z_i-z_j).$$
Explicitly, if $\gamma:[0,1]\to\operatorname{Conf}_q(\mathbb C)$ is an ordinary path with noncolliding endpoints, its holonomy is
$$1+\sum_{m\ge1}\int_{0<t_m<\cdots<t_1<1}\gamma^*\Omega_q(t_1)\cdots\gamma^*\Omega_q(t_m).$$
A tangential endpoint is a limiting collision configuration together with a specified nonzero first-order direction of approach for each colliding cluster. When endpoints have such clusters prescribed by the parenthesizations, the holonomy is the constant term after removing the local logarithmic factors $\exp(t_{ij}\log\varepsilon/(2\pi i))$ at each tangential endpoint. A change between the two parenthesizations of three consecutive strands is encoded by the regularized transport $\Phi_{\mathrm{KZ}}$.

For parenthesized braids the KZ holonomy takes values in the framed strand algebra, where only tangled 4T is imposed; passing from a closed framed strand diagram to an unframed knot applies the quotient by isolated-chord 1T. Fix a standard hump $H$ by starting with the two-critical-point unknot and inserting one local birth of a maximum-minimum pair; thus $H$ has two local maxima. The normalized unframed Kontsevich series of $K$ is
$$
I(K):=Z(K)\,Z(H)^{-r(K)}\in\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C},
$$
The normalization uses one copy of $Z(H)$ for each local maximum; its degree-zero term is $1$, so its inverse is interpreted in the product completion. This definition makes no assertion that the unnormalized KZ coefficients are rational or that equal Kontsevich series separate knot types.

The following figure illustrates the positive Artin generator $\sigma_1$ and parenthesization conventions. Height increases upward, the right-bottom strand is the overstrand under the determinant crossing convention, and the labels at the ends record the ordered parenthesizations; no proof below relies on the drawing.

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.82,thick]
  \draw (2,0) -- (2,3);
  \draw[very thick] (1,0) -- (0.5,1.5) -- (0,3);
  \draw (0,0) -- (0.48,1.44);
  \draw (0.52,1.56) -- (1,3);
  \node at (1,-0.32) {$((1\ 2)\ 3)$};
  \node at (1,3.32) {$((2\ 1)\ 3)$};
  \node at (1.2,2.55) {$\sigma_1$};
  \node at (2.45,1.5) {$t$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
For every integer $q\ge2$, let $\operatorname{Conf}_q(\mathbb C)$ be the space of ordered $q$-tuples of pairwise distinct complex points, and let $\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathbb C}(q)$ and $t_{ij}$ be as defined for parenthesized braids. Write $\sigma_i$ for the positive geometric half twist interchanging adjacent strands $i$ and $i+1$ in a disk containing no other strand. The Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov form
$$\Omega_q=\frac1{2\pi i}\sum_{1\le i<j\le q}t_{ij}\,d\log(z_i-z_j)$$
satisfies $d\Omega_q=0$ and $\Omega_q\wedge\Omega_q=0$. Consequently the degreewise iterated-integral holonomy depends only on the homotopy class of a path with fixed endpoints. On geometric braids this holonomy respects the distant commutation relations $\sigma_i\sigma_j=\sigma_j\sigma_i$ for $|i-j|\ge2$ and the adjacent braid relations $\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i=\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}$.

facts:
**Given:** An integer $q\ge2$, the configuration space $\operatorname{Conf}_q(\mathbb C)$, the completed strand algebra $\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathbb C}(q)$ with its infinitesimal braid relations, and the KZ form $\Omega_q$.

[F1] [[def-kontsevich-integral-on-parenthesized-braids]]: the strand algebra is degreewise completed, is generated by $t_{ij}=t_{ji}$, and satisfies $[t_{ij},t_{kl}]=0$ for distinct indices and $[t_{ij},t_{ik}+t_{jk}]=0$ for distinct $i,j,k$; the KZ form is the displayed logarithmic connection.

[F2] [[def-framed-chord-diagram-and-four-term-relations]]: a 4T relation is the alternating four-diagram relation obtained by moving one endpoint past either endpoint of a fixed chord; the framed diagram quotient imposes 4T and does not impose 1T.

[F3] [[def-singular-knot-and-vassiliev-derivative]]: the positive and negative resolutions of a transverse crossing are labelled by the determinant crossing sign, and the positive Artin half twist is positive.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume countable choice, and let $I_m(K)$ be the degree-$m$ homogeneous coefficient of the normalized unframed Kontsevich series $I(K)$ of a smooth oriented knot type $K$. For $n\ge0$, put $I_{\le n}(K)=\sum_{m=0}^{n}I_m(K)$. A function on knot types is of type at most $n$ when its alternating resolution sum on every $(n+1)$-singular knot is zero. Then $I_{\le n}$ is a type-at-most-$n$ invariant with values in the sum of the unframed degree-$m$ chord-diagram modules for $0\le m\le n$. For every $n$-singular knot with chord diagram $D$, its $n$-fold finite difference satisfies $D_n I_{\le n}(K)=D$. In particular, the degree-$n$ symbol is the identity on rational chord diagrams after extending scalars to $\mathbb C$; no rational-coefficient claim is made about $I_m(K)$.

facts:
**Given:** Countable choice, a degree cutoff $n$, and the unframed normalized series of a strict Morse presentation of each oriented knot type.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: countable choice is assumed only through the ambient-isotopy invariance supplier.

[F1] [[def-kontsevich-integral-on-parenthesized-braids]]: $I(K)$ is the degreewise series in the completed unframed 4T+1T chord-diagram module.

[F2] [[def-singular-knot-and-vassiliev-derivative]]: $D_kF(K)$ is the alternating sum over the $2^k$ resolutions of a $k$-singular knot; type at most $n$ means $D_{n+1}F=0$ on every $(n+1)$-singular knot.

[F3] [[thm-kontsevich-universal-associated-graded-proof]]: on a $k$-singular knot with chord diagram $D$, $D_kI(K)$ has zero degrees below $k$ and degree-$k$ component exactly $D$.

[F4] [[lem-kontsevich-braid-and-knot-isotopy-invariance]]: under countable choice, $I(K)$ is independent of the strict Morse presentation and is invariant under ambient isotopy of oriented knots.

[F5] [[def-framed-chord-diagram-and-four-term-relations]]: each degreewise unframed chord-diagram module is the rational 4T+1T quotient, and its complexification is the target of $I_m$.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume countable choice. Let $\mathcal V_n^{\mathbb C}$ be the $\mathbb C$-vector space of ambient-isotopy invariants of oriented knots with values in $\mathbb C$ and type at most $n$, where type at most $n$ means that the alternating resolution sum on every $(n+1)$-singular knot is zero; set $\mathcal V_{-1}^{\mathbb C}=0$. Let $\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{un}}$ be the rational vector space on degree-$n$ circle chord diagrams modulo 4T and 1T; a weight system is a $\mathbb Q$-linear functional on this space. For an $n$-singular knot with chord diagram $D$, define $\sigma_n([V])(D)$ to be the $n$-fold alternating resolution sum of $V$ on that knot. Let $I_{\le n}(K)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}I_j(K)$ be the degree-$n$ truncation of the normalized unframed Kontsevich series. The degree-$n$ symbol map
$$
\sigma_n:\mathcal V_n^{\mathbb C}/\mathcal V_{n-1}^{\mathbb C}\longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Q}(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{un}},\mathbb C)
$$
is surjective. In particular, every rational weight system has a complex-valued finite-type lift; no rationality claim is made about that lift or about the coefficients of $I(K)$. Moreover, for every $n$ and every $V\in\mathcal V_n^{\mathbb C}$ there is a complex-linear functional $\Lambda_V$ on $\bigoplus_{j=0}^{n}(\mathcal A_j^{\mathrm{un}}\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C)$ whose degree-$n$ restriction is the degree-$n$ symbol of $V$ and such that
$$
V(K)=\Lambda_V(I_{\le n}(K))
$$
for every oriented knot type $K$. This recovery statement does not imply that distinct knot types have distinct Kontsevich series.

facts:
**Given:** Countable choice, the unframed finite-difference convention, and the normalized Kontsevich series with coefficients in the complexified chord-diagram completion.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: countable choice is the only axiom needed here, through ambient-isotopy invariance of the normalized series.

[F1] [[def-singular-knot-and-vassiliev-derivative]]: an invariant is of type at most $n$ when its $(n+1)$-fold alternating resolution sum vanishes on every $(n+1)$-singular knot.

[F2] [[def-framed-chord-diagram-and-four-term-relations]]: $\mathcal A_j^{\mathrm{un}}$ is the rational vector space on degree-$j$ circle chord diagrams modulo 4T and 1T.

[F3] [[thm-vassiliev-invariant-induces-weight-system]]: for an unframed invariant of type at most $n$, the $n$-fold derivative is a well-defined rational-linear weight system on $\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{un}}$; the conclusion holds for complex-valued invariants as well.

[F4] [[lem-kontsevich-integral-finite-type-truncation]]: $I_{\le n}$ is type at most $n$, and on an $n$-singular knot with diagram $D$ its $n$-fold derivative is $D$.

[F5] [[thm-kontsevich-universal-associated-graded-proof]]: for each $k$-singular knot, $D_kI$ has no homogeneous terms below degree $k$ and its degree-$k$ term is the chord diagram of that knot.

[F6] [[lem-kontsevich-braid-and-knot-isotopy-invariance]]: under countable choice, each coefficient $I_j(K)$ is a well-defined ambient-isotopy invariant of oriented knot types.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $n\ge0$. For an unframed $R$-valued invariant $V$ of type at most $n$, the degree-$n$ derivative induces an $R$-linear functional on degree-$n$ chord diagrams modulo 4T and 1T. For a framed $R$-valued invariant $V$ of type at most $n$, assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$; its degree-$n$ derivative induces an $R$-linear functional on degree-$n$ chord diagrams modulo 4T. Framed derivatives are not subject to a universal 1T vanishing law: integer-valued framed self-linking has value $2$ on the one-chord diagram with blackboard framing.

facts:
**Given:** A commutative ring $R$, an integer $n\ge0$, and an $R$-valued invariant $V$ of type at most $n$. The 4T and unframed 1T conclusions are choice-free. The framed case and its non-1T witness assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as in [A1].

[F1] [[def-singular-knot-and-vassiliev-derivative]]: the $n$-fold derivative is the alternating sum over independent resolutions; framed type bounds also count framing zeroes as singularities.

[F2] [[def-framed-chord-diagram-and-four-term-relations]]: both framed and unframed symbol modules are generated by ordinary degree-$n$ chord diagrams; 4T is imposed in both and 1T only in the unframed module.

[F3] [[lem-vassiliev-4t-from-singular-reidemeister-move]]: in both categories the derivative value is representative-independent and annihilates every 4T generator.

[F4] [[lem-vassiliev-framing-one-term-relation]]: unframed derivatives vanish on diagrams with an isolated chord; under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, framed self-linking has type at most $1$ and value $2$ on the one-chord blackboard-framed diagram.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ selects one element from each set in a sequence of nonempty sets; it is assumed for the framed normal-bundle branch and the framed witness inherited from [F4], not for the unframed 4T or 1T arguments.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $\mathcal C$ be a ribbon category with chosen left duals and tensor unit $\mathbf 1$. A **finite oriented framed link colored in $\mathcal C$** is a finite disjoint union $L$ of oriented smoothly embedded circles in $S^3$, a homotopy class of nowhere-zero normal vector field on each component, and an assignment of an object of $\mathcal C$ to each component. A framed colored isotopy carries orientations, framings, and component colors. If $F_{\mathcal C}$ is the ribbon-tangle evaluation functor, define
$$\operatorname{RT}_{\mathcal C}(L):=F_{\mathcal C}(L)\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf 1).$$
This value depends only on the framed colored isotopy class. It is not automatically a field scalar; if $\mathcal C$ is $k$-linear and $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf 1)=k$, it is a scalar in $k$. The empty link is assigned $1_{\mathbf 1}$.

facts:
**Given:** The ribbon category, its chosen left duals, a finite oriented framed link, and an object color on every component.

[F1] For arbitrary component colors, the ribbon evaluation assigns a morphism to each colored framed tangle, is invariant under framed graph isotopy, and preserves the empty graph ([[lem-multicolored-ribbon-coupon-evaluation]]).

[A1] Countable choice means every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-countable-choice]]).

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $A$ be an indeterminate, put $q=A^4$, $q_K=A^2$, and $q_L=A^{-2}=q_K^{-1}$, and work over $F=\mathbb Q(A)$. An oriented knot in $S^3$ means a smooth embedded circle with an orientation, considered up to orientation-preserving ambient isotopy. For an integer $r$, put
$$[r]=\frac{q_K^r-q_K^{-r}}{q_K-q_K^{-1}},\qquad [m]!=\prod_{r=1}^{m}[r]\quad(m\ge1),\qquad [0]!=1.$$
For each $N\ge1$, put $q_N=\exp(2\pi i/N)$.
For each integer $N\ge1$, let $V_N$ have basis $v_0,\ldots,v_{N-1}$ and define the $U_{q_L}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ action in the library coproduct convention by
$$K_Lv_j=q_L^{N-1-2j}v_j,\qquad Ev_j=[N-j]v_{j-1},\qquad Fv_j=[j+1]v_{j+1},$$
where $v_{-1}=v_N=0$. In the universal $R$-matrix formula use $q_K$ and $H v_j=(N-1-2j)v_j$; on $V_N\otimes V_N$ its action is the finite sum
$$\mathcal R_N=q_K^{H\otimes H/2}\sum_{r=0}^{N-1}q_K^{r(r-1)/2}\frac{(q_K-q_K^{-1})^r}{[r]!}\,E^r\otimes F^r,$$
and the positive crossing is $c_N=P\mathcal R_N$, where $P(x\otimes y)=y\otimes x$. This is an irreducible module of dimension $N$. Equip these matrices with the Kauffman-bracket half-ribbon data: the twist matrix is the scalar $\theta_N=\lambda_N I$ with $\lambda_N=(-1)^{N-1}A^{N^2-1}$, and the matrix $G_N=(-1)^{N-1}\operatorname{diag}(A^{2(N-1-2j)})_{j=0}^{N-1}$ is the pivotal comparison used in the closure trace. The resulting generic quantum dimension is
$$d_N=\operatorname{Tr}(G_N)=(-1)^{N-1}\frac{A^{2N}-A^{-2N}}{A^2-A^{-2}}.$$
Use the contragredient left-dual action $(x\cdot f)(v)=f(S(x)v)$ on $V_N^*$, with evaluation $\operatorname{ev}(f\otimes v)=f(v)$ and coevaluation $1\mapsto\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}v_j\otimes v_j^*$. The ambient category is the $F$-linear category generated by the modules $V_N$ for all $N\ge1$ under finite tensor products, contragredient duals, finite direct sums and images of module-idempotents, whose morphisms are module homomorphisms, and whose tensor-product action is induced by the stated Hopf coproduct; its tensor unit is $F$ with the trivial action, so its tensor-unit endomorphism ring is $F$. These matrix data satisfy the ribbon-category axioms: braiding and inverse braiding, both duality snakes, monoidal pivotal comparison, balancing and dual compatibility of twist. Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice for the framed-tangle and Markov constructions. An oriented knot $K\subset S^3$ presented as the closure of an $n$-strand braid $\beta$ has generic normalized value
$$J_N^{\mathrm{gen}}(K;q)=\lambda_N^{-w(\beta)}\frac{\operatorname{Tr}(G_N^{\otimes n}\rho_N(\beta))}{d_N}\in F,$$
where, for a word $\beta=\sigma_{i_1}^{\varepsilon_1}\cdots\sigma_{i_m}^{\varepsilon_m}$ with $\varepsilon_j\in\{1,-1\}$, $w(\beta):=\sum_{j=1}^m\varepsilon_j$, and $\rho_N(\beta)$ is obtained by replacing each positive braid generator by $c_N$ on the corresponding adjacent tensor factors and each inverse generator by $c_N^{-1}$, then composing in word order. This quotient is an integral Laurent polynomial in $A^4$. Define the **normalized colored Jones sequence** by the unique $J_N(K;q)\in\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ satisfying $J_N(K;A^4)=J_N^{\mathrm{gen}}(K;A^4)$. Its root value $J_N(K;q_N)$ is obtained by substituting into this Laurent polynomial. The variable transport to the ordinary Jones convention is $t=q^{-1}=A^{-4}$.

facts:
**Given:** An integer $N\ge1$, the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice, the generic module and matrices from the Definition, an oriented knot $K$, and a braid word $\beta$ whose closure represents $K$.

[F1] The library presentation has $K_L E K_L^{-1}=q_L^2E$, $K_L F K_L^{-1}=q_L^{-2}F$, and $EF-FE=(K_L-K_L^{-1})/(q_L-q_L^{-1})$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

[F2] The library coproduct is $\Delta(E)=E\otimes K_L^{-1}+1\otimes E$ and $\Delta(F)=F\otimes1+K_L\otimes F$ ([[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]]).

[F3] A ribbon category has a braiding, chosen duals, and a twist satisfying the balancing and dual-compatibility identities ([[def-braiding]], [[def-left-dual-and-right-dual-object]], [[def-twist-and-ribbon-structure]]).

[F4] For an absolutely simple color with scalar twist $\lambda I$, the generic framed trace corrected by $\lambda^{-w(\beta)}$ is invariant under oriented unframed Markov equivalence, under the stated Axiom of Choice ([[thm-twist-correction-removes-framing]]).

[F5] The framed colored-link value is the ribbon-tangle evaluation in $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf1)$, and a closed braid is evaluated by the pivotal trace of its braid action ([[def-colored-framed-knot-evaluation-from-ribbon-category]]).

[F6] Absolute simplicity means $\operatorname{End}(V_N)=F I$ ([[def-absolutely-simple-object]]).

[F7] The finite matrices satisfy all ribbon identities for every $N\ge1$ and their pivotal trace of the identity is $d_N$ ([[lem-colored-jones-generic-ribbon-data]]).

[F8] The normalized generic quotient for every knot and color belongs to $\mathbb Z[A^4,A^{-4}]$ ([[lem-colored-jones-generic-quotient-is-laurent]]).

[A2] The Axiom of Choice supplies a choice function for every family of nonempty sets ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

[A3] Countable choice supplies a choice function for every sequence of nonempty sets ([[def-countable-choice]]).

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $\omega$ be an indeterminate, set $A=\omega^{-2}$, and put $k'=\mathbb Q(\omega)$, $q_K=A^2$, and $q_L=A^{-2}$. Work over the scalar extension to $k'$ of the library Hopf algebra at $q_L$; $U_{q_K}$ in Korinman's convention is identified by $q_L=q_K^{-1}$ and $K_L=K_K^{-1}$. Use its generic two-dimensional module $V$ over $k'$ with ordered basis $(v_+,v_-)$ and generator matrices
$$E=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad F=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad K_K=\begin{pmatrix}q_K&0\\0&q_K^{-1}\end{pmatrix}.$$
Equivalently, for the library parameter $q_L=q_K^{-1}$ use $K_L=K_K^{-1}=\operatorname{diag}(q_L,q_L^{-1})$ and the library coproduct convention $\Delta(E)=E\otimes K_L^{-1}+1\otimes E$, $\Delta(F)=F\otimes1+K_L\otimes F$. This parameter and Cartan-generator conversion is part of the definition; the two $q$ symbols are not identified.

The object $V$ is absolutely simple in the $k'$-linear representation category.

Equip $V$ with the Kauffman-bracket half-ribbon structure. The half-ribbon operator $\Omega$ is specified by
$$C:=\operatorname{Mat}_{(v_+,v_-)}(\Omega^{-1})=\begin{pmatrix}0&\omega\\-\omega^5&0\end{pmatrix},$$
and its associated twist is $\theta_V=\Omega^2=-A^3\operatorname{id}_V$. In the ordered basis $(v_+\otimes v_+,v_+\otimes v_-,v_-\otimes v_+,v_-\otimes v_-)$, the positive braiding is
$$c_{V,V}=\begin{pmatrix}A&0&0&0\\0&0&A^{-1}&0\\0&A^{-1}&A-A^{-3}&0\\0&0&0&A\end{pmatrix}.$$
Its ribbon quantum dimension is $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$. The half-ribbon and universal $R$-matrix are those of the topological half-ribbon representation category; the selected ribbon element is the Kauffman-bracket one, not the usual $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ ribbon element.

Let $v_+^*,v_-^*$ be the ordinary dual basis. The left-dual action on $V^*$ is the contragredient action $(x\cdot f)(v)=f(S(x)v)$ for the antipode $S$ of the stated library Hopf convention. Identify the displayed copy of $V$ with this left dual $V^\vee$ by $v_+\mapsto v_-^*$ and $v_-\mapsto -A^{-2}v_+^*$. In this identification the evaluation and coevaluation maps are
$$B(v_+\otimes v_-)=1,\quad B(v_-\otimes v_+)=-A^{-2},\quad B(v_+\otimes v_+)=B(v_-\otimes v_-)=0,$$
$$U(1)=-A^2v_+\otimes v_-+v_-\otimes v_+.$$
These are the explicit duality maps used in the closure trace.

The positive Artin generator is drawn with braid height increasing upward; the left input strand ends on the right, and the right input strand passes over it:

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(current bounding box.center),scale=.8]
  \draw[->] (0,-1) -- (.46,-.08);
  \draw[->] (.54,.08) -- (1,1);
  \draw[->] (1,-1) .. controls (.72,-.5) and (.28,.5) .. (0,1);
  \node at (-.2,-1) {$i$};
  \node at (1.2,-1) {$i+1$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

The uninterrupted strand in the drawing is the overpassing strand. This is the crossing convention for the displayed matrix; the proof below uses its matrix entries and the half-ribbon source formulas, not the drawing.

facts:
**Given:** The generic parameter $A$, the basis $(v_+,v_-)$, and the two explicitly distinguished parameters $q_K=A^2$ and $q_L=A^{-2}$.

[F1] The Drinfeld–Jimbo presentation has $K E K^{-1}=q^2E$, $K F K^{-1}=q^{-2}F$, and $EF-FE=(K-K^{-1})/(q-q^{-1})$ in the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ case ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

[F2] In the library convention, $\Delta(E)=E\otimes K^{-1}+1\otimes E$, $\Delta(F)=F\otimes1+K\otimes F$, and the antipode is $S(E)=-EK$, $S(F)=-K^{-1}F$, $S(K)=K^{-1}$ ([[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]]).

[F3] A braiding is a natural isomorphism $c_{X,Y}:X\otimes Y\to Y\otimes X$ satisfying the two hexagon identities ([[def-braiding]]).

[F4] A ribbon twist is a natural automorphism satisfying $\theta_{X\otimes Y}=(\theta_X\otimes\theta_Y)\circ c_{Y,X}\circ c_{X,Y}$ and compatible with duality ([[def-twist-and-ribbon-structure]]).

[F5] In the generic two-dimensional module, Korinman's full-text §2.2 fixes $q_K=A^2$, the matrices of $E,F,K_K$, the half-ribbon matrix $C$, the positive braiding matrix, and the Kauffman-bracket quantum dimension $-q_K-q_K^{-1}$ ([Korinman, §2.2](https://msp.org/agt/2023/23-3/agt-v23-n3-p05-p.pdf)).

[F6] Snyder–Tingley Theorem 5.2 proves that the half-twist $\Omega$ makes the generic completed $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ representation category a topological half-ribbon category, with ribbon element $\Omega^{-2}$ and positive braiding induced by its $R$-matrix ([Snyder–Tingley, §5](https://msp.org/ant/2009/3-7/ant-v3-n7-p04-p.pdf)).

[F7] Absolute simplicity means $\operatorname{End}(V)=k'\operatorname{id}_V$ ([[def-absolutely-simple-object]]).

[F8] A left dual has evaluation $V^\vee\otimes V\to\mathbf1$ and coevaluation $\mathbf1\to V\otimes V^\vee$ satisfying both snake identities ([[def-left-dual-and-right-dual-object]]).

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be a field and let $\mathcal C$ be a $k$-linear ribbon category with $k$-bilinear tensor product and $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf1)=k$. Let $X$ be absolutely simple, so its twist is $\theta_X=\lambda\operatorname{id}_X$ for a unique $\lambda\in k^\times$. For $n\ge1$ and $\beta\in B_n$, let $t_n(\beta)$ be the value of the blackboard-framed $X$-colored closure and let $w(\beta)$ be the exponent sum, with positive Artin generator and positive stabilization conventions fixed as in the supplied ribbon-trace formulas. Then
$$J_X(\widehat\beta):=\lambda^{-w(\beta)}t_n(\beta)$$
depends only on the oriented unframed link type of $\widehat\beta$ when every component has color $X$. This statement makes no normalization by the categorical dimension.

facts:
**Given:** The Axiom of Choice; the $k$-linear ribbon category and absolutely simple color in the Statement; a braid $\beta\in B_n$ with $n\ge1$.

[F1] The braid evaluation is $t_n(\beta)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(j_{X^{\otimes n}}\rho_n(\beta))$, where $j=u\theta$ is the ribbon-induced pivotal comparison ([[def-ribbon-evaluation-of-an-x-colored-closed-braid]]).

[F2] Categorical trace is cyclic: $\operatorname{Tr}_L(ac)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(c^{\vee\vee}a)$ for the stated typed morphisms ([[thm-basic-properties-of-the-categorical-trace]]).

[F3] The two stabilization values are $t_{n+1}(\iota_n(\beta)\sigma_n^{\pm1})=\lambda^{\pm1}t_n(\beta)$ when positive stabilization closes to the positive curl ([[lem-scalar-twist-controls-the-two-markov-stabilizations]]).

[F4] The exponent sum is unchanged by conjugation and satisfies $w(\iota_n(\beta)\sigma_n^{\pm1})=w(\beta)\pm1$ ([[def-exponent-sum-and-writhe-of-a-braid]]).

[F5] Two braids have equivalent oriented closures exactly when they are related by conjugations, stabilizations, and destabilizations ([[thm-markovs-closed-braid-equivalence-theorem]]).

[F6] The Axiom of Choice implies countable choice ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]).

[A1] Absolute simplicity means $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(X)=k\operatorname{id}_X$, so each automorphism of $X$ is a unique nonzero scalar multiple of the identity ([[def-absolutely-simple-object]]).

[A2] The Axiom of Choice is the assumption that every family of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
An **effective field** is a field whose elements have finite encodings and whose exact addition, subtraction, multiplication, equality test, and inversion of nonzero elements are terminating procedures. Input a finite-dimensional strict matrix realization of a $k$-linear ribbon category with $\operatorname{End}(\mathbf1)=k$, finite-dimensional color objects with fixed bases, exact matrices for every braiding and inverse braiding used, duality and twist data, and the induced pivotal matrix $J_W$ for the tensor word $W=V_{a_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes V_{a_n}$. Also input a finite braid word $\beta$ on $n\ge1$ strands and the top color tuple $(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$. The matrices are assumed to satisfy the stated ribbon-category axioms; an implementation does not infer those axioms from arbitrary matrices.

Use the strand-position permutation homomorphism $\pi:B_n\to\operatorname{Sym}(\{1,\ldots,n\})$ given by $\pi(\sigma_i)=(i\ i+1)$. Read the braid letters in composition order, updating the current color tuple at each crossing by swapping its adjacent colors. For a positive letter $\sigma_i$, use the matrix of
$$1\otimes\cdots\otimes c_{V_{a_i},V_{a_{i+1}}}\otimes\cdots\otimes1,$$
and for a negative letter use its inverse. Let the blackboard-framed closure join the bottom and top endpoint at each position by the identity pairing. Reject the input if the final color tuple differs from the initial tuple: the tuple records the colors at the paired endpoints, so equality is exactly the condition that the closure carries a consistent color on every component. Starting with the identity matrix, multiply the typed crossing matrices in word order to obtain $M_\beta:W\to W$, then return
$$\operatorname{Tr}(J_WM_\beta)\in k.$$
This is the exact ribbon evaluation of the blackboard-framed colored braid closure in the given matrix realization. No algorithm is asserted for arbitrary abstract ribbon categories without effective finite matrix data.

facts:
**Given:** The effective field, valid finite-dimensional matrix ribbon data, the braid word, and its top color tuple.

[F1] The closed colored link is assigned the endomorphism of the tensor unit obtained from the ribbon-tangle evaluator ([[def-colored-framed-knot-evaluation-from-ribbon-category]]).

[F2] The multicolored evaluator assigns each crossing the correctly typed braiding or inverse, uses the chosen duality maps for cups and caps, and is invariant under framed isotopy ([[lem-multicolored-ribbon-coupon-evaluation]]).

[F3] The categorical trace of a morphism into the double dual is defined by composing the morphism with the duality evaluation and coevaluation maps ([[def-the-categorical-trace-of-a-morphism-into-the-double-dual]]).

[F4] For $n\ge2$, $B_n$ is generated by $\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_{n-1}$ with the Artin braid and distant-commutativity relations ([[def-braid-group-by-the-artin-presentation]]).

[F5] $\operatorname{Sym}(\{1,\ldots,n\})$ is the group of bijections of the strand-label set under composition, and $(i\ i+1)$ is the transposition interchanging $i$ and $i+1$ ([[def-symmetric-group]]).

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. For every integer $N\ge1$ and every finite braid word $\beta$ on $b\ge1$ strands whose closure is a knot, the normalized generic quotient
$$\lambda_N^{-w(\beta)}\frac{\operatorname{Tr}(G_N^{\otimes b}\rho_N(\beta))}{d_N}$$
belongs to $\mathbb Z[A^4,A^{-4}]$. Consequently there is a unique $J_N(K;q)\in\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ whose substitution $q=A^4$ equals that quotient. It is independent of the braid representative, has $J_N(\bigcirc;q)=1$, and agrees with the normalized colored Jones convention of Murakami’s explicit matrix definition in the variable $q$. Its value at every nonzero complex $q$, in particular $q_N=e^{2\pi i/N}$, means evaluation of this Laurent polynomial; it never means division by the specialized quantum dimension.

facts:
**Given:** Integers $N\ge1$, $b\ge1$, the knot-closing braid word $\beta$, and the two choice assumptions.

[F1] The generic matrices, nonzero $d_N$, scalar $\lambda_N$, absolute simplicity of $V_N$, representative independence under the choice hypotheses and unknot normalization are established in [[def-normalized-colored-jones-sequence]]. Their admissibility is proved, for every $N$, in [[lem-colored-jones-generic-ribbon-data]].

[F2] Symmetric Gaussian quotients $\begin{bmatrix}m\\r\end{bmatrix}_{q_K}$ are integral Laurent polynomials in $q_K$, and their Gauss product and alternating-sum identities hold ([[lem-quantum-pascal-recurrence-and-gaussian-integrality]]).

[F3] Under Countable Choice a colored framed tangle is evaluated by its ribbon matrices; compositions, tensor products and closures agree with their corresponding contractions ([[def-colored-framed-knot-evaluation-from-ribbon-category]], [[thm-a-ribbon-object-defines-a-unique-framed-tangle-evaluation-functor]], [[lem-ribbon-trace-equals-the-framed-closure-evaluation]]). Absolute simplicity says that every color endomorphism is a scalar ([[def-absolutely-simple-object]]).

[A1] The Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]).

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Choice and the prescribed generic matrix ribbon data for the $N$-dimensional color, where $N\ge1$. For every finite braid word $\beta$ on $n\ge1$ strands whose closure is a knot, the algorithm performs finitely many exact operations, including exactly one crossing-matrix update per letter and one finite pivotal-trace contraction, and returns the generic normalized value $J_N^{\mathrm{gen}}(\widehat\beta;q)$. If two such braid words close to the same oriented unframed knot, their returned generic values agree. The unique Laurent representative belongs to $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$, and its evaluation at any nonzero complex $q$ is defined, including at $q_N=e^{2\pi i/N}$.

facts:
**Given:** The Axiom of Choice, an integer $N\ge1$, the prescribed generic matrix ribbon data, a finite braid word $\beta$ of length $m$ on $n\ge1$ strands, and a knot closure.

[F1] The procedure forms the positive and inverse crossing matrices, calls the finite matrix ribbon evaluator, computes the exponent sum, and returns $\lambda_N^{-w(\beta)}t_N(\beta)/d_N$ over the exact field $\mathbb Q(A)$ ([[alg-colored-jones-from-ribbon-evaluation]]).

[F2] For valid finite-dimensional matrix data over an effective field and a color-preserving braid word of length $m$, the ribbon evaluator makes exactly $m$ crossing-matrix updates and one finite pivotal-trace contraction and returns the framed colored-braid value ([[thm-ribbon-evaluation-from-colored-braid-word-procedure-properties]]).

[F3] In the generic definition, $d_N\ne0$ in $\mathbb Q(A)$, $\lambda_N\ne0$, and $J_N^{\mathrm{gen}}=\lambda_N^{-w(\beta)}t_N(\beta)/d_N$ ([[def-normalized-colored-jones-sequence]]).

[F4] For an absolutely simple color with scalar twist $\lambda I$, the corrected framed trace $\lambda^{-w(\beta)}t_n(\beta)$ is invariant under conjugation and both Markov stabilizations when the Axiom of Choice is assumed ([[thm-twist-correction-removes-framing]]).

[F5] The framed ribbon-tangle evaluator is defined under Countable Choice ([[def-colored-framed-knot-evaluation-from-ribbon-category]]).

[F6] The Axiom of Choice implies Countable Choice ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]).

[F7] The quotient has a unique integral Laurent representative in $q=A^4$, proved by [[lem-colored-jones-generic-quotient-is-laurent]].

[A1] The Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

[A2] Countable Choice has its usual sequence-of-nonempty-sets meaning ([[def-countable-choice]]).

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: For every valid input of the colored-braid evaluation algorithm, where the braid word has $m$ letters and the total tensor-product dimension is $D$, the procedure terminates after exactly $m$ crossing-matrix updates and one finite pivotal-trace contraction. It returns the ribbon-category evaluation of that framed colored braid closure in the given matrix realization. The stated bound concerns the number of matrix updates; each update is a finite exact matrix multiplication over the effective field.

facts:
**Given:** A valid effective matrix input, a color-preserving braid word of length $m$, and the algorithm specified above.

[F1] The algorithm initializes the identity matrix, multiplies the typed positive or inverse braiding matrix for each word letter, checks final color preservation, and returns $\operatorname{Tr}(J_WM_\beta)$ ([[alg-ribbon-evaluation-from-colored-braid-word]]).

contract.heading: Open problem
contract.text:
Let $K$ be an oriented smooth knot in $S^3$, let $E_K$ be its compact exterior, and equip $\operatorname{int}(E_K)$ with a complete finite-volume hyperbolic metric $g$ having exactly one peripheral torus cusp. Write $\operatorname{Vol}_g(K)$ for its Riemannian volume. Let $J_N(K;q)\in\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ be the normalized $N$-dimensional colored Jones Laurent polynomial with $J_N(\bigcirc;q)=1$, in the variable $q=A^4$ declared in the generic color definition. Put $q_N=\exp(2\pi i/N)$. The conjecture is that $J_N(K;q_N)\ne0$ for all sufficiently large $N$ and that
$$\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N}\log|J_N(K;q_N)|=\operatorname{Vol}_g(K).$$
This is the real absolute-value formulation; the complex-volume refinement is a separate conjecture.

scope: Literal contract/Facts extraction only; accepted proof body not inspected.

contract.heading: Example

facts:
**Given:** The admissible generic color matrices, their normalization from the preceding definition, and the positive two-strand braid $\sigma_1^3$; for the general fundamental-color identity, assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice.

[F1] The generic matrix value is $J_N^{\mathrm{gen}}(\beta;q)=\lambda_N^{-w(\beta)}\operatorname{Tr}(G_N^{\otimes n}\rho_N(\beta))/d_N$, with $d_N\ne0$ in $\mathbb Q(A)$ ([[def-normalized-colored-jones-sequence]]).

[F2] For the fundamental ribbon color and any blackboard-framed braid closure, the ribbon trace satisfies $t_n(\beta)=\delta\langle\widehat\beta\rangle$, with $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$ and twist scalar $-A^3$; this statement assumes Countable Choice ([[lem-quantum-sl2-ribbon-trace-matches-hecke-and-bracket]]).

[F3] Under the Axiom of Choice, the library Jones polynomial satisfies $V_K(t)=f_K(t^{-1/4})$, where $f_K$ is the writhe-normalized Kauffman bracket and $t=A^{-4}$ ([[thm-bracket-state-sum-matches-library-jones-specialization]]).

[F4] Every braid group element is represented by a finite word in the Artin generators and their inverses, and under AC the Artin presentation identifies these words with geometric braid classes ([[def-braid-group-by-the-artin-presentation]], [[thm-the-artin-presentation-is-complete-for-geometric-braids]]).

[F5] A geometric braid closure joins each strand endpoint to the endpoint prescribed by its permutation ([[def-closure-of-a-geometric-braid]]).

[F6] The positive Artin half twist has determinant crossing sign $+1$ in the declared oriented projection ([[def-oriented-crossing-sign-writhe-and-blackboard-framing]]).

[F7] The opposite geometric half twist is the group inverse of the positive half twist ([[def-elementary-geometric-half-twist]]).

[F8] The exponent sum of a word is the sum of its signed generator exponents ([[def-exponent-sum-of-a-braid]]).

[F9] Under AC, every nonempty oriented link in $\mathbb R^3$ is equivalent to a closed geometric braid with at least one strand ([[thm-alexanders-closed-braid-theorem]]).

[A1] The Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

[A2] Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]).

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $r\ge0$ and $\tau>0$. In the one-dimensional Gaussian location experiment with parameter $\theta\in[-r,r]$, action space $\mathbb R$, observation density
$$p_{\theta,\tau}(y)=\frac{1}{\tau\sqrt{2\pi}}\exp\!\left(-\frac{(y-\theta)^2}{2\tau^2}\right)$$
with respect to Lebesgue measure, and squared-error loss, let $M(r,\tau)$ be the minimax expected risk over all measurable deterministic or randomized estimators. Put $b=\min\{r,\tau\}$ and take the prior assigning mass $1/2$ to each of $-b$ and $b$. The better of the estimators $y\mapsto0$ and $y\mapsto y$ has worst-case risk $T(r,\tau)=\min\{r^2,\tau^2\}$, and this prior has Bayes risk at least $T(r,\tau)/\sqrt{2e}$, so $M(r,\tau)\ge T(r,\tau)/\sqrt{2e}$.

facts:
[F1] [[def-ip-gaussian-sequence-inverse-model]]: A scalar coordinate in the positive-noise sequence experiment is a Gaussian location observation with positive variance; the coordinates are independent.

[F2] [[def-statistical-experiment]] and [[def-measurable-space]]: An experiment consists of a measurable sample space, a parameter set, and parameter-indexed sampling probabilities.

[F3] [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]] and [[def-lebesgue-measure-and-the-lebesgue-sigma-algebra]]: The scalar sample space uses the Borel sigma-algebra on $\mathbb R$ and its density is integrated against Lebesgue measure.

[F4] [[def-loss-function-and-risk]], [[def-randomized-procedure-as-a-markov-kernel]], and [[def-bayes-and-minimax-risk]]: Squared-error risk is the expected nonnegative loss; a randomized rule is a parameter-independent probability kernel from data to actions; minimax risk is the infimum of worst-case risks, and every supported prior has Bayes risk no larger than the minimax value.

[F5] [[def-hyperbolic-functions]]: $\cosh x=(\exp x+\exp(-x))/2$, $\tanh x=\sinh x/\cosh x$, and $\operatorname{sech}x=1/\cosh x$.

[F6] [[thm-hyperbolic-identities-and-derivatives]]: $\cosh$ is even, $\cosh x\ge1$, it is increasing on $[0,\infty)$, $(\tanh x)'=\operatorname{sech}^2x$, $(\cosh x)'=\sinh x$, and $(\operatorname{sech}x)'=-\operatorname{sech}x\tanh x$.

[F7] [[def-real-exponential-function-and-e]]: $e=\exp(1)$.

[F8] [[thm-gaussian-integral]]: $\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-x^2}\,dx=\sqrt{\pi}$.

[F9] [[thm-substitution]]: On compact intervals, a differentiable affine change of variable transforms the corresponding continuous-function integrals by its constant derivative.

[F10] [[thm-derivative-of-exponential]], [[thm-chain-rule]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], and [[cor-mean-value-theorem]]: The exponential, product and composition rules differentiate the displayed smooth functions, and a differentiable function's increment on an interval equals its derivative at an intermediate point times the interval length.

**Given:** $r\ge0$, $\tau>0$, the Gaussian location experiment, squared-error loss, and the endpoint prior specified in the Statement.

facts:
[A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: Countable Choice is assumed by the compact singular-system and spectral-power definitions.

[F1] [[def-ip-gaussian-sequence-inverse-model]]: The right singular vectors form a complete orthonormal basis of $N(K)^\perp$, and their coefficient map identifies that subspace isometrically with $\ell^2(\mathbb N,\mathbb R)$.

[F2] [[def-ip-power-source-set]]: $X_{\nu,\rho}(K)=\{|K|^\nu w:w\in X,\ \|w\|_X\le\rho\}$.

[F3] [[def-ip-statistical-ellipsoid-class]]: A weighted statistical ellipsoid is $\{\theta\in\ell^2:\sum_j a_j^2\theta_j^2\le Q^2\}$ for positive nondecreasing weights.

[F4] [[thm-singular-value-decomposition-for-compact-operators]]: $|K|v_j=s_jv_j$, and $(v_j)$ is a complete orthonormal basis of $N(K)^\perp$.

[F5] [[def-compact-spectral-filter-and-qualification]]: A compact spectral multiplier acts on each singular eigenspace by its scalar multiplier and vanishes on the kernel for a positive spectral power.

[F6] [[lem-ip-index-source-elements-are-minimum-norm]]: Every element of the power source ball lies in $N(K)^\perp$.

[F7] [[def-real-power]] and [[thm-real-power-laws]]: Positive-base real powers obey $(s_j^2)^{\nu/2}=s_j^\nu$ and $s_j^{-\nu}=1/s_j^\nu$; [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]] gives $(x^{-\nu})'=-\nu x^{-\nu-1}$ on $(0,\infty)$.

[F8] [[cor-mean-value-theorem]]: A function continuous on a closed interval and differentiable on its interior has increment equal to its derivative at an intermediate point times the interval length.

**Given:** Countable Choice, the compact real infinite-rank operator $K$, its fixed positive singular system $(s_j,v_j,u_j)$, and $\nu,\rho>0$.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $Q\in[0,\infty)$ and let $a=(a_j)_{j\in\mathbb N}$ be a nondecreasing sequence of positive real numbers, so $0<a_1\le a_2\le\cdots$. The statistical ellipsoid of radius $Q$ and weights $a$ in the Gaussian sequence inverse model is
$$\Theta_a(Q)=\left\{\theta\in\ell^2(\mathbb N,\mathbb R):\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}a_j^2\theta_j^2\le Q^2\right\}.$$
No assumption that $a_j\to\infty$ is included. In particular, this definition does not assert that the ellipsoid is compact in $\ell^2$.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume Countable Choice. Fix $\epsilon>0$, $Q\ge0$, a nonincreasing sequence $s_j>0$ with $s_j\to0$, and a nondecreasing sequence $a_j>0$. Observe $Z_j=\theta_j+\epsilon s_j^{-1}\xi_j$ for $j\ge1$, where the $\xi_j$ are independent standard normal variables, and let the unknown parameter range over
$$\Theta_a(Q)=\left\{\theta\in\ell^2(\mathbb N,\mathbb R):\sum_{j\ge1}a_j^2\theta_j^2\le Q^2\right\}.$$
Let $R_*(\epsilon)$ be the square root of the minimax expected squared $\ell^2$ error over all measurable deterministic or randomized estimators from the product Borel data space to $\ell^2$, and put
$$R_{\rm cut}(\epsilon)=\left[\inf_{D\in\mathbb N_0}\left\{\frac{Q^2}{a_{D+1}^2}+\epsilon^2\sum_{j=1}^{D}s_j^{-2}\right\}\right]^{1/2},\qquad\mathbb N_0=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}.$$
Then $R_*(\epsilon)\le R_{\rm cut}(\epsilon)\le2.2R_*(\epsilon)$.

facts:
[A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: Countable Choice is assumed by the compact SVD and complete-basis coordinate identification used by the Gaussian sequence model.

[F1] [[def-ip-gaussian-sequence-inverse-model]]: $Z_j=\theta_j+\epsilon s_j^{-1}\xi_j$ for independent standard normal coordinates, with parameter $\theta\in\ell^2(\mathbb N,\mathbb R)$ and data in the product Borel space $\mathbb R^\mathbb N$.

[F2] [[def-ip-statistical-ellipsoid-class]]: $\Theta_a(Q)=\{\theta\in\ell^2:\sum_{j\ge1}a_j^2\theta_j^2\le Q^2\}$, where $0<a_1\le a_2\le\cdots$; no divergence assumption on $a_j$ is made.

[F3] [[alg-ip-svd-truncated-estimator]]: For $D\in\mathbb N_0$, the cutoff estimator retains $Z_j$ for $j\le D$ and sets the other coordinates to zero.

[F4] [[thm-ip-truncated-estimator-exact-risk]]: Its proof establishes, for each $\theta\in\Theta_a(Q)$, $R_\theta(D)=\epsilon^2\sum_{j=1}^{D}s_j^{-2}+\sum_{j>D}\theta_j^2$; taking the supremum gives $Q^2/a_{D+1}^2+\epsilon^2\sum_{j=1}^{D}s_j^{-2}$, with the empty sum zero at $D=0$.

[F5] [[lem-ip-univariate-gaussian-projection-minimax-comparison]]: In a scalar coordinate with noise standard deviation $\tau$ and interval half-width $r$, the prior on $\{-b,b\}$, $b=\min(r,\tau)$, has Bayes risk at least $\min(r^2,\tau^2)/\sqrt{2e}$.

[F6] [[def-loss-function-and-risk]], [[def-randomized-procedure-as-a-markov-kernel]], and [[def-bayes-and-minimax-risk]]: Risk is expected nonnegative loss, a randomized rule is a parameter-independent kernel from data to actions, minimax risk is the infimum of worst-case risks, and the average risk under any supported prior is no greater than worst-case risk.

[F7] [[def-real-exponential-function-and-e]], [[def-factorial-and-falling-factorial]], and [[thm-geometric-series]]: $e=\sum_{n\ge0}1/n!$ and $\sum_{k\ge0}3^{-k}=3/2$.

[F8] [[lem-finite-measure-uniqueness-on-a-pi-system]]: Finite probability measures agreeing on a generating pi-system of cylinder sets agree on the generated product Borel sigma-algebra.

[F9] [[thm-euclidean-heine-borel-pseudocompactness-and-extreme-values]]: A continuous real-valued function on a nonempty closed bounded subset of finite-dimensional Euclidean space attains its maximum and minimum.

[F10] [[thm-continuous-preimages-of-borel-sets-are-borel]]: A continuous map has Borel preimages of Borel sets; $(\theta,a)\mapsto\|\theta-a\|_{\ell^2}^2$ is continuous and hence Borel measurable, and a finite-coordinate cutoff rule is Borel measurable.

**Given:** Countable Choice, the positive-noise Gaussian sequence experiment, $Q\ge0$, positive nonincreasing singular numbers $s_j\to0$, positive nondecreasing ellipsoid weights $a_j$, and the RMS minimax value $R_*(\epsilon)$ over all measurable deterministic or randomized rules.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Input a normalized sequence observation $z=(z_j)_{j\in\mathbb N}\in\mathbb R^{\mathbb N}$ from the Gaussian sequence inverse model and a cutoff $D\in\mathbb N_0$, where $\mathbb N_0=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$. Output the finite-support estimate $\widehat\theta_D(z)\in\ell^2(\mathbb N,\mathbb R)$ defined by
$$\widehat\theta_{D,j}(z)=\begin{cases}z_j,&1\le j\le D,\\0,&j>D.\end{cases}$$
For $D=0$ the output is the zero sequence.

scope: Literal contract/Facts extraction only; accepted proof body not inspected.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume Countable Choice and let $\epsilon\ge0$. In the Gaussian sequence inverse model with positive singular numbers $(s_j)_{j\in\mathbb N}$, let $Q\ge0$ and let $(a_j)_{j\in\mathbb N}$ be positive and nondecreasing. For each $\theta\in\Theta_a(Q)$, define the squared sequence risk of the cutoff estimator at $D\in\mathbb N_0$ by
$$R_\theta(D):=\mathbb E_\theta\!\left[\|\widehat\theta_D(Z)-\theta\|_{\ell^2}^2\right].$$
Then its exact worst-case squared sequence risk is
$$\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_a(Q)}R_\theta(D)=\frac{Q^2}{a_{D+1}^2}+\epsilon^2\sum_{j=1}^{D}s_j^{-2},$$
where the sum is $0$ for $D=0$. The supremum is attained by the one-coordinate truth $\theta^\star=(Q/a_{D+1})e_{D+1}$, with $\theta^\star=0$ when $Q=0$.

facts:
[F1] [[def-ip-gaussian-sequence-inverse-model]]: For $\epsilon>0$, $Z_j=\theta_j+\epsilon s_j^{-1}\xi_j$ with $\mathbb E\xi_j=0$ and $\mathbb E\xi_j^2=1$; at $\epsilon=0$, $Z_j=\theta_j$ deterministically.

[F2] [[def-ip-statistical-ellipsoid-class]]: $\theta\in\Theta_a(Q)$ means $\theta\in\ell^2$ and $\sum_{j\ge1}a_j^2\theta_j^2\le Q^2$, with $0<a_1\le a_2\le\cdots$.

[F3] [[alg-ip-svd-truncated-estimator]]: $\widehat\theta_{D,j}(Z)=Z_j$ for $1\le j\le D$ and $0$ for $j>D$.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: Countable Choice is assumed only for the upstream compact SVD coordinate identification; it is not used in the finite-coordinate risk calculation.

**Given:** Countable Choice, $\epsilon\ge0$, positive singular numbers $(s_j)$, a cutoff $D\in\mathbb N_0$, and the ellipsoid $\Theta_a(Q)$ with positive nondecreasing weights.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume Countable Choice, $Q>0$, and $p,\kappa>0$. As $\epsilon\downarrow0$, the minimax RMS error over $\Theta_a(Q)$ has the following order-sharp rates: if $s_j\asymp j^{-p}$ and $a_j\asymp j^\kappa$, then $R_*(\epsilon)\asymp\epsilon^{\kappa/(\kappa+p+1/2)}$; if $s_j\asymp e^{-pj}$ and $a_j\asymp j^\kappa$, then $R_*(\epsilon)\asymp[\log(1/\epsilon)]^{-\kappa}$; if $s_j\asymp j^{-p}$ and $a_j\asymp e^{\kappa j}$, then $R_*(\epsilon)\asymp\epsilon[\log(1/\epsilon)]^{p+1/2}$; and if $s_j\asymp e^{-pj}$ and $a_j\asymp e^{\kappa j}$, then $R_*(\epsilon)\asymp\epsilon^{\kappa/(p+\kappa)}$. Here $u_j\asymp v_j$ as $j\to\infty$ or $f(\epsilon)\asymp g(\epsilon)$ as $\epsilon\downarrow0$ means the ratio is bounded above and below by positive constants on the indicated tail; the constants may depend on $Q,p,\kappa$ and the axis comparison constants.

facts:
[A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: Countable Choice is inherited through the compact SVD coordinate model.

[F1] [[def-ip-gaussian-sequence-inverse-model]] and [[def-ip-statistical-ellipsoid-class]]: The observation coordinates are $Z_j=\theta_j+\epsilon s_j^{-1}\xi_j$ and the parameter set is $\Theta_a(Q)=\{\theta\in\ell^2:\sum_j a_j^2\theta_j^2\le Q^2\}$ with positive nondecreasing weights.

[F2] [[thm-ip-truncated-estimator-exact-risk]]: At cutoff $D\in\mathbb N_0$, the exact worst-case expected squared risk is $B_D=Q^2/a_{D+1}^2+\epsilon^2\sum_{j=1}^D s_j^{-2}$.

[F3] [[thm-ip-general-source-minimax-comparison]]: The minimax RMS error satisfies $R_*(\epsilon)\le(\inf_D B_D)^{1/2}\le2.2R_*(\epsilon)$.

[F4] [[def-natural-logarithm]] and [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]]: $\log$ is the inverse of $\exp$ on positive reals, is increasing, and obeys $\log(xy)=\log x+\log y$.

[F5] [[def-real-power]], [[thm-real-power-laws]], and [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]]: Positive-base real powers obey the exponent laws and $x^\alpha$ is increasing for $\alpha>0$.

[F6] [[thm-geometric-series]] and [[thm-exponential-is-strictly-increasing]]: For $p>0$, the geometric sums of $e^{2pj}$ are bounded above and below by positive constants times their final term.

[F7] [[thm-exponential-beats-every-polynomial]]: $x/\exp(x)\to0$ as $x\to+\infty$.

**Given:** $Q>0$, $p,\kappa>0$, positive nonincreasing singular values $s_j\to0$, positive nondecreasing weights $a_j$, and a positive noise level $\epsilon$ tending to zero.

contract.heading: Example
contract.text: Assume Countable Choice, take $Q>0$ and Sobolev-type weights $a_j\asymp j$ in the Gaussian sequence inverse model. If the singular values satisfy $s_j\asymp j^{-1}$, the minimax RMS error is of order $\epsilon^{2/5}$ as $\epsilon\downarrow0$; if instead $s_j\asymp e^{-j}$, it is of order $[\log(1/\epsilon)]^{-1}$. The comparison constants may depend on the fixed ellipsoid and axis constants.

facts:
[F1] [[cor-ip-mild-and-severe-estimation-rates]]: For polynomial singular values and polynomial ellipsoid weights, $R_*\asymp\epsilon^{\kappa/(\kappa+p+1/2)}$; for exponential singular values and polynomial weights, $R_*\asymp[\log(1/\epsilon)]^{-\kappa}$.

[F2] [[def-ip-gaussian-sequence-inverse-model]] and [[def-ip-statistical-ellipsoid-class]]: The model uses the positive singular sequence and the parameter class $\sum_j a_j^2\theta_j^2\le Q^2$.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: Countable Choice is inherited from the sequence model.

**Given:** Countable Choice, $Q>0$, $p=\kappa=1$, and either the polynomial or exponential singular-value regime in the Example.

contract.heading: Example
contract.text: Assume Countable Choice and let $Q=\rho>0$, $\nu=1$, and $K$ be a compact real infinite-rank operator. Over its minimum-norm power source ball $X_{1,\rho}(K)$, if $s_j\asymp j^{-1}$ then the minimax RMS error in the Gaussian sequence inverse model is of order $\epsilon^{2/5}$; if $s_j\asymp e^{-j}$ then it is of order $\epsilon^{1/2}$ as $\epsilon\downarrow0$. The constants may depend on $\rho$ and the fixed singular-value comparison constants.

facts:
[F1] [[lem-ip-power-source-class-as-statistical-ellipsoid]]: $X_{\nu,\rho}(K)$ has ellipsoid weights $a_j=s_j^{-\nu}$ and radius $Q=\rho$.

[F2] [[cor-ip-mild-and-severe-estimation-rates]]: For polynomial singular values with polynomial axes, the rate is $\epsilon^{\kappa/(\kappa+p+1/2)}$; for exponential singular values with exponential axes, the rate is $\epsilon^{\kappa/(p+\kappa)}$.

[F3] [[def-ip-power-source-set]] and [[def-ip-gaussian-sequence-inverse-model]]: The source class is $X_{\nu,\rho}(K)=\{|K|^\nu w:\|w\|_X\le\rho\}$ in the real Gaussian sequence inverse model.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: Countable Choice is inherited through the compact singular system.

**Given:** Countable Choice, $\rho>0$, $\nu=1$, and either $s_j\asymp j^{-1}$ or $s_j\asymp e^{-j}$.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented diagram of a link with $n_+$ positive crossings, $n_-$ negative crossings, writhe $w=n_+-n_-$, and $n=n_++n_-$. For each resolution state $v$, let $k(v)$ be its number of circles and let $D_v$ use the A-smoothing at coordinates $0$ and B-smoothing at coordinates $1$. Put $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$ and define the normalized bracket
$$f_D(A):=(-A^3)^{-w}\sum_{v:C(D)\to\{0,1\}} A^{n-2|v|}\delta^{k(v)-1}.$$
For integral unreduced Khovanov cohomology, define $\chi_q(Kh(D))=\sum_{i,j}(-1)^i\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Z}Kh^{i,j}(D)q^j$. For reduced cohomology use its basepoint quantum grading $\widetilde j$ and define $\widetilde\chi_q=\sum_{i,\widetilde j}(-1)^i\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Z}\widetilde{Kh}^{i,\widetilde j}(D,p)q^{\widetilde j}$. Under $q=-A^{-2}$ and $t=q^2=A^{-4}$,
$$\chi_q(Kh(D))=(q+q^{-1})f_D(A),\qquad \widetilde\chi_q(D,p)=f_D(A).$$
Thus the unreduced unknot factor is $q+q^{-1}$ and the reduced unknot factor is $1$.

facts:
**Given:** A finite oriented link diagram, its ordered Khovanov state cube, and the integral unreduced and based reduced cochain complexes.

[F1] The Kauffman state sum is $\langle D\rangle=\sum_v A^{n-2|v|}(-A^2-A^{-2})^{k(v)-1}$, with each state using the prescribed A/B smoothing chart ([[def-kauffman-bracket-smoothing-and-loop-value]]).

[F2] The writhe is the sum of crossing signs, so $w=n_+-n_-$ ([[def-oriented-crossing-sign-writhe-and-blackboard-framing]]).

[F3] A state with circle labels $1,X$ has cohomological degree $i=|v|-n_-$ and quantum degree $j=|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum\deg(a)$; $\deg(1)=1$, $\deg(X)=-1$, and edge maps preserve $j$ ([[def-khovanov-frobenius-algebra-and-cube-of-resolutions]]).

[F4] The reduced state module kills the based-circle $X$ label and subtracts one from the original quantum degree, so the surviving based label $1$ contributes degree zero ([[def-reduced-khovanov-cohomology-of-a-knot]]).

[F5] The Khovanov procedure returns a bounded bigraded cochain complex with finite-rank free state groups ([[thm-khovanov-chain-complex-from-diagram-procedure-properties]]).
