contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $V_L(t)$ be the library Jones polynomial of a nonempty oriented link $L$, normalized by $V_{\bigcirc}(t)=1$. For every diagram $D$ of $L$, put $q=-A^{-2}$ and $t=q^2=A^{-4}$. Then the integral rank Euler characteristics satisfy
$$\sum_{i,j}(-1)^i\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Z}Kh^{i,j}(L)q^j=(q+q^{-1})V_L(t).$$
If $L=K$ is a knot with any basepoint $p$ away from the crossings, then
$$\sum_{i,\widetilde j}(-1)^i\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Z}\widetilde{Kh}^{i,\widetilde j}(K,p)q^{\widetilde j}=V_K(t).$$
The unreduced factor $q+q^{-1}$ and reduced factor $1$ are the respective unknot normalizations.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, a nonempty oriented link $L$, its finite-diagram complexes, and the library Jones polynomial.

[A1] Full AC means every family of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

[F1] Full AC implies AC$_\omega$ ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]).

[F2] For a fixed finite diagram $D$, the integral rank Euler sums of its Khovanov cohomology are $(q+q^{-1})f_D(A)$ unreduced and $f_D(A)$ reduced, where $q=-A^{-2}$ and $f_D$ is the writhe-normalized state sum ([[lem-khovanov-graded-euler-characteristic-jones-normalization]]).

[F3] Under full AC, the normalized bracket state sum equals the library Jones polynomial at $t=A^{-4}$ ([[thm-bracket-state-sum-matches-library-jones-specialization]]).

[F4] Under AC$_\omega$, the unreduced groups are independent of the diagram, and the reduced groups of a knot are independent of the diagram and basepoint ([[thm-khovanov-homology-is-an-oriented-link-invariant]], [[thm-reduced-khovanov-basepoint-and-reidemeister-invariance]]).

contract.heading: Statement refuted
contract.text: For every finite regular oriented diagram $D$, form the integral Khovanov state cube but omit the cohomological shift $-n_-$ and quantum shift $n_+-2n_-$. The false claim is that the resulting raw cohomology groups are invariant under oriented Reidemeister moves and that their graded rank Euler characteristic equals the Jones polynomial with the usual unreduced unknot factor $q+q^{-1}$, under $q=-A^{-2}$ and $t=q^2=A^{-4}$.

facts:
**Given:** The crossingless unknot, its positive and negative one-crossing curls, and the raw cube with both normalization shifts omitted.

[F1] The algebra $\mathcal A$ has basis $1,X$ in quantum degrees $1,-1$, and the edge operations are $m$ and $\Delta$ with the displayed values ([[def-khovanov-frobenius-algebra-and-cube-of-resolutions]]).

[F2] In the declared smoothing chart, the positive one-crossing curl has a two-circle $0$-resolution and one-circle $1$-resolution joined by $m$; the negative curl has one-circle $0$-resolution and a two-circle $1$-resolution joined by $\Delta$ ([[def-kauffman-bracket-smoothing-and-loop-value]], [[def-oriented-crossing-sign-writhe-and-blackboard-framing]], [[alg-khovanov-chain-complex-from-diagram]]).

[F3] A crossingless one-circle diagram has a unique state with no differential ([[alg-khovanov-chain-complex-from-diagram]]).

[F4] Each oriented type-I curl is realized by an ambient isotopy, so the curled diagram and the crossingless diagram represent the same oriented unknot ([[def-oriented-reidemeister-moves]], [[lem-each-oriented-reidemeister-move-is-realized-by-ambient-isotopy]]).

[F5] The signed cube differential squares to zero, and the raw cube is a bounded complex of finite-rank free abelian groups ([[lem-khovanov-cube-differential-squares-to-zero]], [[thm-khovanov-chain-complex-from-diagram-procedure-properties]]).

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume countable choice. Let $S\subset S^3\times[0,1]$ be a compact smooth properly embedded oriented surface, with product collars and boundary the finite oriented links $-L_0$ and $L_1$ in the two ends. Components of $S$ and either boundary link may be empty. After an ambient isotopy fixed on smaller prescribed end collars, $S$ has a finite movie consisting of planar isotopies, oriented Reidemeister moves R1, R2 and R3, births, oriented saddle band moves, and deaths. All exceptional times are distinct. The movie's actual smoothly embedded trace is ambient isotopic to the given $S$ relative to those collars, with its boundary orientations and parametrizations retained. Prescribed regular endpoint diagrams may be retained. This is movie existence; it asserts no equivalence theorem for two movies.

facts:
**Given:** Countable choice, the compact collared smooth surface $S$, and any prescribed regular endpoint diagrams.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]] is used in Sard, transversality, the regular-band flow and isotopy extension. All surface charts and slabs selected after compactness are finite.

[F1] [[thm-parametric-transversality]] supplies good parameters for a finite-dimensional family whose evaluation is transverse. [[lem-manifold-bump-for-a-compact-set-inside-an-open-set]] supplies supported chart bumps. A differential transverse to the zero section has invertible Hessian at its zeros; this is also the coordinate calculation used below.

[F2] [[cor-a-morse-function-on-a-compact-manifold-has-finitely-many-critical-points]] and [[lem-separating-critical-values-far-from-the-boundary]] supply finiteness and distinct values. [[thm-morse-lemma]] supplies the quadratic forms at these points.

[F3] [[lem-normalized-gradient-crosses-a-compact-regular-band-in-controlled-time]] trivializes a compact band with no critical point by a flow satisfying $dh(X)=1$.

[F4] [[lem-a-smooth-isotopy-of-links-can-be-put-in-general-position]] supplies arbitrarily small perturbations of a link isotopy, fixed on stationary regular ends, with finitely many distinct ordinary cusp, double-tangency and triple events and no higher events. Its proof controls independent finite jets and excludes accumulation at deleted source diagonals. [[lem-a-generic-isotopy-of-links-has-only-reidemeister-singular-times]] identifies exactly R1, R2 and R3, with their actual over/under orders and orientations.

[F5] [[lem-every-oriented-link-admits-a-regular-projection]] supplies finite regular diagrams. [[thm-morse-sard-for-smooth-manifolds]] makes the image of a smooth surface in $S^3$ null. [[thm-isotopy-extension]] extends compact embedding isotopies under countable choice. For an isotopy fixed near part of the source, its velocity is zero there; the extension can be cut off away from a smaller such neighbourhood.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume countable choice. Let $F\subset B^4\subset\mathbb R^4$ be a compact connected oriented smoothly properly embedded surface of genus $g$, with its supplied smooth boundary collar and oriented boundary the knot $K\subset S^3$. There is an orientation-preserving ambient diffeomorphism $\Psi:B^4\to B^4$ equal to the identity on a neighborhood of the outer boundary, and $0<\varepsilon<1$, such that $\Psi(F)\cap B^4_\varepsilon$ is exactly a flat two-disk in a plane through $0$. The surface $\Psi(F)\setminus\operatorname{int}B^4_\varepsilon$, in the explicitly round shell $B^4\setminus\operatorname{int}B^4_\varepsilon\cong S^3\times[0,1]$, is a connected smooth oriented knot cobordism between $K$ and a standard unknot, with genus $g$ and Euler characteristic $-2g$. Both boundary components have product collars in a shell identification fixing $K$ and the inner sphere. The ambient diffeomorphism $\Psi$ fixes a sufficiently small restriction of the supplied outer collar; the shell coordinates may be adjusted there to make that surface collar a product. No assertion about the complement of an arbitrary embedded four-ball is used.

facts:
**Given:** Countable choice and the compact smoothly embedded surface in the unit Euclidean ball.

[F1] Compact embedding isotopies extend to ambient isotopies supported in any prescribed neighborhood of their tracks, under countable choice. The source may have boundary, and no endpoint stationarity is required by clause4 ([[thm-isotopy-extension]]).

[F2] Smooth proper surface charts, the supplied smooth boundary collar and its restrictions have the meaning specified in [[def-locally-flat-proper-surface-and-concordance-collars]].

[F3] The smooth Euclidean inverse function theorem holds without choice ([[lem-choice-free-smooth-inverse-function-theorem-in-euclidean-space]]). Apply it to projection from a smooth surface chart for the local graph, and to the map sending a collar chart to its boundary parameter and radial coordinate for the collar reparametrization. At a boundary point use the smooth chart extension and restrict its inverse to the half-space.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]] is the precise axiom inherited from [F1].

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text: Assume countable choice. Let $K_0,K_1\subset S^3$ be smooth oriented knots. A smooth oriented knot cobordism from $K_0$ to $K_1$ is a compact smooth properly embedded oriented surface $\Sigma\subset S^3\times[0,1]$ whose boundary is $(-K_0\times\{0\})\sqcup(K_1\times\{1\})$, with product collars at both ends. A **generic movie** for $\Sigma$ is obtained by choosing a generic projection of the slices $S^3\times\{t\}$ to the plane and a Morse height function on $\Sigma$, then recording the oriented link diagram at each regular level. Intermediate regular levels may be links with any finite number of components. After choosing the projection and height generically, the finitely many exceptional levels are isolated and distinct: between them the diagrams change by planar isotopy or one oriented Reidemeister move, and at them the surface height has one nondegenerate minimum (a birth), one nondegenerate maximum (a death), or one index-one critical point (a saddle band move). A movie includes its ordered list of frames and these elementary changes; no claim that two movies of the same cobordism are equivalent is part of this definition.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: The integral signed Khovanov cubes have the local graded cancellation models described below. They are chain homotopy equivalences over every fixed exterior resolution, commute with exterior saddle differentials, and commute with multiplication by $X$ at every marked point outside the local disk. Consequently they also give chain homotopy equivalences after taking the reduced quotient. For the crossing with A-smoothing the identity matching and B-smoothing the cap-cup matching, the two three-crossing braid cubes with words $121$ and $212$ retract to the same three-term complex. The two-crossing inverse-pair cube retracts to the identity matching in local cohomological degree one and quantum shift upward by one. All retractions are integral; their homotopies and the two cancellations in the three-crossing cube are specified in the proof.

facts:
**Given:** The algebra $A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$, its Frobenius maps, and cube signs $(-1)^{\sum_{a<j}v_a}$, with local crossings ordered before exterior crossings.

[F1] The Frobenius maps and their basis values are those of [[def-khovanov-frobenius-algebra-and-cube-of-resolutions]]. The corresponding signed cubes square to zero by [[lem-khovanov-cube-differential-squares-to-zero]].

[F2] In the reduced quotient the distinguished component has module $M=\mathbb Z$, with $X=0$, $m_M(1\otimes u)=u$, $m_M(X\otimes u)=0$ and $\Delta_M(u)=X\otimes u$ ([[def-reduced-khovanov-cohomology-of-a-knot]]).

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. If $D$ and $D'$ are finite regular diagrams of the same nonempty oriented link, then their rational Lee cochain complexes are related by a cochain homotopy equivalence whose maps and homotopies preserve the decreasing quantum filtrations after normalization. Consequently their Lee homology groups with induced filtrations are isomorphic, and the spectral sequences from the rational Khovanov page onward are isomorphic. These filtered groups and pages therefore depend only on the oriented link.

facts:
**Given:** $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, two finite oriented diagrams of the same link, and their Lee complexes with normalized gradings.

[F1] The rational Lee saddle maps differ from the degree-preserving Khovanov maps only by terms that raise quantum degree by $4$ ([[def-lee-deformed-khovanov-complex]]).

[F2] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, diagrams of the same oriented link are related by finitely many planar isotopies and oriented Reidemeister I, II, and III moves ([[thm-oriented-reidemeister-equivalence-theorem]]).

[F3] The signed local cancellation coordinates, inverse blocks, and homotopies for the two-crossing and three-crossing cubes are explicit in [[lem-khovanov-signed-local-cancellation-models]].

[F4] In the signed Reidemeister II model, the four state modules retract by explicit identity pivots to the identity matching in local cohomological degree one and quantum shift upward by one; the two Reidemeister III cubes cancel to a common three-term complex ([[lem-khovanov-signed-local-cancellation-models]]).

[F5] Cochain homotopy equivalence induces cohomology isomorphisms ([[def-chain-homotopy-equivalence]]).

[F6] The associated-graded Lee differential is the integral Khovanov differential, and its filtered spectral sequence has rational Khovanov cohomology as its homology page ([[lem-lee-filtered-spectral-sequence-and-two-orientation-classes]]).

[A1] $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is the axiom that every countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-countable-choice]]).

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For every finite regular based oriented knot diagram, the odd exterior-algebra cube admits a square-compatible edge assignment and defines a bigraded cochain complex; its mod-2 reduction is chain homotopy equivalent as a marked $\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)$-complex to the Bar–Natan complex reduced modulo $(2,h)$. After inverting $h$, the Bar–Natan complex is chain homotopy equivalent to one free rank-one module in cohomological degree $0$ and odd quantum degree over the localized coefficient algebra. Based diagram changes preserve the odd complex up to chain homotopy equivalence, and pointed connected sums give the chain-level tensor product over $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$ for the odd complex and over $\mathbb R=\mathbb Z[h,X]/(X^2-hX)$ for the Bar–Natan complex, in each case with the quantum shift $\{-1\}$.

facts:
**Given:** Countable choice, the finite based diagram, and the coefficient rings and state modules.

[F1] The odd and Bar–Natan state maps, gradings and right marked actions are defined in [[def-odd-khovanov-barnatan-and-leo-triple]].

[F2] Full oriented face prescriptions, constructive integral edge signs and marked vertex-sign comparison are proved in [[lem-odd-cube-oriented-face-parity-and-sign-existence]].

[F3] Complete marked RI/RII contractions and the two-pivot signed RIII common complex are proved in [[lem-odd-marked-reidemeister-i-ii-contractions]] and [[lem-odd-marked-reidemeister-iii-common-complex]].

[F4] The based odd/BN movie maps, their common reduction, and the localized rank-one knot retraction are proved in [[lem-based-odd-barnatan-movie-maps-and-localized-concordances]].

[F5] The fully admissible marked tensor-product isomorphisms are proved in [[lem-pointed-odd-barnatan-tensor-product-over-marked-rings]].

[F6] Integral odd and Bar–Natan pointed spherical recharting isomorphisms, including the complete zero-face cyclic-order calculation and exact common reduction, are proved in [[lem-pointed-spherical-recharting-preserves-odd-barnatan-complexes]].

[F7] Every prescribed based diagram has the explicit protected germ normalization and spherical long endpoint presentation of [[lem-based-planar-diagrams-admit-spherical-long-endpoint-presentations]].

[F8] [[lem-marked-knot-isotopies-admit-protected-reidemeister-movies]] proves relative R-only comparison for common compatible long endpoints, including the actual common puncture/closure endpoint planar isotopies and the relative center–tangent contraction that makes its ambient coordinates identity in both end collars.

[F9] [[lem-marked-knot-concordances-admit-finite-movies-away-from-the-mark]] proves a finite protected marked movie for a collared annulus with a specified proper marked arc, retaining compatible long endpoints and recording all spatial coordinate identifications.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For every nonempty oriented link $L$, the bigraded integral groups $Kh^{i,j}(L):=H^i(C^{*,j}(D))$, where $D$ is any finite regular oriented diagram of $L$ and $C(D)$ is the normalized Khovanov cochain complex, are independent of the choice of $D$ up to bigraded isomorphism.

facts:
**Given:** AC$_\omega$, two finite regular diagrams of the same oriented link, and their normalized cochain complexes.

[F1] AC$_\omega$ is the axiom that every countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-countable-choice]]).

[F2] Under AC$_\omega$, diagrams of the same oriented link are connected by a finite sequence of planar isotopies and oriented Reidemeister I, II, and III moves ([[thm-oriented-reidemeister-equivalence-theorem]]).

[F3] Every planar isotopy and oriented Reidemeister I, II or III move induces a bigraded chain homotopy equivalence of the normalized complexes ([[lem-khovanov-reidemeister-chain-homotopies]]).

[F4] A bounded cochain complex has defined cohomology in each bidegree, and chain homotopy equivalent complexes induce isomorphic cohomology ([[thm-khovanov-chain-complex-from-diagram-procedure-properties]], [[def-chain-homotopy-equivalence]]).

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text: An oriented circle is a smooth one-dimensional manifold diffeomorphic to the standard oriented circle. An abstract oriented cobordism from an oriented circle $C_0$ to an oriented circle $C_1$ is a compact oriented smooth surface $F$ together with orientation-preserving identifications of its incoming and outgoing boundary components such that $\partial F=-C_0\sqcup C_1$. Here $-C_0$ denotes the same circle with its orientation reversed. The cobordism is abstract: no embedding of $F$, $C_0$, or $C_1$ into a common three- or four-manifold is included in the data.

scope: Literal contract/Facts extraction only; accepted proof body not inspected.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ be an oriented knot admitting a finite regular diagram $D$ with $n$ positive crossings and no negative crossings, and let $k$ be the number of circles in its oriented resolution. Then Rasmussen’s invariant satisfies
$$
s(K)=n-k+1.
$$

facts:
**Given:** $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and a positive diagram $D$ of the knot $K$.

[F1] The canonical orientation class is a basis vector in Lee homology, and its filtration level is $s_{\min}(K)$ ([[thm-lee-homology-of-a-knot-has-two-generators]], [[lem-lee-filtered-spectral-sequence-and-two-orientation-classes]]).

[F2] Rasmussen's convention is $s(K)=s_{\min}(K)+1$ ([[def-rasmussen-s-invariant]]).

[F3] In the normalized Lee complex, a state with $|v|$ one-resolutions and labels $1,X$ has quantum degree $|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum\deg_q(a)$ ([[def-lee-deformed-khovanov-complex]]).

[A1] $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is inherited through the diagram-independent definition of $s$ ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-rasmussen-s-invariant]]).

[A2] The crossing-sign convention has $n_-=0$ for a positive diagram, and its oriented smoothing at each crossing is the $0$-resolution ([[def-oriented-crossing-sign-writhe-and-blackboard-framing]], [[def-khovanov-frobenius-algebra-and-cube-of-resolutions]]).
scope: Literal contract/Facts extraction only; accepted proof body not inspected.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice.

Let $K^\dagger$ be the reverse mirror of an oriented knot $K$. Then
$$
s(K^\dagger)=-s(K).
$$

facts:
**Given:** A finite regular diagram $D$ of $K$.

[F1] The normalized Lee cube has state quantum degree $|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum\deg_q(a)$ and the deformation differential preserves or raises this grading ([[def-lee-deformed-khovanov-complex]]).

[F2] For a knot, the two extremal Lee filtration levels differ by $2$, with $s=s_{\max}-1=s_{\min}+1$ ([[thm-lee-homology-of-a-knot-has-two-generators]], [[def-rasmussen-s-invariant]]).

[F3] The reverse mirror is obtained by the fixed orientation-reversing reflection followed by reversal of the knot orientation ([[def-reverse-mirror-of-oriented-knot]]).

[A1] $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is the axiom branch inherited from diagram independence of Lee filtration levels ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-rasmussen-s-invariant]]).

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Local-equivalence classes of LEO triples form an abelian group under the shifted tensor product
$$
(C,D,f)\otimes(C',D',f')=(C\otimes_{\mathbb A}C'\{-1\},\ D\otimes_{\mathbb R}D'\{-1\},\ f\otimes f'),
$$
with identity the unknot triple and inverse the shifted graded dual. The assignment sending a smooth oriented knot to its odd/Bar–Natan LEO triple is a well-defined homomorphism from the smooth knot concordance group to this abelian group.

facts:
**Given:** $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and the class of LEO triples from the Definition.

[F1] A local map consists of compatible module chain maps on the odd and Bar–Natan complexes, with the Bar–Natan map becoming a homotopy equivalence after inverting $h$ ([[def-odd-khovanov-barnatan-and-leo-triple]]).

[F2] The LEO conditions include finite freeness and a localized rank-one Bar–Natan complex ([[def-odd-khovanov-barnatan-and-leo-triple]]).

[F3] The full based knot assignment has the integral marked movie maps, compatible reductions, localized concordance equivalence, arbitrary based-diagram comparison and connected-sum tensor identifications ([[lem-odd-khovanov-and-barnatan-localization-foundations]]).

[F4] Smooth oriented knot concordance classes form a group under connected sum, with the stated reverse-mirror inverse ([[thm-knot-concordance-is-an-abelian-group]]); this item uses only the supplier's proved smooth-category clause.

[A1] The Axiom of Countable Choice is used by the smooth concordance-group and finite-movie inputs; the abstract algebraic group proof below is choice-free ([[def-countable-choice]]).

[F5] The new integral odd/BN spherical chart comparison is [[lem-pointed-spherical-recharting-preserves-odd-barnatan-complexes]]. Its inverse maps are marked-module linear and have exact common mod-two squares.

[F6] Arbitrary endpoint normalization and R-only comparison are [[lem-based-planar-diagrams-admit-spherical-long-endpoint-presentations]] and [[lem-marked-knot-isotopies-admit-protected-reidemeister-movies]]. Their common endpoint-coordinate construction is used explicitly in the full foundations proof.

[F7] [[lem-marked-knot-concordances-admit-finite-movies-away-from-the-mark]] provides the actual protected annulus movie; [[lem-based-odd-barnatan-movie-maps-and-localized-concordances]] provides its module-linear maps and the localized equivalence of the connected composite.

[F8] [[lem-pointed-odd-barnatan-tensor-product-over-marked-rings]] proves the shifted connected-sum identifications and their common reduction; the full foundations proof transfers them to arbitrary based representatives.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere. Let $F$ be a compact connected oriented Seifert surface with boundary $K$, and let $\mathcal H=(\Sigma,\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\beta,w,z)$ be an admissible doubly pointed Heegaard diagram representing $(K,F)$. The associated one-pointed hat chain complex $\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H)$ is the finite-dimensional chain complex over $\mathbb F_2$ obtained from the minus complex by setting its basepoint variable to zero; its differential counts index-one disks with zero multiplicity at $w$. Assume for this specified data that the differential is nonincreasing in the Alexander filtration, that the absolute Alexander formula below takes integer values, and that $H(\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H))\cong\mathbb F_2$. Give a generator $\mathbf x$ its absolute Alexander filtration
$$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$
where $\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)$ is the homology class of the nowhere-vanishing vector field assigned to $\mathbf x$ by the pointed Morse construction, with its prescribed boundary data near the two basepoints; $c_1$ is the first Chern class of the oriented plane field perpendicular to that vector field. To form the zero-framed surgery, remove a tubular neighborhood of $K$ and glue in a solid torus whose meridian is the longitude induced by $F$. The surface $\widehat F$ is obtained by deleting a boundary collar of $F$ and capping its longitude by the meridian disk of that solid torus. This is the standard integer normalization, with the one-generator diagram of the standard unknot at filtration zero. The subcomplex $F_s\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H)$ is spanned by generators of Alexander filtration at most $s$.

More generally, a finite integer-filtered chain complex is a finite-dimensional chain complex $C$ over $\mathbb F_2$ with subcomplexes $F_sC$ such that $F_sC=0$ for all sufficiently small integers $s$ and $F_sC=C$ for all sufficiently large integers $s$. If $H(C)\cong\mathbb F_2$, define
$$\tau(C):=\min\{s\in\mathbb Z:\operatorname{im}(H(F_sC)\longrightarrow H(C))\ne0\}.$$
For the fixed diagram and surface above, write $\tau_{\mathcal H,F}(K)=\tau(\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H),F_*\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H))$. Once diagram and surface independence is proved, their common value is the knot invariant $\tau(K)$. Until that comparison is proved, $\tau_{\mathcal H,F}(K)$ denotes only the value for the specified data.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
The **grid-complex algorithm** takes a finite encoded grid and a mode from $\{\mathrm{tilde},\mathrm{minus\text{-}associated\text{-}graded},\mathrm{minus\text{-}filtered}\}$. It requires an integer grid number $n\ge2$, disjoint $O$- and $X$-markings with exactly one of each in every row and column, and an induced component permutation that is one $n$-cycle. If $n<2$ or the marking conditions fail, return `invalid-grid`; if the component permutation has more than one cycle, return `link-input-not-supported`. No chain complex is returned on either branch.

For a valid knot grid, number the horizontal and vertical circles $1,\ldots,n$ and enumerate all permutations of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ in lexicographic order. The state for a permutation $\sigma$ consists of the $n$ intersections $(i,\sigma(i))$. For each ordered pair of states $\mathbf x,\mathbf y$, if they agree in other than exactly $n-2$ points, add no rectangle terms. Otherwise enumerate the at most two torus rectangles with the four nonshared state points as corners, retain those whose interiors contain no point of $\mathbf x$, and apply the selected mode. In the full filtered mode, each term drops filtration by $n_{\mathbb X}(r)$; the associated-graded mode retains precisely the terms with zero drop, which are the rectangles with no $X$-marking:

1. **Tilde mode.** Work over $\mathbb F_2$. Count a retained rectangle with coefficient $1$ exactly when its interior contains no $O$- or $X$-marking.
2. **Associated-graded minus mode.** Work over $\mathbb F_2[U_1,\ldots,U_n]$, with each $U_i$ of Maslov degree $-2$ and Alexander filtration degree $-1$. Count a retained rectangle exactly when its interior contains no $X$-marking, with coefficient $\prod_{i=1}^n U_i^{O_i(r)}$.
3. **Full filtered minus mode.** Work over $\mathbb F_2[U_1,\ldots,U_n]$, with each $U_i$ of Maslov degree $-2$ and Alexander filtration degree $-1$. Count every retained rectangle, regardless of its $X$-markings, with coefficient $\prod_{i=1}^n U_i^{O_i(r)}$. Use the grid Alexander value for each state and assign filtration drop $n_{\mathbb X}(r)$ to this term.

Return the ordered state list, the mode and coefficient ring, the exact differential matrix obtained by summing coefficients modulo two, the state Maslov and Alexander values, and the filtration data for the full filtered mode. The algorithm returns this finite presentation only; its identification with knot Floer homology and its independence of the chosen grid are separate theorems. The factor $V^{\otimes(n-1)}$ is not multiplied into the output.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume countable choice. Let $K$ be an oriented knot in $S^3$, and let $F$ be a compact connected oriented surface embedded in $S^3$ with boundary $K$ and minimum possible genus; write $g(K)=\operatorname{genus}(F)$. Let $G$ be any toroidal grid diagram for $K$ with grid number $n$. Let $C^-_{\mathrm{grid}}(G)$ be the full filtered minus complex produced by the grid-complex algorithm, and let $C^-_U(G)$ denote this same complex regarded over $\mathbb F_2[U]$ by letting $U$ act as one chosen $U_i$, with the other variables retained independently. For an admissible $2n$-pointed Heegaard diagram $\mathcal H$ compatible with $(K,F)$, define $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ by the same restriction to a single variable action. Write $CFK^-(K)$ for the full filtered complex of an admissible doubly-pointed diagram. The ordinary fully collapsed quotient, obtained instead by setting all $U_i=U$, has type $CFK^-(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)}$; the restriction of scalars $C^-_U$ has type $CFK^-(K)$.

For the absolute Alexander normalization, let $\mathcal H_1$ be an admissible doubly-pointed Heegaard diagram for $(K,F)$. For a generator $\mathbf x$ of $\mathcal H_1$, set
$$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$
where $\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)$ is the relative $\operatorname{Spin}^c$ structure assigned to this generator by the pointed Heegaard construction: it is the homology class of the nowhere-vanishing vector field obtained from the gradient trajectories through $\mathbf x$ and the chosen basepoint pair, after extending the field across small balls around the critical points. Its first Chern class is that of the oriented plane field orthogonal to this vector field. The surface $\widehat F$ is obtained by removing a tubular neighborhood $N(K)$ from $F$ and capping the resulting longitude with the meridian disk of the solid torus attached in zero-framed surgery on $K$. Let $\widehat{HFK}(K)$ be the homology of the Alexander-associated-graded complex obtained from the doubly-pointed complex $C^-_U(\mathcal H_1)$ by quotienting by its sole variable $U$, with this $A_F$ normalization.

Then $C^-_U(G)$ and $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ are filtered chain homotopy equivalent, preserving relative Maslov grading and the $A_F$ filtration, and their Alexander-associated-graded minus complexes are chain homotopy equivalent. For any two grids of $K$, the resulting normalized filtered complexes are filtered chain homotopy equivalent. If $\widetilde{GH}(G)$ denotes the homology of the tilde grid complex over $\mathbb F_2$, then
$$\widetilde{GH}(G)\cong\widehat{HFK}(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)},$$
where $V$ is the two-dimensional bigraded vector space with one generator in bidegree $(0,0)$ and one in bidegree $(-1,-1)$.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume countable choice. Let $\mathcal H$ be any admissible $2k$-pointed Heegaard diagram for an oriented knot in $S^3$, with transverse attaching curves, product tori, and marked points as specified in the pointed-data definition. Admissibility means every nonzero periodic domain with all $w$-multiplicities zero has both positive and negative region coefficients. There is a smooth path $\mathbb J=(J_t)_{t\in[0,1]}$, constant near its endpoints and chosen among perturbations for which all holomorphic-strip representatives used in the differential have nonnegative local multiplicity at every marked point, such that the linearized Cauchy–Riemann operator is surjective for every Maslov-index-$1$ strip class with all $w$-multiplicities nonnegative. Each corresponding moduli space modulo translation is finite. For every Maslov-index-$2$ class with all $w$-multiplicities nonnegative, the compactification of the one-dimensional moduli space modulo translation has as codimension-one boundary broken pairs of index-one strips meeting at an intermediate generator and disk bubbles whose entire boundary lies on one of the product tori (the boundary-degeneration strata). Gluing gives a collar at every broken end, and the boundary-degeneration contributions cancel modulo two in the differential-square count. No sphere bubbling or escape through a nonzero periodic domain gives an additional codimension-one end. Consequently the disk-count differential in the pointed-data definition squares to zero and preserves its Alexander filtration.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume countable choice. Let $K$ be an oriented knot in $S^3$, let $F$ be a compact connected oriented embedded surface with boundary $K$, and let $\mathcal H_0,\mathcal H_1$ be admissible multipointed Heegaard diagrams for $K$. For $i=0,1$, the diagram $\mathcal H_i$ has a closed genus-$h_i$ Heegaard surface and $m_i=h_i+k_i-1$ curves in each attaching system, with $k_i$ ordered $w$-points and $k_i$ ordered $z$-points; each component of either attaching-system complement contains one point of each type, and the connecting arcs represent $K$. A curve isotopy is an isotopy of one attaching curve through embedded curves in its attaching system, disjoint from the other attaching curves and all marked points. A handleslide replaces one attaching curve by its band sum with another curve in the same attaching system, along an embedded arc disjoint from the other attaching curves and the marked points. A Heegaard stabilization forms connected sum with the genus-one splitting of $S^3$ in a disk disjoint from all curves, marked points, and knot arcs; it raises the genus by one and leaves $k$ fixed. A basepoint-pair (index-zero/three) stabilization keeps the genus fixed and adds one curve to each system and one $w,z$ pair along the represented knot. Its inverse removes the following elementary configuration, after relabeling the cyclic pairs: curves $\alpha_0,\beta_0$ bound disks $A_0,B_0$ on the surface, are disjoint from every opposite-system curve except each other, and intersect transversely in two points; $A_0\cap B_0$ is a bigon containing just $w_0$, while $A_0\setminus B_0$ contains just $z_0$ and $B_0\setminus A_0$ contains the next $z$-point along the cyclic pairing. Remove $\alpha_0,\beta_0,w_0,z_0$ and concatenate the adjacent trivial knot arcs. The surviving marked points stay fixed. Thus the move inserts a pair along an existing knot arc rather than adjoining an isolated marked component in an empty disk. Both descriptions include the simultaneous boundary-parallel arc systems and require the stated one-$w$, one-$z$ condition in each attaching complement. Destabilizations are the respective inverse moves. Comparisons may apply the orientation-preserving diagram isomorphisms of the pointed-data definition, carrying the ordered marked points, attaching systems and simultaneous boundary-parallel arcs, before or after the listed geometric moves. Their complex identifications are induced by pushforward of generators, disk classes and almost complex data, rather than by assuming an isotopy acts as the identity. Comparisons also allow the fixed-splitting arc normalizations in that definition before or after the listed moves, retaining the simultaneous bridge witnesses and all ordered marks. They leave the surface attaching and analytic data fixed, so their identification of the actual count operators is the identity; they do not assert a diffeomorphism of a tangential and transverse surface-knot pair. With these identifications, any two such diagrams are related by a finite sequence of the listed moves through admissible multipointed diagrams, preserving the represented oriented knot.

For a diagram with $j$ basepoint pairs, regard its full filtered minus complex as a complex over $\mathbb F_2[U]$ by restriction of scalars along $U\mapsto U_i$ for any one chosen basepoint variable. The resulting complexes of $\mathcal H_0$ and $\mathcal H_1$ are filtered chain homotopy equivalent over $\mathbb F_2[U]$, preserving relative Maslov grading and Alexander filtration, even when the diagrams have different numbers of basepoint pairs. The choice of the single variable action does not affect this type. Restriction retains the independent variables in the chain module; it is different from quotienting by $U_1=\cdots=U_j$. The latter ordinary quotient is the fully collapsed complex and has filtered chain homotopy type $CFK^-(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(j-1)}$, where $V$ has zero differential and bidegrees $(0,0)$ and $(-1,-1)$. Equivalently, a basepoint stabilization before quotienting is modeled by the cone of $U_{j+1}+U_i$ on the polynomial extension of the old complex; after the simultaneous quotient this is a zero-map cone and contributes the displayed extra factor.

For an admissible doubly-pointed diagram $\mathcal H_1$ for $(K,F)$, define $\widehat{HFK}(K)$ to be the homology of the Alexander-associated-graded complex obtained from its full filtered minus complex by quotienting by its sole variable $U$. For a generator $\mathbf x$ use the Alexander grading
$$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$
where $\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)$ is the relative $\operatorname{Spin}^c$ structure assigned by the pointed Heegaard construction from the gradient trajectories through $\mathbf x$ and the chosen basepoint pair, and $\widehat F$ is obtained by removing a tubular neighborhood of $K$ from $F$ and capping the resulting longitude with the meridian disk of the solid torus attached so that this longitude bounds it (zero-framed surgery). The vector-field representative is extended across small balls around the critical points, and its first Chern class is the Chern class of the orthogonal oriented plane field. Use the absolute Maslov normalization in which the unique generator of $\widehat{HF}(S^3)$ has degree zero.

For a diagram $\mathcal H$ with $j$ basepoint pairs, let $\widetilde C(\mathcal H)$ be the Alexander-associated-graded complex over $\mathbb F_2$ obtained from its full filtered minus complex by setting every $U_i=0$; its differential therefore counts only classes with all $n_{w_i}=n_{z_i}=0$. Its homology is $\widehat{HFK}(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(j-1)}$, where $V=\mathbb F_2\langle v_0,v_1\rangle$ has bidegrees $(M,A)(v_0)=(0,0)$ and $(M,A)(v_1)=(-1,-1)$.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Work in the smooth category inherited from the oriented-link convention. In particular, an embedded bridge witness disk means the image of a smooth rank-two embedding of a planar disk, with ordinary smooth boundary or smooth transverse corners at its two marked endpoints; smoothness at a boundary or corner means local smooth extension in its charts. Witness parametrizations can be chosen for the finite disk families. This category convention does not require the knot arcs to meet the Heegaard surface transversely: tangential smooth crossings remain permitted.

Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot. Let $\Sigma$ be a closed oriented surface of genus $h$, let $k\ge1$, and put $m=h+k-1$. A **handlebody** is a compact three-manifold that is a regular neighborhood of a finite connected graph. A **$2k$-pointed Heegaard diagram for $S^3$** consists of a splitting $S^3=U_{\alpha}\cup_{\Sigma}U_{\beta}$ into handlebodies, two systems $\boldsymbol\alpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_m)$ and $\boldsymbol\beta=(\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_m)$ of pairwise disjoint simple closed curves on $\Sigma$ that bound pairwise disjoint properly embedded disks in $U_{\alpha}$ and $U_{\beta}$, respectively, cutting each handlebody into exactly $k$ three-balls, and two ordered sets of distinct points $\mathbf w=(w_1,\ldots,w_k)$ and $\mathbf z=(z_1,\ldots,z_k)$ disjoint from the curves. Curves from different systems intersect transversely in finitely many points. Each component of $\Sigma\setminus\boldsymbol\alpha$ and of $\Sigma\setminus\boldsymbol\beta$ contains exactly one $w$-point and exactly one $z$-point. The diagram also includes trivial arc systems in the two handlebodies: the $\alpha$-arcs join $w_i$ to $z_i$, and the $\beta$-arcs join $z_i$ to $w_{i-1}$, with indices modulo $k$. Each system is disjoint from its compression disks and is simultaneously boundary parallel: its arcs cobound pairwise disjoint embedded disks with arcs in the corresponding components of the attaching-system complement on $\Sigma$. Thus each ball obtained by compression contains one unknotted arc. Together the arcs form an oriented knot, oriented from $w_i$ to $z_i$ in $U_{\alpha}$ and from $z_i$ to $w_{i-1}$ in $U_{\beta}$. The diagram is **compatible with $K$** when this knot is orientation-preservingly ambient isotopic to $K$. For a grid diagram, compatibility uses the row and column orientation fixed in the grid definition, with $w$-points at $O$ and $z$-points at $X$. For a grid representing one knot, the basepoint pairs can be numbered cyclically in reverse order of travel along the oriented knot so that $w_i,z_i$ lie in the same component $A_i$ of $\Sigma\setminus\boldsymbol\alpha$ and $w_i,z_{i+1}$ lie in the same component $B_i$ of $\Sigma\setminus\boldsymbol\beta$.

Comparisons of these embedded diagrams allow **orientation-preserving diagram isomorphisms**: an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism of $S^3$ carrying the two handlebodies, their oriented Heegaard surface, the two attaching systems, the ordered $w,z$ points, and the two simultaneously boundary-parallel arc systems to the corresponding data. Equivalently one may specify the surface isomorphism together with its compatible collared extensions over both handlebodies carrying those arcs. The attaching systems are carried as systems; reordering their curve factors induces the corresponding product identification. Comparisons also allow **arc normalizations in the fixed splitting**: a smooth isotopy of the represented oriented knot, supported near the ordered marks and fixing each mark, during which every open connecting arc stays in its original handlebody and the two simultaneous boundary-parallel witness systems are retained or replaced by embedded witnesses for those same arcs. The surface, attaching curves, marked points and compression disks stay fixed. Such a normalization may replace a tangential marked crossing by a transverse one; the original data are not required to have neat arcs. This is a change of knot representative relative to the fixed surface, not a diagram isomorphism carrying both objects. Analytic and assigned grading data depending on the fixed surface diagram can be kept identical; the corresponding generator and disk-count identification is then the identity. Existence of normalizations with the required witnesses is a separate geometric assertion, not part of this definition. Such a comparison transports the represented oriented knot and any specified Seifert surface as well. For analytic data, it transports $j$, the surface area form, all chosen divisor neighborhoods and $J_t$ by the induced symmetric-product diffeomorphism. The comparison maps on generators and disk classes are their pushforwards under this map; compatibility with the count differential is a mathematical property to be proved. No identity action is part of this convention, even when the ambient diffeomorphism is isotopic to the identity.

The $m$-fold symmetric product $\operatorname{Sym}^{m}(\Sigma)=\Sigma^m/S_m$ is the space of unordered $m$-tuples of points of $\Sigma$, where $S_m$ permutes coordinates. Let $q:\Sigma^m\to\operatorname{Sym}^{m}(\Sigma)$ be the quotient map. The product tori are the images $\mathbb T_{\alpha}=q(\alpha_1\times\cdots\times\alpha_m)$ and $\mathbb T_{\beta}=q(\beta_1\times\cdots\times\beta_m)$. Their intersection points are the generators. A **Whitney disk class** $\phi\in\pi_2(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)$ is a relative homotopy class of maps from a disk to $\operatorname{Sym}^{m}(\Sigma)$ whose two boundary arcs lie on $\mathbb T_{\alpha}$ and $\mathbb T_{\beta}$ and whose endpoints are $\mathbf x$ and $\mathbf y$. Its domain is the integral two-chain of complementary regions with coefficients equal to local multiplicities. Write $n_{w_i}(\phi)$ and $n_{z_i}(\phi)$ for its local multiplicities at the marked points. An almost complex structure $J$ on $\operatorname{Sym}^{m}(\Sigma)$ is a smooth endomorphism of the tangent bundle with $J^2=-1$. Fix a complex structure $j$ and an area form on $\Sigma$. For $m>0$, choose a smooth path $\mathbb J=(J_t)_{t\in[0,1]}$ of nearly symmetric almost complex structures, constant near $t=0,1$: each $J_t$ agrees with the induced integrable structure $\operatorname{Sym}^{m}(j)$ on a fixed neighborhood of the diagonal and of every divisor $\{p\}+\operatorname{Sym}^{m-1}(\Sigma)$ for a chosen interior point $p$ of every complementary region, including every marked point, and tames the form descended from the product area form off that neighborhood. The path is a sufficiently small perturbation in this class. For $m=0$ the symmetric product is a point. Local multiplicities are intersection numbers with these divisors; positivity is a mathematical property to be proved, not an additional choice of disk counts. A $\mathbb J$-holomorphic strip representative is a smooth map $u:\mathbb R\times[0,1]\to\operatorname{Sym}^{m}(\Sigma)$ satisfying $\partial_{\tau}u+J_t(u)\partial_tu=0$, with $u(\tau,0)\in\mathbb T_{\alpha}$, $u(\tau,1)\in\mathbb T_{\beta}$, and limits $\mathbf x,\mathbf y$ as $\tau\to-\infty,+\infty$. Translation in $\tau$ defines an $\mathbb R$-action. The Maslov index $\mu(\phi)$ is the Fredholm index of the linearized Cauchy–Riemann operator at a representative of $\phi$; the relative Maslov grading convention is $M(\mathbf x)-M(\mathbf y)=\mu(\phi)-2\sum_{i=1}^{k}n_{w_i}(\phi)$, up to one overall additive constant.

A **periodic domain** is an integral two-chain in the complementary regions whose boundary is an integral sum of full $\alpha$- and $\beta$-curves; its local multiplicity at a marked point is the coefficient of the containing region. The pointed diagram is **admissible** when every nonzero periodic domain with $n_{w_i}=0$ for all $i$ has at least one positive and at least one negative region coefficient. A path $\mathbb J$ is **regular for a set of disk classes** when the linearized Cauchy–Riemann operator at every holomorphic-strip representative in those classes is surjective. For a path regular on the classes used, let $\mathcal M_{\mathbb J}(\phi)$ be the space of strip representatives. If, for each generator $\mathbf x$, only finitely many pairs $(\mathbf y,\phi)$ with $\mathcal M_{\mathbb J}(\phi)\ne\varnothing$, $\mu(\phi)=1$, and $n_{w_i}(\phi)\ge0$ for every $i$ occur, and each quotient is finite, the multipointed full filtered minus module is the free module over $\mathbb F_2[U_1,\ldots,U_k]$ generated by $\mathbb T_{\alpha}\cap\mathbb T_{\beta}$, with differential
$$\partial^-\mathbf x=\sum_{\mathbf y}\sum_{\substack{\phi\in\pi_2(\mathbf x,\mathbf y),\;\mathcal M_{\mathbb J}(\phi)\ne\varnothing\\\mu(\phi)=1,\; n_{w_i}(\phi)\ge0\ \forall i}}\#_2\bigl(\mathcal M_{\mathbb J}(\phi)/\mathbb R\bigr)\,U_1^{n_{w_1}(\phi)}\cdots U_k^{n_{w_k}(\phi)}\mathbf y.$$
Here $\#_2$ is the count modulo two of the zero-dimensional quotient when it is finite. Quotienting by all $U_i$ leaves the fully blocked multipointed chain complex (the hat chain complex when $k=1$), with terms only from classes satisfying $n_{w_i}=0$ for every $i$; its Alexander-filtered associated-graded complex further retains only classes with every $n_{z_i}=0$. The relative Alexander grading convention is $A(\mathbf x)-A(\mathbf y)=\sum_i n_{z_i}(\phi)-\sum_i n_{w_i}(\phi)$, with an overall additive constant. Each $U_i$ lowers Maslov grading by two and Alexander filtration by one. In a grid diagram, $\Sigma=T^2$, $h=1$, $k=n$, and $m=n$; the horizontal circles are the $\alpha$-curves, the vertical circles are the $\beta$-curves, and the $w$-points and $z$-points are the $O$- and $X$-markings respectively.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Let $\mathsf{Cob}_3$ be the additive monoidal category of oriented cobordisms before the S, T, and four-tube relations are imposed, and let $\mathsf{Cob}_{BN}$ be its quotient by those relations. Suppose $F:\mathsf{Cob}_3\to\mathsf{GrAb}$ is a symmetric monoidal functor to graded abelian groups and homogeneous maps, with a circle sent to $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$, a cup to $\eta(1)=1$, a cap to $\epsilon(1)=0,\epsilon(X)=1$, a merge pair of pants to $m$, and a split pair of pants to $\Delta(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1,\ \Delta(X)=X\otimes X$. Then every sphere component is sent to zero, every disjoint torus component acts by multiplication by $2$, and the two sides of the four-tube relation induce the same map. Therefore $F$ factors through an additive monoidal functor on $\mathsf{Cob}_{BN}$.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume countable choice. Let $\Sigma_0,\Sigma_1\subset S^3\times[0,1]$ be compact smooth properly embedded oriented surfaces from fixed oriented knots $K_0$ to $K_1$, with the same boundary parametrizations and product collars. Suppose their generic movies represent ambient isotopic cobordisms by an isotopy fixed on those collars. Then one movie can be changed to the other by a finite sequence of the fifteen Carter–Saito movie moves, sweep-around moves, and interchanges of two disjoint elementary movie events (including disjoint critical points of the surface-height function). A sweep-around moves a closing arc of a one-interval tangle over the tangle to its other side and back underneath, or reverses that movie; geometrically it is a local sheet passage through the missing vertical arc in a spatial chart $S^3\setminus\{\infty\}$. Every intermediate movie represents a generic surface cobordism with the same fixed boundary data.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $(W,\Sigma,\mathcal A)$ be a decorated knot cobordism from $(Y_0,K_0)$ to $(Y_1,K_1)$, and fix $\mathfrak s\in\operatorname{Spin}^c(W)$. Choose a parametrized Kirby decomposition of $W$, together with admissible Heegaard data and regular almost-complex structures for its elementary pieces. Intermediate pieces may contain links with several components or more than one pair of basepoints. Use the colored multipointed modules with $g+n-1$ attaching curves in $\operatorname{Sym}^{g+n-1}(S)$, and specialize all $w$-colors to $U$ and all $z$-colors to $V$; the displayed doubly pointed formula is the $n=1$ case. For a piece represented by a subordinate Heegaard triple $(S,\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\beta,\boldsymbol\gamma,w,z)$, its triangle-count map has the form
$$
\mathbf x\longmapsto \sum_{\mathbf y}\ \sum_{\substack{\phi\in\pi_2(\mathbf x,\Theta^+_{\boldsymbol\beta\boldsymbol\gamma},\mathbf y)\\ \mu(\phi)=0,\ \mathfrak s(\phi)=\mathfrak s}} \#_2\bigl(\mathcal M(\phi)\bigr)U^{n_w(\phi)}V^{n_z(\phi)}\mathbf y,
$$
where $\Theta^+_{\boldsymbol\beta\boldsymbol\gamma}$ denotes a chosen cycle representative of the distinguished top-degree homology class of the appropriate standard auxiliary Heegaard pair, $\mathfrak s(\phi)$ is the Spin-c structure determined by the triangle class, and the other symbols and coefficient ring are as in the two-color target definition. For a chosen auxiliary cycle with finite support $\Theta=\sum_j p_j\theta_j$, with $p_j\in\mathbb F_2[U,V]$ and basis generators $\theta_j$, interpret the displayed formula by $\mathbb F_2[U,V]$-linearity as $\sum_j p_j F(\mathbf x,\theta_j)$ (or $\sum_j p_j F(\theta_j,\mathbf x)$ for the alpha-triple convention). The elementary 2-handle maps and band maps are triangle-count maps; the 0-, 1-, 3-, and 4-handle maps use the corresponding stabilization or destabilization maps; cylindrical changes of the dividing set use basepoint and quasi-stabilization maps. Compose the elementary maps in the chosen decomposition to obtain a representative
$$
\widetilde F_{W,\Sigma,\mathcal A,\mathfrak s,\mathcal K}: CFL^-_{UV}(Y_0,K_0,\mathfrak s|_{Y_0})\longrightarrow CFL^-_{UV}(Y_1,K_1,\mathfrak s|_{Y_1}).
$$
The subscript $\mathcal K$ records the chosen decomposition and auxiliary data. This is one map for one Spin-c structure; maps for different Spin-c structures are not summed unless a sum is explicitly specified. Independence from $\mathcal K$, regular data, and parametrization is a separate naturality assertion.

facts:
[F1] **External construction input.** Zemke, *Link cobordisms and functoriality in link Floer homology*, arXiv:1610.05207v3, Theorem A (p.3), Definitions 2.1–2.4 (pp.7–8), Proposition 3.5 and §3.4 (p.14), and §12 (pp.85–97), constructs the fixed-Spin-c colored maps for the full decorated category, as filtered equivariant chain maps on transitive chain homotopy types. Boundary parametrizations are retained (Remark 2.6, p.8). Components need not meet both ends: §12.5, Definition 12.8, Lemma 12.9 and equation (55) (pp.95–97) supply puncturing and the 0/4-handle maps. This is an explicitly imported established theorem, not a reconstruction from the local triangle lemma. ([Source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1610.05207v3))

[F2] **External elementary-input convention.** For a two-handle use the standard auxiliary top homology class in Zemke §5. For band surgery the actual inputs are the classes $\Theta^w$ for a type-z band and $\Theta^z$ for a type-w band (§§6.2–6.3, pp.46–47; auxiliary unlink calculation Lemmas 3.7 and 6.4). Choose cycle representatives. Changing a representative by a boundary changes the triangle map by filtered equivariant chain homotopy (§6.2, p.46). There is no canonical chain generator on arbitrary triples. The displayed formula is the beta-triple convention; alpha-triples insert the auxiliary cycle in the other tensor factor. The dividing set chooses the band type. ([Source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1610.05207v3))

[F3] **Two-color scope.** Color every component of $\Sigma_w$ by $U$ and every component of $\Sigma_z$ by $V$. This is a coloring in Definition 2.3 and induces exactly the given endpoint coloring. Remark 2.14 (p.10) gives zero curvature for this specialization, including intermediate links; §3.4 gives the colored polynomial modules and variable-power filtration.

[F4] **Countable-choice specialization of the imported construction.** Use the retained Countable-Choice theorem on full-marked low-dimensional polygons at its stated coherent-relative-face scope, with finite balanced diagrams, fixed labels and all nonnegative marked multiplicities. It supplies regular perturbations, finite counts, compact one-manifolds and gluing for the disk/polygon boundary identities used here. Its permitted small pointed curve choices retain the Spin-c labels and admissibility. The general naturality/move identities, top-input calculations and geometric decomposition theorems remain the explicitly external parts of [F1]–[F2], not conclusions of polygon analysis alone. Their remaining choices are finite topological data and countably indexed analytic families for each specified input/comparison, as detailed below. contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume countable choice. Let $(S,\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\beta,\boldsymbol\gamma,w,z)$ be a strictly strongly admissible pointed Heegaard triple for a decorated knot cobordism, with the strong condition normalized at ALL $w$ marks. Fix one Spin-c structure $\mathfrak s$ and nonnegative $w,z$-multiplicities. In positive symmetric rank $m=h+k-1>0$, among the auxiliary Heegaard data first choose an arbitrarily small pointed Hamiltonian representative with no common intersection of three attaching families, following the pair generators and transporting the actual Spin-c label and strict admissibility. Such positive-rank representatives exist. Fix that representative; this is an explicit curve choice, not a claim that varying the almost-complex tensor alone regularizes constant triangles on the original arbitrary fixed triple.

At rank $m=0$, keep the original empty attaching systems: the target is one point and no triple-torus exclusion is imposed. Its unique constant triangle, when its assigned Spin-c label and zero marked-degree vectors match the specified ones, is regular of index zero and contributes one; all other specified-label or positive-degree sets are empty. The fixed index-one and universal index-minus-one spaces are empty, and a matching one-parameter family is the parameter interval.

In positive rank choose regular end data in the open dense set of allowed genuine constant-collar paths described in the proof. For generic fixed source-dependent almost-complex data compatible with those ends, the Maslov-index-zero triangle moduli spaces used in the triangle-count map are regular zero-manifolds and finite. For generic one-parameter families with those fixed regular ends, the universal triangle moduli spaces are regular with the parameter included in the expected dimension; slice counts are taken at regular parameter values. The compactified one-dimensional Maslov-index-one triangle spaces have precisely the broken triangle/strip strata, with actual gluing collars. In these dimensions no nonconstant one-torus boundary degeneration is allowed: its index contribution is at least two and the remaining triangle would have negative count dimension. In a one-parameter family the compactified universal index-zero spaces additionally have the two parameter-endpoint strata; the zero-dimensional universal index-minus-one spaces define the homotopy terms.

The mod-two boundary counts give the weighted bilinear triangle chain-map equation and its chain homotopy. Inserting an actual intermediate cycle gives the corresponding one-input chain-map equation. All nonnegative marked multiplicities and the fixed Spin-c extension are retained, including intermediate closed three-manifolds beyond $S^3$ and multiple mark pairs. No additional ends arise from sphere bubbling, escape through nonzero periodic domains or uncontrolled marked-point multiplicities. This analytic assertion does not itself establish that a named top generator is a cycle or prove invariance under changing the chosen attaching curves.

facts:

The collar transport carries the lift including torsion and preserves the Chern functional and all old admissibility witnesses. [F3] Actual full-marked low-dimensional polygon analysis proves the open dense good end choices, source-dependent universal transversality, finite counts, index budgets, compact one-manifold boundaries and exhaustive gluing, on general balanced intermediate three-manifolds. [F4] The two-color map convention composes actual elementary maps and inserts the specified intermediate top input. contract.heading: Definition
contract.text: Assume countable choice and fix a generic movie $M$ of a smooth oriented surface cobordism $\Sigma$ from an oriented link $L_0$ to an oriented link $L_1$. For each regular frame $D$, let $Kh(D)$ be the normalized integral Khovanov homology group. The empty frame has the one-term complex $\mathbb Z$ in both gradings zero, using the empty resolution and the zero-fold tensor product. Associate to a birth the unit map $\eta:\mathbb Z\to\mathcal A$, $\eta(1)=1$; associate to a death the counit $\epsilon:\mathcal A\to\mathbb Z$, $\epsilon(1)=0,\epsilon(X)=1$; and associate to a saddle the multiplication $m:\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ when two resolution circles merge, or the comultiplication $\Delta:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A$ when one splits. Each local map is tensored with the identity on unaffected circles. Associate to planar isotopy the induced identification of the cube complexes. For Reidemeister moves, use the following fixed Bar-Natan constructions: the kink retractions $F_+=v-\Delta$, $G_+=e$, $F_-=u$, $G_-=w-m$; the two inverse-crossing strong retractions with degree-zero inclusion $(1,ut)^T$ and projection $(1,-se)$, with their specified reverse-order cube signs; and the third-move equivalences obtained by the explicit source- or target-cone retractions onto the common six-point residual complex. Here $u,e$ are circle birth/death, $v,w$ are punctured-torus birth/death, and the saddle letters denote the actual local bands in these constructions. Use their specified inverses for the reversed moves. Insert these formal surface matrices into the fixed planar outside of the diagram, then apply the integral Frobenius cobordism functor. Normalize a state $v$ to cochain degree $|v|-n_-$ and quantum shift $|v|+n_+-2n_-$. Fix the local coordinate identifications and orientation cases once, with the Koszul crossing-order correction $(-1)^{v(a)v(b)}$ when crossings $a,b$ are interchanged. These local maps are chosen once; composing them with an arbitrary automorphism of a complex is not an allowed change of representative. Compose the induced maps on homology in movie order and denote the result by $Kh(M):Kh(L_0)\to Kh(L_1)$, considered modulo multiplication by $-1$. This definition fixes a movie; independence from changing the movie is not included in the definition.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume countable choice. For each Carter–Saito movie move, the two movie segments have the same incoming and outgoing oriented link diagrams and represent isotopic portions of an oriented surface cobordism relative to their boundary collars. The induced maps on the integral even Khovanov homology groups of those diagrams differ by multiplication by a single overall sign. The same conclusion holds when two disjoint critical points of the height function are interchanged.

facts:
**Given:** Countable choice and either one of the fifteen Euclidean local movie relations in a fixed planar outside, or an interchange of two disjoint surface-height critical events. Work first in the additive formal surface category and apply the closed-surface functor only after inserting the outside.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]] is inherited by the geometric disk-system and link-homology suppliers. The finite cubes and matrix compositions require no further choice.

[F1] [[def-khovanov-cobordism-map-up-to-sign]] fixes the actual Bar-Natan local systems, their inverses, crossing permutations and normalization; it does not permit arbitrary automorphisms as replacement maps.

[F2] [[lem-barnatan-formal-kink-retractions]], [[lem-barnatan-formal-inverse-boundary-crossings]] and [[lem-barnatan-formal-third-reidemeister-equivalence]] provide actual internal degree zero equivalences for the three Reidemeister moves, with their displayed inverses and homotopies.

[F3] [[lem-barnatan-open-pairings-have-scalar-degree-zero-endomorphisms]] says that the degree-zero endomorphisms of a crossingless pairing form $\mathbb Z$ generated by its identity. Its degree-zero homotopy automorphisms are therefore exactly $\pm1$.

[F4] [[lem-barnatan-planar-homotopies-and-conditional-boundary-crossing-simplicity]] gives invariance of this simplicity under degree-zero equivalence and under adjoining a boundary crossing when both crossing inverse equivalences exist. The latter premises are supplied by the two physical orders in [F2]. It also gives signed planar insertion of homotopies.

[F5] [[lem-barnatan-morse-movie-matrices]] proves the five Morse relations MM11–MM15 for exactly the selected systems, including both directions and the cube signs.

[F6] [[lem-integral-khovanov-frobenius-algebra-defines-a-cobordism-functor]] constructs the actual integral functor on closed surfaces, not only a conditional factorization. [[lem-khovanov-frobenius-tqft-respects-barnatan-relations]] makes it descend through S, T and four-tube. Finite matrices and chain homotopies therefore pass to the stated integral cube complexes.

[F7] [[def-carter-saito-euclidean-local-movie-moves]] specifies the fifteen coordinate models. [[def-barnatan-open-tangle-cobordism-complexes]] specifies their formal cubes and signed planar totalization.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$ be the Frobenius algebra with unit $\eta(1)=1$ and multiplication $m$. In the algebraic TQFT, consider the movie that first creates a disjoint circle and then attaches a saddle band merging that circle with one existing circle. The induced local map is
$$
\mathcal A\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal A}\otimes\eta} \mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A\xrightarrow{m}\mathcal A,
$$
and this composite is the identity on $\mathcal A$.

The diagram records the two successive surface events; it is only a description of the movie, while the verification below is algebraic.

```tikz
\begin{tikzcd}
\mathcal A
\arrow[r, "{\operatorname{id}\otimes\eta}"]
& \mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A
\arrow[r, "m"]
& \mathcal A
\end{tikzcd}
```

facts:
**Given:** The rank-two algebra $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$, its unit $\eta(1)=1$, and its merge map $m$.

[F1] [[def-khovanov-frobenius-algebra-and-cube-of-resolutions]] gives the basis $\{1,X\}$, the unit $1\mapsto1$, and multiplication $m(a\otimes1)=a$ for $a\in\mathcal A$.

contract.heading: Statement refuted
contract.text:
Let $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$ with unit $\eta(1)=1$ and counit $\epsilon(1)=0,\epsilon(X)=1$. On a movie with one unaffected circle, birth a disjoint circle and then cap that same circle by a death. The composite operator is
$$
\mathcal A\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal A}\otimes\eta} \mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal A}\otimes\epsilon} \mathcal A,
$$
which is zero and therefore is not the identity, even after allowing multiplication by an overall sign.

```tikz
\begin{tikzcd}
\mathcal A
\arrow[r, "{\operatorname{id}\otimes\eta}"]
& \mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A
\arrow[r, "{\operatorname{id}\otimes\epsilon}"]
& \mathcal A
\end{tikzcd}
```

The movie is a cylinder on the original circle disjoint union a born-and-capped sphere; the diagram specifies the local birth and death sequence and is not used as a proof.

facts:
**Given:** The free abelian group $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$, with $\eta(1)=1$, $\epsilon(1)=0$, and $\epsilon(X)=1$.

[F1] [[def-khovanov-frobenius-algebra-and-cube-of-resolutions]] gives the unit and counit formulas and the nonzero basis element $1\in\mathcal A$.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot with a supplied regular admissible doubly pointed Heegaard diagram and normalized finite filtered hat complex $C_K$ whose total homology is $\mathbb F_2$. Let $K^\dagger$ be its reverse mirror under the fixed orientation-reversing reflection convention, with the reflected Seifert surface and reflected regular diagram. For a finite filtered complex $C$, define its dual complex $C^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb F_2}(C,\mathbb F_2)$ with transposed differential and filtration
$$F_sC^\vee=\{\lambda\in C^\vee:\lambda(F_{-s-1}C)=0\}.$$
Then the reflected diagram's normalized filtered hat complex is filtered chain isomorphic to $C_K^\vee$. In particular, its total homology is $\mathbb F_2$ and
$$\tau_{\mathcal H^\dagger,F^\dagger}(K^\dagger)=-\tau_{\mathcal H,F}(K).$$

facts:
**Given:** A finite integer-filtered chain complex $C_K$ with $H(C_K)\cong\mathbb F_2$, a regular pointed Heegaard diagram for $K$, and the reflected regular diagram for $K^\dagger$.

[F1] [[def-knot-floer-filtration-and-tau]] defines tau as the least filtration level whose inclusion has nonzero image in the one-dimensional total homology.

[F2] [[def-knot-connected-sum-and-prime-knot]] fixes the orientation-reversing reflection $r:S^3\to S^3$ used to form the mirror convention.

[F3] [[def-admissible-pointed-heegaard-floer-data]] defines the differential by mod-two counts of index-one holomorphic strips and the relative Alexander change by the difference of the marked-point multiplicities.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $C$ and $D$ be finite integer-filtered chain complexes over $\mathbb F_2$, with increasing bounded exhaustive filtrations by subcomplexes and with $H(C)\cong H(D)\cong\mathbb F_2$. Give $C\otimes D$ the tensor differential and the convolution filtration
$$F_s(C\otimes D)=\sum_{p+q\le s}F_pC\otimes F_qD.$$
Then $H(C\otimes D)\cong\mathbb F_2$ and
$$\tau(C\otimes D)=\tau(C)+\tau(D).$$

facts:
**Given:** The complexes $C,D$ and their filtrations as in the Statement.

[F1] [[def-knot-floer-filtration-and-tau]]: $\tau(C)$ is the least integer $s$ for which $H(F_sC)\to H(C)$ has nonzero image, when $H(C)\cong\mathbb F_2$.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: For the standard oriented unknot $U$ and its standard genus-zero one-pointed Heegaard diagram, the normalized Alexander-filtered hat complex has total homology $\mathbb F_2$ generated at filtration level $0$. Consequently the diagramwise threshold is $\tau_{\mathcal H,F}(U)=0$.

[F1] [[def-knot-floer-filtration-and-tau]] fixes the absolute Alexander normalization with the one-generator standard unknot diagram at filtration zero.

[F2] [[lem-standard-unknot-hat-diagram-rank-one]] proves that this genus-zero one-pointed diagram has one generator and zero differential, so its total homology is $\mathbb F_2$.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Let $U$ be the standard oriented unknot and take its genus-zero one-pointed Heegaard diagram: $\Sigma=S^2$, each handlebody is a three-ball, there are no $\alpha$- or $\beta$-curves, and one $w$-point and one $z$-point are joined by trivial arcs in the two balls. The associated-graded hat chain complex has one generator, zero differential, and homology of rank one over $\mathbb F_2$. This is a computation for the stated diagram; it makes no invariance claim for other diagrams.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ and $J$ be smooth oriented knots in the standard oriented three-sphere, with chosen minimum-genus oriented Seifert surfaces. A normalized $CFK^\infty(K)$ is a free finite-rank chain complex over $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ with two integer filtrations $(i,j)$, where multiplication by $U$ lowers both coordinates by one. Give the connected sum $K\#J$ the fixed oriented gluing convention and the sum filtrations and Maslov/Alexander gradings. Then $CFK^\infty(K\#J)$ is bifiltered chain homotopy equivalent to $CFK^\infty(K)\otimes_{\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]}CFK^\infty(J)$, with an equivalence and homotopies preserving both filtration coordinates. Moreover, the normalized finite filtered hat complex of $K\#J$ is filtered chain homotopy equivalent to $C_K\otimes C_J$ with tensor filtration $F_s(C_K\otimes C_J)=\sum_{p+q\le s}F_pC_K\otimes F_qC_J$. Consequently,
$$\tau(K\#J)=\tau(K)+\tau(J).$$

facts:
**Given:** Countable choice, the knots and oriented Seifert surfaces, and the fixed oriented connected-sum convention. We work first over $R=\mathbb F_2[U]$ with the full disk differential, retaining every positive $z$ multiplicity; localization will give the infinity complex. An ordinary doubly pointed model has one $w$ and one $z$, with generators placed at $(i,j)=(0,A_F(x))$.

[F1] Actual full-marked disk counts, finite polynomial differentials, connected-generator relative indices and relative Alexander gradings are established. Good end paths exclude nonconstant strips of nonpositive index. [[thm-balanced-knot-data-admit-full-marked-square-zero-holomorphic-counts]] [[thm-balanced-s-three-knot-generators-admit-consistent-relative-gradings]]

[F2] Actual strictly admissible polygon counts apply also to intermediate three-manifolds other than $S^3$. They retain all nonnegative marked degrees, and give finite triangle maps, their chain-map equations, coherent perturbations and the required parameter homotopies. These statements do not themselves give a top cycle or the multiplication equivalence constructed below. [[thm-strictly-admissible-triple-free-polygons-have-full-marked-low-dimensional-counts]] [[lem-os-disk-and-polygon-analytic-foundations]]

[F3] The actual constant-root inverse, torus mean inverse and supported dipole responses, and the exhaustive torus-target plumbing calculation are available. We use the displayed responses of ordinary stabilization, not its conclusion for a cancelling $S^3$ handle, and check below the changed two-crossing torus and marked-point transfer. [[lem-transverse-linear-strip-cauchy-riemann-isomorphism]] [[lem-real-boundary-strip-cauchy-riemann-inverse-with-free-end-constants]] [[lem-flat-complex-torus-cauchy-riemann-mean-inverse-and-normalized-dipoles]] [[thm-balanced-knot-ordinary-stabilization-has-full-minus-inverse-maps]]

[F4] Same-handlebody top generators are actual cycles; their top products have count one and no positive marked terms. Full-minus auxiliary and attaching-move maps have finite polynomial filtered inverses and inverse homotopies. [[lem-same-handlebody-model-top-counts-have-no-positive-marked-terms]] [[thm-balanced-knot-full-minus-auxiliary-continuations-are-filtered-equivalences]] [[thm-balanced-knot-attaching-moves-have-full-minus-inverse-maps]] Its actual small-copy operation retains one positive core in each old region, balances exact-copy lunes, and proves the unique nearest thin triangle by a bounded scalar inverse. [[thm-globally-weak-hat-handleslides-have-explicit-inverse-homotopies]], Proof3.1–6.1.

[F5] The polygon relative index identifies actual Spin-c differences, rather than formal domains only. The negative modified Morse field on the knot exterior has the explicit zero-relative-Euler zero-surgery cap. Its normalized Alexander value is half the relative Euler number of its perpendicular plane on the exterior Seifert surface, with boundary section $\partial_\lambda=-\partial_\theta$; the cap contributes zero. The local tube model is $f=\sin t(1-r^2/2)$, its selected generator trajectory modifications are outside that tube, and its value is preserved by followed mark-free attaching isotopies. The normalized full-minus comparisons preserve this absolute origin and the degree-zero total-hat Maslov origin. [[lem-doubly-pointed-knot-morse-fields-have-a-zero-framed-seifert-extension]] [[thm-doubly-pointed-s-three-moves-preserve-the-seifert-normalized-filtration]] [[thm-handle-cancellation]] [[lem-heegaard-polygon-spin-c-difference-is-the-capped-periodic-domain]] [[lem-heegaard-polygon-relative-maslov-variation-is-chern-plus-marks]]

[F6] Finite filtered complexes with one-dimensional total homology have additive tensor threshold. The fixed oriented boundary gluing represents the well-defined oriented connected sum.
