contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $S$ be a connected compact smooth oriented surface properly embedded in $S^3\times[0,1]$, with product collars and oriented boundary $-K_0\times\{0\}\sqcup K_1\times\{1\}$ for smooth oriented knots $K_0,K_1$. Let $g$ be the genus of $S$, and use the standard absolute Alexander normalization for the endpoint knot Floer complexes. Then
$$|\tau(K_1)-\tau(K_0)|\le g.$$
In particular, a smooth concordance annulus gives equal tau values, and a genus-$g$ surface from a knot to the unknot gives the four-ball genus estimate.

facts:
**Given:** The Axiom of Countable Choice, the collared smooth oriented cobordism $S$, its endpoint knots, and the fixed Alexander normalization.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]] states that every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function; the declared movie and diagram route uses this axiom.

[F1] [[thm-grid-homology-independent-of-grid-and-equals-knot-floer]] supplies the retained normalized full filtered grid/analytic comparison, including the actual chosen-variable versus collapsed-variable stabilization factors. That completed interface is reused without reading its proof; the historical grid hold is not a current missing input here.

[F2] [[lem-knot-floer-holomorphic-triangle-transversality-compactness-gluing]] supplies actual full-marked triangle regularity, finite counts, compactified boundaries, gluing and fixed-end auxiliary-data homotopies on its explicit positive-rank generic representatives with transported Spin-c and strict admissibility, and on the direct rank-zero point model. Its bilinear chain-map equation requires an actual cycle for a distinguished inserted top input. It does not assert an absolute Alexander shift or large-surgery nonvanishing.

[F3] [[lem-rational-heegaard-floer-absolute-grading-and-cobordism-maps]] supplies actual fixed-Spin-c infinity/plus cobordism maps between rational homology spheres, their handle-presentation independence and the absolute Maslov degree $(c_1^2-2\chi-3\sigma)/4$. This completed grading interface is reused directly. The theorem's degree is a Maslov degree, not a knot Alexander-filtration bound; it does not identify a knot large-surgery threshold or assert an adjunction inequality for every embedded surface.

[F4] [[lem-tau-threshold-under-nonzero-filtered-maps]] supplies the exact finite algebra: nonzero maps on one-dimensional total hat homology with filtration shift at most $g$ in both directions imply $|\tau(K_1)-\tau(K_0)|\le g$.

[F5] [[lem-tau-connected-sum-filtered-tensor-product]] and [[lem-tau-additive-for-filtered-tensor-products]] supply additivity of the normalized threshold. [[lem-knot-floer-duality-and-filtration-swap]] supplies normalized reverse-mirror duality; the finite annihilator-functional calculation gives $\tau(-K)=-\tau(K)$.

[E1] **External input, authorized by the run-specific source boundary.** Ozsváth–Szabó, *Knot Floer homology and the four-ball genus*, Geometry & Topology 7 (2003), Proposition 3.1, printed pp.625–626 (§3.1), gives the following actual finite-diagram statement. For a fixed knot $K\subset S^3$, normalized knot complex, and integer $m<\tau(K)$, choose a sufficiently large finite positive integer $n$. The map on $\widehat{HF}$ for the negative-$n$ two-handle trace $X_{-n}(K)$, in the actual Spin-c class $\mathfrak s_m$ with
$$\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_m),[\widehat F]\rangle-n=2m,$$
is nonzero on the $S^3$ generator. The large-surgery identification is the finite subquotient $C\{\min(i,j-m)=0\}$ with its displayed map; this is an external knot-filtration identification, not a consequence of the retained rational Maslov formula [F3]. No assertion at $m=\tau$ is needed. The proof uses the normalized filtered inclusion/quotient exact diagram and the large-surgery identification cited there.

[E2] **External input, at the same fixed compact trace scope.** In the proof of Theorem 1.1, printed pp.630–631 (§3.4), using Lemma 3.5, pp.629–630, the following vanishing is proved. Cap an actual smooth connected genus-$h>0$ spanning surface in $B^4$ by the core in $X_{-n}(K)$. Its closed cap has square $-n$. If a fixed Spin-c extension has Chern evaluation $n+2m$ on that cap and $2m>2h-2$, the corresponding trace map on $\widehat{HF}$ is zero. The mechanism is the actual tubular disk bundle of the capped surface, punctured at the incoming ball; its map vanishes when $\langle c_1,[\widehat F]\rangle+[\widehat F]^2>2h-2$, and the trace map factors through it. This imports the stated fixed-map factorization/vanishing, not merely the numerical degree-shift formula. Only the trace with ambient $B^4$ is used: no Donaldson diagonalization, arbitrary negative-definite four-manifold, or uncountable family of bundle choices is imported.

[E3] **Coefficient and choice scope of the imports.** The trace statements [E1, E2] are used for individually specified finite admissible diagrams, a finite integer $n$, and finitely many compact handles, with coefficients $\mathbb F_2$. Hom, *A survey on Heegaard Floer homology and concordance*, arXiv:1512.00383v3, explicitly fixes $\mathbb F_2$ coefficients on printed p.2; §3.1, Theorem 3.1(2) and §3.2.1, Theorem 3.4, printed pp.8–9, record respectively the same normalized genus inequality and the actual large-surgery map. This resolves the coefficient convention; it is not an integral rank calculation.

The CC use is the following bounded specialization of the published construction. A particular smooth compact surface, its finite handle description, and a particular endpoint diagram are fixed before the construction. Its capped surface, tubular bundle, and the two trace decompositions use finitely many charts, collars and handles. The relative homotopy, periodic-domain and Spin-c labels of each finite Heegaard multi-diagram are countable. The moduli-space data for those labels and the finitely many required count/homotopy identities are exactly the retained CC analytic inputs [F2], not a simultaneous choice over all knots or all smooth four-manifolds. The large integer $n$ is one witness for the single $m$ used, and all ensuing matrices and Chern evaluations are finite. The proof of [E1] is an exact diagram of these finite chain maps; the proof of [E2] is the disk-bundle calculation and these finite handle compositions. Thus the imported operations here require only the given CC analytic choices and finitely many geometric choices. This is an audit of that fixed-trace specialization, not a blanket inference that a theorem proved under full Choice is valid under CC, and not a local reconstruction of the imported large-surgery or disk-bundle calculations.

Actual source extent: Proposition 3.1 and its full proof, printed pp.625–626; Lemmas 3.4–3.5 and their full proofs, pp.628–630; both genus cases in §3.4 and the Corollary 1.3 deduction in §3.5, pp.630–632; Theorem 1.1/Corollary 1.3 on p.617; Hom's coefficient convention and the cited pp.8–9. No whole-paper reading is claimed.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $(W,\Sigma,\mathcal A)$ be a decorated knot cobordism between doubly pointed knots in $S^3$, and let $\mathfrak s\in\operatorname{Spin}^c(W)$. The representative maps from any two parametrized Kirby decompositions and admissible regular Heegaard choices are filtered $\mathbb F_2[U,V]$-equivariantly chain homotopic. If the decorated cobordism is a composite of $(W_1,\Sigma_1,\mathcal A_1)$ followed by $(W_2,\Sigma_2,\mathcal A_2)$, then for fixed Spin-c structures $\mathfrak s_i$ on $W_i$,
$$
\widetilde F_{W_2,\Sigma_2,\mathcal A_2,\mathfrak s_2}\circ \widetilde F_{W_1,\Sigma_1,\mathcal A_1,\mathfrak s_1} \simeq \sum_{\substack{\mathfrak s\in\operatorname{Spin}^c(W)\\ \mathfrak s|_{W_i}=\mathfrak s_i,\ i=1,2}} \widetilde F_{W,\Sigma,\mathcal A,\mathfrak s}.
$$
The sum is over Spin-c structures on the glued cobordism restricting to the specified structures on the two pieces. For $W=S^3\times[0,1]$, $\operatorname{Spin}^c(W)$ has one element, so the sum has one term and the composition law is ordinary composition up to filtered equivariant chain homotopy.

facts:
[F1] **External full naturality theorem.** Zemke, arXiv:1610.05207v3, Theorem A (p.3), gives a fixed-Spin-c $\mathbb Z^P$-filtered $\mathbb F_2[X_p:p\in P]$-equivariant chain map, invariant under diffeomorphism up to filtered equivariant chain homotopy. Diagram changes are compared by the transitive system of Definition 2.15 and Proposition 3.5 (§§2.2 and 3.3, pp.11–14). Theorem 11.5 and its proof (pp.74 and 84–85), followed by Theorem A' and its fourteen-move proof (§12.4, pp.91–95), supply changes of parametrized Kirby decomposition. Definition 12.8, Lemma 12.9 and the final proof of Theorem A (§12.5, pp.95–97) supply empty-end puncturing and its independence. These are imported results; their move checks are not claimed as locally reconstructed. ([Source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1610.05207v3))

[F2] **External Spin-c composition theorem.** Zemke, Theorem B (pp.3 and 97–98), gives the exact extension-sum formula in the Statement. Its proof stacks decompositions, reorders the elementary maps, applies the two-handle composition law (Proposition 5.10, p.43), and handles empty ends by puncturing. The sum and its chain-homotopy interpretation are part of this imported theorem; no unique global extension is assumed in a general gluing. ([Source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1610.05207v3))

[F3] The map Definition binds these imports to the specified full dividing-set category and to the two-color specialization, with actual representatives of the required auxiliary homology classes and natural endpoint transition maps. Its explicit finite/countable choice specialization supplies the stated CC scope; the publication is not assumed to have made that foundations analysis itself. The existing local analytic triangle theorem is preserved at its stated scope and is not used as a substitute for [F1] or [F2]. ([[def-knot-floer-cobordism-map]])

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For every smooth oriented knot $K$ in the standard oriented three-sphere, the common normalized filtered knot Floer threshold $\tau(K)$ is independent of the admissible diagram and is invariant under smooth concordance. For all smooth oriented knots $K,J$, it satisfies
$$\tau(K\#J)=\tau(K)+\tau(J).$$
If $g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$ is the minimum genus of a smooth compact connected oriented properly embedded surface in the four-ball with boundary $K$, then
$$|\tau(K)|\le g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K).$$

facts:
**Given:** The Axiom of Countable Choice, smooth oriented knots, and the standard normalized filtered knot Floer models.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]] states that every sequence of nonempty sets admits a choice function; this is the axiom branch used by the slice-genus minimum and the finite diagram choices.

[F1] [[lem-tau-of-the-unknot-is-zero]] computes the normalized tau value of the standard unknot as zero.

[F2] [[lem-smooth-and-topological-slice-genus-minima-exist]] proves that the nonempty set of smooth slice-surface genera has a least element under its stated countable-choice branch.

[F3] [[lem-puncturing-smooth-four-ball-surfaces-gives-genus-preserving-knot-cobordisms]] moves an interior point of a smooth properly embedded genus-$g$ four-ball surface to zero, flattens it near zero by supported ambient isotopies, and removes a sufficiently small actual round ball. The explicitly concentric shell is $S^3\times[0,1]$ and the residual surface is a connected genus-$g$ smooth cobordism with product collars between its boundary knot and a standard unknot. It fixes a sufficiently small restriction of the supplied outer collar, not an arbitrary entire collar.

[F4] The normalized knot/grid and analytic comparisons supply diagram independence, the actual hat threshold, and common absolute Alexander normalization. [[lem-tau-is-independent-of-heegaard-grid]]

[F6] The genus-$g$ inequality $|\tau(K_1)-\tau(K_0)|\le g$ is supplied for the actual smooth oriented knot cobordism with its product collars. Its proof explicitly imports the fixed large-negative-surgery nonvanishing and trace-cap vanishing operations from Ozsváth–Szabó, Proposition3.1, Lemma3.5 and the proof of Theorem1.1, and gives the finite-data ACω specialization and local integer/surface argument. It does not claim a completed general decorated-movie construction. [[lem-knot-floer-large-surgery-and-filtered-cobordism-input]]

[F5] The full supplied filtered connected-sum tensor comparison gives tau additivity in the same normalization. [[lem-tau-connected-sum-filtered-tensor-product]]

contract.heading: Example
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $U$ be the standard unknot, let $T_{2,3}$ be the closure of the positive two-strand braid with three crossings, and let $T_{2,3}^{\dagger}$ be its reverse mirror. In the normalized right-trefoil staircase over $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$, generators $a,b,c$ have Maslov gradings $0,-1,-2$, Alexander levels $1,0,-1$, and differential $\partial b=Ua+c$, $\partial a=\partial c=0$; multiplication by $U$ lowers both filtrations by one. Choose the polynomial minus lattice $C^-=\mathbb F_2[U]\langle a,b,c\rangle$ inside this Laurent complex, with each displayed generator at first filtration coordinate zero. Its hat complex is the quotient $C^-/UC^-$; setting $U=0$ refers to this lattice quotient, not to the Laurent complex in which $U$ is invertible. The full reverse-mirror Laurent staircase is the filtered dual, with generators $a^\vee,b^\vee,c^\vee$ at Alexander levels $-1,0,1$ and differential $\partial a^\vee=Ub^\vee$, $\partial c^\vee=b^\vee$, $\partial b^\vee=0$. Its chosen polynomial dual lattice has hat quotient with $\partial c^\vee=b^\vee$ and $\partial a^\vee=\partial b^\vee=0$. The normalized unknot complex has one generator at level zero and zero differential. These models give
$$\tau(U)=0,\qquad \tau(T_{2,3})=1,\qquad \tau(T_{2,3}^{\dagger})=-1.$$
Both trefoils have smooth four-ball genus one.

facts:
**Given:** The standard unknot, the positive right-handed trefoil, its reverse mirror, and Countable Choice. The displayed staircases are conclusions to be identified, not additional geometric hypotheses.

[F1] [[def-knot-floer-filtration-and-tau]] defines the normalized threshold by the first nonzero filtered inclusion into total hat homology.

[F2] [[lem-tau-of-the-unknot-is-zero]] supplies the normalized one-generator unknot complex.

[F3] [[lem-diagonal-five-grid-filtered-staircase-reduction]] supplies the complete finite calculation for the grid $O_r=(r+1/2,r+1/2)$, $X_r=((r+2)\bmod5+1/2,r+1/2)$: its all-variable-zero filtered complex is $S_-\otimes V^{\otimes4}$, where $S_-$ has $(M,A)=(0,-1),(1,0),(2,1)$ and only $\partial c=b$. contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Work over $\mathbb F_2=\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $C=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$ be its finitely generated free $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ chain complex with Maslov grading $M$ and bifiltration coordinates $(i,j)$. Multiplication by $U$ lowers each filtration coordinate by one and lowers $M$ by two; the differential lowers $M$ by one and does not increase either filtration. The total homology is $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ with its generator normalized in Maslov grading zero.

For a filtration region $R$, write $C\{R\}$ for the corresponding subquotient of the bifiltered complex; in particular $C\{i=0\}$ is the vertical complex, $C\{j=s\}$ is the horizontal complex at Alexander level $s$, and $C\{i=0,j\le s\}$ is the subcomplex of the vertical complex at levels at most $s$. Define
$$ \tau(C)=\min\{s\in\mathbb Z: H_*(C\{i=0,j\le s\})\longrightarrow H_*(C\{i=0\})\text{ is nonzero} \}. $$
For each integer $s$, let $F_s$ be the homology map induced by the chain map from $C\{i=0\}$ to $C\{\min(i,j-s)=0\}$ obtained by quotienting by $C\{i=0,j<s\}$ and then including the quotient. Let $G_s$ be the homology map from $C\{\max(i,j-s)=0\}$ to $C\{i=0\}$ obtained by quotienting by $C\{i<0,j=s\}$ and then including. The epsilon invariant is
$$ \epsilon(C)=\begin{cases} 1,&F_{\tau(C)}=0,\\ -1,&G_{\tau(C)}=0,\\ 0,&F_{\tau(C)}\ne0\text{ and }G_{\tau(C)}\ne0. \end{cases} $$
Here zero and nonzero refer to the induced homology maps. This definition fixes the sign convention; invariance under stable equivalence is a separate claim.

facts:

[F1] [[lem-bifiltered-two-hook-maps-cannot-both-vanish]] proves that a vertical class represented at $j\le s$ and killed by $F_s$ is in the image of $G_s$, by explicit northeast/southwest hook projections. It uses no simultaneous horizontal simplification theorem.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and $C=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$ a finitely generated free $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ complex. Choose a finite homogeneous basis $\{x_r\}$, with $M(x_r)$ and Alexander filtration $A(x_r)$. The translate $U^k x_r$ has Maslov grading $M(x_r)-2k$ and filtration coordinates $(i,j)=(-k,A(x_r)-k)$. The total homology is $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$; use the standard normalization in which its Maslov-zero tower generator first appears at algebraic filtration level $i=0$, and denote it by $\xi_K$.

For $t\in[0,2]$ and a nonzero finite chain $z$, define
$$ F_t(U^k x_r)=(1-t/2)(-k)+(t/2)(A(x_r)-k),\qquad F_t(z)=\max\{F_t(U^k x_r):U^k x_r\text{ has nonzero coefficient in }z\}. $$
Let $\mathcal Z_0(C)$ be the set of Maslov-zero cycles representing $\xi_K$. Set
$$ \nu_t(C)=\min_{z\in\mathcal Z_0(C)}F_t(z),\qquad \Upsilon_K(t)=-2\nu_t(C). $$
The minimum is over cycles representing the normalized homology generator, not over individual basis terms. For comparison, let $C^-(K)$ be the $\mathbb F_2[U]$-span of the chosen basis and form its $t$-modified complex over the ring $\mathcal R$ of formal sums $\sum_{\alpha\in S}c_\alpha v^\alpha$ whose support $S\subset[0,\infty)$ is well-ordered (every nonempty subset of $S$ has a least element). The coefficient extension uses $U=v^2$. In the extended Laurent complex, $v$ lowers both filtration coordinates by $1/2$ and Maslov grading by one, so a diagonal $U$-translation lowers the extended $t$-grading by two. On arbitrary homogeneous Laurent terms this grading is $M-t(j-i)$; the formula $M-tA$ below is specified on the chosen generators at $i=0$. A homogeneous generator $x$ has $t$-grading $M(x)-tA(x)$, extended by $\operatorname{gr}_t(v^\alpha x)=\operatorname{gr}_t(x)-\alpha$. If a term $U^k y$ occurs in $\partial x$, its $t$-modified differential coefficient is $v^{\operatorname{gr}_t(y)-\operatorname{gr}_t(x)+1}$; thus for $\partial x=\sum_y c_{xy}U^{(M(y)-M(x)+1)/2}y$, define $\partial_t x=\sum_y c_{xy}v^{\operatorname{gr}_t(y)-\operatorname{gr}_t(x)+1}y$. This differential lowers $t$-grading by one. The comparison between its non-torsion tower grading and the finite cycle minimum is the separate filtered tower-splitting claim.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $G$ be an $n\times n$ toroidal grid diagram representing a knot. Let $GC^-(G)$ be the finite grid complex over $\mathbb F_2[U_1,\ldots,U_n]$ with its Maslov grading $M$ and Alexander filtration $A$. Form the diagonal quotient
$$ D_G=GC^-(G)/(U_1-U_2,\ldots,U_1-U_n), $$
regarded as a finitely generated $\mathbb F_2[U]$ complex with $U=U_1=\cdots=U_n$.

For a finitely generated Maslov-graded, Alexander-filtered complex $D$ over $\mathbb F_2[U]$ with a fixed finite homogeneous basis, its $t$-modified complex for $t\in[0,2]$ is the free $\mathcal R$-module on that basis, where $\mathcal R$ is the ring of formal $\mathbb F_2$-series $\sum_{\alpha\in A}c_\alpha v^\alpha$ with support $A\subset[0,\infty)$ such that every nonempty subset of $A$ has a least element. A homogeneous generator $x$ has $t$-grading $\operatorname{gr}_t(x)=M(x)-tA(x)$, extended by $\operatorname{gr}_t(v^\alpha x)=\operatorname{gr}_t(x)-\alpha$. The coefficient extension uses $U=v^2$; this action lowers the extended $t$-grading by two. The formula $M-tA$ is specified on the chosen polynomial generators. On Laurent translates, the extended grading is $M-t(j-i)$, with $v$ lowering both filtration coordinates by $1/2$. If
$$ \partial x=\sum_y c_{xy}U^{(M(y)-M(x)+1)/2}y, $$
then the modified differential is
$$ \partial_t x=\sum_y c_{xy}v^{\operatorname{gr}_t(y)-\operatorname{gr}_t(x)+1}y. $$
A homogeneous homology class is **non-torsion** if no nonzero element of $\mathcal R$ annihilates it. For $0\le t\le1$, define $\Upsilon_G(t)$ to be the maximum $t$-grading of a homogeneous non-torsion class in $H_*(D_G^t)$. For $1<t\le2$, define $\Upsilon_G(t)=\Upsilon_G(2-t)$. This is the grid convention compared with the original cycle-minimax invariant.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $C(K)=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$ have a finite homogeneous basis $x_1,\ldots,x_m$ with Maslov grading $M(x_r)$ and Alexander filtration $A(x_r)$. Let $C^-(K)$ be the subcomplex spanned over $\mathbb F_2[U]$ by $U^n x_r$ for $n\ge0$, with $M(U^n x_r)=M(x_r)-2n$ and $A(U^n x_r)=A(x_r)-n$, and assume $H_*(C^-(K))\cong\mathbb F_2[U]$ with generator in Maslov degree zero. For each integer $s$, let $\mathcal A(K,s)$ be the subcomplex spanned over $\mathbb F_2$ by those terms $U^n x_r$ with $n\ge0$ and $A(x_r)-n\le s$. For any Maslov-graded $\mathbb F_2[U]$ complex $D$, let $\delta(D)$ be the maximal Maslov grading of a homogeneous non-torsion class in $H_*(D)$, with $\delta(D)=-\infty$ if no such class exists. Define $\nu^-(K)$ to be the least integer $s$ for which $\delta(\mathcal A(K,s))=0$. Then
$$ 0\le \nu^-(K)\le g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K), $$
where $g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$ is the minimum genus of a smooth compact connected oriented properly embedded surface in the four-ball bounded by $K$.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $G$ be any $n\times n$ grid diagram representing a smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$. Form the diagonal grid complex by setting every marking variable $U_i$ equal to a single variable $U$, and define $\Upsilon_G(t)$ by the t-modified non-torsion grading on that complex for $0\le t\le1$, extended by $\Upsilon_G(t)=\Upsilon_G(2-t)$ for $1<t\le2$. Then for every $t\in[0,2]$,
$$ \Upsilon_G(t)=\Upsilon_K(t), $$
where $\Upsilon_K$ is the finite cycle-minimax invariant defined from $\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$. In this statement the quotient with all $U_i$ identified carries the factor $W^{\otimes(n-1)}$, where $W$ has generators in Maslov/Alexander bidegrees $(0,0)$ and $(-1,-1)$; this factor is retained in the proof and is not counted as an improvement to the grid-state complexity bound.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $G$ be a toroidal grid representing one oriented knot, and let $\partial^-$ be the full filtered minus differential over $\mathbb F_2[U_1,\ldots,U_n]$. Call $O_i$ and $O_j$ consecutive when the $X$-marking in the row of $O_i$ lies in the column of $O_j$. Let $X_\ell$ be that marking and define the module map
$$H_\ell(\mathbf x)=\sum_{\mathbf y}\sum_{\substack{r\in\operatorname{Rect}^{\circ}(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)\\X_\ell\in\operatorname{Int}(r)}}\left(\prod_{a=1}^{n}U_a^{O_a(r)}\right)\mathbf y.$$
Then $\partial^-H_\ell+H_\ell\partial^-=(U_i+U_j)\operatorname{id}$. The map $H_\ell$ has Maslov degree $-1$ and does not raise the Alexander filtration. Consequently multiplication by any two variables $U_i,U_j$ is filtered chain homotopic, since the consecutive relation follows the single cycle of the knot grid.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $K$ and $J$ be smooth oriented knots, and use the epsilon sign convention from the preceding definition. If their knot Floer complexes are stably filtered equivalent, meaning that there are totally acyclic bifiltered complexes $A$ and $B$ with $\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)\oplus A$ filtered-chain-homotopy equivalent to $\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(J)\oplus B$, then $\epsilon(K)=\epsilon(J)$. The acyclic summands here need not be acyclic after taking either associated-graded filtration.

The invariant satisfies $\epsilon(-K)=-\epsilon(K)$, $\epsilon(K)=0\Rightarrow\tau(K)=0$, and the tensor rules
$$ \epsilon(K)=\epsilon(J)\Rightarrow\epsilon(K\#J)=\epsilon(K),\qquad \epsilon(K)=0\Rightarrow\epsilon(K\#J)=\epsilon(J). $$
The converse of $\epsilon(K)=0\Rightarrow\tau(K)=0$ fails: the knot $T_{2,5}\#-T_{4,5}\#T_{2,3;2,5}$ has $\tau=0$ and $\epsilon=1$, where $T_{p,q}$ is the positive $(p,q)$ torus knot and $T_{2,3;2,5}$ is the $(2,5)$ cable of the right-handed trefoil with longitudinal winding two. Epsilon is not an integer-valued homomorphism on the smooth concordance group: the right-handed trefoil has $\epsilon=1$ and its connected sum with itself also has $\epsilon=1$, not $2$.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
For every smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$, the function $\Upsilon_K:[0,2]\to\mathbb R$ defined by the finite cycle minimax is continuous and piecewise linear with finitely many breakpoints, satisfies $\Upsilon_K(0)=0$ and $\Upsilon_K(t)=\Upsilon_K(2-t)$, and has right derivative $\Upsilon'_K(0+)=-\tau(K)$. For smooth oriented knots $K,J$ and $t\in[0,2]$,
$$ \Upsilon_{K\#J}(t)=\Upsilon_K(t)+\Upsilon_J(t),\qquad \Upsilon_{-K}(t)=-\Upsilon_K(t), $$
where $-K$ is the reverse mirror, the inverse under connected sum in the smooth concordance group. If $g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$ is the minimum genus of a smooth properly embedded compact connected oriented surface in the four-ball with boundary $K$, then
$$ |\Upsilon_K(t)|\le t\,g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K)\qquad(0\le t\le1). $$

**Given:** A smooth oriented knot Floer complex with its finite bifiltered basis, normalized Maslov-zero total-homology generator, and the $F_t$ cycle-minimax convention.

[F5] The full geometric connected-sum comparison supplies the actual Maslov-graded bifiltered Laurent tensor equivalence, inverse and homotopies. [[lem-tau-connected-sum-filtered-tensor-product]]

[F9] The auxiliary threshold exists and is nonnegative by its local $V_s,H_s$ exponent proof. Its smooth genus upper bound uses the explicitly external OSS/Hom–Wu theorem in the exact same delta-threshold convention, with fixed finite/countable choice scope. [[lem-upsilon-nu-minus-four-ball-bound]]

[A3] [[def-smooth-and-topological-slice-genus]]: the intended bound is the smooth four-ball genus branch; no locally flat/topological surface branch is used.

[F6] The supplied normalized doubly pointed polynomial complex $B=C\{i\le0\}$ has quotient $B/UB$ equal to the ordinary normalized hat model, whose total homology is $\mathbb F_2$ in degree zero. The differential retains every positive $z$ multiplicity as filtration. These are the accepted marked-variable/analytic knot interfaces, not arbitrary-link or cobordism assertions. [[def-knot-floer-filtration-and-tau]], [[thm-grid-homology-independent-of-grid-and-equals-knot-floer]], [[lem-heegaard-floer-holomorphic-disk-regularity-compactness-gluing]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sm}}$ be the smooth knot concordance group, with addition induced by oriented connected sum and inverse represented by reverse mirror. The function $\epsilon: \mathcal C_{\mathrm{sm}}\to\{-1,0,1\}$ is well-defined and concordance-invariant, but it is not a homomorphism to $\mathbb Z$. The map
$$ \Upsilon:\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sm}}\longrightarrow \mathrm{PL}([0,2],\mathbb R),\qquad [K]\longmapsto\Upsilon_K, $$
is a group homomorphism, where $\mathrm{PL}([0,2],\mathbb R)$ is the abelian group of continuous piecewise-linear real-valued functions under pointwise addition. For every representative $K$ and $0\le t\le1$, its value satisfies $|\Upsilon_K(t)|\le t\,g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$.

**Given:** The smooth concordance group, the epsilon invariant, the Upsilon function, and the smooth four-ball genus with the conventions stated above.

[F1] [[thm-knot-concordance-is-an-abelian-group]]: in the smooth branch, the operation is oriented connected sum, the inverse is reverse mirror, and a class is zero precisely when represented by a smoothly slice knot. The smooth proof branch was inspected; the topological branch is not used.

[F2] The Upsilon supplier proves its model invariance, finite piecewise linearity, reflection, tensor additivity, mirror sign and initial slope. Its smooth four-ball genus clause uses the explicitly external OSS/Hom–Wu nu-minus bound recorded there. [[thm-upsilon-additivity-mirror-and-genus-bound]]

[F3] The completed epsilon supplier gives its actual stable-core/hook trichotomy, stable-equivalence invariance, normalized conjugation/dual sign and tensor rules, and admitted trefoil and torus/cable witnesses. In particular the trefoil and its double both have epsilon1, proving integer nonadditivity. This does not itself prove smooth-concordance descent. [[lem-epsilon-stable-equivalence-and-not-a-homomorphism]]

[F4] Smooth concordance implies stable filtered equivalence using the explicitly external Hom slice splitting and the preserved local finite tensor-stabilization argument. Its actual normalized model and tensor interfaces are supplied. [[thm-smooth-concordance-implies-stable-filtered-knot-floer-equivalence]]

contract.heading: Example
contract.text:
Let $T_{2,3}$ be the right-handed trefoil and $-T_{2,3}$ its reverse mirror. A filtered basis for $\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(T_{2,3})$ is $x_0,x_1,x_2$ with $(M,A)(x_0)=(0,1)$, $(M,A)(x_1)=(-1,0)$, $(M,A)(x_2)=(-2,-1)$ and differential $\partial x_1=Ux_0+x_2$, $\partial x_0=\partial x_2=0$. Under the conventions of this page,
$$ \epsilon(T_{2,3})=1,\qquad \Upsilon_{T_{2,3}}(t)=\begin{cases}-t,&0\le t\le1,\\ t-2,&1\le t\le2.\end{cases} $$
The graph has its unique interior breakpoint at $t=1$. For the reverse mirror, $\epsilon(-T_{2,3})=-1$ and $\Upsilon_{-T_{2,3}}(t)=-\Upsilon_{T_{2,3}}(t)$.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Let $K$ be a null-homologous knot in a closed connected oriented $3$-manifold $Y$, let $F$ be a genus-$g$ Seifert surface, and let $(M,\gamma)$ be the balanced sutured manifold obtained by cutting the compact exterior of $K$ along $F$. Under the hypotheses of a horizontal decomposition, the induced chain map realizes Ni's horizontal decomposition formula. Under the hypotheses of a separating product annulus with connected $R_+$ and $R_-$, the induced chain map realizes Ni's product-annulus tensor formula. These assertions use the specified basepoint domains, periodic-domain admissibility, and exact characteristic-product-region hypotheses; they make no claim that generic Heegaard disk existence alone supplies the decomposition maps.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot, and let $g(K)$ be the least genus of a compact connected oriented embedded surface in $S^3$ with boundary $K$. With the integral Alexander normalization, the maximum Alexander grading in which the hat knot Floer homology of $K$ is nonzero is $g(K)$:

$$g(K)=\max\{i\in\mathbb Z:\widehat{\mathrm{HFK}}(S^3,K,i;\mathbb Z)\ne0\}.$$

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Let $K$ be a null-homologous knot in a closed connected oriented $3$-manifold $Y$, let $Y\setminus K$ be irreducible, and let $F$ be a genus-$g$ Seifert surface. If the integral top Alexander group $\widehat{\mathrm{HFK}}(Y,K,[F],g;\mathbb Z)$ is isomorphic to $\mathbb Z$, then the sutured manifold obtained by cutting the compact knot exterior along $F$ is a product sutured manifold. The argument uses Ni's homology-product reduction, the horizontal and separating product-annulus decompositions, the characteristic product region, and Gabai's taut-foliation input under their stated hypotheses.

**Given:** The knot, exterior, surface and integral group in the Statement. Full Choice is available through [[def-axiom-of-choice]]. A Seifert surface is connected, compact, oriented and properly embedded in the compact exterior, with its one boundary component the preferred longitude.

[F1] The resolved signed top/outer comparison in [[lem-ni-holomorphic-disk-and-jsj-analytic-inputs]] identifies the actual grading-$g$ complex with the actual $F$-cut complex, with its induced coherent orientation class. Thus it identifies their integral homologies. This is also the exact external Theorem 1.5 of Juhász, *Floer homology and surface decompositions*, published p.300, for a null-homologous knot in any closed connected oriented $Y$ and any Seifert surface $F$; no three-sphere or rational-homology-sphere hypothesis occurs.

Corollary 7 says that the characteristic product pair then surjects onto $H_1(M)$. The corrected main proof on p.3 supplies the product reduction in the original arbitrary-$Y$ setting. contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $K$ be a null-homologous knot in a closed connected oriented $3$-manifold $Y$, and suppose that the knot complement $Y\setminus K$ is irreducible. Let $F$ be a genus-$g$ Seifert surface for $K$. If the integral top Alexander group satisfies

$$\widehat{\mathrm{HFK}}(Y,K,[F],g;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z,$$

then $Y\setminus K$ fibers over $S^1$ with fiber $F$.

**Given:** The knot, exterior, actual surface $F$ and integral grading-$g$ group in the Statement.

[F1] Under exactly these hypotheses, [[lem-ni-fiberedness-sutured-floer-and-gabai-inputs]] proves that the compact exterior cut along the actual $F$ is a product sutured manifold. Its proof explicitly imports the general balanced sutured vanishing and nonproduct rank results and records Ni's corrected characteristic-pair formulation; the resolved local signed comparison and hierarchy dependencies are preserved.

contract.heading: Example
contract.text: For the right-handed trefoil $T(2,3)$, the symmetrized Alexander polynomial is $t-1+t^{-1}$, the maximum Alexander grading is $1$, the integral top knot Floer group is $\mathbb Z$, and the knot is fibered. For the standard alternating knot $5_2$, the symmetrized Alexander polynomial is $2t-3+2t^{-1}$, the maximum Alexander grading is $1$, the integral top knot Floer group is $\mathbb Z^2$, and the knot is not fibered. The $5_2$ rank calculation uses the alternating-knot formula; its signature determines the Maslov grading shift.

facts:
**Given:** The right-handed trefoil and standard alternating knot $5_2$ with the original integral normalization and classical choice branch declared in the dependencies.

[E1] **External input.** Ozsváth–Szabó, *Heegaard Floer homology and alternating knots*, Geometry & Topology 7 (2003), Theorem 1.3, printed p.230 (PDF p.6 of arXiv:math/0209149v3): if $K$ is alternating and its normalized symmetric Alexander polynomial is $a_0+\sum_{s>0}a_s(t^s+t^{-s})$, then
$$\widehat{HFK}(S^3,K,s;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^{|a_s|},$$
supported in Maslov degree $s+\sigma(K)/2$. This is the INTEGRAL theorem, including freeness; no integral conclusion is inferred from the retained mod-two grid comparison. Its signature convention has left trefoil signature $+2$.

[E2] **External finite table input.** Knot Atlas, pages `3_1` and `5_2`, section “Polynomial invariants / Alexander polynomial”, records respectively $t-1+t^{-1}$ and $2t-3+2t^{-1}$. These two finite entries and their standard knot diagrams identify the table knots. The same polynomials result from the standard genus-one disk/band Seifert matrices
$$V_3=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad V_5=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&2\end{pmatrix}$$
(up to simultaneous handedness/sign conventions): $\det(V_3-tV_3^T)=1-t+t^2$ and $\det(V_5-tV_5^T)=2-3t+2t^2$. Multiplying by $t^{-1}$ gives the stated symmetric polynomials. The TABLE/diagram identification is external input; the two determinant calculations are finite local checks, not an assertion that an abstract matrix by itself identifies a knot.

[E3] **External input at the exact $S^3$, integral scope.** Manolescu, *An Introduction to Knot Floer Homology*, printed/PDF p.5, Theorem 2.3, gives $g(K)=\max\{s:\widehat{HFK}(K,s;\mathbb Z)\ne0\}$ for every knot in $S^3$. Theorem 2.5 on that same page gives that a knot in $S^3$ is fibered if and only if its integral top genus group is $\mathbb Z$. These exact specializations of the established Ozsváth–Szabó/Ghiggini/Ni/Juhász results are imported. This does not assert completion of the held local general-$Y$ signed comparison or product-criterion proofs. The source explicitly states these as integral groups.

These are explicitly authorized external imports under the run-specific source boundary. The original full-choice branch is retained; no integral full-choice theorem is silently cast as a CC theorem.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Assume full AC for the instanton constructions. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth knot with a marked point $x$ and a preferred nonzero normal vector $v$ at $x$. Choose a small disk $D$ normal to $K$ at $x$, let $L=\partial D$, and let $\omega$ be the radius of $D$ from $x$ to a point of $L$. Then $K^\natural:=K\cup L$ is the based earring link. Choose disjoint closed tubular neighborhoods $N(K)$ and $N(L)$ of its two components, set $X=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}(N(K)\cup N(L))$, and truncate the endpoints of $\omega$ at $\partial X$ to obtain $[\omega]\in H_1(X,\partial X;\mathbb Z/2)$.

Here $PU(2)=U(2)/U(1)\cong SO(3)$; a principal $PU(2)$ bundle $P\to X$ is equivalently an oriented real 3-plane bundle, and $w_2(P)\in H^2(X;\mathbb Z/2)$ denotes its second Stiefel–Whitney class. Poincaré–Lefschetz duality for the oriented compact 3-manifold $X$ with boundary is the isomorphism $PD:H_1(X,\partial X;\mathbb Z/2)\to H^2(X;\mathbb Z/2)$. Include a bundle $P$ with $w_2(P)=PD([\omega])$ in the singular bundle data.

In a local meridional angular coordinate $\theta$, an $SU(2)$ lift of the singular connection has the standard model $A_0+\frac14\begin{pmatrix}i&0\\0&-i\end{pmatrix}d\theta$, where $A_0$ is smooth in an $O(2)$ reduction. Parallel transport (holonomy) around either meridian is conjugate in $SU(2)$ to $\operatorname{diag}(i,-i)$; its image has order two in $PU(2)$. Define $I^\natural(K;\mathbb Z)$ to be the singular instanton Floer homology $I^\omega(S^3,K^\natural;P)$ associated to these data by [[lem-instanton-knot-complex-asd-analytic-foundations]], which supplies its analytic complex and independence of auxiliary choices under full AC. This does not assert sutured closure independence or a distinguished canonical class.

For the sutured version, let $E_K$ be the compact knot exterior and put two oppositely oriented meridional sutures $\gamma$ on its boundary torus. Choose a connected oriented annulus $T$, attach $[-1,1]\times T$ along the annular sutured region, and glue the two resulting boundary surfaces by an orientation-compatible diffeomorphism fixing a chosen point from $T$. The result is a closed oriented 3-manifold $\bar Y$ with a distinguished torus $\bar R$; the fixed point determines a standard circle meeting $\bar R$ once. Choose a line bundle $w\to\bar Y$ whose first Chern class is Poincaré dual to that circle, so $\langle c_1(w),[\bar R]\rangle$ is odd. Let $I_*(\bar Y,w;\mathbb Q)$ denote the closed instanton Floer group with rational coefficients, using the admissible fixed-determinant theory in the external input below. For a homology class $z$ of dimension $0$ or $2$ in $\bar Y$, let $\mu(z)$ denote the standard instanton Floer operator associated to $z$; the point and surface operators commute and have degrees $4$ and $-2$, respectively. If $y\in\bar R$, define the closure group $KHI_{\bar Y,\bar R,w}(K;\mathbb Q)$ by
$$
KHI_{\bar Y,\bar R,w}(K;\mathbb Q)
:=\{a\in I_*(\bar Y,w;\mathbb Q):\mu(\bar R)a=0,\ \mu(y)a=2a\}.
$$
This is the simultaneous eigenspace with eigenvalues $(0,2)$ specified by the instanton closure convention. The closure group is considered up to isomorphism, with independence of these auxiliary choices supplied by the external input below and the stated well-definedness justifier; no canonical vector or preferred basis is part of this definition.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC and the actual based earring and marked admissible closure data in the definition. The singular complex is supplied by the preserved local analytic theorem.

[F1] **External admissible closure input.** Kronheimer–Mrowka, *Knots, sutures and excision*, arXiv:0807.4891v2, §7.1 and Definition 7.3, supplies the ordinary instanton group for a fixed determinant line bundle with odd pairing on an integral surface and the commuting point/surface operators. Definition 7.10 and its following closure-independence argument (§7.4, PDF p. 59), using Theorem 7.7 excision and Propositions 7.8–7.9, give independence of the allowed auxiliary surface and marked gluing choices. The auxiliary surface has a closed curve whose two boundary-surface copies are nonseparating; in this annular knot construction its core has that property. The marked gluing fixes the point determining the standard determinant circle. Genus one is permitted.

[F2] **External torus and coefficient normalization.** The same source's Definition 7.13 (§7.6, PDF pp. 60–61) identifies the knot group with the torus closure above and its simultaneous $(0,2)$ eigenspace; it has half the dimension of the full determinant-one ordinary group, not an additional doubled factor. The source uses complex coefficients for convenience. The rational version used here is explicitly permitted in Kronheimer–Mrowka, *Khovanov homology is an unknot-detector*, §1.1, PDF p. 3, immediately before Proposition 1.4.

These are explicit published external inputs under CLAUDE.md §12 for the current run, not a locally reconstructed ordinary all-genus/excision argument. The well-definedness theorem [[thm-sutured-instanton-khi-rank-detects-unknot]] uses these inputs with the preserved local singular construction. Its proof supplies the rank and rational bridge separately; neither a canonical element nor an integral eigenspace splitting is included in this definition.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Assume full AC. For a based smooth knot $K\subset S^3$ with the earring and admissible singular-bundle data above, let $C^
atural(K;\mathbb Z)$ be the integral singular-instanton cochain complex: its generators are regular critical points of the perturbed Chern–Simons functional on the corresponding singular configuration space, and its degree-one differential counts oriented zero-dimensional moduli spaces of trajectories for the perturbed singular anti-self-dual equation. Here finite energy is the flow energy $2\int_{\mathbb R}\|\partial_tB\|_2^2dt$ in temporal gauge, equivalently the perturbed topological energy of the relative trajectory class, rather than unrenormalized curvature energy over the infinite cylinder. The grading is relative modulo four, and the differential has degree one. Define $I^
atural(K;\mathbb Z):=H^*(C^
atural(K;\mathbb Z))$ using the analytic construction and independence of choices established in [[lem-instanton-knot-complex-asd-analytic-foundations]]. Write $I^
atural(K;\mathbb Q):=I^
atural(K;\mathbb Z)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$. The invariant class specified here is the isomorphism class of this group with its relative grading; the continuation identifications retain the declared overall sign ambiguity.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume full AC and fix a smooth based knot $K\subset S^3$ with the earring and admissible singular bundle data of the preceding definitions. For regular perturbation data, the perturbed Chern–Simons critical points and finite-energy singular anti-self-dual trajectories define a finite free cochain complex $C^\natural(K;\mathbb Z)$ with differential $d$ satisfying $d^2=0$. Its homology is independent of the chosen regular metric and perturbation up to the declared overall sign and is invariant under isotopy of the based knot data.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume full AC. Let $D$ be a finite based diagram of a smooth knot $K\subset S^3$ with ordered crossings $c_1<\cdots<c_n$. The singular instanton resolution complex admits a finite filtration whose first page, with its first differential, is isomorphic to the reduced Khovanov cube of the reflected based diagram $\overline D$. Its spectral sequence converges to $I^\natural(K;\mathbb Z)$. The cube sign at the edge changing $c_j$ is $(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}v_i}$, and the edge operation is multiplication for a merge or comultiplication for a split. Thus its $E_2$ page is the reduced integral Khovanov cohomology of $\overline D$. The claim includes coherent instanton orientations and the unlink group and saddle-map identifications; it asserts no diagram-invariance of intermediate pages.

[F4] The primitive integral unlink bases, their finite planar compatibility and actual merge/split maps are [[thm-integral-earring-unlink-saddles-are-the-reduced-frobenius-operations]]. They use no unproved general split-link excision or arbitrary concordance formula.

Its signed differential is checked in [[lem-khovanov-cube-differential-squares-to-zero]]. The finite-filtration spectral sequence is [[thm-bounded-filtered-complex-spectral-sequence-abuts-to-filtered-homology]].

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Let $(D,p)$ be a finite regular oriented diagram of a knot with a basepoint $p$ away from the crossings, and let $C(D)$ be its normalized integral Khovanov cochain complex. At each resolution state, let $X_p$ act by multiplication by $X$ on the tensor factor for the circle containing $p$, and by the identity on every other circle factor. The basepoint action is the direct sum of these statewise maps. Define the reduced cochain complex by
$$\widetilde C(D,p):=C(D)/\operatorname{im}(X_p),$$
with the same cohomological grading and with reduced quantum degree $\widetilde j=j-1$ for the class represented by a state whose basepoint circle is labelled $1$. Its cohomology is the reduced integral Khovanov cohomology $\widetilde{Kh}^{i,\widetilde j}(D,p)$. The unknot is normalized so that its reduced group lies in bidegree $(0,0)$.

Equivalently, cut the based knot at $p$ to a one-interval tangle. Put $M=\mathbb Z$ in quantum degree $0$ with $X\cdot1=0$. A resolution with $k$ closed circles and the distinguished interval is assigned $\mathcal A^{\otimes k}\otimes M$. An edge that merges a circle into the interval uses $m_M(1\otimes1)=1$ and $m_M(X\otimes1)=0$; an edge that splits the interval uses $\Delta_M(1)=X\otimes1$, where the circle factor is written first and the interval factor second. Edges not meeting the interval use $m$ or $\Delta$. This based tangle cube is the quotient complex above, with the stated quantum shift.

facts:
**Given:** A based knot diagram $(D,p)$ and the normalized integral Khovanov cochain complex defined in [[alg-khovanov-chain-complex-from-diagram]].

[F1] On a resolution circle, $X^2=0$, $\Delta(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1$, and $\Delta(X)=X\otimes X$; multiplication is the product in $\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$ ([[def-khovanov-frobenius-algebra-and-cube-of-resolutions]]).

[F2] The differential is the signed sum of edge maps, each equal to multiplication or comultiplication on the factors meeting that edge and the identity on all other factors ([[alg-khovanov-chain-complex-from-diagram]]).

[F3] The signed cube differential squares to zero, so these state modules form a cochain complex ([[lem-khovanov-cube-differential-squares-to-zero]]).

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume full AC. For every smooth knot $K\subset S^3$, the rational sutured instanton knot homology $KHI(K;\mathbb Q)$ is finite-dimensional and has dimension at least one; it has dimension one if and only if $K$ is the unknot. Moreover, excision gives an isomorphism $I^\natural(K;\mathbb Q)\cong KHI(K;\mathbb Q)$.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, a smooth classical knot $K\subset S^3$, its two oppositely oriented meridional sutures, and the chosen admissible closure from the preceding definition. Remaining established gauge-theoretic inputs below are explicitly imported under the run-specific permission in CLAUDE.md §12, not claimed as locally reconstructed proofs.

[F1] The local singular analytic construction gives the finite integral earring complex, its square-zero differential and continuation independence with the declared relative grading and overall sign convention. [[lem-instanton-knot-complex-asd-analytic-foundations]]

[F2] The local integral unknot calculation gives $I^\natural(U;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z$, hence $\dim_{\mathbb Q}I^\natural(U;\mathbb Q)=1$. Its generator is specified only up to orientation sign. [[lem-singular-earring-instanton-homology-of-the-unknot-is-integrally-rank-one]]

[F3] **External ordinary determinant-$w$ surface input.** For a closed oriented three-manifold $Y$ and a Hermitian line bundle $w$ with odd pairing on an integral surface class, use the determinant-one gauge group of a $U(2)$ lift with fixed determinant $w$. Its admissible instanton homology and commuting operators $\mu(R),\mu(y)$ are defined. For $S^1\times R$, $g(R)\ge1$, with $c_1(w)$ dual to $S^1$, the ordinary-$w$ product calculation has the spectrum in Kronheimer–Mrowka, *Knots, sutures and excision*, Proposition 7.1; the common extreme eigenspace $I_*(S^1\times R\mid R)_w$ is one-dimensional by Proposition 7.4. On the point-$+2$ kernel the extreme surface factor is simple, as stated immediately after Proposition 7.4. Corollary 7.2 and Proposition 7.5 give the surface bounds on a general admissible $Y$, including the case where $w$ pairs evenly with the other surface; Corollary 7.6 gives the simultaneous generalized-eigenspace decomposition. These are imported published all-genus ordinary-$w$ results, not consequences inferred here from an altered $u$ or $uw$ module. Locators: arXiv:0807.4891v2, §§7.1–7.2, PDF pp. 52–56.

[F4] **External excision and closure input.** Theorem 7.7 of the same source gives excision for two oriented embedded positive-equal-genus surfaces, with equal odd $c_1(w)$ evaluations, an orientation-compatible gluing diffeomorphism and its chosen determinant-bundle lift; when $Y$ is connected the two surfaces are required not to be homologous, and for two components one lies in each. The disconnected group is interpreted as a tensor product. Definition 7.10 and the closure-independence argument following it establish that the sutured group is independent, up to isomorphism, of the allowed auxiliary surface and marked gluing choices. The closure has $c_1(w)$ dual to the standard circle through the fixed auxiliary point. Genus one is permitted. In the meridional knot case Definition 7.13 identifies the annular-auxiliary closure with the torus closure; its group is precisely the simultaneous $(\mu(\bar R),\mu(y))=(0,2)$ eigenspace, equivalently the point-$+2$ half, not the doubled full Floer group. Locators: arXiv:0807.4891v2, Theorem 7.7, Definition 7.10 and its following argument, Definition 7.13, PDF pp. 56–61. The source works over $\mathbb C$ for convenience; the rational version is explicitly allowed in the detector paper's §1.1, PDF p. 3.

[F5] **External decomposition, nonvanishing and genus/rank input.** For a balanced sutured manifold decomposed along a surface $S$ with no closed components, and with the closed components of $S\cap V$ parallel oriented boundary-coherent simple closed curves for each component $V$ of $R(\gamma)$, Proposition 7.11 gives the decomposed sutured instanton group as a direct summand (the precise hypotheses of Theorem 6.8, PDF p. 48); Theorem 7.12 states that a taut balanced sutured manifold has nonzero sutured instanton homology. For a classical genus-$g$ knot, Proposition 7.16 gives $KHI(K,g)\ne0$, with the genus decomposition and its opposite extreme as in §7.6. In particular a nontrivial classical knot has $\dim KHI(K)>1$. Locators: arXiv:0807.4891v2, §§7.5–7.6, PDF pp. 59–64, and Kronheimer–Mrowka, *Khovanov homology is an unknot-detector*, §1.1, PDF p. 3, which explicitly records this rank consequence and permits $\mathbb Q$ coefficients. These decomposition/nonvanishing conclusions are imported established results; no local cap/module or taut-hierarchy proof is asserted here.

[F6] **External rational singular-to-sutured bridge.** For a based smooth knot in $S^3$, Proposition 1.4 of *Khovanov homology is an unknot-detector* states $I^\natural(K;\mathbb Q)\cong KHI(K;\mathbb Q)$. Its §5.4, Proposition 5.7, uses the actual earring link $K\cup L$ and its connecting $w_2$ arc; the two tubular-boundary tori are glued exchanging meridians and longitudes and matching the arc endpoints. The excision has a Hopf-link factor $\mathbb Z$ and the complementary torus closure. The determinant-one group and the larger gauge quotient are distinguished there: the full ordinary knot group has twice the rank, and the point-$+2$ summand is $KHI$. The stated rational bridge includes this normalization. Locators: Proposition 1.4, PDF p. 3, and §5.4, Proposition 5.7 and its following paragraphs, PDF pp. 74–75. No integral bridge or distinguished canonical vector is inferred.

contract.text: Assume full AC. For every smooth knot $K\subset S^3$, there is a finite spectral sequence of abelian groups whose $E_2$ page, after forgetting the Khovanov bigrading, is $\widetilde{Kh}(\overline K;\mathbb Z)$ and which converges to $I^\natural(K;\mathbb Z)$. contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ be an oriented knot and let $(D,p)$ and $(D',p')$ be finite regular oriented diagrams of $K$ with basepoints away from all crossings. Then the reduced integral groups $\widetilde{Kh}^{i,\widetilde j}(D,p)$ and $\widetilde{Kh}^{i,\widetilde j}(D',p')$ are isomorphic for every $(i,\widetilde j)$. In particular, they are invariant under Reidemeister moves supported away from the basepoint and under transport of the basepoint along the knot.

facts:

[F1] AC$_\omega$ is the axiom that every countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-countable-choice]]).

[F2] An isotopy of smooth embeddings of a compact knot circle extends under AC$_\omega$ to an ambient isotopy ([[thm-isotopy-extension]]).

[F3] The cut one-interval tangles of any two based diagrams of the same oriented knot admit a smooth isotopy relative to the two endpoints and collars, and a finite relative Reidemeister movie. The moving-ball and terminal Alexander-scaling constructions, and the spatial-cutoff general-position proof, are supplied by [[lem-marked-knot-cut-tangles-have-relative-reidemeister-movies]], proof steps 1.1–6.1.

[F4] Every local move away from the mark induces a bigraded chain homotopy equivalence of the reduced quotient complexes; all local chain maps and homotopies commute with $X_p$ before quotienting ([[lem-khovanov-reidemeister-chain-homotopies]]).

[F5] A cochain homotopy equivalence induces mutually inverse maps on cohomology ([[def-chain-homotopy]], [[def-chain-homotopy-equivalence]]).

contract.text: Assume full AC. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth knot. The total normalized integral reduced Khovanov cohomology is isomorphic to $\mathbb Z$ concentrated in bidegree $(0,0)$ if and only if $K$ is the unknot.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth knot with chosen exterior $E_K$ and ordered meridian-longitude basis $(\mu,\lambda)$. A **surgery triad** is a cyclically ordered triple of primitive unoriented slopes $s_0,s_1,s_\infty$ on $\partial E_K$ whose pairwise geometric intersection numbers are one, together with the oriented fillings $Y_j=E_K(s_j)$ and the three 2-handle surgery cobordisms in the cyclic order $Y_0\to Y_1\to Y_\infty\to Y_0$. Choose primitive representatives $v_j=(p_j,q_j)$ in the ordered basis $(\mu,\lambda)$ so that $\det(v_0,v_1)=\det(v_1,v_\infty)=\det(v_\infty,v_0)=1$; the cyclic order is the one for which this orientation convention holds. The geometric intersection number of $s_j$ and $s_k$ is $|p_jq_k-p_kq_j|$.

For a closed oriented Riemannian 3-manifold $Y$, a principal $SO(3)$-bundle $P\to Y$ is a locally trivial bundle with fiber $SO(3)$ and right structure-group action. A connection $A$ is a smooth right-$SO(3)$-invariant horizontal distribution on $P$ complementary to its vertical tangent spaces. In a local trivialization its curvature is $F_A=dA+\tfrac12[A\wedge A]$; it is **flat** when $F_A=0$. Let $\mathcal A(P)$ be the space of smooth connections and let $\mathcal G(P)$ be the group of bundle automorphisms covering the identity of $Y$. The configuration space is the quotient $\mathcal B(P)=\mathcal A(P)/\mathcal G(P)$. The associated oriented rank-three real vector bundle has second Stiefel–Whitney class $w_2(P)\in H^2(Y;\mathbb Z/2)$.

Fix an $SO(3)$-invariant inner product on $\mathfrak{so}(3)$ and normalize the Chern–Simons functional on its covering of $\mathcal B(P)$ so that its differential at $A$ in a connection variation $a$ is $d\mathrm{CS}_A(a)=\int_Y\langle a\wedge F_A\rangle$. A **holonomy perturbation** is a finite sum of gauge-invariant terms formed by integrating smooth class functions of holonomy around a finite family of embedded loops against compactly supported smooth weights. A critical point of a perturbed Chern–Simons functional is called a perturbed flat connection. At a nondegenerate critical point, the gauge-fixed Hessian is self-adjoint; the **spectral flow** along a path of such Hessians is the signed count of eigenvalues crossing zero and supplies the relative grading convention. Give $\mathbb R\times Y$ the product metric and orientation $dt\wedge\mathrm{or}(Y)$. Fix a holonomy perturbation $f_\pi$ and write $V_\pi(B)=\nabla_{L^2}f_\pi(B)$ for its gradient. A **finite-energy perturbed anti-self-dual trajectory** is a gauge-equivalence class with a temporal-gauge representative $A=B(t)$ on the pullback bundle satisfying
$$\frac{dB}{dt}=-\bigl(*_YF_B+V_\pi(B)\bigr)=-\nabla_{L^2}(\mathrm{CS}+f_\pi)(B),$$
with specified limiting critical points $\beta_-,\beta_+$ of that same perturbed functional at the two ends, and with finite flow energy
$$E_\pi(B):=\int_{\mathbb R}\left\|\frac{dB}{dt}\right\|_{L^2(Y)}^2\,dt=\int_{\mathbb R}\|*_YF_B+V_\pi(B)\|_{L^2(Y)}^2\,dt<\infty.$$
Equivalently, in this gauge its four-dimensional equation is $F_A^++\widehat V_\pi(A)=0$, where $\widehat V_\pi(A)=\tfrac12(dt\wedge V_\pi(B)+*_YV_\pi(B))$. When $\pi=0$ this reduces to the ordinary anti-self-duality equation. On a chosen real lift of the Chern–Simons functional along the trajectory, the chain rule gives $d(\mathrm{CS}+f_\pi)(B(t))/dt=-\|dB/dt\|_{L^2}^2$; whenever the functional has the specified endpoint limits, the energy is their difference. For nonzero perturbations those endpoints need not be flat, so no finiteness of the unperturbed curvature integral $\int_{\mathbb R\times Y}|F_A|^2$ is imposed. If the analytic Fredholm construction is established, the expected dimension is the index of the gauge-fixed linearization of the perturbed equation with the stated asymptotic conditions; translation decreases dimension by one for a nonconstant trajectory.

The **candidate instanton surgery-triangle input data** consist of a principal $SO(3)$-bundle on each $Y_j$, compatible bundle identifications on the three cobordisms, the invariant inner product and Chern–Simons normalization, the allowed perturbation class, and the grading convention. After separate proofs of analytic existence, regularity, compactness and gluing, these data may be used to define critical-point complexes and cobordism maps. Chain complexes, exactness of the three-term Floer sequence, and independence of the choices are separate theorem obligations. This definition asserts none of those analytic or Floer-theoretic conclusions.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K,K'\subset S^3$ be smooth knots with chosen compact exteriors $E_K,E_{K'}$, and let $h:E_K\to E_{K'}$ be a homeomorphism. Exactly one of $K,K'$ cannot be the unknot. If both are unknotted, they are ambiently equivalent, but this particular $h$ need not preserve their knot-meridian slopes. If both are nontrivial, $h(\mu_K)$ is carried to $\mu_{K'}$ by an isotopy through homeomorphisms of the boundary torus, and $h$ extends across their tubular solid tori to a homeomorphism of pairs $(S^3,K)\to(S^3,K')$; that extension preserves ambient orientation when $h$ preserves orientation and reverses it when $h$ reverses orientation.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, two smooth knots in $S^3$, chosen compact exteriors, and a homeomorphism between those exteriors.

[F1] For a nontrivial knot, a filling of its exterior is homeomorphic to $S^3$ only at the meridional slope. [[lem-s-three-filling-detects-the-meridian-slope]]

[F2] The boundary of a nontrivial knot exterior has no properly embedded compressing disk. [[lem-nontrivial-knot-exterior-boundary-incompressible]]

[F3] A boundary homeomorphism of solid tori whose image meridian is ambiently isotopic to the target meridian extends over the solid tori carrying core to core and with the same orientation sign. [[lem-meridian-preserving-torus-homeomorphism-extends-over-solid-torus]]

[F4] In the standard model $U=\{(z,0):|z|=1\}$ in the unit sphere $S^3\subset\mathbb C^2$, the exterior of the radius-$\epsilon$ tube $|w|\le\epsilon$ is homeomorphic to $D^2_{\sqrt{1-\epsilon^2}}\times S^1$ by $(z,e^{it})\mapsto(z,\sqrt{1-|z|^2}e^{it})$. Its inverse is $(z,w)\mapsto(z,w/|w|)$, and $D^2_{\sqrt{1-\epsilon^2}}\times\{1\}$ is a proper meridian disk with essential boundary. The standard circle and exterior convention are those of the knot definitions. [[def-oriented-link-in-s-three-and-ambient-isotopy]] [[def-knot-exterior]]

[F5] If two normalized tubular-neighbourhood embeddings of the same compact core use the same normal bundle and induce the same normal identification, they are ambiently isotopic after shrinking near the core. [[cor-tubular-neighbourhoods-are-unique-up-to-ambient-isotopy]]

[F6] The exterior is the complement of the interior of its chosen closed tubular neighbourhood; in normal-disk coordinates, the region between nested radii is a product boundary collar. [[def-knot-exterior]]

[F7] A slope is an unoriented isotopy class of an essential simple closed curve on the boundary torus, and the oriented filling type is independent of the gluing map once its meridian image is fixed. [[def-oriented-slope-and-knot-dehn-filling]]

[F8] Here “unknotted” means ambiently equivalent, after forgetting component orientation, to the standard one-component circle; ambient equivalence uses the smooth orientation-preserving ambient-isotopy convention. [[def-oriented-link-in-s-three-and-ambient-isotopy]]

[F9] If a continuous disk map into a compact connected orientable smooth three-manifold has boundary in the relative interior of a compact connected smooth boundary subsurface with class outside a specified normal subgroup, the smooth Loop theorem supplies a smoothly properly embedded disk whose boundary has class outside that subgroup. It need not preserve the original boundary curve pointwise. [[thm-smooth-loop-theorem-and-incompressibility-criterion-in-orientable-three-manifolds]]

[A1] Full AC is the assertion that every set-indexed family of nonempty sets has a choice function. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[L1] Full AC implies countable choice by applying its choice function to any countable family of nonempty sets. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Let $V=D^2\times S^1$ and $V'=D^2\times S^1$ be solid tori, with meridian curves $\mu=\partial D^2\times\{1\}$ and $\mu'=\partial D^2\times\{1\}$. Suppose $h:\partial V\to\partial V'$ is a homeomorphism and there is an isotopy $H_t:\partial V'\to\partial V'$ through homeomorphisms, with $H_0=\mathrm{id}$, such that $H_1(h(\mu))=\mu'$. Then $h$ extends to a homeomorphism $\overline h:V\to V'$. The extension may be chosen to carry the product core $\{0\}\times S^1$ onto the product core of $V'$, and has the same orientation sign as $h$ with respect to the boundary orientations.

The false assertion is that the abelianized peripheral system $\bigl(H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z),[\mu],[\lambda]\bigr)$ determines the ambient-equivalence class of every smooth knot $K\subset S^3$, where $[\mu]$ is the positive meridian class and $[\lambda]$ is the preferred longitude class.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text: Assume full AC. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot with chosen compact exterior $E_K$ and boundary torus $T_K=\partial E_K$. A simple closed curve on a surface is **essential** if it is not null-homotopic there. A surface $S\subset E_K$ is properly embedded if $S\cap\partial E_K=\partial S$ and its interior lies in the interior of $E_K$. It is **incompressible** if it has no embedded disk with interior disjoint from $S$ and essential boundary in $S$; it is **boundary-incompressible** if it has no embedded disk whose boundary is the union of an arc in $S$ that does not cut off a disk and an arc in $\partial E_K$. A **boundary slope** of $K$ is the unoriented isotopy class of an essential simple closed curve on $T_K$ that occurs as the boundary of a properly embedded, orientable, incompressible, boundary-incompressible surface. Using the positive meridian $\mu$ and preferred longitude $\lambda$ as a homology basis, a primitive class $a[\lambda]+b[\mu]$ has slope $b/a\in\mathbb Q\cup\{\infty\}$, with $a=0$ interpreted as $\infty$. A boundary slope is **strict** if it has a realizing orientable, incompressible, boundary-incompressible surface which is not a fiber of any locally trivial fibration $E_K\to S^1$; a fiber is the inverse image of a point under that bundle projection.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume full AC. Let $(Y,y)$ be a path-connected, locally path-connected, semilocally simply connected based space, and fix an isomorphism
$$\langle x_1,\ldots,x_n\mid r_1,\ldots,r_m\rangle\ \cong\ \Gamma=\pi_1(Y,y)$$
from a finite presentation. Let $P$ be its presentation $2$-complex, with its one vertex $p$. Choose based loops in $Y$ representing the specified generators. They extend, after choosing fillings of the finitely many relators, to a based map $f:P\to Y$ inducing the specified isomorphism. No CW structure on $Y$ is required. For every left $\mathbb Z[\Gamma]$-module $A$, interpreted as the base fibre of a local system with $g a=T_{\bar g}a$ in the first-loop-first convention, this map induces an isomorphism
$$H_1(P;f^*\mathcal A)\ \xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }\ H_1(Y;\mathcal A).$$
This assertion does not require $Y$ or its universal cover to be aspherical and does not assert that $P$ is a spine or a homotopy-equivalent model of $Y$.

There is the following explicit finite-chain form. Give universal-cover chains the right action $c\cdot g=T_{g^{-1}}c$, and choose the lifted presentation vertex $e_0$ and generator edges $e_j$ starting there. For a word $w$ in the generators and their inverses, let each positive letter $x_j$ after prefix $q$ contribute $e_j\cdot q^{-1}$, and each negative letter $x_j^{-1}$ after prefix $q$ contribute $-e_j\cdot(qx_j^{-1})^{-1}$. Denote the sum by $c_w$. Then
$$\partial c_w=e_0\cdot w^{-1}-e_0.$$
If $u\in A$ is fixed by $w$, the tensor $c_w\otimes u$ is a cycle. Under the displayed isomorphism its class is the class of the actual based loop in $Y$ represented by $w$, with initial coefficient $u$; it is independent of the word representative and the relator fillings of $f$.

In particular let $j:(T^2,*)\to(Y,y)$ be a based torus map with ordered based loops $(\lambda,\mu)$, choose words $w_\lambda,w_\mu$ for their images, and let $u$ be fixed by both. The two finite cycles $c_{w_\lambda}\otimes u,c_{w_\mu}\otimes u$ compute the images of the actual torus classes in precisely this order. If $A$ is a finite-dimensional vector space over a field $F$, the presentation complex gives finite matrices $B:C_2\to C_1$, $C:C_1\to C_0$ and these two cycle columns $U$, with $CB=CU=0$. The actual kernel of the two peripheral classes mapping into $H_1(Y;\mathcal A)$ is exactly
$$\ker\{F^2\xrightarrow{U}\ker C/\operatorname{im}B\}.$$
Thus a one-dimensional image of those two actual peripheral classes is equivalent to $\operatorname{rank}_F(B\mid U)=\operatorname{rank}_FB+1$. All matrix entries are finite sums of matrices for generator words and their inverses. For the left coefficient action $\operatorname{Ad}\rho$ of an $SL_2$ representation they are polynomial in the representation entries and in the chosen vector $u$. For a torus restriction with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho(\mu))^2\ne4$, one may take $u=\rho(\mu)-\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}(\rho(\mu))I$ in characteristic different from $2$; the two torus classes are then a basis. This applies, in particular, to an actual compact smooth knot exterior and its based peripheral torus map. No existence of a generic representation family or generic exterior rank is inferred.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, the based space and specified finite presentation, the coefficient module in the stated convention, and the torus/field/adjoint data when those clauses are invoked.

[F1] A finite wedge of $n$ circles has fundamental group freely generated by its oriented circle loops; Seifert–van Kampen computes the group of a two-set open cover as the pushout ([[thm-fundamental-group-of-finite-wedge-of-circles]]; [[thm-seifert-van-kampen]]).

[F2] A path-connected, locally path-connected, semilocally simply connected space has a simply connected universal cover; based maps from a simply connected locally path-connected source lift uniquely after fixing the image of one point ([[thm-universal-cover-existence]]; [[thm-covering-space-lifting-criterion]]). Under the no-reversal deck identification, cover chains are free right group-ring modules on supplied oriented cell lifts, with $c\cdot g=T_{g^{-1}}c$ ([[def-right-group-ring-action-on-the-chains-of-a-universal-cover]]; [[thm-deck-group-of-a-universal-cover-is-the-fundamental-group]]).

[F3] For a path-connected space, integral $H_1$ is the abelianization of its fundamental group; ordinary cellular chains compute integral singular homology ([[prop-the-first-hurewicz-map-in-degree-one-is-abelianization]]; [[thm-cellular-homology-computes-singular-homology]]). Free modules are projective under AC ([[thm-free-modules-are-projective-with-choice-boundary]]; [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

[F4] Augmented projective complexes exact in degrees0/1 have unique comparison isomorphisms on first homology after tensoring with an arbitrary module on the opposite side; no flatness or exactness in degree2 is required ([[lem-partial-projective-resolutions-determine-tensor-homology-in-degree-one]]).

[F5] Intrinsic singular local chains are defined on arbitrary spaces, with coefficients in the fibre at the first vertex and transport on the zeroth face. For connected CW spaces they agree with right-cover-chain tensor left-coefficient-module chains, with $g a=T_{\bar g}a$; cellular comparison is natural, and a based homotopy preserves the induced local homology class with the prescribed coefficient transport ([[def-singular-and-cellular-chain-complexes-with-local-coefficients]]; [[thm-cellular-chains-compute-homology-with-local-coefficients]]; [[prop-local-coefficient-homology-and-cohomology-are-functorial-for-a-map-with-a-coefficient-morphism]]).

[F6] The adjoint torus calculation gives an explicit basis with invariant vector $M-\operatorname{tr}(M)I/2$ when $\operatorname{tr}(M)^2\ne4$, together with a chain contraction of the complementary plane ([[lem-nonparabolic-adjoint-torus-homology-has-explicit-peripheral-basis]]).

[F7] The actual compact smooth knot exterior is path-connected: the open complement is path-connected by the local Alexander-duality calculation in [[lem-the-complement-of-an-oriented-link-is-a-connected-smooth-three-manifold]], Proof1.3–2.1, and retracts onto the chosen compact exterior by the explicit radial formula in [[lem-maximal-abelian-cover-link-exterior-retraction]], Proof1.1. We use only these proved connectedness/retraction portions; the former carrier's separate quoted finite-triangulation input is not used. Boundary tube charts make the compact exterior a smooth manifold with boundary.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text: Assume full AC. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot, let $p,q\in\mathbb Z$ be coprime and not both zero, and let $E_K(p/q)$ be the Dehn filling whose attached solid-torus meridian is identified with $p[\mu]+q[\lambda]$. A closed 3-manifold $Y$ is **$SL_2(\mathbb C)$-abelian** if every homomorphism $\pi_1(Y)\to SL_2(\mathbb C)$ has abelian image. The slope $p/q$ is an **$SL_2(\mathbb C)$-abelian surgery slope** for $K$ if $E_K(p/q)$ is $SL_2(\mathbb C)$-abelian. The knot admits infinitely many such surgeries if infinitely many distinct rational slopes have this property.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text: Assume full AC. Let $G=\pi_1(E_K)$ be the group of a smooth oriented knot exterior, with positive meridian $\mu$ and preferred longitude $\lambda$. For a finite presentation $G=\langle g_1,\ldots,g_n\mid r_1,\ldots,r_m\rangle$, the **$SL_2(\mathbb C)$ representation variety** is the algebraic set of tuples $(A_1,\ldots,A_n)\in SL_2(\mathbb C)^n$ for which every relator matrix $r_j(A_1,\ldots,A_n)$ equals the identity. The group $SL_2(\mathbb C)$ acts on this set by simultaneous conjugation. Its affine categorical quotient, whose coordinate ring is the invariant ring of regular functions, is the **$SL_2(\mathbb C)$ character variety** $X(E_K)$. For a representation $\rho$, its character is the function $\gamma\mapsto\operatorname{tr}(\rho(\gamma))$. A representation is **reducible** if its matrices preserve a common one-dimensional subspace of $\mathbb C^2$; otherwise it is irreducible. The peripheral torus group is $\pi_1(T_K)\cong\mathbb Z^2$, generated by the meridian and preferred longitude; its image in $G$ is generated by their commuting classes and need not be isomorphic to $\mathbb Z^2$. Their image under any representation is a commuting pair of matrices, so it has a common invariant line and is simultaneously triangularizable over $\mathbb C$. Choosing a common invariant line gives meridian and longitude eigenvalues $(M,L)\in(\mathbb C^*)^2$; the unordered boundary character identifies $(M,L)$ with $(M^{-1},L^{-1})$. Simultaneous diagonalizability is stronger than simultaneous triangularizability.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Let $K\subset S^3$ be a fibered knot with exterior $E_K$ and fiber surface $F$. If $S\subset E_K$ is a connected, orientable, nonseparating, incompressible properly embedded surface whose boundary is a nonempty union of longitudes, then $S$ is isotopic to $F$. After their boundary curves are identified by an isotopy in the boundary torus and this alignment is extended across a collar, the concluding isotopy may be taken relative to the aligned boundary.

facts:
**Given:** The surface and fibered exterior in the Statement, with full AC as authorized for their homology and geometric suppliers. This is not a claimed choice-free proof.

[A1] Full AC implies the countable-choice assumptions used in the smooth surface and isotopy suppliers. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] The relative exterior group $H_2(E_K,\partial E_K;\mathbb Z)$ is generated by the oriented fiber, and its intersection-dual meridian class generates $H^1(E_K;\mathbb Z)$. [[thm-knot-exterior-homology-and-longitude]]

[F2] Geometric incompressibility of a neat two-sided smooth surface is equivalent to fundamental-group injectivity. Broad smooth boundary-preimage surfaces first admit a boundary-fixed embedding neatification, and their actual smooth disk obstructions pass to that representative. [[thm-smooth-loop-theorem-and-incompressibility-criterion-in-orientable-three-manifolds]], [[lem-compact-smooth-boundary-preimage-surfaces-admit-neat-embedding-isotopies]], [[lem-angular-boundary-neatification-preserves-smooth-disk-obstructions]]

[F3] A finite disjoint family of essential longitude curves on a smooth torus admits a simultaneous smooth normalization to the corresponding parallel affine circles. Its isotopy extends into the boundary collar by applying its time parameter times a collar cutoff. [[lem-choice-free-smooth-torus-curves-and-annulus-strips]]

[F4] An injective map of compact finite PL oriented surfaces with nontrivial source group is homotopic to a finite covering or to an annular boundary collapse. A boundary local homeomorphism can be fixed throughout. The actual thirteen-row proof gives subgroup cores, the boundary orientation-chain calculation, cutting-arc normalization and disk extension. Smooth compact surfaces have compatible finite cellulations; relative finite simplicial approximation gives the PL map in this interface, preserving an already matched boundary triangulation. [[thm-pi-one-injective-finite-pl-surface-maps-are-covers-or-annular-collapses]], [[lem-compact-c2-surfaces-admit-finite-cellulations-relative-to-a-finite-embedded-graph]], [[thm-finite-simplicial-approximation-for-maps-of-pairs]]

[F5] Connected subgroup covers and their map-lifting criterion exist. Finite surface graph thickenings give the disk conclusion for a simply connected compact surface with nonempty boundary; cellular relative homology computes the orientation-chain degree. [[thm-classification-of-connected-covering-spaces]], [[thm-covering-space-lifting-criterion]], [[lem-finite-chart-surface-normal-forms-supply-jordan-disks-and-torsion-free-groups]], [[thm-relative-cellular-homology-computes-relative-singular-homology]]

[F6] The actual boundary-relative homotopic-surface theorem supplies a downstairs embedded family-innermost product patch and the intersection-reducing isotopy. Its proof includes the relative half-product normalization and verifies the boundary-complement injections in the cut fiber product; it does not project an arbitrary cover isotopy. [[thm-boundary-relative-homotopic-incompressible-surfaces-in-fibered-exteriors-are-isotopic]]

[F7] Compact smooth manifolds with corners admit finite compatible triangulations relative to admissible triangulated boundary faces and protected collar neighborhoods. Cutting the smooth pair at its transverse surface faces gives exactly these compatible corner data; paired face subdivisions are matched before regluing. [[thm-compact-smooth-manifolds-with-corners-admit-relative-finite-triangulations]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume full AC and let $G=\pi_1(E_K)=\langle g_1,\ldots,g_n\mid r_1,\ldots,r_m\rangle$ be a finite presentation of a knot-exterior group. The set of homomorphisms $G\to SL_2(\mathbb C)$ is the affine algebraic subset of $SL_2(\mathbb C)^n$ cut out by the matrix-entry equations $r_j(A_1,\ldots,A_n)=I_2$ for $1\le j\le m$. After each inverse letter is replaced by the adjugate of its determinant-one matrix, these equations have integer coefficients in the matrix-entry coordinates.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC and the finite presentation $G=\langle g_1,\ldots,g_n\mid r_1,\ldots,r_m\rangle$.

[F1] The knot group has a finite Wirtinger presentation ([[thm-knot-wirtinger-presentation-correctness]]).

[F2] If $A=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}\in SL_2(\mathbb C)$, then $A^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}d&-b\\-c&a\end{pmatrix}$, an integer-polynomial expression in its entries: multiplying by the displayed matrix gives $\det(A)I=I$ entrywise.
