contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
There are the following explicit valid finite planar codes, with the standard right/up orientation of the plane and positive based meridians using compatible common upper-collar access paths.

The counterclockwise square with vertices $(0,0),(1,0),(1,1),(0,1)$ is a crossing-free unknot code. It has one under-arc and gives $\pi_1(S^3\setminus U)=\langle x\mid\ \rangle\cong\mathbb Z$, with $x$ the positive meridian.

An oriented figure-eight code has crossings $C_1,C_2,C_3,C_4$. The letters $O,U$ mean over and under, and $i,o$ mean incoming and outgoing. Its integer plane-drawing certificate is

| $r$ | $C_r$ | $rOi$ | $rOo$ | $rUi$ | $rUo$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $1$ | $(-423,0)$ | $(-627,102)$ | $(-363,-30)$ | $(-363,30)$ | $(-627,-102)$ |
| $2$ | $(0,-9)$ | $(-33,-6)$ | $(99,-18)$ | $(-99,-18)$ | $(33,-6)$ |
| $3$ | $(0,9)$ | $(33,6)$ | $(-99,18)$ | $(99,18)$ | $(-33,6)$ |
| $4$ | $(423,0)$ | $(627,-102)$ | $(363,30)$ | $(363,-30)$ | $(627,102)$ |

The complete cyclic visit list is $$1O,\ 2U,\ 3O,\ 1U,\ 4O,\ 3U,\ 2O,\ 4U.$$ For every successive pair $rB,sD$ in this list, including the last-to-first pair, use the three straight segments of the route $C_r\to rBo\to sDi\to C_s$. At each crossing pair $rOi$ with $rOo$, and $rUi$ with $rUo$; the first pair is over. Smooth the degree-two bends in disjoint small disks. The cyclic orders at crossings are the counterclockwise lists $(rOo,rUi,rOi,rUo)$ for $r=1,4$ and $(rOo,rUo,rOi,rUi)$ for $r=2,3$.

Label the under-arcs $x_1:U4\to U2$, $x_2:U2\to U1$, $x_3:U1\to U3$, $x_4:U3\to U4$. In each oriented over-branch chart, let $L$ denote its left under-side (target of the positive in-plane normal), and $R$ its right under-side (source). The exact crossing table is

| crossing | over | $L$ (target) | $R$ (source) | under traversal | $\operatorname{sign}\det(\text{over},\text{under})$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $R_1$ | $x_1$ | $x_2$ | $x_3$ | target to source | $-1$ |
| $R_2$ | $x_4$ | $x_2$ | $x_1$ | source to target | $+1$ |
| $R_3$ | $x_2$ | $x_4$ | $x_3$ | source to target | $+1$ |
| $R_4$ | $x_3$ | $x_4$ | $x_1$ | target to source | $-1$ |

Thus its actual positive-meridian presentation is $$\pi_1(S^3\setminus 4_1)=\langle x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4\mid x_1x_2=x_3x_1,\ x_1x_4=x_4x_2,\ x_3x_2=x_2x_4,\ x_3x_4=x_1x_3\rangle.$$ The last relation follows from the first three. Starting on $x_1$, the underpasses occur at $R_2,R_1,R_3,R_4$, and the self-writhe is zero. All drawing data, validations and algebra in this statement are finite and use no choice axiom.

facts:
**Given:** The integer coordinates, routes, orientation, branch pairings, over/under choices and square specified in the statement.

[F1] [[def-knot-planar-code]] specifies the exact rational drawing tests, one-component tracing, smoothing and under-arc convention.

[F2] [[alg-knot-wirtinger-presentation-from-code]] checks this finite input and emits one positive-meridian generator per under-arc, with crossing relation $x_o^{-1}x_Rx_ox_L^{-1}=1$.

[F3] [[lem-wirtinger-local-meridian-conjugacy]] proves that the over-tangent's positive in-plane normal points from source $R$ to target $L$, and gives exactly the based positive-meridian rule in [F2].

[F4] [[thm-knot-wirtinger-presentation-correctness]] identifies that presentation with the fundamental group of the actual smooth knot complement, with these positive meridians.

[F5] [[def-free-group]] and [[def-group-presentation]] give the universal properties of the free group and of imposing the listed relators.

[F6] [[thm-simple-polygon-admits-a-triangulation]] constructs a finite face-to-face triangulation of a simple filled polygon by vertical slabs and convex cells. Its finite polygon construction is used only to extend the paired face boundaries in the figure-eight admission.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume full AC and use the standard oriented four-crossing figure-eight code of the explicit oriented Wirtinger-code lemma, with its positive based under-arc meridians $x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4$ and compatible diagram access paths. Put $u=x_1$, $v=x_2$, and $w=uv^{-1}u^{-1}v$. Then $$\pi_1(E_{4_1})=\langle u,v\mid vw=wu\rangle,$$ with $u$ a positive meridian. In this presentation $$X_3=uvu^{-1},\qquad X_4=v^{-1}uvu^{-1}v=w^{-1}v$$ are the old $x_3,x_4$. The preferred longitude based compatibly with $u$ is represented by $$\lambda=X_4u^{-1}vX_3^{-1}.$$ In particular its trace in any representation is the trace of this explicit word. The formula does not identify a zero-homology centralizing word as a longitude without the diagram-parallel calculation.

facts:
**Given:** The stated oriented figure-eight code, compatible positive based diagram meridians, and the selected initial strand $x_1$.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]] is retained for the named knot-exterior branch; all new operations are finite.

[F1] [[lem-explicit-unknot-and-figure-eight-oriented-wirtinger-codes]] gives $R_1:x_1x_2=x_3x_1$, $R_2:x_1x_4=x_4x_2$, $R_3:x_3x_2=x_2x_4$, and $R_4:x_3x_4=x_1x_3$. Its full proof shows $R_4$ follows from the first three. Its actual oriented under-arc cycle is $x_1\to x_2$ at $R_2$, $x_2\to x_3$ at $R_1$, $x_3\to x_4$ at $R_3$, $x_4\to x_1$ at $R_4$; the local coordinate charts specify the source and target sides and positive crossing signs.

[F2] [[lem-link-peripheral-longitude-word-from-diagram]] proves that a positive component traversal contributes the over-meridian with exponent $+1$ for source-to-target underpasses and exponent $-1$ for target-to-source. Their ordered product is the based blackboard parallel; multiplying by the initial meridian to minus the self-writhe gives its preferred zero-self-linking longitude.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text:
Assume full AC. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot, $E_K$ its exterior, and $ho:\pi_1(E_K)	o SL_2(\mathbb C)$ a representation. The **adjoint local system** $\operatorname{Ad}ho$ has fibre $\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)$ and left group-module action $\gamma\cdot v=ho(\gamma)vho(\gamma)^{-1}$. In the first-loop-first intrinsic convention, this means forward path transport $T_\gamma(v)=ho(\gamma)^{-1}vho(\gamma)$; equivalently the corresponding right action is $v\cdot\gamma=ho(\gamma)^{-1}vho(\gamma)$. Its twisted homology $H_*(E_K;\operatorname{Ad}ho)$ is the intrinsic local-system homology with these transports, equivalently the homology of the cellular local-coefficient complex for a supplied CW structure; the same convention defines boundary-torus twisted homology and the inclusion map $i_*:H_1(\partial E_K;\operatorname{Ad}ho)	o H_1(E_K;\operatorname{Ad}ho)$. An **admissible adjoint representation** is one for which there is a nonzero vector $v_ho\in\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)$ fixed by the peripheral adjoint action such that $\{[v_ho\otimes\lambda],[v_ho\otimes\mu]\}$ is a basis of $H_1(\partial E_K;\operatorname{Ad}ho)$ and $\ker i_*$ is one-dimensional. For an irreducible affine character curve $X$, its function field $\mathbb C(X)$ is the fraction field of its coordinate domain. A **tautological representation** over $\mathbb C(X)$ is a homomorphism $ho_X:\pi_1(E_K)	o SL_2(\mathbb C(X))$ whose character is the generic character of $X$. A **smooth projective completion** consists of a smooth complete curve $\overline X$ with a dense open subset $U$ identified with the normalization $X^
u$ of $X$, with its finite birational normalization map $
u:U	o X$ recorded. When $X$ is smooth, $
u$ identifies $U$ with $X$, recovering the usual completion. An **ideal point** is a point $x\in\overline X\setminus U$; points of $U$ over singular affine points of $X$ are affine branches and are retained inside $U$. Such an ideal point defines the discrete valuation $v_x(f)=\operatorname{ord}_x(f)$ on $\mathbb C(X)$. The valuation ring is $\mathcal O_x=\{f:v_x(f)\ge0\}$, and a **uniformizer** is an element $\pi\in\mathcal O_x$ with $v_x(\pi)=1$. Its residue field is $k_x=\mathcal O_x/(\pi)$. An $\mathcal O_x$-lattice in $\mathbb C(X)^2$ is a free rank-two $\mathcal O_x$-submodule spanning $\mathbb C(X)^2$; two lattices are homothetic if one is a nonzero scalar multiple of the other. The **Bruhat–Tits tree** has homothety classes of these lattices as vertices, with two vertices adjacent if representatives satisfy $\pi\Lambda\subsetneq\Lambda'\subsetneq\Lambda$ and $\Lambda/\Lambda'$ is one-dimensional over $k_x$. Whenever the tautological representation exists, it acts on this tree. The ideal point, valuation, action, and any essential surface produced from the action are its Culler–Shalen data; that surface is called the associated Culler–Shalen surface.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Let $X$ be the based presentation $2$-complex with one vertex, oriented $1$-cells $x_1,\ldots,x_n$, and oriented $2$-cells attached along words $r_1,\ldots,r_m$ in the free group $F_n$. Let $G=\langle x_1,\ldots,x_n\mid r_1,\ldots,r_m\rangle$ be its presented fundamental group, let $\rho:G\to\mathrm{GL}_d(\mathbb F)$ be a representation, and let $\psi:G\to H$ be the declared free-abelian deck map. For $\Phi:\mathbb F[F_n]\to M_d(Q)$ induced by $x_j\mapsto\rho(x_j)\psi(x_j)$, the twisted differential $\partial_1$ has blocks $\rho(x_j)\psi(x_j)-I_d$, and the $i$th block row of $\partial_2$ is

$$\left(\Phi\left(\frac{\partial r_i}{\partial x_1}\right),\ldots,\Phi\left(\frac{\partial r_i}{\partial x_n}\right)\right),$$

where coefficient vectors are written as rows and differentials act on the right: the matrix of $\partial_1$ is the stacked column of blocks $\rho(x_j)\psi(x_j)-I_d$, while the matrix of $\partial_2$ is the $md$-by-$nd$ block matrix whose $i$th row is the displayed Fox row. The Fox derivatives use the product and inverse recursions in the Wada definition. Thus the evaluated Fox-Jacobian blocks are exactly the cellular boundary blocks of the based twisted complex of this presentation $2$-complex.

facts:
**Given:** The finite based presentation $2$-complex, its presentation generators and relators, $\rho$, $\psi$, and the twisted coefficient map $\Phi$.

[A1] AC is inherited from the twisted-chain convention; the finite word calculation uses no choice principle. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] A presentation $2$-complex has one vertex, one oriented $1$-cell for each generator, and one oriented $2$-cell attached by each relator word. [[def-group-presentation]]; [[def-free-group]]

[F2] Fox derivatives satisfy $\partial x_k/\partial x_j=\delta_{kj}$, $\partial(uv)/\partial x_j=\partial u/\partial x_j+u\partial v/\partial x_j$, and $\partial x_k^{-1}/\partial x_j=-x_k^{-1}\delta_{kj}$. [[def-knot-wada-quotient-for-deficiency-one-presentation]]

[F3] The group ring has basis indexed by group elements and multiplication $[g][h]=[gh]$; the coefficient map $\Phi$ is the ring homomorphism prescribed in the Wada definition. [[def-group-ring]]; [[thm-group-ring-is-a-unital-algebra-with-basis-g]]; [[def-knot-twisted-chain-complex-and-reidemeister-torsion]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume full AC. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot with a finite Wirtinger presentation by words in generators and their inverses, and let $\mu,\lambda$ be its marked meridian and preferred-longitude words. Let $\mathcal E_K\subset(\mathbb C^*)^2$ consist of the pairs $(M,L)$ for which some representation $\rho:\pi_1(E_K)\to SL_2(\mathbb C)$ has a common eigenline for $\rho(\mu)$ and $\rho(\lambda)$ with eigenvalues $M$ and $L$. Then the Zariski closure of $\mathcal E_K$ is defined over $\mathbb Q$: its radical vanishing ideal in $\mathbb C[M^{\pm1},L^{\pm1}]$ is obtained by extending scalars from a radical ideal in $\mathbb Q[M^{\pm1},L^{\pm1}]$.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, a finite presentation of $G=\pi_1(E_K)$ over $\mathbb Z$, and the marked peripheral words $\mu,\lambda$.

[F1] The representation variety is cut out by polynomial matrix equations with integer coefficients after inverse letters are replaced by adjugates ([[lem-sl2-representation-variety-is-affine]]).

[F2] The meridian and preferred longitude are commuting peripheral words in the finite knot-group presentation ([[thm-knot-wirtinger-presentation-correctness]], [[def-knot-meridian-and-preferred-longitude]]).

[F3] An arbitrary subset of a finite-dimensional algebraic torus stable under all coordinatewise automorphisms of $\mathbb C/\mathbb Q$ has radical vanishing ideal equal to the scalar extension of a radical rational ideal, by the actual finite row-reduction argument in [[lem-automorphism-stable-laurent-ideals-descend-to-rational-coefficients]]. This applies to the point set itself; its image need not already be closed.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume full AC and let $G=\pi_1(E_K)$ have a finite presentation. There is a finite list of words $w_1,\ldots,w_N\in G$ whose trace functions generate the coordinate ring of $X(E_K)$, so the map $[\rho]\mapsto(\operatorname{tr}\rho(w_1),\ldots,\operatorname{tr}\rho(w_N))$ is a closed embedding into $\mathbb C^N$, with defining ideal the kernel of the induced map $\mathbb C[z_1,\ldots,z_N]\to\mathbb C[\operatorname{Hom}(G,SL_2)]^{SL_2}$. On the irreducible-character locus, equal trace coordinates determine conjugate representations; on the reducible locus, the quotient records the semisimplified diagonal character, not the possibly non-diagonalizable representative.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC and the finite Wirtinger presentation of the knot group.

[F1] The character quotient coordinate ring is generated by traces of words ([[lem-sl2-character-trace-coordinate-algebra]]).

[F2] The character quotient is affine with finitely generated reduced coordinate algebra, the quotient map is onto, and generators give its actual closed coordinate model ([[thm-invariant-ring-finite-generation-and-affine-categorical-quotient]]).

[F3] [[lem-equal-irreducible-sl2-traces-determine-conjugacy]] proves by the actual rank-two matrix-algebra and trace-pairing argument that equal irreducible trace characters are conjugate in $SL_2(\mathbb C)$, and a reducible representation has the trace character of its diagonal semisimplification. This is a pointwise proof, not an assertion of a representation over a function field.

contract.heading: Definition
contract.text: Assume full AC. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot, let $\rho:\pi_1(E_K)\to SL_2(\mathbb C)$ have admissible adjoint local system, and let $v_\rho$ be a nonzero peripheral-adjoint-invariant vector for which $[v_\rho\otimes\lambda],[v_\rho\otimes\mu]$ form the specified ordered basis of $H_1(\partial E_K;\operatorname{Ad}\rho)$. If a generator of the one-dimensional kernel of inclusion is $a[v_\rho\otimes\lambda]+b[v_\rho\otimes\mu]$, the **Bénard–Florens–Rodau slope** is $s_K(\rho)=-b/a\in\mathbb C\cup\{\infty\}$, with $a=0$ interpreted as $\infty$. Rescaling $v_\rho$ or the kernel generator does not change this projective ratio. A rational function on an irreducible character component means an element of its function field, the fraction field of its coordinate domain. A projective-valued rational function means a point of the projective line over that field; it may be identically $\infty$. The slope's rational extension has this projective meaning. Unless its generic value is $\infty$, it is an ordinary rational function, whose individual infinite values are poles. Its rational extension is not a value assigned to every singular or inadmissible character.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume full AC and let $K=J(2,-2)$ be the figure-eight knot. Use the two-bridge group presentation $\pi_1(E_K)=\langle u,v\mid v w=w u\rangle$, where $w=uv^{-1}u^{-1}v$, and take $\mu=u$. On the one-dimensional irreducible character component, define $x(\chi)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(u))=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(v))$ and $y(\chi)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(uv))$. Then
$$2x^2+y^2-x^2y-y-1=0,$$
and the preferred-longitude trace is $\operatorname{tr}(\rho(\lambda))=x^4-5x^2+2$. The displayed curve equation is irreducible over $\mathbb C$, and $x$ is nonconstant on it.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, the standard figure-eight knot, its positive meridian and preferred longitude, and the two-bridge group presentation in the Statement.

[F1] The four-crossing figure-eight code gives a one-component Wirtinger presentation ([[lem-explicit-unknot-and-figure-eight-oriented-wirtinger-codes]]; [[thm-knot-wirtinger-presentation-correctness]]).

[F2] [[lem-figure-eight-two-meridian-presentation-and-preferred-longitude-word]] derives the exact two-meridian presentation from that actual four-crossing code and proves, using its crossing traversal and zero writhe, that the preferred longitude is $C=X_4u^{-1}vX_3^{-1}$ with $X_3=uvu^{-1}$ and $X_4=v^{-1}uvu^{-1}v$. It is not inferred merely from commutation and zero exponent sum.

[F3] [[lem-two-generator-sl2-word-traces-reduce-to-three-coordinates]] proves the actual four-matrix word table. In the equal-generator-trace case, every word trace is a polynomial in $x=\operatorname{tr}u=\operatorname{tr}v$ and $y=\operatorname{tr}uv$.

[F4] Word traces generate the character coordinate algebra by [[lem-sl2-character-trace-coordinate-algebra]]. The actual quotient is onto and any finite algebra generators give its closed affine coordinate model by [[thm-invariant-ring-finite-generation-and-affine-categorical-quotient]].

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume full AC and let $a>b\ge2$ be coprime positive integers. With the meridian-longitude and exponent conventions used for the enhanced A-polynomial, the enhanced A-polynomial of $T_{a,b}$ is, up to multiplication by a Laurent unit,
$$\widetilde A_{T_{a,b}}(M,L)=\begin{cases}1+M^{2a}L,&b=2,\\-1+M^{2ab}L^2,&b>2.\end{cases}$$
If $K$ is the unknot, then $\widetilde A_K=1$. The nontrivial torus-knot Newton polygon is therefore a line segment whose slope in the $(a,b)\mapsto M^bL^a$ convention is $ab$.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, the oriented positive coprime torus knot and original meridian-longitude and Newton-coordinate conventions.

[F1] The actual torus-knot group/peripheral supplier gives $G=\langle x,y\mid x^a=y^b\rangle$, central $h=x^a=y^b$, positive meridian $\mu=y^\alpha x^\beta$ with $a\alpha+b\beta=1$, and preferred longitude $\lambda=h\mu^{-ab}$ ([[thm-torus-knot-group-presentation]]).

[F2] For exactly these group words, the complete irreducible peripheral eigenvalue-locus ideal is $(1+M^{2a}L)$ for $b=2$ and $(M^{2ab}L^2-1)$ for $b>2$. The proof supplies explicit irreducible matrix families with a cofinite set of meridian values and proves the exact radical ideal, including exceptional representations ([[lem-torus-presentation-irreducible-peripheral-eigenvalue-curves]]).

[F3] The crossing-free unknot has group $\mathbb Z$, by the actual one-generator, no-relator calculation in [[lem-explicit-unknot-and-figure-eight-oriented-wirtinger-codes]].

[F4] The enhanced A-polynomial defines the reduced union of one-dimensional peripheral eigenvalue-image closure components from irreducible characters, with primitive integer normalization ([[def-enhanced-a-polynomial]]).

contract.heading: Open problem
contract.text:
Assume full AC. Let $Y$ be a closed connected oriented smooth $3$-manifold and let $K\subset Y$ be an oriented knot with irreducible exterior $E=Y\setminus\operatorname{Int}\nu K$. Choose a parametrized tubular neighborhood and an oriented integral basis $(\mu,\lambda)$ on its boundary torus $T$, where $\mu$ bounds a meridian disk in $\nu K$ and $\lambda$ is a chosen framing; no preferred null-homologous longitude is assumed. For each primitive pair $(p,q)$, filling along $p\mu+q\lambda$ means attaching a solid torus whose meridian has that unoriented class.

Define $Z^{\mathrm{irr}}_{E,T}\subset(\mathbb C^*)^2$ to be the Zariski closure of the pairs $(M,L)$ arising on a common peripheral invariant line of an irreducible representation $\pi_1(E)\to SL_2(\mathbb C)$, in the chosen basis. Let $C^{\mathrm{irr}}_{E,T}$ be the union of its one-dimensional irreducible components. Use a square-free Laurent equation over $\mathbb C$ of this reduced curve as the enhanced polynomial, up to a Laurent unit, with $1$ for the empty curve. This definition selects curve components; it does not assert that higher-dimensional peripheral-image components are impossible or detected by that equation.

Do the following analogues hold for such closed ambient manifolds: (i) the Newton polygon of this enhanced polynomial is contained in an affine line if and only if $E$ admits a Seifert fibration over a disk with at most two exceptional circle fibers; and (ii) infinitely many distinct primitive filling slopes on $T$ give manifolds whose every $SL_2(\mathbb C)$ representation has abelian image if and only if $E$ admits that Seifert fibration? What additional hypotheses, if any, are required for these equivalences and for the curve-component convention to capture the relevant peripheral representations? An exceptional circle fiber has multiplicity greater than one.

contract.heading: Open problem
contract.text: For a Laurent polynomial $f(M,L)=\sum_{i,j}c_{ij}M^iL^j$, its Newton polygon is the convex hull of the exponent support $\{(i,j):c_{ij}\ne0\}$. For a nontrivial knot $K\subset S^3$, is $K$ a torus knot if and only if the Newton polygon of its ordinary A-polynomial is a parallelogram with nonzero area?

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume full AC. Let $X$ be an irreducible component of the $SL_2(\mathbb C)$ character variety of a knot exterior that contains irreducible characters and has a nonempty dense Zariski-open locus of scheme-smooth, non-boundary-parabolic admissible characters. On this locus the Bénard–Florens–Rodau slope is invariant under conjugation and extends to a rational map $X\dashrightarrow\mathbb P^1(\mathbb C)$; when $X$ is one-dimensional its generic value lies in $\mathbb P^1(\mathbb C(X))$, and unless it is identically $\infty$ it is an ordinary rational function in $\mathbb C(X)$.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, the irreducible character component and its dense open smooth, non-boundary-parabolic admissible locus from the Statement; all its hypotheses are retained.

[F1] An irreducible character component has an actual absolutely irreducible generic representation over a field of degree at most two over its function field. It spreads to representatives of every complex character on a dense principal open; the quadratic automorphism is explicit simultaneous conjugation. [[lem-irreducible-sl2-character-components-have-specializing-quadratic-models]]

[F2] For an actual knot exterior, the finite presentation matrices compute its actual twisted first homology and the actual ordered peripheral inclusion, without a presentation-spine assertion. Their entries and the two word-cycle columns are polynomial in representation entries and a supplied invariant vector. [[lem-presentation-complex-computes-twisted-first-homology-and-peripheral-cycles]]

[F3] A nonparabolic commuting torus pair has a common invariant vector given by either nonparabolic matrix minus half its trace. The complementary plane contracts explicitly; the two ordered torus classes are a basis and commute with conjugation and field extension. [[lem-nonparabolic-adjoint-torus-homology-has-explicit-peripheral-basis]]

[F4] Finite matrix rank charts give actual homology bases and the peripheral kernel line, with specialization compatibility after finite localization. The line is unchanged by chain basis changes, boundary corrections and common nonzero rescaling of both peripheral columns. [[lem-finite-homology-kernel-lines-have-rational-rank-charts]]

[F5] Equal irreducible complex trace characters determine simultaneous conjugacy. The slope of the ordered kernel line is the projective ratio in the original Definition. [[lem-equal-irreducible-sl2-traces-determine-conjugacy]] [[def-character-variety-logarithmic-slope-invariant]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume full AC and let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot with exterior $E_K$, meridian $\mu$, and preferred longitude $\lambda$. Restriction to the peripheral torus induces an algebraic map from the character variety of $E_K$ to that of the torus. Every one-dimensional peripheral eigenvalue image component is contained in the zero set of the ordinary A-polynomial, while isolated image points are not treated as curve factors. For a primitive pair $(p,q)\in\mathbb Z^2$ (with $q=0$ denoting the meridional slope), a representation $\rho:\pi_1(E_K)\to SL_2(\mathbb C)$ descends to the filling that kills $p[\mu]+q[\lambda]$ exactly when $\rho(\mu)^p\rho(\lambda)^q=I_2$. If the peripheral matrices are simultaneously diagonalizable with eigenvalues $(M,L)$ on a common eigenline, this matrix condition is equivalent to $M^pL^q=1$; without that diagonalizability, the eigenvalue equation is only necessary and the matrix relation must be checked.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, the marked knot exterior and peripheral basis, a finite presentation of its group, a representation, and coprime integers $p,q$.

[F1] The boundary inclusion induces restriction on representations; evaluation of each fixed peripheral word is regular in matrix entries because inverse letters in $SL_2(\mathbb C)$ are adjugate polynomials ([[lem-sl2-representation-variety-is-affine]]). This restriction is equivariant under simultaneous conjugation, and the character variety is the affine categorical quotient ([[def-sl-two-character-variety-and-peripheral-eigenvalues]]; [[thm-invariant-ring-finite-generation-and-affine-categorical-quotient]]).

[F2] The ordinary A-polynomial defines the reduced union of one-dimensional components of the peripheral eigenvalue image; zero-dimensional image components are omitted ([[def-knot-a-polynomial]]; [[lem-knot-a-polynomial-boundary-elimination]]).

[F3] Dehn filling kills the primitive slope $p[\mu]+q[\lambda]$ and glues a solid torus ([[def-oriented-slope-and-knot-dehn-filling]]).

[F4] Seifert–van Kampen identifies the filled fundamental group with the pushout of the exterior and attached solid-torus groups ([[thm-seifert-van-kampen]]; [[thm-group-pushout-as-an-amalgamated-quotient]]).

[F5] A deformation retraction induces mutually inverse isomorphisms on fundamental groups at each basepoint of the retract ([[prop-retracts-inject-fundamental-groups]]).

[F6] The fundamental group of the quotient circle is isomorphic to $(\mathbb Z,+)$ by the degree map ([[thm-fundamental-group-of-the-circle]]); the based homeomorphism $[t]\mapsto e^{2\pi i t}$ identifies it with the unit circle.

[A1] Full AC implies countable choice, the hypothesis of the collar theorem ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]; [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]).

[F7] Under countable choice, a smooth manifold with boundary has a smooth collar; a collar is a product embedding of the boundary with a half-open interval whose image is a neighbourhood ([[thm-collar-neighborhood-theorem]]; [[def-smooth-collar-of-a-manifold-boundary]]).

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume full AC and let $K\subset S^3$ be a nontrivial smooth knot. Form the Newton polygon of the ordinary A-polynomial using the exponent convention that the lattice point $(a,b)$ represents the monomial $M^bL^a$, so edge slopes are measured in the preferred meridian-longitude convention. Every finite rational slope or infinite slope of an edge of this Newton polygon is a boundary slope of an incompressible, boundary-incompressible, orientable surface in the knot exterior. This statement does not assert that the realizing surface is non-fibered or that the slope is strict.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, the nontrivial smooth knot with its chosen compact exterior and peripheral marking, and the stated Newton edge.

[A1] Full AC is retained. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] The exterior is compact orientable and irreducible, with no proper compressing disk. Full AC supplies the countable choice needed by its smooth Schoenflies branch. Its tube is a smooth $S^1\times D^2$ product by the normal-circle frame supplier, so the boundary is the marked smooth torus. It is connected: join two distinct exterior points by an embedded spherical arc, perturb it relative to its endpoints to be transverse to the knot, and use $1+1<3$ to conclude it misses the knot. Radial projection of nonzero tube fibers to their boundary fixes the exterior and retracts that arc to an exterior path; equal endpoints need the constant path. [[lem-knot-exterior-is-irreducible]] [[lem-nontrivial-knot-exterior-boundary-incompressible]] [[lem-knot-normal-circle-bundle-trivialization]] [[lem-choice-free-relative-transversality-for-a-compact-smooth-embedding]]

[F2] Every selected Newton edge has an ACTUAL finite representation field and extending local curve valuation with peripheral eigenvalue pair a positive multiple of its primitive minimum normal. For an enhanced edge the representation is absolutely irreducible, including when its factor is also $L-1$. [[lem-newton-edges-have-valued-finite-peripheral-representation-models]]

[F3] For that valued representation, the actual lattice-tree/equivariant-map construction gives a connected orientable smooth essential surface with nonempty boundary whose primitive class annihilates the valuation pair. It proves both incompressibility and boundary-incompressibility by map-preserving compression complexity. With an absolutely irreducible representation it also proves that the chosen component cannot be a fiber. [[thm-nonelliptic-lattice-tree-actions-produce-essential-boundary-surfaces]]

[F4] In the stated marking $a[\lambda]+b[\mu]$ has slope $b/a$, including $a=0$ as infinity. [[def-boundary-slope-of-an-incompressible-surface]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume full AC and let $K\subset S^3$ be a knot. The input package required by the Baldwin–Sivek thin-knot and infinitely-many-abelian-surgeries arguments consists of the following conclusions with their stated hypotheses: (i) a nontrivial $\mathrm{SU}(2)$-averse knot has a unique rational accumulation slope and either it or its mirror is an instanton L-space knot; (ii) a nontrivial instanton L-space knot is fibered and its symmetrized Alexander polynomial has coefficients in $\{-1,0,1\}$ with nonzero coefficients alternating in sign; (iii) the L-space satellite restrictions and the pattern/companion surgery-transfer statements exclude the satellite cases used in §§3–5; and (iv) the hyperbolic Dehn-filling theorem and the knot-exterior JSJ classification reduce the remaining cases to torus knots. This carrier records the exact imported result interfaces and does not assert that these conclusions have been proved locally.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC and the full original input-package scope. The finite representation/pillowcase argument below is retained. Its gauge-theoretic premises are explicit external inputs, not locally reconstructed instanton proofs.

[F1] Filling with primitive slope $p[\mu]+q[\lambda]$ imposes the actual group relation $\mu^p\lambda^q=1$. Abelianization of a knot group is generated by its meridian. A unitary reducible two-dimensional representation is simultaneously diagonal: the orthogonal complement of its invariant line is invariant as well. Consequently its image is abelian, and a representation with abelian image factors through the cyclic abelianization of the filled group. Thus SU2-abelian and SU2-cyclic are equivalent here, including the zero-slope case. [[def-sl-two-abelian-surgery]] [[thm-knot-exterior-homology-and-longitude]]

[F2] The actual finite representation and common-eigenline incidence varieties have finitely many irreducible components. For each component, dimension of its affine image is the transcendence degree of its coordinate function field. The generic adjoint trace pairing, cap identity, pair exact sequence and word derivations apply over the actual finitely generated characteristic-zero field. [[lem-sl2-representation-variety-is-affine]] [[lem-classical-affine-algebraic-set-finite-irreducible-components]] [[thm-affine-domain-dimension-transcendence-degree]] [[lem-generic-adjoint-peripheral-kernel-is-the-logarithmic-conormal-line]]

[F3] The ordinary A-polynomial is a nonzero square-free Laurent equation for the one-dimensional peripheral eigenvalue-image components, including the abelian component. It omits isolated image components but not points on a curve component. [[def-knot-a-polynomial]]

[F4] The actual marked pattern/companion filling transfers, including reducible nonabelian SL2 cases, and the closed hyperbolic holonomy lift are already supplied. They do not establish the instanton alternative [L1], L-space surgery, or Alexander coefficient restrictions. [[lem-satellite-sl2-abelian-fillings-transfer-to-pattern-and-companion]] [[lem-closed-oriented-hyperbolic-holonomy-has-a-faithful-sl2-lift]]

The classical knot trichotomy used in their Proposition 2.15 and proofs in §§4–5 is imported at that knot-exterior scope: a nontrivial nontorus nonsatellite knot is hyperbolic. No arbitrary atoroidal manifold assertion is inferred from a definition. These are established external results, not new local proofs of their gauge or hyperbolization foundations.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume full AC. A smooth knot $K\subset S^3$ admits infinitely many distinct rational $SL_2(\mathbb C)$-abelian Dehn surgeries if and only if $K$ is a torus knot, with the unknot included as a torus knot with one parameter of absolute value one.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, the actual marked knots and primitive rational filling convention. The completed local operations and the explicitly imported full converse are distinguished below; the original full Statement is not narrowed.

[F1] The signed torus group has central $h=x^a=y^b$ and preferred longitude $\lambda=h\mu^{-ab}$. A knot meridian normally generates its group. Exterior homology is generated by that meridian, with preferred longitude zero. [[thm-torus-knot-group-presentation]] [[lem-satellite-peripheral-representations-transfer-thinness]] [[thm-knot-exterior-homology-and-longitude]]

[F2] Filling kills precisely the primitive peripheral word. An abelian satellite filling transfers to the same pattern-closure slope and, for signed $w\ne0$, to the companion slope divided by $w^2$, through the actual diagonal, Jordan and central-character-twist constructions. [[def-sl-two-abelian-surgery]] [[lem-satellite-sl2-abelian-fillings-transfer-to-pattern-and-companion]]

[F3] A supplied complete finite-volume hyperbolic knot metric has complete closed smooth hyperbolic fillings at all but finitely many primitive slopes. The complete metric has a universal $\mathbb H^3$ cover and faithful projective holonomy. For a CLOSED oriented smooth such manifold the actual complete-Heegaard Spin frame cover supplies a faithful SL2 lift. Finite-sheet covers of compact spaces are compact. [[thm-thurston-hyperbolic-dehn-filling]] [[lem-complete-curvature-minus-one-manifolds-are-kleinian-quotients]] [[lem-closed-oriented-hyperbolic-holonomy-has-a-faithful-sl2-lift]] [[thm-compactness-is-invariant-under-finite-sheeted-coverings]]

[F4] For a smooth fibered essential satellite with nontrivial companion and noncore pattern, the actual cut-fiber construction gives $w\ne0$, component fibrations and $g(K)=g(P(U))+|w|g(C)$. Nonzero adjacent highest Alexander coefficients force $P(U)$ nontrivial. A nontrivial knot has positive genus. This supplier does not assert that an arbitrary knot is fibered. [[lem-fibered-satellite-cuts-give-nonzero-winding-and-genus-splitting]] [[lem-knot-genus-zero-iff-unknot]]

[F5] Positive-meridian Alexander modules have square Seifert presentations and determinant orders. Mayer–Vietoris applies to the actual collared satellite cover. Signed torus polynomials have the explicit symmetric absolute-parameter formula. [[thm-seifert-matrix-presents-knot-alexander-module]] [[thm-seifert-determinant-is-the-knot-alexander-polynomial]] [[thm-mayer-vietoris-sequence-in-singular-homology]] [[thm-torus-knot-alexander-and-genus-formulas]]

They are not consequences asserted from the local ASD foundations alone.

[L2] The retained minimal-genus derivation uses the actual knot-exterior trichotomy, with the residual metric step described in [[thm-thurston-hyperbolization-for-atoroidal-knot-exteriors]]. Its local proof is not certified here. The full original classification is instead supplied directly by [E1], retaining all actual signed filling and satellite operations already proved locally.

[E1] **External input:** Baldwin–Sivek, arXiv:2405.19197v2, Theorem 1.1 (p.1), with Theorem 5.1 and its proof in §5, asserts for ANY knot in $S^3$ that infinitely many distinct rational $SL_2(\mathbb C)$-abelian surgeries occur if and only if it is a torus knot. Here “abelian” means EVERY homomorphism has abelian image, not only every irreducible homomorphism; this is their opening definition. Their §2 includes the unknot among torus knots. The actual statement, definitions and §5 theorem/transfer interfaces were consulted directly; the remaining published classification proof is imported, not locally reconstructed.

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume full AC and let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth knot. For a nonzero Laurent polynomial $f(M,L)$, its Newton polygon is the convex hull in $\mathbb R^2$ of exponent pairs $(a,b)$ for which the coefficient of $M^bL^a$ is nonzero. The enhanced A-polynomial is **thin** when this polygon is contained in an affine line; the constant polynomial $1$ has a one-point Newton polygon and is thin. Then the enhanced A-polynomial of $K$ is thin if and only if $K$ is a torus knot, including the unknot.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC and the smooth knot in the Statement. The accepted local torus, hyperbolic and conditional satellite arguments are retained. The remaining established classification is imported explicitly in [E1].

[F1] The positive coprime torus-knot formula, with its separate $b=2$ and $b>2$ cases, and the unknot formula are proved by the explicit irreducible peripheral matrix calculation. [[lem-torus-knot-enhanced-a-polynomial]], [[lem-torus-presentation-irreducible-peripheral-eigenvalue-curves]], [[def-coprime-torus-knot]], [[lem-torus-knot-unit-slope-is-unknot]]

[F2] Complete one-cusped holonomy has an actual smooth complex ordinary deformation curve and an augmented eigenvalue-ratio logarithm coordinate $u$, with longitude logarithm $v(u)=\tau u+O(u^2)$ and $\operatorname{Im}\tau\ne0$. The forgetful map is the stated branched trace-squared map, so this is not an unproved choice of a logarithm on the ordinary quotient. [[lem-one-cusped-deformation-parameters-and-holonomy]], [[thm-augmented-finite-volume-hyperbolic-holonomy-coordinates]]

[F3] The exterior retracts from the complement of the smooth knot; Alexander duality computes its integral homology, and the universal coefficient theorem computes its mod-two cohomology. Its compact smooth core has a compatible finite triangulation. [[thm-knot-exterior-homology-and-longitude]], [[thm-alexander-duality-for-compact-locally-contractible-subsets-of-a-sphere]], [[thm-universal-coefficient-theorem-for-cohomology-over-a-pid]], [[thm-compact-smooth-manifolds-with-corners-admit-relative-finite-triangulations]]

[F4] Finite presentation matrices define the actual representation variety; peripheral eigenvalue images of its one-dimensional irreducible-character components contribute to the enhanced curve. [[lem-sl2-representation-variety-is-affine]], [[def-sl-two-character-variety-and-peripheral-eigenvalues]], [[def-enhanced-a-polynomial]]

[F5] The actual proof of the generic adjoint peripheral kernel computes its boundary inclusion rank by Lefschetz duality and pair exactness, and pairs arbitrary field derivations with actual word cycles, including a moving peripheral eigenbasis. These particular field-linear arguments do not require its Statement's curve hypothesis; their extension to the generic field used below is explicitly supplied in step 2.5. Affine-domain dimension is transcendence degree, and Noetherian algebraic sets have finitely many irreducible components. [[lem-generic-adjoint-peripheral-kernel-is-the-logarithmic-conormal-line]], [[thm-affine-domain-dimension-transcendence-degree]], [[lem-noetherian-space-has-finitely-many-irreducible-components]]

[F6] Cyclic-cover Mayer–Vietoris is the ordinary exact sequence on the lifted collared union, with its natural deck action. The knot Alexander module has a square Seifert presentation and its determinant is the normalized Alexander polynomial up to a Laurent unit. The torus polynomial has its explicit rational formula. [[thm-mayer-vietoris-sequence-in-singular-homology]], [[thm-seifert-matrix-presents-knot-alexander-module]], [[thm-seifert-determinant-is-the-knot-alexander-polynomial]], [[thm-torus-knot-alexander-and-genus-formulas]]

[F7] Every nonzero root of an ordinary or enhanced Newton-edge polynomial is a root of unity, including the entire Newton segment in the thin case. The actual relative-determinant central extension and boundary fundamental-chain commutator proof supply every prescribed root. This makes all constants of the thin peripheral graphs finite order; it does not exclude a vertical segment. [[lem-knot-newton-edge-roots-are-roots-of-unity]]

Its smooth disk/window rerun retains the smooth category. A nontrivial smooth knot has positive genus by the actual genus-zero unknot equivalence; full AC supplies its countable-choice hypothesis. [[lem-fibered-satellite-cuts-give-nonzero-winding-and-genus-splitting]], [[lem-knot-genus-zero-iff-unknot]], [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]

[F9] The actual pattern exterior has meridian/longitude homology markings and representation extensions which transfer enhanced thinness to the pattern closure and, for $w\ne0$, to the companion with slope divided by $w^2$. The pointwise pattern extension includes exceptional matrices; the companion operation uses finite generic fields and then closure, not false simultaneous diagonalization at every parabolic representation. [[lem-satellite-peripheral-representations-transfer-thinness]]

[F10] The actual smooth Seifert-fibered knot-exterior branch is a torus knot or the unknot, by the finite base/filling-group and marked genus-one construction. [[thm-seifert-fibered-smooth-knot-exteriors-have-torus-knot-models]], [[lem-smooth-tori-in-s-three-give-marked-unknotted-or-satellite-models]], [[thm-jsj-decomposition-of-knot-exteriors]], [[lem-knot-exterior-is-irreducible]], [[lem-nontrivial-knot-exterior-boundary-incompressible]]

[L1] The instanton/representation premises used in the retained local converse are external inputs of [[lem-baldwin-sivek-instanton-surgery-and-newton-polygon-inputs]]. In particular the knot-or-mirror L-space, fiberedness, alternating-unit and adjacent-top properties are not inferred merely from the ASD foundations. Their §2.3 and (1.1) define the same enhanced polynomial by irreducible peripheral curves, with $A_K=\operatorname{lcm}(\widetilde A_K,L-1)$; their torus convention includes the unknot (§2 opening). contract.heading: Statement
contract.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M=\Gamma\backslash\mathbb H^3$ be a connected oriented complete finite-volume hyperbolic three-manifold, with a compact smooth core $N$ and $k\ge1$ standard rank-two torus cusp ends. Thus $M$ is the interior of $N$ and each end has metric $dt^2+e^{-2t}g_i$, where $g_i$ is a flat torus metric. Let $\rho_0:\pi_1(N)\to G=\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb C)$ be its holonomy. Choose a positively oriented basis $(\mu_i,\lambda_i)$ for each oriented horotorus, so its translation lattice can be normalized to $\langle1,\tau_i^0\rangle$ with $\operatorname{Im}\tau_i^0>0$.

The germ of representations modulo conjugacy at $[\rho_0]$ is a smooth complex manifold of dimension $k$. The functions $s_i(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}^2\rho(\mu_i)$ are local holomorphic coordinates near their values $s_i=4$. Trace squared is well defined in $G$, independently of an $SL_2$ lift.

Augment a nearby representation by choosing one common invariant line for each peripheral subgroup, and quotient these data by simultaneous conjugacy. The germ of this augmented space at the complete representation and its unique peripheral fixed lines is a smooth complex $k$-manifold. It has holomorphic coordinates $u=(u_1,\ldots,u_k)$, where $u_i$ is the eigenvalue-ratio logarithm for $\mu_i$ on the selected line, and the forgetful map is
$$s_i=4\cosh^2(u_i/2).$$
The corresponding logarithms $v_i$ for $\lambda_i$ are holomorphic and satisfy
$$v_i(u)=\tau_i(u)u_i,\qquad \tau_i(0)=\tau_i^0,\qquad \operatorname{Im}\tau_i(u)>0$$
on a sufficiently small neighborhood. In particular $u_i=0$ if and only if $v_i=0$, and for $k=1$ one has $v(u)=\tau^0u+O(u^2)$. No positive or nondegenerate ideal triangulation is assumed. The statement concerns the augmented space, not a single-valued eigenvalue logarithm on the ordinary conjugacy quotient.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, the finite-volume quotient, its supplied compact core and standard cusp models, the complete holonomy and the positively oriented peripheral bases.

[A1] AC supplies DC and Countable Choice for the listed suppliers, finite-dimensional choices and the sequence of formal extensions below. [[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]

[F1] Every closed smooth square-integrable one-form with values in the homogeneous-metric adjoint bundle has a smooth square-integrable primitive. [[lem-adjoint-hyperbolic-ltwo-one-forms-are-exact]]

[F2] The compact core has a finite CW model, and the local-coefficient pair sequence and Poincaré–Lefschetz duality apply. Over $\mathbb C$, the invariant nondegenerate pairing $\operatorname{tr}(AB)$ identifies the adjoint local system with its dual. [[lem-compact-smooth-manifolds-have-finite-cw-models-under-countable-choice]], [[thm-pair-long-exact-sequences-with-local-coefficients]], [[thm-poincare-lefschetz-duality-with-local-coefficients]]

[F3] A holomorphic equation with invertible partial Jacobian has a unique local holomorphic solution. [[thm-holomorphic-implicit-function-theorem]]

[F4] Commuting affine holonomies $w\mapsto e^{u_i}w+a_i$ and $w\mapsto e^{v_i}w+b_i$, with nonzero complete translations and nonreal complete ratio, satisfy $v_i=\tau_i u_i$ for a holomorphic $\tau_i$ extending that ratio, on arbitrary reduced analytic parameter spaces. [[lem-commuting-affine-peripheral-holonomy-logarithm-factorization]]

contract.heading: Statement
contract.text: Assume full AC. Let $a\ge b\ge1$ be coprime positive integers, and let $T_{a,b}\subset S^3$ be the corresponding torus knot. If a knot $K\subset S^3$ has the same enhanced A-polynomial as $T_{a,b}$ up to a Laurent unit and the same Alexander-polynomial breadth (highest exponent minus lowest exponent of its symmetrized Alexander polynomial), then $K$ has the same underlying unoriented knot type as $T_{a,b}$. When $b\ge2$, the absolute torus parameters of $K$ agree with $\{a,b\}$.

facts:
**Given:** Full AC, a knot $K$, a positive torus knot $T_{a,b}$, equality of enhanced A-polynomials up to a Laurent unit, and equality of Alexander breadths.

[F1] A knot whose enhanced A-polynomial has Newton polygon contained in a line is a torus knot. For a nontrivial torus knot $T_{a,b}$ with $a>b\ge2$, its enhanced A-polynomial has a line-segment Newton polygon of slope $ab$ in the stated convention; the unknot has enhanced A-polynomial $1$ ([[thm-enhanced-a-polynomial-newton-polygon-detects-torus-knots]]; [[lem-torus-knot-enhanced-a-polynomial]]).

[F2] For signed coprime parameters, the Alexander breadth of $T_{p,q}$ is $(|p|-1)(|q|-1)$; changing both signs reverses knot orientation and changing one sign takes the mirror ([[thm-torus-knot-alexander-and-genus-formulas]]; [[def-coprime-torus-knot]]).

[F3] A torus knot with one parameter of absolute value $1$ is the standard unknot ([[lem-torus-knot-unit-slope-is-unknot]]).

[A1] Full AC implies countable choice, the hypothesis used by [F3] ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]; [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]).

[E1] The classification used in [F1] is now complete with the explicit external input Baldwin–Sivek, arXiv:2405.19197v2, Theorem 1.2. Their Corollary 1.4 (p.2) independently states detection by the enhanced polynomial together with Alexander degree; the finite parameter-recovery proof below is retained locally. The source statement was consulted directly, not its gauge-theoretic proof reconstructed. The breadth used here is twice the degree of the symmetric polynomial for torus knots, so equality of breadths gives exactly the equality used in step2.1.

contract.heading: Statement refuted
contract.text: Let $U,V\in SL_2(\mathbb C)$ commute and have a common invariant line on which their eigenvalues are $M,L$, respectively. For every primitive pair $(p,q)\in\mathbb Z^2$, if $M^pL^q=1$, then $U^pV^q=I_2$.

facts:
**Given:** $N=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$, $U=I_2+N$, $V=I_2$, and the primitive pair $(p,q)=(1,0)$.

[F1] $N^2=0$, so $U$ is upper-triangular unipotent with determinant one and is not the identity.

[F2] The identity matrix commutes with every matrix, and the eigenvalues of an upper-triangular matrix are its diagonal entries.
